The Cellars.name: The Cellars
The Cellars.text:
The cellars were the domain of Castle Arudora’s servants. These rooms are isolated from, and extend beneath, the ground floors of the reception halls and the temple (yet are above the deeper dungeons even further below). It was here the castle’s cooks, launderers, maids, groundskeepers, maintenance workers, and more lived and toiled, all under the guidance of the castle’s majordomo, Enoch Grashikin. The eastern side of the cellars housed the castle guards, including barracks and an infirmary. As long as the reception halls remain inaccessible, easy access between the east and west wings of the cellars is limited to a passageway that runs below, connecting the barracks to the kitchens where the castle’s brewery was located.

Many of the servants perished the night the curse descended. As the horrors spread, they fled into the cellars as the brave-but-doomed guards remained outdoors. It didn’t matter, and after the guards were slain, the servants were too. The souls of most of the servants were reborn as animal-headed phantoms, and today, these phantoms populate much of the area. They work with very little rest or respite, transforming raw ectoplasm into the food, drink, and distractions demanded by the area’s new lord, Augsten Arudora. Transformed by the curse into a brutish ogre to match his bullying personality, Augsten fancies himself king, allowing none of his subjects to leave the cellars without his express permission once the PCs unlock the area.

Entering the Cellars.name: Entering the Cellars
Entering the Cellars.text: The PCs should be 7th level before they start to explore the castle’s cellars. There are several entrances into the cellars from the castle grounds; when the PCs unlock this area by returning @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.fZDL0jQQy1jQTg4c]{Jinnivere’s Riding Crop} to the fountain at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3}, make sure to describe to them how the structure housing the groundskeepers’ station (areas @UUID[.1tfiJnjtQbAUTr1s]{C1}–@UUID[.u9oNbVptkOpdYsZo]{C11}), as well as the lower castle exteriors along the west and east sides of the main structure, solidify out of the green mist, so it’ll be obvious where they can go next. These entrances are all summarized in @UUID[.aAIJLDj5OPYa6xZu]{Cellars Connections}.

The Skies Above.name: The Skies Above
The Skies Above.text:
The skies grow dark and remain overcast all day long. Temperatures remain crisp and cool, but the periodic breezes are now more common, and now and then rise to a gust. At every sunset, the sound of distant thunder rumbles. The waves of Lake Laroba are choppy and now require a @Check[athletics|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim} in the wind-tossed waters.

Sunrise is at 8:30 a.m., and sunset is at 6:30 p.m. The days are 10 hours long and the nights are 14 hours long.

Cellar Ambushes.name: Cellar Ambushes
Cellar Ambushes.text:
Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.HDF02TkzQISYCgLN]{Phantom Knights x4}

If the PCs rest in an unsafe area in the cellars, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:5]. On a failure, they are ambushed while they camp by four phantom knights.

These phantom knights move in and out of walls with ease and take advantage of this fact to ambush the PCs anywhere they might have holed up in the cellars. These knights are not a part of those found in the encounter areas of the cellars, but instead form and reform as needed from trapped souls whenever an ambush takes place.

Lucid Nightmares.name: Lucid Nightmares
Lucid Nightmares.text:
After unlocking the cellars, the nightmare changes. The PC is now one of the castle servants, scrambling frantically to appease their supervisors and to dodge insults and abuse from nobles and Arudoras who are engaged in one form of revelry or the next. As the PC delivers food, takes drink orders, cleans messes, and delivers drinks, they realize the next aristocrat they are to serve is the mysterious figure with the staff. This time, they can tell the figure is a human man clad in leather armor, but cannot see his face under the shadows of his cloak hood. Upon spotting the figure, the PC commits a horrific faux pas—dropping a carried meal, slipping and falling into an aristocrat, or even suddenly losing their pants or vomiting onto a well-dressed noble. The guests and Arudoras alike descend upon the PC in a fury, chasing them through the castle halls and demanding blood. The PC wakes just as they find shelter with their fellow servants (among whom are the other PCs), only for them to turn on the PC as well.

The Disastrous Party

Resist Nightmare @Check[will|dc:23|name:The Disastrous Party|options:lucid-nightmare]

Critical Failure The PC wakes with enochlophobia (fear of crowds), and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} whenever they become flanked during the next 24 hours.

Research @Check[performance|dc:25|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to turn your faux pas into an entertaining bit of comedy, or @Check[diplomacy|dc:28|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to successfully navigate the demands of the aristocrats you’re serving

Effect

@UUID[Item.skaR0p8AEpv7FvBs]{Enochlophobia}

If a PC critically fails to resist this nightmare, use the linked effect to automate a Note reminder whenever they are attacked by a flanking foe.

Ground Floor Features.name: Ground Floor Features
Ground Floor Features.text:
The cellars were lit by lanterns and torches before the curse fell, but now that the servants themselves have become phantoms, they no longer need light to see. These unlit light sources are located on the walls in every room, but the PCs must light them themselves to take advantage of them, otherwise the chambers within the cellars are dark. Walls are of either worked stone (along exteriors) or of wood (on the interiors), and in each case can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climbed} with a @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check. Unless otherwise noted, ceiling heights are 10 feet on both the ground and underground floors of the cellars. Doors are made of reinforced wood and, unless indicated in the text, cannot be locked.

There are many halls and rooms in the cellars. When combat breaks out, feel free to have things spread into nearby adjacent rooms to make for a more dynamic and complex battle, but be wary of having too many encounters bleed into each other—remember that if two Trivial encounters merge, it becomes a Moderate encounter, and so on.

Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

All locations in the ground floor portion of this chapter can be found in the Castle Grounds level.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.ONTeDjH5dol5Cnoz]{Inside Bastardhall}

As the PCs enter the indoor areas of Bastardhall, you can play this ambience sound.

Tight Squeezes

Chimneys and pit toilets provide narrow connections to other regions of Bastardhall (assuming the region in question is unlocked), but are generally far too narrow for a Medium or larger PC to navigate. A Small creature can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeeze} down one of these shafts with a @Check[acrobatics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Squeeze.Title|options:action:squeeze|traits:exploration,move] check. A Tiny creature can move freely (or, at worst, treat the narrow shaft as difficult terrain), but they must also Climb with a @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check to do so or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Qf1ylAbdVi1rkc8M]{Maneuver in Flight} with a @Check[acrobatics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.ManeuverInFlight.Title|options:action:maneuver-in-flight|traits:move] check if they’re flying in the narrow confines.

Groundskeeper's Entrance.name: Groundskeeper's Entrance
Groundskeeper's Entrance.text:
The floor of this room is made of worked stone. Glass windows look out into the courtyard near the entrance door, while further into the room, there are two shelving areas for boots, cloaks, and frequently-used groundskeepers’ tools like rakes and shovels.

The northwestern door leads out into the castle grounds (area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1c}). The equipment stored here is old and mundane. A PC who approaches the southeastern door can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:25] check to notice the faint odor of decaying meat faintly wafting through the cracks from somewhere beyond; once the door is opened, the smell of decay is obvious—the source can be found in area @UUID[.DZXL8wmfM3EFjooO]{C7}.

Tool Storage.name: Tool Storage
Tool Storage.text:
Various landscaping and gardening tools are stored here, either on hanging racks or strewn atop tables. A pair of dirty windows in the east wall sit just above one such table.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.N8yek3Gh2x8ZVJAl]{Tool Storage}

Most of the tools stored here are mundane and unremarkable, but a PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the room discovers a wand of speak with plants among the disorganized mess on the table by the windows.

Wormy Fertilizer.name: Wormy Fertilizer
Wormy Fertilizer.text:
Several wooden barrels stand along the walls of this dank, stuffy chamber.

The barrels were used to store fertilizer for gardening work in the days before the curse, but its contents are now corrupted. A PC who opens a barrel finds it to be infested with foul-smelling worms that hiss and click disturbingly. The worms are harmless unless a PC puts a hand into the soil, at which point they chew and bite, dealing 1d6 piercing damage per round (@Check[reflex|basic|dc:20] save). A PC who takes any damage from these worms risks becoming infected with their hunger; they are exposed to the curse of the ravenous (see below) and must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:20|traits:curse,magical] save to resist the affliction. Frustratingly, these worms seem only interested in biting the PCs—they won’t attack any of the inhabitants of Bastardhall.

Treasure

These worms are one of the five ingredients the PCs might be asked to gather by the cooks in area @UUID[.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40}. A PC can gather enough worms for the meal into a container as a 1 minute activity, during which they must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:20|options:damaging-effect] save to avoid being bitten for @Damage[1[piercing]]{1 point of piercing damage} (and subsequent exposure to the curse of the ravenous).

Curse of the Ravenous

Curse 5

  • Curse
  • Magical

This hideous curse kills through constant hunger. You become gaunt and repeatedly gnash your teeth as your body begins to consume itself.

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:20|name:Curse of the Ravenous|traits:curse,magical]

Effect No matter how much you eat, you aren't satiated. After 1 day, you begin starving. Each week, you receive a new saving throw against the curse.

Seed Bins.name: Seed Bins
Seed Bins.text:
Four wooden bins sit against the walls of this room, two to the north and two to the south, although the southeastern bin is surrounded by several small pouches.

These bins each contain dozens of small bags of various seeds once used in the garden (area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.XTFntNXqyFNvra51]{B4}), but years of exposure to the curse has rendered nearly all of the seeds non-viable.

Encounter

Trivial 7

@UUID[Actor.fbeZ9bH41S2ko3yt]{They Grow Inside}

Hazard: On the night of the curse, one of the groundskeeper’s assistants tried to hide in the bin, not realizing that by making enough room to do so, she was making it obvious (via the discarded seed bags) that someone was hiding here. She was swiftly found by a sahkil and murdered. Her body remains stuffed in this bin, a look of horror on her face. Her corpse has fertilized a riot of moist, diseased looking plants, and the corrupted seeds have grown through her flesh—ironically, keeping her body fresh but infested. The first PC who opens this bin finds out the hard way that her spirit lingers within her remains.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Open Seed Bin" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to open the bin, revealing the infested corpse within!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.MXq56jLWXSeIbsx1]{Horrified Corpse}

After the haunt has triggered, the PCs can spend 1 minute @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the body to find a small iron key on a leather cord around the assistant’s neck—this key unlocks the door in area @UUID[.2tXKE2JE45z1vCAd]{C38}.

Woodworking Shop.name: Woodworking Shop
Woodworking Shop.text:
This room is a well-stocked and well- organized, if dusty and neglected, workshop. A sturdy workbench stands to the east, while shelves stocked with tools and supplies stand to the north and south.

The tools and equipment here are particularly well maintained, even with the layer of dust on them. A PC who uses this workshop to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.rmwa3OyhTZ2i2AHl]{Craft} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.bT3skovyLUtP22ME]{Repair} wooden objects gains a +2 item bonus to the check from the equipment and materials in this room.

Effect

@UUID[Item.3TuYn7B1fIZCfxCL]{Wooden Object Repairs}

Use this effect to give the PCs a toggleable bonus to Craft and Repair checks.

Lounge.name: Lounge
Lounge.text:
A pair of leather sofas stand against the north and south walls of this room, while the floor features a ratty-looking bearskin rug. To the west stands a cast-iron stove. Two small containers sit on a nearby windowsill.

The gardeners and groundskeepers used this room as a place to take a break, and would sometimes cook meals or heat drinks on the stove when they weren’t feeling up to making the trip to the mess hall (area @UUID[.DqhDfn8rAdJqBC6g]{C17}) to eat.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.erbYzP6cZTMxsaNU]{Lounge Containers}

One of the two containers on the windowsill contains 20 matchsticks, while the other contains four small vials. These vials once each held a dose of a special narcotic the groundskeepers enjoyed on occasion, but time and the curse have corrupted and transformed the contents of these vials into four doses of tangle root toxin.

Common Room.name: Common Room
Common Room.text:
A large brick fireplace, several high-backed chairs, a few low tables, and a large leather sofa adorn this room, giving it the air of a place of comfort and relaxation—or at least they would, had those tables not been strewn with well-gnawed bones and the fireplace filled with an unnerving amount of stacked skulls carved with strange runes and designs.

Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.UAgosUUeyJkx3EbY]{Ghoulish Gardeners x3}

Creatures: Once a common room for the gardeners and groundskeepers to rest and relax, this room serves mostly the same purpose today, even after those laborers became transformed into ghouls. As undead, they can’t starve to death, but it’s been long... sooo long... since they’ve had a fresh meal to chew on. And no, the body of their one-time coworker in the seed bin doesn’t count—it’s tainted by plants, and that’s not what connoisseurs of well- aged meat, like these three, have any interest in.

In lieu of feeding, these three ghoulish gardeners spent many years entertaining each other with a wide range of riddles and wordplay games, but after a time even those ran out, and without much else to do, they’ve dwindled into a sort of patient hibernation. The three sit to the south—two on the sofa and one on the chair, slumped a bit so as to look like nothing more than dust-covered corpses who died where they sat. However, they are very much awake and awaiting.

If the PCs manage to reach this area without alerting them, the ghouls are slow to rouse and take a –4 penalty to initiative, but otherwise they leap to attack as soon as the first PC comes within striking distance, rolling Deception for initiative. The ghoulish gardeners are eager to kill the PCs, and might not even be able to wait for the meat to decay to deliciousness before they eat. They each cast fear on the first round before switching to jaws and claw Strikes, but as soon as one is destroyed, the other two realize they might be in over their heads and make a fighting retreat to the east toward area @UUID[.u9oNbVptkOpdYsZo]{C11} to join with their leader, using wall of thorns to fill the area behind them to make pursuit difficult.

Effect

@UUID[Item.BYaAGCpU7GWMiGEI]{Initiative Penalty}

If the PCs sneak up on the ghouls and they are slow to rouse, apply this effect to the ghouls before you roll initiative their initiative to automate their penalty.

Groundskeeper's Tower.name: Groundskeeper's Tower
Groundskeeper's Tower.text:
A pair of long planter boxes filled with long-dead plants sit to either side of this circular room. Stairs lead up and down in opposite directions from a landing to the southwest.

The stairs leading up are blocked by a wall of impenetrable green mist as long as the reception halls remain locked, but once they’re opened, the stairs lead up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.SdfuOIpfDT5Z9sfc]{D19}. No such mists block the route down to area @UUID[.2tXKE2JE45z1vCAd]{C38} below.

Gardener's Rooms.name: Gardener's Rooms
Gardener's Rooms.text:
A twin bunk bed, a writing desk, and a single chair are this room’s only features.

Both of these rooms were used by the four gardeners who worked for the groundskeeper. Now that they’re all ghouls or dead, they’ve not returned to either of these rooms, leaving them to gather dust. Area C9a between the two contains a pit toilet that leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.lsZGGT5sRWOqjV37]{E5a} once the dungeons are unlocked.

Meeting Room.name: Meeting Room
Meeting Room.text:
A wooden table with a chair to the north and south sits in this room atop an old, dusty throw rug. Behind the southern chair stands a bookshelf on which several dead houseplants, a few ceramic pitchers and vases, and several books and scroll tubes sit under thick layers of dust.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.vmdyERKOQp1fPoBw]{Southern Shelves}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the shelves to the south for a minute uncovers, under all that dust, two scrolls of safe passage, and a scroll of vital beacon being used as a bookmark in a book about poisonous fungi of Ustalav.

Groundskeeper's Room.name: Groundskeeper's Room
Groundskeeper's Room.text:
A plain-looking bed sits against the far wall of this room, opposite a desk and chair near a wall. Drooping plants with glistening seed pods that look more like pimples or boils of meat than vegetable matter grow in planter boxes sitting on the floor, on shelves, or hanging from the ceiling in dangling pots, giving the room a loamy smell that mixes unpleasantly with the lingering stink of decay.

The small closet (area C11a) contains a cozy little upright tub and a small counter of personal items, the most notable of which are a journal and a scroll tube (see Treasure, below). The plants in here look merely diseased at first glance, but a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} them and is at least expert in Nature can tell that they’re being magically kept on the verge of death through some sort of corrupt primal magic.

Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.2Vy5g8i9t6hyudO8]{Milsindi Mopsindur}

Creatures: The castle’s groundskeeper, a gnome woman named Milsindi Mopsindur, lived and died here. Like the gardeners who once worked for her, she’s become a ghoul. For the first hundred or so years of the curse, she tried and failed over and over to cultivate corrupted plants that would grow delicious rotten meat, but the best she could do are the verdant abominations in this room. Since then, she’s languished in this room, patiently waiting for something delicious to break the monotony. It’s likely she’ll be alerted by one of the fleeing ghouls from area @UUID[.DZXL8wmfM3EFjooO]{C7}, but regardless, she attacks as soon as she spots the PCs, fighting until destroyed. If one of the PCs carries a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JmlPFAbjPvbhhKeu]{Vile Remnant}, though, she senses the magic item and demands the PCs hand it over. If they agree to do so, she lets them leave the building unharmed, only to rebury the vile remnant elsewhere in the castle grounds before leading any surviving ghouls (including the “ghoulrilla” down in area @UUID[.2tXKE2JE45z1vCAd]{C38}) on a hunt to finish the PCs off.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.bB5TPcExJNvGLuO2]{Counter}

The journal on the counter in area C11a focuses on Milsindi’s groundskeeper tasks and landscaping budgets and goals from before the curse. The journal also contains a wealth of information about Jinnivere Arudora, whom Milsindi loathed for her disregard in how she rode her horses around the castle grounds and did all sorts of damage to the landscaping. A PC can use the journal to research Jinnivere.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.6tXqaoCmhlHFRm3I]{Jinnivere Arudora}

Groundskeeper’s Journal: You spend an hour reading through the groundskeeper’s journal, taking notes on her distaste for Jinnivere Arudora.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[nature|dc:23|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to swiftly understand and skim over the less interesting notes about gardening and landscaping and focus on the gossip, or @Check[perception|dc:25|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to notice the sections where she talks about Jinnivere.

Servant's Hall.name: Servant's Hall
Servant's Hall.text:
This twenty-five-foot-wide stone-floored hall winds south and around the corner. Several doors are set into the walls, but the double door to the southwest looks particularly notable with carvings of dancing skeletons adorning it. Another double door to the east looks elegant, with curtains hanging over what appear to be glass panels.

The skeleton-decorated door looks charmingly spooky, but is otherwise unremarkable; it leads to the servants’ shrine (area @UUID[.yYVET9FqdVmC0NwM]{C13}). The northernmost door (area C12a) opens into the castle courtyard (area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1f}), while the elegant door to the east (area C12b) leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.78A34DGpyfbsAqFq]{D7a} in the reception halls—but until that area is unlocked, anyone who parts the curtains to peer through the glass panes in the door sees only impassable green mist. The two doors at area C12c both lead down to area @UUID[.MYRPJK8EXNQC5NLs]{C44a}.

Servants' Shrine.name: Servants' Shrine
Servants' Shrine.text:
The air in this large shrine reeks of decay. A row of destroyed wooden pews sits between stone pillars, all facing an upraised pulpit to the south. Walls and pillars alike are festooned with strips of pulsing, bleeding meat, as if dozens of people had been flayed into strips to decorate the room. A nest of broken timbers, bones, and torn clothing sits atop the altar to the south, while in opposite corners of the shrine, blood-dripping statues of Pharasma stand. In each case, the statue’s head is missing, and it’s from the neck that this blood drips. For all the crimson seepage from the statues and walls, or dripping from the ceiling above, the floor itself never becomes completely saturated—as if the ground were eagerly drinking up this offering.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Move Headless Statue" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to move the southwestern statue and open the secret door!

A hidden switch near the southern statue can be spotted by a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the area and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. Flipping the switch causes the statue to slide to the north, revealing a short hallway behind it leading south. A second switch to control the statue secret door can be spotted automatically inside the hall itself; throwing it a second time causes the statue to slide back into place. The second secret door further south is of more traditional construction but much harder to see—it can be discovered if a PC Seeks and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check, but until the castle temple is unlocked, opening this door only reveals a shimmering wall of green mist. Once the temple is unlocked, this secret door leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1d}.

Encounter

Moderate 7

@UUID[Actor.CzNZG7eukyjlg28r]{Vinlach} @UUID[Actor.dawMb9pgXKeQ5qgS]{Blasphemous Blood}

Creatures: A blasphemous monstrosity has taken up residence in the shrine—a hideous tangle of wings and beaks and legs known as a vinlach sahkil. When the PCs enter, the vinlach is crouched atop the altar to the south, where they’ve made an unsettling nest for themself out of shredded Pharasmin raiment, bones, splintered wood, an their own dusty feathers. They call out to the PCs, telling them that they stand before the one who would ferry Pharasma’s soul to torment, in her afterlife at the end of all things, and then invites them to step forward and bow before their glory. Any PC who does so triggers the room’s hazard, which delights the sahkil, who then flies into the air and attacks. The fiend fights to the death, but does not pursue PCs out of this area.

Hazard: When the curse struck, the temple that looms above this area became fully engulfed in Charg’s influence, but the curse found less to lash out against there, as Ryhasphinea Arudora had already corrupted the structure from Pharasma’s faith. That is not the case with this smaller shrine. The curse overwhelmed decades of worship and tradition, and where once these walls were a place that would bring peace to the mourning and joy to new parents, now it only brings pain and horror, and as soon as any intruder steps too far into the church, the beheaded statues unleash a particularly grisly manifestation of the Bastardhall curse.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.BZdKRo7gdORL6hCG]{Behind Statue} @UUID[Actor.r1OSHDNtF2j15p5W]{Filthy Nest}

A PC who Seeks near the northeastern statue and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers a soulheart on the ground behind the statue. The first PC to touch this soulheart receives a brief memory of Shirail visiting the shrine and praying to Pharasma on her first night on the isle before she moved into the Maiserene church.

Amid the filth in the sahkil’s nest, obvious to anyone who Seeks or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the area, is a greater staff of healing.

Priest's Room.name: Priest's Room
Priest's Room.text:
This chamber features a small bed with a single blanket, a desk and chair, and a shelf on which sits a small shrine. An hourglass filled with sand all the colors of the rainbow sits on the shrine, while atop the desk are stacked dozens of loose parchments under a small silver statuette of a songbird. An easel with a painting covered by a draped cloth is tucked into the northeast corner.

This room once served as the personal quarters for the oracle who cared for the servants’ shrine. A devout worshipper of both Pharasma and Shelyn, she was away from Bastardhall visiting an ailing family member when the curse struck, and while she lived with survivors’ guilt for decades after, she nonetheless lived for those decades rather than dying like the rest who stayed here.

Once the sahkil and hazard are cleared from area @UUID[.yYVET9FqdVmC0NwM]{C13}, this area is a safe haven to rest in.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.mQYfxTXBfbLNcqPC]{Shrine} @UUID[Actor.8S2ntBoXABdf82Qt]{Desk Parchments} @UUID[Actor.kOfP2ew6U1PZcQzG]{Easel}

The hourglass on the shrine is an elegant work of art. It’s 1 Bulk, but is worth 100 gp. An unusually colorful 3rd-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4ZGte0i9YbLh4dRi]{Item Facade} on the hourglass maintains the prismatic appearance of its sand.

The stack of parchments on the desk are a combination of sermons written by the oracle who once lived here, mixed in with a fair number of notes on Augsten Arudora. A PC who glances through the notes can tell that the oracle didn’t think much of Augsten, particularly his penchants for bullying the help and lording over the servants and guards. These notes were her way of gathering evidence she hoped one day to present to Lord Raudltz to have him correct his son’s behavior. That day never came, but the PCs can use these notes to Research Augsten.

At the bottom of the parchments are two scrolls: a 4th-rank scroll of heal and a 4th-rank scroll of cleanse affliction.

The painting under the cloth on the easel is an oil portrait of a serene, beautiful woman in an elegant wedding gown. If the PCs have accumulated at least 1 Research Point on the topic of Tasifinie Arudora, they automatically recognize the portrait’s subject as she appeared on her wedding day. The oracle had just finished restoring this painting (which had suffered some minor water damage), but hadn’t yet returned it to where it belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}). The portrait is 1 Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it triggers a memory of Tasifinie’s joy at wedding her lover, Eragayl. The PC experiencing the memory hears her whisper, “I love you, my brave tiger”—a playful lover’s nickname she had for him that could be useful to the PCs if they later encounter Eragayl’s ghost in the vaults below (area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.MG8bJRohTuzWIbDI]{H6}).

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.7ZSvhlTTOzKZNUJZ]{Augsten Arudora}

Oracle’s Observations: You spend two hours reading through the unknown oracle’s observations about Augsten.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[religion|dc:23|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to correctly interpret religious metaphors the writer used in describing Augsten and his personality, or @Check[perception|dc:25|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to navigate the steam-of-consciousness notes and piece together relevant details.

Servant's Lounge.name: Servant's Lounge
Servant's Lounge.text:
Several comfortable-looking but plain and threadbare chairs, couches, and tables stand throughout this chamber. A pair of shelves in the room’s southern corners are filled with decorations, ewers, and utensils, and even a few books and board games. A large fireplace looms to the north, but it is cold and unlit. Thin throw rugs lie haphazardly on the stone floor.

The castle servants once used this room as a place to relax, socialize, and gather for meetings.

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.7KhhBPqRFYMDZmtm]{Servitor Phantom x10}

Creatures: The most populous inhabitants of the cellars are the servitor phantoms—the remnants of the maids, cooks, laborers, and more who remain behind today as the oppressed and obsessed followers of ogreish Augsten Arudora. These phantoms appear human from the neck down, but their heads are the skulls of animals. The type of animal skull a phantom gained upon their transformation from life to this transitory state depended upon their role before the curse fell, and each type of skull grants a different benefit. Servitor phantoms are smarter than the animals whose skulls they have, but their minds and thoughts are clouded and slow when they’re put to any task other than their particular specialty. They’ve all forgotten their individual names as a result of this, and eagerly accept any new names the PCs might decide to give them. There are 10 servitor phantoms present in this room—four cat-skulled housekeepers, four dog-skulled valets, and two bird-skulled cooks. Even more so than in their previous lives as living servants, these phantoms understand and embrace the notion that they aren’t meant to be interacting with the Arudoras or their guests in any way beyond service. This includes the PCs. If attacked, a servitor phantom either shrieks and runs away, or drops to their knees to beg for mercy. Note that by the time the PCs reach the cellars, the 2nd-level servitor phantoms are too low level for the party to earn XP by defeating them in combat. While servitor phantoms can take part in larger battles, they’re equally intended to be role-playing complications or even hapless victims to save, as detailed in the encounters to follow.

If a PC addresses a servitor phantom, they reply with deferential comments, bows, and apologies, speaking slowly as if slightly drugged. Only when they’re engaged in their purpose or asked about their specialty do their voices grow a bit more animated. Any servant can answer questions about their specialty by using that Lore to Recall Knowledge, and do so without hesitation if a PC asks, but beyond this, servitor phantoms are generally indifferent to the PCs—with the exception of the first time they encounter them: see @UUID[.#side-quest:-the-servants-request]{The Servants’ Request} sidebar for more details. The servants all know quite a bit about Bastardhall and the Arudoras, but much of what they know is commonplace knowledge. A PC can spend a half hour speaking to a servitor phantom to research Bastardhall or the Arudora family, but most of them don’t have anything more to say about other topics (including about specific family members)—exceptions are noted in the text. Servitor phantoms generally reform [[/gmr 1d6#Days until Servitor reforms]] days after they’re killed, and remember their “past lives”—particularly their recent destruction—as unsettling, half-recalled nightmares.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.PAMDhjQNkAm8rB5R]{Bastardhall} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.tbO0Ti0FI6DfZlgf]{The Arudoras}

What the Servants Know: You spend a half hour chatting with a servant, asking about the castle’s current state or about the Arudoras as a whole.

Maximum RP 2 (Bastardhall), 3 (the Arudoras); Research Checks @Check[intimidation|dc:21|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to capitalize upon the servitor phantom’s feelings of insecurity to demand clear and helpful answers, or @Check[diplomacy|dc:23|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to question the phantom more gently.

Special If you fail or critically fail on an Intimidation check, that particular servitor phantom grows nervous and no longer answers your questions; they instead apologize for not being helpful while trying to get away and resume their work.

Side Quest: The Servants' Request

The servitor phantoms may have been created by the curse, but they are not themselves sinister forces. In fact, their existence is more one of perpetual victimhood. The first time the PCs encounter any servitor phantoms, the animal- headed spirits seem caught between the urge to flee in terror and a hesitant desire to approach. As long as the PCs don’t attack, one of the servitor phantoms asks the PCs if they can be of assistance. The phantom goes on to tell the PCs that a winged blasphemy has taken over the servants’ shrine to the southwest, that the majordomo has transformed into a flesh-drinking and face-stealing horror to the south, and that the sommelier downstairs has become a murderous, bloodthirsty killer. If these three monsters could be killed, the servants would be ever so grateful. Asked for more details, the phantom sobs in frustration admitting, “Our minds... they’re not the same... the curse prevents us from remembering who we were, just that now we’re all victims for the monsters among us...”

If the PCs can destroy the vinlach sahkil (area @UUID[.yYVET9FqdVmC0NwM]{C13}), the majordomo (area @UUID[.TE8crk2kfOeKF5yG]{C24}) and the sommelier (area @UUID[.O2hrZos99pNTSbdj]{C47}), the next group of servitor phantoms they encounter thank them gratefully for allowing them to now worship, relax, and rest whenever they wish. They are quick to add that they won’t let this impact their productivity, and offer their services to aid the PCs.

Reward: Grant the PCs 40 XP for helping the servitor phantoms by defeating these three foes.

Laundry Storage.name: Laundry Storage
Laundry Storage.text: While actual laundry work was done in the basement below, these rooms were used by the servants to gather and stage the work. Both of the rooms to the west (areas C16a) contain a pair of laundry chutes that drop 20 feet down into area @UUID[.AYafugrItFeoydrX]{C43} below (a character can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb} these chutes with a @Check[athletics|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check, but Medium characters treat the narrow chutes as difficult terrain). The eastern rooms (areas C16b) are closets for fresh linens, towels, tablecloths, and other non-clothing items ready to be swapped in as needed elsewhere in the castle.

Servants' Mess Hall.name: Servants' Mess Hall
Servants' Mess Hall.text:
A pair of long dining tables with wooden benches sit in the middle of this room. A cabinet containing a wide range of utensils, mugs, and plates stands in the northwest corner of the room, while a long sideboard with cupboards stands to the east. A cold fireplace stands to the southwest, while to the northeast sits a smaller serving table on wheels.

The flight of stairs to the north leads down to the kitchen (area @UUID[.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40}). A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} nearby can find the secret door in the east wall with a @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check—alternatively, the servitor phantoms can alert the PCs to the door once the @UUID[.zV2odqRawrPRFwP1#side-quest:-the-servants-request]{Servant's Request} side quest is complete. Until the reception halls are unlocked, the door opens into impassible green mist, but once that area is open and accessible, it leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mSXvr9F8dglGoNEQ]{D6a}.

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.buABPmUgUvhWxVaS]{Servitor Phantom x6}

Creatures: A group of six servitor phantoms (three housekeepers and three valets) mill about this room, going through the motions of cleaning. See area @UUID[.zV2odqRawrPRFwP1]{C15} for more details on servitor phantoms. If the PCs appear to be heading for the door to area @UUID[.YtT4L1aUQ52wV56D]{C18}, the servitor phantoms grow worried and warn them that “bugs” have gotten into the bakery. Asked for more details, they appear to concentrate, then expand the description to “big bugs... mean bugs... whispering bugs...”

Bakery.name: Bakery
Bakery.text:
Three large brick fireplaces stand against the west wall of this room, with bins for firewood tucked in between them. A half dozen barrels are stacked to the northwest, while shelves containing cooking utensils and ingredients occupy several walls. A brick bin with two circular lids sits near the north wall next to a few shelves filled with sacks of grain. The central portion of the room contains a single long, wide table with a shorter length jutting to the side. The tabletop is heaped with dough, flour, and other bakery supplies that are moldering.

This was a bustling bakery before the castle’s fall. The grains here were grown down on the farm (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Oz08GUWUIID0kaMb]{A16}) and were hauled here before being sent to the mill below (area @UUID[.Lb4pe34hTD16VRyR]{C41}) for grinding into flour. The castle retained several bakers among the serving staff who were responsible for baking the bread, pastries, desserts, and other foodstuffs that served the basis of so many of the castle’s meals.

The round lids on the brick bin can be opened to reveal a pair of shafts, each only a foot square, that drop down into lower bins in the mill below (area @UUID[.Lb4pe34hTD16VRyR]{C41}) for easy delivery of bags of grain to be ground. A PC who opens a lid can hear the slow, inexorable sound of the grindstone rumbling up from below. The nearby door to the east opens into the reception halls (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.Zn0JGlSQklSYFnfc]{D2}), but until this area is unlocked, opening the door reveals only an impassable wall of green mist.

Encounter

Moderate 7

@UUID[Actor.hj7in3ZZlTu8n4vi]{Wihsaaks x2} @UUID[Actor.sldauWtSyK4JEiRl]{Centipede Swarms x2}

Creatures: Several servants huddled in here when the curse struck, only to be slaughtered by an eruption of centipedes brought in by the curse. Additionally, a pair of wihsaak sahkils, embodying the fear of crawling vermin, remain here to this day. The two insectile sahkils are endlessly patient, lurking in the rafters above and waiting for phantoms to lose track of what’s in the room so they can be terrified all over again. The servitor phantoms’ resistance to physical damage means they’re rarely slain in these attacks before they flee, but death isn’t what the wihsaaks are after.

The arrival of the PCs gives the sahkils a rare treat, but they wait for the swarms of centipedes that infest the mounds of decaying dough on the tables to burst out first before they swoop down to attack from above, rolling Stealth for initiative. The wihsaaks take advantage of their swarmwalker ability to lurk unharmed amid the centipede swarms, and open combat with Droning Distraction. After which, they use defensive spells and suggestion to try and influence PCs who aren’t confused, doing their best to aid allies while avoiding melee and confused PCs. Once one of the wihsaaks drops below 50 HP, both move forward to fight in melee, focusing their attacks on the most damaged PCs. They and the centipedes fight to the death.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.7N5l2D8sbedvWSLu]{Spoiled Dough}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the spoiled dough and other ingredients on the tables for 10 minutes discovers a soulheart caked in some of the stuff. The first PC to touch this soulheart receives a brief memory of Esmira visiting the bakery, chatting with the cooks and purchasing several cinnamon buns to share with the children in her class that day.

Once the monsters in the bakery are slain and the PCs have completed the side quest to defeat the antagonists who vex the servitor phantoms, a group of servitor phantom cooks occupy the bakery. Their presence draws upon ambient ectoplasm to purify the ingredients, and thereafter they can produce two @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.QXW6txYvNIlQK0qE]{lesser poet’s fritters} per day for the PCs. These fritters spoil if not eaten within 24 hours of their creation. Once the PCs unlock the Bastardhall temple at the start of @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk]{Chapter 7}, the servants grow more adept at their task, and they instead craft two @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.iWiKC10ojE0fiykT]{moderate poet’s fritters} per day.

Pantry.name: Pantry
Pantry.text:
Shelves filled with canned goods, bags and pouches, and bins of moldy-looking ingredients line the walls of this dusty pantry.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.toHduBZIs5DclC5D]{Pantry}

Most of the supplies here are spoiled or rotten, but a PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the pantry discovers a jar of pickled eggs tucked behind a few bags of foul-smelling turnips. These pickled eggs are more than old enough to serve as the “hundred-year eggs” the PCs might be called upon to gather for the cooks in area @UUID[.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40}.

Restrooms.name: Restrooms
Restrooms.text: Both of these rooms contain a dry washbasin and two pit toilet stalls. The pits under these toilets all lead to area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.cOpok2j0xfaDhU1O]{E5b} once the dungeons are unlocked.

Servants' Quarters.name: Servants' Quarters
Servants' Quarters.text:
Each of these rooms is identical in appearance.

A pair of double bunk beds stand against the far side of this room, with a dresser drawer standing between the two.

These eight rooms served as quarters for all 32 of Castle Arudora’s servants. The dresser in each room contains an array of clothing and miscellaneous, but relatively worthless, personal items.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.EVIfc30fVIMcskv8]{Dresser}

At first glance, area C21a looks no different from the other rooms, but a PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} this room (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the dresser and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:23|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check) discovers an object of apparent value—a dawnsilver corkscrew etched with Shelyn’s religious symbol worth 350 gp. This corkscrew could come in handy when confronting Brensen Firecask in area @UUID[.O2hrZos99pNTSbdj]{C47}.

Servants' Atrium.name: Servants' Atrium
Servants' Atrium.text:
A pair of threadbare couches sit to the northeast of this atrium with a withered, dead houseplant leaning in a nook between them. Three equally dead plants sit in the opposite corner, two of which flank a grandfather clock that seems to have stopped working long ago.

Before the curse, this room served as the atrium for the servant’s wing from the reception halls. The door to the southeast opens into an impassible wall of green mist until the reception halls are unlocked, after which the door leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.JsQ28KTjNnWncruE]{D10}.

The grandfather clock is still functional, but requires a little bit of maintenance before it can resume its chronological duties. A PC who spends 30 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:25] check can restore the clock to functionality, but on each critical failure the clock is damaged further, increasing the DC of all future Crafting checks to restore it by 2. Once restored, the PCs can set the clock to the proper time as a 1 minute activity (assuming they can determine the approximate time by succeeding at a @Check[survival] check against a DC equal to the current lucid nightmare Will save DC).

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.buABPmUgUvhWxVaS]{Servitor Phantoms x2}

Creatures: Two housekeeping servitor phantoms bustle about this room, nervously and quietly cleaning up the nonexistent dirt that they believe sullies the room, or tending to the very dead houseplants. See area @UUID[.zV2odqRawrPRFwP1]{C15} for more details on servitor phantoms. If the PCs appear to be heading for the door to area @UUID[.UumLlw3rcDAtjgKa]{C23}, the servitor phantoms grow anxious and warn them, “The majordomo isn’t seeing anyone now, and should not be disturbed!” Despite this, they won’t do much more than cluck their spectral tongues in disapproval if the PCs push onward.

Majordomo's Office.name: Majordomo's Office
Majordomo's Office.text:
A desk and chair sit near a door to the south, while a second chair sits in the opposite corner of the room. Cobweb-encrusted paintings hang on the walls.

This area was where one of the servants served as the majordomo’s assistant, and scheduled meetings with him as needed. There’s nothing of interest here now, but the PCs can hear the muffled sounds of voices talking loudly through the doorway to area @UUID[.TE8crk2kfOeKF5yG]{C24}. A PC who listens at this door and makes a successful @Check[perception|dc:20] check can make out what the voices are saying—see area @UUID[.TE8crk2kfOeKF5yG]{C24} for details.

Majordomo's Room.name: Majordomo's Room
Majordomo's Room.text:
A large, canopied bed sits in the northeast corner of this room, and the floor is mostly covered by a thick green carpet. A low nightstand next to the bed supports an ewer and a few mugs. A desk and chair sit to the west, while a set of shelves covered with various trinkets and sculptures sits to the east. To the south, a large diagram showing a pair of floor plans hangs on the wall.

This room was the personal quarters for Enoch Grashikin, the castle’s majordomo. Compared to the guest rooms or private Arudora estates, this bedroom looks almost humble, but put next to the lesser servants’ quarters it’s an excess of luxury. Area C24a contains a dry bath and a pit toilet (the latter of which connects to the midden at area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.obtffCMeRJgG4QyY]{E5c}), while area C24b is a walk-in closet with a wide range of elegant clothing for the many occasions Enoch had to interact with guests or family members on behalf of the staff.

Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.Z5aAKfImD4oGdZrx]{Enoch Grashikin}

Creatures: Enoch dwells here still, but no longer interacts with the Arudora family—those days have long passed since the curse twisted and transformed him into an undead monstrosity known as a totenmaske. In life, he was something of a taskmaster—some would even have called him a bully. In undeath, these traits have only intensified. He spends his time in the form he wore in life, a middle-aged Garundi man with an impressive set of sideburns, a broad build, and a patient demeanor, yet when he gets frustrated, this facade begins to slip. A few things increasingly give away the truth that lurks below his living form: glimpses of sharp teeth in a mouth that, for an instant, might seem to be far too wide; the conviction that his eyes for a moment might just be painted on; and noticing out of the corner of one’s vision that the fingers of his idle hand are far too long.

When the PCs first arrive, Enoch is engaged in an intense argument with himself as he struggles to decide on the best way to discipline the servants, who he feels are slacking in their duties. He was originally set to dock their pay, but then became convinced that the staff’s been distracted by heavy meals and needs to be put on a strict diet, only to increasingly think that the right call is to send staff on “short trips downstairs” to the dungeons to be punished in the torture chamber.

Upon spotting the PCs, Enoch mistakes them for minor Arudora family members. In a deep, blustering voice, he quickly outlines the problem, then asks the PCs for their advice—should the servants have their pay docked, be put on a strict diet, or be punished downstairs? Give the players a moment to talk things over, but when they have their answer, one PC must deliver their decision with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:25] check. On a success, Enoch lauds the PCs on their fine choice. On a failure, or if the PCs suggest no punishment at all or otherwise dodge the answer (including if they simply attempt to leave or attack), Enoch roars in frustration as he realizes the PCs are intruders.

In all cases, the end result is that Enoch attacks. If he realizes the PCs are intruders, the fight proceeds normally. He shifts to his true form and focuses his attacks on the PC who failed their Diplomacy check, or otherwise chooses a target randomly to focus on—switching to a new target only when the initial one is downed. He fights until destroyed, but will only pursue PCs out of this room until a round ends with no PCs in sight, at which point he returns here to resume debating the best course of action.

If a PC succeeded at the Diplomacy check, though, they party gains an advantage for the ensuing fight; Enoch grows distracted and baffled by the PCs’ words, and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for the duration of the fight as he spends precious time each round wrestling with his own thoughts. If the PCs escape him, this restriction on Enoch is lifted, and if they encounter him later, he simply attacks on sight.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.XqSI31MLcb8XEzDK]{Nightstand} @UUID[Actor.INUF4Cr0985NvZYg]{Hidden Chest} @UUID[Actor.mRldm2ablx0jBmpa]{Majordomo Closet}

The ewer and mugs on the nightstand are fine pottery works of art; the ewer is worth 25 gp and each of the three mugs is worth 5 gp.

The floor plan on the south wall is a depiction of the servant’s and groundskeeper’s quarters (areas @UUID[.1tfiJnjtQbAUTr1s]{C1}–C24), as well as the cellar dungeons (areas @UUID[.2tXKE2JE45z1vCAd]{C38}–@UUID[.O2hrZos99pNTSbdj]{C47}). These areas are depicted and labeled, along with complex work and rest schedules. While the schedules are out of date, the layout of these rooms includes all secret doors and a brief description of each area, potentially making it much easier for the PCs to explore these rooms.

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the main room for 10 minutes finds a chest tucked deep under the bed. It’s unlocked, and within lies the wages that were intended to pay the staff in the months following the curse: a total of 200 gp.

A PC who Searches the closet (area C24b) for 10 minutes determines that of the outfits stored therein, 14 are fine outfits (worth 2 gp each), and one is a cloak of illusions.

North Security Entrance.name: North Security Entrance
North Security Entrance.text: This empty stone room served as a guard post before the curse fell, but is currently empty. The northern door opens into an impenetrable wall of green mist if the reception halls aren’t yet unlocked; if they are, it leads into area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.goyxlKit1QLHYYuh]{D1e}.

Secret Tunnel.name: Secret Tunnel
Secret Tunnel.text:
This long, hidden tunnel was used by the guards to move quickly between several areas in the cellars and certain rooms in the reception halls. All of the secret doors in this hall are plainly visible within the tunnel; see the rooms they connect to for the Perception DCs required to locate them from the other side.

Four of the secret doors in this tunnel lead to different areas in the reception halls. Until that area is unlocked, opening any of these doors reveals an impassable wall of green mist. Once the reception halls are unlocked, though, the door at area C26a leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.goyxlKit1QLHYYuh]{D1d}, the one at area C26b to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.eud7t2JugdlGBTk7]{D3}, the one at area C26c to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.Rgs6JrkwqfHvbTQn]{D4b}, and the western one at area C26d to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mSXvr9F8dglGoNEQ]{D6b}.

Guards' Lounge.name: Guards' Lounge
Guards' Lounge.text:
A couple of round tables, several wooden chairs, and a long leather couch provide various areas to relax in this room. A brick fireplace sits in the southern wall. Old bloodstains mar the edge of the door to the east and leave a trail of rusty red splatters all the way to the southern door.

The castle guards used this area as a place to relax, play cards, gossip, or even catch a quick nap when they were on break or off duty. The bloodstains were left by the master of the guard, @UUID[Actor.WWFWK13MvVwpZ7Zj]{Korven Willachur}, after he lost both hands when the door slammed on them (see area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.srvDTVrA5ZcIuWjR]{B8}). A PC who Searches this room for 10 minutes or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} near the location of the secret door can discover the entrance to area @UUID[.dRUkDhLTYQRs48GB]{C26} with a successful @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The door to the east leads out to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1h} of the castle grounds.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.GHVGz8hs6LsvkkvG]{Lounge Couch}

A PC who succeeds at @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check while Seeking near the couch (or critically succeeds while Searching the room), finds a frozen lava of Blackpeak that slipped out of a guard’s pocket and got lodged between the couch frame and cushion.

Mustering Hall.name: Mustering Hall
Mustering Hall.text:
Two long wooden tables with built-in benches sit in the middle of this large room. To the north is a brick fireplace, while in the northeast, a wooden platform with steps rises a few feet off the ground. A skeletal body clad in plate armor lies slumped on the platform. A trail of old bloodstains lead from the northern door to the body.

A PC who Searches this room for 10 minutes or Seeks near the location of the secret door can discover the entrance to area @UUID[.dRUkDhLTYQRs48GB]{C26} with a successful @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check.

The doors to areas @UUID[.XXXge4mgm6Ye0xrQ]{C29} and @UUID[.ZgxPpTjTDYasArJx]{C32} are both barricaded shut from the other side. A @Check[athletics|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check is enough to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} either door.

Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.WWFWK13MvVwpZ7Zj]{Korven Willachur}

Creatures: On the night of the curse, Korven Willachur, master of the guard, was holding open outer door for those fleeing into the castle. When the curse struck, the door slammed shut and severed both his hands at the wrist. He then managed to stagger his way into this room, where he heroically tried to rally what few guards made it here into organizing a defense of the castle. When sahkils attacked those guards, however, Korven could do little but watch before he bled to death.

His spirit remains bound here as a bitter ghost. He is convinced that if his hands were returned to him, he’d be able to use his sword and shield to fight back. Korven calls out to the PCs as soon as they enter (unless they do so stealthily), demanding that the bravest of “you soldiers” step forward to sacrifice their hands to him so that he might save the castle.

A foolish PC who does so, cutting off their hands for the voice, will be disappointed, as Korven realizes these hands are no replacement for his own. In this case, or if no attempt to offer hands is made, Korven’s ghost manifests atop his remains and attacks. Swift-thinking PCs who offer the skeletal hands (and ring) from area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.srvDTVrA5ZcIuWjR]{B8} might, at your discretion, be able to put the ghost to rest without a fight.

Once combat begins, Korven manifests as a wild-eyed, mustached human man clad in ghostly plate armor. An equally ghostly shield and longsword strapped to his back and side, respectively, remain where they are as he shrieks in rage and reaches for the nearest PC with severed wrists that bleed what appears to be real blood, increasingly splattering the floor, walls, and PCs as he fights. Korven’s ghost fights until destroyed, but cannot leave area C28 to pursue those who flee.

Closer inspection of Korven’s remains on the floor reveals that both hands are missing. If the PCs place the skeletal remains of his hands (including his signet ring) from area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.srvDTVrA5ZcIuWjR]{B8} among the remains, Korven’s ghost is put to rest and will not rejuvenate. His bones fade away, leaving behind his armor and weapon, and his ring transforms into a magical item—see Treasure below for details.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.T3UipysM4urC3BEZ]{Guard's Remains}

Korven’s remains still wear his plate armor. While his shield is a nonmagical steel shield, his longsword is a +1 striking longsword. If the PCs returned his remains and ring, permanently laying the ghost to rest, the bones vanish and the signet ring becomes a commander’s signet. In one of his pockets, he carried an iron key (this opens the chests in areas @UUID[.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48} and @UUID[.WUfxobQnHYYwiStb]{C49}).

Guards' Mess Hall.name: Guards' Mess Hall
Guards' Mess Hall.text:
One long table and two much shorter ones, each with built-in bench seating, decorate this mess hall—and mess is the proper word, for bits of meat, spilled bowls of stew, moldy bits of bread, cracked bones, lumps of sweaty-looking cheese, and a wide range of utensils (most of which have been stabbed into the top of the tables, including the spoons) give the place a foul, lived- in look. A blisteringly hot fire burns in a large fireplace to the west.

If the PCs didn’t enter the area from the northwestern door, they’ll note as well that this door has been nailed shut with several planks of wood. Area C29a is a washroom with two lavatories—all of which are even more filthy than the main mess hall. The pit toilets drop into the midden at area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.EsLiuckmn2VDsB8z]{E5d} in the dungeons below.

The food and fire in this room are manifestations of the curse—comforts afforded to what became of the castle guards.

Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.2DdJrqM3R6iCcGtl]{Slaughtermay} @UUID[Actor.httXfBPGseF9csXa]{Bugbear Tormentors x4} @UUID[Actor.Mw0cHFd5a4RGEqPn]{Servitor Phantom}

Creatures: Those rank-and-file castle guards who were unfortunate enough to survive the initial assault on the castle during the night of the curse were transformed by its power, their limbs growing lanky, ears spreading and widening, and flesh sprouting thick, matted fur. These guards have become bugbear tormentors, and the woman who once served as their lieutenant and the second in command under Captain Korven has long since forgotten her name. Now the most violent bugbear in Bastardhall, she goes by the name of Slaughtermay.

The bugbears enjoy their lives in Bastardhall, even if such lives are somewhat repetitive. The curse keeps them fed and sometimes guides phantoms into their midst to torment—the fact that it’s difficult for them to actually damage incorporeal phantoms doesn’t lessen the joy they gain from such tortures or the pain inflicted on the phantoms in question. Such a pastime is precisely what the bugbears are engaged in now, as Slaughtermay looks on from her seat atop the mess in the middle of the longest table.

The bugbears gasp in shock as soon as the PCs enter the area—particularly if they smash through the door from area @UUID[.wO8FX9GQqMgltKx6]{C28}. They live in fear of the ghost of their old captain, and while their barricade is largely ceremonial (and pointless, considering Korven can’t leave area C28), the idea that intruders might have come from that area unsettles them. If the PCs enter from that door, all of the bugbears take a –4 penalty to their initiative checks.

Effect

@UUID[Item.BYaAGCpU7GWMiGEI]{Initiative Penalty}

If the bugbears are unsettled by the PCs' entrance as described above, use this effect to automate their initiative penalty.

The servitor phantom they’re tormenting is a snake-skulled brewer, and the only such servant outside of those kept as workers for Brensen in the brewery below (area @UUID[.jVrtk8KjGIvJavQ9]{C46}). He’s cowering in the middle of the room while the bugbear tormentors hack and stab at him with daggers and sickles. The servitor is down to only 10 HP from the abuse. Once combat begins, Slaughtermay shrieks and races in to fight in melee; three bugbear tormentors join her, while the fourth stubbornly hangs back to keep stabbing the servitor, hoping to be the one to deal the “killing” blow before joining the others. Slaughtermay fights to the death, but as soon as she’s killed, the remaining bugbear tormentors panic and make a fighting retreat to area @UUID[.lQdheEdZiY5D3YIS]{C34}, then down the stairs in hopes of joining the guards at Augsten’s side in area @UUID[.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48}.

If the bugbears in area @UUID[.lQdheEdZiY5D3YIS]{C34} still live, they’ll come join the fight here on the third round of combat, when it’s apparent to them that what’s going on in the mess hall isn’t a regular disagreement between bugbears (or sooner, if the PCs use a particularly noisy and non-bugbear effect in combat).

If the PCs manage to defeat the bugbears before they can destroy the servitor phantom, the grateful phantom thanks them, but then tells them his companions are being brutally worked by that “iron- soled monster Brensen” in the wine cellar below (area @UUID[.O2hrZos99pNTSbdj]{C47}). The phantom can describe the shortest route to the wine cellar (via the stairs from area @UUID[.lQdheEdZiY5D3YIS]{C34}, straight through the double doors, and then through the brewery at area @UUID[.jVrtk8KjGIvJavQ9]{C46}) and tells the PCs that if they remind Brensen of his lost faith in Shelyn, the sudden flood of memories from before he became a monster might distract him. Pressed for further answers, the phantom grows frustrated as his clouded mind has trouble recalling details—at this point all he wants is to return to his bunk to “sleep.”

Reward

If the PCs rescue the phantom and learn about Brensen, grant the party 20 XP.

South Security Entrance.name: South Security Entrance
South Security Entrance.text: The southern door of this hallway leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.78A34DGpyfbsAqFq]{D7e} in the reception halls, but until that area is unlocked, only impassable green mist awaits beyond the door.

Barracks.name: Barracks
Barracks.text:
Treasure

@UUID[Actor.I9Bp7ukOdnQdyF9c]{Under the Pillow}

Each of these rooms features an identical trio of double bunks and footlockers. Once where the off-duty castle guards slept, most of these rooms are now empty—with one exception. The southeastern room served as the higher ranking guards’ sleeping quarters, and a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} this room for 10 minutes (or someone who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the southern bed and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check) discovers a “lucky charm” left under the pillow by the bunk’s previous lieutenant before she was transformed into Slaughtermay: a jade frog the size of a thimble. The carving isn’t magic, but it is finely made, and is worth 100 gp.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
A brick stove to the northwest hosts a small fire, with a bubbling cauldron dangling above the flames from a set of chains. There are counters in the western corners of the room, and a circular table in the center that bears the scraps of a meal including bits of roast pork, apples, spiced squash, and a few bread crusts.

If the PCs didn’t enter the area from the northern door, they’ll note as well that this door has been nailed shut with several planks of wood.

Augsten’s influence over this part of the cellars is stronger, and his appetite demands an ever-changing menu of delights “as befits one of his stature.” The Bastardhall curse accommodates this by manifesting a wide range of food and drink in this kitchen three times a day—once at 9:00 a.m., once at noon, and once at 6:00 p.m. The food that manifests earlier in the day is generally left to the bugbears to gather and distribute, but the later one is all Augsten’s, and he sends bugbears up to gather his daily repast without fail. Unfortunately, while the food that the curse manifests here looks and smells delicious, to the PCs it is toxic. A PC who eats any of the food from here finds it to taste awful, like decaying meat or mold, and must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:20|traits:curse,magical] save to resist being afflicted with the @UUID[.ANFq6x3eEsQ7H4vg]{curse of the ravenous}. A PC already suffering from this curse (perhaps as a result of shenanigans undertaken in area @UUID[.ANFq6x3eEsQ7H4vg]{C3}) who fails this saving throw immediately becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} and takes @Damage[8d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:23|basic] save) from the momentary conviction that they’ll be starving to death in moments.

If the PCs enter this room within 15 minutes of 6:00 p.m., they’ll encounter the four bugbear tormentors from area @UUID[.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48} here, gathering up Augsten’s meal. Encountered here, the bugbears abandon the meal and race back to area @UUID[.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48}, hoping to lure the PCs into a deadly fight with their ogre leader.

Storage.name: Storage
Storage.text:
Shelves filled with preserved foodstuffs and kitchen supplies line the walls of this room. A barrel sits to the north and south.

While the water in the barrels is refilled daily by the servants from the well downstairs, the foodstuffs here are all well past their prime.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.NIrEdGjAd6XZaJx7]{Dusty Shelves}

A PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the dusty contents of this room’s shelves finds a jar of pickled Laroba lampreys tucked away in the southwestern corner behind a bag of mummified potatoes. This is one of the five ingredients the PCs must gather for the cooks in area @UUID[.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40}. In addition, a search of the storeroom reveals a jar containing six bulbs of preserved garlic—the only garlic to be found in Bastardhall (and potentially of great use against the vampires of the private halls in @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8]{Chapter 6}).

Emergency Infirmary.name: Emergency Infirmary
Emergency Infirmary.text:
Scattered almost haphazardly throughout this room sit nine cots, each of which is heaped with mounds of filthy rags and furs. Ancient bloodstains mar the floors, and even the walls in places. A chair behind a wooden desk sits in a wide alcove to the west, while here and there, empty weapon racks hang from the stone walls.

The flight of stairs beyond the northwest door leads down to area @UUID[.MYRPJK8EXNQC5NLs]{C44e}.

A PC who is at least expert in Medicine recognizes the disarray of this room as a sort of emergency infirmary, likely set up in a rush to deal with an unexpected number of patients. When the curse struck and the first of the guards began to fall, they were brought here to this training hall to be triaged and attended to while the priests were otherwise involved with their own disaster in the castle temple to the west. The bodies of those who died here after their mortal encounters with curse-spawned monsters were largely eaten—a cruel fate, yet at least the soldiers who died here moved on to the afterlife.

Encounter

Trivial 7

@UUID[Actor.httXfBPGseF9csXa]{Bugbear Tormentors x4}

Creatures: To the bugbears, the barracks they used in their pre-curse life bring unpleasant, melancholic dreams, and they’ve taken to using this room as a communal sleeping area. The first time the PCs enter here, four bugbear tormentors fresh off of guard duty at Augsten’s side sleep on various cots, yet they slumber quite lightly and are quick to spring to combat if the PCs aren’t stealthy (these bugbears do not suffer penalties to their Perception checks while sleeping).

If a fight breaks out and one of the bugbears falls here, the rest retreat downstairs to area @UUID[.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48} to warn Augsten and fight at his side if the PCs pursue.

Slaughtermay's Room.name: Slaughtermay's Room
Slaughtermay's Room.text:
A bed heaped with filthy rags sits in the corner of this room, while a broken chair leans against the northern wall. Seven human skulls are lined up in a row on a shelf to the east. The first and the seventh skulls face the wall, rather than into the room like the other five.

Slaughtermay claimed the former castellan’s room as her personal quarters. She’s encountered here between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m., and unlike the bugbears in area @UUID[.lQdheEdZiY5D3YIS]{C34}, she is a standard sleeper.

Encounter

Trivial 7

@UUID[Actor.bXEpVQIdCVkMTu0b]{Poisoned Skulls x2}

Hazard: The seven skulls on the shelf are a simple trap placed here by Slaughtermay to punish anyone who might creep into her room. Trusting that few would be able to resist fiddling with skulls set up in such a strange array, she coated the first and seventh in a rare, mind-muddling toxin meant to punish trespassers and also brand them so that she could know who’d been messing with her stuff.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.chSbFuO7hkqQFjpV]{Hidden Nook}

Slaughtermay carries most of her valuables, with one exception—an emerald worth 200 gp that she keeps hidden in a hollow space she carved into one of the bedposts against the wall. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the room for 10 minutes or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the bed discovers this hidden nook with a @Check[perception|dc:23|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check and can claim the gemstone as their own.

Storage Room.name: Storage Room
Storage Room.text:
This storage room is filled completely with boxes, crates, weapon racks, armor mannequins, chairs, tables, and more, to the extent that actually entering the room or making out its exact dimensions isn’t possible without a lot of unpacking.

When the curse hit and the guards turned the training hall into an infirmary, they cleared space by quickly packing the room’s other contents into this chamber. Unpacking the room to properly @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} it and get a good look at its dimensions is a task that’ll take two hours of work, but doing so is worth it. Once the room’s cleaned out, the PCs discover a crate that was stacked near the ceiling in the back that has a curious elongated puncture mark in the top.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.TQBi9bJucYum7Rtu]{Punctured Crate}

While almost none of the objects stored in here are noteworthy, the contents of the punctured crate are. One of the brass gears from the clock tower phased through several walls as it was hurled from the temple, phasing back just in time to become lodged in a crate filled with spare parts for the construction of armor mannequins. See the @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.t1s9G6BjLx2VvxXt#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

Holding Cells.name: Holding Cells
Holding Cells.text:
A stout wooden desk and chair sit in the south. Atop the desk is a lantern on a stand, a large ledger, and a slender metal wand with a tiny bell hanging from its tip. To the east and west, the room is divided by sets of iron bars, creating four cells, each of which contains a filthy straw mat, a bucket, and a wooden plate. Each cell contains a single humanoid skeleton clad in rags.

The secret door leading to the northern stairs can be discovered if the PCs @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} this room for 10 minutes and then succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:23|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The stairs beyond the secret door lead down to area @UUID[.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48}.

While the Arudoras had no legal standing to keep anyone imprisoned for extended periods of time, when criminals were caught in the act on the isle, they would be brought here to be interrogated and held—typically for less than a week, after which they would be released if the crime was minor, or sent off to stand trial in the town of Cesca (or for particularly heinous crimes, all the way to Caliphas). Prisoners the Arudoras wanted to “keep to themselves” and deal with personally were instead brought quietly down to the dungeon via the secret door, after which most were never seen again.

Each iron cell door is locked (three @Check[thievery|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick a Lock} or one @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force a door Open}; these DCs increase by 10 if attempted from inside a cell).

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Trigger Join Us Forever" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to move the skeletons in the cages forward!

Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.ughj4w37cFYLudzJ]{Join Us Forever}

Hazard: A few days before the curse descended on the castle, members of the castle guard finally broke open a long-standing case—a secretive smuggling ring that had been operating out of the castle dungeon for years. They apprehended four compromised members of their own guard who had been helping to perpetuate this smuggling ring of dangerous poisons, elixirs, and drug. The guards were about to break the case wide open with proof of criminal involvement from the Bruiser Boys (see area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Mr8Gsi42znsNq3XB]{A23} for their fate) and an alchemist in the Arudoras’ employment, Junth Rundel (area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.8h6QErLBhi0Ro2tn]{E7}).

Then the curse struck, and over the following days, the guards who remained imprisoned here met a fate far worse than harrowing interrogations and losing their jobs.

The bugbears who were once their fellow guards gave them enough water and food to stay alive, but only to see how long it would take them to snap under an endless imprisonment. The prisoners all died of old age in here before Bastardhall made its first return to Golarion, and their souls went on to haunt this prison. Ironically, the chamber the bugbears used for cruel entertainment is now one they themselves fear to enter.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.ySZOQhZ2xGx2lBny]{Holding Cells Desk}

The ledger contains notes on the smuggling ring as well as the guards’ plans to use their prisoners to find proof that Junth Rundel was the mastermind of the operation. While the notes would have been enough on their own to get Junth fired, the guards were waiting to get enough intelligence to ensure he’d be punished to the maximum the law allowed.

The metal wand on the desk looks like a candle snuffer but is, in fact, a tool the guards built with the aid of a priest from the shrine at area @UUID[.DqhDfn8rAdJqBC6g]{C17}: a wand of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.aewxsale5xWEPKLk]{Ring of Truth}.

Keys to the cell doors can be found in the desk.

Seasonal Storage.name: Seasonal Storage
Seasonal Storage.text:
A large, square basement room extends the lower floor of this circular tower. Crates, barrels, and other containers have been pushed into the corners, while in the middle of the room, an iron ring is staked into the floor with a few feet of broken chain still attached to it. A flight of stairs to the south winds upward, while a double door stands closed to the east.

The door to the east is locked and can be unlocked with the key found in area @UUID[.uvh9KJliEvdWQknO]{C4}.

Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.6dBcCjhYDsxvP8Lj]{Ghoulrilla}

This chamber was originally used to store seasonal tools and supplies for groundskeeping, but a few days before the curse fell, the castle’s groundskeeper Milsindi blew a fair amount of her savings on an unusual purchase.
