A traveling menagerie had come to Castle Arudora, bringing exotic animals to marvel at for a week-long soiree; among their exhibitions was a gorilla. Milsindi was taken by the creature’s plight at being treated as caged entertainment, and on the day of the curse, she arranged for the animal’s purchase.

Using a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.BBvV7qoXGdw09q1C]{Speak with Animals} spell and a fair amount of empathic discussion, she convinced the gorilla to come with her and stay for a bit in the basement here while Milsindi dealt with the logistics of having the creature sent back home to the jungles of Vidrian. Of course, the curse fell before anything more could be arranged, and it was shortly after Milsindi became a ghoul that she used her ability to speak with animals to convince the would-be rescue to share her forbidden cravings. Now, the creature is a ghoul as well and has taken to its cursed environments, growing more powerful than it ever would have become in life. Milsindi took to calling the undead ape her pet “ghoulrilla,” and while the gorilla is now smart enough to understand a few languages, he has few interests other than finding food, having grown quite violent as the years wore on. Now, the ghouls above only come down here when they have to, or if they’re chased by the PCs, as more than once a ghoul above has been savaged by this larger, less patient ghoul below.

The ghoulrilla roars as soon as he spots the PCs, screaming out in Common, “YOU! FOOD! COME HERE! GET EATEN!” before attacking. He starts combat with a Grisly Display, then lumbers forth to attack the PCs. Once reduced to fewer than 80 Hit Points, the ghoulrilla grows even more uncaring in his violence, and thereafter treats allied ghouls as equal enemies, splitting his attacks between any of them in the area and the PCs. The ghoulrilla fights until destroyed, and pursues PCs relentlessly until they flee into an area that the Large ghoul can’t comfortably fit (through any non-double door or into a five-foot-wide area), after which he returns here.

Water Room.name: Water Room
Water Room.text:
Three water barrels stand against the north wall of this room. To the west, a three-foot-wide circular hole in the wall opens into a vertical shaft. A spool of rope attached to a crank sits in the space between, with the far end of the rope dangling out of sight into the shaft beyond.

The rope and contraption once allowed the servants to draw water from the castle well. A wooden bucket dangles just out of sight over the edge, but as long as the castle dungeons remain locked, the well itself is filled a little bit deeper still by impassable green mist. Once the dungeons are unlocked, the mist clears, revealing a 110-foot drop into the waters of area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.0CdaOwJhcWtoKSkm]{E3} below. The rope itself is 120 feet long, more than enough to lower the bucket and draw water—or to lower the bucket and provide aid in climbing, but a @Check[crafting|dc:20] or @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check made while Seeking the rope confirms that it’s a bit frayed and could be unsafe. Without the rope, it’s a @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb} the walls of the well. With the rope, this becomes a @Check[athletics|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check, but at the end of any round a Medium or larger creature uses the rope to aid in climbing, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:18]. On a failure, the rope snaps, and the climbing creature falls unless they can make a @Check[reflex|dc:25|options:action:grab-an-edge|traits:manipulate] save to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.3yoajuKjwHZ9ApUY]{Grab an Edge} and cling to the rough walls.

In the other direction, it’s merely 20 feet up into area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.RFIcObAU8wgYbWiU]{B14} of the castle grounds.

Main Kitchen.name: Main Kitchen
Main Kitchen.text:
Several long food-preparation tables stand in this room, along with a few wall-mounted shelves on which various kitchen implements and containers are stored. Two large brick fireplaces stand unused in the west wall.

The stairs beyond the door in the northwest corner of this room lead down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.LPkJFQogdqN9LE0s]{E4b} of the castle dungeon, but until the dungeon is unlocked, impassable green mist prevents a descent of more than a few dozen feet. The secret door to the southeast leads to area @UUID[.OV17X9YalFG6v52z]{C42} , and can be discovered with a @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check if the PCs @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the kitchen for 10 minutes, or if they Seek that particular part of the room.

Encounter

Trivial 7

@UUID[Actor.DlkyUtA9bcC8TpgG]{Elite Mummy Guardian} @UUID[Actor.7KhhBPqRFYMDZmtm]{Servitor Phantoms x3}

Creatures: The first time the PCs visit this area, they find three cook servitor phantoms bustling around the table closest to the fireplaces. They are arguing over the best method to prepare an unusual and dangerous meal for a group of eccentric guests who have gathered in the banquet hall (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mSXvr9F8dglGoNEQ]{D6}) above.

The primary ingredient for this meal is a mummy. The dish, called mummiranth, is favored by particularly decadent Ustalavic nobles but has fallen out of style in the past several hundred years.

Mummiranth consisted of select portions of a mummy’s bones and flesh ground into a powder and mixed into a flatbread dough; when baked, it was stuffed with cheese, olives, and spiced meats. This dish was on the schedule for an upcoming meal for several visiting nobles from Carrion Hill when the curse struck. The curse did two things: it cut short this meal (transforming those nobles into something altogether different), and it infused what was originally a normal mummy with unlife. Said mummy is now just biding its time before it rises up, just as it has countless times before, to slaughter the phantoms before returning to wait for these phantoms to reform, return, and start the cycle of pain all over.

The servitor phantoms are currently arguing over whether it’s better to hand-grind the mummy, to place it into the grindstone in area @UUID[.Lb4pe34hTD16VRyR]{C41}, or to not use a real mummy at all and simply bake a normal meat-and cheese-stuffed pastry for the guests, but once they notice the PCs, they grow distracted and step in between the party and the table on which the mummy lies, presenting their case and asking the PCs which of the three options they feel is best. As the PCs think over their answer, though, the mummy strikes, rising up from the table to attack one of the phantoms with their fist. The phantoms quickly panic and flee through the room at this, and the mummy is just as quick to turn its hungry need for mayhem to the PCs—it’s more satisfying to crush flesh and bone and choke the life out of the living than to flail away at nearly-helpless phantoms, after all. The mummy fights until destroyed, pursuing the PCs relentlessly through the cellars.

Once the mummy on the table has been destroyed, any surviving cook servitor phantoms return and thank the PCs for saving them. If this is the first group of servitors the PCs have met, see The @UUID[.zV2odqRawrPRFwP1#side-quest:-the-servants-request]{Servants’ Request} for the gist of their initial interaction. In addition, the servants offer to cook special meals for the PCs (see Treasure below) and note that, “Should you need us to cook up anything really special, such as for anyone upstairs, you just let us know and we’ll be happy to help!” The PCs don’t know it yet, but they’ll have a chance to cook for the nobles upstairs in area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mSXvr9F8dglGoNEQ]{D6}, see @UUID[.#side-quest:-the-main-course]{Side Quest: The Main Course}.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Animate Mummy" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to hide the inanimate mummy tile and reveal its token!

Treasure

The cooks are free to work after the mummy’s been dealt with and they can reward the PCs by periodically cooking food for them. To do so, they draw upon the ambient ectoplasm, ingredients supernaturally refreshed from cupboards, and their own skill. The cooks inform the PCs they have supplies to cook up any of the following alchemical foods (but can’t guarantee how many servings they can create): @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.5a6pudUj6WG8RITy]{strawberry egg cream fizz}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.zg4aR2ndtTzO1osa]{galvanic chew}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.awPkC6AWcHS3T4oz]{greater cooperative waffles}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.3tCtnomxBkdyG43X]{diplomat’s charcuterie}. Once the party chooses, they can come pick up the food 24 hours later—roll [[/gmr 1d4#Servings]] to determine how many servings the cooks managed to prepare. They can only prepare each of these four meals once.

Side Quest: The Main Course

As the PCs start to explore the reception halls in the next chapter, they’ll likely find themselves in a position where they’ll need to see to the creation of a particularly obscure and unpleasant-sounding meal (see area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mSXvr9F8dglGoNEQ]{D6}). In that encounter, they’re directed down to area C40 to have the cooks get started on the meal, and while the cooks are eager to do so, they’ll need a bit more help, as five of the meal’s more obscure ingredients are missing.

Fortunately, the cooks come up with substitutions. The catch here is that the cooks need to get started on the other parts of the complicated preparation process. They need the PCs to gather those five substitutions. They give the following list (along with vague directions complicated by foggy, phantasmal memories):

  • 1: Glowfly grubs can be substituted with hissing worms that infest the fertilizer stores somewhere in the groundskeeper’s outbuilding (areas @UUID[.1tfiJnjtQbAUTr1s]{C1}–@UUID[.u9oNbVptkOpdYsZo]{C11}).

  • 2: Hundred-year eggs are rare commodities, but there might be some pickled eggs up in the bakery pantry above (area @UUID[.z5Vo8C8NVRaipRTo]{C19}).

  • 3: Laroba lampreys are a local delicacy, but they’re “off season.” Fortunately, there might be some pickled lampreys in storage over in the guards’ kitchen storage (area @UUID[.jlajriJ43JNbKTyy]{C33}).

  • 4: For the Varisian raspberry wine, the PCs are in luck—there should be some stored in the wine cellar (area @UUID[.O2hrZos99pNTSbdj]{C47}) near the main kitchen (area C40). However, once the PCs investigate that area they’ll learn that the only remaining bottles were brought upstairs to one of the guestrooms (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.fTnqkD249KyhYjdW]{D22}).

  • 5: The cooks have all of the herbs and spices they need, with the exception of fresh flayleaf leaves. If anywhere in Bastardhall has some of this euphoric plant, it’d be the smoking parlor (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.kT2NnMz4rMwEAZWM]{D13}).

Cooking the Meal: Once the PCs have delivered the substitutions, the cooks prepare the meal after an hour of work, after which it must be served to the guests in area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mSXvr9F8dglGoNEQ]{D6} within 30 minutes for it to have its optimal flavors retained. The meal itself is 10 Bulk; the PCs can split up the load between themselves however they wish, but if they’re attacked before they deliver the meal, at your discretion a portion might be ruined.

Reward: Grant the PCs 40 XP for delivering these ingredients.

Milling Room.name: Milling Room
Milling Room.text:
An immense grindstone with four wooden shafts extending from its sides takes up the center of this room. Shelves filled with burlap sacks and repair tools sit on the walls to the east and west, while to the north, an empty wooden bin sits under a pair of openings in the ceiling above.

The farm on the western shore produced a fair amount of grain, much of which was hauled up to the castle to be processed here. Without a river to power the water wheel, the castle’s grindstone was instead powered through labor. While the Arudoras weren’t against long hours or indentured servitude for those they deemed below them in status (particularly in the years leading up to the curse), they knew the optics of such “money-saving measures” would have caused the rest of the help to become recalcitrant, and so Raudltz came up with a solution that didn’t involving living creatures.

Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.Gxn47A5xWacBglVu]{Grinder-Widgets x4}

Creatures: Raudltz chose to power the mill with four constructs specially crafted for the task. He purchased and then modified a set of four dig-widgets to grip onto the millstone’s four handles and ceaselessly march in circles to keep the castle’s supply of ground wheat and other grains in stock. Since the curse’s fall, no one’s bothered to order these four dig-widgets to stop. They continue to trudge circles around the mill, grinding at nothing but stone on stone, the centuries of passage of their metal feet having worn a circular furrow in the stone beneath them.

The years without maintenance have weakened these so-called grinder-widgets, but those same years of exposure to the ambient malevolence of Bastardhall have also made the constructs particularly violent. As soon as they notice the presence of any living creatures, they immediately abandon their task and attack. Unlike the typical dig-widget, these four have had their drills replaced by a pair of pliers-like grippers that they can use to not only Grab PCs, but force them into the grindstone. After dark, the power of the curse grows and these grinder-widgets lose their weak adjustment, transforming this area into a Moderate 7 encounter. Regardless of time of day, the grinder-widgets fight until destroyed but do not pursue fleeing foes.

Chef's Nook.name: Chef's Nook
Chef's Nook.text:
This small, not-quite-cramped room features a desk, a chair, and a cozy-looking bed. Several books and a lantern sit atop the desk, as does the upper half of a skeleton dressed in rags, its left hand clutching something tightly in its bony digits.

Encounter

Trivial 7

@UUID[Actor.69ZMdRQKHRbPtTnM]{Lavinia Bavah}

Creatures: This room once served the head chef (now just one of the many other servitor phantoms of Bastardhall) as private quarters, but ever since the curse took over, it’s become the safe retreat of a singular individual—the ghost of Lavinia Bavah, the scullery maid who played a key (if accidental and innocent) role in bringing the curse down on the Arudoras. On the afternoon before the curse struck, Lavinia had the ill fortune to have a day off. She chose to celebrate the late afternoon picking apples in the orchard (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.iKQ1sh7QyLC4On4P]{A21}) with the intent of baking an apple pie when she noticed a single small rowboat approaching across the lake.

Curious, she went down to the boathouse’s pier (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.iKQ1sh7QyLC4On4P]{A21a}) to meet the traveler, only to be astounded by a man who was almost the spitting image of Eragayl Arudora, founder of the castle. He carried with him a bundle swaddled in cloth that Lavinia assumed was an unusually quiet baby (considering how the bundle within the cloth seemed at times to move). The man introduced himself as Velicarn and asked to be taken up to the castle to meet with its lord, indicating that Raudltz would be very interested in what he had to show him (indicating the swaddled bundle). To sweeten the deal, Velicarn paid Lavinia a platinum coin for her aid—more money than she’d seen in one place in her life. Lavinia eagerly agreed and led Velicarn up through the castle to the grand library (area @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.HiXOGKLx6aYdwEd4]{F1}) before retreating back down to the cellars, apple pie forgotten, to polish her brand new platinum coin. Yet as the sun set, something gnawed at Lavinia. The way the swaddled “baby” never cried or made a sound seemed increasingly off, but by the time she had decided to share her suspicions, it was too late. The curse descended upon the castle, and Lavinia, like so many others, was slaughtered. She died here, hiding in the chef’s nook, racked with shame about what she believed was her fault. She had let the curse into the castle, and now she goes on as a ghost.

If the PCs visit during the night, they find Lavinia overwhelmed by the curse, and her ghost rises up from her bones with a shriek to attack. If they defeat her or flee, then return later during the day, she has no memories of this attack (assuming she’s rejuvenated if she was destroyed). If the PCs visit during the day, though, when her ghost rises up from her remains she is quiet, meek, and sobbing in shame. She asks the PCs tearfully if they’re here to undo the horror she brought to the castle. It takes little urging for her to tell her story as outlined above—while she doesn’t know for certain what went on between Velicarn and the lord of the castle, she has her suspicions. In any event, his name is an important clue for the PCs, and allows them to potentially begin researching this mysterious visitor (see Speaking to Lavinia below). Beyond this, Lavinia has little more to offer the PCs other than to ask them one favor (see @UUID[.#side-quest:-the-cursed-coin]{Side Quest: The Cursed Coin}).

If the PCs agree to help Lavinia by taking her coin, her spirit grows quiet, and this room becomes a safe haven in which the PCs can rest.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.vVSZoKgcMp6TiSNI]{Maid's Remains}

The object Lavinia’s remains clutch is the same platinum coin paid her by Velicarn, but over the years, this coin has become cursed. Velicarn’s cursed coin is detailed fully in the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.4ReRWI6jbQLPj80G]{Adventure Toolbox}.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.ICuUq6iK6NdzE7Fp]{Velicarn}

Speaking to Lavinia: You spend an hour speaking to the ashamed ghost of Lavinia Bavah, helping her to remember details about the mysterious person she escorted up into the castle on that dreadful evening.

Maximum RP 4; Research Checks @Check[diplomacy|dc:23|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to gently encourage Lavinia to recall details from her hazy memories, or @Check[deception|dc:25|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to trick her into remembering things she’d rather forget.

Reward

If the PCs avoid combat with Lavinia and learn about her shame, grant them XP as if they’d defeated her in combat. In order to put Lavinia to rest, the PCs must either lift the curse on Bastardhall, or they must complete the Cursed Coin side quest.

Side Quest: The Cursed Coin

The coin Velicarn paid to Lavinia has become cursed, and she wants it returned to the man, or at least placed among his remains. If the PCs agree to take the coin from her and return it, her shame ends and she is put to rest. She doesn’t know what became of him or where he might be now, but she can sense his presence somewhere above in the castle heights. Her advice to the PCs is to begin their search for the mysterious stranger in the grand library, which is the last place she saw him.

Asked for precise directions or a map, Lavinia does her best to help, but in her shameful undeath, her memories have become distorted and twisted. Other than confirming that the grand library she delivered Velicarn to is on the second floor of the private halls, she can offer no more navigational aid, much to her frustration.

Reward: Grant the PCs 40 XP for returning the cursed coin to Velicarn’s remains.

Laundry.name: Laundry
Laundry.text:
Three washbasins sit in the northwestern portion of this room, while to the south stands a long, low table for folding clothes. Lines for drying laundry hang between slender poles and the eastern wall. Several alcoves nestle further into the east wall, above which are laundry chutes. A pair of larger alcoves to the southwest are closed off by curtains.

The chutes lead up to area @UUID[.2OYB0V57DTNIzxuh]{C16a}; see that area for additional details.

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.buABPmUgUvhWxVaS]{Servitor Phantoms x4}

Creatures: A group of four housekeeper servitor phantoms stand listlessly about this chamber, staring forlornly at the empty drying lines, dry washtubs, and bare tabletops. Unlike the phantoms encountered elsewhere, these phantoms do nothing upon spotting the PCs—they don’t even react if they’re attacked, and just stand there, taking the hits, until they’re destroyed. The only thing that breaks these four out of their fugue is if the PCs place at least 5 Bulk of laundry (soiled or otherwise) on the sorting table, at which point the phantoms animate and go through the motion of laundering clothes—despite the fact that their incorporeal hands can’t pick up clothing and that there’s no water in any of the basins. The futility of the entire thing interacts strangely with the ambient curse energies in the room, and all PCs in area C43 must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:23] save to resist becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.EoSBuBID0gW6lHmO]{Laundry}

If the PCs trigger the servitors’ work, the curse’s energies do more than just potentially fatigue the PCs. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check notices that something shimmering and new has manifested among the laundry they placed on the table. If the PCs gather up the laundry they automatically discover this—the curse has manifested a cursed greater masquerade scarf among the other objects. Of course, as a manifestation of the curse, this scarf also has a drawback—the first time it’s activated, it fuses with the PC. Thereafter, whenever the scarf’s activation ends, the PC takes @Damage[4d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:23|basic] save) as they revert to what the scarf regards as a less interesting appearance. If the PC goes for 24 hours without activating the scarf at least once, they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for the following 24 hours.

Basement Hall.name: Basement Hall
Basement Hall.text: This long hallway serves to connect the basement of the servants’ wing with the basement of the guards’ wing. Areas of interest in the basement hall are detailed below.

Shelyn's Hideaway.name: Shelyn's Hideaway
Shelyn's Hideaway.text:
Three circular alcoves, each containing a short statuette on a pedestal, are this room’s only features. All three statues depict the same woman—the one to the west in a dancing pose, the north in a contemplative pose, and the east in a reclining pose as she sleeps.

When he first constructed the castle, Eragayl Arudora knew that not every one of his descendants would equally respect the time and talent of the help staff, and so he had this chamber built, then hid it behind a secret door. He entrusted the servants with the location of the door, but told no one else, and over the years to follow, none of his descendants ever suspected the servants had a place like this to go to rest and relax.

This room can serve as a safe haven for the PCs to rest in; they won’t be ambushed by foes within this secret chamber.

The three statutes all depict Shelyn, and are magical items bonded to this room. Through a minor miracle, the magic enchanting them remained untouched by the curse itself as well. A PC who inspects the statues and succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:23|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[arcana|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[nature|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], or @Check[occultism|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic} understands how to activate the three statues. Upon doing so, they and anyone they explain the process to can use Shelyn’s Grace.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.8Ze3B6HWu2fyKETM]{Shelyn's Grayce} 2

  • Concentrate

  • Divine

  • Healing

@Embed[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.8Ze3B6HWu2fyKETM inline]

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.LgnwTMJUkpMjy27l]{Alcove}

In addition to the three statues, a fourth object of note is found here. A PC who Seeks the northern statue or Searches the room for a minute discovers a small alabaster statuette of a unicorn with a dawnsilver horn. The statuette has light Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it triggers a memory of Jinnivere’s first (and only) time spotting a unicorn in the wild—a unicorn that tossed its head in disdain before racing away from the disappointed equestrian. This unicorn statuette belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}); see @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{Lost Artwork} for more details.

Brewery.name: Brewery
Brewery.text:
A wooden walkway wraps around this room save for in the east, overlooking a ten-foot-deep lower level in which vats, barrels, kettles, and grinders stand, many connected by wooden troughs. The entire thing is a small but efficient-looking brewery. Fires burn under the kettles, causing the contents to bubble and steam, and the air in the room is humid and bitter smelling. Condensation on the walls drips down along moldy patches.

Encounter

Trivial 7

@UUID[Actor.Mw0cHFd5a4RGEqPn]{Servitor Phantoms x4} @UUID[Actor.r1yrKVUxXjZ3a9bh]{Vile Brew}

Creatures: Castle Arudora was well known for some of its seasonal ales, particularly apple-sweetened wheat ales, brewing small batches that were then distributed throughout Ustalav. When the curse struck, four of the brewers perished here—they toil on today as phantoms, but the ale they produce is bitter and upsetting to drink. Themselves incapable of directly manipulating the machinery, the deer- skulled phantoms simply go through the motions of the process, while the haunted machinery itself produces the ale, then recycles it to start the process all over.

As soon as the phantoms notice the PCs, they wave their hands in warning and issue hissing commands to “stay still and be quiet!” If the PCs comply, one of the phantoms moves up to them and quietly explains “the brew is unhappy today” and that if the PCs know what’s good for them, they’ll leave the way they came in. If they don’t promptly leave, the hazard below activates.

Hazard: The entire mass of brewing equipment has become haunted. This is in part because of the Bastardhall curse, but mostly because Brensen Firecask stashed a vile remnant into one of the mash tuns a month after the curse fell. He was curious to see how the fragment of Charg might alter the flavor of ale produced here. It did more than alter it—it made the whole operation dangerous for living creatures to approach!

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Trigger Vile Brew" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to reveal the sludge bubbling up out of the pipes!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.HmgiqvgRfh841vPF]{Tun}

Once the haunt’s been disabled or destroyed, the PCs can discover the now-dormant @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.iQLEbANowf4fT8hK]{vile remnant} hidden in one of the tuns if they @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the room for 10 minutes.

Once the PCs make this area safe by disabling the haunt, removing the vile remnant, and defeating Brensen Firecask in area C47, the servitor phantoms can brew up alchemical treasures for the party by drawing upon the ambient ectoplasm of the area and their own skill. The brewers inform the PCs they have supplies to brew any of the following alchemical concoctions (but can’t guarantee how many servings they can create): @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.BeX3ForBrKTQD4T5]{lesser mournful fury cocktail}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Jgv2PAJic7LPoGQx]{whiskey soothing toddy}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.lIExlUFBKvBue8hb]{moderate silvertongue mutagen}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.XfcSVHwMA60JxUXJ]{moderate bottled catharsis}. Once the party chooses, they can come pick up the drink 24 hours later—roll [[/gmr 1d4#Servings]] to determine how many servings the brewers managed to prepare. They can only prepare each of these drinks once—although if the PCs gather supplies from elsewhere, they might be able to add to this list!

Wine Cellar.name: Wine Cellar
Wine Cellar.text:
As soon as a PC starts to open one of the two doors into this room, a sudden, raspy yell sounds out in the room beyond. The voice, screaming in Varisian, shouts out, “WHERE’S MY DAMNED DAWNSILVER CORKSCREW? IT WAS RIGHT HERE! WHO THE HELL TOOK IT?” before receding into angry muttering that, for a few moments, is accompanied by strange, rasping squawks. The voice repeats variations of these shouts every 30 minutes or so.

A pair of long shelves to the north and six wooden alcoves to the south of this chamber store hundreds of bottles of wine, leave no room for confusion about what went on here—this was the castle’s wine cellar.

The majority of the wine stored here has not only gone bad, but has become particularly toxic smelling and tasting. A PC who drinks any of the wine found here must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:23|options:inflicts:sickened] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). Furthermore, when combat occurs in this room, each time a creature critically fails a Strike or uses an area effect that deals physical, force, or sonic damage, roll a @Check[flat|dc:11]. On a failure, some bottles shatter in the nearby area, creating a @Template[burst|distance:5] of fouled air for one round somewhere in the area that includes the triggering creature. A creature that ends its turn in the area must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:21|options:inflicts:sickened] save to avoid becoming sickened 1 (sickened 2 on a critical failure). A creature can deliberately attempt to smash bottles on an adjacent shelf by Striking a shelf with an attack, but in this case it’s a @Check[flat|dc:15] to create a @Template[burst|distance:5] of fouled air.

Encounter

Low 7

@UUID[Actor.ns5h9AY1kPboyPln]{Brensen Firecask} @UUID[Actor.MrzlaE7k1PEsd3iQ]{Cockatrice x2}

Creatures: Before the curse fell, Brensen Firecask served as Castle Arudora’s sommelier. Originally from Highhelm, the dwarf carried himself with dignity, was soft spoken but intense when necessary, and dressed impeccably. When he first came to the castle, he regarded the opportunity to curate a noble estate’s wine cellar as the realization of a lifelong dream, as he’d always preferred the elegance of wine over the beer and ale favored by his family and friends back in Highhelm. Yet he soon discovered something even more incredible—Aron Mordimus, the affable innkeeper of Orm’s Rest and the love of his life. They spent much of their free time together, often taking working vacations to seek out new wines to stock the castle cellar or Orm’s Rest with, and had just started to plan for a long-delayed wedding when the curse struck.

Brensen was here in the wine cellar when things went bad, and as he realized the severity of the disaster he did his best to fight his way down to Maiserene to find Aron, yet he never even made it out of the castle—he was cut down by the talons of a pair of terror birds who had escaped from the menagerie up in the reception halls. He rose some time later as a redcap and returned here to his beloved wine cellar—all other memories faded. He was joined by the two terror birds who originally slew him, themselves now transformed into cockatrices who felt a strange, warped kinship with the grizzled redcap.

Both Brensen and his “pet” cockatrices are sustained in this room, and have no need for food, drink, or rest. The cockatrices follow him around as he makes his perpetual rounds through the cellar, where he takes inventory as fast as he forgets his counts. Every 20 to 30 minutes, he pats down his pockets and grows enraged for a moment at having lost his lucky dawnsilver corkscrew.

As soon as he and his pets spot the PCs, Brensen points his glaive at them in a threatening manner and shrieks out, “You! You took it! Give it back! Give back my lucky corkscrew!” He attacks at once, and his two cockatrice pets joining him in battle. If one of the cockatrices is slain, the other panics and runs to hide, tucking its head into an empty corner behind a barrel and assuming it’s out of sight; if it’s attacked again, it fights to the death. Brensen fights to the death as well, and pursues foes out of the wine cellar, but if he loses sight of his foes he’ll return here. If the PCs have found his corkscrew up in area @UUID[.Xf4qL7Jkr5pL5Zgf]{C21a}, they can use it to trigger Brensen’s Divine Revulsion.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.4ycNhGBgRHHdxhwa]{Cellar Shelf}

If the PCs seek any of the Varisian raspberry wine the cooks at area @UUID[.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40} may have sent them to fetch, it takes them only a minute to follow their directions and identify the section in the northeast corner where the vintage was kept. Unfortunately, the shelf is empty but for a scrap of paper, on which is scribbled in Elven the following: “IOU three bottles of Varisian raspberry wine; I promise, this time, to make good!” The note is signed “Danrasteian the Magnificent.” To retrieve the “borrowed” wine, the PCs must track down his guest room and search it (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.GBDZrpXoEXkQKLZT]{D26d} in the reception halls above).

Brensen assumed that the soulheart he kept was yet another of his “lucky charms” and never knew of its true significance. The first PC to touch this soulheart receives a brief memory of Brensen and Aron, before the curse, enjoying a candlelit dinner here in the wine cellar. Brensen reaches into his pocket to produce a gold ring set with seven tiny green gemstones, but just as he opens his mouth to ask Aron a very important question, the memory ends.

Side Quest Completion

If the PCs slay Brensen, his body crumbles to the ground as the ghostly figure of a handsome, well-dressed dwarf man rises up from the remains. He sobs out, “I’m sorry, my love...” before fading away, his soul at last moving on to the afterlife. Reporting this to Aron Mordimus in Maiserene completes his side quest.

Dungeon Guard Post.name: Dungeon Guard Post
Dungeon Guard Post.text:
While this room’s decor suggests it was once some sort of guard post, it currently appears to serve more as the throne hall for a particularly slovenly lord. The room’s filthy appearance is bolstered by a collapsed set of shelves to the south and piles of rubble that once set apart storerooms to the north. Yet the bulk of the room’s filth is in the east, where two tables heaped with food and drink flank a haphazard and oversized throne of broken timbers and furs. The thick, cloying smell wafting from these sloppy meals suggests just how long the food and drink has been sitting there. Just past the throne to the southwest, a ten-foot-wide archway is blocked by an iron portcullis.

The two storerooms to the north (C48a) once held supplies for the guards, but the rooms are now empty and the rubble of the collapsed walls is difficult terrain. The secret door to area C48b can be discovered by a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in the corner of the room or Searches the entire area for 10 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The portcullis to area C48c can be raised using the lever in area @UUID[.WUfxobQnHYYwiStb]{C49}. The stairs here lead down through a series of landings and switchbacks to the dungeon (area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.eqVhH8FR4IerjtmY]{E12a}), but until that region is unlocked, the stairs end at a wall of impenetrable green mist before they reach the first landing. The stairs beyond the door at area C48d lead up to area @UUID[.gxVn7eUIGm4UF4FV]{C37}.

Encounter

Severe 7

@UUID[Actor.gbuh5CHc7mr2YU2A]{Augsten Arudora} @UUID[Actor.httXfBPGseF9csXa]{Bugbear Tormentors x4} @UUID[Actor.Th7iJykrTmTt9CDg]{Skirrin}

Creatures: Augsten is the youngest of the Arudoras, a familial position that wore heavy upon his mind the older he grew. He made up for what he perceived to be favoritism in his parents eyes for his more talented elder sister Jinnivere by fostering a sharp set of bully’s skills and tormentor’s knacks, and Jinnivere was often the target of his cruel japes. He was also quite fond of fine food and drink, and this combination eventually led him to spend more and more time down here in the castle cellars—a place many high-bred nobles only consider visiting infrequently and as a last resort. But here, Augsten found the perfect subjects for his bullying—the house guards and servants. As employees of his father, they dared not stand up to Augsten’s demands for increasingly complex meals. When complaints to Lord Raudltz about Augsten’s increasing meddling in day-to-day affairs were met with remarks akin to “humor the lad, it does him good to build up his leadership skills,” and “you’re not here to help me raise my children,” Augsten became an endurance test to be humored and worked around.

When the curse struck, it found in Augsten’s bullying temperament and ravenous appetite fertile soil to grow. He doubled in size, transforming into a creature as brutish and hideous as his personality: an ogre. Despite the fact that he spends the majority of his time slouched in the makeshift throne of broken timbers, his physique has not faltered. The ruined nature of the chamber around him is a testament to his swiftly-changing temper, and the rotting food a revelation of how indiscriminate his palate has become.

Unlike his sister in the castle grounds above, Augsten does not remain in hiding, yet neither does he seek to leave his throne room. If bugbear guards from above have fled down here to warn him of the PCs, Augsten shows the bugbears what he thinks of cowards who flee from a fight. The PCs find any bugbears who fled down here are spread about the room in bits of broken, bloody fragments—some of which Augsten is enjoying as a light snack. He’s attended by four bugbear tormentors, and upon spotting the PCs, orders them to attack at once. His true bodyguard, though, is his pet, Skirrin. Like Augsten, the curse has done its work here too, and Skirrin is no longer a scrappy tom cat, but an enormous saber-toothed tiger.

As soon as one of the bugbear tormentors dies, Augsten guffaws in delight, then snaps his fingers to send Skirrin in to attack as well. He prefers to sit back and watch the battle, taking part only to issue a Bullying Command each round and to use Reactive Bullying whenever a PC triggers the reaction. This continues until he is targeted himself by an attack, he’s down to only one bugbear, Skirrin is slain, or a PC attempts to bully him, whichever comes first. At this point, he roars in excitement and lurches up from his throne to enter the battle. He’ll pursue the PCs throughout the castle once his blood is up, shouting insults at any who flee or use “coward’s tactics” (such as fighting from confined areas he has a hard time fitting into).

As soon as Augsten is slain, he staggers back, grasping at the killing blow with a stupefied expression on his face, as if having a difficult time comprehending how he could have just been killed. A moment later, he collapses to the floor with a thundering thud, then grows ghostly and translucent before rising up through the ceiling, his soul returning to his tower. His gear remains behind, and his cudgel is the key to unlocking the reception halls of Bastardhall.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.NiqPhspnTmi8nUTW]{Treasure Chest}

A single treasure chest sits behind the secret door to area C48b. The chest is locked—without the key (which can be found in area @UUID[.wO8FX9GQqMgltKx6]{C28} on Korven’s remains), three @Check[thievery|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}, or a @Check[athletics|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force it Open}. The chest contains the guards’ payroll for the next few months, amounting to 300 gp.

Captain's Quarters.name: Captain's Quarters
Captain's Quarters.text:
A large, sturdy bed sits in one corner of this room, opposite an empty desk and plain-looking chair. An empty weapon rack sits against the east wall, while to the southwest sits an iron-banded treasure chest. An iron lever protrudes from the wall in the northeast corner.

The lever on the wall operates the portcullis blocking access to area @UUID[.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48c}; raising the lever causes this portcullis to lower down into the ground.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.uLI7ArUCCYsE7f08]{Captain's Chest}

Once the personal quarters of the captain of the guard Korven Willachur (the man whose ghost now haunts area @UUID[.wO8FX9GQqMgltKx6]{C28}), the only thing of interest here now is the treasure chest. Like the chest in area @UUID[.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48b}, this one is locked and can be opened with the same key, but if it’s @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Forced Open}, the potions found within all shatter and are ruined. Inside, Korven kept a spare set of armor he only wore for special occasions, as he preferred wearing full plate. This is a suit of +1 raiment padded armor. In addition, the chest contains four moderate healing potions, a potion of quickness, a truth potion, and a set of clawed bracers.

Lower Floor Features.name: Lower Floor Features
Lower Floor Features.text:
Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

All locations in the lower floor portion of this chapter can be found in the Cellars level.

Like the ground floor, the lower floor of the cellars was lit by lanterns and torches, but is now unlit. Walls are all worked stone, and ceilings are 10 feet high. Doors are made of reinforced wood and, unless indicated in the text, cannot be locked. The lower floor lies 20 feet below the ground floor above.

Servant's Stairs.name: Servant's Stairs
Servant's Stairs.text: These stairs lead up to area @UUID[.rcdV1Q52IsBUDbDz]{C12c} above. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the area (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the stairwell for 10 minutes) and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:23|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers the secret door on the landing.

Supply Closet.name: Supply Closet
Supply Closet.text: This closet contains tools and supplies for the laundry room (area @UUID[.AYafugrItFeoydrX]{C43}).

Dungeon Entrance.name: Dungeon Entrance
Dungeon Entrance.text: This reinforced wooden double door is locked. It can be unlocked with the key found in area @UUID[.WUfxobQnHYYwiStb]{C49}, with three @Check[thievery|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}, or with a @Check[athletics|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} the doors. Until the dungeons themselves are unlocked, though, an impassible wall of green mist blocks the stairs after descending 15 feet. Once the mist is cleared, these stairs wind 100 feet down, past several landings where the stairs switch directions to the south or north, until they reach area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.FBPDuStK6Zlej0n5]{E6a}.

Guards' Stairs.name: Guards' Stairs
Guards' Stairs.text: These stairs lead up to area @UUID[.lQdheEdZiY5D3YIS]{C34} above.

The Haunted Shore.name: The Haunted Shore
The Haunted Shore.text: As detailed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.oIog1W3hftKUYySh]{Bastion of Blasphemies Player's Guide}, the PCs have been hired by a woman named Florin Kindler to serve as guards, advisors, and traveling companions on her journey to the mysterious ruins of Bastardhall. Each PC begins this campaign knowing the basic details of Bastardhall's story—that the castle stands in ruins for most of each century, only to mysteriously rebuild itself for a short period of time once per century as a mysterious black coach rides out in search of passengers. Those who accept the invitation vanish, while those who refuse soon meet horrible fates—only those who hide and avoid contact entirely with the coach (or who are not targeted in the first place) escape unscathed. The PCs also know their employer lost her parents on the most recent manifestation of the castle's curse several years ago. Now that she's come of age, she's eager to explore the ruins and put to rest the family tragedy that has, for the past 12 years, defined her life.

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
When you’re ready to begin the Adventure Path, inform the players that their characters have been traveling with their companion, Florin, for several hours through the lonely hills of Varno. Then, a moment after they round the final bend in the road and catch their first ominous sight of the ruined castle from the shores of Lake Laroba, a sudden sense of dread wells up in the hearts of each PC. An instant later, Florin cries out in terror, shrieking “I didn’t know!” before the entire world flashes with a blast of green light. Each PC can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:20] check—those who succeed see Florin suddenly grow translucent, as if she’s become a ghost, and then her ghostly form is pulled violently through the air toward the castle. A moment after that, all the PCs experience the same sensation, save that they remain physical and solid during this journey. Then, nearly as soon as it began, the PCs find themselves standing on the shore of Arudora Isle, looking up at a very different, intact version of Bastardhall. What happened to Florin and why she didn’t arrive at the same place on the island shore is but the first of many mysteries the PCs will, in time, have a chance to solve.

The PCs arrive at area @UUID[.XyjmNWjgPGNrEVim]{A1}. Proceed with that encounter immediately. Regardless of what time it was when the PCs left, it’s now close to sunset. When the sun sets, be sure to describe the strange, forbidding sense of doom that settles over the PCs. Things always look more menacing after dark, but here in Bastardhall, they feel much more so. Lean in to Gothic horror tropes—strange red eyes peering from the tangles of roots, twisted tree branches scraping against each other in the wind, flights of bats fluttering overhead, wisps of fog curling through the weeds below. Bastardhall after dark doesn’t look safe, and it should encourage the PCs to seek shelter from the night!

The Skies Above.name: The Skies Above
The Skies Above.text:
The storm has yet to break. Skies are mostly clear, with only a few clouds visible. Temperatures are crisp and cool, and the wind is limited to periodic breezes that feel refreshing rather than cold.

Sunrise is at 7:30 A.M. and sunset is at 7:30 p.m.; days and nights are both 12 hours long.

Haunted Shore Ambushes.name: Haunted Shore Ambushes
Haunted Shore Ambushes.text:
Encounter

Low 5

@UUID[Actor.yPYQC2bfOYmqcfIB]{Imps x6}

If the PCs rest in an unsafe area on the haunted shore, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:5]. On a failure, they’re ambushed while they camp by 6 sahkil imps—these hideous tangles of insectile wings, tendrils, biting mouths, and disturbingly humanoid eyes generally remain up in the skies above but sometimes fly down below to torment creatures. A sahkil imp has the same statistics as the typical imp, save that when they use Change Shape, they assume the appearance of a Small or smaller bat or flying insect.

Lucid Nightmares.name: Lucid Nightmares
Lucid Nightmares.text:
The first nightmare the PCs each endure on the haunted shore is of being greeted by a strange figure swathed in mist and carrying a staff from which hangs an eerie green-glowing lantern. The figure speaks in a whisper: “Who are you to stand before Caydserris Arudora?” before he points out to the waters of the lake. The PCs then find themselves in a skiff far from shore. An immense beast surges from below to capsize their vessel, tossing the PCs into the waters. The remainder of the dream involves the PC swimming away in fear—if they reach the shore, they clamber up trees or cliff walls, still convinced that what hunts them from the lake depths can chase them onto land. Each PC hears the unseen creature kill their companions somewhere in the distance, and just as this huge entity looms from behind to swallow them whole, the PC wakes.

The Beast in the Deep

Resist Nightmare @Check[will|dc:20]

Critical Failure The PC wakes with thalassophobia (fear of deep bodies of water) and takes a –2 status penalty to Athletics checks made while the waters of Lake Laroba are in sight for the next 24 hours.

Research @Check[stealth|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] check to hide in the dream so they can watch and learn in relative safety or @Check[athletics|dc:25|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] check to Escape by swimming and then take advantage of the reprieve to learn more.

Effect

@UUID[Item.WENXlprEY6ORnkWb]{Thalassophobia}

If a PC critically fails to resist this nightmare, use the linked effect to automate their status penalty to Athletics checks caused by their thalassophobia.

Restoring Maiserene.name: Restoring Maiserene
Restoring Maiserene.text:
Before the curse of Bastardhall engulfed it, the village of Maiserene was home to about five dozen artisans, laborers, priests, soldiers, and peasants, but nearly half the populace perished when the curse took the island. They were the lucky ones, whose souls moved on to the Boneyard. Those who took part in the burning of the Laroba Causeway or openly fought against the monsters unleashed by the curse were, like so many servants, guests, and family members within the castle walls, transformed by the curse into monsters—with six notable exceptions.

Among the villagers, six leaders stepped forward to plot and orchestrate an attempt to quarantine the curse and organize the burning of the bridge. While their attempt to stop the curse failed, Charg took note of these six and their doomed but heroic attempt to oppose him and denied them the agency of becoming monsters. Instead, the souls of these six leaders were bound to six areas along Arudora Isle’s haunted shore that once brought them pleasure and pride in life. Yet this was no reward, for as these six locations became corrupt and ruined, the bound souls were forced to endure this corruption. Charg consigned them to centuries of torment amid the ruins of places they once held dear.

While this punishment is horrific, it also created an unintended flaw in the curse, for if these souls could be released from their prisons, they would return to their homes in Maiserene and manifest as incarnations of hope and defiance. The PCs can release them by visiting the six sites along the haunted shore and overcoming the challenges they meet there. As they do so, each trapped soul returns to their home in the village proper, manifesting as a unique phantom allied to the PCs.

Once the PCs restore all six leaders to their rightful places as phantoms in the village, they take their first real step toward lifting Bastardhall’s curse, for restoring these six leaders unlocks the castle grounds and allows the PCs to proceed into @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL]{Chapter 2}.

Even after a soul becomes an allied phantom, they can be bolstered by using a fragment of memory formed from crystallized ectoplasm—these crystals are known as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.8WxFFZm6OcBCCARR]{Soulhearts} and can be found within Bastardhall’s walls at locations where powerful emotions once held sway. Using a soulheart to bolster a phantom increases their rank from a starting rank of 0 to a maximum rank of 3. As each Maiserene phantom increases in rank in this way, the benefits and advantages they can offer to the PCs increases as well. The specific advantages vary from phantom to phantom, as detailed in the individual entries on @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2]{Adventure Toolbox}.

If a trapped soul is released but their home in Maiserene isn’t yet cleared, the soul remains in limbo until the PCs clear that area. Once cleared, the soul immediately manifests as detailed in that area’s encounter text.

Memories of the Arudoras.name: Memories of the Arudoras
Memories of the Arudoras.text:
Once any of the phantoms have reached rank 1 and have physically manifested, their memories become clearer and they can be interviewed to learn fragments of what they recall about the Arudoras. The PCs can use this opportunity to research any of the Arudoras save Caydserris or Florin Kindler (both of whom were not present before the time of the curse for gossip and rumors to spread). For six of these Arudoras, one Maiserene leader is particularly knowledgeable (as indicated on the @UUID[.#maiserenes-phantoms]{Maiserene’s Phantoms} table), and interviewing that phantom about that Arudora reduces the Research check’s DC by 2. Each phantom knows which Arudora the others knew best, and while they suggest the PCs speak to them on the topic first, they’ll do what they can to answer questions if the PCs persist. (Since he largely operated behind the scenes and is believed to be dead, no leader grants this bonus on the topic of Irrokcis Arudora.)

Research

Any Arudora (except Caydserris or Florin)

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.CzkcMKPWphpJlkPp]{Demiterus} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.gBlukTRHytlzwC1D]{Eragayl} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.6tXqaoCmhlHFRm3I]{Jinnivere} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.FZDFAjuHckZz0QW0]{Neesha} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.PNW896yOsktDWXwT]{Tasifinie} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.o5n22VwGbRDh0it6]{Zasha} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.7ZSvhlTTOzKZNUJZ]{Augsten} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.mJYN4Onwrp1JCt7X]{Alisendra} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.BzucncWfHopUCsz3]{Dazerien} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.m0khEHYdDxDw9B1G]{Raudltz} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.7VX2SBgHGbICdyYi]{Ryhasphinea} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.qi00xNaMBgtsO0LH]{Irrokcis}

Maiserene’s Memories: You spend an hour chatting with one of Maiserene’s physically manifested phantoms to discuss their memories about one of the Arudoras.

Maximum RP 2 per Arudora; Research Checks @Check[diplomacy|dc:20|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to carry on a productive conversation, @Check[society|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to understand the relationship between the aristocracy and the villagers and to avoid making an unintentional gaffe during the discussion, or @Check[perception|dc:25|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to listen closely and make accurate assumptions about things that might have been left unsaid.

Haunted Shore Features.name: Haunted Shore Features
Haunted Shore Features.text:
The haunted shore consists of wooded slopes sandwiched between a lakeshore that varies from mud to cliffsides and the rising bulwark of bedrock atop which Bastardhall itself stands. As long as the lake waters are calm, it’s only a @Check[athletics|dc:10|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim}, and where the shore rises to cliffs along the northern and western sides of the isle, there are plenty of handholds, making it a @Check[athletics|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb}. These cliffs are a 40-foot drop into the deep lake waters below.

When traveling along the shore or the main path encircling the isle, elevation changes are minor, but the ground rises steeply when one travels inland toward the castle walls, often leading to cliffs. Bastardhall is built on an upthrust slab of granite that elevates its already high walls even further. The base of this granite cliff looms 80 feet above the shore, while the sheer rock walls that rise up to the base of the curtain wall do so for another 60 feet. The walls themselves tower a further 40 feet above that, so that those who stand atop the curtain wall can look down at the lake from a lofty height of 180 feet— and yet the towers of the castle itself rise hundreds of feet higher still. The castle walls and stone cliffs here alike offer very little in the way of handholds—it’s a @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check to Climb either.

Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

All locations in this chapter can be found in the Shore level of Arudora Isle.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.iD40miQekZaJNJXO]{Shore}

As the PCs wake up in the haunted shore, you can play this ambience sound.

The Waking Shore.name: The Waking Shore
The Waking Shore.text:
Ripples of lake water lap against a muddy shore amid swaths of reeds and cattails. To the north and south rise immense stone pillars. Two of those nearby to the west still extend up well over a hundred and fifty feet, while those near the lakeshore have fared more poorly, with the one to the north missing its top half and the southern one having collapsed entirely. More of the immense pilings stretch off to the west in the lake, all the way to the distant hazy wooded shore on the far side, but if these stone pillars once supported a bridge or causeway above, no sign of it remains today.

As grand as these immense pillars might be, the sight to the east renders them almost an afterthought, for here looms Bastardhall. Perched atop a massive upthrust slab of granite and surrounded by a stark gray curtain wall, Bastardhall is an exercise in Gothic excess, its towers stretching hundreds of feet more into the sky above. Yet this castle, unlike the surrounding shore and the ruined buildings that stand to the north and south, seems strangely impermanent. At one moment, appearing solid and then flickering and shimmering as if the entire structure were made of mists and shadows.

A muddy trail leads up from the lakeshore to a guardhouse at the base of the castle’s granite perch to the east. There, the trail becomes an overgrown road, leading south toward a stone church and north to a ruined village of leaning wooden shacks, yet the castle looms over all, rendering what squats on this dreary shore insignificant and small.

Once you’ve set the scene for the PCs, give them a few moments to decide where in the immediate area they’re located. The mud is wet and cold, and clings to footwear, while the 3-foot-tall lakeside reeds poke and scratch at exposed skin. As soon as the PCs start to express an interest in exploring or trying to find out what just happened, though, more pressing matters slosh up out of the cold, dark lake.

Encounter

Low 5

@UUID[Actor.dEpqEmmwRgGnMAiB]{Grindylow Stalkers x4}

Creatures: The souls of the peasants who once dwelled in the nearby village of Maiserene exist still, but the Bastardhall Curse has seen to it that they reincarnate over and over again into grindylows. These grindylows subsist primarily on fish caught in the waters of the lake, and they prefer to live in the ruined buildings just to the north.

While most of the grindylow “villagers” are typical specimens of their kind, the four stalkers who have taken note of the PCs are more dangerous. These four traveling along the shore, preparing to swim out to start the night’s fishing only to have stumbled across what might be a bigger, if more curious, catch—the PCs!

The grindylows don’t attack at once and instead speak to the PCs in gurgling voices, pointing and snickering and licking toothy lips. Any PC who can understand Thalassic can hear the monsters calling “dibs” on various items of equipment the PCs carry, wondering if they “fell out of the Ghost House,” making unsettling comments about the best way to prepare the meat of these strange “fish” who washed up on shore or debating the wisdom of whether it’s better to bring them back to “Mama Ilgrunthin” alive or dead. If a PC addresses the grindylows in Thalassic, the monsters are shocked that the “weird fish” can talk too and might engage in a bit of back and forth before they grow impatient—and before they give away any information of real import to the PCs.

When they attack, the four grindylows hiss and gurgle, calling out tactics to each other as two of them work to gang up on the least-armored PC. A third casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4koZzrnMXhhosn0D]{Fear} on a heavily armored PC, while a fourth hangs back to use ranged spells against the poor PC the first two have targeted. Once it becomes apparent the PCs are tougher than they expected (as soon as the first grindylow stalker is slain), the other grindylows hiss and shriek in fear, slither into the lake, and Jet north to the workshop (area @UUID[.XdkSCjX3BA3dp5sE]{A6}) to join with the grindylows located there.

Maiserene.name: Maiserene
Maiserene.text:
A sad collection of eight thatched-roof wooden hovels perched on short wooden pilings lean against each other for support to either side of the weedy road that leads north. Soft sounds of rustling and whispering come from behind shuttered windows, and here and there doors that were ajar snap shut. Larger buildings in slightly better repair stand to the north, yet no sign of welcome—no curls of smoke from chimneys, no beckoning flicker of light in a window, and no sign of any animal life at all—are apparent in this forlorn hamlet. A rickety wooden sign on a leaning wooden post sits beside the road.

The sign on the post reads, “Maiserene.” A PC can attempt a @Check[society|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} to recognize the name as that of a village whose inhabitants vanished over 500 years ago on the night Bastardhall’s curse began. Each of these houses contains two to four grindylow occupants, all of whom are standard creatures of their ilk—and thus below any sort of real challenge for 5th level PCs as a result. These grindylow villagers cower and hide inside their homes, and howl and flee into the lake rather than fight. Unless the PCs are stealthy as they move through the ruined village, chances are excellent that the grindylow leader, Ilgrunthin, steps out of her home to the north (Orm’s Rest, area @UUID[.msh8hhX94bXBPpbi]{A8}) to challenge the PCs; see that area for further details on how this first encounter with Maiserene’s larger-than-life leader goes.

Treasure

While hovels don’t contain any treasure, desperate PCs can discover food supplies in the form of freshly caught fish and edible lake weed totaling [[/gmr 1d4#Days worth of food]] days’ worth of food for one person per hovel.

Western Watch Post.name: Western Watch Post
Western Watch Post.text:
The double doors to this building are made of stone and barred from the inside. To open them from outside, the PCs must either @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force it Open} with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check (this leaves the doors broken and unable to be closed until they’re repaired) or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.cYdz2grcOcRt4jk6]{Disable the Device} that holds the doors shut with a much trickier successful @Check[thievery|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.DisableDevice.Title|options:action:disable-a-device|traits:manipulate] check. Alternatively, a Small creature could @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeeze} through one of the arrow slits into the interior with a successful @Check[acrobatics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Squeeze.Title|options:action:squeeze|traits:exploration,move] check.

The interior of this stone building has a high roof, with wooden beams occupying the upper five feet of the twenty- foot-high ceiling. A pair of tables with built-in benches sit in the middle of the room, while double bunks stand in alcoves to the north- and southeast. Between them, a stone fireplace and a small table occupy a central alcove—here, a few swords, daggers, bows, and arrows lie scattered on the ground. Broken and empty weapon racks stand against the walls between the alcoves. Pairs of arrow slits to the north- and southwest provide feeble ventilation for the dank chamber.

Encounter

Trivial 5

@UUID[Actor.nvkI4G9QR7hAxVy0]{Despair is Thy Reward}

Hazard: The town’s guards once occupied this watch post, with Maiserene’s sheriff living above while the town’s four deputies shared the bunks here. Those four deputies perished centuries ago as they failed to defend their village from monsters that flew down from the castle above.

They died before the curse fully took hold, and while their souls were thus able to escape to the afterlife, the despair, shame, and fear they endured at failing to protect their home left a dangerous supernatural wound in this watch post, nevertheless.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Trigger Despair is Thy Reward" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to toggle the ghostly lights and play an @UUID[Playlist.aGCIKeSAO2yb078H.PlaylistSound.mMkEm0YNpxFORiCv]{ambience sound}!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.OS32DWVoEJgqWQGN]{Scattered Weapons}

Most of the weapons that the soldiers dropped in the alcove centuries ago are rusty and broken, but among them are a few valuable treasures: a low-grade cold iron longsword, a +1 shortbow, and a type II spellstrike arrow containing an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9h9YCncqah6VNsKf]{Acid Grip} spell (DC 19).

Restoration

Once the haunt is disabled, the phantom of Ausken Dast manifests here once his soul is rescued from the eastern watch post (area @UUID[.D7PNbqVhoW8hFd61]{A18}). His presence cleans and restores the building. The fireplace burns with a cozy fire, and the two weapon racks are restored and contain an assortment of common weapons worth no more than 10 gp each (ranged weapons are accompanied by 10 units of ammo each). Every day, Ausken can replenish these weapon racks with whatever common weapons the PCs desire, but doing so causes the previous day’s weapons and ammunition to revert to ectoplasm and then vanish.

Reward

Once this location is restored by Ausken’s presence, grant the PCs 10 XP.

Maiserene Schoolhouse.name: Maiserene Schoolhouse
Maiserene Schoolhouse.text:
A one-story red brick building sits at the base of a looming cliff face to its southeast. A pair of wooden doors provide entrance, and several windows to the northeast are tightly shuttered. The wood-shingle roof above has been almost completely destroyed—all that remains are scorched wooden beams from an ancient fire.

The village of Maiserene never counted many children among its population, so this humble schoolhouse was more than adequate to provide education for young ones whose parents didn’t apprentice them to artisans or laborers and others who wished to continue learning. As the villagers tried to burn the original causeway when the curse manifested, flying monsters from the castle above gleefully wrenched burning timbers from the fire and threw them about the town. In particular, they targeted the roof of the schoolhouse, where students and their teacher, Esmira, had taken shelter. That none of those who sheltered here lived long enough for the curse to capture their souls is a bitter mercy indeed.

Restoration

Once the haunt in the schoolroom is disable and Esmira Vermidian’s will-o’-wisp incarnation at the standing stones (area @UUID[.Ez53diEo41YhLat7]{A14}) is ended, her phantom manifests here. Her presence causes the roof of the building to become fully restored and repairs all of the books and supplies within.

Reward

Once this location is restored by Esmira’s presence, grant the PCs 10 XP.

Schoolroom.name: Schoolroom
Schoolroom.text:
The main room of this dilapidated red brick building was obviously a schoolroom. Eight desks face the northeast, where a larger desk sits attended by a wooden chair. A door to the southwest hangs ajar, and the three windows in the room are all tightly shuttered, while above the roof is missing entirely, leaving scorched beams exposed to the sky.

The ashes and weeds growing in this ruined area make it difficult terrain until it’s restored.

Encounter

Trivial 5

@UUID[Actor.Er9C1qCEcQjbaqhz]{The Sky is Burning}

Hazard: On the night of the curse, all manner of flying creatures took cruel delight in tossing burning rubble down through the increasingly exposed roof. The fear and terror of those trapped within lingers to this day as a dangerous haunt.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Trigger The Sky is Burning" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to toggle the ghostly lights and play an @UUID[Playlist.aGCIKeSAO2yb078H.PlaylistSound.HjDpjyBa1CHsj909]{ambience sound}!

Effect

@UUID[Item.akwsZECWxYbnScgy]{Flare-Up Protection}

When applicable, you can use this effect to automate the PCs' bonus to Reflex saves against The Sky is Burning's flare-ups.

Maiserene Library.name: Maiserene Library
Maiserene Library.text:
Bookshelves fill this room, with an exception of a small reading desk to the south. Above, the roof has long burned away, leaving the scorched ceiling beams exposed. Below, the shelves have largely collapsed into weed-tangled rubble.

This room is difficult terrain until it’s restored.

Restoration

Once restored by Esmira’s presence, the books here cover a wide range of topics, and the library can be used to perform @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n]{Research on Bastardhall}.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.PAMDhjQNkAm8rB5R]{Bastardhall}

Restored Maiserene Library: Several of the holdings here are focused on the history of Castle Arudora, which mysteriously includes scrolls and letters that might contain information about Bastardhall after it became cursed.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[library-lore|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to peruse the books or @Check[society|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to efficiently navigate the dense historical records.

Schoolteacher's Room.name: Schoolteacher's Room
Schoolteacher's Room.text:
The roof of this ruined bedroom has burned away, leaving the furniture below covered in layers of ash that have long since given root to patches of weeds.

This room is difficult terrain until it’s restored.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.RWpp2Riey1et6NJ2]{Schoolteacher's Room}

A PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} through this room (or 1 minute doing so after the schoolhouse is restored) finds an old schoolteacher’s bonnet tucked safely away between the wall and the bed. This mage’s hat once belonged to Esmira; if asked about it, she graciously gifts it to the PCs.

Trading Post.name: Trading Post
Trading Post.text:
The air in this run-down storefront is musty as a result of the swaths of mold and dust that encrust most every available surface. It’s tough to determine what items lie stacked on the numerous shelves throughout the area due to the thick layer of furred fungal growth and other detritus.

The thick dusty air in this room makes breathing difficult. A breathing creature who doesn’t hold their breath must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:20|name:Tainted Air|options:inflicts:sickened] save if they end their turn in the trading post to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} by the tainted air. The air in area A5b (once the bedroom of the trading post’s owner, Banijer Greely) is even worse; those who fail the save become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.

Encounter

Moderate 5

@UUID[Actor.zpd6b6UPP72ZELCj]{Poltergeists x2}

Creatures: While most of the villagers who survived the first cursed night were swept up by its power and transformed into grindylows, Banijer’s two shop assistants managed to resist this fate, only to be slain by the grindylows. Traumatized by their doom, they became poltergeists who haunt this shop still. The grindylows have learned to avoid this shop, and for the past several centuries the poltergeists have waited, silently but patiently, for a reason to rage. The PCs are that reason—the two undead manifest one round after the PCs enter the shop, attacking at once by hurling moldy and filthy items from the shelves. They use Telekinetic Storm each round to attack the party, following that up with attempts to frighten the PCs. If all potential PCs are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened}, the poltergeists instead hurl a telekinetic object.

Faced against foes who use ghost touch weapons or other tools capable of harming them, they’ll cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.mrDi3v933gsmnw25]{Telekinetic Maneuver} to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm} the weapon. The poltergeists can’t leave the trading post but continue to hurl objects at PCs through doorways or windows as long as targets remain in sight.

If they’re destroyed, they rejuvenate in the trading post after [[/gmr 2d4#Days until Rejuvenation]] days unless Banijer’s presence restores the building, which causes them to be permanently destroyed.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.s48Rz01gMGmXtWzA]{Pile of Moldy Clothing}

The items on the shelves here are all old and ruined (although they’ll be restored once Banijer returns; see Restoration, below). One notable exception can be found in area A5b. A PC who spends a round @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeking} in this room (and potentially choking on the spores and dust in the air) and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:22|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers a lifting belt under a pile of moldy clothing in the corner. If the PCs don’t find the belt before Banijer returns, he offers the belt to them as thanks.

Restoration

Once the poltergeists are destroyed, the phantom of Banijer Greely manifests here once his soul is rescued from the farmlands (area @UUID[.Oz08GUWUIID0kaMb]{A16}). The mold and dust vanish, and the shop’s shelves become full of items for sale, as detailed further in Banijer’s entry on Adventure Toolbox. Now and then, PCs might catch glimpses out of the corners of their eyes of the two faint spirits of his assistants, freed from their existence as poltergeists but not yet able to escape Bastardhall—and for now, content to be with their friend once again.

Reward

Once this location is restored by Banijer’s presence, grant the PCs 10 XP.

Workshop.name: Workshop
Workshop.text:
Shelves filled with broken tools and ruined supplies line the walls of this large, high-ceilinged workshop. Three workbenches sit in the shop. The two on the east side are heaped with stones, bones, pieces of wood, and other materials, while the one to the west has a partially completed scale model of Bastardhall made from these fragments.

Encounter

Low 5

@UUID[Actor.dEpqEmmwRgGnMAiB]{Grindylow Stalkers x4}

Creatures: The grindylows of Maiserene view Bastardhall with a mix of fear and awe. Vague ancestral memories of their lives before the curse have merged with the memories of many lives since, and today they revere the place as the “Ghost House.” The grindylow stalkers in the ruined village have long worked at trying to build and perfect this model as a sort of homage to the Ghost House but can never quite get it right. They work in shifts of four on the never-ending project, spending the first few hours of each shift bitterly taking apart the “mistakes” the previous shift introduced.

As long as the PCs aren’t particularly noisy when they enter the workshop, the four grindylow stalkers currently stationed here are all gathered around the western workbench, muttering advice or whispering complaints to one another as they work on the model and won’t initially notice the PCs. If the PCs attack, the grindylows take a –4 circumstance penalty to initiative. If the PCs do nothing or remain quiet, 3 rounds after they enter, one of the grindylows huffs in frustration and turns to slither over to one of the mounds of supplies, then hisses in shock and anger at the intruders. If the PCs speak to them, they attack unless the PCs address them in Thalassic, in which case the surprised grindylows listen for no more than a minute. Their initial attitude is hostile, but if the PCs can make them indifferent with a critical success at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.MakeAnImpression.Title|options:action:make-an-impression,workshop-grindylow|traits:auditory,concentrate,exploration,linguistic,mental] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Make an Impression}, or if they @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coerce} them with a @Check[intimidation|dc:18|name:PF2E.Actions.Coerce.Title|options:action:coerce|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental] check, the grindylows suggest that the PCs speak to “Mama Ilgrunthin,” and even offer to escort the PCs to their leader in area @UUID[.msh8hhX94bXBPpbi]{A8}. Asked about the model, the grindylows puff up proudly and say, “It’s our gift to the glory of the Ghost House—may its ghosts forever remain up on high and leave us alone!” Compliments about the model grant PCs a +2 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks, while threats to destroy it grant them a +2 circumstance bonus to Coerce them.
