Any actual violence directed at the model forces them to attack.

In combat, the grindylows form a defensive barrier around the model as best they can, using their spells to attack at range. The model is AC 15 and has Hardness 5 and 20 HP (10 BT). Each time the PCs damage the model, the grindylows become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} if the model is under its BT). If the model is destroyed, the grindylows howl in panic and flee the workshop into the lake. They’ll return in a few days and start the process of rebuilding it if they can.

Restoration

Once the grindylows are slain or driven off, the phantom of Ilana Greenbough manifests here once her soul is rescued from the scenic overlook (area @UUID[.02Vj3Jr4cxdBLdUl]{A19}). Her presence cleans the workshop, restores the two eastern workbenches to full order, and organizes the tools and supplies, stocking the shelves fully. The model of Bastardhall takes on a shimmering ghostly appearance, becoming a much more accurate representation than before. While this can give the PCs a bird’s eye view of the castle layout, it doesn’t reveal any of the dangers within or a look into areas that are indoors or underground.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.UUqGlDCzpRnwqovv]{The Bastardhall Curse}

Spectral Bastardhall Model: Curiously, though, a PC who meditates before the model can open their mind to the area’s spiritual nature and perform research on the nature of the Bastardhall Curse. Ilana suggests the PCs try this if they’re curious but warns them it could be dangerous, and that it might be wisest to wait until they’ve at least explored some of the castle a bit more (at the very least, the castle grounds, cellars, and reception halls) before trying it.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[religion|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to draw upon your own faith to help guide you through the visions, @Check[occultism|dc:28|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to open your mind to the supernatural mystery and observe its secrets, or @Check[perception|dc:31|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to simply meditate and stare into the ghostly images in hopes of catching a revelatory glimpse.

Special Each time a PC critically fails a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.t5nBkpjroaq7QBGK]{Research} check on the spectral Bastardhall model, the curse lashes out with a harrowing vision of an immense roiling monstrosity—a version of Bastardhall made of flesh and sinew and bone, in which the PCs are slowly being digested. This deals @Damage[10d6[spirit]] damage on the PC (@Check[will|dc:26|basic] save).

Reward

Once this location is restored by Ilana’s presence, grant the PCs 10 XP.

Village Storehouse.name: Village Storehouse
Village Storehouse.text:
This storehouse has a high, raftered ceiling, which is obscured by thick layers of countless cobwebs. Below, stacks of dusty crates sit heaped to the south, while to the north is a crumbling old shelf. Double doors to the west hangs ajar, opening out onto a ten-foot-wide pier that’s partially collapsed into the lake. The middle of the room contains the crumbled ruins of a large horse-drawn wagon.

The storehouse once held all the food and other supplies needed by the villagers but also served as a staging point for similar supplies needed for the castle itself, with the wagon serving as a mode of transport to deliver the supplies up to the castle grounds. None of the village leaders have any real domain over the storehouse, so this location remains in ruins even after the PCs have returned all six phantoms to town.

Encounter

Trivial 5

@UUID[Actor.A4VgQIHsqJKssQOM]{Hunting Spiders x4}

Creatures: A group of four blue-and-black pony-sized spiders lurk amid the cobwebs in the rafters. They watch quietly as the PCs explore the area below, then Descend on a Web from their hiding spots 30 feet up near the hidden ceiling to attack the PCs. They fight to the death but do not pursue fleeing PCs.

Each time one of the spiders is slain, it curls into a ball of spindly legs, releasing the spectral vision of a horse that faintly neighs before galloping off into nothingness—before the curse, these spiders were the village’s four workhorses.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.MpDcdbjPa2OKKu7L]{Wagon's Ruins}

A 10-minute @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} of the storehouse and a successful @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check turns up a few valuables nestled amid the wagon’s ruins: a leather pouch containing 5 pearls worth 10 gp each and a low-grade alloy orb, a horse marvelous miniature, and a wand of ant haul.

Orm's Rest.name: Orm's Rest
Orm's Rest.text:
A faded wooden sign depicting an enormous sea serpent wrapped around Arudora Isle hangs above this building’s main doorway. Double doors leading to what appears to be an attached stable stands further up to the northeast.

Written under the sign is the name of this inn: “Orm’s Rest.” This place also served Maiserene as a tavern and town hall when needed. Area A8b was once the private residence of innkeeper @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.0LOtv52aD44VMt6N]{Aron Mordimus}, while the six smaller rooms labeled A8c were used by paying guests. Area A8d was a rarely-rented-out “comfort suite” for those few visitors who wanted more room but hadn’t yet secured permission to enter the castle itself. The main room (area @UUID[.Z57dhdZQtoGonua3]{A8a}), on the other hand, was a public space.

Orm's Rest Tavern.name: Orm's Rest Tavern
Orm's Rest Tavern.text:
This room appears to have once served as the town’s tavern. A pair round tables sit in the middle, while to the west stands a compact harpsichord. Not quite opposite to the northeast is a brick fireplace, while a counter set with a pair of benches may have once been a place to wet one’s whistle. Mud and rotting lake weed, not to mention several decaying half-eaten fish, lie strewn about the place, while behind the bar itself lies an immensely nasty-smelling nest of mud, sticks, lake weeds, and bones.

Encounter

Low 5

@UUID[Actor.wBWh3kFEDBTeqSVu]{Ilgrunthin}

Creature: Before the curse, Maiserene was led by six public figures, each of whom were in turn beholden to the castle’s majordomo and the Arudoras. Today, a single relatively immense grindylow runs the show. Known to her followers as “Mama Ilgrunthin,” this grindylow towers at a height of nearly 7 feet upon a dozen wriggling tentacles. Each generation, a new grindylow leader arises, but whether they’re known as “Mama” or “Papa,” they retain the same eldritch supernatural abilities that simultaneously awe and frighten the grindylows.

If the PCs arrive here without an escort, Mama Ilgrunthin attacks at once. On the other hand, if the PCs are escorted here by grindylows (most likely the four stalkers in area @UUID[.XdkSCjX3BA3dp5sE]{A6}), Mama Ilgrunthin puffs up menacingly but stays her hand, instead demanding first in Thalassic and then in Common to know what the PCs are doing here. She listens impatiently, waving away any questions with a hand with a dismissive “Not important.” Each PC can, in turn, attempt a @Check[deception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|options:action:lie|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie} to her, a @Check[diplomacy|dc:20] check to simply explain things, or a @Check[intimidation|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Coerce.Title|options:action:coerce|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coerce} her. A PC who addresses her in Thalassic gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their check. If at least half the PCs succeed at these checks, they temporarily appease Ilgrunthin. When the discussion is over, she orders the PCs to leave Maiserene and never return, telling them that they need to deal with their problems elsewhere without bothering her or her subjects. If at least half the PCs succeeded with critical successes, they earn the right to travel through the village as they wish as long as they don’t attempt to enter any buildings or harm any grindylows.

Otherwise, Ilgrunthin attacks. As she does, she roars loud enough that the other grindylows in the village hear and quickly slither out of their homes to gather in the village square just south of the inn to watch with wide eyes—but they don’t join the fight. If the PCs were escorted there by any grindylow stalkers, they do join her in battle (but even then, these grindylows panic and flee as soon as they take any damage).

Ilgrunthin prefers not to move from her mud-and-stick nest. She casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.TVKNbcgTee19PXZR]{Shield} each round as well if she’s not threatened in melee—if there are adjacent targets, she instead uses her third action after casting a spell to attempt a Strike with her tentacles. If she’s reduced to fewer than 20 Hit Points, she surrenders and begs for mercy, offering the PCs her wand and all the treasure in the fireplace in return for her life. Even if the PCs don’t demand it, she flees Orm’s Rest as soon as possible, returns to the depths of the lake, and doesn’t return.

If Ilgrunthin is slain or flees, the remaining grindylows in the village flee as well, leaving Maiserene alone for the remainder of the Adventure Path. In this case, grant the PCs XP for the grindylow stalkers in area @UUID[.XdkSCjX3BA3dp5sE]{A6} as if they’d defeated them in combat if they hadn’t done so already.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.yFYGXylGKUFThcco]{Fireplace}

Among a large number of disgusting and worthless offerings heaped in the fireplace are a few valuables the grindylows have scavenged and given to their leader: a silver-and-jade necklace worth 25 gp, six shining arrows, an emerald grasshopper talisman affixed to a rusted chain shirt, and a serpent dagger.

The ring Ilgrunthin carries is something she found in the inn. It belongs to Aron Mordimus, and if the PCs return it, he sobs in a mix of joy and sadness, explaining his fiancé had given it to him and that they were planning to wed soon—see his side quest on @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.0LOtv52aD44VMt6N#side-quest]{Adventure Toolbox} for more details. Once the PCs hand it over, it vanishes and a ghostly duplicate appears on his ring finger.

Restoration

Once the grindylows are slain or driven off, the phantom of Aron Mordimus manifests here once his soul is rescued from the orchard (area @UUID[.iKQ1sh7QyLC4On4P]{A21}). His presence cleans the establishment, freshens the rooms, and makes itself ready for guests: the PCs!

Reward

Once this location is restored by Aron’s presence, grant the PCs 10 XP. If they return his engagement ring, grant them an additional 20 XP.

Church.name: Church
Church.text:
The interior of this church may have once been soothing, but now it lies in ruins. The many fifteen-foot-high stained glass windows are long broken, leaving only empty frames hinting at the scenes once depicted showing Pharasma or Shelyn attending their duties. The ceiling remains mostly intact, twenty-five-feet high and supported by stone pillars, while three long pews lie in semi-collapsed states. Near the west entrance, a dry holy water font leans against the wall, while a moldy wooden altar stands at the far side of the room. Only vague hints of a once-beautiful mural of Pharasma and Shelyn striding through a graveyard filled with wildflowers remains on the eastern wall beyond the altar.

The villagers of Maiserene, like the Arudoras, worshipped Pharasma and Shelyn even after the lord and lady of the castle turned away from their worship to their own decadent desires and pastimes. Since the curse took Bastardhall, this church has become deconsecrated. Area A9a is a small office where Shirail, the leader of the church, once met with her parishioners, A9b contained the church records (mostly of births and deaths, but also several copies of holy text to Pharasma and Shelyn for loan to locals as needed), and A9c was Shirail’s private quarters. All three of these rooms are in ruins and contain nothing of interest.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Animate Herexens" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to hide the inanimate tiles and reveal their tokens as they attack!

Encounter

Low 5

@UUID[Actor.oNR29GreK0AxLucN]{Herexens x4}

Creatures: Before the curse fell, Shirail was assisted in her duties by four acolytes of Pharasma. When Shirail perished on that awful night, these four acolytes lost their faith and prayed to the unknown-to-them perpetrator of the curse to be saved. Charg ignored them, and when the four were soon thereafter slain by shadowy undead, they became herexens.

The four undead remain here to this day, not so much out of a need to keep a building they once adored safe, but out of a twisted urge to remain within its walls to ensure that none worship here again. The four herexens stand motionless in the church, and have done so for so long that layers of dust and growths of mold and lichen have covered them to such an extent that they look, at first, like filth-encrusted statues.

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} one of these statues and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:16|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check realizes the awful truth, perhaps as a finger twitches or an eye shifts to meet a gaze. During daylight hours, the four herexens remain motionless unless one of them is attacked, at which point all four cast off their filthy shells and roll Perception for initiative. At night, the herexens instead roll Deception for initiative—this is a slightly worse check for them, but they’ll animate soon after the PCs enter rather than waiting to be attacked first. Once a fight begins, the herexens fight until destroyed. They’ll pursue fleeing PCs, but after spending 3 rounds outside of the church or the graveyard, they abandon the chase to return to their positions in the church.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.JIDpUhUHdkYe9Clo]{Reliquary}

If the PCs spend 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the church, with a successful @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check they discover a very well-hidden panel in the stone wall near the floor, directly east of the altar. This panel can be opened easily once the church is restored (see below), but doing so before this point requires a PC to either offer a prayer to Pharasma and succeed at a @Check[religion|dc:25] check, succeed at a @Check[athletics|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check to Force it Open (this damages the reliquary within, but it can be Repaired with a successful @Check[crafting|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Repair.Title|options:action:repair|traits:exploration,manipulate] check and the expenditure of 50 gp of raw materials that can be purchased at the trading post), or by smashing it open with weapons (Hardness 5, 30 HP). Smashing it with weapons destroys the reliquary and increases the difficulty to Repair it to DC 30 (@Check[crafting|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Repair.Title|options:action:repair|traits:exploration,manipulate]) and the cost to do so to 200 gp of raw materials. Within the reliquary is a +1 striking ghost touch silver dagger, a set of healer’s gloves, and a shining symbol.

Restoration

Once the herexens are destroyed, the phantom of Shirail Animender manifests here once her soul is rescued from the corrupted sunset shrine (area @UUID[.NoRsDoZrbNHsWUCD]{A22}). Her presence causes the church to become cleaned and restored, including the repair to all the broken stained glass windows. This also restores the church records in area A9b (which can be used to research the Arudoras as a family, but not as individuals), and causes the font near the entrance to fill with a dose of holy water once per day—Shirail encourages the PCs to gather these doses if they wish.

If the PCs haven’t yet discovered the reliquary, Shirail reveals it to them and encourages them to take the items kept within. If the PCs have already done so, she doesn’t ask for their return but does ask the PCs to repair any damage they did to the reliquary. If the PCs ask her about the topic or if she learns about the vile remnants hidden throughout Bastardhall, she tells the PCs that she can hide one vile remnant in the reliquary at a time, so a PC need not endure the disadvantage of carrying it and to prevent any of the denizens of Bastardhall from finding it and hiding it. As she grows more powerful, she can hide more of these remnants within the reliquary—provided the reliquary is undamaged, of course!

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.tbO0Ti0FI6DfZlgf]{The Arudoras}

Maiserene Church Records: A PC peruses the church records for mentions of the Arudora family as a whole (not individual Arudoras).

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[pharasma-lore|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to efficiently go through the records, @Check[religion|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to be able to navigate the records swiftly, or @Check[perception|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to simply read through the records.

Reward

Once this location is restored by Shirail’s presence, grant the PCs 10 XP.

Graveyard.name: Graveyard
Graveyard.text:
A rusty iron fence runs along the side of the road, the spiky jagged tops of the twelve-foot-high fence promising infection with the merest scratch. Beyond the fence stretches an overgrown graveyard, the paths and most of the gravestones are obscured by four-foot-high spear grass and other weeds.

The door into the graveyard from the church works fine, but the gates from the road are rusted shut and must be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Forced Open} with a @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check. The fence can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climbed} with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check as well. A critical failure at either check indicates that the PC slipped and was scratched or punctured by a fragment of rusty iron fence, taking @Damage[1d4[piercing]|shortLabel] points of piercing damage and exposing them to tetanus.

Tetanus

Disease 1

  • Disease

An infection introduced through open wounds, tetanus can produce stiffness, muscle spasms strong enough to break bones, and ultimately death.

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:14|name:Tetanus|traits:disease]

Onset 10 days

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (1 week)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} and can't speak (1 day)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} with spasms (1 day)

Stage 4 death

Encounter

Moderate 5

@UUID[Actor.DBTbqI9QQRtlJwWh]{Wights x4}

The overgrown graveyard is unsettling but safe to explore during the day. This isn’t the case after dark, when four wights who lurk in shallow graves rise up from the earth with howls of rage soon after anything living intrudes upon their domain. The wights attack immediately and pursue PCs for up to 3 rounds beyond the graveyard’s borders before they give up and return to their graves. If the PCs spend the night in the area between the southern buildings of Maiserene and the walkway at area @UUID[.P8DWUDP9moicwHQC]{A11}, they could attract the wights’ attention, causing the four undead to rise up and attack them in their camp.

During the day, a PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the graveyard and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers one of the wights’ shallow graves and can spend another minute digging it up to expose the undead monster slumbering in the dirt. (After the wights rise up, discovering their shallow graves the next day is automatic.) As long as the sun remains up, a wight remains motionless in its exposed grave, curled in a fetal position, but they aren’t particularly bothered by sunlight, so once an exposed wight takes damage or a PC attempts to interact with them, they rise up to attack. Since the wights only rise up individually like this during the day, this is the best time to clear these undead from the graveyard.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.MhSM5ke7jlOeQAIx]{Wight Belongings}

The second wight grave the PCs investigate contains a dirt-encrusted minor sturdy shield, while the wight from the fourth grave wears 4 silver armbands engraved with images of singing turtles; the armbands are worth 25 gp each.

Rickety Walkway.name: Rickety Walkway
Rickety Walkway.text:
A rickety wooden walkway leads across a lake inlet here. Pilings are regularly spaced along the walkway, and while several of them are adorned with hanging lanterns, none are lit. The castle’s stone foundation drops sheer along the east side of the walkway, but a ten-foot-wide opening near the northern side of this inlet leads underground—wide enough for a skiff or a small barge to enter, although it’s filled with churning green mist.

The entrance that leads under the castle was once used for deliveries of various supplies directly into the dungeon, and while it theoretically would have served as an escape tunnel when the curse descended on Bastardhall, no one was able to use it before they were captured, killed, or worse. Entry deeper into Bastardhall via this route is blocked by the impassable green mist until the PCs unlock the dungeon. Once they do so, the mist clears, and this tunnel leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.mJ7qNpJ3GNVNEVcR]{E1}.

The boardwalk creaks alarmingly if it’s crossed, but is safe to traverse.

Encounter

Moderate 5

@UUID[Actor.F0t6Eogd0KJdboXq]{Bastardhall Rats x2}

Creatures: Bastardhall’s dungeon is infested with immense rats, their mangy hides covered with blisters and pustules, their eyes glowing an unnerving yellow. A pair of these enormous rats have become stranded here after the castle’s most recent visit to Golarion, and they’ve taken up residence in a nest under the northern part of the boardwalk. Unless the PCs attempt to be stealthy when they cross the walkway, the two rats automatically take notice.

One of them quietly slips into the water, eager to attack anyone who falls, while the other one waits for the last PC to step onto the bridge before clambering up the escarpment and onto the bridge to attack. The rats fight to the death.

If these rats still live when the PCs unlock the dungeon, they return to their nest in area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.k9MS0A9QhgJfPA7G]{E2}.

Northern Watch Post.name: Northern Watch Post
Northern Watch Post.text:
The path approaches an open portcullis in the side of a forty-foot-high stone building built into the side of the castle wall. To the north, a cliffside looms forty feet above the lake waters below. Within the building, two balconies overlook the pathway. Between them, a stone ramp leads upward to a closed portcullis in the south, beyond which stretches Bastardhall’s courtyard. This portcullis shimmers with green mist that appears to fill the entire courtyard beyond.

Wheels within the watch post can be used to raise or lower the open portcullis, but the southern, lowered portcullis can only be raised from within Bastardhall. Of course, until the PCs unlock the castle grounds, they won’t be able to enter the castle grounds at all. Once the PCs unlock the castle grounds, a successful @Check[athletics|dc:40] check to lift the portcullis or a successful @Check[acrobatics|dc:30|options:action:squeeze|traits:exploration,move] check by a Small creature to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeeze} between the bars can allow the PCs access to the area beyond—and more importantly, to the nearby mechanism at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1a} that can be used to raise the gate. A spell like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.VlNcjmYyu95vOUe8]{Translocate} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.V8wXOsoejQhe6CyG]{Vapor Form} can also be used to bypass the gate, and shrink can resize a PC to slide through the bars with minimal effort, but the PCs might also find aid in opening the gate if they befriend this area’s occupant.

Encounter

Trivial 5

@UUID[Actor.EW55vYwOpZPT9kRd]{Lucinero}

Creature: While no actual guards stand watch over the area, one creature of note does linger here—a frustrated and frightened (although he’d never admit it) catrina psychopomp named Lucinero. While following up on obscure rumors and minute disturbances in the River of Souls, he did what few catrinas do—he traveled to the world of the living to investigate further. The disturbances he’d sensed were the building energies of Bastardhall; he was there one fateful evening in 4713 when the castle manifested, and sensing the powerful echoes of distraught souls from within, he bravely investigated only to be swiftly overwhelmed by the castle’s defenses. After being wounded by several nightgaunts, he escaped the slavering jaws of the barghest Rembles Worthy (see area @UUID[.HKiy1R40vKOTFV0j]{A17}) by tossing his magical garland of flowers to one side to distract the creature (who was rightfully intrigued by its scent) and then took advantage of the distraction to hide in the ruined farmhouse at area @UUID[.Oz08GUWUIID0kaMb]{A16a}. When he emerged at what he thought was the next sunrise, though, Lucinero discovered to his horror that he’d become trapped: Bastardhall had shifted back to the Ethereal Plane with him inside.

For the next several years, Lucinero did what he could to comfort the lost spirits of the haunted shore, to little success. At times he considered simply leaving and wandering the wilds of the Ethereal Plane in hopes of stumbling upon a way back home, but the sheer vastness of this prospect plus the untenable notion that he’d be leaving behind so many trapped souls to their fates ultimately kept him here. And so Lucinero turned his attention to studying the nature of Bastardhall, doing what he could to learn of the strange place.

When the PCs arrived along with Florin Kindler, Lucinero was distracted by the sight of Florin’s soul being wrenched, screaming, up into the ghostly towers far above and didn’t at first realize that still-living travelers—the PCs—had arrived as well. If the PCs don’t visit this area and encounter Lucinero on their own, the catrina might seek them out as they camp, potentially turning what would otherwise be an ambush into an unexpectedly positive encounter.

Yet Lucinero knows that mortals are often untrustworthy. Unless the PCs are stealthy in their approach, he becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} before they enter this area, and he observes them quietly for a time until they look like they’re about to leave, at which point he casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.i35dpZFI7jZcRoBo]{Illusory Disguise} to appear as a member of an ancestry present in the party. He speaks to them via @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SwUiVavHKMWG7t5K]{Truespeech}, asking who they are and why they’ve come to this cursed place. If the PCs ask about Florin and describe her, Lucinero is visibly startled and admits he saw a tormented soul with her description being pulled into the towers above not long ago.

Effect

@UUID[Item.CiR36rbkhYSbM2BU]{Lucinero's Illusory Disguise}

You can apply the effect linked above to disguise Lucinero as a human!

Before Lucinero fully trusts the PCs, though, he wants to be sure that they’re true to their word and capable. He tells the PCs that he, too, is trapped here, and mentions that it might be good for them to compare their discoveries and pool their resources, but before he’s ready to do so he asks the PCs to perform him a favor—to travel to the mire on the southeast section of this island and retrieve his garland of flowers, taken from him by a “slavering beast” that dwells in the swamp. If the PCs agree, Lucinero awaits their return, but if they don’t agree to help, he interprets this as evidence of their base nature and uncooperative personalities. He reiterates “If you seek my help, you must help me first” before vanishing—either by invisibility or by casting translocate and then hiding elsewhere on the island.

If the PCs attack, he sighs in disappointment before fighting back. If reduced to fewer than 25 Hit Points he translocates 120 feet away to the east, then turns invisible and hides in the farmhouse at area @UUID[.Oz08GUWUIID0kaMb]{A16a} until the next sunrise before returning here. He attacks the PCs again if they return, unless they bring his @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.FeTIulA91s33rExI]{Graverose Garland} and give it to him as a peace offering, in which case he agrees to speak to them. Overall, if attacked, as someone who can cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.FM3SmEW8N1FCRjqt]{Talking Corpse}, Lucinero thinks these untrustworthy mortals might be safer to speak with after they’re dead.

Speaking with Lucinero

If the PCs secure the graverose garland from area @UUID[.HKiy1R40vKOTFV0j]{A17} and return it to Lucinero, he appears before them again in his illusory disguise and thanks them for their kindness. At this point, he agrees to share what he knows with the PCs, but first he reveals to them his true form—a final test. If the PCs attack, he sighs in disappointment and fights back as detailed previously, but if they accept him for what he is, he’s convinced they can be strong allies. He asks the PCs to share with him what they’ve learned of the region in their time here—use this as a chance for the players to put into their own words what they know, and perhaps remind them on things they’ve learned but forgotten. After that, Lucinero shares with the PCs his own theories of what’s going on.

“We’re trapped in a castle adrift in the Ethereal Plane, and without the ability to travel via magic, we’ll stay here until the castle returns to your world... if even it shall. I for one do not wish to wait, but so much of this place is out of phase with the rest. I can sense many more souls trapped within the castle—some unwilling captives, and others willing tormentors—but unless we can force the rest of the castle to manifest for us, we can learn nothing from it. “But there are some souls here, adrift on this haunted shoreline, who exist apart from the castle. I can sense their ancient ties to the land, but they must be rescued. I tried to contact them myself when I first became trapped here, but I could not speak with them. Something in the nature of their condition sets them apart from me, yet you, as living mortals with souls of your own... I believe you can aid these forlorn souls in ways I cannot. This should be your primary task—to seek these six out and save them from their fates.”

If the PCs have already rescued one or more of the trapped leaders of Maiserene, Lucinero congratulates them and notes, “I knew my hunch to trust you was the right one.” He can give the PCs directions to all six of the lost spirits, noting that they seem to be trapped in “the small islet to the north, within the scarecrow in the farm fields to the east, below the statue looming above the eastern watch post, within the building on the island’s southeast corner, in the southern orchard, and at the old shrine near the wall to the southwest.” Asked for further information, he sadly shrugs, saying that he’s only attempted to aid one of the souls—the one trapped in the scarecrow—only to fail in his attempt to speak to the soul he sensed trapped within. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:23|name:PF2E.Actions.SenseMotive.Title|options:action:sense-motive|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1xRFPTFtWtGJ9ELw]{Sense Motive} can discern the likely truth—despite his supernatural nature, Lucinero has been traumatized by his experiences here and fears risking further investigation on his own.

His initial attitude after the PCs return the graverose garland is friendly, but if the PCs ask him to accompany them on their adventures to aid them, he demurs and claims that “my powers have little hold in this place.” If the PCs can make him helpful by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Making an Impression} with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.MakeAnImpression.Title|options:action:make-an-impression|traits:auditory,concentrate,exploration,linguistic,mental] check, or once the PCs prove themselves again by rescuing at least three of the trapped souls, Lucinero finds his bravery and agrees to accompany them. In a fight, he begins combat by attempting to Compel Condemned, then resorts to his fists if that tactic doesn’t work. He generally suppresses his Calming Presence aura so as to not inconvenience the PCs (he’ll activate it if they ask, though). Lucinero is a potent ally for the PCs, and the monsters and foes they’ll fight should recognize this—they should focus much of their fury on the psychopomp as a result. If he’s slain, Lucinero cries out in anguish before his bones clatter to the ground, lifeless.

If he survives long enough, once the PCs unlock the castle grounds, Lucinero can translocate past the portcullis in the south of area A12 and easily raise the gate using the winch at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1a}. He increasingly balks at accompanying the PCs into the castle interior and would instead much rather settle in to the graveyard at area @UUID[.IUvLkR8jgiDvCOUo]{A10} (and may recruit the PCs to help slay the wights there if they haven’t done so already).

The PCs can also spend some time speaking to Lucinero to research topics about Bastardhall, as detailed below.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.PAMDhjQNkAm8rB5R]{Bastardhall}

Lucinero’s Bastardhall Observations: A PC speaks to Lucinero about what he’s learned about Bastardhall.

Maximum RP 2; Research Checks @Check[architecture-lore|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to help contextualize some of his observations, @Check[society|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to help Lucinero organize his thoughts, or @Check[perception|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to listen carefully to what he says and have your own epiphanies about Bastardhall.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.UUqGlDCzpRnwqovv]{The Bastardhall Curse}

Lucinero’s Curse Theories: A PC works with Lucinero to develop, troubleshoot, and refine his theories about the curse.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[religion|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to explore the spiritual nature of the curse, @Check[occultism|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to bring knowledge of occult magic to the conversation, or @Check[diplomacy|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to guide Lucinero’s own thoughts into new revelations.

Treasure

Once the PCs rescue all six of the souls, Lucinero is impressed enough that he gifts the party his @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.FeTIulA91s33rExI]{Graverose Garland} in appreciation for their efforts to aid the dead when he could not.

Reward

Grant the PCs XP as if they’d defeated him in combat if they manage to become allies with Lucinero by returning his garland.

Ruined Bridge.name: Ruined Bridge
Ruined Bridge.text:
Rows of soggy, leaning pilings are all that remains of what was once perhaps a bridge that connected the main island to the smaller, forested islet to the northwest. On the far isle, an overgrown trail winds up into the trees and out of sight.

The water between the pilings—what was originally under the bridge that existed here long ago, is only 3 feet deep. A Small creature must @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim} to cross here (@Check[athletics|dc:10|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] during this chapter), but a Medium creature can wade, treating the water as greater difficult terrain.

The first time the PCs pass this point, have them all attempt a @Check[perception] check. Whoever rolls the highest notices what appears to be the light of a single handheld lantern glowing deep in the woods on the islet to the northwest, as if someone were carrying a lantern while they went about some sort of business in the trees. During the day, the check might instead notice the sound of soft singing from the woods. In either case, this is a trick; the will-o’-wisp on the island is attempting to lure prey in among the old standing stones (area @UUID[.Ez53diEo41YhLat7]{A14}).

Standing Stones.name: Standing Stones
Standing Stones.text:
A narrow path through the thick tangles of berry bushes and looming trees reaches a barren clearing in the woods, in which five twelve-foot-tall stone menhirs protrude from the muddy earth. Between each of these standing stones sits a smaller three-foot-tall boulder. All the stones are encrusted with swaths of moist fungus that mostly, but not entirely, obscures the twisting runes carved into the stone’s inward-facing sides.

These standing stones predate Bastardhall, raised thousands of years before the castle’s construction by the indigenous Kellids who dwelled in the region. The stones themselves were erected on a site of power, and the runes helped to focus the minds of those who spent time meditating within so that they could emerge rejuvenated, focused, and ready to tackle any complicated task they might face.

Eventually, those Kellids moved on, and the site was left unattended for many centuries until a clan of qlippoth-worshipping cultists discovered the stones and attempted to use them to open a portal to the Outer Rifts. These cultists’ defeat was one of several acts of heroism Eragayl Arudora performed that led up to the county gifting him this island for his home, but once Eragayl’s influence over his family waned and his descendants lost interest in the old ways, the corruption those cultists once imbued in the stones slowly returned.

Encounter

Moderate 5

@UUID[Actor.YhVYGhzNrOFQROui]{Cythnigots x2} @UUID[Actor.L3vRwN2JcJVk88Ij]{Esmira Vermidian}

Creatures: Ironically, the Bastardhall Curse overwhelmed the qlippoth corruption with its own, but not before a small amount of supernatural spores leaked through. These spores infested a pair of squirrels, as well as the stones themselves. The fungus growing on the stones is unpleasant but ultimately harmless, while the fungus growing inside the squirrels transformed them into cythnigots.

The sight of a flickering light and the sound of muffled singing are likely to draw the PCs to this area first: they’re produced by Esmira, a will-o’-wisp who was once Maiserene’s tutor.

After her death, her soul was caught up by the Bastardhall Curse and she was reincarnated as a will-o’-wisp. The latent fear that infuses all of Bastardhall is not only enough to keep her sustained but has granted her an exceptionally long life as well. For a time, she wandered the haunted shore freely, but by the end of the first century she settled here. It was her favorite place to relax in her previous life, and now she enjoys it for the slow leak of negative emotions the fungus-encrusted stones provide.

Once Esmira realizes intruders are near, she does her best to lure them closer, hoping they’ll stumble into the standing stones. She Goes Dark and silent before the PCs catch their first sight of the stones. The two cythnigots lurk amid the fungal growths within, and lurch up to attack as soon as any PC steps into the ring of stones, rolling Stealth for initiative. Esmira does as well, but the only actions she takes in combat initially is to invisibly drift, waiting for one of the PCs to become affected by a cythnigot’s sickening display. Once they do so, Esmira glides to a position in range to Feed on Fear from that PC, whereupon she becomes visible. While she retains the skull-like appearance of most will-o’-wisps, Esmira’s glow extends outward to create a spectral “shell,” making her appear as a skull-faced ghost of a woman dressed in scholar’s robes.

The cythnigots fight to the death and do not pursue the PCs beyond the islet’s shores. Esmira also fights to the death, and she’ll chase the PCs down throughout the haunted shore until the schoolhouse (area @UUID[.nnYID8EKpPF0zOoR]{A4}) becomes visible to her. At this point, she comes up short, gasps in shock, and flees back here to lurk. Left alive, with the knowledge that the PCs are still out there, she continues to try to ambush them every time they camp in an unsafe area along the haunted shore.

Once the will-o’-wisp is slain, the creature’s skull fades away, but its ghostly body remains—its face now transformed into that of a middle-aged human woman with an expression of overwhelming relief and thanks.

The figure curtsies gracefully before the PCs, then makes its way at a fly Speed of 25 to the schoolhouse (area @UUID[.nnYID8EKpPF0zOoR]{A4}). Once she reaches the schoolhouse, Esmira’s presence there restores the place, and she can speak to the PCs. See her entry in @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.M6cCO4Hg8Hj8yTBY]{Adventure Toolbox} for information on how she can support the PCs.

Treasure

The berries that grow in profusion on this islet are plentiful, delicious, and nutritious. Once the islet’s dangerous creatures are dealt with, a PC can gather food here by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.49y9Ec4bDii8pcD3]{Subsisting} with a successful @Check[survival|dc:10|name:PF2E.Actions.Subsist.Title|options:action:subsist|traits:downtime] check. The party can attempt such checks here up to five times before the berries worth harvesting are depleted.

A PC who examine the runes on the standing stones and can read Hallit can spend 10 minutes studying the ancient writing to realize the standing stones’ purpose by succeeding at a @Check[occultism|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.DecipherWriting.Title|options:action:decipher-writing|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.d9gbpiQjChYDYA2L]{Decipher the Writing} of the archaic runes. This becomes a @Check[occultism|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.DecipherWriting.Title|options:action:decipher-writing|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check if the PCs first spend an hour cleaning the stones of the fungus clinging to it. Once a PC comprehends the purpose of these meditative stones and explains this to other PCs, any PC can take advantage of the stones to perform the following activity.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Clean Standing Stones" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager clean the fungi off the standing stones!

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.j6MnMZ8ADhhEiUTA]{Meditate Among the Stones}

  • Concentrate

  • Exploration

@Embed[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.j6MnMZ8ADhhEiUTA inline]

Farm.name: Farm
Farm.text:
Overgrown farm plots sprawl across this flat, unforested portion of the island. While these small fields were once used to support the village with potatoes, wheat, rye, and oats, today, these crops fight for dominance against tangles of weeds and shrubbery. The collapsed ruins of a farmhouse lie closer to the castle foundation to the west on the opposite side of the road from the overgrown fields. A lone scarecrow hangs askew from a leaning wooden pole in the center of the fields, casting a long shadow.

The farmhouse ruins (area A16a) are difficult terrain. A PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} here uncovers three skeletons—the remains of the farmhouse matron and her two adult children.

Encounter

Moderate 5

@UUID[Actor.vRAdYovWcy2euwuL]{Snapping Flytraps x2} @UUID[Actor.B597QiPcxXkMejnz]{Elite Scarecrow}

Creature: The fields are a different story. These overgrown fields also function as difficult terrain if one steps off the less-overgrown pathways that run between them. The scarecrow’s pole is located at the point on the map labeled A16b.

This is no mere set of farmer’s clothing stuffed with straw and topped with a burlap sack—this is an elite scarecrow animated by the trapped soul of Maiserene’s trader, Banijer Greely. When he died on the night the curse took the castle, his soul was snatched by Charg and redirected into the scarecrow that stood in the midst of the farm he and his family once tended. Banijer then had to watch helpless from within the scarecrow as the animated monster leapt off its pole and made straight for the farmhouse where his family was still huddling within. The scarecrow made short work of Banijer’s family, and it was a mercy that his soul “blacked out” as it happened. The scarecrow returned to its perch, but not before it buried some of the remains below it, as one might plant a seed.

Since that moment, Banijer’s consciousness has remained in its void, unknowing and unfeeling, but it still provides an animating force for the scarecrow. The creature waits patiently if the PCs approach, maintaining its mundane appearance. Once the PCs come within 20 feet of the scarecrow, other dangers make themselves apparent—a pair of snapping flytraps lurch out of the undergrowth to attack. These carnivorous plants are fueled by Charg’s influence and hunger for flesh—both fight to the death. The scarecrow waits for 1 round before leaping off its perch to join the fight. All three creatures fight until destroyed. The flytraps pursue foes until there’s none visible within 50 feet before returning to the fields, but the scarecrow is relentless. Only if it comes within sight of the trading post (area @UUID[.dTtF0ayazcyuCKJ1]{A5}) does it balk before fleeing back to the safety of its pole.

When the scarecrow is destroyed, the clothes, sack, and straw collapse in a pile. Standing in its place is a ghostly human figure of a handsome man. He drops to his knees, cries out in anguish, and then moves flies with a Speed of 25 feet to the collapsed farmhouse and frantically begins searching for the remains of his family. There, he ineffectually attempts to uncover them, but his incorporeal nature prevents him from doing so. If the PCs spend 10 minutes clearing the rubble and exposing the bones, Banijer’s soul drops to his knees before the remains, sobbing for a few moments before he rises, a look of determination on his face, and flies off to return to the trading post. Once he arrives, Banijer’s presence there restores the store, and he can speak to the PCs. See his entry on @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.UTLSqT61vU6a2H9C]{Adventure Toolbox} for information on how he can support the PCs

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Animate Scarecrow" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to hide the inanimate scarecrow tile and reveal its token as it comes to life!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.jGmSIkgjUA9MPA5i]{Buried Remnant}

The “seed” of defiled human remains the scarecrow buried in the field beneath his perch has, over the centuries, grown into a dormant @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.iQLEbANowf4fT8hK]{vile remnant}. The remnant lies buried a foot under the topsoil near the scarecrow’s pole. A PC who Searches the area and succeeds at a @Check[survival|dc:30] check or a @Check[perception|dc:33] check notes a faint disturbance in the soil that suggests something is buried there. A PC who digs into the soil finds the vile remnant after 1 minute of digging.

The Mire.name: The Mire
The Mire.text:
The road hugs close to the looming castle foundation here, for to the east a thirty-foot-high precipice drops down into a tangled mire of willow trees, brambles, and thick plumes of tall spear grass. What appears to be a collapsed shack is just visible near the heart of the swampy morass, yet no trail or boardwalk leads out to it.

The escarpment down to this mire can be climbed by a PC who succeeds at a @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check. The mire itself is muddy and thickly overgrown, with about a foot of standing water over the mud itself. The entire area functions as greater difficult terrain.

The collapsed shack in the swamp was once the home of a curious old man named Rembles Worthy, who was employed by the Arudoras to live on the island as a hermit—a practice still observed in some places among the elite and wealthy of Ustalav.

Encounter

Low 5

@UUID[Actor.Gva6GAH3WjjRi8Wd]{Rembles Worthy}

Creature: Rembles huddled inside of his shack the night things went bad, and while no monsters found him that night, the curse nevertheless did. Charg’s influence transformed the novelty hermit into a slavering creature—a barghest—and allowed Rembles to retain just enough of his memories and personality so that he could focus on the rage and humiliation he sometimes felt toward the Arudoras. While the pay was good, life as a novelty hermit, as someone for the Arudoras to show off to their visitors, felt unfulfilling at times, and after his transformation, these momentary moments of dissatisfaction have bloomed into a monstrous fury to match his new life.

As a barghest, Rembles often wanders the haunted shore, taking delight in how far the once-proud family has fallen or bullying and tormenting the pack of wolves who live in the orchard (area @UUID[.iKQ1sh7QyLC4On4P]{A21}). A relatively recent fight with the psychopomp Lucinero was a welcome new distraction, and Rembles has grown quite fond of the treasure he stole from him—a graverose garland whose scent allows Rembles to, now and then, remember simpler times filled with easy comforts of life as a hermit. Invariably, these memories overwhelm the barghest, causing him to seek out wolves to bully or simply sending him racing around the haunted shore.

When the PCs first come near this area, the mournful sound of Rembles’ howl echoes up from the swamp below. A successful @Check[perception|dc:22] check allows the PCs to spot the intimidating hound-like beast howling amid the ruins of the shack near a garland of black roses draped over a fallen timber. Once he notices the PCs, Rembles howls again, but this time the sound is filled with anger as he charges out of the swamp to attack them. Rembles fights until reduced to below 20 HP, at which point he casts invisibility and tries to flee. If the PCs flee he lets them run, marking them for later torment. At some point thereafter, whether he or the PCs fled, he uses Change Shape to appear as the bedraggled man he was in life, seeks the PCs out, and attempts to lure them into a trap—to be torn apart by the wolves in the orchard if they still live or perhaps over to the twigjack nest at area @UUID[.Mr8Gsi42znsNq3XB]{A23}. Once a fight begins, Rembles resumes his true form to join in the battle, this time fighting to the death.

Once Rembles is slain, his barghest body collapses, but his human spiritual form rises up. He silently smiles at the PCs in thanks then drifts back to his ruined shack. He passes a hand over the remnants of his fireplace, causing the stone hiding his old belongings to glow until the PCs move it. Then he fades away, his soul finally released to the afterlife.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.rLKn4ZUCEJIrhyqm]{Fallen Timber} @UUID[Actor.W5VRTXbZTrP6yc6H]{Shack Cache}

The garland of flowers draped over the timber that’s intrigued Rembles is the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.5c7sZCKtujF0U6wg]{graverose garland} he stole from Lucinero (area @UUID[.FuifNpUpaAG0LzlR]{A12}).

A PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} Rembles’ collapsed shack and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers a hidden cache behind a false stone on the side of the fireplace that still stands amid the ruins. If Rembles has been slain and he’s touched this stone, a PC automatically notices the hidden cache if they Seek in the area. Behind the stone are three ancient leather pouches, crumbling with age. One of them contains Rembles’ life savings of 67 gp. The second contains a moderate healing potion and two potions of water breathing. The final pouch contains the one item Rembles brought with him from his previous life as a barrister in Caliphas: a diplomat’s badge.

Eastern Watch Post.name: Eastern Watch Post
Eastern Watch Post.text:
The heavy reinforced wood double doors on the eastern wall of this watch post stands ajar, but the rusty hinges squeal loudly if they’re opened. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the doors and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check notes the rusty hinges; opening the doors slowly as a three-action activity allows them to be opened without making sound.

This thirty-five-foot-square room features a stone flight of spiral stairs at its center, leading thirty feet up through the ceiling above. To the north and south stand a pair of weapon racks on which ruined bows and swords hang, although one of the bows in the southwestern-most rack appears to be in fine condition. Twin statues of a handsome human man dressed in armor and carrying a sword stand to the west to either side of a second set of double doors in the westernmost wall. Four rusty glaives and equally rusty scattered suits of disarticulated plate mail, perhaps from as many as four suits, lie strewn over the floor.

The spiral staircase leads up into the grand statue of Eragayl Arudora above, but at the point where the stairs lead through the ceiling, impassable green mist blocks the way. The doors to the west open into an archway filled with similar impassible mist. Once the PCs unlock the reception halls, the mists in the western double doors clear and lead to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.78A34DGpyfbsAqFq]{D7f}. To unlock the stairs, the PCs must unlock the castle grounds, at which point they can ascend the stairs to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.hqbneLnZW6Vn6LLx]{B2d} above.

Encounter

Low 5

@UUID[Actor.v83koNIO6mZA3cL5]{Wrathful Armor x4}

Creatures: The scattered rusty mess on the floor consists of four dormant suits of animated armor. As long as the PCs @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.VMozDqMMuK5kpoX4]{Sneak} through this room with a successful @Check[stealth|dc:16|name:PF2E.Actions.Sneak.Title|options:action:stealth|traits:move,secret] check, the armor remains quiet, but as soon as a character makes any noise in this room (including the loud squealing of rusty hinges from the eastern doors), the fragmented pieces of armor suddenly shimmer with prismatic radiance. A moment later, they reconstitute into full suits, each clutching a glaive, and immediately attack.

Each of these suits of armor is animated by another lost soul—this time, that of Maiserene’s sheriff, Ausken Dast. As the PCs fight the armor, they’ll periodically catch glimpses of a human man’s ghostly face within the open helmets of the animated armor—a face twisted in grief and horror. Ausken perished in the defense of Maiserene long ago, and when he did, Charg saw to it that his soul was split into four portions to animate the ceremonial suits of armor that once stood on display in this room. He can do nothing but watch as the suits of armor his soul animates does their best to destroy the PCs. The suits of armor pursue the PCs relentlessly from this area once they animate, but any suit that comes in sight of the western watch post (area @UUID[.1m1bEKrAzlrKvJxc]{A3}) freezes a moment, then flees back here, crumbling apart to its individual pieces once again upon returning.

Note that the rusty glaives might inflict tetanus on PCs struck by them. Furthermore, each time a suit of armor is destroyed, Ausken’s soul abandons it and bolsters the remaining animated suits. Once the final suit of animated armor is destroyed, it collapses into its individual parts, leaving behind the ghostly figure of Ausken in its place. He appears to be breathing heavily but then salutes the PCs and takes off toward the western watch post (area @UUID[.1m1bEKrAzlrKvJxc]{A3}) at a fly Speed of 25 feet. Once he reaches the watch post, his presence there restores the place, and he can speak to the PCs. See his entry in @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.5oJGMvwqnrQybliF]{Adventure Toolbox} for information on how he can support the PCs.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.0NlelVhWI8hNYWuB]{Weapon Rack}

While the remnants left behind from the destroyed suits of animated plate mail are without value, the bow in the southwestern rack is a +1 striking longbow.

Dawn's Watch.name: Dawn's Watch
Dawn's Watch.text:
The double doors on the western wall of this large observation plaza are sealed tight during daylight hours, with shimmering ripples of darkness seething along the gaps and locks. A PC can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} these doors with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock} with three consecutive successful @Check[thievery|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks. After dark, this barrier fades, and the double doors crack open to hang ajar and can be opened with ease. The balconies on the other three walls look out over the shoreline 30 feet below; a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check is required to climb the walls from below up to these alternate entrances.

A set of four stone pillars rise up to support the forty-foot ceiling of this large structure. The western entrance sits at a height of thirty feet above the floor, with stairwells descending to the ground to either side. Wooden viewing decks look out to the north, south, and east from the inner balcony level. Down below is a large, empty stone bath, its inner surface dull with dried algae.

This location was used as a place to relax in the scented waters of a bath while watching the sun rise over the eastern edge of the lake. Before the curse, the tub here was enchanted to refill, purify, scent, and heat the water within with magic that helped quicken recovery from illness. Instead of simply running dry, the bath has become a dangerous haunt.

Encounter

Low 5

@UUID[Actor.nauKeeLKERwPZNDI]{Bring Dusk to Dawn} @UUID[Actor.56C6i1KxNU1plrQN]{Shadow (Minion)}

Hazard: Originally intended as a retreat for everyone who lived on Arudora Isle, when the curse fell upon the castle, Dawn’s Watch was mostly used by the villagers of Maiserene—the occupants of the castle had fancier places to relax, after all. Of all the villagers, none enjoyed baths here more than Ilana Greenbough, Maiserene’s resident artisan. To her, a sunrise soak in the bath was the best way to find inspiration for the day’s projects.

When she was killed the night the curse fell, Charg sent her soul here to fuel a cruel haunt meant to shroud the interior of the bath house with shadow so that even the illusory sun of the imprisoned castle could never shine within.

The umbral haunt that Ilana’s soul powers is the source of the shadows that, when night falls, seek out any who sleep in unsafe parts of the haunted shore, but at Dawn’s Watch the haunt itself is much more dangerous. Once the PCs disable or destroy the shadowy haunt, though, the darkness fades and the waters of the bath magically refill. A ghostly phantasmal halfling woman rises up from the waters and gives a grateful sigh and thankful nod to the PCs before she flies off at a Speed of 25 feet to the workshop (area @UUID[.XdkSCjX3BA3dp5sE]{A6}). Once she arrives, her presence there restores the place, and she can speak to the PCs. See her entry in @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.ckjkw2MuZPwvb7z1]{Adventure Toolbox} for information on how she can support the PCs.

Treasure

Once the haunt is destroyed and Ilana’s soul freed, the bath itself refills with water. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[arcana|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[occultism|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], or @Check[religion|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic} understands how to take advantage of the bath.

By stepping into the waters and spending an hour relaxing in the bath, the PC can immediately attempt saving throws against any ongoing disease they’re currently suffering from in an attempt to reduce the stage or recover. The result of this saving throw can’t increase a disease’s stage. If the time the PCs spends during the soak includes sunrise, they additionally become inspired for the remainder of the day and gain a +1 item bonus to all Crafting checks made to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.rmwa3OyhTZ2i2AHl]{Craft}. Up to four Small or Medium creatures or one Large creature can use the bath at a time, and once they do so, the creature can’t benefit from the bath’s magic again for a week.

Effect

@UUID[Item.Y2ix3ISFWBhXLsE0]{Crafting Inspiration}

Use this effect to automate the PC's item bonus to Crafting checks made to Craft.

Southern Watch Post.name: Southern Watch Post
Southern Watch Post.text:
This large rectangular chamber has a thirty-foot high ceiling. Along the southern wall is a long wooden shelf which contains several ancient cloaks, fishing supplies, and boots. To the north, a single statue of a man holding up a longsword faces double doors to the north. The tip of his sword nearly touches the ceiling above and twin flights of stairs lead up in the middle of the room. Doors stand in all the corners of the room; those to the south are double doors, while those to the north are smaller, typical doors. Plaques bearing short messages adorn the northern doors. A human skeleton, still wearing a chain, lies slumped at the statue’s southern base, a wrinkled parchment clutched in one bony hand and its skull sitting in its lap.

Impassable green mist blocks the way up both flights of stairs and through the doors to the north once they’re opened. When the PCs unlock the castle grounds, this mist clears from the stairs and the doors to the northeast and northwest. The stairs lead up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.jJMjmV5oA7dfQfjN]{B2e}. The northwest door’s plaque bears the message, “Shrine,” and leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1k}, while the northeast door’s plaque bears the message, “Maze” and leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1m}.

The green mist fades from within the northern double doors once the PCs unlock the reception halls,and provide access to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.3hduGPZ55keA2HRA]{D15c}.

The statue is of Eragayl Arudora. A plaque at its feet on the north side reads, “Eragayl Blesses Our Castle.”

The dead soldier was a mid-ranking castle guard who fled here during the night of the curse, abandoning his command. As he listened to the death and destruction all around him, he quickly wrote a letter confessing his cowardice. He didn’t finish it, and the wound that ended his life remains obvious—his head lies in his lap, still adorned by its helm. The letter’s contents are short and read as follows before ending mid-sentence in a death scrawl.

“It happened so fast. Lord Raudltz sent riders out, but I hear not for help. The Arudoras have brought this on us, and I will not give my life to save them from this doom. I will wait for dawn and—”

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.mwDK30jwwmRn32H0]{Fallen Soldier}

The chain shirt the hapless soldier wears is a +1 chain shirt that has a shark tooth charm talisman affixed to it.

Orchard.name: Orchard
Orchard.text:
The steep hillside slopes away from the castle foundation here. While this hillside may have once been a well- cultivated orchard of apple and pear trees, today it’s an overgrown forest in which the once-orderly fruit trees grow randomly. What appear to be narrow animal trails crisscross the hillside.

A PC who moves into this steeply slowed terrain has two options—they can treat it as difficult terrain, or they can move at full speed. If they opt to move at full speed, they must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:20|options:inflicts:prone] save or slip and fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. On a critical failure, they roll down the hill until they splash into the water, taking @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]] damage from the descent (@Check[reflex|dc:20|basic] save). While the rickety wooden pier at area A21a is solid, the nearby boathouse shimmers as if it were a ghostly phantasm (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.SORum03a5tQWw4Xp]{D31}). Once the PCs unlock the reception halls in @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi]{Chapter 4}, the boathouse solidifies and can be explored.

Encounter

Low 5

@UUID[Actor.BN5Lb6IsQ9Wyu3rL]{Wolves x6}

Creatures: The Arudoras kept deer stocked on the island, and allowed the villagers of Maiserene to hunt them one at a time on certain days of the year. When the curse swept over the land, these deer were transformed into ravenous wolves, many of whom tore each other apart. The six who survive are lean and constantly hungry—but they have a singularly awful source of food.

Every day, the soul of Maiserene’s hapless innkeeper manifests as a living dwarf here, only for the wolves to eat him alive. This hapless doomed man is Aron Mordimus, and in life he often came to the orchard here to gather apples to prepare fillings for his pies and pastries. In death, his soul was lured here by a false promise of safety, and now, every day, he’s consumed.

When the PCs arrive, the six wolves are in the process of tearing into Aron for their daily meal, ripping out entrails and barking and snarling at each other as they bicker. While these six wolves are physically typical of their species, they’re quite atypical in their behavior. As soon as they notice the PCs, they attack, eager to add new flavors to their meal. The wolves fight to the death—each time one dies, it howls in rage as its spirit is drawn up and out of its physical body, then down into the ground where they’ll join the wolf spirits who serve the werewolf Dazerien down in Bastardhall’s dungeon.

Once all six wolves are slain, Aron’s mangled body suddenly gasps for breath, horrifically alive for one final moment before expiring from his grisly wounds. A moment later, his spirit rises up from his remains with a relieved sigh. He glances at the PCs, smiles broadly, and gives them a friendly wave. He flies at a Speed of 25 feet, returning to the inn he ran while he lived—Orm’s Rest (area @UUID[.msh8hhX94bXBPpbi]{A8}). Once he arrives there, his presence there restores the place, and he can speak to the PCs. See his entry in @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.0LOtv52aD44VMt6N]{Adventure Toolbox} for information on how he can support the PCs.

Treasure

The apples that grow on the trees are large and filling. Once the wolves are dealt with, a PC can gather food here by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.49y9Ec4bDii8pcD3]{Subsisting} with a @Check[survival|dc:10|name:PF2E.Actions.Subsist.Title|options:action:subsist|traits:downtime] check. The party can attempt these checks here up to five times before the apples worth harvesting are depleted.

Aron’s body swiftly melts away into the soil—this was never a real body but merely a shell that existed as a means to torment his soul. Strangely, his +1 striking clan dagger remains behind where he died; if the PCs offer it to Aron, he’ll suggest they bring it to Ausken once the sheriff is back so he can transfer the clan dagger’s runes to PC weaponry. Aron doesn’t need these runes, after all—it’s just the clan dagger itself that’s important to him, and even then, just as a memento of his adoptive human father.

Sunset Shrine.name: Sunset Shrine
Sunset Shrine.text:
The interior of this fifty-five-foot-long, twenty-five-foot-wide building is in ruins. Once an elegant and beautiful shrine, the stained glass windows have all been shattered, and years of being exposed to the elements have left mold, windblown leaves, and unusually large mounds of bat guano all over the floor. Three benches, each wide enough to accommodate a pair of worshippers, face a small pulpit to the west near which a ruined wooden altar sits. To the east, a set of partially collapsed wooden steps lead up to a landing and a door in the wall. The southern wall may have once graced the shrine with a twenty-foot-long mural depicting a beautiful, pastoral landscape, but today its colors are all but washed away by water damage and mold, leaving only hints as to its original beauty.

Originally, the residents of Arudora Castle and Maiserene worshipped Pharasma and Shelyn. The church to the north was devoted to Pharasma, the village’s primary patron, but this shrine existed for those who worshipped Shelyn to show their devotion. Time has not been kind to the shrine, though, and a PC who looks through the area must make a @Check[religion|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} to realize this place was once devoted to the goddess of love and art.

The steps leading up to the door to the west, as well as the platform, are made of wood and immediately collapse under any attempt to climb them. They’re only 5 feet above the ground, though, and a PC takes no damage and must only succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:20|options:inflicts:prone] save to avoid landing @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} after the short fall. Beyond the door is a much more stable stone-and-wood stairwell that ascends the side of the castle foundation, switching back on itself a few times and leading all the way up to a closed door at the base of the castle wall some 60 feet above. This sturdy door is locked—it can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Forced Open} with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check or unlocked with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}, or it can be opened with the key hidden in the altar (see Treasure below). Of course, even if it’s opened, impassable green mist bars further entry. Once the PCs unlock the fallen temple in @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk]{Chapter 7}, the mist vanishes and they can proceed into area @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1g}.

Encounter

Moderate 5

@UUID[Actor.xnpuGO8jEMba9wy5]{Giant Bats x3} @UUID[Actor.iICvyvPzfyJe4vzk]{Cockroach Swarm} @UUID[Actor.JNU54O7l5O6lWPNJ]{Cursed Mural}

Creatures: This shrine is the home of a trio of giant bats, but they’re not encountered here if the PCs visit during the night. During the night, the bats abandon the rafters 20 feet above to squeeze out through the broken windows to hunt in the skies above Bastardhall. The PCs can watch the giant bats emerge and return every dawn and dusk.

While out hunting, the bats don’t attack creatures on the ground below—their favorite meals consist of the sahkil imps that flop and flap around up above.

A swarm of cockroaches dwells here as well, coprophages whose insatiable hunger help to keep the guano from building up too much in the shrine. The swarm’s appetites are adaptable, and they immediately surge out of their nest under the rickety stairs to attack PCs when they enter, regardless of time of day. During the day, the three bats nesting above join the fight. While the cockroaches fight to the death, the bats do not—they flee the shrine if reduced to fewer than 10 HP, returning the next sunrise.

Hazard: Bats and bugs aren’t the only danger present in this chamber. The mural to the south has not only been defaced by neglect and exposure, but by Charg’s cruelty. When Maiserene’s resident priestess, @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.OoslGgDkvU7MPY5k]{Shirail Animender}, perished in her attempt to keep the church safe, Charg seized her soul and embedded it in what was once a glorious mural depicting Shelyn playing a harp for a vast audience of animals, fey, and humanoids. When Shirail’s soul became trapped in the mural, the Bastardhall Curse drew upon the more frightening and unsettling aspects of Pharasma’s faith as goddess of death, resulting in a blasphemy that’s been waiting centuries for victims.

Once the PCs disable or destroy the cursed mural, the mural’s colors suddenly bloom, and the grime falls away as the entire thing is miraculously restored over the course of a single round—even if the PCs stopped the haunt by destroying the mural. Immediately thereafter, one of the images in the mural of an elven woman enjoying Shelyn’s performance, steps out of the mural to become a phantasmal manifestation—Shirail herself. Tears of gratitude streaming down her cheeks, she bows in thanks to the PCs before flying off at a Speed of 25 feet to the church (area @UUID[.oQOmNJ7YInR10ecC]{A9}); once she reaches the church, her presence there restores the place, and she can speak to the PCs. See her entry in @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.OoslGgDkvU7MPY5k]{Adventure Toolbox} for information on how she can further support the PCs.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.npo6c9ZoFRKxCcKf]{Hidden Panel}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} around the altar and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers a hidden panel near the base. Within sits a rusty iron key that can open the door at the top of the stairs behind the shrine described earlier in this page, a leather scroll tube containing a scroll of holy light and a scroll of heal (3rd-rank), and a wand of cleanse affliction (3rd-rank).

Brambleheart.name: Brambleheart
Brambleheart.text:
A thick tangle of thorny vines grow in profusion on this peninsular extension from the main island. The southern land approach is barely above the water level and thick with mud and reeds, while from the east bank, a wooden walkway extends out to connect to the longer boardwalk. A ghostly thirty-foot-wide tower rises to a tapered height of over two-hundred feet from the center of the brambles, the tower’s pointed top rising higher than the castle walls above. Dozens of hand-sized fetishes hang from twines throughout the brambles.

The southern approach through the mud is difficult terrain, while the thick brambles growing throughout this area are both greater difficult terrain and hazardous terrain that deals @Damage[1d6[piercing]] damage. The brambles themselves seem almost to twist and clutch at anyone attempting to move through them, save for the twigjacks who nest within—they can move through the brambles safely and with ease as the thorny plants part for their passage. The brambles themselves are moist and clammy, and have resistance 5 to fire—they’re difficult to burn away.

The ghostly tower itself was known as Eragayl’s Spire and served as both a watch post and, during storms, an impromptu lighthouse to help warn lake travelers of the island’s presence and the surrounding shallow waters. The entire spire is out of phase at this time, but once the PCs unlock the dungeon in @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ]{Chapter 5}, the tower becomes solid and can be explored, with its four doors leading to area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.AsVGoGtlVEkWPNv4]{E16}. A PC who Investigates the waters surrounding this spit of land finds submerged pilings and ruined piers that once extended from here, providing a place for visitors to dock their boats (usually people traveling to Maiserene, delivering supplies, or those who didn’t have permission to approach via the Laroba Causeway above).

A PC who studies one of the fetishes might at first think they’re crude images of a wagon wheel. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:20] check realizes they symbolize something else, that the placement of colorful red stones suggests not a wagon wheel but an execution wheel used to rack and torture heretics and heathens in some faiths. However, they learn nothing more. A critical success at this Religion check is enough to identify the crude fetishes as being variants on the religious symbol of the sahkil tormentor, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.kKdvt2m8MdsJ5aFb]{Charg}, and that the “wheel” is intended to depict a wall through which monstrous red eyes peer.

Encounter

Moderate 5

@UUID[Actor.9sGgANyNFCKnu06t]{Twigjacks x4}

Creatures: The source of the creepy fetishes in the brambles are a clutch of four twigjacks who dwell within. Before the curse, these four constituted Maiserene’s “thieves guild,” such as it was—a gang of four surly young men who called themselves the Bruiser Boys and augmented their general bullying with a small-time smuggling operation that utilized the dungeon entrance to the castle at area @UUID[.P8DWUDP9moicwHQC]{A11}.

Their arrangement with Junth Rundel, the castle’s apothecary, was to pick up the illegal substances he brewed and stashed in outgoing shipments then distribute the drugs themselves on the mainland before sending half of the proceeds on different barges heading back into the dungeon.

With little nostalgia or loyalty to Maiserene, when the curse struck, the Bruiser Boys could have escaped, yet their greed prevented them from doing so—instead of rowing for safety to the lake’s far shore, they rowed out here to grab their stashed supply of coins they’d been skimming off the top of payments to Junth.
