This was long enough for all four to be slaughtered by nightgaunts, and they were reborn here among the brambles as twigjacks. Today, the four have little memory of their previous lives. They know only that the coins buried near the western side of the ghostly tower are theirs and theirs alone, and that they now serve at the whims of this land’s true ruler, the Typhon Wheel, Charg. The twigjacks see all fleshy life as meat for their lord, but rarely travel far from this area out of fear of leaving their gold unprotected. They attack as soon as any PC attempts to enter the brambles or otherwise approaches, fighting to the death. As they do, they cry out oaths and threats to the PCs in Fey, often including Charg’s name—“You belong to Charg!” or “Meat for Charg!” being two favorites. They do not pursue foes, and when confronted with range superiority, they seek concealment and cover among the brambles.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.SKNjMBtBH3gFzlP8]{Abandoned Backpack}

The brambles make a thorough search of the area difficult. It’s possible to clear them with a combination of slashing weapons and fire over the course of 8 hours of miserable labor. After which, if a PC succeeds at @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check made while @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the cleared land, they find a suspicious leather strap protruding from a lump of earth near the western side of the spire. It’s possible to discover this curiosity by spending an hour carefully and slowly Searching the area before the brambles clear, but doing so deals @Damage[6d6[piercing]] damage from the thorns (@Check[reflex|dc:20|basic] save) and requires a successful @Check[perception|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check.

The strap leads to a barely-buried leather backpack that contains several decayed cloth pouches filled with silver coins—the results of the Bruiser Boys’ skimming efforts. In all, there are 530 sp here, along with a few potions they stole (after Junth’s suspicion about the Boys’ claim that these potions were stolen by bandits, he never trusted them with actual magical deliveries again). These include an invisibility potion, an oak potion, a potion of leaping, two shrinking potions, and four moderate healing potions.

Sewage Outflow.name: Sewage Outflow
Sewage Outflow.text:
The path comes to a shallow waterway here—not so much a creek as a five-foot-wide reed-choked ditch. A rickety wooden bridge crosses the waterway. Where the ditch meets the stone cliffside to the west, it continues deeper underground, with just enough room for a person to traverse bent over, but after five feet the passage becomes filled with opaque green mist.

This ditch serves as the outflow for the castle sewers—when the castle was fully functional before the curse struck, sewage was swept out from the castle dungeon along this waterway into the lake. Since the dungeon remains locked, the waterwheel that once created this cleansing current (and the hapless servants who attended it) hasn’t functioned for centuries, and in that time, the ditch has become a tangle of reeds and foul-smelling muddy water.

The point under the castle foundation where the ditch continues west at A15a is blocked by impassable green mist until the PCs unlock the dungeon. Once they do so, the mist clears, and this tunnel leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.htYveToKD0tnBIiJ]{E8}.

While the bridge looks unsafe, it remains sturdy and won’t collapse under the PCs’ weight.

Haunted Shore Connections.name: Haunted Shore Connections
Haunted Shore Connections.text:
There are several locations on the haunted shore that remain inaccessible when the PCs first begin to explore this initial region of Bastardhall, but will manifest later as the PCs defeat various Arudoras and unlock more regions of the castle by returning their heirlooms to the fountain at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3}. If an area connects physically to another part of Bastardhall, the point of transition to that area is blocked by an opaque wall of shimmering green mist until the location beyond is unlocked. If an area is a freestanding structure that doesn’t physically connect to another part of Bastardhall, the structure appears as a ghostly image that cannot be interacted with. These connections are summarized in the following table.

Haunted Shore

Unlocked by

Connects to Exit

Laroba Bridge (above @UUID[.XyjmNWjgPGNrEVim]{area A1})

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.0LrDMdMNqUb9cxSV]{Irrokcis's Medallion}

@UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.vLK5DU1IqUQjOhmx]{Area J1}

Delivery entrance (@UUID[.P8DWUDP9moicwHQC]{area A11})

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.kasxhW2drfCOZZq1]{Alisendra's Fan}

@UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.mJ7qNpJ3GNVNEVcR]{Area E1}

Northern Watch Post (@UUID[.FuifNpUpaAG0LzlR]{area A12})

The Vault.name: The Vault
The Vault.text:
Centuries before Caydserris arrived in Bastardhall to establish of a site devoted to Charg, Irrokcis Arudora had his first true taste of fear: He found his mother’s body, bloated and awful from thousands of spider bites, in her bedroom. Since that day, fear has grown into Irrokcis’s greatest obsession—both in how to stanch his own terror and how he might use fear to bring others to their knees.

Irrokcis’s discovery of a large cavern hundreds of feet below Castle Arudora enabled him to continue his increasingly awful experiments into the nature of fear, gave him a place to imprison his father, and became the site of his transformation into a lich—all of which took place before the Bastardhall Curse took hold. When the curse fell, it reached down into the depths below and took with it Irrokcis’s cavern and laboratory, a region he often referred to as his personal vault. Since then, Irrokcis has come to the conclusion he was only the first in a line of pawns and that he was never meant to be Charg’s final and greatest agent. While he remains an irredeemable and cruel monster, his research into how one might strike back at the sahkil tormentor could give the PCs exactly what they seek to lift Bastardhall’s curse—provided they can survive the terrors of Bastardhall’s vault.

Entering the Vault.name: Entering the Vault
Entering the Vault.text:
This immense cavern makes up the Bastardhall vaults and was once a part of the Darklands realm of Nar-Voth; now, it’s trapped in limbo with the rest of the castle above. All of the old connections to the Darklands’ deeper reaches presently lead to the dangerous wilds of the Ethereal Plane, leaving the occupants—including Irrokcis and his victims—as trapped and sustained by the curse as those who dwell in the castle far above.

The central cavern of the vault lies over 400 feet below ground, its depths sinking as low as Bastardhall’s towers rise. Given this fact, the PCs won’t see the vault unlock when they place @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.3c9AEoBCXmdltdr2]{Ryhasphinea’s Hourglass} in the fountain at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3}. Instead, they feel a deep, unsettling rumbling from below—not so much an earthquake, but a trembling in the primal part of the mind where fear lives. A few moments later, a sudden expulsion of foul, mephitic vapor belches upward from the castle’s well (area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.RFIcObAU8wgYbWiU]{B14}) and out of both waterway entrances to the dungeon (areas @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.P8DWUDP9moicwHQC]{A11} and @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.OWdcr3QHPHrYyFXD]{A15a}), along with clouds of shrieking, albino bats. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} identifies these bats as a species native to the Darklands, suggesting that, as the bats stream into the storm above, a new path has opened somewhere deep below.

The Skies Above.name: The Skies Above
The Skies Above.text:
Although the PCs will largely be sheltered from the weather during their explorations during this chapter, the storm hits in full force. Rain comes down in torrents, covering Bastardhall’s courtyard to a depth of a few inches in some places. This water drains through various holes in the curtain wall, soaking the haunted shore even more and causing many new rivulets to wind their way to the shore. Outdoors, vision-based Perception checks take a –3 circumstance penalty from the downpour, and the wind causes a –3 circumstance penalty on ranged Strikes. Unprotected small open flames outside are snuffed out by the wind or rain. The temperatures remain mild cold during the day but drop to severe cold outdoors between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. Near midnight, brief flurries of snow might hit. Lake Laroba’s surface is now truly dangerous to navigate—it’s now a @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim} through these storm-tossed waters. Waves surge along the haunted shore, making anything within 10 feet of the shoreline on land into difficult terrain. Thunder strikes often, and lightning strikes blast once or twice an hour—sometimes perilously close to the PCs (but at this point, no PC is in danger of being struck).

While the vault is largely sheltered from this storm, the dungeon isn’t, and it begins to flood. The wooden walkways in areas @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.k9MS0A9QhgJfPA7G]{E2}, @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.0CdaOwJhcWtoKSkm]{E3}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.FBPDuStK6Zlej0n5]{E6} become submerged underwater to a depth of 2 feet, making it difficult terrain to wade through these areas. The storm surge isn’t enough to do much more than to periodically wash over edges into other parts of the dungeon, though, and none of the waters reach either entrance to the vault. Sunrise is at 1:00 p.m., and sunset is at 3:00 p.m. The days are 2 hours long, and the nights are 22 hours long.

Vault Ambushes.name: Vault Ambushes
Vault Ambushes.text:
Encounter

Low 12

@UUID[Actor.919AP58ceDMPI5IU]{Anophilexes x2}

If the PCs rest in an unsafe area in the vault, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:7]. On a failure, they’re ambushed while they camp by two anophilex sahkils.

Lucid Nightmares.name: Lucid Nightmares
Lucid Nightmares.text:
After unlocking the vault, the nightmare changes. This time, the PC seems to awaken in some vast underground location. They begin wandering the tunnels, only to realize they’re hopelessly lost, and no matter where they go, the tunnels become tighter and more constrictive. Worse, the skittering sounds of spiders pursuing them through dark passages only grows. The PC hears a voice from somewhere ahead, beckoning them, but they recognize that voice as the hooded man. As they see the green glow of his lantern around a tunnel ahead, they know that if they make that turn, they’ll die. Yet still they push forward, and as they make that final turn, they slide into a sharply- sloped, web-choked tunnel and directly toward the slavering jaws of an immense hungry spider before they awake with a shriek.

Into the Deepening Dark Below

Resist Nightmare @Check[will|dc:30|options:lucid-nightmare,into-the-deepening-dark-below]

Critical Failure The PC wakes with arachnophobia (fear of spiders), and when in combat against creatures that resemble spiders, they’re @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}. Whenever a spiderlike creature scores a critical hit on the PC with a Strike, or the PC becomes affected by spiderwebs, they also become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} from growing panic.

Research @Check[nature|dc:32|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to find peace and comfort in the beauty of a spider’s form, or @Check[survival|dc:35|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to be on the lookout for signs of spidery activity in the area

Effect

@UUID[Item.pXJNt2NxwKZHPFPj]{Aracnophobia}

If a PC critically fails to resist this nightmare, use the linked effect to give your player a toggle to gain the off-guard condition whenever appropriate, as well as a reminder to yourself about the slowed condition when they are critically hit.

Vault Features.name: Vault Features
Vault Features.text:
The central cavern of the vault is constantly bathed in dim light from numerous patches of eerie, glowing fungus and mold, while further into Irrokcis’s laboratory compound, the chambers are kept completely unlit save for the idle flickering of candles and other small open flames. The central cavern is 150 feet high, while within the laboratory, the ceiling height averages at 20 feet unless otherwise noted in the text. Doors are made of reinforced wood and unlocked, while cell doors are made of iron bars and are kept locked. When locked, a PC can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} a reinforced wood door with a @Check[athletics|dc:35|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check or open it with three @Check[thievery|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}. These DCs increase by 5 each for iron cell doors (@Check[athletics|dc:40|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] and @Check[thievery|dc:35|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] respectively)

Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

All locations in this chapter can be found in the Vault level of Arudora Isle.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.LsRHJINIEl1ACq5P]{Vault}

As the PCs begin exploring the Vault, you can play this ambience sound.

Grand Staircase.name: Grand Staircase
Grand Staircase.text:
This ten-foot-wide spiral of stone stairs emerges from a cavern ceiling amid dozens of ten-foot-long stalactites, then proceeds downward for an additional 110 feet with not so much as a ridge for a railing. The stairs end at the top of a terraced hilltop, its sides sloping down roughly 10 feet per step save for three mold-encrusted ramps.

The stairs wind upward to area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.81VUnUk6FgVIeWfO]{E9}. Descending the stairs, which are slick with mold, must be done slowly—moving faster than a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.UHpkTuCtyaPqiCAB]{Step} every action requires a PC to succeed at a @Check[acrobatics|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Balance.Title|options:action:balance|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.M76ycLAqHoAgbcej]{Balance}, with a critical failure indicating a fall from the stairs to the ground below for regular falling damage.

Throughout the main cavern, over a dozen smaller caves branch out from the walls. Each of these cavern entrances are at different heights above the nearby cave, requiring flight or a series of @Check[athletics|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb} the cave walls to reach them. The height to each of these smaller caves is indicated on the map near the cave.

To the west, three wide tunnels lead away from the cavern. These tunnels once led deeper into the Darklands, but after only a hundred or so feet from the cave, they open directly into the Ethereal Plane. Whether or not the PCs can navigate the Ethereal Plane to emerge into the waters of Lake Laroba somewhere “above” is left to you to determine, but it should always be easy enough to return to the tunnel from which the PC just emerged.

Encounter

Low 12

@UUID[Actor.KkvwNJShZzZQxGgN]{Vault Bats x6}

Creatures: The small caves surrounding the main cavern are the homes of human-sized phantasmal vault bats with glowing red eyes and wings made of smoke. These vault bats spend much of their time wheeling and circling about the central stairs; each time the PCs enter the cavern via the stairs or start to climb them, roll [[/gmr 1d4+1#Nearby Vault Bats]] to determine how many of the vault bats are nearby.

They attack as soon as the PCs are at a height of more than 30 feet on the stairs—immediately if the PCs emerge from above. The bats each fight until they’re reduced to fewer than 90 Hit Points. At that point, the bat attempts to Grab Item to steal something from a PC; if they’re successful, they flee back to one of their cave lairs (areas H1a–H1f, determined randomly). A PC who wants their item back must pursue. Confronted in their cave, the vault bat fights to the death.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.t4ehKPxUtAq2Vl46]{Northern Cave} @UUID[Actor.IKe8UcV0vL8qj0XU]{Eastern Cave} @UUID[Actor.hs4cbAtYtPlfS55H]{Southern Cave}

In addition to any treasure a vault bat might steal from a PC, three of their caves contain additional items stolen from other unfortunates who came upon this area while traveling through the Ethereal Plane. Area H1b has a flying broomstick, area H1c has a +2 striking flaming warhammer and area H1d has a 5th-rank wand of teeming ghosts.

Eldritch Shrine.name: Eldritch Shrine
Eldritch Shrine.text:
A ring of eight immense gray standing stones, each about twenty-five-feet in height, protrude from the cavern ground here. The stones and ground within the ring are thickly overgrown with pale lichens and mold, yet the large red stone at the center appears to be completely free of any fungal growth at all. This center stone is carved into the image of a crouching bat with a single, three-lobed eye. A soft noise, like the rasping of crawling insects or perhaps the whispering of dozens of unhinged minds, issues from the stone.

With a successful @Check[religion|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}, a PC recognizes that the central altar depicts the sahkil tormentor, Charg.

Encounter

Severe 12

@UUID[Actor.QLyDRZPvMsYGZEeN]{Gugs x6}

Creatures: When Irrokcis first discovered this cavern, it was far from uninhabited. Many creatures and minor Darklands denizens were swept up and transformed into phantoms or other monsters by the curse, but the small clan of gugs who dwelled here were curiously unaffected. Irrokcis was delighted by the powerful but relatively easy-to-trick monsters, and he took advantage of their crude worship site of standing stones and central altar.

Under the cover of invisibility one night, as most of the gugs slept in the stone circle, he cast a 7th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2oH5IufzdESuYxat]{Illusory Object} on the central altar to transform it into a glowing red stone and then followed that up with a 2nd-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.yV7Ouzaoe7DHLESI]{Ventriloquism} to speak from the stone from hiding and quickly convince the gugs he was their god. Through this manipulation, he convinced the gugs to quarry onyx from a vein in the south of the cavern (which would soon thereafter flood and eventually become transformed by the curse into the lake of rotten blood at area @UUID[.mrOzlklF18CqGW2D]{H3}). By the time he had the gugs working to build the onyx ziggurat at area @UUID[.nk1c8QgLT7wGiRvG]{H4}, they believed his voice to be that of their god, Nyarlathotep, and Irrokcis’s sphinx agent Aznithakantus to be a manifestation of that Outer God.

The advent of the Bastardhall Curse is, to the six gugs, just another indication of their “god’s” power, and they attribute their long life and enforced isolation to him, expecting some day to be called upon to emerge from this cavern to do his bidding. While a sphinx, Aznithakantus, remains ever atop the onyx ziggurat, the gugs no longer approach her since the curse made her unpleasant, and they haven’t heard the voice of their god in ages. They remain hopeful, though, and the PCs present the gugs with a chance to curry new favor from Nyarlathotep. They attack on sight, fighting to capture, not to kill, as they plan to bind the PCs and then carry them to the pyramid as an offering to Nyarlathotep (aka Aznithakantus). However, as soon as the PCs kill at least four gugs, any remaining gugs surrender if reduced to fewer than 30 Hit Points. A captured gug can provide the PCs with a distorted history of their past several hundred years here, warning them to not approach the ziggurat without an offering of a living sacrifice if they wish to speak to the “Haunter of the Dark.” They don’t know the name Irrokcis at all.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.LdxZVV9BiCruJHK0]{Shrine Cache}

As part of the early facade, Irrokcis had Aznithakantus deliver several objects of value to the gugs for them to keep and guard, giving them an additional goal in life when not serving in other ways. These items include 1,200 gp in various pieces of strange jewelry, a +2 striking greater fearsome greatsword, a greater staff of providence, and the gugs’ most adored treasure, a elegantly carved ruby and obsidian statuette depicting Nyarlathotep in his bat-like form as the Haunter of the Dark worth 1,300 gp—a treasure Irrokcis stole from the Sinkomakti School in Versex shortly before the curse took Bastardhall.

Among these treasures is something new that has baffled the gugs—a major soulheart. This treasure appeared on the night of the curse. The first PC to touch this major soulheart receives a brief memory of Ilana Greenbough having increasingly vivid dreams in which all of Castle Arudora became engulfed in a cloud of darkness. These dreams were actual visions of the impending curse brought on by some of Ilana’s occult studies, but she’d forgotten the dreams long ago. If the PCs bring the topic up with her, her eyes widen as she admits having forgotten them, and then she despairs, for had she acted upon them, maybe she and some of the others of Maiserene could’ve escaped the curse before it engulfed them all.

Carrion Lake.name: Carrion Lake
Carrion Lake.text:
The vast red lake here appears to actually be filled with blood. Certainly, the foul rotting stink that rises from the placid, opaque fluid reeks of decay, although much of that odor might be coming from the mound of dead bodies that rises, like an island, from the lake’s center. Directly above the bodies is a twenty-five-foot-wide hole in the ceiling one hundred and fifty feet above.

The air above and around this polluted lake is befouled with a nauseating stench. Any creature that begins its turn within 20 feet of the liquid’s surface must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:28|options:inflicts:sickened|traits:olfactory] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure); this is an olfactory effect. Once a creature saves against the stink, it’s temporarily immune to the smell for 1 hour. A creature that’s fully immersed in the lake of rancid blood (another manifestation of Charg’s curse) must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:30|options:inflicts:sickened] save against the same (now non-olfactory) effect. The blood is thick and murky, obscuring vision completely beyond 5 feet, and averages at about 30 feet in depth. Much of its depths are worked and squared off; this flooded area was the source of the onyx the gugs quarried for the ziggurat to the north. A PC unfortunate enough to ingest any of the carrion lake’s blood is exposed to a level 12 variant nightmare fever with a DC 30 Will save that causes those who suffer from it to endure nightmares of spiders eating them alive as they sleep.

Nightmare Fever

Disease 12

  • Disease

  • Occult

Thought to be caused by a divine curse, nightmare fever inflicts you with terrible nightmares of spiders eating you alive, and you awaken with the wounds you received in your dreams. Damage and the fatigued condition caused by the disease can't be healed until the disease is removed.

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:30|traits:disease,occult]

Stage 1 @Damage[2d6[slashing]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[4d6[slashing]] damage and fatigued (1 day)

Stage 3 @Damage[4d6[slashing]] damage, fatigued, and whenever you take slashing damage, you must succeed at a Will save against the disease's DC or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (1 day)

Stage 4 @Damage[6d6[slashing]] damage, fatigued, and whenever you take slashing damage, you must succeed at a Will save against the disease's DC or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} for 1 round (1 day)

Stage 5 @Damage[6d6[slashing]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}

The central island of decaying bodies is heaped up all the way from the lake bed below. A PC who traverses this island finds the bodies shift, slide, and burst as they’re traversed, making this whole island into greater difficult terrain. The shaft above the center of the corpse island leads up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.Zkj5BrXf9tgddGZ7]{E15}.

The island of corpses consists of all the bodies tossed down the shaft above by Dazerien Arudora over the centuries—hundreds of oft-reincarnated bodies of souls doomed to live the same life of torture over and over again. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the island for 10 minutes finds one item of value (see Treasure, below) but is exposed to a level 10 variant of scarlet leprosy with a DC 27 Fortitude save.

Scarlet Leprosy

Disease 10

  • Disease

  • Virulent

Scarlet leprosy is widely feared for its devastating effects, crushing bones and organs while making recovery nearly impossible. Damage taken from scarlet leprosy can’t be healed until the disease is cured.

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:27|traits:disease,virulent]

Onset 1 day

Stage 1 @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]] damage (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]] damage, and whenever you gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Yl48xTdMh3aeQYL2]{Wounded} condition, increase the condition value by 1 (1 day)

Stage 3 @Damage[4d6[bludgeoning]] damage and can't heal any Hit Point damage (1 day)

Encounter

Moderate 12

@UUID[Actor.wBNWND1eplOJklQw]{Gogiteths x2}

Creatures: Nothing lives in the polluted waters of this lake, but there remains a danger here in the form of a pair of strange, blood-red gogiteths who have the constant ability to walk on water. The spiderlike horrors lurk under the surface of the blood, in areas near the corpse island. They burst up from the water as soon as anything comes within 10 feet of the island (or falls onto it) and attempt to carry off any prey they catch to their den, the cavern at area H3a. Each gogiteth also retreats to this cavern if reduced to fewer than 50 Hit Points, but if encountered there, they fight to the death.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.zWLLGasNvIWn4McV]{Corpse Island} @UUID[Actor.X2iX87DdhpUwdCVf]{Victims Remains}

The first PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the corpse island (see above) finds a bronze gear impaled in the back of a dead man’s head. This gear is one of those missing from the gearworks above—see @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details. The gogiteth cavern is littered with the bones of past victims, among which is a skeleton still clad in a +2 resilient chain shirt. A standard-grade adamantine scimitar lies nearby, but who knows which of the destroyed skeletons here it once belonged to.

The Onyx Ziggurat.name: The Onyx Ziggurat
The Onyx Ziggurat.text:
An immense, five-tiered ziggurat made of dark onyx rises from the cavern floor here, built up against the far wall. A central flight of stairs leads up to the ziggurat’s apex, where large stone double doors are set into the cavern wall.

Encounter

Low 12

@UUID[Actor.YUJG5Ou3TJvt1eGI]{Aznithakantus}

Creatures: One of Irrokcis’s oldest allies stands guard here, a sphinx named Aznithakantus who came here soon after his laboratory expansions uncovered the entrance to the soul vortex (area @UUID[.EPAmP1TdzmePRO9b]{I}). Irrokcis first made contact with Aznithakantus during an exploratory casting of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.yM3KTTSAIHhyuP14]{Dream Message} he’d developed to seek out and converse with like-minded worshippers of Charg. He’d done so in hopes of finding someone or something that could help him understand the incomplete soul anchor he’d discovered deep below Castle Arudora. Aznithakantus was intrigued by his research, made the long journey to Castle Arudora to join Irrokcis, and served as his assistant for many years.

When the curse struck, Aznithakantus died and then rose swiftly as an undead, desiccated version of herself. Now a mummy, she’s settled into a sort of guardian role for the entrance to Irrokcis’s domain, content to spend most of her time simply relaxing and soaking up the ambient fearsome energies that suffuse her new home.

Upon spotting the PCs, though, Aznithakantus perks up, as she doesn’t often have visitors. She calls out to them as they draw near, demanding to know their purpose in visiting “Lord Irrokcis’s laboratory.” She confirms that this location lies beyond the doors she guards but also notes that none can enter, for “the lord has been at toil on a great project these past few centuries and must not be disturbed.” As she speaks, she idly tosses a glowing crystal back and forth in her paws—something the PCs should immediately recognize as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.05h3LWflr74iJiVg]{major soulheart}.

Fortunately for the PCs, Aznithakantus is somewhat bored. If they ask her for a favor—be it information about Irrokcis, access to the laboratory beyond, or to bargain for the shiny gemstone she’s playing with—a thoughtful expression crosses her dry, leathery visage before she says, “Prove to me you are worthy of the Arudora secrets, and perhaps we can do business.”

Each favor the PCs ask of her must be paid for in a gift of their own knowledge about Bastardhall, the curse, or any of the Arudoras. They share this knowledge in the form of answering a strange riddle she composes on the spot about one of those topics. In order to earn her favor, the party must correctly answer one to three of these riddles while risking her ire should they answer poorly. Knowledge “prices” for three example favors are listed below; use these values to estimate the price she’d ask for other favors not listed.

  • Knowledge Trade: For the cost of one correct simple answer, Aznithakantus agrees to tell the PCs what she knows of one key subject matter associated with Bastardhall. For each of these, she can convey information equivalent to 1 Research point on any of the research topics presented in @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.UUqGlDCzpRnwqovv]{The Bastardhall Curse}, with the exception of Florin Kindler. Her knowledge of these topics comes to her in “dreams and visions,” and since Florin is a very new addition to the castle’s victims, she hasn’t been present long enough for Aznithakantus to notice her.

  • Spellcasting Services: For the cost of one correct difficult answer, Aznithakantus agrees to cast one of her innate spells for the PCs.

  • Major Soulheart: Aznithakantus agrees to hand over the major soulheart to the PCs at the cost of two correct difficult answers.

  • Access to Irrokcis’s Laboratory: For the cost of two simple and two difficult answers, Aznithakantus steps aside and won’t oppose the PCs’ entry into the laboratory, although she warns them there are guardians and wards within that might well lay them low and that it’s not her place to aid the PCs in navigating them.

When she asks her riddle, you can pose the question to the PCs for them to answer based on player knowledge, but it might be easier to simulate the answer by simply having a PC answer her riddles by attempting a DC 28 skill check for a simple question or a DC 32 skill check for a difficult one. The skill in question can be any of the following, depending on the flavor of the question:

  • @Check[architecture-lore|dc:28|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle] @Check[architecture-lore|dc:32|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle]

  • @Check[genealogy-lore|dc:28|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle] @Check[genealogy-lore|dc:32|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle]

  • @Check[heraldry-lore|dc:28|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle] @Check[heraldry-lore|dc:32|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle]

  • @Check[occultism|dc:28|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle] @Check[occultism|dc:32|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle]

  • @Check[society|dc:28|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle] @Check[society|dc:32|name:Answer Riddle|options:aznithakantus-riddle]

If a PC fails their check, Aznithakantus sneers and gleefully notes that their intellect doesn’t brand them as worthy of that favor, forbidding that particular PC from answering questions again. A critical failure insults Aznithakantus (as does any display of overt rudeness or obvious attempts to steal the soulheart or to enter the laboratory) and compels her to attack. (If you’re asking the players to answer these riddles with their own knowledge, a player who answers two questions wrong is cut off from further answers, and if they insist on answering a third time—or once all the players are cut off—Aznithakantus attacks.)

If combat begins, her roars are enough to draw any surviving gugs from area @UUID[.oEtULN89SUVVuFR7]{H2} to aid her in battle—you can assume these gugs arrive in pairs once every 3 rounds of combat. If the PCs don’t defeat them quickly, this fight can swiftly spiral out of control. Aznithakantus’s first act in combat is to cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.8Umt1AzYfFbC4fui]{Spellwrack} on a character she suspects might be the recipient of another PC’s magic, then follows that up with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.KSAEhNfZyXMO7Z7V]{Outcast’s Curse} on that PC. She then uses melee Strikes on PCs closest to her (or daze against foes who remain at range). She fights until destroyed but doesn’t pursue the PCs far from her perch here.

Hazard: Aznithakantus has protected the entrance to area @UUID[.i2pRckD9YVygbyxz]{H5} with a Riddler’s Rune (7th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.R8bqnYiThB6MYTxD]{Phantom Pain})—something she doesn’t tell the PCs and expects them to deal with on their own. If the PCs trigger the rune, she giggles in delight at the results but only attacks if the PCs do so first, perhaps in anger that she didn’t warn them in the first place about the trap. The riddle glows softly on the door as soon as the PCs approach: “When bloodline breaks and form betrays, whose claws twist grace through sudden decay?” The answer is Charg and allows the PCs to pass unharmed.

Treasure

The first PC to touch the major soulheart Aznithakantus has receives a brief memory of Aron Mordimus and his lover Brensen Firecask as the two creep about in the Bastardhall dungeon. The two are obviously drunk and have come to the mysterious stairs leading down to the vault. The two playfully dare each other to descend the stairs, and eventually, Brensen gives in... but less than a minute after he descends out of sight, he returns utterly sober, racing up the stairs, with his face pale and expression fearful. He’s unwilling to return, and he never tells Aron what he saw down those steps.

Reward

If the PCs manage to navigate this encounter without combat by successfully answering Aznithakantus’s riddles, grant them XP as if they’d defeated her in combat, plus an additional 10 XP per riddle answered, to a maximum reward of 60 XP for answering riddles.

Laboratory Entrance.name: Laboratory Entrance
Laboratory Entrance.text:
The walls of this thirty-foot-wide hallway slope inward, creating a triangular space whose peak extends to a height of sixty feet above. Intricate carvings of dead people drifting in an immense coiling line through all manner of ruined city and strange landscapes adorn both walls. These lines make it apparent the dead are approaching the doors at the eastern end of the hall. A pair of ten-foot wide alcoves house statues of an imperious man that are built into each wall.

Encounter

Moderate 12

@UUID[Actor.VBjnI1Usx93DcKkh]{Elite Stone Bulwarks x2}

Creatures: If the PCs have seen an image of Irrokcis before (most likely in area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.AmMkpYoDAJKpuurO]{D5}, although he appears much healthier and more robust in these statues than he did in his portrait in that location), they recognize the statues as depicting the ancient Arudora. The two statues in the easternmost alcoves aren’t statues at all, but elite stone bulwarks created by Irrokcis to stand guard. Unless the PCs sneak by, these two constructs step out of their alcoves and position themselves in front of the laboratory entrance, blocking the way. They don’t attack unless they’re attacked first or if any PC attempts to bypass them to get to the door to area @UUID[.MG8bJRohTuzWIbDI]{H6}. Combat with these creatures is loud and alerts Irrokcis in his laboratory. The stone bulwarks won’t pursue PCs out of this hallway in either direction and otherwise fight until destroyed.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Animate Stone Bulwarks" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to hide the inanimate stone statues and reveal the bulwark tokens!

Irrokcis's Laboratory.name: Irrokcis's Laboratory
Irrokcis's Laboratory.text:
The air in this large chamber is foul. Chemicals, soot, and blood have left the stone floor discolored and stained, and bookshelves line many of the walls. A system of pulleys, tracks, and hanging chains from the rafters some thirty feet above give the chamber a soft echo of jangling metal. Workbenches, laboratory tables, chests, and wheeled carts heaped with magical and alchemical supplies and jars of strange specimens are spread throughout the room’s center, while four alcoves to the east each contain tall glass tanks filled with murky green fluid. A large fountain of similar liquid bubbles in the southeast corner near a set of steps that lead up to a huge stone door. To the north, the most astounding decoration hangs—a spherical cage of iron suspended over the ground by thick chains. Within the cage floats a circular platform on which an almost skeletal figure, his flesh pulled tightly to his bones, twitches and moans in muffled agony.

The prison to the north is one of Irrokcis’s great achievements—a magical oubliette that keeps whoever is imprisoned within alive long after they should be dead, but it does nothing to soothe the agonies and humiliations of age advanced well beyond one’s natural life span. The books, research supplies, and tools here are what one might expect of an occultist like Irrokcis, including a mix of alchemical tools, construct building materials, and various magical supplies. Interspersed with the tools are stacks of research notes, reference books, and strange little keepsakes and objects that have meaning, to Irrokcis, but to others, they look like bits of dead body parts or broken tools.

Encounter

Severe 12

@UUID[Actor.V90ggUnKvweg3G0q]{Irrokcis Arudora} @UUID[Actor.G1AeunND7RAqoL2C]{Cevairiel} @UUID[Actor.LN7MXD38Zs2bDoW6]{Eragayl Arudora} @UUID[Actor.iiNuVMrWmIblcCZ3]{Zasha}

Creatures: Irrokcis Arudora toils here, as he has for the past five centuries, enjoying the peace and quiet as he spends years at a time on different research topics. Often, he’ll circle back to previous obsessions and start over, hoping to build something new and stronger. His favorite focuses here are the enhancement of the magical oubliette to the north, researching applications for the soul vortex to the south (area I), tinkering with the new “body” he built for his long-dead wife Zasha, and scrying upon other parts of Bastardhall. Yet increasingly, he spends his time scouring his laboratory for spiders.

The fact that, now and then, actual pests scuttle in here (creatures created and sent here to torment him by the curse) only complicates his frequent hallucinations. As the PCs enter the room, Irrokcis is near the northernmost tank on the east wall, having just squashed the last of the latest wave of intruders and obliterating the bodies.

A PC who’s seen depictions of Irrokcis elsewhere recognize him at once, although mostly for the unique gold, red, and lavender robes he wears, along with the deep purple and gold fez perched atop his head. His actual features have become distorted, for Irrokcis is a lich, and his flesh is even more leathery and taut against his bones than the poor unfortunate to the north in the magical oubliette. As soon as he notices the PCs, he cackles in delight, welcoming them to his workshop and asking them how he can be of assistance. As he waits for answers, his eyes, which are uncomfortably fresh and moist looking in their sockets, sparkle with anticipation. Irrokcis listens to anything the PCs have to say, but regardless of their answers, he’s sizing up their bodies for “spare parts” with which he can augment his wife’s body. He keeps the discussion going, hoping that the PCs spread out a bit, and might even ask one of them to check the southern tank for leaks. As soon as anyone approaches within 20 feet of his position or is adjacent to the southernmost tank, he attacks, rolling Deception for initiative. If the PCs attack before this point, he rolls Perception for initiative.

Irrokcis isn’t alone in this room and is attended by three of his closest “allies”—one he made from body parts, and the other two he tortured into undead servants. When Irrokcis attacks, his allies do as well.

The first of these allies is a charnel creation currently floating in the southernmost tank. This 13-foot-tall monstrosity has been cobbled together from body parts harvested from hundreds, all patched and stitched together in a shape coming close enough to what Zasha looked like in life that PCs who have seen her image can recognize her, but this rendition appears completely horrific more than anything else. On a close inspection, a PC discerns that Zasha’s left arm, which appears to be curled against her side, actually cradles a horrific shape that looks like a baby—it isn’t a real baby, but Irrokcis did his best to approximate his second child nonetheless. When combat begins, Zasha smashes out of her tank by rolling for initiative using Athletics. She charges forward, seeking to land fist Strikes on the closest PCs each round, and fights until destroyed. If Irrokcis is still a combatant when she’s destroyed, he roars in anger and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} for 1 minute. He can use the extra action only to Strike the PC who destroyed Zasha.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Animate Charnel Creation Zasha" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to break her tank open and reveal her token!

Irrokcis’s other two allies aren’t mindless constructs. The first of them once attempted to come to his father Eragayl’s aid, only to become another of Irrokcis’s captives. This entity was the angel Cevairiel, who’s been transformed into an undead monstrosity—a carrion angel. Enough of his previous mind remains that, as he swoops down from hiding up in the rafters above, he cries and sobs in shame and horror at both what he’s become and what he’s doing to the PCs once he attacks. He rolls for initiative with Stealth and prefers to spend his rounds casting a spell (focusing on obvious divine casters) and then Striking with a claw. If he’s reduced to fewer than 100 Hit Points, he activates Living Facade and Lies to the PCs; he tells them that he’s managed to overcome his corruption, and that if they can heal him, he’ll join them in fighting the remaining foes. Of course, he’s deceiving them, and he instead drops his facade and attacks the PCs again once they’ve cast healing spells on him (or as soon as they see through his lies). He fights until destroyed.

As tragic as Cevairiel is, Irrokcis’s final ally is worse. As the battle begins, he calls out, “Come to my aid, father! Show these fools what a real hero can do!” His father’s body is imprisoned in the spherical cage to the north, but while the body is alive, it’s without a soul; Irrokcis extracted that part of his father to transform him into a ghost. As a ghost, Eragayl Arudora appears as he did in the prime of his life, clad in plate armor adorned with Shelyn’s regalia and wielding a gleaming longsword. All of this gear is ghostly, and Strikes with his longsword resolve as a normal ghostly hand Strike. If the PCs found @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.w7usWIc20eklVVXT]{Fearcutter} in area @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.Bow5E5zzvV1g4WjZ]{G7}, they recognize this ghostly sword as a duplicate of that blade. Eragayl uses Blasphemous Decree each round, targeting obvious worshippers of Shelyn in preference to others (even though doing so is risky), then Flies and uses his Frightful Moan or Strikes with his longsword. He’ll use Telekinetic Assault whenever he’s surrounded.

As these other three agents attack, Irrokcis starts combat by casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.A2JfEKe6BZcTG1S8]{Fly}, then remains up near the ceiling, using the rafters as cover as he casts spells down at the PCs. He favors curse spells, like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.nQS4vPm5zprqkzFZ]{Curse of Death}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.f45JpY7Ph2cAJGW2]{Evil Eye}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.z2mfh3oPnfYqXflY]{Mariner’s Curse}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.KSAEhNfZyXMO7Z7V]{Outcast’s Curse}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.8Umt1AzYfFbC4fui]{Spellwrack} (enhancing as needed with Reach Spell), so he can potentially gain temporary Hit Points from his @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.jHCPejseO01ki3lO]{Accursed Staff}. If he’s reduced to fewer than 100 Hit Points, or if the PCs seem resistant to his curses, Irrokcis switches over to casting damage-causing spells. Although he’s a lich and doesn’t fear destruction, he does know that if the PCs destroy him, his body will be forced to return to his soul cage, which is kept up in his tower (area @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.7rtJA41bt42SO4VG]{J3g}), from which he won’t be able to emerge until the next time Bastardhall manifests on Golarion or until the PCs unlock the towers—furthermore, his gear will be left behind. As such, if he’s brought to fewer than 30 Hit Points, he pulls out a scroll of translocate from his major retrieval belt and teleports up to the master bedroom (area @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.pNlOS2ZetwxxrwrG]{F13}) since he knows that area must be unlocked if the PCs have made it here. From there, he does his best to recruit new allies from any surviving creatures, then plans a new attack on the PCs in the future.

As soon as his body is destroyed, Irrokcis’s soul shoots upward into his tower, returning to his soul cage. His gear remains behind, including his telescope—the key to unlocking the final area of Bastardhall: @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.gtabIEQFkkyVJdtc]{the towers}.

If Eragayl joined the PCs in fighting against Irrokcis, after the battle, he thanks the PCs for the clarity they granted him but warns them he can feel his corruption returning. He remains motionless for 1 more minute, during which he begs the PCs to flee or destroy him, even though he knows he’ll rejuvenate in a few days. If they don’t do either, he resumes his attacks and is no longer bothered or affected by his nickname or the sight of someone carrying Fearcutter.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.smeyhOfTWSRkid1M]{Lab Cache} @UUID[Actor.RYrWBhq2hcxKtyB5]{Shelves} @UUID[Actor.N5QUiTBxJV6W5NMN]{Oubliette} @UUID[Actor.HWtwwQA3HLwsMNBe]{Tank}

When Cevairiel is slain, his remains swiftly decay away, and his angelic quintessence is released to return to Heaven, but as his soul passes on, he gives the PCs a glance of thanks. A shining, glittering shard of crystal drops quietly to the floor where he died—this is an angelic soulheart. The first PC to touch this soulheart realizes that to fully defeat the Bastardhall Curse and not simply escape it will require the favor of Shelyn and Pharasma—the two deities most blasphemed against by the curse on the castle. You can use this vision to further guide the party toward the Adventure Path’s @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.iIIzG8EEQwsCV7an]{secret ending} as much or as little as you wish.

Searching the rest of this large chamber is a daunting task and takes 2 hours of work, but at the end of the search, the PCs make numerous discoveries—some of which require Perception checks.

  • A total of 2,000 gp in raw materials for crafting magic items can be salvaged from the room.

  • If a PC references the books here for 2 hours while attempting to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} using Occultism or Religion, the books grant a +2 item bonus to the check.

  • A total of six 6th-rank scrolls can be found throughout the shelves: a scroll of mislead, a scroll of scrying, a scroll of wall of force, a scroll of illusory creature, a scroll of vampiric exsanguination, and a scroll of truesight.

  • A pair of dust-covered spectacles of inquiry sit forgotten on a bookshelf to the northeast.

  • With a successful @Check[perception|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check, the PCs discover something awful among the shelves to the southwest—a large jar filled with murky rusty liquid in which a middenworm the size of a hearty sausage twitches and writhes. This creature is Irrokcis’s familiar, and it’s harmless despite its unnerving habit of crying like a baby if extracted from its jar. If the PCs destroy the familiar (this requires a single Interact action), then Irrokcis is without a familiar for 1 day after he rejuvenates, during which time he can’t prepare spells. After this time, his new patron, Charg, grants him a new familiar.

  • The magical oubliette in which Eragayl’s living, moaning, soulless body is imprisoned can be understood by a PC who succeeds at a @Check[arcana|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] or @Check[arcana|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[nature|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], or @Check[religion|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic}. They understand that killing Eragayl’s body is a mercy—if they do so, the body crumbles to dust, and his ghost takes [[/gmr 4d6#Days to Rejuvenate]] days to rejuvenate instead. Whether the PCs grant this mercy or not, the only thing other than rags the unfortunate body wears is a general’s signet.

  • Mounted on the rafters directly above Eragayl’s body is a glamorous portrait of the man and his wife that depicts the two on their wedding day. Both look happy and carefree. This elegant painting was a wedding gift, and for many years, it hung in the Arudora gallery, but Irrokcis stole it and mounted it here to torment his father soon after imprisoning him (the other family members never learned the truth and thought the painting had been stolen by one of Eragayl’s enemies). The painting is 1 Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it triggers a memory of Eragayl’s anguish as his son, Irrokcis, mockingly puts the painting on display just out of reach but in full sight of his prison. This painting belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}); see @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{Lost Artwork} for more details.

  • The other three tanks along the north wall contain partially completed charnel creations, but in the northern one, a vile remnant that looks like a knot of a dozen tongues and teeth sits where the charnel creation’s head should be. Irrokcis was curious if, over time, this blasphemous item would infuse a charnel creation with some sort of mind, but after a few centuries of no results, he forgot it was in here.

Reward

If the PCs convinced Eragayl to switch sides and then destroyed him, grant them XP as if they’d defeated him in combat plus an additional 80 XP.

Soul Vortex.name: Soul Vortex
Soul Vortex.text:
The long tunnel that leads south from the laboratory grows increasingly cold and moist as the PCs continue, descending several natural terraces with large steps until they finally reach a chamber directly below the hanging tower of Bastardhall above.

The wide tunnel comes to a sudden end over what appears to be a bottomless pit that drops away into an eternity of glowing green mist. Above, the ceiling rises up like an inverted funnel to a height of two-hundred feet at its apex from the tunnel edge. On the ceiling, large pools of what looks like water collect in puddles and blobs, as if gravity itself had been inverted. At the center of the space churns a whirling mass of blue and green energy, a slowly spinning vortex made up of thousands of distorted ghosts and tormented wailing spirits. The screams from these ghosts fill the room, or so it seems at first, for after a few moments, it becomes apparent the screaming of these myriad souls is all in the mind.

This room opens directly into the Ethereal Plane. A PC who steps into it doesn’t fall and finds they can move about through force of will in the area as if they had a fly Speed equal to their base Speed, and if they don’t take an action to Fly, they don’t fall—they simply float in place. Those who seek to head out into the vast below once the mist is gone are at risk of becoming lost in the Ethereal Plane if they travel out of sight of the mass of rock “above” that is Bastardhall.

The “water” pooling above is in fact raw ectoplasm—a side effect, almost like sweat, formed from the churning of the soul vortex, which fills the central portion of this area.

Before the curse, this chamber contained an ancient but incomplete object known as a soul anchor—a corruption of the River of Souls that sometimes allowed those who perished in its vicinity to retain their memories after death. Irrokcis discovered the partially completed soul anchor and tried for a time to complete it, then turned his attention to reverse engineering it. Before he could make any progress, though, the curse took everything away and used the soul anchor as a catalyst, transforming it into a soul vortex. This vortex contains all of the souls of those who perished that night as well as the souls of all Arudoras who were brought to Bastardhall since then. Other creatures that find their way into the area sometimes become caught by the soul vortex too, and over the course of centuries, it has grown full and is close to bursting. When the last Arudora is fully absorbed into the soul vortex, Caydserris can transport the castle fully back to Golarion to establish it as a locus for Charg’s power in the heart of Avistan.

The soul vortex is frightening and unsettling, but it has no ability to affect a living creature—the PCs can pass through the vortex with little more than a case of gooseflesh and the weird sensation of someone walking over their grave. If a PC dies in such close proximity, though, their soul is automatically swept up in the vortex—any attempt to restore them to life that isn’t attempted in this room must succeed at a @Check[flat|dc:11] or fail to bring them back to life.

Encounter

Severe 12

@UUID[Actor.95TfQgYDh4rl6SgP]{Mymnians x2}

Creatures: A pair of powerful mymnian sahkils, fiends who embody the primal fear of ghosts and vengeance from beyond the grave, have come here to bask in the strange energies exuded by the soul vortex. Unlike the PCs, sahkils are affected by this chamber—they become quickened as long as they remain in this room and can use the extra action only to Fly. The energies also affect the sahkils as if they were mildly drunk, and they function as if @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} as well. When the PCs arrive, the sahkils are in the center of the cave near the soul vortex. They don’t immediately notice the PCs, but once they do, they attack and fight to the death.

Research

Any Research Topic (see below)

Communion with the Soul Vortex: Once the sahkils are dealt with, the souls trapped in the vortex are able to communicate with the PCs, but this communication is random and undirected; each time a soul passes through a PC, they experience a random memory fragment—the scent of a rose, the sting of a bee, the taste of fine wine, sadness from a broken heart, and so on.

These souls know much, and a PC who spends a minute @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EwgTZBWsc8qKaViP]{Investigating} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the area realizes that they can open their mind and concentrate to become more receptive to these souls. Doing so allows the PCs to Research any and all of the Research topics listed in @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n]{The Bastardhall Curse} journal category, provided they know that topic exists to research—only the topic of Florin Kindler can’t be researched here, as her soul hasn’t yet been taken by the soul vortex. They can research like this as many times as they want, but only to a maximum number of 5 RP per day, and unlike other research opportunities, there are real dangers to exposing yourself to the dead for too long! Each attempt to commune with the soul vortex takes 1 hour.

Maximum RP 5 per day; Research Checks @Check[occultism|dc:28|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] or @Check[religion|dc:30|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to understand the perils and tricks of speaking with souls, @Check[will|dc:32|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] save to resist being unsettled and baffled by the rush of information, or @Check[perception|dc:35|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to simply absorb what the souls have to share on the topic. A PC who fails a Research check becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} with an unlimited duration, while a PC who critically fails becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} with an unlimited duration, as portions of their own memories are scrambled and lost. This can be removed with proper methods and is a 12th-level curse effect with a @Check[counteract|dc:32|name:Counteract Curse].

The Fallen Temple.name: The Fallen Temple
The Fallen Temple.text:
Eragayl Arudora was a champion of Shelyn, but it was to Pharasma that the castle’s temple was devoted to, partly in honor of the church’s power in Varno at the time though also in memory of his parents—both of whom were devoted Pharasmins. It was their untimely deaths that propelled Eragayl into the life of an adventurer, and even as his faith in Shelyn helped see him through countless ordeals, he never forgot his family’s traditions. When he fell in love with a Pharasmin named Tasifinie, the denomination of the castle’s temple was settled. While smaller shrines and galleries devoted to Shelyn would be erected on the isle, it was the temple of Pharasma—and it’s stunning clocktower (an extravagance that alone cost more to construct than any other single feature of the castle)—that helped to establish Castle Arudora as a place sacred to the Lady of Graves.

Yet after Tasifinie’s horrific accidental death and Eragayl’s vanishing, local worship of Pharasma began to dwindle. Priests left the island for one reason or another, and by the time Raudltz took over the lordship, none remained to tend to the cathedral. He had the place closed up, and it remained empty for nearly two decades as the Arudoras increasingly drifted away from the family’s traditions of faith into obsessions and interests of their own.

When Raudltz’s older sister Ryhasphinea came to the castle after fleeing her home (her claims of “unjust persecution by intolerant magistrates” being nothing but lies to cover up the very real murder of her husband in a failed attempt to claim his fortune), Raudltz accepted her and her son into the family. When she asked if she could restore the temple, he shrugged and said “fine,” not really caring what she was planning. Part of him perhaps knew his sister’s reasons for fleeing her home were suspect and that she’d become a worshipper of Urgathoa, but family ties are strong, and Raudltz liked the idea of an Arudora helping to restore a part of the castle that had increasingly become an eyesore.

Ryhasphinea demanded privacy as she worked to rebuild the temple, and she had full control over those she hired to do the work, relying on contractors and labor forces who were devotees of the Pallid Princess. Yet mere days before she was ready to reveal the completed corruption to her family, the curse struck. Ryhasphinea raged against this unwanted disruption of her plans and tried a desperate gambit to halt the curse by calling upon Urgathoa to stop time in hopes of stymieing the curse’s progression so she could defeat it with ease. This final blasphemy, a brazen appeal to Urgathoa over a domain traditionally held by Pharasma, enraged the Lady of Graves, and she reached out to block the intervention from beyond. The result was a cataclysmic explosion in the height of the clocktower that sent 13 of its gears phasing in and out of reality to become scattered throughout the castle—a devastation that simultaneously caused the temple to collapse from within. As the ceiling came down, transforming the metaphorically fallen temple into a literal one, Ryhasphinea perished, and the curse whisked the castle away.

Yet as chastised as she was by this brief divine clash, Urgathoa didn’t entirely abandon Ryhasphinea. While Urgathoa dared not rescue her from the ruins, the goddess did grant her the gift of unlife. As Castle Arudora drifted into the depths of the Ethereal Plane, Ryhasphinea rose as an undead child of Urgathoa. She remains in the cathedral to this day, yet she no longer seeks its reconstruction. Instead, Ryhasphinea has spent the past several centuries brooding and plotting revenge on Pharasma. During this time, she’s plucked and pulled at various agonies suffered by souls brought to Bastardhall, drawing out slivers associated with Urgathoa’s three tenets of disease, gluttony, and undeath. She knows she can’t strike directly at Pharasma, and so she’s settled on the next best thing: the creation of a horrific contagion engineered to spread through Pharasma’s faithful via food and drink. Once spread, this contagion will cause those who perish to rise from death as herexens or other undead mockeries. Her work nears completion, and once Caydserris’s own plot completes with the last Arudora, Ryhasphinea’s plague will be ready to unleash upon Ustalav and beyond!

Entering the Fallen Temple.name: Entering the Fallen Temple
Entering the Fallen Temple.text:
The fallen temple of Bastardhall is located in the southwest portion of the castle. Once the PCs return Raudltz’s telescope to the fountain at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3}, the solidification of the temple isn’t only obvious, it’s dramatic. At first, the structure grows solid in its original glory as a looming cathedral with a breathtaking clocktower, only to then collapse silently in on itself. The faces of the clock explode outward, sending gears flying, and the roof of the central cathedral tumbles down into the structure, replaying the original devastation. As the collapse completes, the fallen temple phases fully into reality, the faces of the clock freezing at the precise time the Bastardhall Curse took hold: two in the afternoon.

If Lucinero is still around (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.FuifNpUpaAG0LzlR]{A12}), the psychopomp cries out in anguish as he feels this ancient clash between Pharasma and Urgathoa. He’ll seek the PCs out to warn them to take care, telling them that what they witnessed was an echo of a clash between the two goddesses on the night of the curse. While he’s certain that this clash wasn’t the source of the curse, he can feel a great power associated with Urgathoa lurking within. However, if the PCs can defeat this power—whatever it might be—Pharasma might reward them... if not with aid in escaping Bastardhall, then perhaps just aid in enduring what’s still to come. While Lucinero is quite outclassed by the threats that await within, he still volunteers to accompany the PCs into the fallen temple to aid them in their efforts. Wise PCs might push back, and it won’t take much to convince Lucinero of the wisdom of letting them take care of things while he hangs behind. If Lucinero survives to the end of this chapter, regardless of whether he accompanied the PCs on their adventures or he wisely agreed to hang back, grant the PCs 40 XP.

The Skies Above.name: The Skies Above
The Skies Above.text:
The storm grows in power. Rain pelts down constantly and leaks through the roof in places, leaving puddles on the floor indoors. Outdoors, vision-based Perception checks take a –3 circumstance penalty from the downpour, and the wind causes a –2 circumstance penalty on ranged Strikes. Unprotected small open flames outside are snuffed out by the wind or rain. The temperatures remain mild cold outside, and Lake Laroba’s surface remain storm-tossed—it’s now a @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim} in these waters. Waves surge along the haunted shore, making anything within 5 feet of the shoreline on land into difficult terrain. Thunder strikes two to three times an hour and is often accompanied by lightning strikes. Now and then, a bolt of lightning strikes one of the still-locked towers of Bastardhall above.

Sunrise is at noon, and sunset is at 4:00 p.m. The days are 4 hours long, and the nights are 20 hours long.

Temple Ambushes.name: Temple Ambushes
Temple Ambushes.text:
Encounter

Low 11

@UUID[Actor.ZQ7lS9TYOFv07m1a]{War Wraiths x3}

If the PCs rest in the fallen temple, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:5]. On a failure, they’re ambushed while they camp by three war wraiths.

Lucid Nightmares.name: Lucid Nightmares
Lucid Nightmares.text:
After unlocking the fallen temple, the nightmare changes. This time, the PC has come to a cathedral to meet with someone in keeping with their character—perhaps they’re here in search of comfort or absolution from a priest, or maybe they’re here to provide comfort. They could even be here to confront the other. Whatever the cause, just as they approach whoever they’re focused on, that person turns and grows large before them, revealing themself to be the hooded figure. The hooded figure cackles in delight as he spreads wide his hands, and the church ceiling above flies apart to reveal a dark sky with a hole torn within, churning and spinning in a spiral like a hollowed-out wheel around a monstrous figure far above. As the PC falls up into this gaping maw, they awaken.

Enduring the Hungry Vast Above

Resist Nightmare @Check[will|dc:28]

Critical Failure The PC wakes with agoraphobia (fear of open spaces), and when in outdoor areas (including areas that lack a roof, such as the cathedral), they’re @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} from the overwhelming fear.

Research @Check[religion|dc:30|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to find protection and safety in prayer or @Check[acrobatics|dc:33|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to tumble through the air in a way that affords a last-minute chance to clutch at a portion of intact ceiling.

Effect

@UUID[Item.dwZa70BULRhlaE6V]{Agoraphobia}

If a PC critically fails to resist this nightmare, use the linked effect to give that character's player a toggle to make their character off-guard as needed.
