Fallen Temple Features.name: Fallen Temple Features
Fallen Temple Features.text:
The majority of the fallen temple lies in ruins, exposed to the storm above and filled with rubble below. A few areas (notably the clocktower, Ryhasphinea’s room, and the underground crypts) survived this devastation, but what were once several chambers adjoining the cathedral (a scriptorium, priests’ cells, a choir, and more) are now all part of the central gaping ruination. This area receives natural light, but the other areas are unlit. Doors (those that survived) are of reinforced wood and unlocked unless otherwise noted in the text. When locked, a door can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Forced Open} with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:33|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check, or with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}.

Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

The Fallen Temple's locations span multiple scene levels! Here is the breakdown:

  • @UUID[.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1} is found in the Castle Grounds level, as are the ensuing encounters in Stage 1 through Stage 4.

  • @UUID[.QSqT538Ma6NnufC7]{G2} and @UUID[.jZnvyQePE7QRZcmH]{G3} are found in the Private Halls (Lower) level.

  • @UUID[.osl3dmryGXkoTcAc]{G4} is found in the Clocktower level.

  • @UUID[.e6z8NTXgpq400EZk]{G5}-@UUID[.xusIZ6ZnpPAUUJTS]{G8} are found in the Crypts level.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.ONTeDjH5dol5Cnoz]{Inside Bastardhall} @UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.Ggl8VZ7v1J5Mo1er]{Bastardhall Outdoors}

The Fallen Temple features a mix of indoor areas and the partially exposed temple. As the PCs explore these various areas, you can play these ambience sounds accordingly.

Fallen Cathedral.name: Fallen Cathedral
Fallen Cathedral.text:
This once-staggering cathedral now lies in ruins, the ceiling having long ago collapsed into an immense mound of rubble piled in the central portion of the chamber below. Pillars that emerge here and there, broken off at different heights, are all that indicate the catwalks and chambers that might have once been supported above. Ruined pews, crushed statues, and an unpleasant scattering of bones add final touches to the wreckage, all of which glistens with rainwater. The water itself has started to pool in the lower regions of the ruins, slowly flowing over the stone floor.

Once the fallen temple phases back into reality, the torrential rainfall drenches everything within it. This rainwater seeps out of the cathedral through cracks in the exterior walls so that the room never floods deeper than an inch or so, but it also slips under doors to create a growing puddle near area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.78A34DGpyfbsAqFq]{D7b} of the reception halls as well as near the secret door at the statue in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.yYVET9FqdVmC0NwM]{C13} (this reduces the DC of the Perception check to spot that door from area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.yYVET9FqdVmC0NwM]{C13} by 5). The falling rain imparts the standard –3 circumstance penalty to vision-based Perception checks, but the walls mostly block the wind and negate the circumstance penalty normally applied to ranged Strikes.

The ground floor area is strewn with smaller bits of rubble and—along with the pooling rainwater—make these open areas difficult terrain. The darker gray areas indicate places where the ceiling and upper areas have collapsed; movement through this area is treated as greater difficult terrain.

Some of the exits here open into other portions of Bastardhall. The main doors at area G1a open into area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1e}. The smaller side door to the south at area G1b leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1i}. A wooden door to the west at area G1c opens to a flight of stairs that leads down to the crypts (area @UUID[.cvqO7qaa6g64fMDL]{G6a}). The secret door at area G1d can be discovered by a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the area with a successful @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check; it leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.yYVET9FqdVmC0NwM]{C13}. The large doors at area G1e lead to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.78A34DGpyfbsAqFq]{D7b}.

The high walkways are 50 feet above the floor, and while they look precarious, those that remain are quite stable and capable of supporting the weight of Large creatures with ease. The door at area G1f leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.HiXOGKLx6aYdwEd4]{F1a}, while opposite to the west at area G1g, the doors open outside to a winding stairwell that descends all the way down to the Sunset Shrine in the haunted shore (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.NoRsDoZrbNHsWUCD]{A22}).

The western doors into the clocktower (area @UUID[.jZnvyQePE7QRZcmH]{G3}) are mostly buried under rubble, and it’ll take days to clear that entrance—an easier access is via the walkway above.

Far to the south, just at the southern edge of the central rubble, a once-elegant altar lies in ruins, not far from a caryatid that supports the chamber above—this pillar has been carved into the image of Urgathoa, but a PC who Investigates the pillar for 10 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] or @Check[perception|dc:33|traits:secret] check can tell that skilled hands have used magic and chisels to alter what was once a different depiction—with a critical success, they confirm that the original carving depicted Pharasma.

This immense chamber is the domain of Ryhasphinea and her minions. However, most of them remain out of phase when the PCs first enter the ruined cathedral, held in a form of stasis just outside the PCs’ reality as the priestess of Urgathoa continues to gather and build upon the energy she needs to be ready to release her cursed contagion—soulphage—upon the world once Bastardhall returns to Golarion. The PCs can force successive elements associated with the three stages of soulphage to manifest in the cathedral simply by spending a short amount of time in the area, as their life forces prove too much for the monstrosities who serve Ryhasphinea to resist. Once the PCs force three waves of creatures to appear, Ryhasphinea and her final allies arrive—giving the party a chance not only to claim her hourglass to unlock the vaults far below, but to save central Avistan from a deadly plague.

Confronting Ryhasphinea

Unlike the other areas of Bastardhall, the ruler of the fallen temple, the child of Urgathoa Ryhasphinea Arudora, is encountered in what’s likely the first area the PCs enter—the cathedral ruins (area G1). But in order to force the powerful priestess of Urgathoa to manifest, they must first defeat layers of spiritual defenses she’s erected—layers that coincide with the fell energies she’s been gathering, harvesting, and shaping to unleash her cursed plague upon Golarion. These four combats all occur in the same area but take a short time to manifest—in between each battle, the PCs have 10 minutes to rest and recover, or perhaps simply to flee. If the PCs defeat some of these battles and then abandon the fight to seek shelter elsewhere, the next phase is ready to trigger the instant they return to area G1; only this time, the foes within have had time to prepare and all enemies gain a +4 circumstance bonus to initiative.

Effect

@UUID[Item.aFmS2EXTOKlECIiW]{Initiative Bonus}

If an enemy gains a +4 circumstance bonus to initiative, you can automate it using this effect.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Clear Clocktower Entrance Rubble" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager if the PCs take on the arduous task of clearing that entrance!

Stage 1: Undeath.name: Stage 1: Undeath
Stage 1: Undeath.text:
The first stage of opposition in the church manifests quickly, not long after the PCs initially enter the cathedral. The indications that something strange is building up become apparent to anyone who has line of sight to the Urgathoa caryatid to the south, as trickles of blood slowly begin to run from Urgathoa’s bones to splatter into the rainwater below.

One minute after the PCs enter area @UUID[.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1} (or as soon as anyone attempts to interact with the caryatid), a wave of unholy energy sweeps through the cathedral, causing the falling rain to turn to blood. All PCs in the area must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:25|options:inflicts:drained] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} by this pulse of unholy energy.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Stain Temple Water" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to stain the pools of water in area G1 with blood!

Encounter

Low 11

@UUID[Actor.5meW7DytYnF7Iq2V]{Greater Shadows x3} @UUID[Actor.V4rVnbjJbcOIdC4Z]{Skeletal Hulks x3}

Creatures: An instant after the wave of draining energy washes through the cathedral, three towering skeletal shapes rise up from the rubble—one near the buried doors to the clocktower, one near the middle of the area, and one just north of the ruined altar. These three skeletal hulks appear as 30-foot-tall giants, and they immediately move to attack the PCs. At the same time, three dark shapes emerge from the caryatid of Urgathoa to the south—a trio of greater shadows. All of these undead fight until destroyed. They won’t pursue the PCs out of the area and heal back to full Hit Points after an hour.

Stage 2: Disease.name: Stage 2: Disease
Stage 2: Disease.text:
The second stage of opposition begins 10 minutes after the PCs defeat the undead of stage 1 or immediately upon the PCs entering the cathedral if they leave the area for more than 10 minutes before returning. This time, a foul-smelling crust of filth seeps from the caryatid of Urgathoa, and a moment later, the falling rain transforms into a cloud of buzzing, glistening flies. This wave of unholy energy carries contagion. All PCs in the area must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:25|options:inflicts:enfeebled] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 24 hours as their bodies grow weary and agonized from sickness.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.aGCIKeSAO2yb078H.PlaylistSound.KSQriZbmLRt3Vlag]{Flies}

As the second stage starts, you can play this buzzing ambience sound!

Encounter

Moderate 11

@UUID[Actor.bb5Z4z4EHb5LbCLK]{Leukodaemons x4}

Creatures: The flies revert to rain an instant later as four leukodaemons appear on the walkways above—one near the entrance to the clocktower at area @UUID[.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1c}, one to the south on the upper floor near the entrance to area @UUID[.QSqT538Ma6NnufC7]{G2}, one to the east above the secret door at area @UUID[.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1d}, and one on the walkway clinging to the northeast wall.

These leukodaemons can sense PCs who are enfeebled from the flies via their plaguesense and prefer to target those PCs. The daemons open combat by attacking at range with their longbows and make free use of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.VlNcjmYyu95vOUe8]{Translocate} to reposition in the cathedral as needed to get better shots at the PCs. As soon as one of these daemons is engaged in melee, the others converge to aid them. As with the undead, the daemons fight to the death but don’t pursue foes out of the cathedral, and they heal back to full Hit Points if left alone for an hour.

Stage 3: Gluttony.name: Stage 3: Gluttony
Stage 3: Gluttony.text:
The third stage of opposition begins 10 minutes after the PCs defeat the leukodaemons of stage 2 or immediately upon the PCs entering the cathedral if they leave the area for more than 10 minutes before returning. This time, the wet, uncomfortable sound of countless mouths chewing and gnashing unseen food fills the air as the rain takes on a disturbingly warm and greasy sensation, as if it had become the drool of thousands of sloppy eaters somewhere far above in the churning storm. This manifestation of the curse’s energies is more subtle than a rain of blood or cloud of flies yet remains just as unpleasant to experience. All PCs in the area suddenly taste and smell all matter of overly textured and strangely off-flavored favorites on their tongues and in their mouths; they must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:25|options:inflicts:clumsy] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 24 hours as they suddenly feel bloated and tired from overeating.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.aGCIKeSAO2yb078H.PlaylistSound.C479mnuOo7i7SZ4X]{Cacophony Of Gluttony}

As the third stage starts, you can play this ambience sound for the cacophony of gluttony!

Encounter

Moderate 11

@UUID[Actor.G3D4rcYmVv4eusog]{Soul Gluttons x2}

Creatures: A moment after this unsettling sensation, a pair of dark clouds descend from above. These clouds swiftly coalesce into a pair of extraplanar predators known as soul gluttons, and as they descend, their toothy mouths open and their claws reach out to grasp the PCs. The soul gluttons use their magic for the first few rounds of combat while they fly above the PCs before descending to engage in melee. As with the undead and daemons, the soul gluttons fight to the death but don’t pursue foes out of the cathedral, and they heal back to full Hit Points if left alone for an hour.

Stage 4: Final Fight.name: Stage 4: Final Fight
Stage 4: Final Fight.text:
The fourth and final stage of opposition begins 10 minutes after the PCs defeat the two soul gluttons, but at the start of those 10 minutes, the storm outside intensifies. The rain returns to blood, clouds of flies fill the air, and a sickly-sweet smell of rotting, formerly delicious food wafts from everywhere. These effects are purely cosmetic but persist until those 10 minutes pass (or until the PCs leave the area for more than 10 minutes before returning, in which case these strange effects don’t extend out into the surrounding storm).

Encounter

Severe 11

@UUID[Actor.HxfGix5hfdApKP1A]{Ryhasphinea Arudora} @UUID[Actor.fCsCDQAH23UOtECx]{Zombie Dragons x2}

Creatures: Once the strange phenomena passes, the caryatid of Urgathoa suddenly seems to animate, the stone turning to rotten flesh and bone as a raspy feminine voice calls out to the PCs, words cutting through the sound of the raging storm with ease. “You who would stand before my kin’s attempt to return this blessing to your world. Approach and be judged—not by the goddess of your false and comforting death, but by the goddess of true death! Bow before me, and know what it is to serve eternal, without fear of what lies beyond! This can be your forever as well, if you but bend the knee to my command!”

As she speaks, the figure appears to peel off from the column, manifesting as a 14-foot-high monstrosity—her upper half resembles a horned woman, while ethereal tatters of flesh and corpse cloth churn in a gown of decay from her lower half.

This individual isn’t Urgathoa, but one of her high-priestesses—Ryhasphinea Arudora. PCs foolish enough to obey and bow before her are quickly rewarded with a sardonic smile and a devastating blow from her scything blade. The PC takes critical damage from accepting this blow, and if that’s enough to kill them, their soul immediately rises as a ghost bound to Ryhasphinea’s commands. And first among those commands are to aid her in slaughtering those PCs who chose to resist.

As the battle begins, twin roars of fury tear through the cathedral as two massive undead allies rip free from the rubble in the southern part of the room—a pair of zombie dragons. These zombie dragons obey Ryhasphinea’s mental commands, giving them more tactical acumen than most zombies have. She directs them to engage PCs on the ground in melee while she flies up into the higher reaches of the temple to attack them with her magic. She doesn’t quail from melee, however. If the PCs flee, she sends the dragons after them before pursuing herself—hunting them relentlessly. If the PCs manage to evade her, Ryhasphinea turns her attention to Maiserene, making a big show of attacking the village in an attempt to force another confrontation with the PCs. How much damage she does if the PCs continue to avoid her is left to you to determine, but it should be significant.

Once she’s destroyed, Ryhasphinea shrieks in frustration. The vile ritual of the soulphage she’d spent so many centuries preparing inverts, afflicting her rapidly as it causes her to explode, as described in her share blessings ability. Her soul is then visibly whisked away into her tower at area @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.i6VM7zXFCXSnQqKp]{J3c}. All that remains behind is her hourglass—the key to unlocking the vault of Bastardhall.

Treasure in the Cathedral

@UUID[Actor.hF8ywT18xB3jVJuK]{Altar} @UUID[Actor.bL4MDcKVzr1Atity]{Column} @UUID[Actor.bCu8ZhGGPS7A8P0J]{Buried Treasure}

Once Ryhasphinea and the zombie dragons are destroyed during phase 4, the storm reverts to normal, and the PCs feel a wave of relief, as if a pall of dread that had unknowingly settled over them had suddenly been washed away. Any @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled} conditions any characters currently suffer is removed.

Any PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} among the ruins of the broken altar finds a softly glowing gemstone under the shattered remains: a major soulheart. The first PC to touch this major soulheart receives a brief memory of Ausken Dast visiting the cathedral with a sobbing blond woman. The two approach a dusty, abandoned altar, and he offers her comfort as she places flowers on the altar, obviously mourning someone. Seconds later, their private moment is interrupted by a shrill woman who storms in and orders them out of the cathedral—this is Ryhasphinea, soon after her arrival, sending Ausken and his lover away with words of warning that “the cathedral is closed to visitors until it can be restored.”

A PC who Seeks the caryatid column now sees that it no longer depicts Urgathoa and that it has reverted to a depiction of Pharasma—although a brass gear has been impaled in Pharasma’s neck, almost as if it flew at the pillar with great force in an attempt to decapitate her. A PC can pull the gear free with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open}; this gear is one of those missing from the gearworks above—see @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

A Search of the entire cathedral is a grueling task that takes 3 hours in the rain and rubble, but doing so rewards the PCs with the discovery of several additional items of value buried in the detritus: a standard grade dawnsilver dagger, a horn of exorcism, a wand of breath of life, and bracers of devotion.

High Priest's Room.name: High Priest's Room
High Priest's Room.text:
Broken stained glass windows adorn the walls of this large room. Rain splashes through the frames, slowly soaking the furniture and carpet within. The room is dusty with cobwebs but might have once been a fine bedroom for a priest. A personal shrine with five skulls sitting on it stands in the northeast corner facing a fireplace against the opposite wall. Dark blue curtains partially obscure the sleeping area to the south, which includes a large four-poster bed, writing desk, and tall, elegant armoire. A brass gear has been impaled into the top of the armoire.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.Sg63Fq17xN7daPYI]{Shrine} @UUID[Actor.Nb0fM0GUVpwJTRM0]{Inside Armoire} @UUID[Actor.EE2nRRxW5SzWlukQ]{Armoire Top}

Ryhasphinea was the most recent occupant of this room, although since the curse struck, she’s lost her inclination to visit and never returned here. The shrine near the wall is devoted to Urgathoa—the skulls atop the shrine were secretly taken by Ryhasphinea from the crypts below and belonged to the five priests of Pharasma who died while serving in Castle Arudora. See area @UUID[.cvqO7qaa6g64fMDL]{G6} for more details should the PCs seek to return these skulls.

Inside the armoire hang several moldering vestments, but a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} inside the armoire and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:23|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check (or who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the room with a successful @Check[perception|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check) discovers a hidden panel in the back Ryhasphinea never noticed—inside hangs a suit of +2 resilient greater ready chainmail decorated with Pharasma’s religious symbol. A +2 striking astral dagger is tucked into one of the deeper pockets of the outfit, along with a scroll tube containing a scroll of field of life.

Finally, the brass gear embedded in the top of the armoire is one of those from the gearworks, having lodged here after phasing through several walls during the fall of Castle Arudora. Removing the gear takes a simple Interact action—see @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

Clocktower.name: Clocktower
Clocktower.text:
A hallway surrounds a curving staircase that wraps around a ten-foot-wide pillar in the middle of this octagonal chamber. The hallway’s outer walls are carved with depictions of dozens, perhaps hundreds, of people from all walks of life standing in lines winding through an immense graveyard, yet someone has defaced these images to add crude but effectively frightening flocks of ravenous birds swooping down to peck at faces and pluck out eyes.

With a successful @Check[religion|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}, a PC recognizes the carvings as typical decorations in clocktowers associated with the church of Pharasma—here are depicted the recent and not-so-recent dead standing in line in the Boneyard, awaiting judgment from the Lady of Graves. The birds were added by less talented sahkil hands as a way to defile the carvings.

The stairs wind down to area G3b on the ground floor, which was once the main entrance to the clocktower but is now sealed off by rubble outside in the cathedral. Several crates of clockwork repair tools, spare parts, and containers of oil can be found here. The stairs also wind upward, climbing to one of the highest points of Bastardhall—the gearworks (area @UUID[.osl3dmryGXkoTcAc]{G4}) are some 220 feet above the level of the cathedral floor.

Encounter

Low 11

@UUID[Actor.CzNZG7eukyjlg28r]{Vinlachs x4}

Creatures: Once a towering monument to one of Castle Arudora’s strongest patrons, the church of Pharasma, and an audacious display of wealth and technology, the Arudora clocktower now stands silent, the home of sahkils whose very presence defiles the place even further. Four vinlachs roost in this central chamber now—one on the lower floor, two here on the upper floor, and another one 100 feet above on the stairs. If combat takes place in area @UUID[.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1}, these four sahkils all gather on the upper floor (area G3a) and lie in wait for an hour, ready to attack, before they retreat back to their previous positions. Once combat begins, the vinlachs fight to the death, pursuing the PCs relentlessly to finish them off if they flee.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.th1WcebHzYH4ywkY]{Embedded Gear}

A PC who enters the lower floor (area G3b) automatically spots another of the missing gears, this time embedded in the ground. A PC can wrench it free with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:28] check; see @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

Gearworks.name: Gearworks
Gearworks.text:
A flight of stairs winds down in the middle of this large octagonal room. The ceiling soars to a cavernous height of over a hundred feet, although the exact distance is hard to tell due to the seven differently sized bells and the tangle of gears, clockwork machinery, and support beams that fill most of the space. More gears adorn the walls of the room. All the clockwork is motionless and, in several places, appears to be missing key gears entirely, while fragments of twisted metal and shattered wood lie scattered across the floor.

Encounter

Moderate 11

@UUID[Actor.Rx11CaeXr31RC7CK]{Pakalchis x4}

Creatures: These gearworks are currently inoperable, but before the PCs can even start the work of getting them back into operation so the clocktower’s clock can once again function, they must deal with this chamber’s current occupants— four pakalchi sahkils. As creatures who prey upon insecurity and broken emotional bonds, these sahkils enjoy the mood and energy in this room—one of the greatest monuments to Charg and Urgathoa’s triumph over the works of the faithful of Pharasma. They attack as soon as they notice the PCs but have an additional advantage—the long, entangling vines each pakalchi extends can reach out to grasp onto the surrounding machinery and gears, giving these creatures a surprisingly swift climb Speed they use to remain out of melee and to attack at range with thorns or spells. They’re particularly fond of using @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OsOhx3TGIZ7AhD0P]{Dominate} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qwlh6aDgi86U3Q7H]{Suggestion} on a PC to wrench free gears and then flee the area with commands to hurl the gears into Lake Laroba. Each PC who succumbs to this demand adds another 8 hours to the initial repair work needed for the gears (in addition to abandoning their allies to the fight), but fortunately, these missing gears, unlike the 13 key gears already scattered throughout Bastardhall, can be replaced with new gears if they can’t be recovered easily. The pakalchis fight to the death but don’t pursue fleeing PCs from this chamber.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.iMXLjWuh600i5YDq]{Small Box}

A 30-minute @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} of the cluttered area (or a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the north wall and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check) turns up a small box that tumbled behind the northern gears. Within can be found a set of sterling clockworker’s tools that grant a +1 item bonus to Crafting checks to repair clockworks and a wand of scouting eye previously used to get a closer look at higher gears and machinery without having to clamber up into the rafters.

Repairing the Gearworks

If the party takes 10 minutes to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EwgTZBWsc8qKaViP]{Investigate} the gears, they can confirm that 13 gears are missing. Before any attempt to replace the gears can take place, the entire structure must be cleaned and oiled with the supplies in area @UUID[.jZnvyQePE7QRZcmH]{G3b}—this procedure requires 8 hours of work, and a PC must succeed at a @Check[crafting|dc:28|options:repairing-the-gearworks] check. On a failure, the time is wasted, while on a critical failure, the gears suddenly turn for a moment before grinding to a halt, but not before dealing @Damage[(4d12+30)[bludgeoning]] damage on the PC (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic] save).

Once the gearworks are prepared, replacing the 13 missing gears is a simple task—provided the PCs have recovered those gears, which are scattered throughout Bastardhall. Replacing a gear requires a single Interact action. Any attempt to replace a missing gear with a brand-new gear always results in the replacement gear being just slightly out of true with the others and thus nonfunctional—only the 13 original gears will do.

Once all 13 gears are replaced, the machinery immediately grinds to life, and the clock automatically resets to the correct time, but as the gears wind and work, the entire thing gives out an eerie, frightening sound not unlike that of a monstrous roar. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[arcana|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} realizes this roar came from some kind of dragon—on a critical success, they identify it as the roar of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core-2.Actor.aX8XLPYr0wNlDX4h]{despair dragon}. Once this roar fades, the clocktower bells ring out every hour without fail, while the clock faces themselves function normally. This draws the attention and awe of most of Bastardhall’s remaining residents but doesn’t otherwise affect encounters in the castle.

What it does affect is Pharasma’s attention. Restoring and repairing the gearworks not only fulfills one of the three requirements for the PCs to achieve a perfect victory over the @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.iIIzG8EEQwsCV7an]{Bastardhall Curse}, but it also invests the PCs with divine intercession.

A complete list of missing gears and their locations can be found on the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.kKMa229quJDLEUfk#gear-locations]{Gear Locations} table.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Clean Clocktower" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager if the PCs successfully clean and oil the structure!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.9BKpC7iNjOJl9EHp]{Unassuming Stool}

Upon returning the 13th gear, in addition to the additional benefits listed in the Reward block below, a sudden flash of light draws attention to an otherwise unassuming stool sitting in the southeast corner of the room. Here, a pure soulheart has appeared. The first PC to touch the soulheart immediately understands how to activate this potent treasure.

Reward

Each time a PC returns a missing gear, that PC gains a variant of @UUID[Item.0vmwZrIhm5rWHkYh]{Pharasma’s minor boon}—once, that PC gains a +2 status bonus to a single check. The PC can apply this bonus after they determine the result, and it can potentially change the degree of success. A PC can earn this boon multiple times, but if they already have the boon, it’s granted to a different PC in the party who doesn’t have the boon. If all PCs currently have the boon, no boon is granted for that work’s return.

Upon returning the 13th gear, instead of granting Pharasma’s minor boon, every PC is granted @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.boons-and-curses.Item.xrSgGobm5QtTcABQ]{Pharasma’s moderate boon}: they all gain mastery over the energies of life and death. Their Strikes deal 1 vitality damage to undead. Spells that deal vitality damage to undead gain a +1 status bonus to damage per spell rank, and their spells that heal the living gain a +1 status bonus to the Hit Points restored per spell rank.

Grant the PCs 80 XP for repairing the gearworks.

Crypts.name: Crypts
Crypts.text:
This ten-foot-wide hallway is lined in brick, with an arched ceiling that reaches a height of fifteen feet. Every several feet along the walls, two ten-foot-wide, three-foot-tall niches are set into the wall, one atop the other. Many of these niches contain plain stone sarcophagi.

The Castle Arudora crypts were meant to house generations of Arudoras, temple servants, and some of the house servants and guards who excelled in service. With room for nearly 60 occupants, Castle Arudora became Bastardhall long before enough generations had passed to require relocating the oldest bones. The stairs in the northwest corner (area G5a) lead down to that ossuary (area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.0Rk4YVTfXBvgVJpW]{E10}) and up to area @UUID[.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1c}.

This northern ring of crypts served as a place for favored guards and servants to be buried, and here, most of the niches contain sarcophagi containing long-dead skeletons The southeast doors to area @UUID[.cvqO7qaa6g64fMDL]{G6} have the following sign carved into the door lintel: “Pharasmin Crypts,” while the doors to area @UUID[.Bow5E5zzvV1g4WjZ]{G7} have this carved above them: “Family Crypts.”

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.maHaC9jJNyUwILdz]{Amondi} @UUID[Actor.ZaC0d2uDojDe1x49]{Jazlin} @UUID[Actor.GRKuCXILfcrpzZDX]{Lerrisu}

Creatures: When the curse took hold of Castle Arudora, the unholy energies corrupted the still-not- judged spirits of three adventurers who once traveled with Maiserene’s priestess, Shirail, who’d arranged soon after her arrival as Maiserene’s priestess for their urns of ashes to be placed in urns herein. These three ghosts were the ones who murdered Shirail on that fateful night, and ever since, they’ve been bound here to the crypts where their ashes remain, freed to wander the surrounding countryside and look for new victims only once every 100 years when Bastardhall returns to Golarion.

The three ghosts are Amondi (once a human rogue who fights with a ghostly knife), Jazlin (once an elf ranger who fights with a ghostly battle axe), and Lerrisu (once a dromaar bard who fights with a ghostly rapier); each ghost appears as a phantasmal version of who they were in life, their ghostly faces now perpetually twisted into visages of hatred and rage. The three ghosts manifest swiftly as soon as the PCs enter the crypts, emerging from their urns at area G5b and knowing only that the living have entered the area. They creep into the surrounding halls, hiding in the walls in search of the PCs—upon finding the PCs, they gather then attack by rolling Stealth for initiative.

On the first round of combat, the three ghosts each attempt to possess a different PC, doing their best to possess someone who either shared their ancestry or class in life. A ghost who manages to possess a PC spends their first action thereafter simply cackling in delight at their new body, then uses that body to attack the other PCs. A ghost who fails to possess a PC abandons that tactic for the rest of the battle and instead fights using tactics similar to those they used in life. While the three ghosts have similar stats, they each possess a unique special ability to play to these tactics, but denied these abilities, the ghosts simply use their ghostly hand Strikes. They can’t leave the crypts unless they possess a body. Otherwise, they fight until destroyed. They pursue fleeing creatures through this area and areas @UUID[.cvqO7qaa6g64fMDL]{G6}–@UUID[.Bow5E5zzvV1g4WjZ]{G7} relentlessly.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.CyoEOOlxRtOwSXEI]{Upper Niche}

While most of the niches contain sarcophagi, the upper niche at area G5b contains three pottery urns, each of which contains the cremated ashes of one of the three ghosts’ long-dead physical bodies. As long as the ghosts are still able to rejuvenate, any damage done to these urns is automatically repaired in seconds—they can’t be destroyed, nor can their ashes be removed until the ghosts are at rest.

Among the urns glows a small gemstone. This item is a major soulheart; the first PC to touch it receives a brief memory of Shirail Animender placing the three urns in the niche, sobbing softly as she offers prayers of remembrance as an elderly priestess of Pharasma looks on behind her.

Side Quest Completion

A PC who brings all three urns down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.oQOmNJ7YInR10ecC]{A9} for Shirail to cleanse them completes her @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.OoslGgDkvU7MPY5k#side-quest]{side quest}.

Pharasmin Crypts.name: Pharasmin Crypts
Pharasmin Crypts.text:
These crypts look similar to those in area @UUID[.e6z8NTXgpq400EZk]{G5}, save that only the lower alcoves contain sarcophagi. Interned within each of these five sarcophagi are the remains of the five Pharasmins who served for a time in the cathedral above before dying of natural causes during the castle’s 95 years before the curse took it. The lids of all five sarcophagi have been pried open, and the skulls of the five skeletons within are all missing.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.eJZnTK2kIvD5HlwM]{Ribs}

Ryhasphinea took the skulls of her five predecessors here as part of her work to befoul the cathedral. The five skulls are kept in area @UUID[.QSqT538Ma6NnufC7]{G2}. Returning a skull to its proper place in its sarcophagus among the other bones causes a soft sigh of relief to issue from the remains. At the same time, a single, strange blue rose suddenly grows from the ribs of the skeleton, and the PC who returned the skull feels a sense of thanks and knows the rose is a gift—a minor manifestation of Pharasma’s thanks for the kindness. Each of them are bonebloom roses. No more than five bonebloom roses grow here, one for the first time each skull is returned.

Family Crypts.name: Family Crypts
Family Crypts.text:
These crypts look similar to those in area @UUID[.e6z8NTXgpq400EZk]{G5}. Here, the Arudoras who dwelled and died in the castle were to be put to rest. While a sarcophagus sits in each alcove, one above the other, only 13 of the 16 have names on them. Of those 13, only seven have dates of death—and of those, only three actually contain bones at all. The sarcophagi for Raudltz (b. 4171), Alisendra (b. 4174), Jinnivere (b. 4192), Augsten (b. 4194), Ryhasphinea (b. 4169), and Dazerien (b. 4188) are empty and contain only their dates of birth. The names and contents of the other seven are as follows.

Demiterus Arudora (4150– 4189) A complete skeleton lies within, but with a minute’s examination, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[medicine|dc:20] or @Check[perception|dc:30] check notes gouges on the ribs, as if the man had been stabbed in the heart by a blade—a curious wound for someone who supposedly died from drowning to suffer.

Eragayl Arudora (4093–4158) If opened, the interior is revealed to be empty, pristine, and unused. While the public believed Eragayl died in 4158, he actually died in 4189, a prisoner of his own son in area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.MG8bJRohTuzWIbDI]{H6} far below; his sarcophagus was never used.

Irrokcis Arudora (4118–4189) Like Eragayl’s, this sarcophagus’s interior is empty and unused.

Neesha Arudora (4150–4189) Like Demiterus’s remains, this skeleton bears signs of death by blade—only this time, the gouges are to vertebrae in the neck.

@UUID[Actor.t7pt2BlRjyDMdeZ1]{Tasifinie Arudora} (4092–4148) If opened, a small swarm of ghostly spiders scuttles out—a harmless but unnerving minor haunt effect that echoes poor Tasifinie’s fate. Her cobweb-tangled bones lie within, and buried alongside her is a longsword in a dusty, cobweb-encrusted scabbard. This is Fearcutter, Eragayl’s legendary sword.

@UUID[Actor.yHY0HbcLqqd9gdEe]{Velicarn} (4192–4213) This sarcophagus’s name is not chiseled on it—it’s instead smeared on the stone in what appears to be fresh blood—a manifestation of the curse, as Velicarn was known to exist only by Raudltz, and even then only for a short time before his death on the night of the curse. Within can be found an unusually bloody vile remnant.

Zasha Arudora (4120–4152) This sarcophagus is empty and unused, as after she died in childbirth in 4152, her widower Irrokcis supposedly sent her body and that of their dead child home to her family—but in fact, he took their remains down into his secret vault far below (area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.MG8bJRohTuzWIbDI]{H6}).

Inner Sanctum.name: Inner Sanctum
Inner Sanctum.text:
A clammy pale fog hangs thick in the air of this room. To the north, two rows of three alcoves line the walls, each containing a smashed stone sarcophagus, while to the south, the room descends down a wide flight of stairs to a domed chamber in which six large dark shapes are slumped against the walls; meanwhile, a softly green glowing altar shimmers atop a low platform in the center of the room under a thirty-foot-high domed roof.

Once the inner sanctum of the cathedral of Pharasma, it was here that Ryhasphinea spent the bulk of her time corrupting and befouling the cathedral’s sanctity in secret, transforming this chamber into one devoted to Urgathoa instead. The sarcophagi to the north were to contain the remains of the various temple high-priestesses, but at the time Ryhasphinea arrived, only three contained any remains—all those (as well as the sarcophagi) were among the first things she destroyed.

As part of her blasphemies, Ryhasphinea maintained an unholy consecration to Urgathoa in this chamber, but the curse augmented those effects to make them permanent as long as the curse persists. In this room, worshippers of Urgathoa (including the creatures who guard within) gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, skill checks, saving throws, and Perception checks, while the PCs take a –1 status penalty to these rolls. While this effect is permanent, it can be countered with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} as if it were a 6th-rank spell. It can also be countered automatically if the chamber’s guardians are slain and a PC either Strikes the altar with Fearcutter or offers a prayer to Pharasma or Shelyn at the altar as a 1-minute activity with a successful @Check[religion|dc:28] check. If this blasphemous effect is ended, the preliminary effects that take place during the four stages of opposition in area @UUID[.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1} no longer occur, and the creatures the PCs face in each remaining stage of those fights are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for the first 2 rounds of combat.

The six “dark shapes” were once towering stone statues of Pharasma that Ryhasphinea systematically reduced to heaps of rubble over the course of dozens of visits here.

Encounter

Severe 11

@UUID[Actor.XbaIHmvgqjLChTKq]{Sanctum Guardians x2}

Creatures: Ryhasphinea was rewarded for her service here by Urgathoa, who graced her with two guardians to stand vigil within this inner sanctum. These living guardians are fiends who resemble Urgathoa herself, sent here from Abaddon to serve the cathedral’s new ruler. Their role hasn’t changed much with the advent of the curse, and as these two guardians have never had cause to leave the inner sanctum, they don’t even realize anything above has changed. Ageless and immune to the effects of starvation or thirst, they swiftly react as they notice the PCs, thick layers of dust cascading from their frames as they lurch into motion for the first time in centuries.

Each of the sanctum guardians has the same statistics as a tomb giant, save that they have the fiend and unholy traits as well as their normal traits. They can hurl fragments from any of the destroyed statues as rocks but prefer to fight in melee with their scythes so they can be ready to use their Font of Death if any foes perish. They fight to the death and pursue fleeing PCs throughout the crypts, returning here only if their victims escape up or down the stairs at area @UUID[.e6z8NTXgpq400EZk]{G5a}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.R49UhAbQIIrfxWpp]{Southern Heap}

Ryhasphinea didn’t destroy all the treasures she gathered from the cathedral, for she recognized their value even though their purpose and appearance annoyed or unsettled her. Instead, she heaped these things against the south wall, intending some day to have them pawned far from the castle or to offer them as future sacrifices to Urgathoa. These items include a +2 greater striking vitalizing dagger, a greater shining symbol, a 5th-rank wand of heal, a moderate cloister robe adorned with Pharasmin imagery, and a thick book about the cycle of souls that contains the formulas for three rituals: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.7Fd4lxozd11MQ55N]{Atone}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Dbd5W6G8U2vzWolN]{Consecrate}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.kqhPt9344UkcGVYO]{Resurrect}.

In addition, Ryhasphinea stashed a stunning work of art here that she received her brother Raudltz’s permission to “borrow” from the castle gallery. This piece is a large, 3 Bulk oil painting—a companion piece to the one in area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.3bUvrSflCdnQOijp]{D12} that depicts a scene from the Shining Crusade that never occurred: a pre-ascension Iomedae being slain by Tar-Baphon. Ryhasphinea was taken with the painting and had plans to some day get it retouched to depict Iomedae being slain by Urgathoa, but she never got around to it and kept the painting in storage here. The first time the painting is handled, it triggers a memory of Eragayl arguing with his son Irrokcis about the appropriateness of displaying this near-blasphemy in the castle gallery. This painting, despite its provocative subject matter, belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}); see @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{Lost Artwork} for more details.

The Private Halls.name: The Private Halls
The Private Halls.text:
The upper floors of Bastardhall were the Arudora family’s private wings. Private dining areas, baths, libraries, lounges, and more were set aside here for the family and their closest friends, while numerous spacious bedrooms gave everyone plenty of privacy of their own. The uppermost reaches of the private halls consisted of a large attic and a solarium that Raudltz converted into a support for another one of his hobbies—astronomy.

It was in this section of the castle that the Bastardhall Curse first took hold, spreading swiftly from the library to consume the entire island. Unlike the other regions of the castle, the private halls were largely empty at the time, with the exception of the castle’s au pair and Raudltz himself. It would take years for these areas to begin to become populated again, with the primary push for that increased population coming from Raudltz.

Transformed by the curse into a vampire, Raudltz spent the first few decades of the first century of his new unlife in a constant state of self-hatred and idle fury, enraged that all he was taken away because of a single indiscretion. It didn’t matter to Raudltz that he’d often cheated on his wife, Alisendra, or that he might have more illegitimate children out there—the one who made it back and brought this curse down upon him was the only one who mattered.

Yet that bastard, Velicarn, was protected and favored by Charg, which Raudltz swiftly learned meant he couldn’t take direct action to avenge himself. Instead, Raudltz grew increasingly obsessed with the idea that even the smallest part of his legacy and holdings could somehow be passed on to Velicarn upon his death. Unable to take direct action, he opted instead for indirect action. For the next several decades, Raudltz worked to fill the private halls with more life—more “children” of his own creation who could become his beneficiaries and erode whatever inheritance Velicarn might be able to claim. That such mundane matters of wills and inheritances were now far beyond him and his estate never even occurred to Raudltz. Only the goal of placing as many “legitimate heirs” between himself and Velicarn mattered. That Raudltz’s new “children” were nothing more than soulbound dolls or other minor constructs infused with fragments of spiritual residue was irrelevant.

Ironically, as the centuries wore on, it was Velicarn who became the main source of “new children” for Raudltz to recruit. Each time Bastardhall manifested on Golarion, Velicarn rode out and gathered those of the Arudora bloodline. When they returned here, Raudltz was quick to recruit those who, to him, represented what he preferred in his new family—strong good looks and hearty appetites. To these chosen few he offered the gift of vampirism, while the others were left to meet their own fates and, soon enough, add their Arudora souls to Charg’s collection.

Now, vampires are the primary denizens of the private halls. While there aren’t many, they all view themselves as Raudltz’s children and constantly jockey for positions of favor, even though Raudltz rarely emerges from his observatory above to grace these vampires with his attention. In order to progress, the PCs must confront and defeat Raudltz Arudora, but if they do so without first undermining and manipulating the web of alliances shared by his children, these vampires rise up in his defense if their “father” is attacked, resulting in a potentially devastating combat the PCs will have little to no hope of surviving.

Entering the Private Halls.name: Entering the Private Halls
Entering the Private Halls.text: The private halls are located above the reception halls in the central reaches of Bastardhall, and the simplest way for the PCs to gain access to these upper floors is via one of the stairwells from the reception hall. Once the PCs return @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.HKSpj0db5owAuA1v]{Dazerien’s thumbscrew} to the fountain at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3}, the solidification of these upper floors should be immediately apparent to the PCs since they’ll have an unobstructed view as the aboveground features of the castle—other than the towers above and the entirety of the temple—form fully into view.

The Skies Above.name: The Skies Above
The Skies Above.text:
The storm now arrives in full force. Rain pelts down for most of the day and night, letting up only for an hour or two each day. Outdoors, during the rain, characters take a –2 circumstance penalty to vision-based Perception checks from the downpour, and the wind causes a –1 circumstance penalty to ranged Strikes. Unprotected, small open flames outside are snuffed out by the wind or rain. The temperatures remain mild cold outside, and Lake Laroba’s surface grows increasingly choppy—it’s now a @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim} in these waters. Thunder strikes once every few hours, bringing with it distant flashes of lightning after dark.

Sunrise is at 11:00 a.m., and sunset is at 5:00 p.m. The days are 6 hours long, and the nights are 18 hours long.

Private Wing Ambushes.name: Private Wing Ambushes
Private Wing Ambushes.text:
Encounter

Low 10

@UUID[Actor.YAGc6gQ5VrvWyR37]{Phantom Beasts x3}

If the PCs rest in an unsafe area in the private wings, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:5]. On a failure, they’re ambushed while they rest by three phantasmal monsters that resemble ghostly Bastardhall rats—phantom beasts manifested from Bastardhall’s ambient ectoplasm reacting to the feral influence of the vampires who dwell in the area. The phantom rats are shrill, with glowing yellow eyes and unnaturally large fangs, and fight until destroyed. If possible, they attempt to steal any items the PCs might be carrying that they could use against vampires (such as handheld mirrors, garlic, religious symbols, or wooden stakes); with a success, the phantom beast attempts to flee to somewhere else in Bastardhall and hide the stolen object, but remember that it can’t pass through solid barriers while telekinetically carrying a solid object.

Lucid Nightmares.name: Lucid Nightmares
Lucid Nightmares.text:
After unlocking the private halls, the nightmare changes. The PC relaxes in a large library with a cozy book and favorite drink at hand before a roaring fire, only to be interrupted by a mysterious figure who looks familiar in a way the PC can’t place. Notably, this figure isn’t the cloaked apparition that’s appeared before, but someone new, and their face is featureless—just an oval of flesh through which they can still speak. The figure makes claims of being an unknown heir, then as they reach for the PC, their blank face begins to fill in with the PC’s own. Someone places something into the PC’s hand, and a voice—that of the hooded figure of Caydserris, leans in to whisper, “Kill them before they take everything from you.” The PC strikes with the object in their hand, only to realize that object is a sword and that they’ve plunged the blade into their own body just as they wake.

Enduring the Death of the Self

Resist Nightmare @Check[will|dc:27|options:lucid-nightmare,enduring-the-death-of-the-self]

Critical Failure The PC wakes with proditiophobia (fear of betrayal) and can no longer be the beneficiary of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.HCl3pzVefiv9ZKQW]{Aid} action by other PCs, nor can they flank foes with allies. Whenever an ally tries to target the PC with a beneficial effect, the PC must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:26] save to accept the effect without fighting back or fleeing.

Research @Check[society|dc:29|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to understand and anticipate the betrayal before it occurs or @Check[deception|dc:32|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to betray the others first

Effect

@UUID[Item.147kd0p9FH3w2zzJ]{Proditiophobia}

If a PC critically fails to resist this nightmare, use the linked effect to automate their inability to flank, as well as suppress any bonus they gain from Aid, caused by their proditiophobia.

Private Halls Features.name: Private Halls Features
Private Halls Features.text:
Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

The Private Halls locations span multiple scene levels! Here is the breakdown:

  • @UUID[.HiXOGKLx6aYdwEd4]{F1}-@UUID[.5NSykzgTFMXg8qGD]{F8} are found in the Private Halls (Lower) level.

  • @UUID[.bD29m8AJelDO4lpJ]{F9}-@UUID[.i0iXgS3LkApsHWXv]{F14} are found in the Private Halls (Upper) level.

  • @UUID[.s7W49LWLccXqRJ3k]{F15} is found in the Statue level.

  • Finally, @UUID[.TMx9HDShPgst6iZI]{F16}-@UUID[.t2z0PeMStqo5gA8Q]{F19} are found in the Attic level.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.KGH5bGQJre7aAqF0]{Private Halls}

As the PCs explore the Private Halls, you can play this ambience sound.

The vampires who rule the private halls, once a place of comfort, excess, and elegance, have allowed these chambers to fall into filthy disrepair. Dust and cobwebs lie in mounds in disused areas, while mangy rats squeak and scurry constantly—both in the walls and out in the open. These rats are legion but harmless, and if the PCs can cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.BBvV7qoXGdw09q1C]{Speak with Animals} or otherwise communicate with these creatures, the rats could even (at your discretion) be compelled to reveal minor secrets about the private halls. Every room includes at least a few ratholes down along the baseboards, allowing these rats (and, of course, vampires who have turned to mist) to swiftly move unseen between the various rooms of the private halls. A PC who makes themself Tiny or otherwise gains the ability to navigate these rat holes (such as via a casting of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.V8wXOsoejQhe6CyG]{Vapor Form}) could theoretically do the same, but navigating the internal maze of tunnels in the walls is vexing. A PC can move through the walls to any other room in the private halls by spending 10 minutes of wandering, but they must succeed at a @Check[architecture-lore|dc:27] or @Check[survival|dc:29] check to arrive at their intended location after that time; on a failure, the PC ends up back where they started.

All of the windows in the private halls have been bricked up and plastered over in an attempt to keep out the sunlight—even if the PCs do recognize a part of a wall that once held a window, smashing it open is no easier than smashing open any of the external walls. The one exception are the windows in the observatory, which Raudltz has kept clear and clean (but curtained during the day) to facilitate his study of the “stars” in the sky above (area @UUID[.t2z0PeMStqo5gA8Q]{F19}). Likewise, there are no mirrors to be found on this floor save for those that are part of Raudltz’s equipment in the observatory.

The reinforced wooden doors are normally kept unlocked unless otherwise noted in the text. When locked, a door can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Forced Open} with a @Check[athletics|dc:32|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check or with three @Check[thievery|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}.

The private halls are well-lit by lanterns, sconces, and chandeliers fitted with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.lfrhhbTG1nf0fNAQ]{Evercursed Crystals}, although the light these crystals shed here is dim and flickering—PCs who wish for bright light must provide their own illumination.

The Children of Raudltz

Raudltz’s “children” are anything but—they’re all adult humans he’s transformed into vampires. While each of the children has their own unique appearance, personality, and reason to be bitter with their “father,” all eight of these vampires have the same statistics as the typical @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.pPQyoQHTxrE2U7px]{Vampire Count}, save that they add mirrors to the list of things that cause them revulsion (along with garlic or religious symbols). Note that while all of these children were Arudoras in life, they were minor distant relations who had no real place in Castle Arudora until, ironically, they fell victim to its curse. As such, their names aren’t ones the PCs might have become familiar with as a result of researching the Bastardhall Curse. While each can explain how they were brought to the castle in the centuries after it first vanished, their memories of their lives before that are hazy, indistinct, and uninteresting to the vampires.

If the PCs visit the private halls during the day, all of these vampire children are asleep in their coffins in the bricked up attic (area @UUID[.TMx9HDShPgst6iZI]{F16}). If the PCs visit the private halls after dark, they encounter the vampires as indicated in the following areas. These eight vampires swiftly come to Raudltz’s aid if he’s attacked, so a wise group takes the time to confront the vampires individually. Destroying them certainly prevents them from coming to Raudltz’s aid, but these eight vampires are bored and restless—by interacting with each in specific ways, the PCs can earn a vampire’s appreciation and confidence, which allows them to potentially learn more about Raudltz (see Speaking with the Children below) or in some cases secure unique advantages in the conflict to come.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.m0khEHYdDxDw9B1G]{Raudltz Arudora}

Speaking with the Children: Once any of the eight vampire “children” of Raudltz have been convinced to aid the party, a PC can spend 10 minutes gossiping with that vampire to learn more about their “father.”

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[diplomacy|dc:27|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to coax secrets out of the vampire, @Check[deception|dc:29|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to trick secrets out of the vampire, or @Check[intimidation|dc:32|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to force secrets out of the vampire. A critical failure on any of these checks causes that vampire to lose interest in speaking to the PCs about Raudltz—if the PCs haven’t yet maxed out their RP for this research topic, they’ll need to secure the cooperation of another of the vampiric children to continue.

Arudora Library.name: Arudora Library
Arudora Library.text:
All doors into this room are locked; Raudltz carries the only key.

Numerous wooden bookshelves turn this large musty chamber into a bibliophilic labyrinth. Dust covers most of the tomes, but here and there, certain areas of the stacks bear the unmistakable sign of relatively recent handling. Under the musty smell of old books lurks a sharper tang—the unmistakable stink of clotting, rotted blood one might expect to smell on a battlefield, not in a library.

If the PCs enter via the southeastern entrance or once they proceed far enough into the library to see into the open area there, read the following as well.

The source of the rotting blood stench is unmistakable—a mound of gore amid a pool of blood lies in what looks like a crater in the floor, surrounded by shattered remnants of chairs and reading tables. Several nearby bookshelves lie in ruins, their books torn to ribbons. An immense, cold fireplace looms in the southeast corner, its surfaces caked with blood.

The doors in the northwestern part of the room at area F1a open into an impassible wall of green mist until the fallen temple is unlocked, at which point these doors lead to area @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1f}.

In this room, the Bastardhall Curse was born—where Velicarn confronted his father, Raudltz Arudora, and revealed the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.iQLEbANowf4fT8hK]{whispering remnant} he’d brought with him in hopes of cursing the Arudoras, and where Raudltz unwittingly consummated this curse by beheading his bastard son in response to the threat. Raudltz fled the room soon after murdering Velicarn and swiftly had all doors to the library locked.

In the moments after Raudltz locked this room tight, Velicarn’s body rose as a powerful dullahan even as his head was devoured by the discarded whispering remnant, bloating into a huge boil of pustulant gore and tumorous flesh that burst, unleashing the Bastardhall Curse in full force upon the castle. While Velicarn’s undead body made good his escape by smashing through one of the now bricked-up windows in the south wall, the remnants of his head collapsed into the horrible, pulsing mound of gore that remains in this room today.

Since then, Raudltz has visited the library several times—first to muse over what took place here, then a few more times to brick over the windows and relock the doors tight. No Arudora has returned to this room since.

Encounter

Moderate 10

@UUID[Actor.919AP58ceDMPI5IU]{Anophilex} @UUID[Actor.ZfoAitVeBHWM837e]{Velicarn's Head (Haunt)} @UUID[Actor.2p3wbBbpEe5N5fKs]{Velicarn's Head}

Creatures: The gory remnants left behind by the explosion of the whispering remnant exist now as a dangerous clot of fiendish potential—a spawning point for sahkil to crawl into Bastardhall at their whim. One such visitor just arrived not long before the PCs first enter this room—a glistening anophilex sahkil, drawn to the area by the promise of old blood to lick and slurp as much as the beckoning call of Charg’s dire influence. The skittering anophilex creeps into the shadows of the nearby bookstacks if they hear the PCs entering the library, hoping to ambush the party once they approach the remnants of Velicarn’s head (see Hazard, below)—otherwise, the PCs find the creature coiled around this mound as they slurp and lick the eternal blood pool that surrounds them.

Once the anophilex attacks, they fight to the death, doing their best to remain in the area of the haunt since it can’t hurt the sahkil and makes it more dangerous to engage the fiend in melee. The anophilex won’t pursue the PCs if they flee but will mark and remember them, and at some point after (likely when the PCs next rest), the sahkil ambushes them.

Hazard: Velicarn’s head now exists as a gruesome mound of gore and meat, constantly dripping blood into the pool that surrounds it as swiftly as it draws the blood back up to feed upon its own drippings... but as soon as intruders approach, the remains awaken most awfully. Once the haunt is disabled or Velicarn’s head is destroyed (whichever comes first), his head shrieks in frustration, then falls to the ground and shrinks back to normal size. If the PCs have a description of him from Lavinia or elsewhere, they can recognize the head for who it once belonged to automatically.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.mRdeW4Wd1PaPPKCE]{Library Cache}

While several of the books in the southeastern portion of the room have been ruined, the remaining books on the shelves consist of a much larger and more complete version of the visitor’s library downstairs (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.CSZBdjguWV1HWdLb]{D9}), with a focus on natural history, occult matters, Ustalavic history, and unsettling fiction. The collection contains enough books of quality that a PC who spends an hour referencing them when attempting a Nature or Occultism check to Recall Knowledge or any check to Recall Knowledge on the topic of Ustalavic history earlier than the year 4213 gains a +2 item bonus.

The books can also be used to research certain topics associated with Bastardhall and some of the older Arudoras—see Arudora Library below. If the PCs spend 2 hours diligently Searching the entire library, they’ll find several items of value, including a scroll of dreaming potential, a 5th-rank scroll of thoughtful gift, a scroll of truespeech, a book titled Exquisite Eating that contains the formula for the fortifying brew ritual, a 4th-rank wand of translate, a moderate thurible of revelation sitting atop the fireplace mantle to the southeast, and a pair of greater obsidian goggles that has been forgotten under a layer of dust on a high corner shelf.

Effect

@UUID[Item.lKrbw91gQKhJMF1E]{Arudora Library}

If your players @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.t5nBkpjroaq7QBGK]{Research} using the materials found here, use this effect to automate their bonus! The bonus will be automatically toggled on if they use one of the check buttons in the Research block below, or if they make a Recall Knowledge check.

Finally, once the sahkil and the haunt have been dealt with, the fact that the vampires avoid this chamber entirely makes it a safe place for the PCs to rest—they don’t risk ambushes while sleeping in here.

Research

Several Topics (see below)

Arudora Library: The PC spends 2 hours sifting through the books here to learn more about historical topics regarding Bastardhall or on any of the Arudoras believed to be dead before the point when the curse took hold.

Maximum RP 3 per topic (@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.PAMDhjQNkAm8rB5R]{Bastardhall}, @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.CzkcMKPWphpJlkPp]{Demiterus}, @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.gBlukTRHytlzwC1D]{Eragayl}, @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.qi00xNaMBgtsO0LH]{Irrokcis}, @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.FZDFAjuHckZz0QW0]{Neesha}, @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.PNW896yOsktDWXwT]{Tasifinie}, or @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.o5n22VwGbRDh0it6]{Zasha}); Research Checks @Check[library-lore|dc:27|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to find the right books quickly (this check also gains the +2 item bonus from referencing the books here), @Check[society|dc:27|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to know what parts of certain books to skim over when searching for clues, or @Check[perception|dc:32|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to stumble upon the information by chance.

Side Quest Completion

If the PCs were asked by Lavinia to return the cursed coin Velicarn paid her to his remains, what’s left of his head is more than enough to suffice. If the PCs place Velicarn’s cursed coin on his head, the head’s eyes snap open in rage, and the mouth wordlessly spits and screams before it falls quiet, dead once more. The coin glows softly for a moment, and the PCs automatically understand the curse has been lifted and that Lavinia’s side quest has been completed—her ghost can now move on to the afterlife. The coin now functions as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.2cWs7heYDt9jCSJ4]{Fortune’s Coin} (treat the Arudora crest as the seraph side when it’s flipped).

Central Halls.name: Central Halls
Central Halls.text:
The central hall that winds through the lowest floor of the private halls is covered in deep green carpet. Several connections to other parts of the castle can be accessed here. Area F2a serves as a storeroom for servants to keep cleaning supplies, linens, silverware, firewood, and other necessities; there’s nothing of value to be found here.

The stairs at area F2b descend to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.klWkYac4yHUOYGlr]{D27a}.

The stairs at F2c ascend to area @UUID[.bD29m8AJelDO4lpJ]{F9a}.

The secret door at area F2d can be discovered by someone who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in the area and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The stairwell beyond leads down to area @UUID[.t2z0PeMStqo5gA8Q]{F19}.

The spiral stairs at area F2e lead all the way down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.UYzcuhyFPr5jTxCy]{E14} in the dungeon; the door to this stairwell is kept locked. One of Raudltz’s keys can open it, as can a PC who succeeds at four @Check[thievery|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock} or a @Check[athletics|dc:32|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force it Open}.

The stairs at area F2f descend to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.I5xBZSgIpeHNyb21]{D21c}.

Classroom.name: Classroom
Classroom.text:
This long, spacious room contains six small desks and chairs, all lined up and facing a larger desk and chair at the north end of the room. Judging by the room’s decor, it once served as a classroom.

Although Maiserene featured a classroom with seating for more students, the Arudoras would never have sent their own children to such a cramped building or left their education to someone not handpicked by the aristocracy to give them a proper education. Never mind the fact that the latest teacher in Maiserene was more devoted and talented than the au pair the Arudoras retained in the castle or the fact that never in the family’s history have there been more than two Arudora children at once to justify a room this large—appearances must be kept up.

If the PCs visit this room during the night, they find it empty.

Encounter

Moderate 10

@UUID[Actor.2kPiynr0PsKZI0LK]{Linisriel} @UUID[Actor.Gu0cJHGwPd547OtC]{Wraiths x4}

Creatures: The latest two Arudora children, Augsten and Jinnivere, were both raised by an elven au pair named Linisriel, who was in charge of not just seeing to the children’s education but also supervising them during playtime, making sure their meals were up to standard and served in a timely manner, and managing all things involving their cleanliness and health. In the last few years, her duties had grown increasingly light, as the two children had become adults and she’d been considering a potential change of venue for weeks when the curse struck.

In life, Linisriel was a philosopher and an intellectual who never stopped working to make the world a better place (as much as the awful entitled antics of the Arudora children tested her). The curse seized upon these pursuits and warped them, transforming Linisriel into a raja-krodha rakshasa. Now, even as she passes her time in her previous elven form, Linisriel spends hours pontificating upon the banality of goodness, the falsehoods of generosity, and the weakness that is kindness, even as she does so in a soothing voice with a kindly smile. Her lectures are oft attended by manifestations of the cruelty of the Bastardhall Curse, who appear as shifting, smoky red-eyed children made of ash and shadow.

When she notices the PCs, Linisriel smiles and invites them to the front of the classroom, thanking them for visiting and becoming her guests for the day’s lesson. The shadowy children loom, leer, and whisper as Linisriel moves from PC to PC, asking each theoretical questions designed to evoke answers that embrace cruelty. Sample questions include ones like the following:

  • “What is the most efficient way to understand the limits of how much pain a creature can endure?”

  • “If you have no choice but to kill, how do you end a life in a way that you’ll find fulfilling and educational?”

  • “Why is it always a bad idea to give to the needy when they’ve done so little to build themselves up?”

  • “What good does it do to apologize when the one who has been slighted deserved it?”

She asks one question of each PC. When a PC answers in a way that sounds cruel or mean-spirited, the shadowy children giggle in delight, and Linisriel compliments them on their wisdom and clearheaded thinking. When a PC answers in any other way, particularly if they take umbrage with the question or go out of their way to reply in a way that promotes kindness, the children heckle, curse, and mock the PCs while Linisriel appears saddened and disappointed by their reply. A PC who attempts to answer cruelly can opt to really sell their reply by attempting a @Check[deception|dc:28] or @Check[intimidation|dc:28] check. If at least half the PCs succeed at these checks to come off as truly cruel, Linisriel thanks them for their honesty and invites them to retire to her quarters (area @UUID[.7sih5tt9N28Ni3qB]{F4}) for tea, and the shadowy children fade away.

Otherwise, as soon as the PCs attempt to leave (or immediately if they attack), Linisriel and the shadowy children (who in fact are four wraiths) attack, rolling Intimidation for initiative. The wraiths fight until destroyed but don’t pursue the PCs, but Linisriel casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.XXqE1eY3w3z6xJCB]{Invisibility} on herself and attempts to flee into the private halls if reduced below 60 Hit Points. She then stalks the PCs, observing from afar and plotting a way she can use Change Shape to appear as a victim who needs “rescue” so that she can later pick the PCs off one by one.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Reveal Classroom Wraiths" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to hide the shadow students and reveal the wraith tokens!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.XR6jt1SGLZuQSdcg]{Desk}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the room or Linisriel’s desk and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers a hidden catch that opens a narrow secret drawer in which Linisriel kept a wand of legerdemain (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.A2JfEKe6BZcTG1S8]{Fly}) that she can no longer use as a rakshasa. Also in this drawer is a softly glowing crystal—a major soulheart. The first PC to touch this major soulheart receives a brief memory of Esmira arriving at the classroom to meet her friend Linisriel and then loaning the au pair a brightly colored book with the title The Three Curious Elves, blushing as she does so.

Au Pair's Room.name: Au Pair's Room
Au Pair's Room.text:
A bed sits in the northeast corner of this room next to a wooden nightstand covered with an elegant tea set. A dressing table to the south that’s missing its mirror stands next to a lit fireplace in which a kettle simmers. A small round table surrounded by four comfortable chairs rounds out the cozy room’s decor.

Encounter

Trivial 10

@UUID[Actor.2kPiynr0PsKZI0LK]{Linisriel}

Creatures: If the PCs visit this room during the night, they’ll find the rakshasa Linisriel here, in her elf form, as she relaxes with a book and a cup of tea. In this case (or if the PCs impress her in the classroom and earn an invite back here for tea), the pleasantly disguised monster asks the PCs to have a seat while she prepares tea for each of them. The tea she prepares, of course, is from the poisoned tea leaves (see Treasure, below). Once the PCs drink and begin to suffer the toxic effects, she giggles in delight, then attacks them.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.0d81pe0SMOimYHop]{Nightstand} @UUID[Actor.FwQxbagMNBEGGWDu]{Narrow Gap}

The tea service on the nightstand is high quality and worth 80 gp as a set. Of the five jars of tea leaves, four are stale and unremarkable. The fifth contains six doses of black tea that have been poisoned with enervating powder poison. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the bed or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the room for 10 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check notices a colorful book that’s fallen into the narrow gap between the bed and the wall. This tawdry romance novel called The Three Curious Elves tells about the dangers and joys of mistaken identity.

Once the PCs defeat Linisriel, this room is a safe place to rest

Side Quest Completion

Delivering The Three Curious Elves to Esmira Vermidian completes her @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.M6cCO4Hg8Hj8yTBY#side-quest]{side quest}.

Statue Approach.name: Statue Approach
Statue Approach.text:
A ten-foot-wide black carpet runs east to west down the middle of this room, laid out across a polished granite floor. A dozen statues of what appear to be a wide range of aristocrats have been placed to the north and south, each towering depiction standing over fourteen feet tall.

Before the curse fell, the statues here depicted 12 Ustalavic notables, all friends of Eragayl, who helped finance the construction of Castle Arudora. On a closer inspection, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:25] check notes that the two clay statues furthest to the east actually depict Pharasma (to the north) and Shelyn (to the south) dressed as Ustalavic aristocrats. These two clay statues were both provided by religious leaders and friends of Eragayl.

The stairs beyond the door at area F5a descend to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.hqbneLnZW6Vn6LLx]{B2d} below. To the north and south, the stairs at area F5b both ascend to area @UUID[.s7W49LWLccXqRJ3k]{F15} above.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Animate Clay Effigies" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to hide the inanimate clay effigies and reveal their tokens!

Encounter
