Moderate 10

@UUID[Actor.IuVoyT5lkzcWJ6sK]{Clay Effigies x2}

Creatures: The two religious-themed clay statues were more than gifts from Eragayl’s affiliated faiths—they were given as guardians. Of course, the curse has distorted and warped the clay effigies, and now they stand patiently awaiting the opportunity to crush intruders. They don’t move until they’re attacked or until as many PCs as possible are standing within the potential area of their Cast Out abilities, at which point the effigies animate and do just that before switching to melee. The clay effigies fight until they’re destroyed but don’t pursue the PCs out of this area.

Baths.name: Baths
Baths.text:
A pair of large stone bath basins sit to the west and south of this stone-floored room, with short flights of steps leading up to the sides to facilitate entry. A wooden bench lies in the middle of the room, and there are cupboards for holding robes and towels to the north.

While the private rooms all have private bathing facilities, these larger stone baths were intended not for hygiene, but relaxation and therapy. Servants would mix a wide range of oils and crystals into these basins for the Arudoras and their favored guests to relax in. The water in each tub now is a nasty green tint—any PC who immerses themself in the water or drinks it exposes themselves to a potent strain of malaria, save that this strain is a level 10 disease with a DC of 27.

Malaria

Disease 10

  • Disease

A pernicious disease spread by bloodsucking insects, malaria sometimes enters long periods of dormancy. If you succumb to malaria, you may continue to be periodically affected by the disease, even if you’re cured. You can’t reduce your @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened} condition while affected with malaria.

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:27|traits:disease]

Onset 10 days

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} (1 day)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}, and disease recurs every [[/gmr 1d4#Months]]{1d4 months} even if cured (1 day)

Stage 4 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} (1 day)

Stage 5 death

Encounter

Trivial 10

@UUID[Actor.mno9JBZ1XgEHo6m4]{Giant Mosquitoes x4}

Creatures: When the curse struck, four such favored guests were trapped here until they were slain by anophilex sahkils. When their souls returned, they carried with them a fear of blood that was distorted into obsession, and they reincarnated as immense, hungry mosquitoes. The vampires see these creatures as something akin to pets, and a vampire who might want to lure the PCs into a trap could well lead them to this room hoping to give the giant mosquitoes something real to feed upon rather than just being sustained by the curse’s fell power. The mosquitoes cling to the walls of the room and immediately buzz to life and attack any living creature they see, fighting to the death.

Lounge.name: Lounge
Lounge.text:
The carpeting in this room is particularly deep and plush. Two couches sit against the west wall beyond a pair of low glass coffee tables, while to the south, a large brick fireplace is attended by a long wooden table and four padded chairs. A wooden counter to the east contains several drawers and a folding top.

Encounter

Trivial 10

@UUID[Actor.x3wX9TXNDVwZbEaK]{Antavian Arudora}

Creatures: The first time the PCs enter this room after dark, they encounter one of Raudltz’s children—a moody, slender man with a powdered face, tricorne hat, and threadbare courtier’s outfit sits alone in one of the chairs near the lit fireplace as he muses over the mournful song plinking out from an elegant looking music box sitting on the coffee table before him. Upon spotting the PCs, the man stands up, offers a florid bow, and introduces himself as Antavian Arudora, “connoisseur of fine music and appreciator of the auditory arts” before he asks the PCs who they might be—more out of polite duty than real interest. If any of the PCs carries a visible musical instrument, or if a PC asks him about the music box, Antavian grows more excited and wants to know if that PC has any musical talent. If the PC claims they do, Antavian demands a performance, right there and then.

A PC who agrees can spend 5 minutes performing for Antavian, after which they should attempt a @Check[performance|dc:27] check. On a success, tears of blood flow from Antavian’s eyes (that he demurely wipes away with a handkerchief as if they were normal tears), and he thanks the PC for their gift. At this point, Antavian’s emotions get the better of him, and the PCs can ply him for information about Raudltz for 10 minutes (20 minutes if they critically succeeded). Antavian then invites the PC up to his room above for an “additional, more private performance.” If the PC agrees to go alone, Antavian does his best to turn that PC into a vampire, resorting to using his Dominate ability if necessary. If the PC declines, Antavian shrugs, then says he needs to spend time alone considering the performance—he Turns to Mist and leaves the room via a rathole, returning to his coffin in area @UUID[.TMx9HDShPgst6iZI]{F16} to contemplate.

If the PC fails the Performance check or if anyone in the party is rude to him (including if the PCs spend more than a few minutes in idle conversation with him), his anger gets the better of him and he attempts to Dominate the PC who he feels might be the best musician, resorting to combat thereafter. If reduced to 0 Hit Points, he Turns to Mist and flees to his coffin in area @UUID[.TMx9HDShPgst6iZI]{F16}.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.aGCIKeSAO2yb078H.PlaylistSound.WUzTAgTZVJEauk6k]{Music Box}

As the music box plays, you can play this provided sound!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.MsqFKmxzfWEmR5vS]{Coffee Table}

The elegant music box plays a mournful Pharasmin dirge after it’s wound, and as it plays, little metal psychopomps pop up, dance, and move about inside of a glass dome atop it. The music box is 1 Bulk, and the first time a PC handles it, it triggers a memory of Alisendra Arudora bringing the music box here to test a visiting singer to see if she could perform the same dirge, only to humiliate her with a scathing review that sent her fleeing form the lounge in tears. The music box belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}), see @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{Lost Artwork} for more details.

Special: If the PCs succeed at performing for Antavian, his emotions continue to run high for 1 week, during which time he’s too distracted to come to Raudltz’s aid. Grant the PCs XP as if they’d defeated Antavian in combat if they defeat Raudltz within this time frame.

Dining Room.name: Dining Room
Dining Room.text:
This large room with polished wood flooring has a fire roaring in a large fireplace to the west before a pair of high-backed chairs. Two different dining areas occupy the north and south portions of the chamber—to the north is a smaller, more intimate setting, while to the south is a long formal banquet table. A flight of carpeted stairs lead upward to the east.

The stairs to the east lead up to area @UUID[.bD29m8AJelDO4lpJ]{F9b}. Beyond the northwest door, a flight of stairs at area F8a leads up to area @UUID[.i0iXgS3LkApsHWXv]{F14a}.

Encounter

Trivial 10

@UUID[Actor.E28CXZD8VbqNENgi]{Children of Raudltz x4}

Creatures: The southern banquet table was used infrequently for full family dinners—there were a few more seats than there were Arudoras, leaving room for special guests now and then. The first time the PCs enter this room after dark, this table is occupied by four of Raudltz’s children—two male and two female vampires all dressed up with powdered faces and ostentatious wigs as they loudly discuss their frustrations that the night’s “dinner” lacks the proper side dishes.

As undead, vampires have no fear of starvation, yet when they’re denied the blood they crave, they grow increasingly violent and feral. Raudltz has no interest in having his beloved “children” fall to such fates—fortunately for him, the Bastardhall Curse frequently reincarnates lost souls from the soul vortex (area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.EPAmP1TdzmePRO9b]{I}) into fresh, frightened victims for the vampires to feed upon. See @UUID[.#rescued-victims]{Rescued Victims} for more details on these poor souls.

One of these victims is bound hand and foot, gagged and hooded, and laid out like a centerpiece on the banquet table—a softly whimpering man who expects to die at any moment. The four vampires are Ismareska, Jorth, Karthus, and Sissaly Arudora, and as soon as one of them notices the PCs, that vampire stands up from their chair with a delighted clap, then bids the PCs to step forward. All four of these vampires believe the PCs to be part of the castle guard—a role, to them, that’s largely interchangeable with any of the servants, including the chefs. The vampires explain as one might to a slow-witted child that they can hardly be expected to enjoy their meal without proper appetizers. The vampire explains that they and their siblings have only just now decided what would be the perfect accompaniment, “And here you are, ready to provide us the assistance we need! What fortunate timing!”

If the PCs are rude, attempt to rescue the “meal” on the table, or attack, the four vampires rise up with hisses—one saying, “These fools will do fine as appetizers!” before they attack. Destroyed vampires Turn to Mist and retreat through ratholes in the wall to the attic (area @UUID[.TMx9HDShPgst6iZI]{F16}).

On the other hand, if the PCs agree to help, one of the vampires explains, “What would really hit the spot, you see, would be a platter in the vein of Nidalese shuddercheese—only none of those boring fly maggots, please. Instead, fill that wheel of cheese with plenty of blood-bloated middenworm larvae, then return with it here as soon as possible, and you’ll have our gratitude!” A PC who succeeds at a @Check[cooking-lore|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] (or similar food-based Lore) or @Check[society|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} knows that Nidalese shuddercheese is a nauseating and notorious meal of cheese intentionally infested and served with insect larvae. To gather up what the vampires are asking for, the PCs must secure a wheel of cheese from Aron Mordimus in Orm’s Rest (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.msh8hhX94bXBPpbi]{A8}) as long as he’s at least rank 1 in his capacity to provide support. Gathering middenworm larvae is a tougher stunt—if the middenworm infestation in area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.obtffCMeRJgG4QyY]{E5c} is still active, gathering enough larvae is a simple matter of scooping up maggots that remain after the infestation is disabled. If the infestation isn’t active, the PCs must spend [[/gmr 1d6#Hours]]{1d6 hours} hunting and catching individual worms as they wriggle in the waters of the dungeon below. Once the worms are gathered up, they must be “blood-bloated,” which requires a volunteer to allow the worms to feed on their blood, taking @Damage[4d8[piercing]] damage and becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 24 hours as a result.

If the PCs can deliver their faux Nidalese shuddercheese back to this area before the last hour of the night, the vampires are delighted and eagerly dig into the nauseating meal. The combination of the filth and excess of the gratuitous feast fully distracts the vampires, and after they finish the cheese, they lean back in their chairs, sated, before they Turn to Mist and return to their coffins to sleep. In this case, these four vampires don’t join in Raudltz’s defense, and the PCs can rescue the frightened “meal.”

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.li1lVdGt2WmSL7kg]{Near Fireplace}

A large ring of keys hangs from a peg near the fireplace. The majority of these keys are non-magical, and each matches one of the locks to one of the bedrooms upstairs (area @UUID[.Mcpm8IomhSfb7Idn]{F10}); the vampires unlock those doors whenever they wish to “harvest” one of the meals trapped within. One of the keys is in fact a greater skeleton key.

Rescued Victims

Most of the victims of the curse the PCs encounter in Bastardhall are phantoms, monsters, or haunts. Finding low-level victims here in the private halls destined to become vampire meals introduces a new factor. Each of these rescued victims is a level –1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-npc-core.Actor.APn9B54hhRtr0oCQ]{commoner}. Feel free to come up with names and personalities for them if you wish, if only to endear them more to the PCs and to encourage the PCs to get the victims to safety. Delivering them to Maiserene is as safe as any of them will get—the allied phantoms there can shelter them for as long as necessary

Reward: Each victim delivered alive and safe to Maiserene earns the PCs a 10 XP reward, for a total possible reward of 60 XP if all six victims are rescued from areas @UUID[.5NSykzgTFMXg8qGD]{F8}, @UUID[.Mcpm8IomhSfb7Idn]{F10}, and @UUID[.tbuXpUsjFaPXpEM2]{F18}.

Upper Halls.name: Upper Halls
Upper Halls.text: The stairs at area F9a descend to area @UUID[.ndtRFPlOc0RB3Vc5]{F2c}, while those at area F9b descend to area @UUID[.5NSykzgTFMXg8qGD]{F8}. The stairs at area F9c ascend to the attic (area @UUID[.TMx9HDShPgst6iZI]{F16a}).

Bedrooms.name: Bedrooms
Bedrooms.text:
All of these rooms have similar interiors, and all of the doors are locked (@Check[athletics|dc:32|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} or three @Check[thievery|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}.)

This cozy bedroom features a large four-poster bed, a chair and desk, a dresser, and a small, cold fireplace. A screened alcove sets apart a washtub and a chamber pot.

None of Raudltz’s children dwell in these rooms, but they do keep the doors to all eight chambers locked, for their meals reincarnate into these rooms. Three of these rooms (the ones labeled F10a) currently contain a frightened, recently reincarnated humanoid victim. These poor souls have no real memories of how they came to be locked in these rooms and wear clothing found in the dresser; they beg to be saved if the PCs open the doors. See @UUID[.5NSykzgTFMXg8qGD#rescued-victims]{Rescued Victims} for more details.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.ZsRtyI9xn8mLgA5s]{Abandoned Bedroom} @UUID[Actor.rYOja19guPniIqtb]{Ruined Bed}

When Ryhasphinea and her son Dazerien came to live in the castle, Raudltz set aside the two northernmost rooms for them to use, but they quickly decided to live elsewhere and never used these rooms. Dazerien’s (area F10b) appears fully unused, but Ryhasphinea’s (area F10c) still contains many of her possessions. While there’s nothing of monetary value here, her left-behind correspondence, books, notes, and belongings can be investigated to learn more about her.

Finally, in area F10d, one of the gears hurled from the clock tower phased through a wall only to manifest an instant before it smashed into the bed, leaving it in ruins. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the bed or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the room finds a particularly large gear the size of a shield (2 Bulk) amid the broken bed—see @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.7VX2SBgHGbICdyYi]{Ryhasphinea Arudora}

Ryhasphinea’s Belongings: The PCs spend a half hour looking through the large amount of personal belongings, seeking clues about their owner.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[society|dc:27|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to look through the materials and make well-founded assumptions, @Check[religion|dc:29|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to understand the significance of many religious metaphors or notations, or @Check[perception|dc:32|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to notice subtle clues.

Jinnivere's Room.name: Jinnivere's Room
Jinnivere's Room.text:
This bedroom features a large four-poster bed, a few tables and chairs, a dresser, and a large, cold fireplace. Two wooden stands to the north hold ancient-looking fine leather saddles, while paintings of all manner of equestrian scenes hang on the walls.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.zvSfn2VJzYr4JiA2]{Sawhorses} @UUID[Actor.Fg2vkdJqZkKxQncE]{Equestrian Cache}

This room belonged to Jinnivere Arudora. The tack and saddles on the sawhorses are of exceptional quality and grant a +1 item bonus to checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.q9nbyIF0PEBqMtYe]{Command an Animal} while they’re ridden; each saddle is worth 55 gp. Other treasures are hidden here as well, but the PCs must spend 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the room to find them. They include four vials of greater oil of weightlessness, a greater healing potion, and a type I spacious pouch containing several days’ worth of horse feed in sacks and a carefully folded barding of the zephyr.

Augsten's Room.name: Augsten's Room
Augsten's Room.text:
This drably colored chamber features a large four-poster bed that sits to the south opposite an unlit fireplace. Tables and chairs, along with shelves, dressers, and a writing desk, round out the furnishings. A set of long, black curtains run along a wall. A single high-backed chair faces those curtains.

This room belonged to Augsten Arudora. His taste in decor reveals a deeply unimaginative mind, with very little personalizing this room save for what lies beyond the black curtains—a wall fitted with manacles from which four human skeletons hang. Each skeleton’s jaws are wired shut with short iron feeding tubes clenched in the jaws—a grim, horrific display of how Augsten treated those who wronged him.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.gxagnAs3HubRLy7T]{Grim Nightstand}

If the PCs spend 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} this room, they’ll find a few items of value in the nightstand next to the bed, including two greater healing potions, four vials of wyvern poison, and a greater demon mask.

Master Bedroom.name: Master Bedroom
Master Bedroom.text:
A table with two chairs, a pair of shelves, and a vanity table make up the eastern half of this room’s decor, along with a rolltop writing desk attended by a high-backed chair. A large number of books and occult objects sit on a central table. To the north, a screened alcove doesn’t quite hide the three coffins within, while a small, bloodstained shrine sits on a marble pedestal built into the wall to the west.

This room was originally intended to serve as a private lounge, but after his wife perished in the original master bedroom, Eragayl Arudora repurposed this room to be the master bedroom after boarding up the old one at area @UUID[.i0iXgS3LkApsHWXv]{F14}.

The bloodstained shrine was once a small shrine devoted to Shelyn, Eragayl’s patron, but it’s been profaned by the curse—the holy water font is now constantly filled with fresh, warm blood—a particular boon to this room’s inhabitants.

Encounter

Moderate 10

@UUID[Actor.LVg1DLd8sJEVgYe7]{Evanessa Arudora} @UUID[Actor.pCZOTuSYEw3ZBc4b]{Lars} @UUID[Actor.P6uxkT2MYs8eDOWw]{Vikter}

Creatures: The first Arudora whom Raudltz transformed into a vampire after she was brought here a hundred years after the curse struck was an elegant, statuesque woman named Evanessa Arudora. After those first hundred years apart from his wife, Alisendra, who’d fully relocated to her own domain over the reception halls, Raudltz at first saw Evanessa as his new wife, yet it wasn’t long before he grew bored of her companionship and left her to her own devices. With the subsequent seven victims, Raudltz instead treated them as his children instead.

As the most powerful of the vampires other than Raudltz himself, Evanessa has never been challenged for control of this room, which contains the ever- full font of blood that allows her to feed whenever she wishes and, perhaps more importantly, never interact with the other vampires—with two notable exceptions. She transformed two of the Arudoras whom Raudltz had little interest in claiming as his own, making these two strapping men, Lars and Vikter, into her “husbands.”

Unlike the other vampires, these three keep their coffins here in the alcove that once held the chamber pot and washbasin (accoutrements Evanessa had hauled up into the attic to make room for her private coffins).

The three vampires sleep in these coffins if the PCs enter during the day (see area @UUID[.TMx9HDShPgst6iZI]{F16} for rules on quietly staking vampires in their coffins, but note a successful @Check[stealth|dc:30] check is required to open Evanessa’s coffin undetected while her companions’ coffins similarly require a successful @Check[stealth|dc:29] check), but the first time they enter this room after dark, they find the trio seated at the central table as they pore over dozens of sheets of papers, books, and occult objects, diligently working on finding a solution to the Raudltz problem. While Lars and Vikter serve Evanessa, they in turn serve at Raudltz’s command, as does Evanessa herself—a condition that she increasingly rankles at. She’s gathered the books and occult tools here from the attic and a few stealthy missions into the library, and for nearly two decades, she’s been patiently but frustratingly researching methods by which she might escape servitude to Raudltz.

The PCs’ arrival in the room intrigues Evanessa. Her husbands stand up and hiss, ready to attack, but she stays their anger with a hand and invites the PCs to introduce themselves. If they do, she explains matter-of-factly that she’s been seeking a way to escape Raudltz’s command for some time, but she admits that the texts she’s gathered here are frustratingly lacking in answers. She asks the PCs if they have anything to contribute to the problem of how a vampire might escape the influence of the one who made them... but before they answer, she in turn orders her husbands to stuff their ears with candle wax (rendering them deafened until they remove the wax with an Interact action).

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[vampire-lore|dc:23|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check or a @Check[religion|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} notes that the death of a vampire can free their thrall and that a powerful enough thrall can sometimes escape their creator’s influence through force of will—Evanessa is impressed if a PC points this out but notes that neither of those options are viable for her, as she can’t turn against Raudltz and, trapped here, is in no position to gain power herself. Maybe, she muses, the PCs can destroy him for her? This would certainly free her, and if the PCs do this favor for her, she promises to reveal to them the combination to the safe Raudltz keeps his greatest valuables in up at his observatory.

With a critical success on either of those two checks to Recall Knowledge, a PC notes another way in which, it’s said, a vampire can escape their creator’s control—by undergoing a significant transfusion of blood from a living host during a ritual performed during the day, while the donor is in sunlight and the vampire to be freed remains protected. This method intrigues Evanessa if the PCs point it out, and if the PCs can succeed at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:28] check to get her to trust them not to betray her, she agrees to the attempt. To perform this transfusion, the PCs must gather up supplies consisting of an expanded alchemist’s lab (such as the tools in area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.8h6QErLBhi0Ro2tn]{E7}) and then perform the 2-hour transfusion rite during daylight. The donor must be a willing living humanoid who must remain within 10 feet of Evanessa’s coffin (which must be located out of direct sunlight), with glass tubing used to transfuse blood from the donor to Evanessa. For the rite to be successful, a non-donor PC must succeed at a @Check[medicine|dc:29|name:Blood Transfusion] or @Check[occultism|dc:29|name:Blood Transfusion] check. Regardless of the result, the donor PC becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 4} as a result of the transfusion, but if the PC succeeds at the check, then Evanessa breaks free from Raudltz’s control—for a time. She swiftly realizes that within 24 hours, the effects will revert, giving her and the PCs that much time to work together to destroy Raudltz before they’ll need to attempt the transfusion again.

Of course, treacherous PCs can use this opportunity to get Evanessa into a compromising position in the daylight and try to use that to destroy her—in this case, they must succeed at a @Check[deception|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|options:action:lie|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check to Lie to her to convince her to trust them.

Special: If the PCs promise to defeat Raudltz for her, Evanessa and her husbands don’t come to Raudltz’s aid when they attack him; in this case, grant the PCs XP as if they’d defeated these three in combat. If the PCs successfully perform the complex transfusion, on the other hand, she and her husbands join them in the fight against Raudltz; in this case grant the PCs XP as if they’d defeated the three in combat, plus an additional 40 XP.

Tasifinie's Room.name: Tasifinie's Room
Tasifinie's Room.text:
The door to this room from the hallway is boarded up. Removing the boards takes 10 minutes of work, or the PCs can just @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} the door with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:35|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check.

The air in this large bedroom is stuffy and dry, and thick drifts of dust cover the floor, carpets, and furniture. Dust-heavy cobwebs hang like sheets across the bed, fireplace, and several ruined pieces of furniture to the west, while a screened alcove to the south sets apart a washtub and a chamber pot. To the northeast rests a grand piano, likewise coated in dust and cobwebs. One item stands out amid the dust and webs—a large, healthy-looking plant with a glistening, bulbous trunk and long green leaves. Several violet flowers blooming in the plant’s upper foliage fill the room with a soothing scent.

Originally, this room was the master bedroom. The secret door in the north wall to area F14a can be found if someone @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the area or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the room for 30 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The secret door is obvious from the north, as it’s been boarded up. Even after it’s discovered, the boards must be removed or the door must be Forced Open, as detailed above. The stairs in area F14a lead down to area @UUID[.5NSykzgTFMXg8qGD]{F8a}, or up half a revolution before being blocked by impassible green mist. Once the castle towers are unlocked, these stairs lead up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.gNwo9gazhGBnNMcu]{J3d}.

Encounter

Low 10

@UUID[Actor.Hd7R87hWYtxYspko]{The Babies are So Hungry}

Hazard: Tasifinie was the first Arudora to perish within the castle walls, back in 4148 when an exotic dreamwell plant she’d paid great expense to be shipped all the way from Katapesh—a plant whose pale, night-blooming flowers were said to fill the air with relaxing scents and to promote soothing dreams—ended in tragedy.

Unknown to anyone, the dreamwell plant she’d purchased was host to an immense amount of spider eggs, and when those spiders hatched during the first night after the plant’s arrival, they poisoned Tasifinie and fed on her as she slept. Her son Irrokcis found her bloated, savaged remains—as well as a room filled with swarming spiders and webs—late next morning, when his father, who’d just arrived back from a trip to Caliphas, bade him to “go wake your mother and let her know I’m home.”

Traumatized by the event, it took Irrokcis weeks to recover, and he still has arachnophobia. His father abandoned the room and reworked the one to the south into the new master bedroom, as this chamber’s memories were too raw to endure. And after rumors of strange sounds and scents in the room spread among the staff, he went a step further and boarded the room up. Tasifinie’s spirit had moved on, but the agony and horror of her death resulted in the castle’s first haunt—one that became even more dangerous when the curse empowered it even further.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.H8A9FIBZethVyXiD]{Decaying Ectoplasm}

No search is needed to take note of how the dreamwell plant melts away into ectoplasm as soon as the haunt is disabled or destroyed. As the haunted plant melts away, something unsettling condenses in its place out of the decaying ectoplasm—a greasy-looking green stone carving of a bloated spider crouched atop a mass of eggs. This item is a horrid figurine that could prove particularly effective in any fight against Irrokcis.

Statue of Eragayl.name: Statue of Eragayl
Statue of Eragayl.text:
The stairs exit into the open air—a rooftop with a commanding view of the lake to the east that’s challenged and blocked by an enormous statue of a man holding a sword high above his head. The verdigris-caked statue stands sixty feet tall, with the top of the raised sword adding another twenty feet to its overall height. Something shiny seems to have lodged in the side of the statue’s head.

This statue is of Eragayl Arudora holding high his sword—a gift from various nobles whose lands were made safer by his heroism before he retired and built the castle in the first place. The statue is hollow and made of copper—a secret door at the western base can be discovered by a PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the area. Within, a metal staircase allows one to clamber up the metal framework to potentially do repair work. A PC who wishes to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb} the statue’s exterior can do so with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:29|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.FdQmgkhKkh8KXwCq]{Statue's Head} @UUID[Actor.mCWHbAI5lUskOAoH]{Balcony Corner}

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check confirms the object lodged in the side of the statue’s head 60 feet up is a brass gear the size of a dinner plate. From outside, pulling the gear free is a simple matter of an Interact action, but from inside, it must be wrenched free with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:27] check. On a critical failure, the attempt results in the character falling 50 feet down the stairs (@Check[reflex|dc:27|options:action:grab-an-edge|traits:manipulate] save to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.3yoajuKjwHZ9ApUY]{Grab an Edge}) for standard falling damage (@Damage[25[bludgeoning]|options:fall-damage]). This is one of the gears from the clock tower—see @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

A much more accessible treasure sits balanced on the northeast corner of the balcony railing—a softly glowing major soulheart. The first PC to touch this major soulheart receives a brief memory of Banijer visiting the statue and admiring its craftsmanship, then leaning over the edge against the balcony to wave at his family down in his farmhouse far below to the north.

Attic.name: Attic
Attic.text:
Dozens of crates, boxes, barrels, and other containers stand stacked haphazardly throughout the perimeter of this enormous attic. Bricks cover the windows. Oddly-spaced wooden beams support the densely scaffolded high-arched ceiling above, where thick dusty cobwebs rule. Thick, black curtains hang amid the beams in the middle of the chamber, blocking the attic’s center from view and obscuring the large space’s true dimensions.

As with most of the chambers in the private halls, the vampires long ago bricked and plastered over the windows, plunging this attic into perpetual darkness. Dust lies thick over most of the boxes, with an exception near the northern exit and amid the coffins in the middle of the room—the vampires generally travel to and from their coffins in mist form.

Moving through loosely stacked containers is treated as difficult terrain, while tightly stacked containers (such as those to the north blocking easy access to the central area from the stairs) can be clambered over with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check. The ceiling is 20-feet high along the east and west, rising to a peaked roof that’s 60 feet high in the center. The PCs can reach the rafters above by clambering up the crates; moving through the rafters is trickier, and a PC must succeed at a @Check[acrobatics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Balance.Title|options:action:balance|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.M76ycLAqHoAgbcej]{Balance} or @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb}.

The stairs at area F16a lead down to area @UUID[.bD29m8AJelDO4lpJ]{F9c}.

Encounter

Moderate 10

@UUID[Actor.tzasu9INtgxq7j2d]{Arthus Arudora} @UUID[Actor.cBYUYki2nvUTRHzy]{Prollus Arudora} @UUID[Actor.7HpyOEQQBVmjVzA8]{The Mistake}

Creatures: If the PCs enter this area during the day, they can find most of Raudltz’s children asleep in their coffins in the central area (with the exception of Evanessa, who sleeps with her own spawn in area @UUID[.pNlOS2ZetwxxrwrG]{F13}). Raudltz himself isn’t in the central coffin (he prefers to sleep, of late, in a different coffin in area @UUID[.tbuXpUsjFaPXpEM2]{F18}).

The heavy curtains and bricked-up windows are more than enough to protect the vampires from sunlight during the day, and while they sleep at this time inside their coffins, it’s no simple matter to just open them up and stake them all. To open a coffin without rousing the vampire within, a PC must succeed at a @Check[stealth|dc:27] check; if they fail, the vampire wakes with an earsplitting shriek that wakes the other vampires. A vampire must Interact with their coffin to open it and is prone until they Stand, but otherwise, they aren’t impacted by having to fight the PCs during the day. If the PCs open a coffin without waking its slumbering occupant, they can spend 3 actions to drive a stake through the vampire’s heart, but doing so is loud enough to wake the other vampires unless the PCs take extraordinary measures (such as by casting a 4th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gIdDLrbswTV3OBJy]{Silence} spell on the PC doing the staking). Note that attempting to hold a coffin shut only delays the vampire by 1 action, as once they realize they can’t open their coffin with an Interact action, they simply Turn to Mist and seep out of the coffin. Confronted here, during the day, the vampires don’t seek to interact with the PCs in any way other than attempting to kill them.

The first time the PCs enter this room at night, most of the vampires aren’t here, with two exceptions: one-time brothers Arthus and Prollus. These two are on guard duty—a post that none of Raudltz’s children enjoy, yet one that they all understand the importance of. These two have just made a poor decision in an attempt to engineer a dutiful guardian that’ll stand watch over their coffins at all times and have retreated to the northern area near the door to area F16a to speak in hushed tones about what they should do next while their bad decision groans and moans in the central area.

This “bad decision” they refer to as “The Mistake” is an awful, tangled mass of blood-coated body parts fused together in a hideous mess—the result of the two vampires attempting to use a @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.iQLEbANowf4fT8hK]{vile remnant} on the bodies of a few recently blood-drained victims to create an undead, easy-to-control guardian. They got the first part right, but not so much the second. Now, this creature, an unrisen, wails and cries out in pain and horror at its fate while flopping about in the central area. The unrisen is presently content to moan and shudder, but it initially attacked the two vampires with a fury that scared them off. The vampires now fear it’s only a matter of time before The Mistake starts smashing coffins, and even if it doesn’t by the time the sun rises, the other vampires returning here will discover their once-safe retreat isn’t very safe anymore.

When they notice the PCs, the two vampires quickly shush them, warning to stay quiet or “The Mistake will hear you!” They aren’t willing to face the unrisen again but quickly see the PCs as an unexpected boon and try to convince the party to go into the central area to take care of The Mistake. They shamefully admit how The Mistake came to be and promise to leave the PCs alone for destroying it for them. They don’t know why their plans backfired but suspect it has something to do with the entity who rules over Bastardhall (they don’t know Charg by name).

If the PCs attack the vampires, they move toward the central area in an attempt to lure the party into a fight against The Mistake before they Turn to Mist and hide in the rafters above; once the PCs defeat The Mistake, they descend and finish the fight. If the PCs destroy The Mistake, the two vampires honor their promise and allow the PCs to come and go through this area. They won’t mind if the PCs claim the vile remnant or the gear as their own, but they go back on their promise and attack if the PCs insist on taking the other treasures from the area. If the PCs keep their agreement with the two vampires, they don’t come to Raudltz’s aid when the party attacks him.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.dI2QAA7xfohIYmnx]{Attic Storage} @UUID[Actor.Reuk9cQ9iw135XYu]{Center Coffin} @UUID[Actor.uYr7LNcQWlpXMVB3]{Rafter}

It takes 2 hours to thoroughly @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the attic, but doing so uncovers a fair amount of valuables among the much larger collection of mundane materials stored here (including a large amount of leftover materials for bricking up windows), including 260 gp in various art objects and coins, a pouch containing three greater mistform elixirs, and a mummified bat talisman. Only one of the coffins contains anything of interest—Raudltz’s, in the center of the room, contains a pair of winged sandals that Raudltz no longer needs, now that he can just turn into a bat.

In addition, this search uncovers a vile remnant that looks like a heart pierced by a dozen ribs and studded with teeth (some of which have cavities). Once the PCs defeat The Mistake, this vile remnant bursts from its remains as it’s destroyed. The vile remnant was previously stored in a set of large crates to the north, along with the blood-drained victims the vampires used for their ill-conceived plan—all that remains now in the crates is a foul smell and some unpleasant stains.

Finally, if a PC succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:27] check, they’ll notice a brass gear lodged in a rafter, 60 feet above the central coffin; it’s one of the gears from the clock tower. See @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

Central Walk.name: Central Walk
Central Walk.text:
The ceiling of this ten-foot-wide hall rises up fifteen feet to an arch. The walls are made of brick and mortar fitted around what looks like a once-delicate iron railing.

This hallway was originally a widow’s walk and open to the air, with glorious views to the east and west, but the vampires bricked up the walls long ago to prevent accidental sunlight from seeping into the rooms to the north and south.

Observatory.name: Observatory
Observatory.text:
Shelves filled with books extend from the northern wall of this observatory, while in the northeast corner, an immense but unlit fireplace sits near a low table and several chairs. Other tables, each covered with books, scrolls, and strange tools, are in the eastern reaches of the room, while three brass telescopes have been arrayed on mounted armatures to the south, aimed at tall windows framed by black curtains and fitted with thick, wooden slatted shutters affixed to chains that run up to runners and pulleys in the rafters above. The most impressive sight, though, is the immense telescope that lords over the southeastern portion of the room under a large cupola fitted with glass skylights, against which pelts the deluge of the storm outside. As with the southern windows, these skylights are fitted with wooden slat shutters affixed to chains that wind up and over pulleys above. These chains in turn all connect to various wall-mounted wheels throughout the room.

The wall-mounted wheels allow one to open and close the shutters on the windows and the skylight swiftly, if one at a time, with an Interact action. Once closed, the shutters automatically lock in place—opening them requires unlocking the wheel using one of the keys carried by Raudltz or with a successful @Check[thievery|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}.

Beyond the doors to the west lies a mostly empty chamber with a flight of stairs that wind upward for a short bit before ending at an impassible wall of green mist. Once the towers are unlocked, these stairs lead up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.i6VM7zXFCXSnQqKp]{J3c}. Behind a thick curtain near the stairs sits another of Raudltz’s coffins.

Encounter

Severe 10

@UUID[Actor.s9deoXkbvvkvX9xZ]{Raudltz Arudora} @UUID[Actor.D2Pe38jYbeBxUaxU]{Niliths (1 or 3)}

Creatures: Raudltz spared no expense having this room set up to appeal to his favorite pastime: astronomy. The immense telescope remains his pride and joy—it grants a +2 item bonus on all checks to pursue stargazing-related pursuits but is far too cumbersome to transport.

If the PCs enter this area during the day, they find the main room empty. Raudltz sleeps in his coffin in area F18a but is far from alone—three oily-hided gray monstrosities clamber and hunker atop or near his coffin, licking and rubbing at the wood as the vampire within sleeps. These three creatures are niliths drawn in from the Dreamlands by the vampire’s delicious nightmares—in return for guarding him as he sleeps, he allows these niliths to sip and drink from his dreams as they use mind reading and other unsavory methods to do so, transmitting what they gurgle up to whatever strange link they share with eldritch entities beyond the proverbial wall of sleep. This doesn’t impact Raudltz other than to ensure he never remembers his dreams–which suits him fine, as he dreams only of the night he beheaded his bastard son and doomed Bastardhall to this cursed existence, never realizing that this nightly dream vampirism keeps him in a perpetual loop of research (see below). The niliths hiss and shriek if they spot the PCs and attack at once, but if the PCs slay them, the PCs can attempt to open Raudltz’s coffin to stake him. While he doesn’t wake to the sound of combat because he dreams deeply, as soon as the PCs open his coffin, they must succeed at a @Check[stealth|dc:32] check to avoid waking him so they can stake him.

After dark, Raudltz is awake and working with a single nilith in the main room. He’s seated at the central worktable while the nilith dangles from above, clinging to chains while it answers his nonstop questions about the interconnected nature of stars and sleep. Raudltz has long believed that if he can simply chart the right view of the stars above through the sky, he can find a way to bring Bastardhall out of its cursed limbo, but every night, his progress resets when the niliths he sees as his advisors drink away his memories. Bound tightly together with rope are two more hapless victims (see @UUID[.5NSykzgTFMXg8qGD#rescued-victims]{Rescued Victims}) whom Raudltz intends to sacrifice to the nilith later this evening after they finish their discussion.

Frustrated with the storm outside since it blocks his view of the stars (never mind the fact that those “stars” are simply phantasms created by the curse), Raudltz keeps the shutters open so that, should the storm abate, he can quickly move to his telescope to begin his search anew. He regards the arrival of the PCs with a mix of impatience and frustration, hissing out a curse and wondering why his children haven’t handled them yet. As he does so, he calls out to his children to come to his side. All those whom the PCs haven’t destroyed or made other bargains with do so as swiftly as possible; they Turn to Mist and move through ratholes in the walls to reach this room soon. Once combat begins, one of his surviving children appears at the start of each round to join the fight until all who can or will reply do so. At the same time, his nilith companion joins the fight. Alone with the nilith, this is a Severe 10 fight, so if his children join the battle, the PCs will quickly be outnumbered. Fortunately for them, Raudltz doesn’t pursue fleeing PCs—but he does take stock of them and turns away from his current projects to torment and hunt them thereafter—first from afar via spells like nightmare, but soon enough, with his children at his side.

Raudltz fights until destroyed, which he expects to be nothing but a momentary inconvenience. He turns to mist and retreats to his coffin here in area F18 if he was defeated elsewhere in the castle, but otherwise, he retreats to his spare coffin in area @UUID[.TMx9HDShPgst6iZI]{F16}. In either case, he hopes that there are allies there to protect him long enough for him to regain consciousness.

As soon as he’s actually slain, Raudltz howls in frustration as his body swiftly decays away, aging several centuries in the span of a few seconds. His soul bursts from his body, through the roof to return to his tower at area @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.daXhK7IZ3yBks2QI]{J3f}—if this takes place in the observatory during the night, as the rain pelts the glass windows above, a moody flash of lightning backlights the ghostly towers above, giving the PCs an unsettling view for a brief moment. His gear remains behind, including his telescope—the key to unlocking the fallen temple of Bastardhall.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.knFIWpVnozz4rKSK]{Shelves} @UUID[Actor.lQbb4nO8oJ44uSTl]{Telescope Interior} @UUID[Actor.gUKCpFWvStgega36]{Southwest Table}

The large amount of books on the shelves here are mostly focused on the topic of astronomy and, if they’re referenced for an hour, grant a +2 item bonus to checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about this topic. A PC who spends 24 hours can sort through these books to gather up the ones of note that, collectively, grant this item bonus, but even then, the collection is large, consisting of 40 Bulk. This collection is worth 600 gp.

If the PCs @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the observatory for 30 minutes and succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check, they’ll notice a section of the wooden platform that supports the large telescope can be pulled open—doing so reveals a coffin-sized interior in which a skeleton wearing a striking, elegant outfit has been stashed. This outfit functions as an entertainer’s cincture, but a PC who succeeds at a @Check[theater-lore|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] or @Check[performance|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to Recall Knowledge recognizes the cut of the outfit as a look made popular centuries ago by an Ustalavic actress named Yasmerra who mysteriously went missing in 4192. On a critical success, the PC recalls rumors that Yasmerra was involved in an affair with Raudltz Arudora. This skeleton is indeed her body, her fate after confronting her lover with their son Velicarn finally revealed.

Scattered among the books on the southwest table are dozens of letters—correspondence from his sister, Ryhasphinea. These letters are numerous, and while the more recent ones are mostly about the logistics of her and her son moving into Castle Arudora, taken as a whole, the PCs can use them to research her in great detail.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.7VX2SBgHGbICdyYi]{Ryhasphinea Arudora}

Ryhasphinea’s Letters: A PC spends 4 hours looking through the long, rambling letters and deciphering Ryhasphinea’s cramped spidery script to learn more about her.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[society|dc:27|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to decipher her handwriting or @Check[perception|dc:29|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to stumble across interesting passages almost by chance.

Secret Stairs.name: Secret Stairs
Secret Stairs.text: Tucked behind a secret door in the hallway marked as area @UUID[.ndtRFPlOc0RB3Vc5]{F2d} is a set of stairs. These stairs lead down to a pair of secret doors—one of which opens to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.BzbrB5DMMnjAcyag]{D11} and the other of which opens into area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1n}. From inside this secret stairwell, both of these secret doors are obvious.

Castle Grounds.name: Castle Grounds
Castle Grounds.text:
The castle grounds and courtyard of Bastardhall are largely open to the sky above. Before the curse, this was a place where one could find the servants, guards, guests, visitors, and the Arudoras themselves mingling, depending on the time of day. Festivals and celebrations were held in the northern courtyard for the entertainment of the people of Maiserene, and various products produced by the castle’s artisans could be purchased by visitors and villages during the festivals (usually at a discounted price). After which, the honey, weapons, horse riding gear, and art would often be bundled in wagons for transport across the Laroba Bridge.

As time wore on and the Arudoras grew more fractured and isolated within their castle walls, the festivals took place less and less. By the time the curse fell, only one of the Arudoras spent any time at all here—Jinnivere Arudora, daughter of Lord Raudltz and Lady Alisendra. Jinnivere was a renowned equestrian and had been crossing the grounds to fetch her horse when the curse struck. Today, she lingers in a transitive state between the carriage house and her tower, but the more the PCs explore the castle grounds, the sooner she’ll take notice and confront them.

Entering the Castle Grounds.name: Entering the Castle Grounds
Entering the Castle Grounds.text: The PCs should be 6th-level before they explore the castle grounds (in fact, if the PCs have exhausted all exploration options on the haunted shore, they’ll be a few hundred XP into 6th-level). The castle grounds contain several points of entry once they’re unlocked, as summarized on the @UUID[.UeiZljzVzt6RMFbS]{Castle Grounds Connections} section, but the PCs could theoretically clamber or even fly over the castle walls at any point.

The Skies Above.name: The Skies Above
The Skies Above.text:
The storm clouds gather as soon as the PCs unlock the castle grounds. Skies become overcast during the day, with the cloud cover breaking only for two hours from 11:00 A.M. to 1:00 p.m. Temperatures remain crisp and cool, but the periodic breezes now carry a noticeable chilling bite. The waves of Lake Laroba are more robust, splashing constantly on the shore, but it remains a @Check[athletics|dc:10|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim} in the water.

Sunrise is 8:00 a.m., and sunset is 7:00 p.m. The days are 11 hours long, and the nights last 13 hours.

Castle Grounds Ambushes.name: Castle Grounds Ambushes
Castle Grounds Ambushes.text:
Encounter

Low 6

@UUID[Actor.HDF02TkzQISYCgLN]{Phantom Knights x3}

If the PCs rest in an unsafe area on the castle grounds, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:7]. On a failure, they’re ambushed while they camp by three phantom knights.

Lucid Nightmares.name: Lucid Nightmares
Lucid Nightmares.text:
After unlocking the castle grounds, the nightmare changes. This time the PC is a guard patrolling the castle walls, talking with another guard about how frustrating it is to be on duty while galas and festivals take place in the castle without them. The clock tower bells ring out twice, indicating it’s two in the afternoon. Then the sky goes dark and winged monsters descend to the hunt. As the sky darkens, the PC turns and sees that the guard they were speaking with is now the same staff-carrying figure who haunted their dream previously. The apparition chuckles ominously as it floats up to join the monsters. For the remainder of the dream, the PCs flee as fire and slaughter play out around them. The dream ends as the PCs make it out onto the great causeway only for it to catch fire and collapse before they can reach the far shore. The dreamer wakes either just as the fire begins to consume them or as the bridge gives way and they plunge over a hundred feet to the lake below.

The Burning Bridge

Resist Nightmare @Check[will|dc:22|options:lucid-nightmare]

Critical Failure The PC wakes with pyrophobia (fear of fire) and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} whenever they take fire damage during the next 24 hours.

Research @Check[athletics|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to seek an alternate route to safety that gives the PC time to observe or @Check[intimidation|dc:27|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to frighten the flying monsters away as they approach.

Effect

@UUID[Item.htPpGj2N2431bfJf]{Pyrophobia}

If a PC critically fails to resist this nightmare, use the linked effect to automate a Note reminder when they take fire damage.

Castle Grounds Features.name: Castle Grounds Features
Castle Grounds Features.text:
The castle grounds appear at first glance to be abandoned, but the PCs will swiftly encounter creatures as they explore. Except where indicated, the grounds themselves are open terrain, although grassy areas are unkempt and weedy. The castle walls are made of stone and offer little in the form of handholds, and scaling them requires a successful @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb}. The internal building walls have more handholds and can be Climbed with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check, but where the walls shift to ghostly images where the castle’s phased out, there’s nothing to grip and climbing is impossible. Building interiors are unlit unless otherwise noted, but during the day, sunlight can filter in through windows as appropriate.

Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

Most locations in this chapter can be found in the Castle Grounds level Arudora Isle. The exceptions are all B2 areas, found in the Walls level instead.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.Ggl8VZ7v1J5Mo1er]{Castle Grounds}

As the PCs enter the castle grounds, you can play this ambience sound.

Speaking to the Dead

Here and there in Bastardhall can be found the skeletal bodies of those who perished when the curse fell. These were the lucky ones, those who died before Charg’s curse could seize their souls and transform them into monsters. Any of these remains could tantalize PCs capable of casting spells like talking corpse. You can assume that any such “set dressing” skeleton has a +11 Will save for resisting such effects. What these remains have to say is left to you—they could simply shriek and wail in agony, or they might be able to warn the PCs of nearby threats or hidden areas, but nothing these remains say can be used to research any of the topics covered in @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n]{The Bastardhall Curse}.

Courtyard.name: Courtyard
Courtyard.text:
Once the region is unlocked, the two areas the PCs can use to gain access to the courtyard of Bastardhall (other than by climbing or flying over the walls) is via the north watch post (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.FuifNpUpaAG0LzlR]{A12}) or the south watch post (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.1O4BfvPuyfyznvYR]{A20}), but as they unlock more areas, their routes open up as well.

Splintered bones, broken weapons, and other remnants of the ancient battle that took place here lie scattered throughout the courtyard. The courtyard itself doesn’t offer much cover—the paths are hard-packed earth, and while the areas between them, once well-manicured by the groundskeeper, are tangled and overgrown, this growth never amounts to anything capable of hiding an approach. While none of the denizens of the various areas within the castle grounds are quick to react to intruders and tend to keep to their own areas, the nightgaunts in area @UUID[.nfL5eMjZjdwi1AkR]{B2} keep an eye out for an opportunity to ambush the PCs.

Castle Wall.name: Castle Wall
Castle Wall.text:
The dark gray stone walls of the looming castle wrap ominously around the weedy courtyard and its outbuildings and decor. Here and there, tangles of clinging ivy hang down from these walls from swaths of verdant overgrowth above. But for the most part, the walls are bare, caked with lichen, or in some places, splattered with blood that seems disturbingly fresh.

The wall itself consists of a 10-foot-wide walkway with four-foot-high battlements along the outer wall. Three-foot-wide merlons rising up to 6 feet in the center of every 5-foot square, giving theoretical archers ample opportunity for cover. While it’s only a 35-foot drop into the courtyard, the drop down from the outer wall into the haunted shore consists of two separate falls—the first being a 40-foot-drop to the 5-foot-wide foundation base surrounding the entire castle, and then from that base, a further 60 feet to the haunted shore below. It’s a @Check[reflex|dc:20|options:action:grab-an-edge|traits:manipulate] save to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.3yoajuKjwHZ9ApUY]{Grab an Edge} on these walls. In places where ivy grows thick atop the wall, passage is difficult terrain, but where indicated on the map, dangling vines into the courtyard provide a much easier place to clamber up and down. At these points, a successful @Check[athletics|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb} the walls is needed, rather than DC 30.

Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

This area, as well as areas @UUID[.zJP8azfSkSFWJ7FH]{B2a} through @UUID[.jJMjmV5oA7dfQfjN]{B2e} can be found in the Walls level. The PCs can travel to this level from the Castle Grounds through regions placed in various stairs along the walls (colored pink in the Region Controls).

Encounter

Low 6

@UUID[Actor.g6sgRVXnvpjkl2KV]{Nightgaunt x3}

Creatures: These areas are the haunt of several nightgaunts who were drawn here from the Dreamlands by the fear and misery that radiates from Bastardhall. The nightgaunts can come and go as they please, flapping off through the Ethereal Plane when the fancy strikes them. Yet the nightmare energies that suffuse Bastardhall are akin to a soothing soak in a hot spring, and so some of them, once they arrive, choose to stay. A dozen nightgaunts come and go more frequently in the skies above. These nightgaunts might ambush PCs who sleep outdoors.

Others, however, dwell on the castle walls—the two watchtowers to the northeast and southwest (both marked area B2c) are individual nightgaunt nests, but a third group of these creatures flutters and frolics along the walls themselves. Unlike those that live on the watchtowers, the group of nightgaunts on the walls take note of anyone they see openly exploring the courtyard below, and noiselessly swoop down to attack as soon as they do.

This first nightgaunt attack should occur a few rounds after the entire party starts to move into the courtyard without attempting to sneak. The three nightgaunts begin the encounter by landing amid the PCs and engaging in melee but won’t attempt to Grab anyone into their clutches until one of the three is slain. At that point, the remaining nightgaunts focus on the PC who killed one of their own and attempt to snatch them up. A nightgaunt who grabs a PC swoops into the air and flies off with them, hoping to drop them somewhere dangerous—either into the garden (area @UUID[.XTFntNXqyFNvra51]{B4}), the training yard (area @UUID[.srvDTVrA5ZcIuWjR]{B8}), somewhere in the hedge maze (area @UUID[.eaV4LD57vEj6Vcr5]{B9}), the temple grove (area @UUID[.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3]{B10}), or the temple pond (area @UUID[.t1s9G6BjLx2VvxXt]{B11}), whichever is closest. They take care to deposit the PC safely, since they enjoy watching them suffer from perches on the nearby castle wall. Once a PC is snatched up, both nightgaunts take up such perches nearby, allowing the other PCs time to give chase and help their ally. If the peril at the spot the PC has been deposited is overcome, the two nightgaunts swoop back down to repeat the process. Once only one of these nightgaunts remains, it gives up the game and flies off into the Ethereal Plane, never to return.

Guard Post.name: Guard Post
Guard Post.text:
The ceiling rises twenty feet above the floor of this room, with plenty of wooden crossbeams to support the roof. A long oak table stands in the middle of the chamber, surrounded by wooden chairs. Weapon racks, a writing desk, and several old cloaks hanging on pegs adorn the walls in between arrow slits and doors in the south half of the room, while to the north stand two dusty, empty pigeon coops. Heaps of... something... lie on each coop’s floor.

This room was used by the castle guards to discuss changes in schedules, as a place to take quick breaks, and to house the castle’s messenger birds. Arrow slits looking out over the haunted shore and courtyard alike allowed for additional defense if needed. The mysterious heaps in the coops are a mix of ancient bird droppings and pigeon skeletons covered with a layer of mold and dust—and perhaps more, if the PCs dig through the stuff.

Encounter

Trivial 6

@UUID[Actor.TynpBOMea7aDkcfw]{Haunted Coop x2}

Hazard: A PC who approaches either of the two bird coops automatically notices the faint acrid smell of fresh bird droppings in the air, and hears the soft cooing of pigeons even though both coops are empty.

Any attempt to interact with a coop or to dig through the mounds within triggers that coop’s haunt.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.oxt739MHQS1wbAWK]{Writing Desk} @UUID[Actor.33GgOGcGGRyTXvdE]{Northwest Coop}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the writing desk on the east wall discovers a partially scribbled note that reads, “Under attack. Monsters everywhere. Lord Arudora has sent runners but not sure help will arrive in time. Will try to—” before bloodstains obscure the rest of the unfinished cry for aid. Next to the doomed guard’s note sit two empty bloodstained vials and one still containing a moderate healing potion.

While the northwest coop’s heaps are unremarkable, the northeast one hides a sneaky key talisman that a PC can discover if they Search through the filth for 5 minutes.

Overgrown Watchtower.name: Overgrown Watchtower
Overgrown Watchtower.text:
A thick carpet of tangled ivy grows across the top of this watch tower. While some vines dangle over the inner side into the courtyard, none do so over the outer walls. A large heap of particularly thorny vines is wrapped around an armored skeleton that’s slumped against the northeastern battlements.

The overgrowth here makes the area difficult terrain.

Encounter

Trivial 6

@UUID[Actor.ex2fJQ7HZgAAl2Xs]{Agonizing Thorns}

Hazard: The vines growing over (and through) the skeleton have become tainted by the residual fear that suffused this hapless captain of the guard who perished here during the first night of the curse. They’ve become a dangerous hazard. If the PCs destroy the vines rather than disable them, roll a @Check[flat|dc:11]—on a success, the armor becomes broken as a result of the violence.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.Zor6fRRpKdV4zgrg]{Skeleton's Armor}

The skeleton’s armor is a suit of +1 full plate. A sturdy iron key can be found on a leather cord around the skeleton’s neck—this key opens the door to the armory (area @UUID[.mG5rb8xF7l3JNp75]{B7}).

Nightgaunt Nests.name: Nightgaunt Nests
Nightgaunt Nests.text:
Encounter

Trivial 6

@UUID[Actor.g6sgRVXnvpjkl2KV]{Nightgaunts x2}

Creatures: Each of these watchtowers hosts a nest of two nightgaunts. Unlike those that lurk on the walls, these nightgaunts don’t notice any PCs exploring the courtyard, but if the ones in the northeastern nest are intruded upon, they attack at once, using the same tactics as their kin in area @UUID[.nfL5eMjZjdwi1AkR]{B2}.

The southwestern nightgaunts are less antagonistic, as they are already dealing with another danger. As soon as they spot the PCs, they crouch down and hold up their hands in a pose that suggests non-aggression. If the PCs attack, they fight back as the others, but if the PCs don’t attack, the nightgaunts silently shudder as if giggling. One then holds up their hands to ask for a bit more patience while the other grabs a stone and scratches a short message onto one of the southern merlons. The message is written in Aklo and reads, “Kill ugly monsters and we be friends!”

If the PCs can read the message and agree (remember, the nightgaunts can’t speak but do understand Aklo), the nightgaunts point to the east toward the guard tower (area @UUID[.jJMjmV5oA7dfQfjN]{B2e}), then mime the action of slitting throats. Provided with writing materials, the nightgaunts can be more informative—they explain that the gargoyles in there are ugly and foul-tempered and need to go, so the nightgaunts can move into their much cozier accommodations. They refuse to aid the PCs in fighting the gargoyles, but once they see proof that the gargoyles are dead, they caper in delight. News of this spreads to the other nightgaunts (excluding the itinerant ones who might ambush sleeping PCs), after which, any surviving nightgaunts leave the PCs alone, and all of them move into area @UUID[.jJMjmV5oA7dfQfjN]{B2e}. From this point onward, the nightgaunts eagerly agree to carry the PCs around if asked—giving the party an unusual mode of transport between the haunted shore, the castle walls, and once unlocked, the upper entrances into Bastardhall. The nightgaunts won’t aid the PCs in any combat, nor will they follow them into Bastardhall itself.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.HV8RVhALLgUzZCFR]{Watchtower Nest}

The southwestern nest is unremarkable, but the northwestern one contains a pair of skeletons dressed in full plate. One skeleton lies atop a +1 ghost touch longsword.

Reward

If the PCs kill the gargoyles and secure the nightgaunts’ aid, grant them XP for the nightgaunts remaining alive on the castle walls as if they’d defeated them in combat, plus an additional 20 XP.

Eastern Guard Tower.name: Eastern Guard Tower
Eastern Guard Tower.text:
A few skeletons clad in armor lie strewn about the floor of this otherwise empty watch post. Arrow slits provide narrow views of the exterior to the east.

The door leading into the stairwell shimmers with green mist as long as the private halls remain locked. Once the PCs can access that area, this door can be opened. The spiral stairs within lead down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.D7PNbqVhoW8hFd61]{A18} and up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.NVMoBdSOjkTMisMU]{F5a}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.hzO0Zfb9XUf8Rzj4]{Eastern Guard Tower}

There are four bodies here, each wearing a suit of plate mail.

Ruined Guard Post.name: Ruined Guard Post
Ruined Guard Post.text:
Narrow arrow slits face to the south of this large room, while a pair of stairwells lead down to the floor below. This place may have once been a meeting room for guards, but the shelves, tables, and weapon racks that once decorated it now lie in ruins. Hideous gargoyle carvings decorate stairwell walls.

The stairs lead down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.1O4BfvPuyfyznvYR]{A20}

Encounter

Moderate 6

@UUID[Actor.cvfIkEF6xmWn2soN]{Gargoyles x4}

Creatures: A group of four guards attempted to hole up in this room during the attack on the castle, but they succumbed to the curse and eventually turned on each other. Each time one died, the curse transformed them, and they live on now as gargoyles. Each gargoyle appears to wear stony plate armor, with their horned helmets merging onto their monstrous faces.

A gargoyle perches in each corner of the room, appearing as a statue, but as soon as they notice the PCs, one of them animates and greets them with a gravelly voice. The gargoyle welcomes the PCs as guests then asks for a favor— there are “skinny pretenders” out on the castle walls that annoy the gargoyles—the nightgaunts in areas @UUID[.nfL5eMjZjdwi1AkR]{B2} and @UUID[.rVs8ReD1ZFC7b27L]{B2c}. If the PCs kill these nightgaunts, the gargoyle promises a great treasure in payment.

This is a lie. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:14|name:PF2E.Actions.SenseMotive.Title|options:action:sense-motive|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1xRFPTFtWtGJ9ELw]{Sense Motive} can tell the gargoyle is being cagey. With a critical success, a PC also realizes that the gargoyle intends to betray them, and their furtive glances about the room reveal that three of their kin lurk nearby.

If the PCs do the gargoyle’s bidding and return, they chuckle in delight and informs the PCs that their reward shall be “a blessed escape from this cursed place.” All four gargoyles spring to life and attack. Once combat begins, for whatever reason, the gargoyles fight to the death, but they won’t pursue PCs outside this area, knowing that doing will invite a mass attack from the nightgaunts.

Arudora Fountain.name: Arudora Fountain
Arudora Fountain.text:
A twenty-five-foot-wide, three-foot-tall stone ring encircles a long-dry fountain. Within it lies a layer of gravel and a few dozen silver coins. The center of the fountain is decorated with a gray stone statue of a mustached man holding an ewer, as if pouring water, but like the pool below, this has also run dry. Eight additional statues stand around the fountain’s edge, each resembling a different person. They appear to have been carved from some sort of glistening green stone, as if each was coated in a layer of lacquer. One of these eight statues to the southeast has almost entirely crumbled away, with only its feet remaining. A glittering piece of jewelry lies between this broken statue’s feet.

This fountain originally served as a wishing well for visitors. In those pre-curse days, only the central stone statue adorned the fountain—a depiction of the castle’s creator, Eragayl Arudora. The eight newer statues manifested on the first night of the curse, crystallizing out of raw ectoplasm into something akin to stone. Seven of these statues represent one of the seven Arudoras trapped within Bastardhall, while the eighth (the ruined one) represents the eponymous bastard himself, Velicarn. If the PCs have accumulated at least 8 Research Points on the topic of the Arudoras, they can automatically recognize each of the seven individuals fully depicted (the crumbled statue will remain a mystery until the final chapter, at which point it’s restored to depict Velicarn—with his head intact). The following table lists which statue represents which Arudora.

Upon closer inspection, it’s apparent that each of the non-destroyed statues is posed so that they appear to be holding something, but the object is missing. All the statues have Hardness 14 and 60 HP. If the central statue of Eragayl is destroyed, it remains so for the rest of the campaign, but if any of the others are destroyed, they reform anew with the next sunset. Each of these seven statues radiates magic, and a PC who succeeds at a @Check[occultism|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] or @Check[arcana|dc:22|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[nature|dc:22|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], or @Check[religion|dc:22|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic} reveals their use (see @UUID[.#activating-a-statue]{Activating a Statue} below).

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.cHogqC3igqd7t1hM]{Fountain}

There’s a total of 45 sp scattered amid the gravel in the dry fountain.

When she was taken upon her arrival, Florin Kindler’s soul was pulled from her body. Her physical remains are now in limbo, but if her soul can be freed from Caydserris at the end of the adventure, she’ll be restored to life. One remnant remained behind, though—as she hurtled upward and her body began to fade, she managed to rip her beloved cameo free and dropped it, infusing it with desperate prayers. The cameo landed here, amid the feet of Velicarn’s destroyed statue. The PCs can use the Kindler cameo to help navigate Bastardhall in addition to its other helpful features.

Activating a Statue

The seven statues are the key to unlocking sections of Bastardhall for exploration. Once the PCs defeat a region’s Arudora, they can search their remains for an @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.XIDqWOe3cACxngGd]{Arudora memento}. By placing the proper memento in the correct statue, that statue animates briefly to accept the offering and then turns to stone. This act imparts a supernatural power to the PCs, intensifies the storm, shortens the day, and causes a region of Bastardhall to solidify in wash of color, grinding stone, and unnerving shrieking—as if the immense sarcophagus of a cursed god were grinding open.

Unlocking Areas

@UUID[Actor.cHogqC3igqd7t1hM]{Arudora Fountain}

In order to unlock an area, your PCs only need to deposit the Arudora Memento they obtained inside the Arudora Fountain loot actor, which you can find linked above and by hovering over the fountain itself on the map.

Doing this will unlock several doors, activate certain scene regions, and make certain changes to the environment such as weather effects and even sunset and sunrise times! You can keep track of this progress with the @UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Campaign Manager}.

Additionally, you can apply the bonus corresponding to the returned memento to keep track of the supernatural power the PCs obtain.
