Reward

Each time the PCs activate a statue and unlock a new area of Bastardhall, grant the party 40 XP.

Glimpsed Memories

While each of the soulhearts the PCs discover in this adventure include a brief glimpse into the memories of one of Maiserene’s six leaders (and thus crystallized from that particular person’s soul), any soulheart can be used to level up any of the phantoms—the PCs don’t have to match the “right soulheart” to its source, allowing the party to pick and choose precisely how they prefer to bolster their allies.

Garden.name: Garden
Garden.text:
A four-foot-high stone wall topped by a further four feet of wrought iron fencing surrounds this overgrown plot of vegetation and apple trees. A wood-and-glass building with a mostly shattered glass roof stands in the eastern portion of this tangled place.

The trails in this garden are difficult terrain, while the rest of the undergrowth is greater difficult terrain. During the night, this area is safe, if awkward, to travel through. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the garden and succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:20] check notices that many of the plants growing here should be flowering, yet no flowers are visible. A critical success at this check allows the PC to spot and recognize one of the lurking mandragoras among the undergrowth for what it is.

Encounter

Low 6

@UUID[Actor.V96EY8vLy7alnun9]{Mandragoras x3}

Creatures: Not everything is safer during the day in Bastardhall. Here in this overgrown garden, the curse has infused the plants and twisted three of them into horrifying parodies of humanity—mandragoras. These blood-drinking monsters are active during the day and hide in the undergrowth so they can ambush the PCs as soon as they venture into the garden. Note that the undergrowth impacts these creatures as well, and so they tend to stick to the trails when in combat, retreating into the thicker undergrowth once reduced to fewer than 20 HP to hide and recover.

At night, the supernatural gloom causes the mandragoras to become sluggish. They prefer to hunker down and wait out the night as a result, and attack singularly after dark, and even then, only after something attacks them first.

If any of the mandragoras use their Piercing Shriek, the occupant of area @UUID[.N0oA9IF4Mzzk1MN8]{B5} prepares as detailed there.

Apiary.name: Apiary
Apiary.text:
The inside of this wooden building features a long shelf of tools and gear to the south, among which are a few full body leather suits with enclosed masks. An alcove to the west features a curved bench, while in the main part of the building stand six 4-foot-tall wooden cupboard- like structures.

A PC who’s an expert in Nature automatically recognizes the intricate wooden structures as bee hives and the entire building as an apiary. Honey was one of the luxury items the Arudoras collected here in small batches, both to elevate their own kitchen and sell at exorbitant prices elsewhere in Ustalav. None of the bees survived the night of the curse, and an investigation of all the hives but one reveals within a sad mix of dead bees, wax, and old honey that’s still edible (once the dead bees are picked out of it).

Encounter

Low 6

@UUID[Actor.I5RtQqy4YfR2oMjo]{Sovina Vosslund}

Creature: The castle’s beekeeper was a pleasant, mild-mannered woman named Sovina Vosslund. She hid here among her beloved bees during the curse but perished after the glass roof collapsed atop her, lacerating her in dozens of places. The glass roof is now restored, and so is Savina, in a way, by being reincarnated into a hideous, deceptive creature: a particularly unusual penanggalan who rests within one of the hives, drenched in honey, rather than a vinegary concoction.

If Sovina is alerted to the PCs’ approach (such as if the mandragoras in the garden shriek), she greets them in her human guise as a plain-looking Keleshite woman wearing a leather armor and a wide-brimmed hat with mesh hanging from the brim that’s tucked into her collar. She stumbles toward the PCs, gasping as if in shock, and tearfully begs them for aid. She claims to have woken up here, alone and confused, with memories of working in the apiary while the castle was bustling with life and asks the PCs what happened to the place. Once they finish, she appears to be shocked that so much time has passed—for her, the night of the curse just happened. She then appears to realize something and tells the PCs that not long before things went bad, she was chatting with a friend up along the eastern wall when she noticed Maiserene’s local farmer and merchant, Banijer Greely, bury something in his fields near the scarecrow. She wonders if, perhaps, what he buried may have had something to do with all this, and offers to lead the PCs down to the fields (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Oz08GUWUIID0kaMb]{A16b}) where she witnessed the event to help them dig the mystery up.

This is all a lie. Once she’s done with her story, roll Sovina’s secret @Check[deception|against:perception|options:action:lie|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check against the party’s Perception DCs. If she succeeds, a PC can still realize that she’s acting cagey with a @Check[perception|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.SenseMotive.Title|options:action:sense-motive|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1xRFPTFtWtGJ9ELw]{Sense Motive}. Even if the PCs don’t believe her, she asks to be escorted to safety outside the castle walls.

The only element of truth to her story is the fact that there is something buried where she claims at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Oz08GUWUIID0kaMb]{A16b}—a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JmlPFAbjPvbhhKeu]{vile remnant} of Charg that’s grown there after poor Banijer’s soul was corrupted and drove him to murder his family. When the curse began, Sovina was transformed into a penanggalan when she attempted to hide in a place where she hoped she’d be safe—inside a hive that’d she’d recently emptied for minor repairs. In life, she was a close friend to Banijer’s family, often visiting their farm to trade gardening tips, and the curse seized on this link—what she senses buried in the field are the remains of the family she was once so close to, yet while the castle regions were locked, she was unable to investigate the alluring sensation of cruelty that beckoned her from below. How things play out from here depends on whether the PCs believe her story. If the PCs already have the vile remnant, she immediately attacks (see Confront Her below) and attempts to claim the object for herself.

  • Follow her Advice: If the PCs agree to help her dig up the vile remnant, Sovina leads them to the location then waits while they uncover the thing. Upon sighting it, she feigns shock, then volunteers to bring it back up to the castle to hide for safekeeping. If the PCs agree, she proceeds as detailed under Lead Her to Safety below. If they refuse to hand over the vile remnant, she attacks.

  • Ignore Her: If the PCs ignore Sovina or simply take too long (at your discretion) to investigate the area, the penanggalan eventually gets over her worries about leaving the castle grounds alone and heads down to the farms herself one night to dig up the vile remnant there, after which she proceeds as detailed below under Lead Her to Safety.

  • Lead Her to Safety: If the PCs simply lead her to somewhere safe but don’t agree to help her dig up the mystery, Sovina nods in understanding. Once she’s left alone, though, she immediately makes her way to the location and digs up the vile remnant. As soon as she has it in her clutches, Sovina returns here to bury the vile remnant in the apiary to activate Hide the Horror. After that, she’ll seek out the PCs—the next time they’re ambushed as they camp, they’re attacked by Sovina.

  • Confront Her: Sovina abandons her story swiftly and attacks if the PCs push back or confront her. She rolls Deception in this case for initiative and starts combat by casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.K2WpC3FFoHrqX9Q5]{Hypnotize}, followed by a proboscis tongue Strike against a PC who resisted the spell. She casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.f8SBoXiXQjlCKqly]{Illusory Creature} on the second round then follows up with spells until her body is destroyed. Once this occurs, she attacks with her tongue and entrails but attempts to flee if reduced to fewer than 30 HP—either back to her apiary or down to the ruins of the Greely farm at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Oz08GUWUIID0kaMb]{A16}, after which she makes plans to dig up the vile remnant (or steal it from the PCs if they have it).

If Sovina is slain, she collapses and melts away swiftly into a nauseating pile of honey-like residue. A moment later, her soul emerges from the remains, manifesting as a harmless phantom. Sobbing and howling in despair, she flies to area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Oz08GUWUIID0kaMb]{A16b} and, still sobbing, hopelessly claws at the ground where the vile remnant is buried. Her incorporeal hands can’t move the dirt, of course. If the PCs dig up the vile remnant, she shrieks in fear at the sight of it, recognizing the remains as those of the Greely family, and then vanishes entirely, her soul finally moving on to the afterlife.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.9ZYi8vwmJX5tp94d]{Southern Shelf} @UUID[Actor.uX87oMz2KLTOR87A]{Hive}

A search of the tools to the south uncovers plenty of beekeeping equipment, along with a suit of +1 leather armor, several long-spoiled and useless vials of antidotes, a traveler’s any-tool, and a wand of sure footing.

While most of the hives contain nothing of note, a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the one that Sovina dwelled in finds the interior to be encrusted with foul-smelling honey (anyone who tastes this honey must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:25|options:inflicts:sickened] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}). Mired in the honey at the bottom of the hive is a soulheart. The first PC to touch this soulheart receives a brief memory of Banijer and his family enjoying a pleasant discussion about gardening tips with Sovina, held in the unruined farmhouse while a comfy fire crackles in the nearby fireplace.

Marshaling Hall.name: Marshaling Hall
Marshaling Hall.text:
The room features a wooden floor and exposed rafters under a wood-shingled roof. To the south, a few chairs have been placed around a circular meeting table, and armor stands and shelves are set against the walls. To the north, a stout wooden desk and high-backed chair look out over two long wooden tables, each arranged with chairs along the outer edge so that one can easily walk back and forth between them. Two bookshelves and a slate board round out the decor to the north, but whatever was once written on the board has been smeared with blood.

The castle guards used this area during the start of a shift for the captain on duty to give assignments as needed, but it also served as an impromptu breakroom for guards to use for a few minutes during long shifts. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EwgTZBWsc8qKaViP]{Investigates} the blood-smeared chalk markings learns (with a successful @Check[perception|dc:25] check) that the guards were frantically trying to collate information about the attackers during the night of the curse when some sort of brutal massacre took place.

Encounter

Low 6

@UUID[Actor.HDF02TkzQISYCgLN]{Phantom Knight x4}

Creatures: When the PCs first enter this room, a dozen ghostly guards manifest in the chairs along the central tables, and the sound of panicked arguments and cries of fear echo through the air. An instant later, they’re all rising to their feet, slaughtering each other. This continues until the guards notice the PCs—only a few seconds later, if the party isn’t taking care to be stealthy. Only four of the guards “survive” the massacre, and they obviously see the PCs as the source of their fear. They shout in anger and rush to attack, moving through tables and chairs alike with ease. The four phantom knights pursue PCs relentlessly through the castle grounds if the party flees and fight until destroyed.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.C5OSwp0eBklHCxkl]{Southeast Corner}

Most of the gear stored along the south walls is old and ruined, but a lion’s shield leans against the shelves in the southeast corner.

Armory.name: Armory
Armory.text:
The door to this room is locked. It can be opened with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}, a successful @Check[athletics|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force it Open}, or via the key found on the skeleton at area @UUID[.E1mrufqRAF8FwaWT]{B2b}.

Weapon racks line the walls of this stone room, although very few weapons remain in storage here, suggesting that most were deployed elsewhere and never returned. A pair of workbenches, each with a whetstone, sit in the middle of the room. Thick layers of dust cover everything.

This area is secure enough that the PCs can rest here without fear of being ambushed.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.4qag3lWdbIqyjH8I]{Armory} @UUID[Actor.jR1BB47oXfmHUZqv]{Adornment}

A PC needs only a few minutes to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} through the dusty remnants of weapons here to gather them all up. The weapons include seven longswords, four shortbows, 43 arrows, six daggers, and five halberds—none of which are magical or particularly noteworthy.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:22|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check during their search finds one thing of note, though, an elegant, small flag meant to adorn the haft of a polearm that bears the colors of Shelyn. This flag’s embroidery features songbirds in flight carrying a wide range of flowers in their beaks and is exquisitely crafted. It belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}) and triggers flashes of memory when first handled. It was stolen a few days before the curse fell by a brash young guard who hoped to impress a paramour when they returned from a long trip to Caliphas. The curse fell first, and the flag has remained stashed here ever since.

Training Yard.name: Training Yard
Training Yard.text:
The dirt path widens into a paved courtyard nestled between the castle wall and the looming structure itself. Nearly a dozen sparring dummies sit against the walls to the east and west, while a staggered row of six archery targets have been placed against the southern castle facade.

The door into the castle at area @UUID[.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1h} opens into the castle cellars, but until that area is unlocked, this door remains impossible to interact with. When the PCs unlock the cellars, the door is unlocked and leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.BfZkDiplNpaK6npm]{C27}. The old bloodstains along the door frame suggest that someone wasn’t quite all the way inside the last time it slammed shut.

Encounter

Low 6

@UUID[Actor.TlDmc2ZKeIAJuD5v]{Giant Crawling Hands x2}

Creatures: Once a place where off-duty guards could practice archery and melee or engage in mock battle, the training yard is now the haunt of a pair of giant crawling hands. These hands, a left and a right, once belonged to the master of the guards—a hapless man named Korven Willachur whose ghost can be found within the castle cellars at area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.wO8FX9GQqMgltKx6]{C28}. His hands, lopped off at the wrist as the door at area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.wO8FX9GQqMgltKx6]{C28} slammed shut on him, have grown into monstrously enormous undead guardians.

One of the giant crawling hands lies barely buried under a low mound of dirt in the northeast corner of the archery yard, while the other lurks amid the hanging vines to the northeast. The hands leap out of hiding to attack any PC who comes within 5 feet of either hiding place, and both attack as soon as the PCs seem to lose interest in the area and begin to leave. They pursue fleeing PCs relentlessly and fight until destroyed. When either hand is destroyed, it swiftly shrinks to human size and decays into a leathery, shriveled limb on the ground.

Treasure

The left hand wears a signet ring worth 25 gp. A PC who studies it and succeeds at a @Check[society|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} can recognize it as a badge of office for a master of the guard in the county of Varno. This ring and the hands themselves are necessary to put their cursed owner’s ghost to rest.

Side Quest Completion

A PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the area and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check notices a small heart carved into one of the wooden supports for the stairs leading up to the castle wall. Inside the heart are initials: “AD and YM.” If the PCs have spoken to Ausken Dast and search for this romantic bit of minor vandalism, the Perception DC is reduced to 20. Reporting back to Ausken where the carving was and that it remains intact completes his @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.5oJGMvwqnrQybliF#side-quest]{side quest}.

Hedge Maze.name: Hedge Maze
Hedge Maze.text:
This enclosed area of the castle grounds is entirely filled with a hedge maze, with ten-foot- high and five-foot-wide walls of foliage hemming in the paths. Every ten to twenty feet, the tops of these hedges grow higher and have been sculpted into hounds that appear perched atop the walls, looking down imperiously on the maze below.

This hedge maze isn’t particularly difficult to navigate but served as a fun distraction for visitors who sought the small reflecting pool located at the maze’s center. The traditional entrance to the maze is via one of the two doors at the western end, be it area @UUID[.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1l} (which leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.3hduGPZ55keA2HRA]{D15} and is inaccessible until the PCs unlock the reception halls) or area @UUID[.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1m} (which leads into area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.1O4BfvPuyfyznvYR]{A20} on the haunted shore). Entrances from the castle walls are all blocked by unlocked gates, while Arudora family members sometimes used the secret door at area @UUID[.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1n}.

Note that navigating mazes isn’t always fun in a tabletop RPG! This hedge maze isn’t meant to be a mapping challenge, and clever PCs can secure a bird’s-eye view of it from the castle walls. The easiest way to run this maze is to assume the PCs can find their way to the central reflecting pool (and back out) after wandering for [[/gmr 1d6+1#minutes of wandering]] minutes or just 1 minute if a PC succeeds at a @Check[survival|dc:20] check.

Encounter

Low 6

@UUID[Actor.if9KbKLH7DtjVugJ]{Hound Topiary x4}

Creatures: Before the curse fell, guests or family could watch people navigate the maze from the windows overlooking the area from above in the reception halls or the private halls. In those days, the only danger the maze harbored was someone getting lost, but now, four of the topiary hounds that stand vigil over the central reflecting pool area have become animated by vile magic. These living topiary hounds attack on sight; they pursue prey throughout the maze but not beyond its borders.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Animate Hound Topiaries" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to hide the inanimate topiary hound tiles and reveal their tokens!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.bjprhR7Lbxsh6Tfl]{Tiled Basin}

The reflecting pool is dry, its tiled basin crusted with dirt and a few splashes of long-dried blood. At the center of the pool glitters a @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.uT2rZ6sr9wmX1Bc2]{soulheart}. The first PC to touch this soulheart receives a brief memory of a younger Ausken Dast and a blond woman, both dressed as castle guards, stealing a kiss at the edge of the reflecting pool.

Temple Grove.name: Temple Grove
Temple Grove.text:
An overgrown park-like grove sits in this secluded corner of the castle grounds. A few dead trees, their bare branches twisted like claws, stand amid the overgrown mess, and faint pathways are barely visible among the weeds. In the middle of the area sits an overgrown fountain filled with algae-thick water. A set of four moss-covered marble benches surround the fountain, while at its center stands a broken statue. Four stone buildings that look almost like mausoleums loom in the corners of the area, their inward- facing facades open to reveal statues standing deep in the shadows within.

This grove gave the priests of the castle temple (and privileged guests) a place to relax and meditate upon the wisdom of Pharasma, but the grove and temple hadn’t been used for many years by the time the curse descended. The temple looms above, for even while still ghostly, the boarded-up structure is still intimidating. The broken statue in the fountain once depicted Pharasma, as do the four statues in the faux mausoleums. These four statues have fared slightly better, and each depicts Pharasma in a different way. The statue at B10a depicts her in her classic appearance as a stern woman siting on a throne, hourglass in hand as she prepares to judge the dead. Area B10b shows her with a kinder expression, standing as she nestles a swaddled infant in her arms. In area B10c, she’s depicted with her hands held high as she looks to the heavens above, ready to receive prophecies and omens of fate. In the final area, B10d, she’s shown as an impossibly old woman with a stooped back and a serene expression on her face as she cradles a sundial in her arms—Pharasma as a goddess of time. These small shrines can be used to ask for Pharasma’s aid as detailed in @UUID[.#the-cycle-rite]{The Cycle Rite}, but as long as the grove remains profaned by the creatures that dwell within it, this rite will not function.

Encounter

Moderate 6

@UUID[Actor.W6L4EeEHa9cbsEIb]{Elite Esipil Sahkils x4} @UUID[Actor.ANptV6ltBi9C3P1l]{Nucol Sahkil}

The one-time sacred nature of this grove has attracted the attention of several fiendish monsters—sahkils—eager to bask in the broken glories of a deity they and their tormentors abhor. Four of these creatures are particularly hearty esipils. They spend their time flopping and splashing in the fouled waters of the fountain.

The fifth sahkil is more dangerous—a piglike nucol that’s currently scratching its pustule-rich flank against the side of the statue of Pharasma in area B10b. The monsters react quickly as soon as they notice the PCs, attacking at once. The esipils open combat with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4koZzrnMXhhosn0D]{Fear} spells then slither forth to attack in melee. The nucol doesn’t bother with magic and charges up to Spray Pus and attack. The sahkils have an eerie ability to sense the faithful of Pharasma, and target PCs who worship her first. They fight to the death.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.I4AKOC4MZDDH3y0W]{Filthy Water} @UUID[Actor.vsCaMzKZMf5oHQPB]{Roots}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the filthy opaque water in the fountain and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers a grime-encrusted brass gear the size of a dinner plate. The gear is 1 Bulk, and once the grime is cleaned away, despite lying underwater for a long time, it appears completely new, without a hint of corrosion. This is one of the missing gears from the clockworks in the temple above.

Of the five dead trees, the one furthest to the east near area @UUID[.0t97LM0jdXi2baWB]{B1j} is notably different. The other five appear dry and brittle, but this one glistens and drips with moisture. Its roots are tumescent with decay and curl upward from the soil, almost as if they seek to grow away from something below. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:22|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} realizes that before it died, the tree was affected by something beneath it. Thirty minutes of digging in the ground under and around the roots turns up the source: a @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.iQLEbANowf4fT8hK]{vile remnant}. This particular remnant took root here after a fragment from the whispering remnant Velicarn brought with him to trigger the curse fell during the night he was led into the castle by the scullery maid, but it’s currently dormant.

The Cycle Rite

A PC who worships Pharasma and is an expert in Religion, or any PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to Recall Knowledge, recognizes these particular depictions of the goddess as part of an obscure Pharasmin ritual meant to clear the mind and focus thoughts. By progressing on a walk in the right order, pausing at each statue to offer a prayer in the form of a bow and a touch to the forehead and then to the lips, one can perform this ritual. Any PC who recognizes the significance knows the right order is fate (area B10c), birth (B10b), time (B10d), and death (B10a). The first time a PC performs this ritual, they hear a distant bell tolling and the tortured grinding of clock tower gears far above—they realize the clock tower is damaged and needs repair.

Missing Gears

When the curse struck, the remaining divine energy that hadn’t been corrupted from the church temple reacted violently as it was finally expunged, causing a devastating explosion in the temple’s clock tower that sent 13 gears shooting off into different parts of the castle. As these gears flew, they slipped in and out of phase, sometimes punching holes in walls, other times passing through them like ghosts. The gears are now scattered throughout Bastardhall, and the first time a PC touches one, they’ll hear the sound of a muffled explosion from the clock tower above the temple followed by the conviction that not only does this gear not belong where it was found, but it yearns to be returned to the machinery it was once a part of. Each of these brass gears resist corrosion and might be worth 25 gp to a clockwork technician or collector. No one in Maiserene will purchase them, as the phantoms instinctively recognize that they belong in the clock tower and suggest @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.osl3dmryGXkoTcAc#repairing-the-gearworks]{returning them}. If one of these items is destroyed, it reforms back in the location it was found in 8 hours. Restoring all 13 gears to the clockworks is one of the required conditions to achieve this Adventure Path’s @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.iIIzG8EEQwsCV7an]{secret ending}, but PCs who neglect to do so can later sell each of the items they’ve gathered once they escape Bastardhall for 25 gp each.

Temple Pond.name: Temple Pond
Temple Pond.text:
Tangles of reeds and thistle plants grow along the muddy banks of this long, oval pool. It’s impossible to tell how deep the water is due to the thick layer of slick green algae that grows atop it.

Encounter

Trivial 6

@UUID[Actor.H2awmVR3ENs0VeYg]{Lovelorns x2}

Creatures: When the curse struck, two of the castle’s cooks fled here. The two were lovers, and the pond had been a favorite place for them to take their lunch, and as everything fell apart around them, they held hands and threw themselves into the waters to drown rather than face whatever horrible fate lay in store for them. Alas, this did not offer escape, and from their bodies burst a pair of lovelorns.

The melancholic undead monsters scuttled back from the water and sought out those who’d been friends with the couple in life, seeking to slay them before the other monsters unleashed by the curse could find them. When their task was done, they returned here and sunk back into the waters.

The lovelorns don’t immediately emerge from the water when their lifesense detects the PCs. Instead, the tiny undead horrors stalk the PCs. If they’re noticed, they attack, but otherwise they wait until the PCs get in a fight with another creature in the area, at which point they pounce, taking advantage of the distraction. If the PCs go to sleep before then, the lovelorns ambush them at night, starting with illusory creatures based on still-sleeping PCs. Once combat begins, the lovelorns fight to the death.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.mjstQmEbSFjIpvWP]{Underwater Skeletons}

Every 10 minutes a PC spends @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the pond, they can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:22|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. On a success, they discover two skeletons in the mud underwater in the middle of the pond. The bones embrace each other, indicating they died in each others’ arms, yet both of their backs have exploded outward. It’s from these rib fragments that the lovelorns created their legs. One of the skeletons wears a heart-shaped charm of resistance that protects against fire, while the other wears a matching charm of resistance that protects against cold.

Houndkeeper's Quarters.name: Houndkeeper's Quarters
Houndkeeper's Quarters.text:
Fur rugs lie scattered over the wooden floorboards of this one-room combination office and bedroom. Against the north wall is a bookcase filled with scrolls and ledgers next to a chair and wooden desk, while to the south sits a bed and a dresser—with a small wood stove between them. A double door stands ajar to the south as well. Nearly two dozen candles flicker in this room, their placement just deliberate enough to suggest some sort of occult activity.

Castle Arudora’s houndkeeper lived here. He was a burly man named Kusk who valued his privacy and agreed to the task of training the castle’s dozen hounds in return for being given his own place next to the kennel. The man’s reason for desiring privacy harbored a sinister truth, for he was secretly a worshipper of Alocer, the infernal duke of beasts and hunters. When the curse fell, Kusk fled to the adjoining kennels and begged Alocer to save him, even sacrificing the Arudora hounds in hopes of attracting his fiendish patron’s attention. Alocer either didn’t notice or didn’t care, and when the sacrificed hounds arose as hell hounds thanks to Charg’s curse, they tore Kusk apart.

Encounter

Trivial 6

@UUID[Actor.VQrtNCtgkoNuCaxn]{Zizminarial}

Creature: The current occupant of this chamber was drawn here after Bastardhall’s first manifestation, a hundred years after Kusk’s death—an unusual venedaemon named Zizminarial. His ability to smell magic is strangely specialized: rather than sniffing out all magic, he can only smell divine magic or prayers uttered in desperation. The stink of Kusk’s final prayers lured Zizminarial here, and he became fascinated by all the tortured souls still stuck in this prison and decided to stay. Over the past several centuries, he’s learned a complex method by which he can capture some of Bastardhall’s souls in the flame of a candle.

Once caught, the flame burns forever without consuming the wax, and the prayers for release wafting up are, to the daemon, as fine a bouquet as he could ask for. The process of trapping a soul in a candle flame is complex and time-consuming, but over the centuries he’s managed to catch 22 souls. Once he’s gathered two more, he’s promised himself a return to Abaddon with his two-dozen curated candle flames, which he hopes to use to barter with more powerful daemons for increased power of his own.

Zizminarial’s filthy, bloodstained robes were once sacred vestments to Shelyn; he enjoys wearing them and takes comfort in the blasphemy. The PCs’ arrival astounds and startles him, as no such thing has happened since his arrival. If he hears the PCs approaching from the courtyard, he’ll cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.i35dpZFI7jZcRoBo]{Illusory Disguise} to appear as a beefy human wearing furs then step out to urge the PCs into his home, warning them about the perils and promising safety within. This is a lie, of course, and Zizminarial uses Deception to trick the PCs. If the PCs fall for his lies, he engages in small talk, asking them where they came from and what they’re up to while he sniffs them out. If any of the PCs can cast divine spells, he decides to make one of them (chosen at random) his new target and tells the PCs that the nearby kennel has plenty of room for them all to rest and recover. He opens doors to the kennel and, with a whistle, commands the hell hounds to attack. At this point, (or earlier, if the PCs attack), Zizminarial focuses his attacks first on his target while the hell hounds fight the others.

Effect

@UUID[Item.nMii0JtBptSgwD01]{Zizminarial's Illusory Disguise}

You can apply the effect linked above to disguise Zizminarial as a human!

If he’s reduced to 30 or fewer Hit Points, Zizminarial casts translocate to escape to the southern shore of the temple pond (area @UUID[.t1s9G6BjLx2VvxXt]{B11}) then flees further south to the grove, casting heal on himself as he goes. He’s on speaking terms with the sahkils and rouses their interest quickly enough so he can lead them back to continue the fight, letting them take on the PCs in melee while he hangs back and uses magic. Brought down to 15 Hit Points on this second fight, Zizminarial attempts to surrender, promising to teach the PCs his secrets if they let him go free. If the PCs agree, the venedaemon agrees to speak to them for a time about what he’s learned about Bastardhall and the curse—see Zizminarial’s Discoveries below.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.sWB1geTAi624rM1r]{Bookcase}

The robes Zizminarial wears aren’t magical, or at least they’re not until he’s slain and the PCs take them and clean them. Such an act is all that’s required to gain Shelyn’s thanks, and the robes become a suit of +1 explorer’s clothing.

A PC who attempts to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic} on any of the soul candles that remain lit after the fight and succeeds at a @Check[occultism|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] or @Check[religion|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] (or a @Check[arcana|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] or @Check[nature|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check) notices the tiny screaming faces and hears the faint cries for release from each candle and understands that these candles have been used to contain souls already captured by the curse of Bastardhall. These trapped souls are of little use to the PCs unless they’re released—while the candles burn forever if left alone, a simple Interact action is all that’s needed to put one out. Each time a PC puts out a candle and frees a soul, they feel a brief sensation of thanks. Once all 22 candles are out and all 22 souls released (either as a result of Zizminarial’s actions in combat or the PCs’ acts of mercy), this room becomes protected and serves as a safe place to rest.

The first time the PCs rest in this room, echoes of those grateful souls bolster them as they sleep, causing them to regain twice the normal amount of HP from the rest and granting them all an additional saving throw to reduce the stage of any afflictions they’re suffering (this additional saving throw cannot cause an affliction to increase its stage on a failure).

The scrolls and ledgers on the bookcase can be used to research Zizminarial’s Discoveries, but a PC who either @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the shelves for 10 minutes or achieves the maximum RP for researching there is able to gather up enough of Zizminarial’s notes and musings to be able to cobble together the formula for the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.MTNlvZ0A9xY5sOg1]{Rest Eternal} ritual.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.UUqGlDCzpRnwqovv]{The Bastardhall Curse}

Zizminarial’s Discoveries: The PCs either speak to a cooperative Zizminarial about what he’s learned about the Bastardhall’s Curse or sift through his tangled and disorganized research notes to do the same.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[intimidation|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] or @Check[deception|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to ask the right questions of Zizminarial in a way he’s compelled to answer honestly, or @Check[occultism|dc:27|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to make sense of his notes.

Kennels.name: Kennels
Kennels.text:
Partially burned wooden bars separate this room into four smaller kennels around a large central area. A badly burned human skeleton clutching a shortbow that lacks any fire damage at all lies on the floor in the southernmost kennel.

Encounter

Trivial 6

@UUID[Actor.RTviEfjYnsXa0wkT]{Hell Hounds x3}

Creatures: When the keeper of the hounds, Kusk, sacrificed them in hopes of earning salvation from his fiendish patron, Charg’s curse quickly brought them back as hell hounds who in turn ripped Kusk to pieces. Over the centuries, the stronger hell hounds have slaughtered their weaker kin as well, so that now, only three remain. They immediately start howling and barking as soon as they spot intruders and attack at once, leaping with ease through or over the mostly-destroyed kennel fencing. The noise is enough to swiftly draw the attention of Zizminarial from area @UUID[.Wph54WLEpDPGxJ06]{B12} if he still lives.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.qrOegrWKN2UccJbE]{Scorched Skeleton}

The scorched skeleton in the southern kennel are Kusk’s remains. The +1 striking fearsome shortbow he owned is still serviceable (the bow is emblazoned with unsettling images of hell hounds hunting frightened families), but the rest of his gear is damaged beyond recognition.

Well.name: Well
Well.text:
A low stone well sits in the middle of a patch of overgrown weeds. A broken rope hangs from the central span built into the little wood roof above—there’s no sign of a bucket.

This well drops 10 feet down to a point where a cloud of roiling green mist billows. Until the cellars are unlocked, no progress further is possible—a PC who falls into the well lands on the mist and finds it as unyielding as solid stone. They can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.3yoajuKjwHZ9ApUY]{Grab an Edge} with a @Check[reflex|dc:20|options:action:grab-an-edge|traits:manipulate] save; otherwise they take falling damage as normal. The rough stone walls can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climbed} with a @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check. Once the cellars are unlocked, the mist in this well drops a further 10 feet, exposing an opening in the east wall 20 feet down that leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0LMAGxf5oiQklEFh]{C39}. Then, once the dungeon is unlocked, the mist clears completely and the well drops 130 feet, all the way into the water in area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.0CdaOwJhcWtoKSkm]{E3}.

It’s tough to see from above, but a PC who peers into the well and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check notes an opening in the well’s eastern wall at the 20 foot depth as well. A PC who climbs or falls down there automatically notices this entrance into an underground room to the east, but access to this room is blocked by more shimmering green mist. When the PCs unlock the cellars, this entrance becomes available and leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0LMAGxf5oiQklEFh]{C39}.

Storeroom.name: Storeroom
Storeroom.text:
Cobweb-draped shelves run along the walls of this wooden storeroom. More crates, barrels, casks, and other storage containers have been pushed up against these shelves, also thick with webbing. The cobwebs make it difficult to see the ceiling above.

This long building served as a generalized storage and equipment shed for those who worked the castle grounds, containing landscaping tools, repair tools, firewood, gardening equipment, and the like.

Encounter

Low 6

@UUID[Actor.TFRt64nosuS3PzmH]{Ether Spiders x2}

Creatures: A pair of relatively recent arrivals to Bastardhall have settled into this area to make a nest. These two ether spiders stumbled upon this “strange scab of solidity” as they call it, and made their ethereal nests within the area. When the PCs unlocked the courtyard and brought solidity to it, the ether spiders were shocked and unsettled but also intensely curious as to what could have caused this change.

When the PCs first enter this area, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:11|traits:secret]. On a success, the two ether spiders are elsewhere and finding, much to their confusion, they can no longer enter the immaterial portions of the castle like they were able to before. The strange development has them a little bit spooked but also even more curious. Once the PCs leave the area, the ether spiders come across them soon in their explorations, likely as the PCs are fighting other creatures in the courtyard (in which case the spiders watch the battle quietly and quizzically) or approaching the PCs the next time they camp (this replaces that camp’s chance for an ambush). If the flat check fails, the ether spiders are present when the PCs enter the storeroom.

Once the spiders encounter the PCs (be it in here on a failed flat check or out in the courtyard) and there’s no distracting combat going on, the slightly larger of the two greets them in Aklo while the other slowly creeps around to the side—as if to flank the PCs. The spider is, in fact, merely trying to get a better view of these strange visitors (as a PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:17|name:PF2E.Actions.SenseMotive.Title|options:action:sense-motive|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1xRFPTFtWtGJ9ELw]{Sense Motive} can confirm). If the PCs can’t understand them or attack, the spiders decide to kill them for food and flee into the Ethereal Plane as soon as one of them is reduced to fewer than 20 Hit Points.

If the PCs speak to them, the spiders are delighted by the conversation and ply the PCs with questions about who they are, where they’re from, what they’re doing here, and if they know why the castle grounds are now solid. If the PCs explain what happened, the spiders are delighted, annoyed, amused, and disturbed, shifting swiftly through all the emotions before admitting, “It’s a shame. We can’t go inside the castle anymore. We don’t know why, but there wasn’t much to see through the haze anyway. It’s very odd in there.” Hearing a talking magic spider describe something as odd should feel particularly of note to the PCs.

Assuming the PCs aren’t too obnoxious, the spiders offer to share what they’ve learned about the place, giving the PCs a chance to do a bit of research on Bastardhall. Once the PCs are done talking to the spiders, the creatures announce that they’re leaving. “This place is more wrong than right, and we want to go.” Before they leave, though, they thank the PCs for their company and, as a parting gift, tell them about some of the important looking things in one of the hidden crates at the southern end of the room—see Treasure, below. “That stuff was here when we got here, and it looks neat, but we don’t want it. You have hands, though, so maybe you do?”

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.dnKWI7sV1giQAQ2n]{Storeroom Crate}

If the spiders tell the PCs where the treasure-bearing crate is, they can find it with only a minute of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching}. Otherwise, every 10 minutes a PC spends Searching the room allows them to attempt a @Check[perception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check to discover the crate. The crate itself is stuffed behind several others, and according to stenciling on the side was intended to be delivered to the “Arudora Gallery.” Through a shipping mistake, it ended up here, forgotten. Inside, the crate is packed with straw and a shipping invoice that catalogs its contents, along with a thank-you from a long-dead painter named Minialee Dreelish in Caliphas for the honor of displaying their artwork at Castle Arudora.

The contents of the crate include a leather satchel containing a dozen now-collector’s-item horror novels worth a total of 100 gp, a pair of lover’s gloves with a short note on a folded piece of blue paper inside the left glove that reads, “Thank you for the wonderful night—I’ll never look at the moon again the same,” and is signed “Your Minialee.” (This note will potentially be quite helpful in area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}.) The final item is a large framed painting wrapped in silk. The silk is fine and worth 20 gp, but the Bulk 2 painting is more valuable. It depicts a strikingly beautiful man with long, dark hair standing along the edge of gentle stream in the middle of a forested valley beneath the light of an unusually large moon. It’s a beautiful, if haunting, work of art—and it was slated to be put on display in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}) only to be accidentally lost here a week before the curse struck. The first time the artwork is handled, it triggers a flash of memory—of a man and a woman in love, enjoying a romantic night alone on the shore of a remote lake with the knowledge that one of them (the same man depicted in the painting) must return home to Castle Arudora come morning. As the PCs might eventually discover, the man with the long dark hair was Ilves Mondain, the curator of the castle gallery.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.PAMDhjQNkAm8rB5R]{Bastardhall}

Talking to Spiders: The PCs chat with the ether spiders, sorting out useful facts about Bastardhall from the non sequiturs and needlessly complicated metaphors they are fond of wallowing in.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[diplomacy|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to gently guide the spiders onto pertinent topics, @Check[occultism|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to be able to grow comfortable with their strange linguistic cadence, or @Check[perception|dc:27|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to notice important facts buried under stilted and florid speech.

Reward

If the PCs speak to the spiders and part peacefully with them, grant them XP as if they’d defeated them in combat.

Stables.name: Stables
Stables.text:
Throughout this straw-floored stable, several thick wooden timbers support the rafters and stone ceiling. The copious number of supports suggests somethings of great weight on the floor above, though the supports are never spaced so closely together as to make it difficult to lead horses through the area. Many wooden stalls fill the building, and a spiral staircase winds up the northeast corner of the room.

The Arudoras kept several horses, mostly at the urging of Jinnivere Arudora, whose spending habits on purchasing new horses for training, only to sell them at a loss or even give them away, had started to become a point of contention between her and her parents. Area B16a was a small workshop where Jinnivere spent much of her time studying the equestrian arts, journaling, and repairing her riding gear. The spiral staircase at area B16b lead upstairs to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.Xo2d6jZMY7tW2fwP]{D20a}, but as long as the reception halls remain locked, walls of green mist prevent progress further up either staircase than what appears on the map for the castle grounds. Area B16d contained crates of oats and other food for the horses, but today those supplies are empty. Area B16e is the entrance to a cursed set of stairs to the south that leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.Xo2d6jZMY7tW2fwP]{D20b}.

Encounter

Moderate 6

@UUID[Actor.X2vz6CrMaHIso0ha]{Skeletal Horses x6}

Creatures: The stable stalls (indicated as area B16c) once housed the Arudora horses, a few of whom were workhorses or carriage horses, but the ones kept in the eastern stables were set aside for Jinnivere. She was constantly frustrated to not have more room for her prized possessions (despite her fondness for horses, she never really appreciated them as companions—merely “servants” she commanded to pursue her love of riding), and whenever she succumbed to the urge to buy a new horse, one of her previous horses either got demoted to workhorse or was sold off at a loss just to get the beast out so the new favorite could move in.

Today, what appear to be scattered horse skeletons lay strewn about these stables, but as soon as any living creature approaches within 5 feet of any stable, all of the skeletons shudder, issue unnerving and distressing sounds (the panicked neigh of a horse, but in reverse), and clatter upward into animation. These skeletal bones are compelled to cruelty by a combination of the Bastardhall Curse and the once-living horses’ unpleasant memories of how they were treated by a woman who saw them only as tools for her own riding entertainment. There are six skeletal horses in all—three in the eastern stalls and three in the western ones, leaving the two stables in the middle empty. They attack at once and pursue living foes relentlessly, fighting until destroyed. A skeletal horse can smash through the rickety wall of a stable by attempting a @Check[athletics|dc:15|traits:manipulate] check as part of an Interact action, and they eagerly do so to get to the PCs.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.ST8OqX7vfnOccqhs]{Stables} @UUID[Actor.GLuLQkX1kaoyQSCO]{Dry Water Trough}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} area B16a for 10 minutes not only discovers a half dozen of Jinnivere’s journals (which can be used to Research her—see @UUID[.#research]{Jinnivere’s Journals} below), but also two empathy charms and a private workshop that resembles (and expands into) a leatherworker’s workshop.

In a dry water trough in the central southern stall sits a @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.uT2rZ6sr9wmX1Bc2]{soulheart}. The first PC to touch this soulheart receives a brief memory of Ilana Greenbough visiting the stable to help Jinnivere with a particularly complicated repair to a saddle. After Jinnivere puts the saddle onto one of the horses and rides out into the courtyard to test it, Ilana watches sadly as she whips the horse swiftly to a breakneck speed. As Ilana steps over to offer a particularly skittish-looking horse an apple, the memory fades.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.6tXqaoCmhlHFRm3I]{Jinnivere Arudora}

Jinnivere’s Journals: The PC pages through several of Jinnivere Arudora’s journals to learn more about her.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[library-lore|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to read through the journals in the most efficient manner, @Check[society|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to read between the lines and make deductions Jinnivere didn’t quite write down, or @Check[perception|dc:27|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to make out some of her illegible writing.

Carriage House.name: Carriage House
Carriage House.text:
This room’s thirty-foot-high ceiling rises to a dome set with several skylights, all cunningly supported by wooden beams along the walls so that the central area remains clear. There’s enough room here for two horse-drawn carriages, but currently there’s only one—a once elegant black carriage now lying in a heap of rubble near several racks of shelves to the north. A wooden flight of stairs leads up to the south.

The stairs to the south lead up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.k9ECGjicvbLkrZvs]{J2}, but until the towers are unlocked, passage beyond the point shown on the castle grounds map is blocked by impassable green mist. The ruined carriage is beyond repair—its twin is missing, claimed by Velicarn for his centennial trips to seek out distant kin.

Encounter

Moderate 6

@UUID[Actor.xDNjxFXDFtl9thUa]{Jinnivere Arudora} @UUID[Actor.ExVmw8bSvUd2wYkI]{Nulferion}

Creature: Jinnivere usually spends her time languishing in up her tower in a higher part of Bastardhall where she can look down and observe the courtyard without being noticed herself, but when the PCs enter this area, her presence becomes more apparent. The first time a PC enters this room, they hear the faint sound of horse hooves clopping on the ground somewhere behind them if they succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check, but a glance in that direction shows nothing. All PCs who enter the carriage room sense faint feelings of resentment toward their allies, as if they were recalling past insults their allies directed their way about their appearance. During the day, these feelings are faint yet noticeable, but after dark, they’re more pronounced.

The first time a PC enters this area after dark, they must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:20|options:inflicts:stupefied] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 hour by the unpleasant conviction their allies dislike them (this duration extends to 8 hours on a critical failure).

Jinnivere herself only takes full notice of the PCs once two of the following conditions are met:

  • The skeletal horses in area @UUID[.JdWKi5eQMFgU0eFf]{B16} have all been destroyed.

  • All three soulhearts (from areas @UUID[.N0oA9IF4Mzzk1MN8]{B5}, @UUID[.eaV4LD57vEj6Vcr5]{B9}, and @UUID[.JdWKi5eQMFgU0eFf]{B16}) have been recovered.

  • PCs who have achieved 7 RP while @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.6tXqaoCmhlHFRm3I]{researching Jinnivere} know that she was teased mercilessly by her brother. Calling out an insulting challenge to her from anywhere in the castle grounds with a successful @Check[intimidation|dc:24] check counts as a condition (or as two on a critical success, causing Jinnivere to manifest immediately)

Alternatively, the first time the PCs approach within 30 feet of this area when they’re 7th level or higher, or the first time they call out to Jinnivere and insult her appearance at that level, Jinnivere automatically manifests.

When she manifests, the northeast doors to the carriage room burst open with a thunderous bang that can be heard throughout the castle grounds. If the PCs are in sight, Jinnivere charges out of the carriage room on her horse with an unearthly howl of fury, otherwise she waits to do so as soon as the PCs return to the area.

Jinnivere appears as a lanky, headless human woman dressed in elegant riding clothes. In one hand she carries her riding crop, while in the other, she wields a bastard sword, riding with supernatural ease while both hands are occupied. She was slain by a sahkil on the night of the curse. In her new existence as a dullahan, she has very little interest in anything other than the slaughter of intruders and the glory of riding her mount at breakneck speed (not that she has a neck to worry about breaking).

Once combat begins, Jinnivere charges toward the PCs on her horse, Nulferion. She spends her first action each round to Command Nulferion to Stride to a PC with a @Check[nature|dc:18|name:PF2E.Actions.CommandAnAnimal.Title|options:action:command-an-animal|traits:auditory,concentrate] check, then she Strikes once with her bastard sword and once with her riding crop. Any time she’s separated from her mount, she’ll Summon Steed to replace him, and whenever a PC is slain, she sets aside all other tactics to go Reap the body. She’ll pursue PCs relentlessly throughout the castle grounds, dismounting from her steed to follow them into buildings, but if they attempt to escape up the stairs onto the castle walls, she rides up after them—to do so she must Command her steed with a @Check[nature|dc:23|name:PF2E.Actions.CommandAnAnimal.Title|options:action:command-an-animal|traits:auditory,concentrate] check, and the warhorse treats the stairs as difficult terrain. She won’t pursue the PCs out onto the haunted shore, but if they later return, they’ll find her patrolling the courtyard relentlessly—she attacks the PCs as soon as she notices them.

Jinnivere fights until she’s destroyed, at which point she shrieks in terror from the empty space where her head should be. A moment later, her mount fades away and her body, thrashing in agony, grows ghostly and translucent as it rises into the air then streaks like a comet up into the sky above to where her tower awaits. At the same time, her gear drops to the ground—her @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.fZDL0jQQy1jQTg4c]{riding crop} is the key to unlocking the cellars of Bastardhall (see area @UUID[.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3}).

North Gate.name: North Gate
North Gate.text: Methods for bypassing this lowered gate from the north side are summarized at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.FuifNpUpaAG0LzlR]{A12}, but once a creature gets on this side of the gate, two separate wheels on the east and west side of the tower each allow for someone to raise the gate after two minutes of cranking (one minute if someone works at each wheel).

Reception Halls Entrance.name: Reception Halls Entrance
Reception Halls Entrance.text: These large double doors are the main entrance to the castle’s reception halls, and were the primary entrance used by guests of the castle, as well as by the Arudoras themselves. Until the PCs unlock the reception halls, these doors remain out of phase and cannot be interacted with. See area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.goyxlKit1QLHYYuh]{D1} for more details on these doors once they’re available for use.

Groundskeeper's Entrance.name: Groundskeeper's Entrance
Groundskeeper's Entrance.text: The groundskeepers came and went from the castle using this entrance. Until the PCs unlock the cellars, this mist-shrouded door remains out of phase and cannot be interacted with. See area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.1tfiJnjtQbAUTr1s]{C1} for more details on these doors once they’re available for use.

Carriage Ramp.name: Carriage Ramp
Carriage Ramp.text: The Laroba Bridge connects to the roof above the stable, and carriages and horses who arrived could move down this stone and wood causeway to reach the courtyard and eventually be sheltered in the carriage house or stable. Until the reception halls are unlocked, the top of this ramp is blocked by impenetrable green mists, but after they’re available, one can use this ramp to reach the causeway platform above (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.Xo2d6jZMY7tW2fwP]{D20c}).

Temple Entrance.name: Temple Entrance
Temple Entrance.text: A pair of large double doors here provide access to the castle’s temple once that region is unlocked, but until then, access to area @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1a} beyond is blocked by impassable green mist.

Servants' Entrance.name: Servants' Entrance
Servants' Entrance.text: This servants’ entrance led to the servants’ quarters. It’s impassible until the cellars are unlocked, after which this door leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.rcdV1Q52IsBUDbDz]{C12a}.

Temple's View Ramp.name: Temple's View Ramp
Temple's View Ramp.text: This stone ramp provides exterior access to the sprawling rooftop plaza called Temple’s View. The top of the ramp is blocked by mist until the reception halls are unlocked, after which this ramp leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.tmNCXndKaS4Bi3tD]{D26a}.

Guard's Entrance.name: Guard's Entrance
Guard's Entrance.text: The castle guards used this entrance to come and go from the courtyard and the nearby training yard. It’s impassable until the PCs unlock the cellars, at which point it leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.BfZkDiplNpaK6npm]{C27}.

Priest's Entrance.name: Priest's Entrance
Priest's Entrance.text: Visitors to the temple rarely used this entrance, leaving it mostly for the temple clergy to come and go. It unlocks once the PCs gain access to the castle temple, and opens into area @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1b}.

West Trophy Hall Entrance.name: West Trophy Hall Entrance
West Trophy Hall Entrance.text: These doors unlock once the reception halls are unlocked, providing access to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.3hduGPZ55keA2HRA]{D15}.

Southern Watch Post West Entrance.name: Southern Watch Post West Entrance
Southern Watch Post West Entrance.text: This door opens into area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.1O4BfvPuyfyznvYR]{A20} of the haunted shore.

East Trophy Hall Entrance.name: East Trophy Hall Entrance
East Trophy Hall Entrance.text: This door unlocks once the reception halls are unlocked, providing access to area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.3hduGPZ55keA2HRA]{D15}.

Southern Watch Post East Entrance.name: Southern Watch Post East Entrance
Southern Watch Post East Entrance.text: This door opens into area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.1O4BfvPuyfyznvYR]{A20} of the haunted shore.

Hedge Maze Secret Entrance.name: Hedge Maze Secret Entrance
Hedge Maze Secret Entrance.text: The castle hedge maze hides several secrets, not the least of which is this secret door entrance into the private halls. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} here can spot the secret door with a successful @Check[perception|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. Once the private halls are unlocked, this secret door leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.t2z0PeMStqo5gA8Q]{F19}.

The Towers.name: The Towers
The Towers.text:
The key to escaping Bastardhall lies in its towers, and over the course of the previous chapters, the PCs have gathered the tools, lore, and secrets they need to do so. Before the night of the curse, the castle’s towers served as little more than vantage points for the Arudoras to look out over their lands and admire the view—only the clock tower above the temple served any additional purpose. But when the curse struck, these high vantages became focal points for the Arudoras themselves. Once every 100 years, the curse gave each of the original Arudoras active in and below the castle a place to look out onto the world and remember what they’d lost. The seven are always inexorably drawn to these towers, trapped like flies in amber on the one night each year when they could just otherwise walk to their individual freedom. Between the centuries, each of the seven is free to wallow in their own shame, obsession, and oblivious self-indulgence, but now, as the PCs have explored and confronted them, these seven Arudoras have once again been banished to their towers.

For in truth, an eight tower now stands—one that never existed before the curse and formed above the soul vortex far below. This tower floats in the air, attached to the rest of Bastardhall by a slim walkway that’s more decoration than architectural necessity. Located directly over the soul vortex, placed on opposite ends of the extreme above and below, this tower serves as a sort of beacon for Charg’s power. Here, the sahkil demigod is closest to Bastardhall, and in this tower, his high priest Caydserris patiently waits for the opportunity to bring Bastardhall back to Golarion as an immense monument to the Typhon Wheel.

Entering the Towers.name: Entering the Towers
Entering the Towers.text:
As the PCs return to the fountain at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3} with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.0LrDMdMNqUb9cxSV]{Irrokcis’s Medallion} in hand, the storm continues, but as soon as they return the medallion to the fountain, the storm intensifies to its full force. A bolt of lightning arcs from the clouds above to strike a ghostly lightning rod atop the floating tower (area @UUID[.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{J4}), then arcs down further to strike the PC who placed the medallion, dealing @Damage[10d6[electricity]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic|traits:electricity] save). A moment later, all the towers solidify except that one, leaving it, the domain of Caydserris and the place closest to Charg, as the only portion of the castle still out of phase. Simultaneously, ghostly ribbons of green ectoplasmic energy, strangely unaffected by the torrential rain and howling wind, stretch from six of the seven towers to this last one. Anchored as they are to the seven Arudora souls trapped within, it should be obvious to the PCs where they must go next to unlock the final tower. (Only area @UUID[.7rtJA41bt42SO4VG]{J3g} doesn’t manifest a ribbon, for it’s likely Irrokcis’s soul is still sheltered by his soul cage.)

Yet before the PCs have a chance to do so, the doors to the carriage house (area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.ROu4mQ4EeW48MQiZ]{B17}) burst open to release the bastard himself. Velicarn and his Black Coach have been unleashed, and the PCs are his new targets—proceed immediately with @UUID[.LlGwz4KdLIrP0aq2]{The Bastard of Bastardhall}.

The Skies Above.name: The Skies Above
The Skies Above.text:
The storm’s force transcends its previous fury, becoming into a full-blown tempest. Outdoors, Perception checks and ranged Strikes take a –4 circumstance penalty. Temperatures remain severe cold outdoors at all times, and occasionally, the rain changes to snow but never quite long enough to reach full blizzard or whiteout conditions. Unprotected, small open flames outside are snuffed out by the wind and rain. Lake Laroba’s waters remain dangerous, still requiring a PC to succeed at a @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim}, and the dungeon remains flooded as in the previous chapter. Waves surge against the shore, making anything within 15 feet of the shoreline on land difficult terrain. Thunder and lightning strike several times per hour. These lightning strikes become dangerous if the PCs are outside among the towers of Bastardhall. Once every 10 minutes while PCs are outdoors here, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:17]. On a success, a bolt of lightning strikes one of the outdoor PCs for @Damage[10d6[electricity]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic|traits:electricity] save.)

The sun rises one final time after this chapter begins, at two in the afternoon, only to immediately set. After this time, the nights are eternal in Bastardhall, and the sun never rises again. Eventually, the storm transforms into a blizzard, the lake freezes, and the weather finally abates, leaving Bastardhall a frozen wasteland, but these changes should take weeks to play out. Hopefully, the PCs triumph before then!

Tower Ambushes.name: Tower Ambushes
Tower Ambushes.text:
Encounter

Moderate 13

@UUID[Actor.G3D4rcYmVv4eusog]{Soul Gluttons x4}

If the PCs rest in an unsafe area in the towers, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:7]. On a failure, they’re ambushed by four soul gluttons.

Lucid Nightmares.name: Lucid Nightmares
Lucid Nightmares.text:
After unlocking the towers, the nightmare changes. This time, the PC stands in the courtyard of Bastardhall, looking up at the towers above. They know that the cloaked figure awaits them in the tallest tower and understand they must confront him to escape... yet as they do everything they can to get to him, horrific monsters attack from all sides, quickly overwhelming the PC. As the monsters tear the dreaming PC apart, the cloaked figure appears in the sky above, but this time, he mocks not the PC. Instead, he looks to the torn hole in the sky and holds his hands wide, offering the slaughtered PC to what awaits above. A single eye opens in the void to gaze hungrily upon its latest offering as the nightmare ends.

Food for the Typhoon Wheel

Resist Nightmare @Check[will|dc:31]

Critical Failure The PC wakes with teraphobia (fear of monsters), and at the start of any combat against a monstrous foe, they must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:31|options:inflicts:slowed,inflicts:stunned] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for the duration of the combat (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3} then slowed 1 on a critical failure).

Research @Check[intimidation|dc:33|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to become a monster yourself and frighten off your foes or @Check[religion|dc:36|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to recognize the eye of Charg and how to make the best of what time remains.

Effect

@UUID[Item.YbupG2YOc3QmxJSZ]{Teraphobia}

If a PC critically fails to resist this nightmare, use the linked effect to automate a Note reminder of the consequences of their Teraphobia whenever they roll initiative.

Campaign Climax.name: Campaign Climax
Campaign Climax.text:
The climax of Bastion of Blasphemies begins with a pair of events that occur close together, after which the PCs must travel to the seven towers to exorcise the souls of the seven Arudoras. Only then will they be able to confront Caydserris in the final tower—but even then, they’ll only truly defeat Charg’s plot if they’ve returned every missing piece of artwork to the gallery and fully restored the clock tower.

Note that the following two encounters could potentially spread throughout previously explored areas of the castle. The first encounter will likely use the maps of the castle grounds and the upper floor of the reception halls, while the second uses the map of the haunted shore.

The Bastard of Bastardhall.name: The Bastard of Bastardhall
The Bastard of Bastardhall.text:
Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

This encounter starts as the PCs are in the Castle Grounds level. Velicarn exits through the @UUID[.k9ECGjicvbLkrZvs]{J2} upper carriage house and descends down the @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.x6CMKIUGh0nDUdy7]{B1d} carriage ramp to meet the PCs!

Encounter

Moderate 13

@UUID[Actor.weLjvcmjY81S9CV9]{Velicarn (Coach)} @UUID[Actor.pRlJ0cepzWAyJeSJ]{Velicarn (Dullahan)}

Creatures: This encounter occurs as soon as the PCs restore the final missing memento to the fountain at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3}. As the PCs stand around the fountain after depositing the memento, Velicarn bursts out of the upper carriage house (area @UUID[.k9ECGjicvbLkrZvs]{J2}), driving the Black Coach. The demonic-looking horses that pull the carriage shriek and rear as he calls out from the void where his head should be, “I recognize you! The lickspittles of the last Arudora! Here to save her? Fools! You’ve only doomed yourselves!”

The sounds of the horses and the bastard’s bellowing fill the air and bounce off the castle walls. He immediately attacks, riding through the rain on the Black Coach down the ramp into the castle grounds and rolling Intimidation for initiative.

Velicarn pursues the PCs relentlessly throughout the castle grounds and beyond, seeking to trample the party as often as possible in his pursuit. In the event the PCs split up or make it difficult to use this tactic, he’ll use his innate spells instead. Although he, his coach, and fiendish horses all appear solid, they’re incorporeal—this allows him to pursue PCs into areas that would be much too small for him to fit were he solid. Remember that each round an incorporeal creature starts its turn within a solid object, it’s @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} until the end of its turn—this at least prevents Velicarn from trampling PCs if they seek shelter inside the castle. Note that there are plenty of large rooms within that would allow him full movement.

While the PCs have likely defeated most of the other inhabitants within the castle by this point, this encounter has a good chance of attracting any remaining denizens and dangers the PCs might not have dealt with yet. These creatures, once engaged, join the fight on Velicarn’s side, but they don’t particularly work well together. Feel free to have any creatures lower than 9th level simply be obliterated by the death coach as it tramples them—this can simultaneously make Velicarn seem even more dangerous but also speeds combat along by not cluttering things up with foes 13th level PCs wouldn’t be afraid of.

Voldrak Rises.name: Voldrak Rises
Voldrak Rises.text:
Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

This encounter starts as the PCs are in the Castle Grounds level. Velicarn exits through the @UUID[.k9ECGjicvbLkrZvs]{J2} upper carriage house and descends down the @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.x6CMKIUGh0nDUdy7]{B1d} carriage ramp to meet the PCs!

Once the PCs defeat Velicarn, give them about 10 minutes to catch their breath and recover, but afterward (or sooner if they immediately start to move to investigate the towers), a thunderous roar and explosion of water rips through the air, easily heard even over the tumult of the storm. This roar and immense splash come from the west, out of the waters of Lake Laroba. If the PCs ignore it, the roar and splashing continue, growing closer each time. If the PCs are inside the castle at this time (whether because they fled into it thinking to avoid Velicarn or went inside after their fight with the death coach), have them roll Perception checks to hear the sounds Voldrak is making. This should be an easy @Check[perception|dc:25] check to ensure the PCs aren’t oblivious to the lake monster’s destruction.

Encounter

Moderate 13

@UUID[Actor.ZNSDataoZlnuv8eP]{Voldrak}

The source of the commotion is Voldrak, the legendary monster of Lake Laroba, finally rising from the depths. Drawn into the region by the curse as well, Voldrak went from a somewhat shy and elusive @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core-2.Actor.ZdQfNuQQjytFzuyd]{water orm} to a truly dangerous foe, and if the PCs don’t quickly move down to the haunted shore, the monster surges onto land and swiftly destroys Maiserene. If they ignore it too long, in time, they’ll hear distant screaming and the destruction of buildings from the area as Voldrak destroys some of the smaller buildings first.

Eventually, he’ll flatten the entire area, which results in the destruction of all six of the PCs’ allied phantoms. This outcome causes them to lose any Hit Points granted through @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.8WxFFZm6OcBCCARR]{soulhearts}, so it’s best for the PCs to move quickly when they first hear the water orm’s roars.

The timing of this attack shouldn’t punish the PCs if they aren’t particularly fast. You want them to see the immense lake monster surging up from the depths toward area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.XyjmNWjgPGNrEVim]{A1} before he crawls up onto land, so try to time the encounter so the PCs meet Voldrak there. If the PCs take longer, they might need to contend with difficult terrain created by destroyed buildings. The order in which Voldrak destroys the buildings that contain allied phantoms goes numerically.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.66abiCNTBf15aDoy]{Voldrak Skeleton}

Once Voldrak is slain, the massive monster rears back its serpentine head to utter one final roar before his massive body crashes down on the shoreline then quickly rots away. The driving rain washes the putrefying meat from his bones so that, within a minute, all that remains is the creature’s skeleton. Voldrak’s bones remain beached for the rest of the campaign, a trophy of sorts reflecting one of the more memorable battles in Bastardhall.

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the skeleton notes that two of Voldrak’s teeth glow—these two teeth can be harvested with a minute’s work, and each one functions as a major potency crystal talisman.

Preparing for the Final Battle.name: Preparing for the Final Battle
Preparing for the Final Battle.text:
After the death of Voldrak, the PCs are free to take their time. They can continue to explore any part of Bastardhall they haven’t yet looked into, or they can start to investigate the areas that they’ve just unlocked—the seven towers and the upper level of the carriage house. The PCs could also use this time to collect any missing art or missing gears they might have overlooked while exploring Bastardhall. If the players seem unaware that they’re close to the final battle, make sure they know there’s still more to do to put the Bastardhall Curse to rest.

While seven similar hazards await them in the towers, no combat encounters (apart from any from previous chapters they haven’t yet instigated) remain until the PCs manifest the floating tower and confront Caydserris (area @UUID[.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{J4}) for control of Castle Arudora.

Laroba Causeway.name: Laroba Causeway
Laroba Causeway.text:
This location appears on the map of the upper floors of the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi]{reception halls}.

The Laroba Causeway was a thing of wonder back before its wooden deck was burned and it collapsed into the lake. The causeway remains here now, a ghostly figment that can’t be interacted with (any attempt to step onto it results in a fall) until the curse is lifted (area @UUID[.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{J4}), at which point the causeway becomes solid. When this occurs, the PCs can simply use it to walk back to Golarion, transitioning out of the Ethereal Plane as soon as they set foot on the far shore. Once they turn around, the causeway is gone, and the castle has returned to its normal appearance, yet now the pall of the curse is gone.

If the PCs achieve the secret ending and defeat Charg’s proxy, the despair dragon Zaurgaulus, the castle and causeway all shift back to Golarion—they can still use it to walk back to shore in this case, of course!

Upper Carriage House.name: Upper Carriage House
