Upper Carriage House.text:
This location appears on the map of the upper floors of the reception halls on page 104.

The air in this room has a heavy feel to it, and a thin layer of mist shimmers over the floor. The chamber is mostly empty—the open space in the center is large enough to house two carriages side by side. Barren shelves line the walls, while a single work desk and chair have been placed in the southeast near a flight of stairs leading downward. In the opposite wall stands a single door.

The southern stairs lead down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.ROu4mQ4EeW48MQiZ]{B17}. The door to the north leads to a flight of stairs that lead upward to area @UUID[.HCjLc7SR5D6ALwqY]{J3a}.

Velicarn languished in this chamber during the centuries between his rides into Ustalav, and as such, the residue of his hateful aura lingers even after his destruction. While there’s no real detriment for being in the room, those who stay too long become morose and irritable. Still, there’s nothing perilous in the chamber once the bastard of Bastardhall is no more.

A PC who spends a few moments studying the mist on the floor makes a startling discovery: This is no mist, but the ghostly shapes of dozens—perhaps hundreds—of blank-faced souls drifting and churning. These are spiritual echoes of all those Velicarn has brought to the castle, all the Arudoras over the centuries who have fallen victim to his lure or died through strange accidents after rejecting his invitation. The PC should catch a glimpse of Florin Kindler among these fragments of souls. A PC can concentrate and meditate on her fragmented soul echo to learn more of her fate.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.QDo0K7VXLVH9D9tI]{Florin Kindler}

Commune with Spiritual Echoes: The PC spends 10 minutes focusing and meditating on the fragment of Florin Kindler’s soul in an attempt to learn more of her fate.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[occutism|dc:31|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] or @Check[religion|dc:31|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to know how to open your mind to spiritual knowledge, @Check[diplomacy|dc:33|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to appeal to the fragmentary memories in the spiritual echo, or @Check[perception|dc:36|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to catch snatches of whispered revelations. A critical failure on any of these checks indicates the PC has become infested with malevolent energy and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 24 hours.

Arudora Towers.name: Arudora Towers
Arudora Towers.text:
Seven Arudora towers rise above the castle roofs in all. By this point, each one contains the soul of one of the seven Arudoras the PCs had to defeat in order to unlock Bastardhall completely. Of these, six will remain trapped here until the next time Bastardhall manifests on Golarion, at which point those six will regress into their monstrous incarnations and once again take up rule of their separate domains. The exception is Irrokcis, who rejuvenates much faster as a lich.

The interiors of each tower differ, as does the thematic nature of the haunt within. Each haunt must be disabled to exorcise that Arudora’s soul, severing its link to the floating tower while hurling the soul down into the soul vortex. Once all seven souls are released, the floating tower—the last part of Bastardhall remaining insubstantial—manifests.

Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

The Arudora Towers span three different scene levels. Here is the breakdown:

  • @UUID[.HCjLc7SR5D6ALwqY]{J3a} and @UUID[.GEtrwYJ9Wy5A0qyw]{J3b} are located in the Towers (Lower) level.

  • @UUID[.i6VM7zXFCXSnQqKp]{J3c}-@UUID[.7rtJA41bt42SO4VG]{J3g} are entered in the Towers (Lower) level, and ascend to the Towers (Upper) level, where their encounters take place.

  • @UUID[.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{J4} is accessed through the bridge in Towers (Upper), and the stairs inside take you to the Floating Tower level.

Jinnivere's Tower.name: Jinnivere's Tower
Jinnivere's Tower.text:
The interior of this wide tower is forty feet across, with a conical roof that rises to a height of thirty feet in the middle. The walls of this room depict horses and riders in various equestrian roles. Five majestic taxidermy horses of different breeds are displayed in proud poses.

This chamber was used by Jinnivere Arudora as a place to display favored horses after they passed on, each lovingly (if disturbingly) preserved by her father. The taxidermy horses are of various quality, as if her father improved at the art as time went on. Some of the creatures are clad in barding, while others simply have harnesses, and one is unadorned.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.RF3OHQRfV4pMPXa1]{Hidden Nook}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} this room for 30 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:33|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check notices a hidden latch on the wall near a depiction in the mural of a horse trampling a peasant. Within is a nook where Jinnivere kept a suit of +2 resilient winged leather armor (a PC who achieved 10 Research Points on Jinnivere can find this hidden panel and its treasure if they Seek near the trampling horse image).

Encounter

Low 13

@UUID[Actor.89txqXQ291LeFesk]{Trapped Jinnivere Soul}

Hazard: See @UUID[.NoCn9mgK3MvOpLEI]{Releasing the Arudoras}.

Dazerien's Tower.name: Dazerien's Tower
Dazerien's Tower.text:
The door leading to the tower is locked (@Check[thievery|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock} or @Check[athletics|dc:35|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open}). Alternatively, the bronze key carried by Dazerien down in area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.rE5yeZ8h5hPBo5Hu]{E13} can open it.

The interior of this circular chamber is thirty feet across, with a conical roof that rises to a height of thirty feet in the middle. The room might have once been used as storage, but all the crates and containers have been pushed to the edges to make room for four wooden poles that display a dozen different skeletons.

When he moved in, Dazerien was granted this old storeroom by Raudltz to do whatever he wished, with a promise no one would ever look within. Raudltz suspected his proclivities and figured keeping such behaviors out of the sight was the safest option. He gave Dazerien the only key to the door. Dazerien repaid this trust by using the room as a place to imprison and kill those whom he caught or had delivered to the castle to fuel his need for cruelty. None of those kept here were alive when the curse struck.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.R7aDKBFq4pqRWiC4]{Felt Sheet}

Most of the contents of the old crates and boxes are mundane tools, extra bedding, and old clothes, many of which are still functional, though the bedding is stale and threadbare. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} this room for half an hour (or succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:33|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check or knows about the armor already while @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeking} through the crates to the west) finds a long-forgotten suit of standard-grade elven chain wrapped in a green felt sheet.

Encounter

Low 13

@UUID[Actor.k0QerxsfdB9LOn6H]{Trapped Dazerien Soul}

Hazard: See @UUID[.NoCn9mgK3MvOpLEI]{Releasing the Arudoras}.

Ryhasphinea's Tower.name: Ryhasphinea's Tower
Ryhasphinea's Tower.text:
This tower rises up two stories above the private halls below. The first story is little more than a landing, but the second functions as a small shrine to Urgathoa—the door leading to it is locked (@Check[thievery|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock} or @Check[athletics|dc:35|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open}); the key is long lost.

This circular room is overwhelmed by a pair of fifteen- foot-high statues made from a mix of giant’s bones below and clay above, each depicting a half-decayed woman holding a large and very real-looking scythe. Between the two stands a small wooden altar atop which is a copper bowl filled with live maggots and a thin-bladed dagger.

Ryhasphinea occasionally used this small shrine before she neared completion of her corruption of the main cathedral. She kept this place locked tight.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.jxcxlRfQRjTeJaWC]{Tower Altar}

The dagger on the altar is a +2 greater striking keen unholy dagger. This dagger is cursed as well with a level 13 version of a bloodbiter curse that doesn’t affect worshippers of Urgathoa.

Encounter

Low 13

@UUID[Actor.FMsMffDj6egOElJq]{Trapped Ryhasphinea Soul}

Hazard: See @UUID[.NoCn9mgK3MvOpLEI]{Releasing the Arudoras}.

Augsten's Tower.name: Augsten's Tower
Augsten's Tower.text:
This twenty-foot-diameter bedroom includes a four-poster bed with drawers built in below, a writing desk, and a plush chair.

Augsten Arudora wasn’t always the bully he ended up being. Early on, he would escape to this room to be on his own and often spent the time fashioning crude woodcarvings of his family members. When his cruelty came to the fore near adulthood, he broke all those toys and stuffed them in the cabinets under this bed, and then forgot completely about them all.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.MwnJ1wN2DU6SGDRa]{Mattress}

A PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} this room and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:35|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers an eye of fortune stuffed into a cleverly hidden tear in the mattress (a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the mattress and knows about the eye patch as a result of achieving 10 Research Points on the topic of Augsten Arudora locates the treasure automatically).

Encounter

Low 13

@UUID[Actor.MwERgzo0507Y2tV6]{Trapped Augsten Soul}

Hazard: See @UUID[.NoCn9mgK3MvOpLEI]{Releasing the Arudoras}.

Alisendra's Tower.name: Alisendra's Tower
Alisendra's Tower.text:
A large vanity table with several drawers and a sturdy chair are this twenty-foot-diameter room’s only furnishings.

Alisendra sometimes used this tower as a place to get some privacy when she wanted to experiment with a new look and didn’t want to risk the humiliation of being seen if even one combination of makeup, wig, and accessory resulted in a fashion disaster.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.q796GBPEAd34yJcc]{Vanity} @UUID[Actor.fFr9oEikUHdWzAMR]{Hidden Compartment}

A minute’s search of the vanity table’s drawers reveals a wide range of grooming supplies but also four panaceas in the lowest drawer.

If the PCs @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the room for 10 minutes and succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:31|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check, they discover a hidden, locked compartment in the wall next to the table. A PC can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} the compartment with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:36|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check, or they can open it with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:33|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}. It opens automatically if the name “Vittorio Vancaskerkin” is spoken aloud in this room, even if the compartment hasn’t been found. Within the compartment, Alisendra kept a keepsake from her Varisian lover: a major trickster’s mandolin.

Encounter

Low 13

@UUID[Actor.RIEGNANwux0GErll]{Trapped Alisendra Soul}

Hazard: See @UUID[.NoCn9mgK3MvOpLEI]{Releasing the Arudoras}.

Raudltz's Tower.name: Raudltz's Tower
Raudltz's Tower.text:
An expensive telescope sits in this room before a tightly shuttered window. A rolled-up bedroll and a few blankets have been arranged nearby.

Raudltz sometimes valued privacy during a long night of stargazing and would come here to do so. It was his own private place to find some quiet within the castle, a place he knew where no one would come to pester him.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.bKaUbVgHMM4bEwev]{Tripod} @UUID[Actor.Ev1DF79riKXOeJl1]{Hidden Telescope Slat}

Standing on a mahogany and brass tripod, the telescope in this room is covered in fine red leather and fitted with gilded rings. The crystal lenses are of the finest clarity. The telescope is an excellently engineered marvel worth 600 gp; it grants a +2 item bonus to any skill check that requires the act of stargazing if the telescope is used. It has 3 Bulk. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} at the telescope and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:33|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check (or who knows where to look as a result of achieving 10 Research Points on Raudltz) discovers a hidden slat on the side of the telescope that, when slid aside, reveals a tiny compartment that contains a scroll of energy aegis, a scroll of retrocognition, a 7th-rank scroll of soothe, and a 7th-rank scroll of dispel magic.

Encounter

Low 13

@UUID[Actor.VrtmdBkBLUHLo0PP]{Trapped Raudltz Soul}

Hazard: See @UUID[.NoCn9mgK3MvOpLEI]{Releasing the Arudoras}.

Irrokcis's Tower.name: Irrokcis's Tower
Irrokcis's Tower.text:
A circular stone tub filled to the lip with ashes sits in the middle of this room. A few closed chests lie near the south wall. The doors to the east look strange—almost like they were formed from the wall’s stone itself.

This tower only formed the doors to the east when the castle became cursed, manifesting this connection to the floating tower (area @UUID[.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{J4}) beyond once the building settled in the Ethereal Plane. Before the seven Arudora souls are exorcised, these “doors” are nothing more than a decorative carving. After all the souls are exorcised, though, the doors open with a touch onto the hanging walkway that crosses the gap over to the floating tower.

If the PCs take too long getting here after they destroy Irrokcis’s body, he might have already re-formed. If so, he’s taken the treasure listed below and started to work on his new plans, which mostly involve avoiding the PCs and waiting to see what they accomplish—if the PCs don’t find and destroy him for good, he’ll escape into Golarion once the curse is lifted.

As long as Irrokcis’s soul remains sheltered in his soul cage, it can’t become trapped in the tower, and thus, no green ribbon of energy initially connects this tower to the floating tower. The lich’s soul must first be set free from the soul cage before the PCs can manifest the floating tower. As soon as the soul cage is destroyed, Irrokcis’s soul becomes trapped here immediately (if his soul was in the soul cage at the time) or as soon as his new body is destroyed, at which point the @UUID[.NoCn9mgK3MvOpLEI]{Trapped Arudora Soul} hazard becomes active.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.2pfk9PZXLnAsOJcB]{Ashes} @UUID[Actor.P91IL7CyXVWziR6Y]{Tower Chest}

The tub of ashes is filled with the cremated remains of countless creatures that Irrokcis has disposed of over the years. Irrokcis hid his soul cage—a tiny coffin-shaped box—deep in the ashes. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in the tub of ashes or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the room for 10 minutes and then succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:31|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check finds the soul cage.

One of the chests to the south contains a few supplies that Irrokcis suspected he’d need should he ever be destroyed and had to re-form a new body: a bag of 500 gp and 30 pp, two scrolls of teleport, a +2 greater striking dagger, a wand of scrying, and a fresh set of clothing.

The other chest contains two skeletons—an adult’s and a baby’s—that are the remains of Irrokcis’s wife and newborn daughter.

Encounter

Low 13

@UUID[Actor.u4bMZDYum96aMKya]{Trapped Irrokcis Soul}

Hazard: See @UUID[.NoCn9mgK3MvOpLEI]{Releasing the Arudoras}.

The Floating Tower.name: The Floating Tower
The Floating Tower.text:
Once the seven Arudora souls have been exorcised and are trapped in the soul vortex, the floating tower and the impossible walkway that connects it to area @UUID[.7rtJA41bt42SO4VG]{J3g} grow solid, giving the PCs a path to the tower. However, the tower’s occupant doesn’t wait idly by for the PCs to come to him on their own terms. Instead, Caydserris emerges from the tower to confront the PCs immediately—proceed with Charg’s Chosen at once. After Caydserris is defeated, the PCs can move on to investigate this final chamber.

The walls of this twenty-foot-diameter room are completely encrusted with writhing red entrails, fingers, mouths, skin, and teeth, giving the impression that hundreds of bodies have been blended together to serve as a horrific, living wallpaper. At the center of the chamber, a pulsing disk of meat and bone in the shape of a distorted, broken wheel slowly rotates in the middle of the room—a deformed multi-eyed red skull leering from its center.

While ending the Bastardhall Curse allows the PCs and Florin to escape and breaks the cycle of Bastardhall’s centennial visits to Ustalav, it doesn’t return the castle to Golarion or wrench it from Charg’s grasp. To do so, the PCs must achieve the secret ending, which requires one final devastating battle that begins here. See @UUID[.iIIzG8EEQwsCV7an]{The Secret Ending} for more details.

Charg's Chosen

Severe 13

@UUID[Actor.aEuFu2OCViPxG08f]{Caydserris Arudora} @UUID[Actor.919AP58ceDMPI5IU]{Anophilexes x2}

When the PCs manifest the floating tower, Caydserris realizes that they’ve accomplished what he assumed would be impossible. The PCs have finally forced him to step away from what’s been occupying his time until this point—the manipulation of Florin’s soul into the final key he needs to return Bastardhall to Golarion. From the start, Florin has fought back, preventing him from accomplishing this goal. The amount of time she can last before he’s finally successful is fluid and should end up being about the same amount of time it takes the PCs to finally reach this point. Frustrated at having his work reach an abrupt end at the last moment, Caydserris brings the fight to the PCs, wherever they might be. If he can defeat them, he’ll have to start his torment of Florin all over from the beginning, but with no one to fight against him this time, it won’t take him very long to finish his work.

Hopefully, it won’t come to that, and the PCs will have at least one last victory left in their future!

Creatures: Caydserris has only dwelled in Bastardhall for 15 years, but in that time, he’s changed dramatically. Before he discovered his hidden Arudora heritage, he was a handsome blonde-haired human man whose prospects were bright. He was serving as one of the prominent professors at the Sinkomakti School, but his discovery doomed him as soon as he sought his legacy by entering the ruins, only to be swept away by the Bastardhall Curse as had so many Arudoras before him.

Yet, Caydserris was a powerful oracle of ancestors and used that power to carve a place for himself in the ruined Bastardhall. In no time, he’d positioned himself as Charg’s voice in the castle, and with his more up-to-date knowledge of the world outside, he was able to guide Velicarn’s ride in 4713 with such efficiency that the bastard gathered more souls than he’d ever collected before on previous rides.

Florin initially escaped that otherwise successful ride, and so when she came to the castle in search of her parents, Caydserris couldn’t believe his luck. Here was the one soul who could speed up Charg’s goal from at least another century to less than a single year. And she came to him, to Bastardhall. However, the arrival of the PCs threw this stroke of fortune into chaos, and now he finally realizes they must die so his—and Charg’s—plans can come to fruition.

When Caydserris confronts the PCs, he does so with a thundering challenge that echoes throughout Bastardhall, as if the storm itself were speaking: “SO BE IT! YOUR SOULS WILL FEED GLORIOUS CHARG BY MY OWN HAND!” This fight can take place across all of Bastardhall, with Caydserris confronting the PCs as soon as they emerge from the building into the open air outside; he starts in the sky some 60 feet above, then points down to the PCs. “There you are! Behold your deliverance! Behold the gifts of Great Charg!”

He rolls Intimidation for initiative and is immediately joined by a pair of anophilex sahkils who manifest in the air to either side of him. Once combat begins, Caydserris is relentless—he and his sahkil companions fight to the death and pursue the PCs nonstop. If the PCs flee into an area of Bastardhall where monsters or hazards still lie in wait, these elements instinctively understand Caydserris to be their lord and follow his commands without hesitation, fighting in unison to destroy the PCs who threaten his plans for power.

In his time in Bastardhall, Caydserris has grown fiendish, transforming into a unique sahkil while retaining only a few vestiges of his human form. Yet the first time he sees the PCs, he wears his original human body as a disguise, his ability to fly without visible wings the only indication that he’s more than he seems.

With one notable exception—Florin Kindler. At the start of the second round of combat, her ghostly form tears herself from Caydserris’s body, causing him great anguish and making him @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for that round. Each round thereafter, starting on the third round, she swirls and loops around him, causing @Damage[4d6[spirit]] damage to Caydserris (@Check[will|dc:38|basic|traits:spirit] save).

Ending the Curse.name: Ending the Curse
Ending the Curse.text:
As soon as Caydserris is defeated, his monstrous body flies apart into fragments that splatter harmlessly but dramatically across a @Template[burst|distance:30]{30-foot radius burst}. At the same moment, Florin’s spirit drifts down to the PCs, floating before them. In a distant, dreamy voice, she apologizes for all the trouble she’s caused the PCs before thanking them for saving her. She explains that she can feel her body calling to her and drifts upward through the air to the floating tower (area @UUID[.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{J4})—she’ll slow her journey to stay abreast of the PCs if they want to accompany her. Upon reaching area @UUID[.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{J4}, her soul and body merge, and the PCs’ employer is restored, alive but traumatized by the event.

Florin is eager to return to Golarion, but her time spent as Caydserris’s prisoner has given her deep insights into the nature of the Bastardhall Curse as well as the legacies of the Arudoras themselves. She can fill in the PCs on any bits of information they haven’t yet uncovered during their research, provided the PCs ask the right questions; use Florin to clear up any lingering mysteries and unanswered questions the PCs might have.

When the PCs are ready, Florin reveals to them the most important piece of information: how to bring about the end of the Bastardhall Curse. She warns the PCs that she can sense Charg’s interest in the castle, and that until the curse ends, he’ll be able to resurrect and repopulate the castle’s inhabitants in a hundred years to continue the cursed cycle—more importantly, ending the curse will allow the PCs and Florin to simply walk back to Golarion across the Laroba Causeway.

To end the curse, Florin explains that the PCs must travel down to the soul vortex (area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.EPAmP1TdzmePRO9b]{I}), where all of the other Arudora souls are now trapped. Once there (and once any remaining sahkil guardians are defeated), they have two options available.

Consecrate the Soul Vortex: The more dangerous option, Florin explains, is to cast a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Dbd5W6G8U2vzWolN]{Consecrate} ritual in the chamber of the soul vortex to any deity other than Charg. Doing so causes the soul vortex to collapse, freeing all of the souls trapped within to make their final journey to the Boneyard and their individual afterlives. Unfortunately, Florin doesn’t know this ritual—it’s possible, she muses, that a copy might be found somewhere in the ruins of the castle’s cathedral for the PCs to learn (she’s correct, but the ritual is found below the cathedral, in the inner sanctum at area @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.xusIZ6ZnpPAUUJTS]{G8}). Even if the PCs learn and cast consecrate, this method is dangerous. The ritual must be heightened to 7th rank, and it’s a DC 37 check for the primary caster and DC 32 for the secondary casters. (Fortunately, for this version of casting consecrate, the secondary casters need not share the same religion as the primary caster—all that’s required is a shared desire to end the Bastardhall Curse). Each time the attempt to cast consecrate on the soul vortex fails, backlash from the soul vortex deals @Damage[15d6[mental]] damage to all casters (@Check[will|dc:32|basic|traits:mental] save). On a critical failure, the PCs must wait a year before trying again (during which time, at your discretion, some of the previously defeated Arudoras might begin to return to life as Charg slowly brings things back to his “normal”).

Sacrifice a Whispering Remnant: Florin notes there’s another option, though. Remnants of Charg, she explains, have grown in hidden places of the castle. If the PCs can gather up all of these @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JmlPFAbjPvbhhKeu]{vile remnants}, then combine them into one powerful @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.14kIZ6GRkAW8vZw8]{whispering remnant}, all they need to do to end the curse is to return the whispering remnant to Charg—simply by throwing it into the @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.EPAmP1TdzmePRO9b]{soul vortex}. No skill check or ritual is needed for this simpler solution, but if the PCs haven’t found all eight vile remnants, they’ll likely need to scour the castle a bit to find the ones they missed (and deal with any dangers still lurking in those areas of the castle).

The Secret Ending.name: The Secret Ending
The Secret Ending.text:
If the PCs return all of the missing artwork to the Arudora Gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}) and repair the clock tower by returning its missing gears, one additional option to end the curse is available. With the restoration of both Pharasma’s and Shelyn’s most significant influences, and the PCs carrying in them the gratitude of both deities, Florin has a revelation when she manifests. Rather than simply sanctifying the soul vortex, the PCs could draw upon the fact that they’re now favored by two deities whom Charg wronged to force him to manifest a portion of his being directly in Bastardhall. She suspects that while this course of action would result in a very deadly fight, it’d be one that, while extremely challenging, the PCs should have a chance to win—and if Charg’s manifestation could be defeated, that would end the curse so completely that Charg himself would be forced to turn away from the site!

If the PCs opt for this option, tell them (through Florin) that this final battle will be the most dangerous challenge they’ve faced yet, but beyond knowing it’ll be a difficult, she has no idea what form Charg’s manifestation will take. They can still use one of the previous options to end the curse if they wish.

If they choose this final secret ending, though, Florin explains that they must simply call out a challenge to Charg while gathered at the point where they delivered the death blow to Caydserris. No idle boast will do. All of the PCs must, together, spend 3 actions in the same round to call out Charg—these actions have the concentrate trait.

Ambience

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

As the encounter with the despair dragon begins, be sure to play some of the provided sounds for Zaurgaulus in the Creatures soundboard!

Encounter

Severe 13

@UUID[Actor.e22OfdurIIrOUdx3]{Zaurgaulus}

Creatures: Once the PCs issue this challenge in area @UUID[.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{J4}, the storm that’s been hammering the castle comes to a sudden stop. The ground outside remains soaking wet and the night sky above overcast, but for a moment, silence reigns. Suddenly, Caydserris rises up from the spot he was slain, but his body grows bloated and distorted. This strange remnant scowls and leers silently at the PCs until someone Strikes it; at this point, the rest of the picture becomes clear as an enormous, horrific dragon manifests before the PCs. The distorted version of Caydserris was nothing more than a bulging tumor at the tip of the dragon’s tongue.

This entity is Zaurgaulus, Charg’s manifestation in the form of a despair dragon. If the PCs Struck at the Tongue Decoy of Caydserris, the manifestation uses Perception to roll for initiative, but if a round passes before then, the manifestation reveals itself and rolls for initiative using Deception. If this manifestation takes place indoors, the dragon manifests in the closest area able to house its Huge size, having extended its tongue as far as needed. This can give the PCs a significant advantage at the start of the battle, but if they don’t engage with the dragon soon, it vents its frustration on Maiserene. Once it confronts the PCs, the manifestation of Charg fights to the death.

Returning Home.name: Returning Home
Returning Home.text:
Once the PCs end the curse, things immediately change. The chamber of the soul vortex transforms into an empty, unassuming cavern, and the PCs can make their way back upstairs to the castle above with ease. As they travel, they find that the castle has become completely uninhabited, and all haunts and other supernatural effects they examine along the way have reverted to mundane features. Upon exiting the castle, they find the storm has ended without a trace, but now, above the castle is a swirling green expanse with no hint of the sky or any astronomical bodies—the curse is over, but Bastardhall continues to drift on the Ethereal Plane.

Should they travel to Maiserene, they find the village in a similar condition to the castle, but any phantom they’ve rescued and restored to a physical body remains—now fully alive once more. These six survivors are nervous, frightened, and wary. They look to the PCs for guidance as to what to do next. It shouldn’t take much to convince them to return with the PCs to Golarion.

Bastardhall, at this point, remains on the Ethereal Plane, but the Laroba Causeway (area @UUID[.vLK5DU1IqUQjOhmx]{J1}) now appears to reach all the way to a visible shore on the far side of the lake. As Florin explains, all they need to do to return to Golarion is to walk across this bridge. When they set foot on the far shore, they’ll be back home in Ustalav. Behind them, the ruins of Bastardhall will, finally, brood in peace—unless the PCs finished the secret ending, in which case the castle returns in its full glory as it was the day before the curse stole it away.

Reward

Grant the PCs 120 XP for rescuing Florin Kindler and ending the Bastardhall Curse.

Releasing the Arudoras.name: Releasing the Arudoras
Releasing the Arudoras.text:
Encounter

Low 13

Hazard: Each of the topmost rooms in the seven Arudora towers has become a shelter and cage for that Arudora’s soul, which causes their spiritual links to the floating tower and Bastardhall’s curse to become visible as ribbons of light connecting those seven towers to area @UUID[.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{J4}. The PCs can’t interact directly with these ribbons of light or the floating tower, but they can unbind each of the Arudora souls and send them hurling down into the soul vortex below the castle. To accomplish this, they must enter a tower’s highest room and disable or destroy the haunt that manifests as a result of the occupying Arudora soul.

Each of these seven haunts have similar stats, but have unique effects representing each Arudora. While each can be disabled with enough successful Religion checks to break the curse’s hold on the trapped soul, the PCs can also use what they’ve learned about the individual Arudoras to defeat the hazard.

Chapter Summaries.name: Chapter Summaries
Chapter Summaries.text:
The PCs begin this adventure at 5th level.

@UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH]{The Haunted Shore}

Level 5

Chapter 1

After being recruited by Florin Kindler to help her unravel the mystery of her missing parents, the PCs awaken on the shores of Lake Laroba as Bastardhall looms above them. Outside the castle walls, the PCs explore the ruined village of Maiserene and rescue six imprisoned phantoms who will help support them in their endeavors.

The PCs should be 6th level by the time they unlock the castle grounds.

@UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL]{Castle Grounds}

Level 6

Chapter 2

Once inside the walls, the PCs explore Bastardhall’s courtyard and outbuildings, and defeat the dullahan Jinnivere Arudora in order to unlock the castle’s cellars and interior.

The PCs should be 7th level by the time they unlock the cellars.

@UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw]{The Cellars}

Level 7

Chapter 3

The PCs can then enter the castle itself, navigate its servant quarters and guard posts, and confront the ogre Augsten Arudora, allowing them access to the castle’s reception halls.

The PCs should be 8th level by the time they unlock the reception halls.

@UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi]{The Reception Halls}

Level 8

Chapter 4

Continuing their progression through Bastardhall, the PCs move up into the ground floor of the main structure and disrupt several haunted galas to draw out the blood hag Alisendra Arudora.

The PCs should be 9th level by the time they unlock Bastardhall dungeon.

@UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ]{The Dungeon}

Level 9

Chapter 5

After disrupting her dance, the PCs descend into Bastardhall’s dungeon and battle the sadistic werewolf Dazerien Arudora in order to unlock the castle’s private halls above.

The PCs should be 10th level by the time they unlock the private halls.

@UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8]{The Private Halls}

Level 10

Chapter 6

In Bastardhall’s upper floors, the PCs confront a family of vampires led by the previous lord of Bastardhall, Raudltz Arudora. Here, like in other parts of the castle, the PCs are able to piece together more of the mystery of Bastardhall’s curse and hone in on the way to break it.

The PCs should be 11th level by the time they unlock the fallen temple.

@UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk]{The Fallen Temple}

Level 11

Chapter 7

After completing the private halls, the PCs move on to the castle’s former temple. The castle temple has fallen, literally and spiritually. In this unholy site the PCs do battle with an undead child of Urgathoa: Ryhasphinea Arudora.

The PCs should be 12th level by the time they unlock Bastardhall’s vaults.

@UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X]{The Vault}

Level 12

Chapter 8

Defeating the blasphemous undead, the PCs are able to unlock Bastardhall’s vault. They must traverse even deeper into the dungeon than their previous incursion to find and defeat the lich, Irrokcis Arudora. After defeating him, Bastardhall’s towers phase into existence.

The PCs should be 13th level once they unlock the towers.

@UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le]{The Towers}

Level 13

Chapter 9

With the castle towers now manifested, the PCs can finally confront the current ruler of Bastardhall: an oracle of Charg named Caydserris Arudora. The PCs explore each tower top, homes to the most powerful of the Arudora souls trapped in the location before clashing with the fiendish Caydserris. After his defeat, if the PCs completed everything there is to do in Bastardhall, they can unlock an additional secret ending.

The PCs should reach 14th level by the end of the campaign.

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
Welcome to Bastion of Blasphemies on Foundry Virtual Tabletop! In this module you will find everything you need to run your players through an epic and terrifying adventure, as their characters find themselves trapped by the infamous curse of Bastardhall, confined to a haunted castle and its surrounding shore, all carefully mapped and implemented into a single scene by our team.

Will your players be able to break the curse of Bastardhall and escape, or are they fated to become the latest in a long line of vanishings into one of Golarion’s most infamous ruins?

Preparing for your Game

Bastion of Blasphemies is an adventure with several moving parts, between the tremendous map of Bastardhall and its surrounding area, the complicated history of the Arudora family, the mystery of the curse that befell them, and much more, preparing to run this adventure may seem intimidating. Here we suggest a few ways you can start.

To get a general overview of this Adventure Path, both from a story and gameplay perspective, head to the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.0OAqbVHajiYOU8GD]{Campaign Overview} category of the Adventure Toolbox journal. There you will find the history of Bastardhall and its curse, advice on running this adventure, a handy campaign timeline, and list of key names.

As for your players, we encourage you to point them to the @UUID[JournalEntry.oIog1W3hftKUYySh]{Player's Guide} journal on their right sidebar to help their character creation, as well as reviewing and discussing this adventure's @UUID[.#content-warning]{Content Warning}.

For technical advice on how to use this module, head over to the @UUID[.GedyPT9i5BeXOcis]{Using this Module} category of this journal, which will outline some of the ways we present information for you, as well as explain some of the tools we provide.

If you want to delve deeper both lore and mechanical information, the Adventure Toolbox mentioned earlier contains several more categories you may find yourself visiting often, including:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n]{The Bastardhall Curse}, as the characters perform Research at various points to uncover the origins and secrets of the curse keeping them trapped.

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.0LOtv52aD44VMt6N]{Maiserene Phantoms}, where you will find the stories, campaign roles, and side quests, of each of the phantom inhabitants of Maiserene, the village outside the walls of Bastardhall.

  • The Items category, specifically the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.kKMa229quJDLEUfk]{Special Bastardhall Items} and @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.9LhH5rguGP8PqSTd]{Keys}, where the locations of important items for the adventure are laid out for your convenience.

Once you feel ready to begin with the first chapter, you can visit the @UUID[.wZyl3gj4oz8l0Ebv]{Chapter Summaries} page to get an idea of each chapter's story, as well as their level milestones, or you may head over to @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH]{Chapter 1} directly.

Content Warning

This adventure includes themes some readers might find troubling, including body horror, confinement, dismemberment, family violence, gore, spiders, and torture, as well as certain encounters that may be evocative of experiences with disordered eating. Additionally, recurring nightmares meant to represent common fears (of open water, open spaces, crowds, and fire, among others) are present throughout. Before beginning this campaign, understand that player consent (including that of the Game Master) is vital to a safe and fun play experience for everyone. You should talk with your players before beginning the adventure and modify descriptions of the narrative as appropriate.

Foundry Credits.name: Foundry Credits
Foundry Credits.text:
The Bastion of Blasphemies module for Foundry Virtual Tabletop was created and produced by a task force of Foundry Virtual Tabletop staff and contractors hand-selected from the Pathfinder community.

Cartography

We'd like to thank our well-known community cartographers, Andrew "narchy" Gordon and Kobold DM, for taking on the arduous and meticulous task of recreating the map of Bastardhall, in all its epic scale, all while maintaining the quality and attention to detail both of them are known for.

This module would not have been possible without not only their artistic skills, but also their communication and patience during development.

Software Development

We'd also like to give Eberhard Höpfner and Ludovic Dey their well-deserved accolades, for the essential task of making the massive Arudora Isle scene performant for as many gamemasters and players as possible. We're additionally thankful for Eberhard Höpfner's work in meticulously setting up the scene's walls and regions, and Ludovic Dey's implementation of the stunning dynamic weather system and water special effects.

Our gratitude goes to Richard Simões, not only for his work as one of the development leads for Pathfinder 2e on Foundry, but also for the implementation of the campaign manager, allowing GMs to keep track of all the moving parts of this adventure, such as unlocking areas, weather controls, sunrise and sunset times, research progress, and more!

Content Development

Our appreciation extends to Rodrigo Calfín for his content development work—including the creation and system implementation of journal entries, items, loot actors, and scene setup—as well as his work on custom styling, co-developed with Richard Simões.

A massive thanks to Shane Martland, for curating and mixing the immersive ambience and sound effects that will accompany your adventures in Bastardhall, and Andrew Clayton for his work on quality assurance and the production of the trailer for this module!

Token Artwork

We'd like to thank Ian Hildebrandt, for creating the tokens your party will be both delighted and terrified to face over the course of this adventure, as well as making them compatible with our Pathfinder Tokens: Character Gallery module.

Furthermore, credit goes to Rodrigo Calfín for the design and implementation of this module's custom dynamic token ring.

PF2E Development Team

The Foundry Virtual Tabletop team would like to express its profound and heartfelt thanks to the development team of the PF2e game system. Their efforts to adapt Pathfinder Second Edition for virtual tabletop play have provided countless fans a place to play and experience Pathfinder at a level of quality unmatched anywhere else. Their adamant refusal to accept payment for their work on the system is a bold statement about the generosity of the Pathfinder community, and we look forward to working together with them for a long time to come.

Foundry Advice.name: Foundry Advice
Foundry Advice.text:
If you ever see a box like the one below, that means we have advice about how to best make use of the module and its content, as it relates to FoundryVTT. The header might include links to effects, ambience sounds, macros, and so on. The following are some of the more common boxes you will encounter.

Effects

@UUID[Item.lELfJ59AJTvZ6i7H]{Example Effect}

An effect represents an often temporary change in an actor, such as a bonus, a penalty, or even more complex benefits, like temporary Hit Points.

When an effect is linked in this box, you can use it by either dragging it onto your players' tokens or sheets yourself, or dragging and dropping it onto the chat box and posting it, allowing your players to apply it to their own characters in the same way.

Ambience Tracks

@UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.ONTeDjH5dol5Cnoz]{Example Ambience}

We have provided ambience sounds for you to play during your adventures. Some of them have been set up to automatically play as the scene is activated, but others benefit from being timed as the characters enter a certain area. When that happens, the box will include a link to the ambience sound in its header. You can simply click on the link to start playing the sound!

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

Sometimes, especially as the characters run into traps or otherwise affect their surroundings, we will point you to the @UUID[.7Yig4E2mbPqpQKNt]{campaign manager}, which contains helpful toggles to automate things like tiles being hidden and revealed, sounds being played, and other effects that will enhance your players' immersion.

Learn more about the campaign manager in the @UUID[.7Yig4E2mbPqpQKNt]{next page}!

Changelog and Bug Reports

If you find a bug with this module, please check out our premium content issue tracker and make sure the issue is not already reported. If it isn't, feel free to open an issue to report it so that we may fix it as soon as possible!

Likewise, if you want check out our changelogs for this module, you can do so through here.

Encounters.name: Encounters
Encounters.text:
When reading area descriptions, you will often come across creatures which the players may end up fighting, or hazards that will need to be disabled or otherwise dealt with. In those places, encounter sections such as these will contain all of the information you'll need to run the encounter.

Of course, not every encounter has to end in combat. Many are optional, or provide the heroes with an opportunity for diplomacy. Just because it's in one of these sections, it doesn't mean that a creature couldn't be reasoned with, or even eventually become an ally!

The actors involved in each encounter will be linked in the encounter description for quick access, and their tokens are already placed for you on each scene. The header will also tell you the encounter's threat category per Pathfinder's encounter design guidelines.

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.F0t6Eogd0KJdboXq]{Bastardhall Rat} @UUID[Actor.JNU54O7l5O6lWPNJ]{Cursed Mural}

This text will often include a information relevant to the encounter as a whole, such as skill checks to possibly avoid combat, or just further context for you as the GM. As shown in this example, you might also see the portrait of one of the encounter participants.

Creature: This section will describe the creatures involved, as well as their tactics or priorities, if any.

Hazard: If there are any hazards in the encounter, they will typically be described in this section.

Of course, you will not have the full picture of the encounter without inspecting the participants' character sheets first, so please make use of the links in the header of each encounter!

Treasure.name: Treasure
Treasure.text:
As the heroes go on their adventures, they may well unearth valuable treasures, coins, or powerful magical items. When that happens, you will see a box like the ones below.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.JIDpUhUHdkYe9Clo]{Example Loot}

The header of this box will typically link to a loot actor, a special type of actor that holds items for you to hand out to your players. These actors also have tokens which are placed on the associated scene, hidden by default.

Giving these items to your players is as simple as revealing the loot actor's token placed on the scene by right-clicking it and selecting the "Toggle Visibility State" option. They will be able to open the loot actor's sheet and take items directly from it by dragging them into their inventories.

Additionally, the description of these loot actors contains GM-only text linking to the journal page where the PCs will come across that treasure.

Rewards & Milestones.name: Rewards & Milestones
Rewards & Milestones.text:
The heroes might obtain rewards other than treasure for their accomplishments, or their actions could result in certain developments. In those cases, you will see a box like the one below.

Experience Points

While most encounters in Bastion of Blasphemies have their @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.ZcddTU02joqYuuoV]{XP Awards} determined by the encounter's threat category, the players might obtain XP for non-combat accomplishments.

Development

As mentioned earlier, this box is also used for developments, such as an area that becomes unlocked when the PCs overcome an encounter, or an event they might witness if they perform certain actions.

Research.name: Research
Research.text:
The Research subsystem is used extensively throughout Bastion of Blasphemies, as such, we recommend you familiarize yourself with its @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.zkQJzslkiNQuUuKd]{rules}. Whenever an opportunity for the PCs to Research appears (known as a "Library"), you will see a box much like the one below.

The header of this box will typically link to the research topic (or topics) that the PCs can make progress towards. This link will take you to that research topic's statblock, which contains its thresholds and other relevant information.

In special cases, there may be too many topics to list, or the topics may be left for you to decide. If so, we may omit the aforementioned links, or include them within the body of the text instead.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.ICuUq6iK6NdzE7Fp]{Example Research Topic}

Library: A library is the source of information the PCs may draw from. Despite its name, it can be anything from an actual library to an abandoned journal, or even an NPC or particular event. The body of this text will describe the nature of the library to you, and may include useful links.

Maximum RP This section will tell you how many Research Points (RP) the PCs can obtain from this library, typically broken down by research topic if there are multiple ones.

Research Checks Lastly, here is where you will find the types of checks the PCs can attempt depending on their specific research task. In most cases, an inline check will be provided for you, allowing you to click on the speech bubble to post the relevant check to the chat for your PCs to attempt, (@Check[society|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration], for example). At times, the particular type of check may be purposefully ambiguous, in which case, a premade button won't be provided.

Campaign Manager.name: Campaign Manager
Campaign Manager.text:
There are many things to keep track of in Bastion of Blasphemies, such as the effects of a growing storm, boons unlocked by the PCs as they explore, and long-lasting changes to the nature of the castle. You can use the Campaign Manager to keep track of these developments.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

To bring up the campaign manager, you can run this macro, or head over to the Actors tab of the right sidebar and click on the castle icon to the right of your party's name!

The campaign manager contains different tabs corresponding to some of the moving parts in this campaign.

Areas

As you will soon learn, the PCs will not have access to the entirety of Bastardhall from the start. As a result, you will find several entrances locked and windows obscured, preventing the players from seeing past or entering them. As they rescue lost souls and defeat each of the cursed Arudoras, these areas will gradually become available.

The Areas tab will help you keep track of the requirements the PCs need to complete to progress to the next area. When those requirements are met, the aforementioned entrances will automatically become useable, unlocking their respective doors, allowing sight past their windows, and enabling scene regions for traveling between levels! Even the weather will shift as a result of these events, which you'll be able to track of, and tweak, in the @UUID[.#environment]{Environment} tab.

Most commonly, the requirement will involve your PCs drag-and-dropping one of the Arudora mementos into the @UUID[Actor.cHogqC3igqd7t1hM]{Arudora Fountain} loot actor, but you will also have the ability to bypass these requirements, if you ever want to test things out or simply want to explore the castle unimpeded.

Environment

The incoming storm is an essential marker of the PCs progress, strengthening and warping as they come closer and closer to confronting the lord of the castle and the true origin of the Bastardhall curse. In this tab, you will be able to tweak the weather effects, and overriding it with your preferred settings.

Likewise, you will notice that days become shorter and shorter, until the entire island is swallowed in eternal nightfall by the climax. As such, you will be able to keep track of the current time and reference how the day-night cycle changes.

Research

As the current victims of this long-standing curse, your PCs will take it upon themselves to researching it. This uses Pathfinder's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.zkQJzslkiNQuUuKd]{Research} rules.

There are an astounding eighteen different research topics, so we encourage you to make use of the Research tab. For each of these topics, you will be able to keep track of whether that topic has been discovered, their number of Research Points, access the Adventure Toolbox page for that topic, and even send the information the PCs should know so far to chat!

Collectibles

While there are vast amounts of treasure to be found within Bastardhall, some items belong in a special category for their importance to progressing through the campaign and unlocking the @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.iIIzG8EEQwsCV7an]{Secret Ending}.

These special items are @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.uT2rZ6sr9wmX1Bc2]{Soulhearts}, @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.iQLEbANowf4fT8hK]{Vile Remnants}, @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.kKMa229quJDLEUfk#gear-locations]{Missing Gears}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.kKMa229quJDLEUfk#lost-artwork-locations]{Lost Artwork}. In this tab you can keep track of the locations for each of these items, and which ones have been found (or in the case of soulhearts, used as well!)

Back to Golarion.name: Back to Golarion
Back to Golarion.text: Once the PCs make it back to Golarion, they’ll have quite the story to tell and will have made a lifelong friend in Florin Kindler. Most of Ustalav never realizes how close they came to devastation, with most who learn the story discounting it as tall tales. It’ll be nearly a hundred years, when Bastardhall fails to return, before the truth of the PCs’ triumph will be impossible to ignore, but by that point, most of the world will have moved on. If the PCs manage to achieve the secret ending, though, their fame spreads far more quickly, and they may even be granted control over the sprawling castle by the Varno county government as a reward for their amazing achievement. Regardless of the ending they obtain, your players have attained an incredible victory in escaping from one of Golarion’s most notorious haunted castles!

Researching the Curse.name: Researching the Curse
Researching the Curse.text:
The curse that afflicts Bastardhall and its occupants has kept the estate trapped in the Ethereal Plane for over 500 years. While the castle and its occupants have remained relatively static over those centuries, compelled to do little more than play out roles in mockery of their previous lives, there is much about the place—both pre-curse and post-curse—that the PCs can learn. By researching Bastardhall, the Arudoras, and the curse itself, they can eventually learn many secrets and fragments of lost lore about one of Ustalav’s most enduring and legendary locales. This information can also guide the PCs’ explorations through Bastardhall and help them navigate some of the castle’s more intricate and devious mysteries. Similarly, it can grant them critical knowledge of how to prevail against the castle’s curse, its monstrous guardians, and its numerous other dangers.

These investigations use the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.zkQJzslkiNQuUuKd]{Research} rules. Make sure you and your players are familiar with them before starting Bastion of Blasphemies, so that when research opportunities come up during play, your players can explore the options before them efficiently. To learn more about a topic, a PC must be located at a specific research site or have in their possession an item or document that can be studied. The PC may then attempt a Research check (using the skill check of their choice as afforded by the location or document) by spending 2 hours to study and investigate. Once all possible Research Points (RP) have been earned from a location or document, inform the players so they can move on to new venues, but note that for locations or documents that allow PCs to research multiple topics, each topic has a separate pool of Research Points to be potentially earned. Obviously, a PC must know the name of the topic and that it exists at all before they can attempt to conduct their research!

Note that once the PCs have access to the soul vortex (area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.EPAmP1TdzmePRO9b]{I}), they can use it to research any of the following topics. Also, while each of these subjects is assigned a level, research check DCs are set by the individual locations and resources.

Research

Any Research Topic

Recalling Knowledge: Each of the topics in this category includes the option to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} as a research check—a PC can attempt to research a topic using the skills listed here anywhere in Bastardhall simply by taking an action to do so (provided they know about the topic they are researching in the first place).

Note that while any PC can attempt this, the Maximum RP that can be earned by Recall Knowledge doesn’t reset for each new PC who attempts this method of research. Make sure to remind the PCs when they discover other topics that they can use this to learn a bit more!

Maximum RP 2 per topic; Research Checks @Check[occultism|dc:20|name:Research|options:action:research,action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] to recall legends about the topic or @Check[society|dc:20|name:Research|options:action:research,action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] to recall historical facts about the topic.

Florin's Fate.name: Florin's Fate
Florin's Fate.text:
Florin doesn’t remember much about her time spent in Bastardhall, recalling her traumatic imprisonment there in the way one half-remembers a harrowing dream. None of this changes the fact that for Florin, there remain unanswered questions. She initially traveled to Bastardhall to discover what happened to her parents; depending on how much they researched the Bastardhall Curse and the Arudoras, the PCs can likely fill her in and share the truth with her. Her parents’ souls were among the many caught in the soul vortex. If the PCs didn’t achieve the secret ending, then the soul vortex remains in Bastardhall, and Florin asks the PCs to free all those trapped souls. Returning to Bastardhall to finish things off should require the use of planar travel, though, since Florin isn’t eager to be a sacrifice to force the way open again!

Once the curse is fully removed and the soul vortex destroyed, Florin can rest easy knowing her parents’ souls are free to move on to the afterlife—unless, of course, you want to expand this plot point by having Charg or some of his agents snatch those two away in a bitter, last-minute grasp at revenge! This would force the PCs to seek out a rescue all the way in the realm of Xibalba, where Charg and the other sahkil tormentors rule.

Restoring Castle Arudora.name: Restoring Castle Arudora
Restoring Castle Arudora.text:
Once the PCs achieve the secret ending and end the curse, they aren’t the only ones who return to Golarion. All of Bastardhall does as well, replacing the ruins that have loomed on Arudora Isle for the past 500 years with the castle as it appears in this Adventure Path. As it is no longer a part of the Ethereal Plane, the natives of that realm now find they are the ones who are trapped. Whether the PCs hire lower-level adventurers to clear out the monsters and haunts that remain or see to the task themselves, the government of Varno swiftly learns of this unprecedented event.

How much or how little bureaucratic interference the PCs encounter is left up to you to determine. Varno’s leaders might quickly understand the role the PCs played and grant them the lands and title to the castle as a reward, or they might grant it to Florin Kindler, the Arudora estate’s last true living heir. Otherwise, they might try to reclaim ownership for themselves, setting up a potential new adventure filled with political intrigue if the PCs want to retain the castle for their own.

At the same time, some of those whom the PCs rescued in the Adventure Path, such as the six leaders of Maiserene or any of the souls rescued from Raudltz’s children in the private halls, now find themselves suddenly alive again, but in a world more than 500 years older than the one they left. These rescued souls may wish to remain in the area or want to find somewhere else to go. How the PCs handle these returnees could potentially lead them into new adventures as they help these refugees from Bastardhall track down their old families and homes, some of which may well be under the rule of other sinister forces!

Charg's Vengeance.name: Charg's Vengeance
Charg's Vengeance.text:
The sahkil tormentors, Charg included, are more prone to traverse the Universe and directly meddle with or influence the lives of mortals. This desire, after all, is what led Charg to set into motion the complex string of events that resulted in the Bastardhall Curse, starting with his patronage of Irrokcis Arudora; had the PCs not stopped him, Bastardhall’s return to Golarion would look much different (see Worst Case Scenario below).

If the PCs escape, Charg might send sahkils or encourage his faithful to seek them out for revenge, possibly even looking to capture and haul them back through the Ethereal Plane to Charg’s domain in Xibalba. This thirst for vengeance only increases if the PCs defeated his despair dragon proxy and ended the curse. In this case, Charg’s cult is likely compelled to torment the PCs, perhaps abducting their allies or undermining their works, all to lure them to a dangerous location on Golarion where they’ll face even more dangerous sahkils, haunts, and monsters. In the end, the PCs might find that the only way to truly free themselves from Charg’s attention is to travel to his domain in Xibalba and confront him directly. Of course, this plot would likely work best for fully mythic heroes or otherwise require a significant amount of preparation by undermining Charg’s power and gathering potent artifacts to use against him.

Worst Case Scenario.name: Worst Case Scenario
Worst Case Scenario.text:
If the PCs simply escape Bastardhall without ending the curse, the castle remains adrift in the Ethereal Plane. As long as the Arudora line persists outside of Bastardhall, though, Charg can’t move on with his plans to use the location as a foothold on Golarion—at least, not for another century or so, when the curse resets, the denizens the PCs defeated are reborn, and the Black Coach rides again to seek out Florin’s descendants.

If the Arudora line dies out before then, though, things escalate. While Charg can’t directly interfere, and though nothing associated with Bastardhall can emerge from the realm before the next centennial, other cultists of Charg could learn about this, seek out Florin, and attempt to kill her. If they succeed and end the line, then it’s only a matter of years before the Bastardhall Curse is able to restore Caydserris and any others, and they can complete the rites they need.

Of course, if the PCs fail to escape and become Bastardhall’s latest victims, then this all happens more quickly. Florin’s soul is absorbed and corrupted mere days after the campaign ends for the PCs, at which point Bastardhall returns to Golarion—but this time, with its monstrous and haunted occupants fully restored. The curse spreads swiftly through the lands, and if Ryhasphinea still exists, her soulphage spreads as well. Ustalav falls to Charg’s cult swiftly, as do many of the western River Kingdoms. How far this new curse spreads, with Bastardhall as its increasingly potent source, depends on whether a future group of heroes can stop what the current ones could not!

The Arudoras.name: The Arudoras
The Arudoras.text:
The Arudoras

Research 6

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.oQOmNJ7YInR10ecC#research]{Maiserene church records} (area A9c), @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.zV2odqRawrPRFwP1#research]{what the servants know} (Chapter 3), @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mp2jSvvSVejhua2M#research]{speak to the spirits} (area D30f)

1 Research Point The Arudoras were an influential noble family who dwelt in a castle in eastern Varno. They and their estate vanished one awful night just over 500 years ago, and ever since, their family castle has been known as Bastardhall. The Arudora family crest is a serpentine creature with a long neck, a long tail, and four flippers curled around a sword in front of a stylized image of the castle.

2 Research Points The Arudora family line persisted after the castle vanished, but none of the surviving family members have ever sought to claim the land. The government of Varno attempted to bestow the castle to other noble families several times, but each attempt ended in tragedy. As of 4237, no further attempt to officially reclaim Bastardhall has been made.

4 Research Points No known Arudoras live today, but it’s possible some who don’t know their name or legacy still live on. The last known Arudora of significance was a strange and mysterious man by the name of Caydserris, who some say learned of his unknown heritage via a strange vision. When he sought answers, alone, at the ruins in 4711, he vanished without a trace.

6 Research Points At the time the curse took hold, there were six Arudoras living in the castle. Raudltz and Alisendra were the castle’s lord and lady, and their children were Jinnivere and Augsten. Raudltz’s sister, Ryhasphinea, had recently returned to live there as well, along with her son, Dazerien. Rumors held that Raudltz had at least one illegitimate child, but even if true, no records of such children exist today. Three previous generations of Arudoras lived in the castle prior to Raudltz’s rule: his parents, Demiterus and Neesha; his grandparents, Irrokcis and Zasha; and his great-grandparents, Eragayl and Tasifinie, who oversaw the family castle’s construction in 4118.

8 Research Points Though each Arudora was their own person, all family members shared certain quirks and mannerisms. The PCs now understand these quirks and gain a +2 circumstance bonus on all checks made to research individual Arudoras as a resul, as well as to checks made to Recall Knowledge about the creatures they have become (though, of course, they can’t attempt such checks until after they first encounter an Arudora in their new form).

10 Research Points The Arudora line is cursed because one of them, the eponymous bastard of Bastardhall (a man named Velicarn), called upon his fiendish patron, Charg, to punish the family for casting him out. In truth, Charg’s interest in the Arudoras likely began years before this final event, and it was through this bastard’s anger that the sahkil tormentor found a vector through which he could bring about the curse.

Boon

@UUID[Item.ngjn7OOaDbQtRjvS]{Arudora Familiarity}

As the party reaches this 8 Research Points, you can apply this boon to grant them a bonus to their relevant Research or Recall Knowledge checks, toggleable via the roll preview dialog.

Bastardhall.name: Bastardhall
Bastardhall.text:
Bastardhall was a sprawling castle located on an island in Lake Laroba in eastern Ustalav, not far from the West Sellen River (the main river trade route up from Taldor that links to northern Ustalav, western Numeria, Sarkoris, and western Mendev). Known historically as Castle Arudora, after the influential Arudora family who dwelt within, Bastardhall today is a notorious haunted ruin that features in numerous tales of terror throughout the Inner Sea region.

Bastardhall’s curse began with the return of a bitter, vengeful man named Velicarn in 4213 AR. When he came to Castle Arudora, he bore with him a bundle wrapped in old swaddling cloth. Velicarn’s eerie resemblance to Eragayl Arudora (the man who, many years before, built the castle and whose face appeared on many paintings and statues within) was enough to convince a scullery maid named Lavinia Bavah to escort him to the castle’s main library (after he paid for the service with a platinum coin). Once at the library, Velicarn confronted Raudltz Arudora, and revealed who he was—Velicarn Arudora, an unwanted, illegitimate son whom Raudltz had abandoned and left for dead. Velicarn proclaimed that if he was to be denied the Arudora name (and the significant inheritance and status that came with it), then none should prosper from it. He made clear he intended to corrupt the souls of all those who bore Arudora blood and make them monstrous affronts to humanity. Then he revealed the contents of the swaddled bundle: a horrific blob of monstrous flesh known as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.14kIZ6GRkAW8vZw8]{whispering remnant} from his sahkil patron Charg, demigod of monsters and catastrophic declines.

Aghast, Raudltz drew his blade and beheaded his bastard, yet this didn’t save him or his family line. The whispering remnant came to life and spread Charg’s influence through the castle, consuming Velicarn’s head and animating his body as an undead horror. As the sahkil tormentor’s curse spread, Raudltz deployed seven messengers from the castle to warn his distant kin of the danger, but these seven would be the last living souls to leave Castle Arudora that night. Those trapped within either fell to the curse and became monsters, or they became prey to be hunted and slain. As the curse spread, Velicarn rode forth on a black coach and chased down the seven messengers, slaying them before any could deliver their warnings. The inhabitants of the small village of Maiserene were swept up as well, as the village was located within the castle’s shadow. The villagers did their best to fight against these forces, and even set fire to the Laroba Causeway in hopes of quarantining the horror to the isle.

When dawn broke, the strange mists parted to reveal Bastardhall bloody and silent. Those who dwelt on Lake Laroba’s mainland shore had heard the screams and witnessed the bridge’s fiery destruction, but when investigators arrived on the isle the following day, they found both Maiserene and the castle devoid of life. Talk among the leaders of county Varno went back and forth about what to do with the castle, but red tape and the fact that no one came forward with a legitimate claim of inheritance for it in the months and years to follow resulted in the place falling into ruined abandonment.

And so the ruin remained quietly forgotten for 100 years, but on the centennial anniversary, evil woke within the castle walls. A spectral version of the Laroba Causeway formed, and once again Velicarn’s Black Coach rode forth. Yet this time he didn’t seek out messengers. This time, he sought those of the Arudora family line who didn’t realize they were related by blood to the curse—descendants of those whom Raudltz had tried (and failed) to warn a century before. As he tracked his targets down, Velicarn invited each to board his coach, promising riches and glories of their forgotten inheritance if they freely accepted his invitation to return to “Bastardhall.” Those who accepted the invitation were bustled back to the castle, never to be seen again.

Those who denied the Black Coach were left alone—for a short time. Within a month—often within a week—the Black Coach rode again, and this time its presence brought not invitations but death in the form of sudden and mysterious accidents. The castle’s new name, “Bastardhall,” took hold in local legends.

Every 100 years thereafter, the black coach rode again, and each time, its range increased as it harvested more and more unknowing descendants of the Arudora line. Then, in the year 4711, 2 years before that century’s scheduled manifestation of Bastardhall’s curse, something changed. For the first time in nearly 5 centuries, one who knew of their connection to the Arudora legacy came to Bastardhall. This was an oracle named Caydserris Arudora, a man whose ancestral memories had revealed the truth of his bloodline and the promise of power that should be his by family right. He came to Bastardhall, and something unprecedented happened as a result: as the first of the bloodline to voluntarily visit the site since the curse struck it so long ago, the castle manifested and welcomed him in. Only then did Caydserris learn the horrific truth— that his own cursed ancestors had lured him home, for Charg desired new blood—a living soul of the bloodline who had full knowledge of their lineage—that would serve the sahkil tormentor as his high priest and voice. Caydserris became Bastardhall’s new lord, and he at once began sinister rites in preparation for what he believed would be an imminent return once the last of the Arudora line could be taken.

When Bastardhall manifested again two years later, the Black Coach rode once more. Under Caydserris’s guidance, it sought out what the curse believed to be the final living descendants of the Arudora line—a woman named Janquill (who had married into the Kindler family and whose own ancestors had long forgotten their Arudora links) and her young daughter Florin. Velicarn invited them as he had done so many times before, but Janquill denied the invitation. The headless coachman departed, leaving Janquill and her daughter to their doom, or so he assumed. For by now, the legend of Bastardhall was well known, and when Janquill Kindler and her husband realized what was happening, they spared no expense in arranging their daughter’s safety. They sent her away to be sheltered safely within the walls of a Shelynite temple, hoping that the wards there would protect her. Florin’s parents then fled, hoping to draw the curse’s attention even further away. They both perished soon thereafter, but when Janquill’s soul joined the other Arudoras in the curse, Caydserris realized with frustration that the last Arudora, young Florin, had escaped.

And so, powerless to emerge and take action on Golarion for another 100 years, Caydserris and the curse began another long wait. Should Florin perish before having a child, then Caydserris could pursue his goal at that time. Should she survive to build a family of her own, a hundred years later, Velicarn would ride forth and claim them all. Bastardhall had waited five centuries already. It was patient. It could wait for one more.

But as fate would have it, this wait would not be long at all. As Florin grew up an orphan under the protection of Shelyn’s faithful, her curiosity about her parents’ fate grew as well. By the time she came of age and left the temple orphanage to begin her own life, she focused her time on researching her parents’ deaths. When she learned that they’d been victims of Bastardhall’s coachman, she dug deeper and discovered that her mother’s lineage went back to the Arudoras. In 4726, she set her sights on Bastardhall itself, intending to explore the ruins in search of an answer to the mystery of her parents’ death, hiring a group of adventurers to serve as escorts and guards. Those adventurers are the PCs.

Florin Kindler’s arrival on Arudora Isle was an unexpected boon to Caydserris, and the curse eagerly took her and her entourage in. Florin, as a member of the family, was swept up into the castle towers and transformed into a monster, but the PCs merely woke on the island’s lakeshore—uninvited guests and collateral damage who are now the best hope to end the five-centuries-long curse once and for all!

Arudora Heraldlry

While the Arudora family’s crest doesn’t play a key role in any of the mysteries in this campaign, the PCs will see it everywhere—worked into fences, adorning doors, carved into lintels, worked into tapestries, etched on glasses and tableware, and so on. The family crest shows a serpentine creature with a long neck, long tail, and four flippers curled around a sword in front of a stylized image of the castle—the creature is a representation of Voldrak, the Lake Laroba monster, while the sword is a depiction of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.w7usWIc20eklVVXT]{Fearcutter}, Eragayl Arudora’s legendary blade.
