Bastion of Blasphemies.name: Bastion of Blasphemies
Bastion of Blasphemies.text:
For centuries, a strange, scorched ruin loomed atop an island in Lake Laroba in eastern Ustalav, the fog-shrouded land of horrors. On clear days, the fire-blackened towers and crumbling walls of this ancient castle are visible to those plying the West Sellen River to the east. On some nights, when the fog is light and thin, one might spy lights flickering, as if from high tower windows, yet no such towers rise above the castle today.

People whisper about the ruins. Travelers avert their eyes when passing them. They speak quietly of how any who try to reclaim the cursed place tend to meet tragic ends or of how treasure seekers eager to uncover abandoned riches find picked-over web-choked rooms and suffer the most unbearable nightmares for weeks to follow—assuming they simply don’t vanish without a trace. But there comes a time, once every hundred years, when the whispers and idle glances sent this ruin’s way turn to outright terror and wards against evil. For on these centennials, strange green mists wash over the ruins, restoring the castle into a looming testament to one of the most infamous curses in all of Ustalav.

On these nights, the Black Coach rides across the spectral span of the Laroba Causeway, its headless coachman seeking specific passengers to take back across the bridge. Those who deny the coachman aren’t forced inside the carriage, but within a week, they meet strange and horrible deaths. Those who accept the invitation to ride back meet fates unknown, for they’re never seen again. Then the mists rise once more, and the castle reverts to an empty ruin, awaiting another hundred years before the curse of Bastardhall returns once more.

Running this Adventure Path.name: Running this Adventure Path
Running this Adventure Path.text:
Bastion of Blasphemies is an Adventure Path for a party of four 5th–level characters. After accepting an invitation to aid a woman named Florin Kindler who intends to travel to the ruined castle and search for clues to the fate of her long-ago vanished parents, the party finds themselves trapped within a strangely reformed castle, one haunted by monsters and much worse. By the time they manage to escape, the PCs will have reached 13th level, or perhaps, if they’re thorough and fortunate, even 14th level—provided the curse of Bastardhall doesn’t claim them first!

Bastion of Blasphemies is, at its heart, a campaign that focuses on exploration and combat against a wide range of monsters and sinister foes, yet there’s more to this Adventure Path than dungeon crawling. A complex mystery and dozens of ancient secrets lie in wait for your players to discover, as well as a wealth of treasures for their characters to claim. And while the primary plot of Bastion of Blasphemies involves the party’s attempt to escape the cursed castle and get back home to Golarion, persistent parties can perhaps undo the trauma and cruelties visited upon the site after over five centuries of an enduring curse!

The PCs begin this adventure at 5th level. The @UUID[JournalEntry.oIog1W3hftKUYySh]{Bastion of Blasphemies Player’s Guide} provides information for players to help them create brand new 5th–level characters for this campaign, including advice for generating extended backstories to cover the adventures they went on during 1st through 4th level and help in determining what gear they start with. Alternatively, you can run Bastion of Blasphemies as a sequel to Troubles in Grayce, an anthology adventure and continuation of the Pathfinder Beginner Box: Secrets of the Unlit Star, or even as a continuation of an introductory campaign of your own design.

Regardless, this Adventure Path begins with the PCs awakening on the shores of a mysterious island dominated by an immense, unnerving castle. The PCs are trapped here, and the castle that looms above them holds the secret (and dangerous) path back to Golarion. When you’re ready to start, before you dive into @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH]{Chapter 1}, make sure you’re familiar with Bastardhall’s features and history, as explored on the following pages.

Adventure Path Structure.name: Adventure Path Structure
Adventure Path Structure.text:
The PCs begin with their gear and companions on the forested shoreline of Arudora Isle at location @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.XyjmNWjgPGNrEVim]{A1} in @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH]{Chapter 1}. Looming above them, the massive curtain wall of Castle Arudora encircles the entire island. Beyond that, Bastardhall is visible, yet these towers and walls periodically flicker and shimmer, as if the structure were a ghost. These areas are initially “locked” to the PCs. As the PCs explore Bastardhall, they’ll face challenges and guardians—the most dangerous of which are the monstrously transformed and cursed members of the Arudora family who had the poor fortune to be within the castle when it became cursed over 500 years ago. By defeating these guardians and restoring items they valued in life to a fountain in the castle courtyard, the PCs “unlock” additional portions of Bastardhall. The PCs are free to explore the areas they unlock at their own pace and order, moving back and forth between chapters as they gain levels and resources. Remember, though, that if a party faces encounters below their level, they’ll earn fewer XP. Likewise, if the party unlocks a later chapter before they reach the appropriate level, they’ll earn more XP—assuming they survive the greater challenges these chapters present!

Escape the Dungeon

Bastardhall is an unusual campaign in that the entire Adventure Path takes place on a single island with very little in the way of support—at least, initially. While the PCs aren’t on any sort of timer to complete this campaign, neither will they have the luxury of “heading to the big city to shop” between adventures, for Bastardhall and all who dwell within—including the PCs—are trapped, adrift, in the depths of the Ethereal Plane. As the PCs continue to explore the early reaches of Bastardhall’s haunted shore in @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH]{Chapter 1}, they’ll encounter six lost souls. These six were once leaders in the village of Maiserene, victims claimed by the castle’s curse who’ve spent the past five centuries trapped at sites along the isle’s shoreline at locations beyond the village that were once important to them. Once they’re rescued and led back to their homes in the ruined village of Maiserene, they’ll manifest as phantoms, at which point they can provide the party with support. As the PCs continue to explore, they’ll recover @UUID[.uT2rZ6sr9wmX1Bc2]{soulhearts}, spiritually charged mementos once valued by these lost souls now scattered throughout Bastardhall. By returning these mementos, they’ll increase the amount of support these lost souls can provide. See @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.ZhFLGUjpu87SUVXX]{Restoring Maiserene} and the NPC entries for the six lost souls at the Maiserene Phantoms category of this journal.

Handling PC Deaths

This is a very self-contained campaign, with not a lot of obvious ways to introduce new PCs if one dies and the player wants to replace them. (Or if a new player joins a game in progress, for that matter!) Once the PCs restore the village priest, @UUID[.OoslGgDkvU7MPY5k]{Shirail Animender}, she’ll be able to help restore fallen PCs to life for a price. There are also items capable of restoring the dead the PCs can discover during exploration as well.

Still, it’s no fun to have a PC die, and if the player of a dead PC wants to replace the lost PC with a brand-new character, they can. While these new PCs can be introduced into the story as captives rescued from creatures or cells in the dungeon, new PCs can just as easily “wash up” on the shores of Arudora Isle and be taken in and given shelter by the villagers of Maiserene. The next time the PCs return to the village, the new PC can join up.

The Ethereal Plane

Bastardhall exists on an island of solidity floating deep within a remote reach of the Ethereal Plane, but for the most part, the PCs won’t have to deal with the complications that arise from this plane. As long as they remain within the confines of Bastardhall as presented in this adventure, they function as if they were back on Golarion.

The view from the shores of Arudora Isle makes it clear that the PCs are on an isle in a lake, with the far shorelines appearing to be heavily wooded hills with no sign of habitation. This, along with the sky above, is but an illusion maintained by Bastardhall’s curse. If the PCs travel more than a thousand feet out onto the lake from any point along the shoreline or fly up into the air to an elevation of higher than a thousand feet, visibility suddenly becomes obscured by swirling green clouds through which the previously visible shores now appear to be ghostly. A PC who experiences this eerie sensation and succeeds at a @Check[occultism|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret], @Check[religion|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check, or a @Check[arcana|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} recognizes the shocking truth—this is the Ethereal Plane! A critical success at this check confirms that while the island of solidity they stand upon seems to function as if it were still part of Golarion, going beyond this boundary puts the PCs at serious risk of being lost to the In-Between.

A PC can physically enter the Ethereal Plane from Bastardhall by moving beyond this encircling boundary, but if they do so, gravity suddenly vanishes. The PC continues to catch glimpses of vague terrain features of the far shores of Lake Laroba through the Ethereal mists, but can never actually reach them. Fortunately, the PCs can move through the plane through sheer force of will, and no matter how far they travel from the borders of Bastardhall, they’ll never find that the return to the border takes more than a few moments of concentration. Whenever the PCs return, they appear on the lakeshore at area A1, once again waking as if from a deep sleep.

As the PCs make their way into Bastardhall, they’ll inevitably reach areas that remain locked to them. Shimmering fields of pale green energy periodically ripple along the borders of these areas, preventing the passage of anything through them. Persistent PCs might attempt to scale these borders to get a better vantage, but doing so requires a @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check. Until these areas are unlocked, these portions of Bastardhall shimmer and flicker, almost as if they were ghostly or illusory constructions that simply don’t look real on close inspection.

Living in Bastardhall

It will take time for the PCs to escape Bastardhall. Depending on an individual group’s motivation and capabilities, it will be many weeks or even months before they can defeat the curse and make it back to Golarion. In that time. they’ll be confined to the isle. Fortunately for the PCs and those they rescue, the nature of this island of solidity adrift in the Ethereal Plane provides. The waters of Lake Laroba are fresh and safe to drink, and there are plenty of fish swimming about—more than enough to sustain a small group like the PCs and the slowly growing village. Likewise, edible plants like berries, watercress, wild lettuce, apples, and other forageable foodstuffs exist in the woodlands on the lower shores of Arudora Isle, and there’s a robust population of rats, rabbits, frogs, snakes, and other small wildlife as well. Animals larger than a rabbit, while they do exist, tend to be dangerous predators, as indicated in various encounter areas. While the nature of the island replenishes its bounty through a supernatural process that involves the accretion of ectoplasm (and thus keeps the animals with all the food they need to sustain themselves), the PCs will have to hunt, gather, and scavenge their food until Maiserene grows large enough to sustain them automatically. Until this point, you’ll need to keep track of the PCs’ supplies. Water is plentiful, but food must be found. Stashes of edible food can be recovered in certain areas of the island and castle as indicated in those locations, and PCs who aren’t particularly skilled at Survival will need to seek out these stashes to avoid starvation. It’s a @Check[survival|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Subsist.Title|options:action:subsist|traits:downtime] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.49y9Ec4bDii8pcD3]{Subsist} on the island’s shoreline—remember that a PC can choose to Subsist after 8 hours or fewer of exploration, but if they do so, they take a –5 penalty to their Survival check. Once the PCs rescue Aron Mordimus’s spirit from the orchard (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.iKQ1sh7QyLC4On4P]{A21}) and increase his support rank to at least 1 through the use of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.8WxFFZm6OcBCCARR]{soulheart}, he’ll be able to support the party automatically at a comfortable level of living, and the PCs no longer need to track food or Subsist in order to survive.

Resting

As the PCs explore, they’ll find certain safe havens where they can rest without fear of being ambushed or attacked. The first of these is likely Orm’s Rest, the village inn in Maiserene, once they rescue the lost soul of the innkeeper, Aron Mordimus. If the PCs rest for the night in any other location, there’s a chance that something sinister and violent stumbles upon their camp. Attempt a flat check once during the rest period (the DC depends on the region). On a failure, the PCs are attacked as they rest, as detailed at the start of each chapter. In addition to the potential threat of attack, whenever the PCs sleep in Bastardhall, there’s a chance they’ll experience haunting visions and harrowing nightmares—they are, after all, sleeping in a realm ruled by a powerful agent of a sahkil tormentor. The PCs automatically experience their first nightmare on their first night of sleeping—none of them remember the details of the nightmare other than flashes of being chased by an unimaginable evil through the passages and chambers of Bastardhall and upon waking are convinced that the creature that chased them watches them even now from somewhere high above—whether from a vantage point in the castle or somewhere higher still, none can say for sure. After this first nightmare, every time the PCs rest, roll a @Check[flat|dc:16] check—on a failure, they share the same nightmares again. The nightmares occur automatically the first night after they unlock a new region of Bastardhall. The unknown source of these nightmares is Caydserris, the current lord of Bastardhall. While he does not physically emerge from his tower to confront the PCs until the Adventure Path’s climax, his very presence threatens dreaming minds. Intended as warnings, they can impact the PCs’ rest and well-being but also provide them with insights into the nature of their tormentor. Each time the PCs have nightmares, the nature of the frightening dream is shared among them. Upon waking, the PCs must each attempt a @Check[will] save against a slowly increasing DC. The theme of the nightmare and the DC to save against it are detailed at the start of each chapter, but the effects remain the same, and they always begin with the PCs encountering a sinister figure carrying a staff with an eerie green-glowing lantern hanging from it.

Critical Success The PC experiences a lucid nightmare—they realize they’re dreaming, and despite the harrowing nature, can use the dream to attempt to research the source of these nightmares as detailed below under “Lucid Nightmares.” They suffer no ill effect on waking.

Success The PC remembers the general gist of the nightmare, and suffers no ill effect on waking.

Failure As success, but the PC remains unsettled by the nightmare for the next 24 hours. The first time during this period when the PC gains the frightened condition, increase the value of the condition by 1. This is a curse effect.

Critical Failure As failure, but the PC suffers from an additional unpleasant effect from the dream for the next 24 hours, as listed in the individual chapter headings. These are all curse effects, and once the PC endures a chapter’s particular phobia, they treat all future Critical Failures from nightmares as failures until they unlock the next region—a PC can only become afflicted by one of a chapter’s nightmare phobias once, and the effects only last for 24 hours, unless the curse is removed before then.

Research

@UUID[.UUqGlDCzpRnwqovv]{Bastardhall Curse} @UUID[.sKX1KQy64oUXrIvb]{Caydserris Arudora}

Lucid Nightmares: The PC takes control of the nightmare and explores it, learning more about the source of these fears as they observe and interact with the dream to research the Bastardhall Curse or directly confront the strange figure with the staff—Caydserris—to learn more about him.

Maximum RP 5; Research Checks As listed in the individual Lucid Nightmare page.

Day and Night in Bastardhall

Although Bastardhall is adrift in the Ethereal Plane, the curse that wraps the castle and its island into a protective shell also creates a realistic illusion of the sky above, including a day and night cycle. The sun, moon, and stars all provide the same sort of illumination and other benefits to those in Bastardhall as they would on Golarion, although the longer the PCs remain trapped here, the more apparent it will become that the sky above is different in certain ways. Every night is a full moon in Bastardhall—the moon never waxes nor wanes, and as a result, the moon’s light fills open outdoor areas with dim illumination. When this Adventure Path begins, the day/night cycle is balanced. The sun rises at 6:00 am and sets at 6:00 pm, splitting each day into equal 12-hour periods of day and night. As the PCs explore and penetrate deeper into Bastardhall, though, the days grow shorter. Each chapter begins with information on how much shorter the days get—an increasingly important factor in Bastardhall, for here the nights are dangerous. After the sun sets, the Bastardhall Curse grows in power. In the waters surrounding the isle, the Lake Laroba monster known as Voldrak grows active, and its glowing eyes can be seen now and then in the dark waters as it patrols, but more importantly, the monstrous inhabitants of Bastardhall grow more dangerous and active. Once night falls and the eternal moon rises, all enemies gain a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative checks and all saving throws against holy effects, and the PCs take a –1 circumstance penalty to all saving throws against fear effects. Note that while the balance between day and night shifts as the Adventure Path progresses, overall day length remains constant at 24 hours.

The Storm

When this Adventure Path begins, the days have clear skies with only a few clouds visible. Temperatures are crisp and cool. With each new portion of Bastardhall the PCs restore, though, the weather grows increasingly hostile and stormy. The start of each chapter, starting with @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL]{Chapter 2}, describes the effects of the worsening weather once the PCs restore a new section of the castle.

The Souls of Bastardhall

The physical structure of Bastardhall is made of solid matter in the same way it existed on Golarion, but living creatures and plants native to the region are maintained and replenished by a mix of the power of the curse and ectoplasm accreted from the surrounding Ethereal Plane. To the PCs, this largely won’t be noticeable, save for areas specifically called out in the text where ectoplasm functions in unusual ways, but it does serve to keep foliage and smaller wild animals alive. Left to its own, this ectoplasm maintains Bastardhall and its occupants in a state of balance, but it’s far from a purely biological system.

The native denizens of Bastardhall gain an unusual boon—they do not age. They might still be killed through violence, illness, or misadventure, but barring such fates, they can live forever. The one exception occurs once per century, when Bastardhall manifests on Golarion, during which the inhabitants age normally for that short period of time. This is also a point where creatures in Golarion can enter the castle—when it returns to the Ethereal Plane for another hundred years, those creatures age normally and are likely doomed to die within the castle.

The souls of native creatures slain (or native undead creatures destroyed) by other natives of Bastardhall (or who succumb to sickness or accidents brought on by the environment) do not enter the afterlife—instead, their souls are swept up by the heart of the curse in a region known as the soul vortex (area I), only to be returned back into Bastardhall as a fully grown version of who they were before (undead are returned not to life but to their previous existence as undead). This is similar to reincarnation, in that such reborn creatures have only hazy memories of their previous “lives” in Bastardhall. In this way wild animals are constantly reborn to feed predators, and other creatures (including many of the phantoms) are brought back for the amusement of some of the crueler occupants who glory in torment and worse. The physical remains left behind are either kept for “ambience” by the curse or slowly decay into ectoplasm, as Charg’s will prefers.

Intruders to Bastardhall’s cycle are rarities, and include plane-traveling oddities and explorers like the psychopomp Lucinero (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.FuifNpUpaAG0LzlR]{A12}) or the will-o’-wisps drawn into the castle by its fearsome aura during its appearances in Golarion (see area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.I5xBZSgIpeHNyb21]{D21} or the Bastardhall dungeon in @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ]{Chapter 5}). These creatures aren’t metaphysically trapped within Bastardhall, and like the PCs, should they perish, their souls move on to the afterlife as normal. Yet only those who have the capability of planar travel can easily escape once they arrive—those who enter without such capacity might not be doomed to remain in Bastardhall forever, but they may well live out the remainder of their lives within.

The rarest of these intruders is a relatively new addition—first, in the year of 4711 with the arrival of Caydserris Arudora, and then more recently with the intrusion of Florin Kindler and her companions, the PCs. In the cases of those of the Arudora bloodline, Bastardhall seized upon their cursed bloodline and drew them in, but such is not the fate of the PCs. They’re the truest of rarities—intruders trapped within Bastardhall, yet ones whose fates and agencies remain their own. They alone have the ability to break Bastardhall’s curse, and the longer the PCs explore and defeat the monstrous creatures within, the more the trapped souls of its long-cursed victims can hope, for each native slain by the PCs finds true escape, in that their souls avoid the soul vortex and move on to the afterlife as normal.

Those Who Wait

When the PCs first arrive in Bastardhall, only the haunted shore surrounding the castle is open for them to explore, yet even though they can’t enter the interior portions of the castle until they unlock them, those entities that dwell within each floor continue to “live out” their lives, experiencing their surrounding floors normally. In effect, each chapter of this adventure presents a sort of “ship in a bottle” for nine different regions within Bastardhall, and until the PCs unlock a region, the inhabitants of any one chapter are free to move about their section but cannot enter outer regions until they’re unlocked by the PCs. Even then, the majority of the creatures rarely drift far from their homes. To these creatures, boredom is never a threat, for each month that passes while their particular portion of Bastardhall remains self- contained, their memories reset. In this way, Charg keeps his playthings “fresh” for his entertainment and prevents his prisoners from effecting any sort of long-term plan to escape. Once the PCs unlock a region in Bastardhall, though, this resetting of memories no longer occurs.

This goes both ways, though. While a few of the Arudoras are able to observe what goes on outside of their domains from afar, the curse keeps these dangerous foes in isolation until the PCs force a conflict. This is certainly an advantage in that their foes won’t realize what the PCs are doing until their own domain becomes unlocked, and even then, most of the Arudoras are too involved in their individual plots to notice until they’re confronted.

Campaign Timeline.name: Campaign Timeline
Campaign Timeline.text:
Key events leading up to the start of Bastion of Blasphemies are listed below.

Date

Event

4113 AR

As a reward for heroism against a plague of monsters that vexed the county of Varno in Ustalav, the champion Eragayl Arudora is granted land and a generous stipend to build a castle on an isle in Lake Laroba in western Varno.

4118

Castle Arudora is completed, and Eragayl moves in with his new wife Tasifinie and newborn son, Irrokcis. Many of those who helped build the castle are retained as servants, while a few stay on in the small village of Maiserene just outside the castle walls.

4148

Tasifinie is bitten to death by spiders in her own bedroom when a swarm hatches out of a rare house plant she’d recently purchased; Irrokcis is the one who discovers her bloated body the next morning.

4150

After two years spent exploring occult mysteries in hopes of finding a way to make contact with his mother’s spirit and to discover a cure for the emotion of fear, Irrokcis falls under the malevolent influence of Charg. His only surviving child, Demiterus, is born the same year.

4151

In search of a place he can carry out his increasingly blasphemous research into the nature of fear, Irrokcis explores a strange crack in the floor in a corner of the castle dungeon with the aid of a vapor form spell and discovers a large cavern hundreds of feet below ground. Construction on a hidden laboratory therein, as well as easier routes to and from the castle above, begin at once with the aid of conjured minions and mind-controlled Darklands denizens.

4152

Irrokcis discovers a false wall in the cavern, knocks it down, and is astounded to find a large chamber within that held a strange source of power—a partially completed soul anchor: a corruption of the River of Souls that, had it been fully completed by its unknown and long-dead architects, would have helped those who died in the area to retain their mortal memories in the afterlife. Much of his studies thereafter would be frustrating dead ends in attempts to both reverse engineer the soul anchor or to complete its construction.

4158

Irrokcis, now a powerful witch whose goals have distorted from curing fear to mastering it, betrays his father Eragayl and imprisons him in the vaults deep below the castle as part of his lengthy process of transforming himself into a lich. He claims the mantle of Arudora patriarch after spreading rumors of Eragayl’s death from complications after a nasty fall.

4159

After months of prayer, Eragayl’s cries for help are heard and an angelic ally of his named Cevairiel comes to provide aid in person, only to be captured and imprisoned in turn by Irrokcis. He breaks his father’s mind and inflicts upon the previously fearless champion his first true taste of terror by allowing him to witness Cevairiel’s sacrifice and subsequent transformation into an undead blasphemy known as a carrion angel, whom he puts in charge of guarding his father’s oubliette.

4169

Ryhasphinea Arudora, daughter of Demiterus Arudora, is born.

4171

Raudltz Arudora, son of Demiterus Arudora, is born.

4188

Ryhasphinea marries a wealthy and aging noble in the city of Carrion Hill, cementing a strong new alliance for the Arudoras. Her first child, Dazerien, is born later that year.

4189

With the aid of the carrion angel Cevairiel, Irrokcis completes his long transformation into a lich by murdering his father (Eragayl) and son (Demiterus) in a vile ritual. Demiterus’s wife Neesha catches wind of the plot and almost stops Irrokcis but fails, and is murdered as well. Irrokcis retreats into the laboratories, and the mantle of rule passes to an 18-year-old Raudltz Arudora. Irrokcis spreads a false story about Demiterus, and Neesha drowning after a boating accident on Lake Laroba.

4190

With the deaths of his parents, Raudltz abandons the family’s traditions of worship, and has the castle’s temple to Pharasma closed down. Worship of Shelyn remains strong among the servants and villagers of Maiserene, but the presence of her faith within the castle walls diminishes as well.

4192

Raudltz marries Alisendra Caliphvaso, following his older sister’s footsteps in wedding into another powerful noble family from Caliphas, further strengthening the Arudora fortunes and prestige. Their daughter, Jinnivere, is born later the same year. A few weeks later, Raudltz is confronted by one of his many lovers, Yasmerra, with whom he had a torrid affair during his courtship of Alisendra. Yasmerra presents to Raudltz their illegitimate son, Velicarn, hoping to secure a life of luxury and privilege for him, but Raudltz denies her, turning her out for fear of ruining his impending marriage into the Caliphvasos. When Yasmerra flies into a rage and threatens to expose the affair, Raudltz murders her and hides her remains in his attic observatory, but can’t bring himself to kill his own son, bastard or not. Instead, he has a trusted servant take the infant Velicarn away to an orphanage in Cesca.

4194

Augsten Arudora is born.

4202

At 10 years of age, Velicarn has already developed a reputation as being a problem child, and the orphanage sends him away to a strict boarding school in Lepidstadt.

4208

Now a devotee of Urgathoa, Ryhasphinea grows frustrated with her husband’s longevity, having hoped she’d by now become a rich widow. She decides to speed along the process by poisoning her husband, but the attempt backfires and most of the family household succumbs. Facing an imminent investigation by the authorities, Ryhasphinea flees with her surviving son Dazerien back to her family home, Castle Arudora. Raudltz acquiesces to his sister’s request to renovate the family temple as a place devoted to the Pallid Princess.

4210

Velicarn’s studies in school focus on occult explorations and mysteries, but it wasn’t until he used a forbidden rite from an ancient text he stole from a professor’s library that his studies gained a hateful focus. In hopes of determining who his actual parents were, he attempted to make contact with his ancestors and unwittingly opened himself to his family’s true patron, the sahkil tormentor Charg. The Typhon Wheel saw promise in Velicarn, revealed his family history, and then showed him a way to regain his birthright by cultivating a malformed eidolon of his denied legacy from his own flesh.

4213

After three years, Velicarn’s gift from Charg is ready. Now a summoner whose eidolon is a half-ectoplasmic manifestation of his hatred, Velicarn travels to Castle Arudora and confronts his father, promising to bring a horrible curse upon his line in return for being denied his birthright. Raudltz decapitates Velicarn, but this doesn’t save anyone—Castle Arudora becomes cursed and Velicarn rides out for the first time as the driver of the Black Coach. The Arudoras become monsters and their castle is pulled into Charg’s clutches, who is now able to corrupt the partial soul anchor deep below the castle into a vortex designed to keep souls trapped. The villagers of Maiserene futilely try to contain the curse by destroying the bridge, but by the next morning, the castle and Maiserene stand empty.

4237

When no surviving member of the Arudora family expresses interest in taking control of the ruins of Castle Arudora, the Varno council abandons attempts to install new nobles within its walls, after a dozen attempts to do so result in tragedy. Castle Arudora is left to fall into ruin.

4313

Strange green mists rise around the abandoned Castle Arudora, and the frightful Black Coach makes its first harvest. The ruined castle comes to be known as Bastardhall.

4413

After a second century of quiet, the mists rise again. This time, the locals of several nearby villages are ready, and a peasant army marches on Bastardhall and burns the place to the ground, leaving its stone shell gutted, scorched, and even more uninhabitable.

4513

Despite the previous attempt to destroy the castle, the mists rise once more, and this time Bastardhall seems larger and even more menacing. The Black Coach rides again.

4613

The mists rise for a fourth time. Another band of peasants led by well-meaning heroes marches on the castle and attempts to destroy it, but they’re all slaughtered.

4711

Caydserris Arudora, an oracle of Charg, becomes the latest Arudora to rediscover his lineage. He travels to Bastardhall and triggers its early manifestation—he vanishes within and becomes the cursed castle’s new lord as he begins to finalize Charg’s sinister plans for the souls trapped within Bastardhall.

4713

The mists rise once more, and the Black Coach invites a woman named Janquill Kindler and her young daughter to return to Bastardhall. She and her husband refuse, then send their daughter Florin into hiding. Janquill and her husband die soon thereafter, but Florin escapes the Bastardhall Curse.

4726

Current year. After spending 12 years in a Caliphas orphanage, Florin spends her first year as an adult researching Bastardhall and makes an astonishing discovery. All those invited to ride are, in some way, distant blood relations to the Arudoras. When she returns to her hometown of Grayce to search her parents’ modest home, she discovers proof of their Arudora lineage in a hidden room in the building’s basement—a strange cameo handed down through the centuries that once belonged to the man who built Castle Arudora: Eragayl. Eager to travel to Bastardhall to investigate the site for clues, Florin engages the services of a group of adventurers and travels northeast, but as she and the adventurers approach, Bastardhall claims them all.

Key Names.name: Key Names
Key Names.text:
Bastion of Blasphemies is not only a dungeon crawl but also a complex mystery dealing with an equally complex aristocratic family. As such, this adventure is filled with NPCs to interact with and others who provide historical context. To help you keep track of some of the names and people in this Adventure Path, the most important ones are compiled here for reference.

@UUID[.mJYN4Onwrp1JCt7X]{Alisendra Arudora:} Lady of the castle, now transformed into a hag. Lady of the castle’s reception halls.

@UUID[.0LOtv52aD44VMt6N]{Aron Mordimus:} Maiserene’s innkeeper, now a lost soul trapped on Arudora Isle.

@UUID[.7ZSvhlTTOzKZNUJZ]{Augsten Arudora:} Son of Raudltz and Alisendra, now transformed into an ogre. Rules the castle cellars.

@UUID[.5oJGMvwqnrQybliF]{Ausken Dast:} Maiserene’s captain of the guards, now a lost soul trapped on Arudora Isle.

@UUID[.UTLSqT61vU6a2H9C]{Banijer Greely:} Maiserene’s merchant, now a lost soul trapped on Arudora Isle.

@UUID[.sKX1KQy64oUXrIvb]{Caydserris Arudora:} High priest of Charg and current ruler of Bastardhall.

@UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.MG8bJRohTuzWIbDI]{Cevairiel:} Undead fallen angel, prisoner of Irrokcis.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.kKdvt2m8MdsJ5aFb]{Charg:} Sahkil tormentor of decline and monsters, patron of Caydserris and Irrokcis, tormentor of Eragayl, and the source of the curse on Bastardhall.

@UUID[.BzucncWfHopUCsz3]{Dazerien Arudora:} Son of Ryhasphinea, now a sadistic werewolf who the inhabitants of the castle dungeon fear.

@UUID[.gBlukTRHytlzwC1D]{Eragayl Arudora:} Grandfather of Raudltz Arudora and founder of Castle Arudora.

@UUID[.M6cCO4Hg8Hj8yTBY]{Esmira Vermidian:} Maiserene’s schoolteacher, now a lost soul trapped on Arudora Isle.

@UUID[.QDo0K7VXLVH9D9tI]{Florin Kindler:} A young woman whose parents were taken by the Black Coach of Bastardhall, and who is destined to vanish into the mysterious castle soon after hiring adventurers to aid her in discovering her mother and father’s fate.

@UUID[.ckjkw2MuZPwvb7z1]{Ilana Greenbough:} Maiserene’s most gifted artisan, now a lost soul trapped on Arudora Isle.

@UUID[.qi00xNaMBgtsO0LH]{Irrokcis Arudora:} Grandfather of Raudltz Arudora, a lich who rarely exits a set of eldritch libraries deep below the castle.

@UUID[.6tXqaoCmhlHFRm3I]{Jinnivere Arudora:} Daughter of Raudltz and Alisendra, now transformed into a dullahan. Haunts the castle grounds.

@UUID[.m0khEHYdDxDw9B1G]{Raudltz Arudora:} Lord of the castle, now transformed into a vampire. Master of the castle’s private wings.

@UUID[.7VX2SBgHGbICdyYi]{Ryhasphinea Arudora:} Sister of Raudltz, now a child of Urgathoa and keeper of the castle’s temple.

@UUID[.OoslGgDkvU7MPY5k]{Shirail Animender:} Priestess of Maiserene, now a lost soul trapped on Arudora Isle.

@UUID[.ICuUq6iK6NdzE7Fp]{Velicarn:} The eponymous bastard of Bastardhall, and the source of the castle’s curse; illegitimate son of Raudltz Arudora; driver of the Black Coach.

Bastardhall Artifacts.name: Bastardhall Artifacts
Bastardhall Artifacts.text: These artifacts are unusual items in that they function only while within Bastardhall while the castle remains cursed and adrift on the Ethereal Plane. Taken from this location, these artifacts become non-magical objects of mild curiosity and mundane construction worth, at most, a few gold coins to a collector. They can be destroyed through normal means while in this state, but if they are destroyed, a duplicate version of the artifact reappears in Bastardhall at the location it was last found. Such an item immediately regains its full powers if brought back into Bastardhall while the castle remains cursed and in the Ethereal Plane.

Arudora Memento.name: Arudora Memento
Arudora Memento.text:
Arudora Memento

Item 14

  • Rare

  • Artifact

  • Occult

Each Arudora memento is unique in appearance, but all seven are approximately the same size. Carried by each of the cursed family members, these mementos have within them the power to unlock entire portions of Bastardhall from the ghostly cursed state the castle traditionally exists in. Each of the seven mementos has the following activation, but the section of castle unlocked by each activation, as well as each memento’s specific benefit granted to the PCs, varies by type.

Activate—Return Memento 3 (manipulate)

You place the memento into the appropriate statue’s clutches in the fountain located in area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3} of Bastardhall. The statue briefly animates to claim the memento, which turns to stone and becomes thereafter a permanent part of the statue, effectively destroying the memento while granting a boon to the party that persists for the remainder of this Adventure Path. A section of Bastardhall solidifies from its ghostly form, unlocking its reaches for the PCs to explore.

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.kasxhW2drfCOZZq1]{Alisendra’s Fan}

When this elegant crimson hand fan is Returned, the dungeon (detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ]{Chapter 5}) is unlocked. The souls trapped in Bastardhall appreciate the end of Alisendra’s dominion and now whisper hints of truths in the ears of those who seek knowledge. The DCs for all checks made to Recall Knowledge are reduced by 1 for the rest of the Adventure Path.

@UUID[Item.hFGe1C4FcZxTexoH]{Returned Alisendra's Fan}

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Z3yVkW6v7hzuXJa2]{Augsten’s Cudgel}

When this bloodstained wooden cudgel is Returned, the reception halls (detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi]{Chapter 4}) are unlocked. Sometimes, violence is the only answer, and swift action to combat is rewarded. For the rest of the Adventure Path, all PCs gain a +1 bonus to any initiative rolls; this special bonus combines with all other bonuses.

@UUID[Item.wzrLdct5VjYM8KZS]{Returned Augsten's Cudgel}

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.HKSpj0db5owAuA1v]{Dazerien’s Thumbscrew}

When this gory bronze thumbscrew is Returned, the private halls (detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8]{Chapter 6}) are unlocked. Rest becomes more rewarding now that the sadist of the dungeon has been defeated. For the rest of the Adventure Path, when the PCs take their 8-hour period of rest, they recover an additional number of Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) times their level.

@UUID[Item.Q0rrFTR06XtWr9rj]{Returned Dazerien's Thumbscrew}

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.0LrDMdMNqUb9cxSV]{Irrokcis’s Medallion}

When this eerie medallion is Returned, the towers (detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le]{Chapter 9}) are unlocked, and the spirits of those trapped in Bastardhall rise up to aid the PCs. All weapon Strikes made by PCs deal an additional 1 spirit damage for the rest of the Adventure Path.

@UUID[Item.ImK58IYuKOAHZ9If]{Returned Irrokcis's Medallion}

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.fZDL0jQQy1jQTg4c]{Jinnivere’s Riding Crop}

When this leather riding crop is Returned, the cellars (detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw]{Chapter 3}) are unlocked. Companions are now more hearty and full of life—PC companions (such as familiars, eidolons, and animal companions) gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws for the remainder of this Adventure Path.

@UUID[Item.8hqCv8eJJxsNzWxA]{Returned Jinnivere's Riding Crop}

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.iPD5FDdwUmRG7Erl]{Raudltz’s Telescope}

When this handheld telescope is Returned, the fallen temple (detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk]{Chapter 7}) is unlocked. Secrets are now more difficult to hide in Bastardhall. Reduce all Perception DCs made when Seeking or Searching by 2 for the rest of this Adventure Path.

@UUID[Item.iRUnURoPuXhATcUP]{Returned Raudltz's Telescope}

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.3c9AEoBCXmdltdr2]{Ryhasphinea’s Hourglass}

When this cracked hourglass is Returned, the vaults (detailed in @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X]{Chapter 8}) are unlocked. Death’s grasp on the PCs wanes—for the rest of this Adventure Path, the DCs for all recovery checks made by a dying PC are reduced by 2.

@UUID[Item.JruarXdgqkKuE0bY]{Returned Ryhasphinea's Hourglass}

Destruction An Arudora memento is destroyed when it’s activated with Return Memento, and the boon it grants upon this returning lasts until the very end of the Adventure Path.

Soulheart.name: Soulheart
Soulheart.text:
Soulheart

Item 5+

  • Rare

  • Artifact

  • Occult

Usage held in 1 hand; Bulk L

A soulheart is a crystallized sphere of red ectoplasm about the size of a human eye. When held by a living creature, a faint red light shimmers within the crystal, pulsating in a synchronized beat with the creature’s heartbeat and providing illumination equivalent to that of a candle.

Activate—Bolster Life 2 (concentrate, manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Effect When held to the chest and focused upon, the soul energy within the soulheart floods outward and bolsters your life force, granting you temporary Hit Points. The number of temporary Hit Points granted depends on the type of the soulheart, but regardless of type, they last for 8 hours.

Activate—Bolster Maiserene Phantom 2 (concentrate, manipulate)

When touched to a Maiserene phantom of the proper rank (depending on the type of soulheart), the soulheart flashes with bright red light and is destroyed. As it does so, it permanently increases the targeted phantom to rank 1, and increases each PC’s maximum Hit Points by 1 for as long as they remain within Bastardhall while the castle remains cursed. More powerful soulhearts can increase higher-rank phantoms and grant more Hit Points.

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.8WxFFZm6OcBCCARR]{Soulheart}; Level 5

When used to Bolster Life, the soulheart grants 6 temporary Hit Points (or 3 temporary Hit Points if it’s nighttime). Bolster Maiserene Phantom can only be activated on rank 0 phantoms. When bolstered, the phantom increases to rank 1, and all PCs gain 1 permanent Hit Point.

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.5nNs3OFkRXH8yU1D]{Greater Soulheart}; Level 10

When used to Bolster Life, the soulheart grants 12 temporary Hit Points (or 6 temporary Hit Points if it’s nighttime). Bolster Maiserene Phantom can only be activated on rank 1 phantoms. When bolstered, the phantom increases to rank 2, and all PCs gain 2 permanent Hit Points.

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.05h3LWflr74iJiVg]{Major Soulheart}; Level 15

When used to Bolster Life, the soulheart grants 18 temporary Hit Points (or 9 temporary Hit Points if it’s nighttime). Bolster Maiserene Phantom can only be activated on rank 2 phantoms. When bolstered, the phantom increases to rank 3, and all PCs gain 3 permanent Hit Points.

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.klQlruwrLO0xvPjl]{Pure Soulheart}; Level 20

A pure soulheart doesn’t have a Bolster Life or Bolster Maiserene Phantom activation—instead, it has the following activation.

Activate—Restore Life 1 minute (concentrate, manipulate); Effect By holding a pure soulheart against the remains of a dead creature of 20th level or lower that has been dead for no more than a year and concentrating for one minute, the pure soulheart flashes with red light and is destroyed. The targeted dead creature is restored to life with 1 Hit Point, no spells prepared or spell slots available, no points in any pools or any other daily resources, and is still affected by any long-term debilitations of the old body.

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Y10KCgi8mOL2iAkS]{Angelic Soulheart}; Level 21

An angelic soulheart doesn’t have a Bolster Life or Bolster Maiserene Phantom activation—instead, it has the following activation.

Activate—Defy Charg 1 (concentrate, manipulate) Requirements Pharasma’s favor (earned by restoring the temple clock tower in Bastardhall), Shelyn’s favor (earned by restoring the gallery in Bastardhall’s reception halls), and Caydserris Arudora is defeated; Effect By presenting the angelic soulheart to Charg at the climax of this Adventure Path, you can fully remove the Bastardhall Curse and free all of the souls trapped within! See page 222 for additional details.

Destruction A soulheart is destroyed when it is activated to Bolster Maiserene Phantom, Restore Life, or Defy Charg.

New PCs and Soulhearts

If a player opts to replace a PC for whatever reason with a new character, all permanent Hit Point increases the party has earned from Bolstering Maiserene Phantoms also applies to new PCs, as long as they remain in Bastardhall during the curse.

Vile Remnant.name: Vile Remnant
Vile Remnant.text:
Vile Remnant

Item 7+

  • Rare

  • Artifact

  • Cursed

  • Occult

  • Unholy

Usage held in 1 hand; Bulk L

When dislodged, mortal fragments like a chewed fingernail, a careless sneeze, or a few strands of hair might fall to the soil and be swiftly forgotten. When a horror like Charg brushes close to reality, the vile remnants cast off from his nightmare form are not so harmless. At other times, the desecrated remains of innocent creatures can be transformed into vile remnants as well. Worshippers of unholy gods and followers of evil philosophies gather these things and covet them as one might the hem of a cloak brushed against an idolized hero, or the visage of a divinity made manifest in a patch of mold on a wall. Vile remnants spread fear and cruelty wherever they're hidden and can corrupt those who discover them. They might be buried in the soil of a farmer's field, dropped into the depths of a village well, or stashed at the bottom of a toy box. Wherever the innocent might stumble across them and become unknowing actors in the decay of morality, the vile remnant works its unholy magic.

A vile remnant appears as a raw, decaying mass of flesh, fur, and gristle—a teratoma consisting of warty skin, sightless eyes, a finger or a toe, tufts of bristly hair, or teeth without mouths or lips to hide them. Each vile remnant's shape is wildly different and uniquely unsettling. A vile remnant automatically imparts to a PC the knowledge of how to use its Hear My Words activation as soon as it's touched, but its other activations must be discovered normally through the use of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic} (and as normal, identifying the presence and effect of the curse it carries requires a critical success at such an attempt).

Unlike most cursed items, a character can discard a vile remnant, yet doing so runs a real risk that it might thereafter fall into the wrong hands. In this Adventure Path, any vile remnant the PCs discard anywhere other than the restored reliquary in the Maiserene Church at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.oQOmNJ7YInR10ecC]{A9} is discovered by one of the monsters of Bastardhall, who then Hides the horror somewhere in the region where it was found. Where the horror is hidden is left to you to decide.

As long as a creature carries a vile remnant, its thoughts and dreams are influenced by cruel notions and temptations to commit violent depravities. A creature that's already predisposed toward these acts derives greater pleasure than before for such atrocities but receives no additional penalty or benefit, while a non-sapient creature is driven to become unnaturally violent in its actions (and over the course of weeks, becomes visibly corrupted by patches of strange fur, warty growths, unsightly teeth, or similar teratomas on its body). A sapient creature that isn't predisposed toward acts of depravity (likely including all PCs) takes an item penalty equal to the number of vile remnants they carry to saving throws against all magical effects that attempt to encourage such acts. Saving throws against spells like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qwlh6aDgi86U3Q7H]{Suggestion} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm} cast by creatures who attempt to push a PC into such acts, any affect by such creatures that attempts to control a PC, or certain specific effects mentioned in the text of this adventure would all be affected by this penalty. A creature with the holy trait reduces the overall item penalty imparted by this curse by 1, to a minimum penalty of 0.

A creature that's foolish enough to consume a vile remnant becomes fused to its curse, at which point the vile remnant remains lodged within the creature's body until the curse is removed from the creature with a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction} spell or similar magic, or upon the creature's death, whichever comes first. At this point, the vile remnant crawls or oozes its way out of the creature's body and flops, once again inanimate, onto the ground, where it waits to be claimed by a new carrier.

As long as you carry a vile remnant somewhere on your person, its curse does have a beneficial side: The power of its influence grants you a +1 item bonus to all saving throws against curses from other sources, as the vile remnant jealously wards against such encroachments on its territory. Unlike the item penalty, carrying multiple vile remnants does not increase this item bonus.

The base version of a vile remnant appears to be lifeless, but the whispering remnant periodically twitches and pulses as if it were alive.

Activate—Become As One 1 minute (concentrate, manipulate)

Effect By piling eight vile remnants in a heap and then concentrating upon the mound of cursed flesh for a minute, you cause the eight vile remnants to slither together and become a single whispering remnant. Once combined in this manner, the resulting whispering remnant cannot be thereafter split into individual vile remnants.

Activate—Hear My Words 2 (concentrate, manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Effect The vile remnant casts a DC 23 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IihxWhRfpsBgQ5jS]{Enthrall} spell to your specifications. Creatures that fail or critically fail to resist this spell perceive and remember the vile remnant in your hand as something commonplace to the region, such as a farming tool, book, or fresh-baked pie, for as long as they remain enthralled. If you don't take advantage of this to subtly guide any affected creatures toward undermining their society, the vile remnant can't be activated to Hear My Words again by you for 1 week. Additionally, the next time you sleep, you endure horrific nightmares and must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:23] save upon waking to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 24 hours (this is a mental effect).

Activate—Hide the Horror 10 minutes (manipulate)

Frequency once per year

Effect You hide the vile remnant somewhere that, in time, it is likely to be found. For the following four weeks, the vile remnant's evil seeps into the surrounding landscape, expanding its influence at a rate of 200 feet per day until it reaches its maximum emanation of 5,600 feet after 28 days. It continues to influence this area for another three weeks before going dormant—it must be recovered and rehidden later once this activation recharges to begin the cycle again. While the remnant's influence is active, any sapient creature that sleeps in the area experiences unsettling dreams of being stalked by monsters they can never quite see or evade. A creature that doesn't worship an unholy deity who experiences these dreams must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:23] save each time they rest to avoid awakening @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued}. On a critical failure, the creature awakens stupefied 1 as well; this condition remains until removed or until they are no longer fatigued, whichever comes first. Creatures who worship an unholy deity or follow a despicable philosophy are immune to this effect. Any skill checks made by such creatures when performing rituals performed in the affected area gain a +1 item bonus, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Uqj344bezBq3ESdq]{Nightmare} spells cast by them within the region have their save DCs increased by 1.

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JmlPFAbjPvbhhKeu]{Vile Remnant}; Level 7

Type @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.14kIZ6GRkAW8vZw8]{Whispering Remnant}; Level 13

A whispering remnant’s Hide the Horror aura expands at a rate of 500 feet per day for 28 days, and the DC’s for its Hear My Words and Hide the Horror activations increase to 30. It imparts a –9 item penalty to all saving throws against deplorable influences and a +3 item bonus to all saving throws against curses as long as it’s carried. Whispering remnants are incredibly rare, and their use is required in many vile rites, such as the one that brought down the curse on Castle Arudora. A whispering remnant gains the following additional activation.

Activate—Heed My Whispers 2 (concentrate, manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Effect The whispering remnant casts a DC 30 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.GP3wewkQXEPrLxYj]{Subconscious Suggestion} spell to your specifications. If the target of the spell fails or critically fails to save against this, they perceive and remember the whispering remnant as being a commonplace item. If you don’t suggest a course of action to the target that causes them to work at undermining their society, the whispering remnant shrieks horribly, but only in your mind—you take @Damage[10d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:30|basic] save), after which the whispering remnant cannot be activated again by you for 1 week.

Destruction A vile remnant can’t be destroyed, but a whispering remnant can be by hurling it into a powerful curse effect created by the deity associated with the remnant. This causes the whispering remnant to become reabsorbed into the deity’s otherworldly body and often has potent side effects on the surrounding region. Disposing of a whispering remnant in the soul vortex of Bastardhall (@UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.EPAmP1TdzmePRO9b]{area I}) after Caydserris has been defeated not only destroys the whispering remnant but helps bring the Bastardhall Curse to an end.

This long, scarf-like garment appears to be made of living vines on which a dozen black roses bloom. While the vines appear to be thorny, they lack the capability to puncture or scratch, allowing the garland to be worn comfortably as a scarf or belt. The scent of the black roses evokes faint feelings of melancholy and nostalgia to the living, but undead find the odor to be unnerving and distracting. As long as you have a graverose garland invested, it grants a +1 item bonus to Deception and Intimidation checks against undead.

Activate—To the Grave with You! 2 (emotion, fear, manipulation, mental)

Frequency once per day

Effect You lift some of the garland to your lips and blow, sending the scent of the black roses outward to target an undead creature you can see within 60 feet. The targeted undead becomes filled with the conviction that it belongs in its grave, and it must attempt a @Check[will|dc:19|options:inflicts:off-guard,inflicts:prone,inflicts:frightened,inflicts:fleeing|traits:emotion,fear,manipulation,mental] save against the following effects.

Failure The undead creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and is off-guard as long as it remains frightened.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3}, and the undead is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} as long as it remains frightened. If the undead knows of a nearby empty grave, it must flee toward that grave—if it enters the grave, it drops @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} into the grave and remains prone until it is no longer frightened.

Soulheart Starting Locations

To aid GMs in providing information to a PC when they activate the Kindler cameo’s ability to Sense Soulhearts, the locations of all 21 soulhearts hidden in Bastardhall are indicated on the maps with symbols. Don’t forget to account for verticality—the closest soulheart might be above or below the PC on a different floor of the castle. Remember, soulhearts found in regions of Bastardhall that the PCs haven’t yet unlocked cannot be detected by the Kindler cameo. Also, the closest soulheart to the PCs when they use this ability might not be the easiest one for them to reach, depending on the barriers and dangers between them.

Don’t worry too much about making sure that the soulheart you allow the PC to detect is actually the closest—the point of this ability is to help guide the PCs toward a goal, so if the soulheart you indicate ends up not being the closest one at the time of activation, that’s fine. Keep in mind as well that soulhearts carried by other PCs will largely render this ability useless—Sense Soulheart is primarily intended to help guide the PCs when they have already used their stores of soulhearts to bolster spirits.

Velicarn's Cursed Coin.name: Velicarn's Cursed Coin
Velicarn's Cursed Coin.text:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.nBSlq58UkK86jYOO]{Velicarn's Cursed Coin}

Item 7

  • Unique

  • Cursed

  • Invested

  • Occult

Usage held in 1 hand; Bulk L

This platinum coin was minted in Caliphas in the year 4192, the same year that Velicarn, the eponymous bastard of Bastardhall, was born. While the design of coins has changed in the 500 or so years since this one was minted, anyone who is at least an expert in Society recognizes that this coin's design resembles no known Ustalavic tradition—and in fact, when the coin became cursed on that vile night in 4213, its imagery forever changed. In the present day, one side of the coin depicts a distorted image of the Arudora family crest, while the other depicts a set of monstrous eyes peering through the cracks in a crumbling wall (identifiable as the religious symbol of Charg with a Religion check to [[/act recall-knowledge skill=religion dc=25]]).

The coin feels unusually heavy for being made of platinum, and no merchant will accept it as cash as a result. Most merchants and collectors who are presented with the coin have an instinctual distaste for its strange weight and slightly greasy feel. As soon as someone carries Velicarn's cursed coin for longer than a minute, it automatically becomes invested, fuses with that person, and continues to count against that character's invested items, even without being reinvested each day. As long as the coin is carried, sahkils prefer to target the coin's carrier with their attacks (although they are not forced to do so), often behaving as if they can smell the "stink of the Typhon Wheel" on them. Fortunately for a character cursed by this item, the coin has no further debilitating effects, save for when it is activated.

Activate—Daring or Dread 1 (manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Effect You [[/r 1dc#Velicarn's Cursed Coin]]{flip the coin}, with a 50/50 chance of getting heads or tails. If the result is heads, you become immune to fear effects for 1 hour. If the result is tails, you gain a –2 item penalty against fear saves for 24 hours. If it's after dark in Bastardhall when you activate Velicarn's cursed coin, you must twice check to determine if you get heads or tails, and you only get the heads result if both coin flips result in heads; otherwise, the result is tails.
