Carrion Angel.name: Carrion Angel
Carrion Angel.text:
Obscure and profane rites enable a blasphemer to transform a captured angel into an undead monstrosity known as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.4rQYgIPrbA83EDVC]{carrion angel}. With their decaying flesh, foul stench of decay, and broken wings crawling with flies, none would mistake a carrion angel for anything but the atrocity they are—that is, unless the carrion angel chooses to cloak themself in a more pleasant, illusory deception. A carrion angel is not controlled by their creator, yet they generally regard their creator as an ally. Most outlast their creators, at which point they seek their own evil agendas in the world. Similar undead atrocities created via sacrifices of other types of celestials exist, and have similar abilities to the carrion angel. Yet for whatever reason, carrion angels are the most well-known and commonly encountered of these rare horrors.

Blasphemous Choices

The typical carrion angel presented here represents the least powerful of their kind, an undead abomination created through vile rites involving an angel’s sacrifice to an evil deity. Yet sometimes, fallen angels seek undeath deliberately—not to avoid immortality, as do so many mortals, but simply to embrace an unwholesome and blasphemous new source of power. These carrion angels are often much more powerful than those who had no choice in their fate.

Middenworm.name: Middenworm
Middenworm.text:
Creepers of sewers and crawlers within urban dump sites, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.8esAIVj311p8wg7K]{middenworms} are dangerous scavengers. Eager to abandon their bottom-feeding ways, they’re known to attack living foes, for fresh blood is their favorite repast. A middenworm is unpleasant to look at, listen to, or smell: a greasy maggot-like worm with hooked jaws at one end that peel back the folds of its body when it bites, and a nest of long, red, blood-drinking tendrils at the other.

Giant Middenworms

Normally, a middenworm doesn’t grow much larger than a dog, as this smaller size affords them more mobility in the sewers they frequent. Yet rarely, when middenworms have more room to grow in an area that’s particularly infused with toxic magic or fiendish influences, these creatures can grow to enormous size.

Anophilex.name: Anophilex
Anophilex.text:
The sight of blood is frightening proof of another’s suffering, and when that blood is one’s own, that fear can turn to blinding terror. Such are the horrors that the skittering, constantly bleeding anophilex sahkil revels in. With a glistening, spiderlike body covered in pulsing sacs of blood caught amid tangles of thorny vines, an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.919AP58ceDMPI5IU]{anophilex}’s head is a freshly skinned skull with sharp fangs and patches of long black hair pulled back to tangle amid the thorns of their bodies. As an anophilex moves, their thorns rip and tear at their bloody blisters and bloated organs, yet the bleeding only flows back along their body to form new thorny lengths in a constant recreation that gives off an unsettling, gurgling susurrus.

An anophilex has little patience for subtlety or manipulation, preferring to skitter through or flap above battlefields, among refugees, or amid any area where the wounded gather, so they can spread fear and drink the wounded’s crimson pain.

About Sahkils

Sahkils are fiends associated with primal fears and phobic terrors that haunt mortal minds. They hail from the depths of the Ethereal Plane and serve sinister demigods known collectively as tormentors, such as Charg himself.

Mymnian.name: Mymnian
Mymnian.text:
A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.95TfQgYDh4rl6SgP]{mymnian} enjoys the unique fear and foolish, panic-induced acts that mortals display when confronted with what they fear to be ghosts. Be it a mymnian that uses their own abilities to mimic a haunted abode or one that settles into an area with actual ghosts, a haunted house under the watchful eye of one of these manipulative sahkils is never a safe place for the living.

Typically, a mymnian wears what appears to be a billowing gray cloak to look like an oversized humanoid figure, only to cast aside the cloak to reveal that their head and torso are a mass of humanoid and animal skulls, melted into a hideous conglomeration with each bony face looking outward in different directions.

They walk upon five long skeletal arms that end in bony, humanlike hands. And that cloak? Nothing less unsettling than long, rippling folds of leathery flesh that hang from their body like a cape.

Eerie Rumors

Towns that host a haunted house would expect most people to steer clear of them, but there’s always a reason for someone new to brave the terrors. Rumors might spread about lost treasures, some might dare friends to “just spend one night,” or others might seek to learn tantalizing secrets from the beyond; whatever the form, these lures are cultivated by a mymnian, eager to draw new victims into their playground.

Vinlach.name: Vinlach
Vinlach.text:
The @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.CzNZG7eukyjlg28r]{vinlach} represents the overwhelming fear of birds—the sharp beaks, the razored talons, the incessantly fluttering wings, the alien all-seeing eyes, and the haunting shrill cry of the raptor when it spots defenseless prey. They appear as a tangled mass of flapping whippoorwill wings, constantly kicking up dander and dust, with a “head” composed of dozens of shrieking whippoorwill heads, all merged together in a twittering knot of meat and bone, eyes peering in all directions at once. The amalgamation stalks about on four long, stork-like legs tipped with murderous talons, and while their body of wings wouldn’t seem to suggest it, they can use them to fly through the air with unnerving grace. Despite their bestial nature, vinlachs are quite intelligent and delight in tormenting sapient creatures, particularly those who have strong beliefs or faiths.

Psychopomp Blasphemers

While all sahkils descended from an initial group of blasphemous psychopomps who betrayed their calling and rebelled against Pharasma, the eerie vinlachs take this corruption one step further in their desecration of Pharasma’s sacred animal—the whippoorwill. They take particular delight in haunting fallen churches of Pharasma or serving priests who have turned their back on the Lady of Graves for more sinister patrons.

Soul Glutton.name: Soul Glutton
Soul Glutton.text:
In the mist-choked fens and smoke-clogged ruins of Abaddon dwell creatures made of solid vapor whose roiling bodies drift among the fogs and effluvia of that wasted realm. Among the most unsettling of those are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.G3D4rcYmVv4eusog]{soul gluttons}: drifting, ravenous monstrosities whose bodies shift and pulse like mist, yet are clammy and all too solid to the touch. While a soul glutton’s favored meal is (naturally) souls, they eagerly attack the living to feed upon their life essence, gulping down the souls as they perish.

Soul gluttons are particularly delighted to be drawn to worlds within the Universe, for here the souls are of a much wider variety of flavors than the twisted, tormented shades that populate Abaddon.

A soul glutton’s eagerness to feed on worldly souls makes them notoriously difficult to control when conjured—but a promise to let them free upon the world after performing a relatively small service is often enough to secure their fleeting loyalty to a short-lived cause.

Eaters of Soul

These creatures have an unnerving affectation—they enjoy knowing those they feed upon, and before consuming a soul will often take time to converse with it while it still lives, or via talking corpse if the creature is already dead. Conversations with healthy creatures hold very little interest to soul gluttons, as life tends to distort the truths they enjoy hearing about. To a soul glutton, the greatest truths can be learned by reading the mind of a creature at the moment it passes away.

Sludge Troll.name: Sludge Troll
Sludge Troll.text:
The lanky, greasy @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.L8qYcku10bEa1LhU]{sludge troll} always seems to look like they just slid out of a pool of noxious sewage or filthy swamp water, with their scaly hide dripping with oily fluids and crusty muck. While they possess the iconic underbite and tusks of the typical troll, their facial features are much more fishlike, with bulging eyes and fin-like ridges on their spine, brow, and forearms.

In addition to possessing prodigious regenerative qualities, sludge trolls are immune to diseases, and as a result, they often wallow and lair in areas infested with sickness for additional defenses. Tunnels and sewage outflows are their favored places to lurk in ambush, particularly if these areas see lots of traffic from underworld denizens.

Generally more stealthy and sneaky than the typical troll, a sludge troll roused to violence is as terrifying and impossible to ignore as any others of their kind.

Sewer Dwellers

While sludge trolls are often found dwelling in mires and bogs, they are also perfectly at home lurking in sewers and cisterns below urban areas. Their lanky limbs and ability to squeeze through smaller areas helps them navigate confines that might prove troublesome for other creatures of their size, yet sewer-dwelling sludge trolls are still careful to avoid attracting too much attention from those in positions of power in the city above.

Voldrak.name: Voldrak
Voldrak.text:
It seems like every lake in Ustalav of any considerable size has its own legend about a lake monster, but in the case of Lake Laroba, these legends have been fact for as long as anyone can remember. The lake’s denizen, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.ZNSDataoZlnuv8eP]{Voldrak}, was only rarely sighted in the days before the curse, despite entire expeditions of hopeful monster-watchers spending extensive hours on the lake.

Now, like all other creatures swept up by the Bastardhall Curse, Voldrak has grown worse. The lake monster torments anyone who dares ply the waters for too long.

He generally prefers to frighten or maim rather than kill, for this new Voldrak enjoys the knowledge that his horrific legend might spread.

Voldrak is a sleek, plesiosaur-like serpent, with four clawed flippers, deep- red eyes, and a long tail that ends in a single long rudder-like fin. His teeth are long and terrible and protrude over his lips even when his mouth is closed.

Voldrak's Fate

Before the curse, Voldrak was an elusive @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core-2.Actor.ZdQfNuQQjytFzuyd]{water orm} regarded by the Arudoras almost as a mascot or pet to such an extent that they worked his image into their family crest. After the curse, though, Voldrak became a much more aggressive and dangerous monster. While he’s unlikely to survive the events of Bastion of Blasphemies, Lake Laroba is deep, and who’s to say the lake monster’s ghost doesn’t survive in its depths after the PCs return home?

Aron Mordimus.name: Aron Mordimus
Aron Mordimus.text:
Aron Mordimus was orphaned at a young age when his parents, part of a trading expedition heading to Thrushmoor from the far side of Lake Encarthan, were lost at sea during a sudden storm. Infant Aron’s survival was a miracle; he was found on the island’s shore by a fisherman, crying but swaddled safe and secure in a lifeboat. He grew up as the adopted child of the fisherman, whose own family had perished a few years before during a similar storm, and took his adoptive father’s family name, Mordimus, as his own—along with the name his father gave him, Aron. His only clue to his heritage was the sheathed clan dagger the fisherman found in the swaddling. When Aron grew older and began to question why he looked so different from his father, elder Mordimus gave him this dagger and told the story of how he’d come into his life. To his surprise, his adopted son proclaimed him his true father, and while he has long been intrigued by the potential legacy of his clan dagger, he never looked into its history since, to him, he already had a family.

After his father passed away of natural causes, Aron did some traveling. During these travels, he became amazed at the variety of inns he encountered, and before long decided innkeeping would be his calling. He eventually settled in the small village of Maiserene and helped to build the inn there, Orm’s Rest, and there he still lived when the curse of Bastardhall changed everything.

Aron is a hearty-looking, middle-aged dwarf man with black hair and a short beard he wears in a more human style than dwarven. Though he has many interests, he loves nothing more than helping weary travelers relax with mugs of hot cider and the promise of a comfortable bed, and listening to tales of their travels. Once every year, on his “finding day” (the day his father found him adrift in that lifeboat, since he never learned his real birthday), he spends a few hours meditating and regarding his clan dagger, yet has never felt the need to investigate its history more. On the night of the curse, he perished among those who led the charge in burning the Laroba Bridge, after which his cursed soul was lured to the orchards he loved so much to endure centuries of torment (see area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.iKQ1sh7QyLC4On4P]{A21}).

Campaign Role

As Maiserene’s innkeeper, Aron’s role in this campaign is to provide the PCs with a safe place to rest and to help them recover from their adventures. He’s always eager to hear stories of what the PCs discover in Bastardhall. Once he physically manifests, he takes great pleasure in the restoration of his sense of taste and smell. He spends time with his old friend Banijer Greely trading recipes and meals—and in time, develops a romantic relationship with the merchant.

Side Quest

Before the curse fell, Aron often visited Bastardhall’s cellars to spend time with another dwarf he’d fallen in love with—the castle’s sommelier, Brensen Firecask. Once the PCs unlock the castle grounds, Aron realizes they might soon do the same for the cellars. At this point, he approaches the PCs with a request to find out what became of Brensen; he’s under no illusions that his lover lives and asks them to put his spirit to rest if he’s been transformed into a monster. If the PCs can provide Brensen an escape from the curse (see area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.O2hrZos99pNTSbdj]{C47}) and break the news to Aron, he sobs in relief and sadness but recovers quickly, vowing to build a lovely wine cellar in Orm’s Rest in his honor once things get back to normal. His overwhelming gratitude manifests a reward for the PCs, crystallizing ambient ectoplasm into a nourishing aeon stone; Aron is startled by this event, but gives the aeon stone to the PCs eagerly in thanks for the closure.

Reward

@UUID[Actor.BttiK1d0KUmufjfi]{Aron's Reward}

Grant the PCs 40 XP for completing this side quest.

Ausken Dast.name: Ausken Dast
Ausken Dast.text:
Ausken knew from a young age that he’d eventually become Maiserene’s sheriff. After all, his father was the sheriff, and his grandfather filled that role before him. So confident was he about his destiny that Ausken decided to start early by becoming both a bully and a snitch among the other children of the village. When one bit of bullying resulted in one of his targets nearly drowning, though, his parents (and particularly his father) were shocked and ashamed that their son would resort to such poor behavior.

Ausken’s father pulled some strings with the nobles and got his son accepted into the castle guard at a young age, hoping the structure and experience would help him learn respect and patience. The following few years proved to be just the thing for Ausken, who learned quickly that “my dad’s the sheriff” carried no weight with those inside the castle walls. He came out of this tough-love apprenticeship a better man, yet when his father died suddenly from an accidental fall while attempting to repair a roof in the village, Maiserene wasn’t initially welcoming of the new young sheriff. It took years, and the consequences of numerous poor choices, for Ausken to grow into the role and earn the trust and respect of the village... and then the curse came, and everything ended.

Ausken is in his early thirties, with a robust mustache, a hearty build, and a stern expression, yet that expression softens when he looks upon the town he spent the last several years of his life defending. When the curse fell, Ausken was the last villager to die, torn apart by monsters even as he fought to defend Maiserene’s ruins.

Campaign Role

Once his soul is restored, Ausken helps the PCs to keep their weapons and armor ready against the increasing dangers they’ll face in Bastardhall, and in time he can provide potent magical effects to both. Once he physically manifests, he often spends his time patrolling Maiserene and can serve to guide any remaining explorations of the haunted shore the PCs might have. He can guide them to areas that still need to be investigated and made safe from monstrous influence.

Side Quest

Soon after the PCs unlock the castle grounds, Ausken approaches to tell them of his time spent serving in the castle guard, likely when they’re resting or maintaining their gear. He can sketch out the rough layout of the castle grounds for the PCs and suggests that of all the locations therein, the armory (area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.mG5rb8xF7l3JNp75]{B7}) might be the safest place to hole up and rest if the PCs can’t make it back to Maiserene. His expression then grows introspective as he recalls the brief romance he had with another guard in training during that time. It’s a relief to him that she left the castle years before the curse fell to seek her destiny as an adventurer in distant lands, but if the PCs can check to see if the romantic pledge they’d carved into wood in the castle’s training yard (area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.srvDTVrA5ZcIuWjR]{B8}) still exists, he’d appreciate the tiny favor. If they ask where the carving was, his brow furrows and, in frustration, he says he can’t recall. If the PCs report back with the information, tears well in his eyes and he thanks them, not only for the report but for the flood of memories they restore to him as they do so. This gratitude causes the ambient ectoplasm nearby to crystallize into a runestone bearing a ready armor property rune. With a chuckle, he tells the PCs a somewhat embarrassing story about how his lover used just such a rune to quickly dress after a tryst, and in so doing managed to keep their affair secret from the guard captain (who frowned on fraternization). After this, he gives the runestone to the PCs, thanking them once more for the gift of memory they brought him.

Reward

@UUID[Actor.omi9oSLHsrhDW2p5]{Ausken's Reward}

Grant the PCs 40 XP for completing this side quest.

Banijer Greely.name: Banijer Greely
Banijer Greely.text:
Banijer was born and raised in Maiserene. As a child, he was precocious and willful, spending much of his youth avoiding his lessons and insulting mentor after mentor until, finally, he’d exhausted all goodwill and opportunities for apprenticeship and education in the village. He has the dubious honor of being the first of Maiserene’s native locals to serve prison time in the castle’s dungeon after he was caught in an ill-advised caper involving smuggling goods. His “partner” in the escapade, the castle’s own apothecary, Junth Rundel, betrayed him and sold him out to cover up his own criminal activities. Bitter and disillusioned after being released from prison several months later, Banijer left his home and spent the next several years of his life traveling Ustalav.

This time away from home was precisely what Banijer needed to find himself. During these years, he had more than a dozen serious (and not-so-serious) flings with men and women alike, but then he met and fell in love with the woman who would become his wife. When she became pregnant, the two decided to return to Maiserene to live a simpler life than the traveling merchant role Banijer had grown into. Upon his return, Banijer was overcome with waves of guilt and nostalgia as, for the first time, he understood the close-knit support and companionship he’d grown up among but had never appreciated.

Over the next 10 years, Banijer did his best to atone for his rebellious youth. His family grew, and he took over the duties of his family’s farm on the east shore of the isle. When the first man he’d apprenticed to died of old age, Banijer was shocked to learn the man had left him the village trading post in his will. Since that day, up until the night of the curse, Banijer spent every day working to bolster the town’s prosperity while seeing to it his children were raised with an appreciation for their home.

Banijer is a middle-aged human man with salt and pepper hair, a wiry frame, and a quirky style that heavily features mismatched colors. He’s eager to laugh and joke, but when he’s alone, his thoughts turn morose, and his expression takes on a haunted visage. On the night of the curse, Banijer raced back to the farmhouse where his family was hiding, then sacrificed himself in a desperate attempt to lure the monsters away from the home. Yet his death was only the start of his agony. His ultimate fate was perhaps the most tragic of all six of the town’s leaders, as Charg seized upon his childhood disdain for local life and forced him to watch from inside the monster the curse had turned him into as it slaughtered his family. Banijer remembers this with shame and a quiet fury but never speaks of it aloud.

Campaign Role

Banijer’s role in the campaign is simple—as the local trader, his influence and presence gives the PCs someone they can sell items to and purchase items from. He can also offer spellcasting services for standard prices. He’s always eager to talk about any treasures the PCs find while exploring, and once both he and Aron Mordimus physically manifest, the two swiftly rekindle their old friendship. This friendship eventually blossoms into a full-fledged romance after Aron helps Banijer come to terms with the cruelty he endured when his family perished.

Side Quest

Once the PCs unlock the castle grounds, Banijer tells them of the time he was put in prison and provides them with a rough sketch of areas @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.mJ7qNpJ3GNVNEVcR]{E1}–@UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.LPkJFQogdqN9LE0s]{E4} and @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.FBPDuStK6Zlej0n5]{E6}–@UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.8h6QErLBhi0Ro2tn]{E7} of the castle dungeon, should they ever find themselves down there (of course, Banijer isn’t aware of the current dangers in these areas). As he gives them the map, he pauses, then notes that as he tried to evade capture that fateful night, he lost the silver sickle his father had given him. At the time, he didn’t really care about it, but now he misses the sickle; he tells the PCs that if they find themselves down in the dungeon, “that two-faced Junth” likely found it and claimed it as his own. If the PCs find it and return it to him, he’s not only grateful, but the gratitude draws upon ambient ectoplasm to transform the sickle into a +1 striking extending silver sickle. Shocked, Banijer offers the sickle to the PCs as a reward. If they refuse, he’s grateful and thereafter provides his spellcasting services to them at no cost.

Reward

@UUID[Actor.y5Sl6hUf03q2OC7c]{Banijer's Reward}

Grant the PCs 40 XP for completing this side quest.

Esmira Vermidian.name: Esmira Vermidian
Esmira Vermidian.text:
Esmira came to serve as Maiserene’s schoolteacher not long after Raudltz and Alisendra’s first child, Jinnivere, was born. She initially applied for the position of castle au pair and tutor, but that job was taken by another (whom, in time, Esmira would befriend). Even though she didn’t get the position, she was so taken with the village of Maiserene that she decided to stay, taking on the role of assistant to the town’s aging schoolteacher. When that teacher passed away from natural causes a few years later, the job fell to her quite naturally, as the villagers had grown fond of her sense of humor and her skill at arcane magic.

Esmira is an elderly but spry Varisian woman with long gray hair and an expression that shifts from pleased delight to stern demand with practiced ease. She wears flowing schoolteacher’s robes and often paces while she talks.

Aside from delight and sternness, another expression that crosses her face is periodic sadness. On the night of the curse, Esmira helped gather the children into the schoolhouse to protect them, only to die with them as the roof burned and collapsed. While it takes her a bit to get over the fact that all of Maiserene’s children are long gone, she soon settles into her new role of aiding the PCs in determining what happened to cause the curse in the first place.

Campaign Role

Esmira can not only provide spellcasting services for the PCs, but she can also aid them in their research and investigation. She’s a wonderful conversationalist and is always eager to sit and chat with PCs about all manner of topics—although she prefers not to hear about the awful things that have developed in the castle. If the PCs haven’t figured out how to use the standing stones at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Ez53diEo41YhLat7]{A14}, yet, she can teach them how to @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Ez53diEo41YhLat7#meditate-among-the-stones]{Meditate Among the Stones}.

Side Quest

After the PCs unlock the castle grounds, Esmira approaches them to ask a favor. She talks about how she was sometimes called upon by the Arudoras to help substitute for the castle’s live-in au pair and tutor when she fell ill or had to travel, and of how much trouble both of the younger Arudoras—Augsten and Jinnivere—were to handle. She listens with horror but, perhaps, not much shock if the PCs eventually share with her what became of these two Arudoras.

Regardless, she notes that while her duties as a substitute instructor largely fell off in the years before the curse (as both children were, by then, adults), she did visit the au pair, Linisriel, frequently to have tea. They soon had built a friendship over the shared exertions of dealing with precocious Arudora children. While she knows Linisriel is likely long gone (if the PCs report to her about her transformation into a rakshasa, she’s shocked and saddened, but thankful her friend’s soul is now at peace), the last time she visited, she loaned Linisriel one of her favorite books—a tawdry romance called The Three Curious Elves. If the PCs come across this book, Esmira would be grateful for its return. She can describe to the PCs the castle grounds, as well as the route she took from the trophy room to Linisriel’s room in the private halls where she’s sure she left the book (describing the layout of areas @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.3hduGPZ55keA2HRA]{D15} to @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.78A34DGpyfbsAqFq]{D7c} to @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.ndtRFPlOc0RB3Vc5]{F2b} to @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.7sih5tt9N28Ni3qB]{F4}).

If the PCs return the book, she gasps in delight. At the same moment, her emotions crystallize the ambient ectoplasm into an accolade robe, which (after her surprise at its manifestation) Esmira eagerly gifts to the PCs in thanks.

Reward

@UUID[Actor.S5jUvqiPxQCNxF84]{Esmira's Reward}

Grant the PCs 40 XP for completing this side quest.

Ilana Greenbough.name: Ilana Greenbough
Ilana Greenbough.text:
Ilana Greenbough was born far from Ustalav, in a Varisian caravan traveling the routes along Varisia’s Lost Cost. This particular caravan had long integrated halflings into their traveling families, and their skills at artistry and on-the-road repair work came naturally to her as she grew older and learned the ways and complications of traveling folk.

Some time after reaching adulthood, tragedy struck when the caravan was ambushed by ogres—Ilana was the sole survivor. Eager to put distance between a land that now only brought back memories of sadness, she traveled east. It was chance that saw her eventually settle in Maiserene, a small town that charmed her with its mix of beautiful landscapes and stunning architecture.

Ilana is a vibrant halfling woman whose hairstyle changes often to match her daily whims. (Not quite as frequently as a gnome’s would, but she’s always trying out new things.) Traditional Varisian tattoos adorn her shoulders, arms, and back. She’s rarely seen without her leather toolbelt and a backpack filled with painting supplies—as she’s eager to point out, “You never know when inspiration might come knocking, or when that knocking might actually be something that needs a quick fix!” When the curse struck Castle Arudora, Ilana was a key element in planning how to destroy the Laroba Bridge with fire—Maiserene’s desperate attempt to contain the horrors after it became apparent the village was doomed. Her solution, jury-rigged trebuchet-like devices meant to fling bottles of flammable liquid, proved to be so effective that the bridge’s destruction was swift. Unfortunately, she didn’t live long after that realization; one of the unleashed monsters snatched her up and dropped her into the very fires she’d helped to ignite.

Campaign Role

Once she returns to her bench in Maiserene’s workshop, Ilana helps to ensure the site remains well-stocked for the PCs’ use and opens the location up for characters to help produce materials so that they can Earn Income, repair items, or even craft their own items. At your discretion, she could even craft items for the PCs, giving them one other way to shop for items beyond the trading post.

Side Quest

Once the PCs unlock the castle grounds, Ilana approaches them with a concern of hers. She tells them about an amazing art gallery in the reception halls she would visit as often as possible, and once that area unlocks, she urges the PCs to check whether it and the pieces on display within survived, or if it’s still being curated by someone (or something). More to the point, though, on the day before the curse struck, Ilana had been visiting the gallery to speak about potentially having one of her own paintings—a landscape of Castle Arudora—displayed in the gallery. She left her painting there with the gallery’s curator, Ilves Mondain, and while she doesn’t expect it to have survived all this time, if the PCs could look for it in the gallery, in Ilves’ office, or anywhere else, she would be grateful.

If the PCs later report to her about what became of the painting, Ilana is utterly astounded. Her pride at how her artwork managed to fight against the power of the curse spills over and influences ambient ectoplasm, resulting in the spontaneous creation of an envisioning aeon stone. She’s as surprised at this development as anyone and asks the PCs if they’d do her the honor of accepting it as a gift as thanks for returning with her painting. The telepathic images this aeon stone sends have the quality of a skilled impressionist painting—not enough to transmit fine details (such as writing), but much more aesthetic to look at than the typical childish sketches that most of these aeon stones produce.

Reward

@UUID[Actor.ntiB4CCaf67kLWpg]{Ilana's Reward}

Grant the PCs 40 XP for completing this side quest.

Shirail Animender.name: Shirail Animender
Shirail Animender.text:
Shirail’s parents impressed the importance of faith upon her from a young age, but they heavily tempered those lessons with an even greater focus on tolerance and acceptance. Her father, a priest of Shelyn, and her mother, a priestess of Pharasma, showed her the ways two very different beliefs could support each other and expand on the core tenets of each religion, so that when she came of age and became an adventurer, she had little difficulty finding a place among such an eclectic group.

Shirail appears as a beautiful elf woman whose expression always carries at least a hint of somber introspection, as if she carries unpleasant memories that are never far from her mind. When the curse struck the castle and the surrounding village, Shirail perished in the defense of the church, grimly standing against undead animated from the remains of her one-time flock until the forces of the curse overwhelmed her.

Once she began adventuring, Shirail’s presence and temperament helped to bolster her group’s teamwork and morale. Things were going fine, at least, until a tragic expedition into a haunted swamp in Versex left only Shirail alive among her group. Unable to singlehandedly transport the bodies of her companions back home to be properly buried according to their cultures and beliefs, Shirail cremated the three in a pyre she built there in the swamp. She stayed until the pyre was cool, then gathered their ashes before fleeing back home.

Her excitement of the adventuring lifestyle waned after that, and when an opportunity arrived to serve as the caretaker and priestess for a new church of Pharasma, it was easy for her to choose to join the villagers of Maiserene. She was ready to stay put and really serve a community.

Campaign Role

Shirail’s power over life and death has grown stronger now that she’s experienced death herself, and her support can help to restore PCs who have perished. She can also perform spellcasting services for the PCs for the standard prices, and can eventually teach certain formulas for a few rituals to the PCs as well.

Side Quest

Shirail kept her companions’ ashes with her for a time, but after she accepted a post at Maiserene and struck up a friendship with the castle’s priestess of Pharasma, she secured permission to have her friends’ ashes interred in urns in the castle crypt. On the night of the curse, as she defended her church, she was attacked and mortally wounded by distorted, ghostly mockeries of her adventuring companions’ ghosts. As she lay dying, she watched the three ghosts mock and deride her before retreating upward to the old temple of Pharasma in the southwestern portion of Castle Arudora above. Shirail had heard rumors in the months leading up to the night of the curse that an Arudora had been at work restoring the temple—but not to the worship of Pharasma. That night confirmed her fears that the new patron of the castle temple was a sinister deity indeed. Once the PCs unlock the fallen temple, Shirail approaches them and relates this story, asking them, when they can, to explore the old temple and find out if the spirits of her three adventuring companions remain within—and if so, to put them finally to rest by defeating the ghosts and bringing their urns of ashes back here to be placed in places of honor in Maiserene’s temple. Once the PCs do so and bring news to her, Shirail’s gratitude triggers a crystallization of the ambient ectoplasm into a set of devoted vestments, which she encourages the PCs to claim to aid them on their continuing adventures. These vestments’ themes and decor shift to match the faith of the PC who wears them.

Reward

@UUID[Actor.hXJiPgMtXsiKOq3m]{Shirail's Reward}

Grant the PCs 40 XP for completing this side quest.

1 Research Point Tasifinie Arudora was the great-grandmother of the castle’s patriarch when the curse took hold. She died of spider bites in her bedroom in 4148 when a swarm burst from a rare houseplant.

3 Research Points Although Tasifinie died well before the curse descended, rumors persisted that her ghost haunted the room where she perished. The experiences of those who ventured inside were so visceral that the room was sealed within a year of her death, never to be used again.

5 Research Points Tasifinie was well-regarded by many of the people of Varno, and her funeral was the most well-attended event ever held at Castle Arudora. Her grieving husband had his legendary sword, Fearcutter, interred with her in the crypt below the castle’s temple, proclaiming that while he could no longer protect his beloved, at least his sword could follow her into the afterlife. (See @UUID[Actor.t7pt2BlRjyDMdeZ1]{Tasifinie Sarcophagus})

Zasha Arudora.text:
Zasha Arudora

Research 6

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.YpwRFAWIviqL68gu#research]{Maiserene’s memories} (haunted shore), @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.HiXOGKLx6aYdwEd4#research]{Arudora library} (area F1)

1 Research Point Zasha Arudora was the grandmother of the castle’s patriarch when the curse took hold. She died in 4152 giving birth to her second child, who also perished during this tragic event.

4 Research Points Zasha’s soul likely moved on before the curse struck, and she is unlikely to maintain a supernatural presence in Bastardhall.

7 Research Points Zasha’s relationship with her husband, Irrokcis, was one of convenience and financial security, not one of love. After she bore her first son, Demiterus, she and her husband grew increasingly apart. He barely reacted to her death, and he had her remains shipped back to her family in Carrion Hill rather than burying them in the Arudora crypts, for reasons he never disclosed.

Augsten Arudora.name: Augsten Arudora
Augsten Arudora.text:
Augsten Arudora

Research 7

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.YpwRFAWIviqL68gu#research]{Maiserene’s memories} (haunted shore), @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.2Ybt21NaXnVfBBQl#research]{oracle’s observations} (area C14), @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.LcfWUDiRFsSPbt9t#research]{Laroba bar ledger} (area D24)

1 Research Point Augsten Arudora was the youngest of two Arudora siblings and the only recognized son of the castle’s lord and lady when the curse took hold in 4213. He and several other members of the family went missing at that time.

3 Research Points Augsten still haunts Bastardhall. He rules over the cellars; somewhere in this portion of the castle, he can be found and confronted in battle.

5 Research Points Augsten was vexed by feelings of insecurity and inferiority. In addition to teasing his sister for her awkwardness, he bullied the castle servants and guards. He spent an increasing amount of time in the castle cellars micromanaging both groups, berating and even beating them for insignificant reasons, yet his father, Raudltz, could never be bothered to correct his son’s behavior. Augsten was rarely seen without his loyal pet tiger, Skirrin.

7 Research Points The servants and guards took to calling Augsten “Little Lord Augie” behind his back. The few times someone called him this to his face, Augsten flew into a blind rage that often confused him to such an extent that he’d lash out at anyone nearby.

10 Research Points Augsten never visited his personal tower after he became an adult, leaving behind broken toys and discarded remnants from a more idyllic youth. Among these old belongings was an eye of fortune he inherited from his grandfather on his mother’s side, which he never had an interest in using. Instead, he stuffed the magic eye patch into his mattress in the tower room just to vex his mother by saying he lost it. (See @UUID[Actor.MwnJ1wN2DU6SGDRa]{Mattress} loot actor)

Alisendra Arudora.name: Alisendra Arudora
Alisendra Arudora.text:
Alisendra Arudora

Research 8

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.YpwRFAWIviqL68gu#research]{Maiserene’s memories} (haunted shore), @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.SORum03a5tQWw4Xp#research]{Arth’s journals} (area D31), @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.8h6QErLBhi0Ro2tn#research]{Junth’s blackmail material} (area E7)

1 Research Point Alisendra Arudora was the matriarch of Castle Arudora when the curse took hold in 4213. She and several other members of the family went missing at that time.

3 Research Points Alisendra still haunts Bastardhall. She rules over the reception halls.

5 Research Points Alisendra fancied herself the “face” of the Arudoras and enjoyed throwing extravagant galas of all types for a wide range of visitors to the castle. She spent the majority of her time mingling with guests in the reception halls or spying on them from afar. A sure way to draw her out into a confrontation is to disrupt any events taking place in the reception halls—or, even better, to steal attention away from her at these events.

7 Research Points The surest way to distract and undermine Alisendra was to steal her guests’ attention during her parties. Her favorite rooms in reception to hold these events were the banquet hall, the ballroom, the trophy hall, the overlook known as Temple’s View, and a room on the second floor that was outfitted to perform seances.

10 Research Points Alisendra still pines for her first lover, a man named Vittorio Vancaskerkin, who perished a year before her marriage to Raudltz. Rumor holds that a voice-activated magical lock in her tower can be bypassed by speaking his full name.

The Bastardhall Curse.name: The Bastardhall Curse
The Bastardhall Curse.text:
The Bastardhall Curse

Research 9

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[.FHoSc4ZgjbMcE5dl#research]{lucid nightmares} (anywhere, see Resting), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.XdkSCjX3BA3dp5sE#research]{spectral Bastardhall model} (area A6), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.FuifNpUpaAG0LzlR#research]{Lucinero’s curse theories} (area A12), @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.Wph54WLEpDPGxJ06#research]{Zizminarial’s discoveries} (area B12), @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.CSZBdjguWV1HWdLb#research]{Madame Skerzana’s investigation} (area D9), @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mp2jSvvSVejhua2M#research]{speak to the spirits} (area D30f)

0 Research Points Bastardhall has been cursed for over 500 years, returning once every century to plague the land. Each time, the mysterious Black Coach rides out to doom what seems to be a random assortment of people it comes across, either inviting them to ride back to Bastardhall (after which they are never seen again) or leaving them to face an unexpected and apparently random death by the end of the month. The PCs automatically know this information as the campaign begins.

2 Research Points Whatever the source of the curse might be, it must involve powerful magic indeed to affect a castle the size of Bastardhall. The curse traps those inside it from leaving, be they living or otherwise, including the PCs! Lifting the curse is likely the only way to escape.

4 Research Points This is no mortal curse, and lifting it will require more than a single spell or ritual. Whatever malevolence powers it must be undone in stages once the entire castle is forced into reality, weakening the heart of the curse so that, in time, it can be struck down. The curse’s source seems to be tied to fiends of fear known as sahkils—it’s likely worshippers of a sahkil demigod triggered the event centuries ago.

6 Research Points Those within Bastardhall experience a self-contained reality—though it seems like they are still on Golarion, they’re in a remote reach of the Ethereal Plane from which escape is impossible without the use of plane-traveling magic. Physical manifestations of the curse are hidden throughout Bastardhall: foul clots of flesh, fur, and bone known as vile remnants. Seeking out these remnants is dangerous, but it’s also likely necessary to end the curse. Gathering these manifestations together concentrates their power but makes it easier to keep them from those who would misuse them. If a safe place could be found to store them, their influence could be minimized. (See @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.iQLEbANowf4fT8hK]{Vile Remnant} for more information.)

8 Research Points The Bastardhall Curse is only the most powerful curse in the castle. There are many minor curses that the PCs might become afflicted by during encounters with certain creatures or hazards, yet these curses all have similar underpinnings. At this point, the party’s understanding of the Bastardhall Curse grants them a +2 circumstance bonus to all checks made to counteract any of these lesser curses.

10 Research Points The source of the curse is a powerful demigod—a sahkil tormentor named Charg. The vile remnants hidden throughout the castle are fragments cast off from his body, and while gathering them does concentrate their power and influence, doing so may play a significant role in removing the curse.

12 Research Points The PCs’ understanding of the curses of Bastardhall grows further; they now gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all saving throws against curse effects while in Bastardhall.

14 Research Points Many of those who were in the castle when the curse took hold were transformed into monsters, and while they might retain some distorted memories of their previous lives, it’s been far too long for them to be saved and returned to their previous forms. Slaying the monsters they’ve become releases their souls into the Afterlife—the one sure way for these long-suffering victims to be given peace.

18 Research Points Key to the curse’s power are the growing number of Arudora souls trapped within Bastardhall. The Black Coach, when it rides every 100 years, seeks out any living descendants of this line, most of whom don’t realize they have lineages linked to the Arudoras. Their ignorance doesn’t save them, however, and once the Black Coach finds them, they are either brought back to become monsters or meet with accidents and die soon thereafter. Regardless, their souls end up trapped somewhere below Bastardhall in a place known as the soul vortex (see @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.EPAmP1TdzmePRO9b]{Soul Vortex}). Some time soon, when the last Arudora soul has been collected, Bastardhall will return to Golarion for good, and Charg’s influence across central Avistan will spread with devastating swiftness.

21 Research Points The PCs’ understanding of the curses of Bastardhall grows, and the party’s circumstance bonus to saves against curses in Bastardhall increases to +4.

Dazerien Arudora.text:
Dazerien Arudora

1 Research Point Dazerien Arudora was the nephew of the castle’s patriarch when the curse took hold. He and several other members of the family went missing at that time.

3 Research Points Dazerien still haunts Bastardhall. He rules over the dungeon and likely dwells somewhere near the old torture chamber.

5 Research Points Dazerien was always a troubled man, and his reputation as a sadist preceded him when he moved into Castle Arudora with his mother in 4208. The servants were warned to avoid catching his eye or annoying him—an easier task once Dazerien began to spend most of his free time down in the castle dungeon, where rumors held that he kept a small group of unfortunate vagabonds he’d captured as long-term torture victims.

7 Research Points Dazerien enjoys prolonging torments, hunting other men and women as if they were game, and torturing the weaker allies of stronger foes, yet he hates to feel pain himself—particularly that brought on by cold. It was rumored that he lost a few toes to frostbite after his father forced him to march dozens of laps barefoot through the snow around the family estate as punishment for brutalizing one of the house servants. Today, Dazerien much prefers the heat and grows unusually agitated in the cold.

10 Research Points Dazerien spent only the first week of his time in the castle in his room upstairs in the private halls. He left a gift from his mother, a suit of elven chain, wrapped in a green felt sheet therein; he never wore the armor because it gave him a rash. (See @UUID[Actor.R7aDKBFq4pqRWiC4]{Felt Sheet} loot actor).

Florin Kindler.name: Florin Kindler
Florin Kindler.text:
Florin Kindler

Research 10

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mp2jSvvSVejhua2M#research]{speak to the spirits} (area D30f), @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.k9ECGjicvbLkrZvs#research]{commune with spiritual echoes} (area J2)

2 Research Points Since Florin didn’t appear with the PCs when they became trapped in Bastardhall, it’s likely she was drawn deeper into the castle’s clutches and needs their help to escape it.

5 Research Points Florin Kindler has indeed been captured by the Bastardhall Curse. It’s not too late to save her, but doing so will require discovering the curse’s source and destroying it.

8 Research Points As the last of the Arudora line, Florin occupies a special place in the plans of the malevolent entities who dwell here, but she can still be rescued. If the PCs haven’t learned Caydserris’s name yet, they do so now and discover he is the one keeping her captive. More importantly, Florin herself now knows the PCs are coming to save her, and can potentially provide assistance in the final battle against Caydserris when the time comes (see @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.dlphikkFc8PSQFfk]{The Floating Tower}).

Raudltz Arudora.name: Raudltz Arudora
Raudltz Arudora.text:
Raudltz Arudora

Research 10

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.YpwRFAWIviqL68gu#research]{Maiserene’s memories} (haunted shore), @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.8h6QErLBhi0Ro2tn#research]{Junth’s blackmail material} (area E7), @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.aZ25PpW3PeKFYrD3#research]{speaking with the children} (Chapter 6)

1 Research Point Raudltz Arudora was the patriarch of Castle Arudora when the curse took hold in 4213. He and several other members of the family went missing at that time.

3 Research Points Raudltz still haunts Bastardhall. He rules over the private halls, where he sees himself as something of a father figure to many others who dwell here. He calls these occupants his “children,” and they’ll swiftly come to his aid if they aren’t distracted, defeated, or otherwise dealt with first.

5 Research Points Raudltz had many hobbies, among them taxidermy, collecting art, and reading salacious novels, but his greatest love has always been astronomy. He converted the old sun room on the top floor of the private halls into a well-equipped observatory, where he spent many of his nights. He was a notorious philanderer until he settled down and married Alisendra, but he was rumored to have carried on a last-minute fling with an actress named Yasmerra during the final months before his wedding.

7 Research Points Raudltz took immense pride in his ancestry and legacy as an Arudora and spoke often of wanting to ensure that his children would carry on the family’s honor. Whispers that he had at least one, if not many, illegitimate children were often whispered, but never in Raudltz’s presence—each time he heard such rumors, he flew into a sputtering fit of anger that threw off his concentration and fully soured his mood. Today, Raudltz is a vampire, and those who serve under him as “children” are previous victims turned into vampires as well.

10 Research Points Raudltz’s tower served as yet another observatory; here, he stashed some powerful magic scrolls in his telescope (see @UUID[Actor.Ev1DF79riKXOeJl1]{Hidden Telescope Slat}). He also had a bastard son named Velicarn with his lover Yasmerra, and he murdered her when she confronted him with this truth before sending his bastard away to be raised in an orphanage. Her remains were never found.

Ryhasphinea Arudora.name: Ryhasphinea Arudora
Ryhasphinea Arudora.text:
Ryhasphinea Arudora

Research 11

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.YpwRFAWIviqL68gu#research]{Maiserene’s memories} (haunted shore), @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.Mcpm8IomhSfb7Idn#research]{Ryhasphinea’s belongings} (area F10), @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.tbuXpUsjFaPXpEM2#research]{Ryhasphinea’s letters} (area F18)

1 Research Point Ryhasphinea Arudora was the elder sister of the castle’s patriarch when the curse took hold in 4213. She and several other members of the family went missing at that time.

3 Research Points Ryhasphinea still haunts Bastardhall. She rules over the fallen temple, where she hides behind several layers of protection and guardians in the central cathedral.

5 Research Points Ryhasphinea’s worship of Urgathoa was an open secret, and while the servants of Castle Arudora opposed her intention to rebuild the fallen temple as a house of worship for the goddess of undeath, they could do little to oppose her since none of the other Arudoras seemed to mind.

7 Research Points Ryhasphinea is disgusted by Pharasma and Shelyn, the traditional divine patrons of the castle. This disgust could, potentially, be used against her.

10 Research Points Ryhasphinea’s tower served her as a private shrine. She kept a +2 greater striking keen unholy dagger there, but the dagger carries a bloodbiter curse that affects anyone who isn’t a worshipper of Urgathoa. (See @UUID[Actor.jxcxlRfQRjTeJaWC]{Tower Altar}).

Caydserris Arudora.name: Caydserris Arudora
Caydserris Arudora.text:
Caydserris Arudora

Research 12

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[.FHoSc4ZgjbMcE5dl#research]{lucid nightmares} (anywhere, see Resting), @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.mp2jSvvSVejhua2M#research]{speak to the spirits} (area D30f)

2 Research Points Caydserris Arudora was a notorious oracle who came to Ustalav in early 4709 and, over the course of two years, made a name for himself as a ruthless collector of old documents and strange occult objects. A major suspect in several murders throughout eastern Ustalav, he vanished in 4711.

5 Research Points Caydserris was living in Korvosa at the beginning of Queen Ileosa’s reign, eking out a living as a petty criminal and fully ignorant of his family lineage. During the blood veil plague, he experienced a frightening vision that revealed him to be one of the last living Arudoras. This is what drove him to become an oracle of ancestors and to travel to Ustalav, where he spent a few years honing his talents and gathering resources before he paid a visit to the ruins of Bastardhall in 4711, only to vanish without a trace.

7 Research Points Caydserris was a devotee of the sahkil tormentor Charg. He believed that one of his ancestors also venerated the so-called Typhon Wheel, and that the demigod was in part responsible for what happened to Bastardhall.

10 Research Points Caydserris lives on in Bastardhall and is now its current ruler, although very few of those who dwell within it realize this. He dwells in its highest tower but can’t be confronted until the curse has been picked apart. Once all Arudora descendants’ souls have been fully absorbed by Bastardhall, he’ll be able to phase the castle back onto Golarion permanently, transforming it into a bastion for the worship of Charg and rendering much of the region inhospitable to all others.

Irrokcis Arudora.name: Irrokcis Arudora
Irrokcis Arudora.text:
Irrokcis Arudora

Research 12

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.YpwRFAWIviqL68gu#research]{Maiserene’s memories} (haunted shore), @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.HiXOGKLx6aYdwEd4#research]{Arudora library} (area F1)

1 Research Point Irrokcis Arudora was the grandfather of the castle’s patriarch when the curse took hold in 4213. It’s believed he perished of a mysterious disease in 4189, but no confirmations of his death were ever made public.

3 Research Points Irrokcis was an accomplished spellcaster, and his knowledge of occult magic was extensive. Rumors that he was a witch who served a sinister patron were popular topics during his lifetime, particularly in the years leading up to his reported death in 4189.

5 Research Points Irrokcis was the one who discovered his mother’s body after she’d been bitten to death by spiders. Ever since then, the man’s imperious nature and intimidating facade always cracked when in the presence of even a single spider.

7 Research Points Irrokcis did not die. Instead, he bargained with sinister forces to escape death to become a powerful undead, then continued to “live” on deep underground in the castle’s vault. He can likely be found there still, working on mysterious experiments.

10 Research Points Irrokcis became a lich and kept his soul cage in his tower even though he spent most of his time far below in the castle vault. His ritual to become a lich required him to commit several atrocities against his own family—abducting and imprisoning his father Eragayl, then later murdering him and his son Demiterus. While Eragayl was already presumed to be dead by the time he was murdered, Irrokcis had to set up a smokescreen for Demiterus and Neesha, who became collateral damage when she tried to save her husband. He staged what seemed to be a boating accident to explain their fates.

Velicarn.name: Velicarn
Velicarn.text:
Velicarn

Research 13

  • Unique

  • Occult

Research Checks @UUID[.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n#research]{Recall Knowledge} (anywhere), @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.OV17X9YalFG6v52z#research]{speaking to Lavinia} (area C42), @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.YpwRFAWIviqL68gu#research]{Maiserene’s memories} (haunted shore)

2 Research Points A mysterious stranger named Velicarn visited Castle Arudora on the evening the curse struck. He was a young human man who wore threadbare aristocratic attire without any obvious family affiliation.

4 Research Points Velicarn was an illegitimate son of Raudltz and an actress named Yasmerra. He sought to confront his father after he bribed Lavinia, a scullery maid. (This result reveals additional information about Lavinia’s encounter with him and how she led him up to the Arudora Library, as detailed in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.OV17X9YalFG6v52z]{C42}).

6 Research Points Bastards in this part of Ustalav were often ridiculed by the aristocracy, such that many opted to keep their scandalous heritage secret. It’s likely Velicarn’s spirit retains this sense of shame even now. One might be able to throw him off his guard by either using this knowledge to ridicule him or by showing him compassion and sympathy.

8 Research Points Velicarn is the mysterious coachman. He, the coach, and the monstrous horses who draw it are all one creature, and while they appear to be solid, they are in fact a ghostly spirit known as a death coach—the PCs can attempt a @Check[religion|dc:36|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about his powers at this point (see @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.weLjvcmjY81S9CV9]{Velicarn (Death Coach)} for his statistics). This check drops to @Check[religion|dc:32|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] if it’s made in his presence.

How to Use this Guide.name: How to Use this Guide
How to Use this Guide.text:
Welcome to the Bastion of Blasphemies Adventure Path! This Player’s Guide will help you prepare for a campaign where you become trapped in a sprawling, cursed castle filled with horrors and nightmares. You begin at 5th level, and by the time your adventure ends, you’ll be 13th or perhaps even 14th level.

This campaign uses Pathfinder’s remastered rules, so all you need to play is Pathfinder Player Core (or Pathfinder Player Core 2) and a character sheet. With your Game Master’s permission, you can also use other Pathfinder rulebooks, campaign setting books, and accessories to customize your character. In particular, you should be familiar with the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.zkQJzslkiNQuUuKd]{Research} subsystem rules.

On the following categories, you’ll find specific advice to help you create a new character for Bastion of Blasphemies.

@UUID[.xPrmHz0RN9fWeIwy]{The Legend of Bastardhall:} This section introduces you to the cursed castle of Bastardhall, where this entire Adventure Path takes place, and describes why you’ve come to this legendary location.

@UUID[.i4xbVCPyTA0UDZiE]{Character Suggestions:} This section provides guidance for creating a 5th-level character that fits seamlessly into this campaign. Though you’re free to make any kind of character you like, taking the following suggestions into consideration will help you get the most out of this campaign.

Before Bastardhall

As touched on later in this Player’s Guide, Bastion of Blasphemies can be played with PCs who have already gone through previous published adventures set in Ustalav, starting with “Secrets of the Unlit Star” from the new Pathfinder Beginner Box and following those in Pathfinder Adventure: Troubles in Grayce Adventure Anthology. Playing these first will bring your PCs up to 5th level—perfect to begin their long stay in a cursed, haunted castle!

The Legend of Bastardhall.name: The Legend of Bastardhall
The Legend of Bastardhall.text:
Known to some as “the Bastion of Blasphemies,” Bastardhall is a sprawling castle located on an island in Lake Laroba in eastern Ustalav. It isn’t far from the West Sellen River, the main river trade route that links northern Ustalav, western Numeria, Sarkoris, and western Mendev.

Known historically as Castle Arudora (named after the influential family that once dwelt in its halls), Bastardhall is a notorious haunted castle that is the subject of many stories told throughout the Inner Sea region. Over five centuries ago, in 4213 AR, the arrival of an unexpected guest who carried a swaddled bundle was followed by the sudden spread of a perpetual shroud of mists and the fall of a dreadful curse that cut Castle Arudora off from the rest of the world. Since then, the mists surrounding Bastardhall clear only once per century to reveal a castle that has grown larger in size. At this time, a sinister black coach rides across a spectral bridge to the mainland in search of unlucky passengers. Those who board the coach are brought back to Castle Arudora and are never heard from again, while those who deny the coach’s invitation invariably end up dead not long after refusing its call.

The black coach last crossed to the mainland not too long ago, in 4713 AR, and the locals who vanished during that night are still missed and mourned in nearby villages and hamlets. The daughter of one of those missing people has since grown up, becoming an obsessed woman named Florin Kindler. Florin has spent the few years since she came of age relentlessly researching Bastardhall, its curse, the Arudora family line, and those who have been taken by the black coach over the past five centuries. Her efforts recently paid off.

Florin believes she’s found a way to enter the cursed castle without being carried into its misty halls by the black coach, yet she is no adventurer willing to brave its dangers alone—and that’s where you come in. Setting out from Grayce, she’s chosen your group of PCs to accompany her on a trip to the far side of Ustalav, where she hopes to explore the ruins, uncover the castle’s secrets, and maybe give herself—and countless others—closure by discovering what happened to all those who have been taken over the years.

What You Know About Bastardhall.name: What You Know About Bastardhall
What You Know About Bastardhall.text:
When this campaign begins, your group has already joined up with Florin Kindler to serve as guards, advisors, and traveling companions on her journey to the mysterious ruins of Bastardhall. During your travels, she’s shared what she knows about Bastardhall with you, though your PCs might already have heard some of these legends themselves.

For most of each century, Bastardhall stands in ruins on an island in the middle of Lake Laroba in eastern Ustalav, but it mysteriously rebuilds itself for a short period of time exactly once per century. On these occasions, a mysterious black coach rides out from beneath its shadow in search of passengers to bring back to the castle. Those who accept the invitation vanish, while those who deny it soon meet horrible fates. Florin Kindler lost her parents during the most recent manifestation of the castle’s curse a few years ago, and she’s eager to explore the ruins to see if she can put a reason to the family tragedy that has defined her life.

Your PCs also know that Bastardhall was once known as Castle Arudora, and that it was named so after a family of retired adventurers (turned aristocrats) who lived there. They dwelt there until a mysterious event just over 500 years ago brought a mysterious and devastating curse down upon the structure and all those inside it.

Each PC should have their own reasons for accompanying Florin on her quest, be they purely mercenary, motivated by curiosity, or perhaps simply their bond of friendship with Florin. The custom backgrounds that appear on page 8 of this Player’s Guide provide built-in reasons, but even if your PC isn’t using one of them, check them out for inspiration. They may help you decide why your character has agreed to accompany Florin on her quest!

Names and Places.name: Names and Places
Names and Places.text:
The following are important people and places mentioned in this guide.

Arudora Family: The family who once dwelt in the sprawling castle known now as Bastardhall.

Bastardhall: A legendary cursed castle on an island in the middle of Lake Laroba in eastern Ustalav.

Florin Kindler: An obsessed woman who hopes to find answers about what happened to her parents after they were visited by the black coach of Bastardhall.

Ancestries.name: Ancestries
Ancestries.text:
Any common ancestry from Player Core is appropriate for Bastion of Blasphemies. While the uncommon ancestries in Player Core 2 should all work fine in this campaign as well, keep in mind that none of these ancestries are particularly well-represented or well-known in Ustalav. Still, since this entire Adventure Path takes place in and around Bastardhall, uncommon choices like these won’t have many issues in play—chat with your GM if you want to play one of these uncommon ancestries.

Thematically, certain versatile heritages fit better than others in Bastion of Blasphemies due to the campaign’s horror-heavy themes. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.heritages.Item.EKY9v7SF1hVsUdbH]{Changelings}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.heritages.Item.UaD5VDoFlILEmbyz]{dhampirs}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.heritages.Item.ZZKZkeSP5TuT62IA]{duskwalkers} are all in this category, as are certain lineages of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.heritages.Item.1oLMOmLpurfWTTff]{nephilim}. Talk with your GM if you want to play one of these versatile heritages—they may have additional advice or know of certain options that might not be appropriate to choose based on events to come in the Adventure Path.

Bastardhall is a sprawling place that features many wide-open chambers and hallways. Large ancestries will still periodically find themselves inconvenienced by doors as well as some halls that were built with the expectation that those who’d traverse them would be human-sized, but none of these inconveniences are insurmountable.

The majority of Bastion of Blasphemies takes place on land, so ancestries who depend on water may face additional challenges. Aquatic ancestries will struggle in this campaign and may even be frustrated by the fact that Lake Laroba is used as a barrier that keeps the PCs trapped on the island atop which Bastardhall sprawls. Though it might seem fun to play such an ancestry near a lake, and though “swimming to safety” might seem like a wise move, your PCs swiftly learn that it isn’t.

Finally, fully undead ancestries are not appropriate for this campaign. If you’re eager to play an undead ancestry, consider instead playing a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.heritages.Item.UaD5VDoFlILEmbyz]{dhampir} or a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.heritages.Item.ZZKZkeSP5TuT62IA]{duskwalker}—or simply set that concept aside for a different campaign.

Classes.name: Classes
Classes.text:
Most classes are appropriate for Bastion of Blasphemies, particularly those that are self-sufficient and don’t require external support. Still, some are more thematically relevant than others.

Clergy: Bastardhall is a haunted and cursed castle, and that means you can expect to face plenty of undead foes, a fair number of fiends, and other unholy terrors. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.rebppVgBVi8J6TT2]{Champions}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.N4ABcd6CcCbqmw3x]{clerics}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.8ElntNAGahQka70r]{druids}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.bqaqOx3naiwTozBX]{oracles}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.fYJruhQfzs4dj0mp]{witches}, and others who excel at opposing such supernatural forces will find plenty to do in most encounters. Likewise, their abilities to aid other PCs in recovering from battle or handling afflictions—particularly curses—can be an important resource. Of special note to druids and other nature-themed classes is that there’s not a lot of wilderness exploration in Bastion of Blasphemies. Early in the campaign, the ability to subsist in the wild can be helpful, but as the Adventure Path progresses, you’ll want to focus more on your role as a healer or as one of the following categories.

Infiltrators: In addition to the numerous foes that lie in wait in the castle, there are many haunts, traps, and secrets to uncover. Characters like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.gdEmPPRYhRai7I1N]{rangers}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.u4qPrDRBagxG9wj8]{rogues}, and others who excel at handling hazards or at exploring the unknown are always useful when navigating yet another section of Bastardhall’s halls. Note that there isn’t a lot of terrain variance in Bastion of Blasphemies, so terrain-based options like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.sgo7J9BVofBqwlsF]{Favored Terrain} aren’t great choices for this campaign.

Researchers: A central premise of this campaign is the discovery, and subsequent research, of many seemingly disparate clues. One of your goals is to piece together the hidden history of Bastardhall, but it’s also crucial that you arm yourselves with the knowledge you’ll need to escape the cursed castle. Characters like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.Om4e4tsgNWrComie]{alchemists}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.Tz0NWVqhZyt8EyUV]{bards}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.omDi7otL3UWLVgct]{investigators}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.ixBx2wZpnf4qUoEv]{sorcerers}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.wDukeO3euLEGn6FA]{wizards} will have the skills, resources, or raw intellect needed to help untangle these mysteries. This includes characters skilled at diplomacy or who are prepared to face other such Charisma-based challenges. While these aren’t quite as common in Bastardhall as haunts and traps, you’ll still encounter many NPCs who might be better served by conversation rather than fighting.

Warriors: Lastly, there’s quite a lot of combat awaiting your group in Bastardhall. Characters who excel in battle, such as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.lvuutBI9BSCU6cWe]{barbarians}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.HZbrRRVzW7w17L2W]{fighters}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.hGKd722Kn4ZxIOJs]{monks}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.kzxu2dI7tFxv6Ix6.JournalEntryPage.rsDTKu4HUuKft7fk]{swashbucklers}, are incredibly helpful in dealing with the monsters that lie in wait in Bastion of Blasphemies! While melee builds are always a strong choice, builds based around ranged strikes or high mobility do have ample opportunities to shine as well—Bastardhall is a sprawling structure, and there are several large areas where one might take advantage of ranged or mobile superiority within and outside the castle walls. That said, though there are also a few places in this campaign where having a mount could add a very fun additional element to play, a mount-focused character will mostly find it difficult, awkward, or even impossible for their steed to come along on the adventure.
