Day and Night

It’s something of a spoiler, but as Bastion of Blasphemies’s story progresses, more of the Adventure Path’s action takes place during the night. As such, options that require daylight hours to function will become increasingly less viable as the campaign continues. With so much of the Adventure Path taking place after the sun sets, PCs who lack darkvision or low-light vision should look into options to combat the darkness, even if that simply means being ready and able to carry a torch or lantern in one hand when things grow dark and spooky!

Archetypes.name: Archetypes
Archetypes.text:
Since you’re creating a 5th-level character, starting out with an archetype is a solid choice for your PC’s build, especially if your choice helps you focus on one of the specific thematic categories detailed under @UUID[.HRZ1ELwaU6pD3s1X]{Classes}.

Thematically appropriate archetypes include (but are not limited to) @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.O79hOcsaQyj3aQC5]{Archaeologist}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.SUDV5hFZ9WocxWqv]{Blessed One}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.Rrjz5tMJtyVEQnh8]{Herbalist}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.mtc5frNxUHORGscz]{Linguist}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.XWkyCVISmVtJ0ZY3]{Medic}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.rlKxNuq1obXe3m5J]{Scrounger}. Use these suggestions to help guide your choice if you decide to pick an archetype from another source. Archetypes that work best in urban or wilderness campaigns that would be somewhat awkward to play in Bastion of Blasphemies include @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.h1zdUIWX1k5PKTnc]{Celebrity}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.s9kLzXOCl2GNT6TY]{Dandy}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.gfhnRp2TEy9JCfHI]{Gladiator}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.bApp2BZEMuYQCTDM]{Scout}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.rtAFOZOjWHC2zRNO]{Vigilante}. Likewise, those that would be far better suited to aquatic adventures, like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.O9P1YgtiCgHlPNp5]{Pirate} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.2CbiV0VtDKZfQNte]{Viking}, are poor choices.

Languages.name: Languages
Languages.text:
While there are a wide range of languages spoken by the creatures dwelling in Bastardhall, there’s no situation where knowledge of a specific language is required to complete an encounter. Of the regional languages listed on page 34 of Player Core, Varisian is the most commonly spoken in Ustalav, and knowledge of it is often helpful. Beyond this, most of the common languages listed on page 89 of Player Core can be useful on occasion, but Common will almost always be an option when interacting with NPCs or while reading texts found in the castle.

That said, there are a few encounters where being able to speak a specific language can open up additional context, clues, or opportunities for roleplay. These languages won’t be used all the time, but picking one of them could give your PC a chance to learn something that the party might have otherwise missed: Aklo, Elven, Fey, Hallit, or Thalassic.

Faiths.name: Faiths
Faiths.text:
The Arudora family traditionally favored the faiths of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.gxwmzxUWBOhdgFSN]{Shelyn} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma}, so either of these gods would be strong thematic choices for worship in Bastion of Blasphemies. Otherwise, any deity that allows a cleric to become sanctified holy or allows for a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal} divine font is a solid pick. Consult the section on skills below to determine what divine skills would make the most sense and be most useful.

Deities whose edicts or anathemas clash against the acts of fighting fiends and undead, battling curses, or seeking to rebuild or explore ruins are poor choices for Bastion of Blasphemies. In particular, worshipping any of the fiend-related or undead-related deities is not a great choice, but if you have a compelling idea and wish for your PC to do so, consult with your GM first to see if your choice would be a particularly bad one for story reasons.

Skills.name: Skills
Skills.text:
All skills are useful in this campaign, particularly those that have constant applications in combat or for recovering from combat, such as Acrobatics, Athletics, Medicine, and Stealth. In addition, the large number of Research topics that you’ll encounter will often call on the use of skills that aren’t normally associated with reading through books and looking for clues.

Crafting: There’ll be chances to pursue downtime activates during Bastion of Blasphemies, and being able to use Crafting to build your own gear could be quite useful at times. Furthermore, this skill is also called on several times while Researching Basthardhall’s many mysteries, and it is also useful in other unique situations.

Environmental: Society and Thievery checks come up very often, particularly in the context of learning about the site’s history or in handling the numerous hazards that lie in wait. Survival is less commonly used throughout, but in the early parts of the campaign, it is still quite useful.

Magic Skills: Of the four skills associated with magic, all are useful, but Arcana is perhaps the one that you’ll be called upon to roll the least often.

Medicine: Medicine checks outside those made to recover from battle or overcome afflictions (which will be significant) are rare in Bastion of Blasphemies, but the skill is still immensely helpful.

Social Skills: Deception, Diplomacy, and Intimidation are used often in this campaign, even beyond standard encounter uses such as when you attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.QNAVeNKtHA0EUw4X]{Feint}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.DCb62iCBrJXy0Ik6]{Request}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize}—all three of these are excellent choices to lean into. Performance is only slightly less useful in this regard, but it still remains a solid choice.

Lore Skills

Lore skills aren’t particularly load bearing in encounters throughout Bastardhall. Library Lore comes up the most often, followed closely by Games Lore and Architecture Lore, and after that, any food-related lore. Lore skills that specifically get called out only once include Genealogy Lore, Heraldry Lore, Labor Lore, and Theater Lore.

Lore skills associated with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.gxwmzxUWBOhdgFSN]{Shelyn} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma} may be helpful, as these are the two religions associated with the Arudoras.

Bastardhall Lore can potentially help with Recall Knowledge checks, but this specific location-based skill isn’t a substitute for exploring and discovering deep lore about the castle—it’s more one you’d use early in the campaign to figure out if your PC knows anything more about the site’s legends. Still, your GM might find other uses for this specialized Lore skill in your game.

Beyond this, Lore checks about specific types of creature categories could be helpful, but revealing which of these skills are particularly useful can delve into spoiler territory. Nonetheless, Bastardhall is a legendary site and there are certain types of creatures and creature categories that, logically, would be useful in this campaign, including the following horror-themed monster categories: Daemon Lore, Demon Lore, Ghost Lore, Ghoul Lore, Mummy Lore, Sahkil Lore, Phantom Lore, Vampire Lore, or Werecreature Lore. All of these and more are represented in Bastion of Blasphemies, although not in even numbers. If you want to take a Lore about a different creature or creature category, work with your GM to determine if the choice is supported by the campaign.

Feats.name: Feats
Feats.text:
Feats that bolster combat options, methods of dealing with traps and hazards, or enhance your ability to be self-sufficient are quite useful in Bastion of Blasphemies. Less helpful are feats that are better suited for play in large wilderness or urban areas. Keep in mind that the entire campaign takes place in a single sprawling castle and the island it looms on when selecting feats. You won’t have the opportunity to spend any time in true wilderness or in urban centers at all.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.Rq5wkA8DtsmbzoGV]{Ride} and other feats that support mounted combat may help in certain situations, but as mentioned in @UUID[.HRZ1ELwaU6pD3s1X]{Classes}, while there are opportunities for mounted combat in Bastion of Blasphemies, they’re few and far between. There are many secrets to uncover in Bastardhall, and that means you’ll spend a lot of time Searching—@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.GdZLxDtFXaQI3Fop]{Expeditious Search} will let you search these areas much more efficiently and quickly. On the other hand, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.9QQnv7nFpsNCGE89]{Thorough Search} is a great choice if you aren’t worried about taking your time when Searching for clues!

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.bh2jHyyYrkLMsIdX]{Prescient Planner} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.lHFz4MmebvPqTb0A]{Prescient Consumable} are solid feat choices, although Prescient Planner is a bit more complex—when the campaign begins, you won’t immediately have a place where you can purchase goods. Once that restriction is lifted, however, you’ll be able to “recharge” Prescient Planner more easily, which could potentially be quite helpful. Prescient Consumable is even more useful as there are a lot of dangers and monsters in Bastardhall capable of hurting you and inflicting afflictions on you. Being able to whip out an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.UqinuuCWePTYGhVO]{Antiplague} or a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.2RuepCemJhrpKKao]{Healing Potion} to face an unexpected peril can make the difference between life and death—or at least life and agony!

Since many of the opportunities to Research information in Bastardhall employ a wide range of different skills, the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.9jGaBxLUtevZYcZO]{Untrained Improvisation} feat can help keep you in the game if you’re otherwise starved for skill training.

The nature of life and death is strange and distorted in Bastardhall in ways you’ll soon figure out. That said, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.fvYwsHM9O1twQa5N]{Consult the Spirits} is an exceptionally strong thematic choice for this campaign—speak with your GM if you’re interested in taking this feat, as they may wish to do some preparation work before you start opening your PC’s body, mind, and soul up to the beyond!

Finally, one feat in particular may well be a requirement for this campaign due to the strong presence of curses in this adventure. Having at least one PC with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.zGrUu3dUtqHrqGuo]{Break Curse} once you reach 7th level could be immensely helpful while navigating a cursed castle, so you might want to plan to select it!

Gear.name: Gear
Gear.text:
If you’re starting Bastion of Blasphemies with established characters, you’ll likely already have gear appropriate for 5th-level PCs, but this is also a great time to work with the GM to adjust existing PC wealth as needed so that no one PC has a disproportionate amount of gear than another. If you’re creating a brand-new 5th-level character, though, you’ll need to purchase your PC’s gear. To ensure fairness for each one, the entire group should work together to choose one of the following methods to generate their gear.

Lump Sum: This method grants a lump sum of 270 gp to each PC for them to spend as they wish on any common items of 5th level or less. With the lump sum method, the total value of your gear may end up being less than what you’d get with Pick your Items or if you organically gained treasure by playing through levels 1 through 5, but you’ll have greater control over the specific levels of items you can gain and can load up on larger numbers of lower level items if you so wish.

Pick Your Items: This method helps players who struggle to decide how to efficiently spend every single coin avoid potential decision paralysis. When you pick your items, you select the following permanent items from any of the common treasures from the GM Core or Player Core 2.

  • One 4th-level item

  • Two 3rd-level items

  • One 2nd-level item

  • Two 1st-level items

  • 50 gp to spend on consumable items of 5th level or lower, or on permanent items of 3rd level or lower, as you see fit.

Subsystems.name: Subsystems
Subsystems.text: Bastion of Blasphemies is relatively light on the various subsystems presented in GM Core, with one exception. The @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.zkQJzslkiNQuUuKd]{Research} subsystem is incredibly important to understand, as your characters will be using this system extensively to learn about Bastardhall’s complex history as well as its many inhabitants.

Backgrounds.name: Backgrounds
Backgrounds.text:
At the start of this campaign, you and your party members are 5th-level adventurers who have only just started to make names for yourselves. The six custom backgrounds created for this Adventure Path present various reasons your PCs might have been chosen by Florin Kindler to accompany her on her quest to Bastardhall. While you aren’t required to choose one of these backgrounds, your character backstory should give your character a reason for Florin to choose you as a traveling companion.

Standard Backgrounds

If you prefer to choose a standard background from Pathfinder Player Core or Player Core 2, appropriately thematic choices for Bastion of Blasphemies include @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.CAjQrHZZbALE7Qjy]{Acolyte}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.6irgRkKZ8tRZzLvs]{Artisan}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.y9OyNsxGfmjqdcP0]{Artist}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.3YQ1Wcjzk8ftoyo7]{Astrologer}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.3gN09dOT2hMwGcK2]{Cook}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.dVRDDjT4FOu6uLDR]{Detective}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.FKHut73XDUGTnKkP]{Field Medic}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.3frMfODIYFeqTl2k]{Fortune Teller}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.2bzqI0D4J3LUi8nq]{Laborer}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.Yu7Cl0Lk94LdPRi6]{Noble}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.r9fzNQEz33HyKTxm]{Pilgrim}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.RC4l6WsxPn89a1f8]{Raised by Belief}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.ns9BOvCyjdapYhI0]{Root Worker}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.vHeP960qjhfob4Je]{Scavenger}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.v0WPfxN6G8XFfFZT]{Scholar}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.WrKVeUQ6KeRCm9uH]{Teacher}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.i79pgNIAtJfkkOiw]{Tinker}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.IXxdCzBS0xP20ckw]{Ward}. If you want to take one of the rare backgrounds from Player Core 2, both @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.j2G71vQahw1DiWpO]{Cursed} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.backgrounds.Item.pGOlKz4Krnh7MyUM]{Haunted} could be fun options, but make sure to get permission from your GM before taking one of these options!

Bastion of Blasphemies Backgrounds

The following new backgrounds are designed specifically for the Bastion of Blasphemies Adventure Path. You can use these backgrounds to inspire personality traits and details that tie your character to Florin Kindler and her quest to investigate Bastardhall.

Note that these rare backgrounds each grant a little bit more to your character than a standard background! Also, if you’re starting Bastion of Blasphemies with an established character, speak to your GM about potentially swapping out your previous background for one of these choices. Provided you, your GM, and the other players are willing to stretch verisimilitude a bit in ret-conning this element of your character’s history, swapping out the background you chose at 1st level (perhaps as part of playing through “Secrets of the Unlit Star” in the Pathfinder Beginner Box and/or Troubles in Grayce) for one of these more thematic options can go a long way toward making your Bastion of Blasphemies experience more fun. You can even use these backgrounds as selections when making your character for the previous adventures, with your GM’s approval. In which case, your association with Florin Kindler can carry through those first four levels of adventure in the background, only to step up to center stage as you begin this Adventure Path!

The Reception Halls.name: The Reception Halls
The Reception Halls.text:
Visitors often traveled to Castle Arudora. Some were sightseers there to marvel at the castle or sycophants seeking sponsorship from the family, while others were merchants or entertainers looking to foster lucrative new alliances or plumb performance opportunities. Aristocrats and artisans, on the other hand, arrived to ply the family with favors or patronage. Increasingly, as Eragayl’s legacy faded and Raudltz’s self-centered leadership grew more prominent, others came to Castle Arudora for more personal (and often illegal) pursuits, either invited by one of the family members or following up on rumors that their particular skill sets might find support among the Arudoras. In the final years leading up to the curse, however, each individual Arudora became increasingly focused on their own personal obsessions and distractions, and the lady of the castle, Alisendra Arudora, took to hosting decadent galas and parties within the castle’s sprawling reception halls.

When the curse engulfed the castle, she had five different galas in progress, and those who’d gathered for these different events swiftly succumbed to its influence. Some perished, but most were transformed into monstrous distortions of their individual professions and pursuits. Today, the curse’s power maintains these monsters so that earthly needs like food, drink, and rest are cared for, and each day, the cursed inhabitants begin their celebrations anew.

Soaking in the adoration, accolades, whispers, and cheers behind the scenes is the perennial party’s accidental orchestrator, Alisendra Arudora. Like the others, she was transformed by the curse and now exists behind the scenes as a blood hag—she doesn’t actually physically dwell in these halls. Instead, she drifts beyond their boundaries, merged with the walls and floors and ceilings so she can watch, spy, and enjoy the antics of her invitees without needing to do the hard work of entertaining in person. To progress and unlock the next wing of Bastardhall, the PCs must disrupt the five concurrent galas in the reception halls. Combat is a viable way to do so, but the best method to undermine them is to take attention away from Alisendra and claim it, thereby forcing her to manifest in a more weakened state.

Entering the Reception Halls.name: Entering the Reception Halls
Entering the Reception Halls.text: The PCs should be 8th-level before they enter the reception halls, at which point they can choose between entrances available to the public from the castle grounds or those used by the servants and guards in the cellars. They can’t do so before they unlock the region by returning Augsten’s cudgel to the fountain at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3}, however; these entrances are summarized in the @UUID[.6ge4HqVcBe9kXUch]{reception halls’ connections} section. When they do, make sure to describe how the central lower floors of the castle and the upper floors of the northwestern outbuildings shimmer and solidify. Perhaps most astonishing is the ghostly manifestation of the Arudora Causeway that now gleams as it stretches off toward the far (and unattainable) shore of the lake. This causeway will eventually offer the PCs a way out of Bastardhall, but for now, its manifestation is little more than a bit of visual foreshadowing.

The Skies Above.name: The Skies Above
The Skies Above.text:
A clammy fog rolls in. While the breeze and gusts of wind cease, the fog is hardly an improvement, and it coats everything in a dank layer of condensation. Outdoors, vision-based Perception checks take a –2 circumstance penalty, and fog grants @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealment} to creatures 50 feet away. The fog clears from the hours of 10:00 p.m. through 2:00 a.m., letting the unsettling full moon shine down. Temperatures in Castle Arudora remain crisp and cool, dropping to mild cold after dark, and Lake Laroba becomes suddenly calm. A PC attempting to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim} in its waters must succeed at a @Check[athletics|dc:10|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check.

Sunrise is at 9:00 a.m., and sunset is at 6:00 p.m. The days are 9 hours long, and the nights are 15 hours long.

Reception Halls Ambushes.name: Reception Halls Ambushes
Reception Halls Ambushes.text:
Encounter

Low 8

@UUID[Actor.MRlVMpd6UntdsBgU]{Ghostly Guests x3}

If the PCs rest in an unsafe area in the reception halls, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:5]. On a failure, they’re ambushed while they camp by three hungry ghosts, all of whom are dressed like aristocratic visitors to the castle.

Lucid Nightmares.name: Lucid Nightmares
Lucid Nightmares.text:
Upon unlocking the reception halls, the nightmare changes. The PC is now a guest attending one of the five galas being thrown at the castle, and they excitedly anticipate the event with other guests. Then, as the clocktower rings out two-o’clock, the sky darkens and screams fill the air. Monsters erupt onto the scene, and chaos spreads. As creatures tear apart the guests, the PC is forced to seek a hiding place in the castle, but when they find a hiding spot that’s dark and secluded, the sounds of the violence only grow worse. The PC suddenly realizes they share this hiding place with the hooded, staff-bearing figure, who whispers to them, “You shall join us forever now.” The PC emerges from hiding into a castle plunged into darkness and wakes soon thereafter as unseen claws and fangs catch them in the murky black.

Claws and Fangs in the Dark

Resist Nightmare @Check[will|dc:24|options:claws-and-fangs-in-the-dark,lucid-nightmare]

Critical Failure The PC wakes with nyctophobia (fear of darkness), and whenever they’re not in an area of bright light, they suffer a –1 circumstance penalty to Will saves; this increases to a –2 circumstance penalty when in darkness.

Research @Check[survival|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to manage to start a handheld fire to light your way or @Check[stealth|dc:29|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to find a particularly good hiding spot.

Effect

@UUID[Item.TZrFb7uKRubH0yQx]{Nyctophobia}

If a PC critically fails to resist this nightmare, use the linked effect to add a toggle for their penalty to Will saves to their character sheet.

Reception Halls' Features.name: Reception Halls' Features
Reception Halls' Features.text:
The reception halls were lit by a combination of natural lighting and elegant-looking lanterns, chandeliers, sconces, or table settings fitted with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.mRz8Jmk4Q06SsZpC]{Everlight Crystals} that have become evercursed crystals. While there are over a hundred of these glowing lights in the reception halls, they’re of no value to the PCs once plucked from their mountings. If the number of evercursed crystals in a room becomes important (and the area’s description doesn’t say otherwise), assume that a room has one crystal per 40 square feet.

Walls are composed either of worked stone (along exteriors) or wood (on the interiors); both can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climbed} with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check. Ceiling heights on both floors of the reception halls is 20 feet unless otherwise noted. Doors are made of reinforced wood and can’t be locked unless indicated in the text.

While there are plenty of exits out of the reception halls to the castle grounds, as the PCs continue to climb Bastardhall’s floors, the rooftops of nearby lower levels can provide emergency routes of escape. These are generally quite steep and must be Climbed with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check—this increases to @Check[athletics|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] when it’s raining.

Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

The Reception Halls' locations span multiple scene levels! Here is the breakdown:

  • @UUID[.goyxlKit1QLHYYuh]{D1}-@UUID[.3hduGPZ55keA2HRA]{D15} are found in the Castle Grounds level.

  • @UUID[.goyxlKit1QLHYYuh]{D16}-@UUID[.mp2jSvvSVejhua2M]{D30} are found in the Reception Halls (Upper) level.

  • Finally, @UUID[.SORum03a5tQWw4Xp]{Laroba Boathouse} is found southeast in the Shore level.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.ONTeDjH5dol5Cnoz]{Inside Bastardhall} @UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.Ggl8VZ7v1J5Mo1er]{Bastardhall Outdoors}

The Reception Halls features a mix of indoor and outdoor areas. As the PCs explore these various areas, you can play these ambience sounds accordingly.

Servitor Phantoms in Reception

In many areas of the reception halls, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bastion-of-blasphemies-bestiary.Actor.buABPmUgUvhWxVaS]{servitor phantoms} bustle about on tasks that echo the roles they fulfilled before the castle was cursed. These are the same phantoms as those the PCs may have encountered in the cellar, but when encountered in the reception halls, the servitors are quiet, unobtrusive, and take pains to avoid the PCs. Any servitor phantoms slain in these encounters reform after 24 hours to resume their duties.

Phantom Aid

The first time the PCs encounter servitor phantoms in Bastardhall when there are no enemies or hazards in the room, they warn the PCs that the lady of the castle, @UUID[.o8YugBCyrr2aYbfq]{Alisendra Arudora}, observes from the walls of the reception halls, taking delight in the antics and intrigues of her guests. The phantoms inform the PCs that galas are taking place in five different rooms, and that by securing the attention of those taking part in those galas, the PCs can draw Alisendra out for a confrontation. If asked about the nature of the galas or where they’re taking place, a phantom tries to remember, but their muddled mind can offer little more clarity.

Entrance Hall.name: Entrance Hall
Entrance Hall.text:
When one looks upon this grand entrance hall, it’s possible to imagine how beautiful it was in more glorious times. Now, the place is in ruins, its tapestries and rugs rotted, its furniture and birdcages smashed, and its planters destroyed. Upturned earth and scattered bits of plant matter are strewn about the floor, mixed with splatters of blood and the uncountable skeletal remains of those who seem to have participated in some furious and deadly melee that once took place here. The one part of the room that appears to have escaped this calamity sits in an alcove under the balcony to the east, where a single podium stands, a leatherbound book sitting closed atop it. The ceiling rises to a spacious height of forty feet.

The large doors to the northwest at area D1a open into area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1b} of the castle grounds. The stairs at area D1b lead up to the balcony at area @UUID[.Q4E4XuFlsDe1Kezf]{D16a}, while those at area D1c lead to area @UUID[.Q4E4XuFlsDe1Kezf]{D16b}. The secret door at area D1d can be discovered if the PCs @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} near the area, or if they @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the entrance hall for 30 minutes and succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check; it leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.dRUkDhLTYQRs48GB]{C26a}. The door at area D1e leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.BfZkDiplNpaK6npm]{C27}.

The areas where the rubble is particularly dense are treated as difficult terrain.

The entrance hall was the site of a massacre on the night the curse took hold, as many of the guests’ servants fled here in hopes of escaping the castle only to be set upon by monsters and slaughtered one and all. The resulting scene is unnerving and dour when the PCs visit during the day, but after dark, things grow much worse.

Encounter

Moderate 8

@UUID[Actor.WQYzPF4cN4msA8lw]{Shambler Troops x8}

Creatures: If the PCs visit the entrance hall after dark, what appeared to be skeletal remains during the day now look to be the sprawled corpses of over a hundred men and women of various ancestries. This is far more than the number of visiting servants and guests that originally perished here—their numbers have been bolstered over the centuries by the bodies of non-Arudoras who were accidently brought to the castle (such as the attendants and companions of Arudoras carried back to the castle by Velicarn).

These dozens of victims are no mere corpses—each and every one is a shambling zombie that staggers to its feet as soon as any living creature enters the hall after dark. In all, these zombies comprise no fewer than eight shambler troops, and they surge forward in a wave of dead flesh and grisly wounds to attack mercilessly. The shambler troops pursue foes up into the balconies (area @UUID[.Q4E4XuFlsDe1Kezf]{D16}) but do not chase them out into the castle grounds or further into the castle itself.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.0QuRGMnHp0tEhv5m]{Podium}

A guest register sits on a podium in the eastern alcove. This leather book dates all the way back to the first visitors to Castle Arudora, after the castle was completed in 4118 AR. While the book is worth 10 gp as a curiosity, its greater value to the PCs is as a reference. If they know the names of any of the guests who were staying in Castle Arudora during the night the curse was unleashed (such as @UUID[.GBDZrpXoEXkQKLZT]{Danrasteian the Magnificent}, the man who borrowed the Varisian raspberry wine from the wine cellars in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.O2hrZos99pNTSbdj]{C47}), they can confirm which of the many guest bedrooms that guest was staying in, simplifying any searches they might need to conduct on the second floor.

Breakfast Lounge.name: Breakfast Lounge
Breakfast Lounge.text:
This cozy room features two large sofas against the east wall, well attended by coffee tables and end tables. The central area of the room features a long rectangular dining table surrounded by chairs, and an astonishing and delicious looking spread of baked goods sits atop it, filling the chamber with tantalizing scents. Serving tables covered with utensils, plates, and mugs sit against the walls to the northwest and west.

The door in the northwest corner leads to the bakery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.YtT4L1aUQ52wV56D]{C18}). This room was a place for guests to enjoy fresh baked goods delivered from the bakery or to enjoy some light snacks and drinks away from the rest of the castle.

Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.XhMloMPbPL7IUlG7]{It's Never Enough}

Hazard: The PCs may be suspicious of the spread of baked goods on the table, and for good reason. These delicious-looking pastries, breads, pretzels, and cups of coffee and tea are a cruel manifestation of the Bastardhall Curse.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Disable It's Never Enough Haunt" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to replace the delicious-looking food with its rotten (and real) counterpart!

Meeting Chamber.name: Meeting Chamber
Meeting Chamber.text:
A long wooden table surrounded by chairs fills the middle of this room. Paintings on the walls depict wilderness landscapes.

The secret door in the east wall can be discovered if a PC @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in that part of the room or spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the area and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The door leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.dRUkDhLTYQRs48GB]{C26b}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.NcXcXU2b5IZclDel]{Meeting Chamber}

This room was used by the Arudoras or their agents to meet with visitors. The paintings on the wall are all landscapes by famed (and long dead, even when the castle was being built) halfling artist Candace Casterellin—each depicts a scene from her homeland along the Lost Coast of Varisia. There are 8 paintings in all. Each is 2 Bulk and worth 10 gp, and any one of them could serve as a distracting memento for Danrasteian in area @UUID[.tmNCXndKaS4Bi3tD]{D26}.

Northern Hall.name: Northern Hall
Northern Hall.text:
Old planter boxes containing dead plants line the walls at this hall’s wider northern section. To the south stand a set of double doors with an elegant sign on the lintel above them, while to the west, a spiral staircase winds upward around a stone statue of a man in armor.

The sign above the southern doors reads, “Hall of History.”

The secret door near area D4c can be discovered if a PC @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in that part of the hall or spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the area and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The door leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.dRUkDhLTYQRs48GB]{C26c}.

The stairs at area D4a lead up to area @UUID[.I5xBZSgIpeHNyb21]{D21a}, while the stairs at area D4c lead up to area @UUID[.I5xBZSgIpeHNyb21]{D21b}. The statue in the spiral staircase is a representation of Eragayl Arudora.

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.buABPmUgUvhWxVaS]{Servitor Phantom}

Creature: A single housekeeper servitor phantom bustles about this hall, sweeping at the floors with a phantom broom that does nothing at all to clean.

Hall of History.name: Hall of History
Hall of History.text:
A pair of long, C-shaped stone benches covered with rotting cushions sit to either side of an enclosed circular space at the center of the room, accessible via four archways. The room’s walls are hung with several paintings, many of which are different landscapes of Castle Arudora in gentler times, but among these are thirteen portraits of different people, each of which bears a small bronze plaque to identify the person illustrated. A fourteenth frame about the same size as these thirteen portraits lies face down on the floor in the middle of central circular area.

Alisendra often greeted new visitors to the castle here, giving them a history of her family before having servants escort them up to their rooms. The paintings adorning the walls helped to show the castle from different views and in different times, while the portraits were there to provide context to the family history. Alisendra would note in her greetings that the Arudora line went back further than Eragayl, but that only those who actually dwelled in the castle are portrayed here. She joked that as soon as Jinnivere and Augsten had children of their own, they might need to expand the size of this hall, as there was very little room for more than a few more paintings on the walls.

While the landscapes are simply decor to the PCs, the portraits can be useful to them, for each carries with it the name of the Arudora it depicts. There are a dozen portraits in all, each corresponding to one of the dozen Arudoras listed in @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.gRFl7AZFdxcRUo8n]{The Bastardhall Curse}—they can provide the PCs with names they haven’t heard yet, potentially jogging their memories (and allowing them to attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about them to research the person in question). The portraits also give them additional context, letting them automatically recognize Arudora visages when they appear in this adventure.

A PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EwgTZBWsc8qKaViP]{Investigating} the portraits notices a few strange irregularities, as summarized below (all of these are subtle manifestations of the Bastardhall Curse).

  • Alisendra’s portrait has a bloody handprint smeared across it.

  • Augsten’s portrait reeks of rotten food.

  • The frame of Dazerien’s portrait is ragged and imparts wood splinters at even the lightest touch.

  • Demiterus’s portrait, along with that of his wife Neesha, are soaking wet.

  • Eragayl’s portrait gives the viewer a strange sense of claustrophobia and despair.

  • Irrokcis’s portrait exudes a faint scent of decay.

  • Jinnivere’s portrait hangs crooked, no matter how often it is straightened out, and exudes a faint barnyard scent.

  • Raudltz’s portrait is damaged, as if someone had scraped down across his face with their fingers to leave furrows in the paint.

  • Ryhasphinea’s portrait has patches of mold growing on its frame. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:20] check identifies this as fungus that normally grows only on decaying flesh.

  • Tasifinie’s portrait has cobwebs encrusting it and a spider crawling on it.

  • Zasha’s portrait emits the faint sounds of a weeping baby.

Encounter

Low 8

@UUID[Actor.riAGYsZjzTETR2Pw]{The Bastard's Portrait} @UUID[Actor.Gu0cJHGwPd547OtC]{Wraiths x3}

Hazard: The thirteenth portrait in this room lies face down on the floor and was never actually hung on the walls before the curse struck. It’s a supernatural manifestation of Velicarn’s anger and a dangerous hazard to those who meddle with it.

Banquet Hall.name: Banquet Hall
Banquet Hall.text:
Chandeliers hang from the ceiling of this large banquet hall, looming above four long tables with seating for nearly fifty people in all. Two sideboard tables stand to the northwest, while a large brick fireplace sits at the southwest.

This banquet hall looks clean, inviting, and well lit, for this chamber is the focus of one of the five galas Alisendra Arudora had arranged before the curse took hold—a banquet featuring the work of one of Caliphas’s most talented chefs, Ilza Vindranuff. Known for her daring and unusual meals, Ilza was invited to present a multicourse meal for nearly four dozen aristocrats, artisans, and friends of the Arudora family. The meal Ilza had planned took advantage of a wide range of local herbs, plants, and Lake Laroba fish, and things were just gearing up for the main course when the curse struck the castle. The Bastardhall Curse latched on to Ilza’s ambitions and transformed her into a lamia matriarch who swiftly slaughtered her guests before gorging on their remains.

The secret door in the east wall at area D6b can be discovered if a PC @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in that part of the room or spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the area and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The door leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.dRUkDhLTYQRs48GB]{C26d}. The secret door in the west wall at area D6a can be discovered if a PC Seeks in that part of the room or spends 10 minutes Searching the area and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The door leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.DqhDfn8rAdJqBC6g]{C17}.

Encounter

Moderate 8

@UUID[Actor.oltkbUona5p9ZIr1]{Ilza Vindranuff} @UUID[Actor.7KhhBPqRFYMDZmtm]{Servitor Phantoms x4} @UUID[Actor.CqDFc8hpip1Jc751]{Disgruntled Diners}

Creatures: The physical remains of the original guests are long gone, but the phantasmal echoes of over 40 of the meal’s participants are seated at the tables, going through the motions of enjoying a ghostly banquet. While these phantasms appear to be engaged in friendly discussions as they enjoy the meal, no sound of conversation or clatter of utensils comes from them.

The first time the PCs enter this area, they come upon four bird-skulled cook servitor phantoms who simper and stammer as they’re dressed down by an angry Varisian woman dressed in elegant purple and blue clothing. The woman doesn’t immediately notice the PCs, giving them time to listen in as she harangues the cooks for claiming they don’t have the ingredients to serve the main course. As soon as the PCs make their presence known (or automatically after a few rounds of watching), the woman gasps as she takes note of them. This is Ilza Vindranuff in her human form, and she sees the PCs not as adventurers but as higher-ranking members of the house staff. She dismisses the servitors and steps forward, asking the PCs to work with their staff to make sure they have what they need to present the night’s main course.

If the PCs agree to help, she tells them to head down to the main kitchen (area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40}) to talk with the cooks there and figure out what they need to finish the meal. She impresses on them that it should only take the cooks an hour to prepare the meal and requests that the PCs deliver the plates no more than 30 minutes after the cooks complete their task. More importantly, the meal must arrive here in the banquet hall at some point between the hours of 6:00 and 7:00 p.m. (after dark). If the PCs can deliver the meal during this hour and serve it, Ilza watches, pleased, as the phantoms eat the meal over the course of the next 10 minutes and spends the entire time thanking the PCs and telling them what a lifesaver they’ve been. When the meal is finished, the guests fade away (causing the hazard below to automatically become disabled), and Ilza suddenly crumbles to dust and bones, leaving behind a lamia matriarch skeleton and her +1 striking scimitar as her soul moves on to the afterlife.

If the PCs don’t agree to take care of this for Ilza, if they treat her with disrespect for more than a few moments, if they fail to deliver the meal during the proper hour, or if they draw their weapons, Ilza hisses in anger, says, “Never mind the fish and wine. You lot will do just as well for the main course!” and attacks, transforming back into a lamia matriarch on the first round of combat. Ilza fights to the death but won’t pursue the PCs if they flee the banquet hall—and if they return after a few hours have passed, she’ll give them one more chance to do her bidding. Otherwise, she fights again, and this time, she pursues them throughout the castle, fighting to the death. Once combat breaks out in this area, the servitor phantoms flee through the secret door at area D6a (while they don’t actually open the door and just mime the action before moving through the “wall,” observant PCs can use this as a clue to look in that part of the room for a hidden door).

Hazard: The phantom diners at the table are harmless as long as Ilza remains calm, but as soon as she attacks, these guests become violent and dangerous, transforming into a haunt that complicates a fight with her inside the banquet hall.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Scatter Banquet Hall Cutlery" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager as the disgruntled diners begin hurling it at the PCs!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.cKu2Ad9ORznS3znJ]{Banquet Hall}

In addition to Ilza’s +1 striking scimitar, a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} this room turns up 100 gp in fine silverware. This Search takes 5 minutes, or 30 minutes if the hazard is triggered and the valuables are strewn about the room haphazardly.

Reward

If the PCs deliver the meal to Ilza’s approval, grant them XP as if they’d defeated her and the hazard normally. Note that when the PCs finally compel Alisendra to manifest, she’ll be at a disadvantage because the PCs have successfully stolen away Ilza’s attention.

Southern Hall.name: Southern Hall
Southern Hall.text:
The hall widens out here into a wide carpeted hallway with many doors and a few side halls providing access onward. Some of the double doors each bear a small plaque above them, and a small free-standing wood frame holds a larger announcement between the eastern doors.

The doors to areas @UUID[.HDn0BDLl89tn8dPZ]{D8}–@UUID[.CSZBdjguWV1HWdLb]{D9} and @UUID[.BzbrB5DMMnjAcyag]{D11}–@UUID[.3hduGPZ55keA2HRA]{D15} all bear signs indicating the name of the room that lies beyond. The door at area D7a (further north from the main hall) leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.rcdV1Q52IsBUDbDz]{C12b}, while the door at area D7b opens into a wall of impenetrable green mist. This mist clears once the PCs unlock the fallen temple, at which point this door leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.tYPsUVZ4XOqnICsM]{G1e}. The spiral stairs in area D7c lead upstairs to the second floor, to area @UUID[.klWkYac4yHUOYGlr]{D27a}. Area D7d once served as a marshaling area for the castle’s security, but is now empty and abandoned. The northeastern door at area D7e leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.1eOgRGREQTc9DvPd]{C30} in the castle cellars, while just south of this a spiral staircase (D7f) leads down to an atrium with a set of double doors that open out onto the haunted shore at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.D7PNbqVhoW8hFd61]{A18}.

The announcement on display between the eastern doors to area @UUID[.BzbrB5DMMnjAcyag]{D11} reads: “Masquerade Ball begins tonight at 7:00. Masks required for entrance! Enjoy the traditional music of Galduria’s Ghostlight Sisters!”

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.buABPmUgUvhWxVaS]{Servitor Phantoms x4}

Creatures: A group of four servitor phantoms are always encountered here, going about the business of cleaning or just quietly talking among themselves near a wall. Once they spot the PCs, though, these chatty servants immediately get back to “work.”

Baths.name: Baths
Baths.text:
Several large rooms sectioned off by curtains and stone walls provide semi-private bathing here. A long shelf used to store sponges, towels, scented oils, and other bathing supplies runs along the eastern wall, which also hosts a few drawers and closets to store clothing while bathing. To the southwest sits a fireplace for heating water as well as an empty wood bin and several tall stacks of pails.

The Castle Arudora baths were a popular place to relax, but when the curse fell, these chambers happened to be empty—as a result, there are no dangerous haunts or monsters lurking in this area. The baths themselves are all dry, and they (as well as the dressing rooms to the south) make for safe places to rest. The PCs won’t risk being ambushed during long rests taken in this area.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.0a0i3RmIWfgl5e04]{Chimney}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} this area for 10 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check notes a strange crack in the upper back wall of the fireplace. As they look more closely, they discover a brass gear stuck in the lower part of the chimney. A successful @Check[athletics|dc:25] check is required to wrest the gear free from where it became lodged after phasing through a few walls when it was hurled from the temple. See @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.t1s9G6BjLx2VvxXt#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

Visitor's Library.name: Visitor's Library
Visitor's Library.text:
Floor-to-ceiling bookshelves line the walls of this long library, with two additional free-standing cases running down the center. The books themselves are in disarray, with most scattered across the floor rather than where they belong on the shelves. Further adding to the library’s air of neglect is the darkness, for the sole source of light here is a single flickering candle that has only a small amount of wax left to burn and is balanced atop a skull set at the center of the room’s lone round reading table.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Tidy Visitor's Library" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to put the books back in their bookcases and disable the scene region automating greater difficult terrain!

The layer of books on the floor makes this room difficult terrain until someone spends 4 hours putting things back on the shelves.

Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.Yztj3ptEzuC35z1u]{Madam Skerzana}

Creature: When the PCs first enter this room, the chamber’s sole occupant is nestled away in the northeastern corner. If the party brings any source of bright light into the room, or if they allow the light from the brightly lit hallway in area @UUID[.78A34DGpyfbsAqFq]{D7} inside, a raspy voice calls out from the room’s darkest corner, saying, “Put out that light! You’re letting out the shadows, you fools!”

This voice belongs to Madam Skerzana, a fortune-teller once employed by Mister Moxie’s Traveling Oddities (see area @UUID[.tmNCXndKaS4Bi3tD]{D26}) who claimed to possess a right eye that could see into the past and a left eye that could see into the future.

When the curse struck, she was in the visitor’s library looking through the collection of occult books the Arudoras had put on display for visitors to peruse. The Bastardhall Curse took both of her eyes when it transformed her into a stygira, and now she can see only through the face of the silver mirror she carries with her (a variation on the typical stygira, who must use a crystal to see). If the PCs refuse to return the room to near darkness, she issues a string of shocking profanities and rushes out of the darkness to attack them. She fights to the death to protect “her books,” but if the PCs flee the library, she slams the doors shut and returns to her futile search through the books for a way to undo the curse that afflicts her.

If the PCs comply with her request to put out the light, Madam Skerzana calms down but remains hidden in the northeast corner, inviting her visitors to have a seat around the candle and asking, in a voice that sounds like chalk dragged across stone, what brings them to visit “Madam Skerzana.” She informs them that while her eyesight isn’t what it used to be, she can still perform readings for the right price. If the PCs ask for a reading, she shuffles out into the candlelight and holds out a gnarled palm, then requesting a payment of 40 gp to give one PC the “answers they seek.” She accepts any object worth at least 40 gp as payment, then asks the PC who paid her what they’re looking for. If the PC requests information about Bastardhall, the curse, or any of the Arudoras, Madam Skerzana cackles with delight and admits these topics vex and intrigue her as well, and she’s eager to share what she’s learned for free if the PCs do the same. This allows the PCs to Research the Bastardhall Curse by speaking to her (see Madam Skerzana’s Discoveries below). Once the PCs have grown tired of speaking to her or once they’ve earned all possible RP, Madam Skerzana offers to give them the real reading they paid for.

If the PCs accept a reading from Madam Skerzana, she casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.pkcOby5prOausy1k]{Read Omens} to their specifications. Depending on what the PCs ask, you should use the results of this spell to guide and encourage them to explore Bastardhall, perhaps giving them a hint that recovering the missing art from the gallery or repairing the clocktower’s gears could be a key part of lifting the curse. Regardless of how the read omens spell goes, near the end of its 10-minute duration, Madam Skerzana suddenly grows silent. A moment later, an expression of terror twists her mouth and she cries out, “No… No! I did not mean to pry! Run, fools! The Typhon Wheel sees you!” An instant later, she cries out in pain, and then, in a gory, horrific display, she melts away into a puddle of steaming filth and decay—Charg has grown tired of her meddling and has taken this opportunity to use her destruction to send the PCs a dire and unignorable warning. (While this might make the PCs nervous about casting read omens themselves, they have nothing to fear from Charg, as they haven’t spent centuries as his prisoners... yet!)

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.SdCFDAydM2FbYzYy]{Amid the Books}

Madam Skerzana’s silver mirror is a work of art worth 50 gp. If the PCs @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the room for 30 minutes and succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check, they discover a few magic scrolls amid the books. If the PCs take the time to clean the library and reshelve the books, they discover these scrolls automatically. The scrolls are a scroll of ghostly weapon, a scroll of haste, a scroll of suggestion, and a scroll of vision of death.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.UUqGlDCzpRnwqovv]{Bastardhall Curse}

Madam Skerzana’s Investigation: The PCs either trade the information they have about the Bastardhall Curse with Madam Skerzana to learn about what she’s discovered (taking 5 minutes per Research check), or they sift through the books in this room looking to duplicate her work (taking 4 hours per Research check or 1 hour per check if the room is cleaned and the books are reorganized).

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[occultism|dc:22|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] or @Check[diplomacy|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to give Madam Skerzana the information she needs to learn something she knows, or @Check[library-lore|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] or @Check[perception|dc:29|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to look through the books in the library for these answers.

Reward

If Madam Skerzana casts read omens for the PCs, grant them XP as if they’d defeated her in combat after she melts.

Supply Room.name: Supply Room
Supply Room.text:
Shelves line the walls and stand in the middle of this supply room, each filled with dusty objects suited to a wide range of uses—firewood, brooms, buckets, linens, repair tools, bed warmers, chamber pots, and more.

Enoch Grashikin, the Arudora’s majordomo, used the door here to surreptitiously travel between the reception halls and the cellars (area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.iSr8lkxVqQ1hBRGC]{C22}).

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.kihMX5QQ6Q0yCYYT]{Supply Room Shelves}

This room was used by the servants to store frequently-needed tools and supplies for their day-to-day jobs, so that they wouldn’t have to trudge all the way back to the cellars as often. While most of the supplies here are old and in poor repair, if the PCs spend a half hour Searching the room (or if they simply @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} near the southern shelves and succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check), they discover a misplaced recipe book that has the following message written in black ink on its inside cover: “DO NOT REMOVE FROM MAIN KITCHEN!” The book contains many delicious-looking recipes, including the formula to craft an alchemical food called @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.zg4aR2ndtTzO1osa]{Galvanic Chew}. It’s worth 30 gp, but if the PCs return it to the servitor chefs in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40}, the chefs add galvanic chew to the list of foods they can prepare for the PCs.

Ballroom.name: Ballroom
Ballroom.text:
This immense ballroom is brightly lit by gleaming chandeliers that hang from the domed ceiling some forty feet above, the intricate network of crossbeams and supports an architectural wonder that leaves the vast space of the floor below open. To the west, an enormous, fireplace looms, its mantle arching up like a tiered ziggurat to a stone chimney above. Lastly, to the southeast, a raised stage looks out over the room.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.aGCIKeSAO2yb078H.PlaylistSound.5OKw6W6FPoWmsJBL]{Ballroom}

As the PCs enter the Ballroom, you can play this ambience sound.

The secret door in the south wall is exceptionally difficult to locate—a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} near this area of the ballroom and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check can discover it. Unfortunately, until the private halls are unlocked, this secret door opens to reveal nothing but an impassable wall of green mist.

Encounter

Moderate 8

@UUID[Actor.br1fuSnpsRfkYW1z]{The Ghostlight Sisters x3} @UUID[Actor.HDF02TkzQISYCgLN]{Phantom Knights x2}

Creatures: If the PCs enter this room during daylight hours, the place is empty save for four servitor phantoms who bustle about as they sweep, dust, and mop the place. Being phantoms, their efforts shouldn’t have any effect on the room, yet the space somehow still benefits from their attentions.

In addition to any aid the phantoms might give the PCs (see @UUID[.bYyP1moxduDE7caw#servitor-phantoms-in-reception]{Servitor Phantoms in Reception}), they helpfully inform them that the Ghostlight Sisters haven’t arrived yet, and that the masquerade ball itself will take place between the hours of 7:00 p.m. and midnight tonight.

If the PCs arrive at D11 during that window of time, they find the ballroom to be a quite different place. The room is filled with dozens of ghostly guests all dressed in extravagant masks—they mill about, gossip, snack at one of several ghostly trays of food and drink, or dance. The sound of conversation and music in the room has a distorted and eerie context, just enough that the PCs can’t understand the words or recognize the melodies. The music itself comes from the stage, where three animated human skeletons dressed in garish robes and scarves perform with three different instruments—a dulcimer, lyre, and violin. These are the Ghostlight Sisters, a trio of Varisian performers hired by Alisendra to provide music for the gala. When the curse struck, they and the guests here were slaughtered by monsters, only to rise as undead thereafter. The mass of phantasmal dancers are little more than a conglomerate of soul echoes and are harmless illusions, but the Ghostlight Sisters are quite dangerous.

If the PCs wear masks, they can enter the ballroom and mingle about as they desire, but if they don’t have masks, they’re stopped at the entrance by a pair of phantom knights who politely remind the PCs that this is a masquerade ball, and that they should go get their masks; the knights helpfully suggest that the PCs may have left their masks in their guest rooms above. If the PCs insist on entering the ballroom without masks, the guards grow angry and attack, which also draws the Ghostlight Sisters into battle. They remain on stage using their ranged attacks and supernatural abilities while the phantom knights engage in melee, but if the PCs harry the Ghostlight Sisters from beyond the range of their Trio’s Torment ability, they’ll descend from the stage and move into the ballroom to ensure the PCs can be affected. Neither the guards nor the Ghostlight Sisters pursue PCs who flee from this room, and should the PCs return at a later time clad in masks, any surviving Sisters or phantom knights don’t seem to recognize them, allowing them to take part in the ball.

While finding masks in the guest rooms above is one way to fulfill the phantom knights’ requirements for entrance, any mask will do as long as it’s not shabby and amateur in appearance. An illusory disguise can provide a mask, as can the captain’s raiment armor (found in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.WUfxobQnHYYwiStb]{C49}). The PCs can also craft masks for themselves in the Maiserene workshop (area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.XdkSCjX3BA3dp5sE]{A6}), but these masks must be worth at least 5 gp to pass muster. Full helms from armor most certainly do not count as wearing a mask—how uncouth!

A masked PC finds that they can hear the music and understand the conversations here with ease, and the milling ballroom guests become a little more clear and less indistinct. Such a PC also instinctively feels unseen eyes on them and intuits that there are three ways they can divert attention away from Alisendra, as detailed below.

  • Dance: A PC can attract attention by dancing for an hour on the ballroom floor and succeeding at a @Check[performance|dc:24|options:divert-attention-from-alisendra] check.

  • Gossip: A PC can spread salacious but false rumors among the crowd by spending an hour milling about and succeeding at a @Check[deception|dc:24|options:divert-attention-from-alisendra] check.

  • Intrigue: A PC can take advantage of the mystery surrounding their identity and build intrigue about who they might be by spending an hour quietly mingling and succeeding at a @Check[society|dc:24|options:divert-attention-from-alisendra] check

  • Assist: While not an activity capable of helping to directly distract the room, a PC can assist another PC who is dancing, gossiping, or intriguing by following them for the hour and observing the reactions of the ghostly attendees. With a successful @Check[perception|dc:24] check, they grant the PC they’re assisting a +2 circumstance bonus to their check (+4 bonus on a critical success).

Effect

@UUID[Item.lELfJ59AJTvZ6i7H]{Diversion Assistance}

If a PC successfully assists another, add this effect to the PC being assisted to automate their circumstance bonus. The bonus from this effect will be toggled when the PC uses one of the skill check buttons above, otherwise the bonus can be toggled in the roll dialog.

If the party fails to achieve at least four successes at these pursuits by the end of the ball at midnight, or if the party accumulates 4 or more critical failures, the Ghostlight Sisters suddenly call them out as intruders—they attack at once and are joined by the two phantom knights.

On the other hand, if the party accumulates four successes at these activities before midnight, they attract the attention of the Ghostlight Sisters, who invite the PCs up on stage to join them in their final performance of the night. For the next 30 minutes, a PC can attempt one of the following checks to keep up with the Ghostlight Sisters—a @Check[performance|dc:22|options:final-performance] check to join them in music or dance, a @Check[acrobatics|dc:24|options:final-performance] check to provide astounding distractions, a @Check[society|dc:26|options:final-performance] check to single out the more influential-looking guests among the phantasmal crowd on the ballroom floor and direct the performance toward them, or a @Check[fortitude|dc:29|options:final-performance] save to keep pace with the show without faltering. These checks earn Victory Points, and if the PCs earn at least 2 Victory Points during this performance, the ballroom guests fade away alongside the two phantom knights. The three Ghostlight Sisters bow graciously before the party before crumbling to dust, leaving their instruments behind. If the party fails to earn at least 2 Victory Points, the Ghostlight Sisters accuse them of ruining the show and attack.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.DWWBBQOIKG2iBVdg]{Fireplace}

In addition to the three magical instruments the Ghostlight Sisters carry, a PC who Seeks near the fireplace or searches the ballroom for 10 minutes discovers something a guest had the misfortune to lose a few hours before the curse fell: a fortune’s coin.

Reward

If the PCs earn an invitation up to the stage and successfully take part in the Ghostlight Sisters’ finale, grant them XP as if they’d defeated the Ghostlight Sisters and the phantom knights in combat, and note that when the PCs finally compel Alisendra to manifest, she’ll be at a disadvantage because the PCs have successfully stolen away the phantasmal dancers’ attention.

Drawing Room.name: Drawing Room
Drawing Room.text:
A half-dozen easels stand to the south, facing three large windows hung with deep purple curtains. Curiously, the two easels to the southeast have been positioned close to each other. Elsewhere in this room are tables, comfortable chairs, and a large sofa. Cupboards on the walls and shelves hold ancient art supplies.

Guests could use the supplies in this room to pursue all manner of artistry in the hope of producing a piece of art that would catch the eye of one of the Arudoras and earn them a place in the castle gallery (area @UUID[.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}) for at least a few months.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.IdB9oY5iELBfBs64]{Art Supplies} @UUID[Actor.YIoZSJr5stCPxmjE]{Easel}

Most of the art supplies in storage here are old and ruined, but a PC who spends 30 minutes sorting through them can assemble a collection of tools that functions as a sterling artisan’s toolkit for creating paintings or drawings.

While most of the easels are empty, the two to the southeast that have been placed adjacent to one another contain objects of interest. The western of the two bears a half-completed and relatively amateurish attempt to duplicate the haunting painting that sits on the eastern easel. This portrait depicts a powerful figure fighting several undead monstrosities upon a grisly battlefield—a PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:15] check identifies the figure as Arazni and understands that this is a depiction of the Shining Crusade. This painting is 1 Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it triggers a memory of Alisendra Arudora attempting to duplicate the eastern painting, only to become frustrated at her lack of skill. This drawing belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}). See @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{Lost Artwork} for more details.

Smoking Parlor.name: Smoking Parlor
Smoking Parlor.text:
A trio of large leather sofas and a round table surrounded by comfortable-looking high-backed chairs furnish this room. Two cabinets stand against the north wall. The air here carries the faintly lingering scent of expensive pipe weed.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.T1nb3RFN1bRuY9cV]{Northern Cabinets} @UUID[Actor.VEeT0RjijmHwemGT]{Sofa}

The cabinets to the north once contained a wide and expensive selection of smoking paraphernalia and supplies, but the passage of time has left them in poor condition. Still, a PC who spends 5 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the cabinets can discover a few tins of ground flayleaf here. While the stuff has long lost its potency as a narcotic, it can still suffice as an ingredient for the cooks in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40}.

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} near the sofa to the southwest and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check or Searches the whole room for a half hour discovers something shiny nestled between two of the cushions: a greater soulheart. The first PC to touch this greater soulheart receives a brief memory of Ausken Dast, who was seated here as he enjoyed an imported cigar alongside Korven Willachur, the captain of the castle guard. The two enjoyed a rare moment to relax and talk shop a few days before the curse fell.

Arudora Gallery.name: Arudora Gallery
Arudora Gallery.text:
Display shelves line the north and south wall of this long art gallery, while a similarly-long display table sits in the middle of the room. A wide range of objects sit on these shelves and table, all of which appear to be strangely transparent. In a few instances, objects appear to be missing from their spots entirely. Stairs lead up to a balcony above, where the walls are adorned with dozens of paintings. Like the art objects on display below, these paintings appear ghostly, and several seem to be missing entirely.

At the time the curse fell, this gallery was attended by a man named Ilves Mondain, a perfectionist and well-known art critic who left behind a burgeoning career in Absalom to accept a post as the castle’s gallery curator, as he had grown tired of the hustle and bustle of urban life. Given free rein to pick and choose the works displayed here, he’d boosted the prestige of the Arudora gallery significantly by the end of his first year of employment, and visitors often came to the castle simply to enjoy his showcases.

In the weeks leading up to the curse, though, Ilves had grown distracted, for not only had he started to miss the culture and opportunities a big city provided, but he’d also fallen in love with a talented painter from Caliphas named Minialee. Though Ilves had begun to consider tending a diplomatic resignation from his post, he was worried (rightfully so) that Alisendra Arudora would take his request poorly and make his life thereafter—whether he chose to stay employed at the castle or to move on to Caliphas—utterly impossible. In an awful way, the curse solved this problem for him.

The small room to the west (area D14b) served three purposes—as a meeting place for Ilves to chat with potential art donors, as a workshop for him to restore artwork, and as his bedchambers.

Encounter

Low 8

@UUID[Actor.l5relJ9F1Ko1dpOB]{Ilves Mondain}

Creature: The curse twisted and distorted Ilves, warping his artistic knowledge and keen eye as it transformed him into a multi-limbed horror known as a blood painter. Denied the view of the artwork he once kept here and frustrated that 13 pieces are missing, he now spends his time stomping around on the two floors of this gallery, sustained by the curse over the centuries and continually patrolling in hopes of discovering the missing artwork. He has little interest in discussion with the PCs and is likely to roar and attack as soon as he spots them—with two exceptions.

If a PC wears the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.nZE16PtiyY7DWlzd]{Lover’s Gloves} from area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fQvQS0zYiON5P7HI]{B15} or if one is carrying Minialee’s painting on their person, Ilves comes up short, just shy of rolling initiative. He lowers the eyes in his hands to regard the PCs more closely, then says, “I can smell her artistry on you. What have you done with my Minialee? Have you seen her? Does she... remember me?” The PCs can attempt to Lie to him with a @Check[deception|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|options:action:lie|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check, or they can give him the short note she wrote (also found in area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fQvQS0zYiON5P7HI]{B15})—either course causes Ilves to stay motionless in thought for 1 round before he utters a long, quaking sigh. “She is gone. Dead. And there is nothing for me anymore. Thank you. You have done a kindness to an old, old soul... I come now to join you, Minialee!” At this point, the ghostly manifestation of a man with long dark hair rises out of the blood painter’s form—PCs who have examined the painting from area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fQvQS0zYiON5P7HI]{B15} recognize him as the man depicted therein. Ilves’ soul rises up and vanishes, and the blood painter body left behind visibly withers and shudders before roaring again. Bereft of a soul, the blood painter gains the weak creature adjustments, and at the end of every round, it takes @Damage[2d6[spirit]] damage, even as it lurches to attack the PCs. The blood painter won’t pursue PCs outside this area but otherwise fights to the death.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.4n6yz38plAAvd8av]{Ilves' Peace}

The works of art that remained on display here were corrupted by the curse and reworked into intangible, distorted mockeries, and a PC who looks through the remaining cases gazes upon ghostly paintings, sculptures, and other works of art that depict scenes of cruelty, depravity, and horror. Only the 13 empty settings for the missing art lacks such atrocities—see @UUID[.#returning-the-artwork]{Returning the Artwork} for more details.

If the PCs bring Ilves peace either by Lying to him or by delivering Minialee’s final note, the love he felt for his long-dead paramour infuses the lover’s gloves the PCs found in area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fQvQS0zYiON5P7HI]{B15}—wherever they are, the gloves are immediately enhanced and become a 10th-level item worth 900 gp that grants a +2 item bonus to Diplomacy checks, and they may be activated twice per day. If the PCs sold the lover’s gloves to Banijer Greely at the trading post, the next time they visit him, he shows the gloves to the PCs, astounded at how they’ve grown in power. He offers to return them to the PCs at no cost.

In Ilves’ office, the PCs automatically notice a shimmering painting that sits on his desk where the man left it, long ago, on the night the curse took hold. This is Ilana Greenbough’s painting—the one she submitted for consideration to be included in the gallery. Ilves had decided to accept the painting and penned a short note to Ilana, but he never had a chance to deliver confirmation of this decision. Like the artwork on display in the main gallery, this painting is now a ghostly reflection of what it once was, but unlike the other artwork, its beauty has not only persisted but has become stronger. Any PC who looks upon it can sense Shelyn’s protection on the painting but also understands intuitively that 13 other works of art hidden throughout Bastardhall must be returned to their places in the gallery to undermine the curse. Ilana’s painting cannot be moved from this room, but once per day, a creature adjacent to it can activate it as a two-action activity to cast a 5th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}; the painting has a counteract rank of 9th and a +15 modifier for the roll.

Side Quest Completion

If the PCs discover what’s become of the painting Ilana submitted to Ilves for consideration and deliver Ilves’ note to her in Maiserene, they complete her side quest.

Reward

If the PCs sooth Ilves’ spirit and weaken the blood painter, grant them XP as if they’d defeated it at full power rather than as a level 8 weakened version. Once the blood painter is slain, area D14b becomes a safe place to rest.

Lost Artwork

At the time the curse struck the castle, several exhibits from the castle’s gallery at area D14 were missing—either loaned out, stolen, or misplaced. The first time a PC touches one of these pieces of art, they’ll experience a brief flash of memory. Each of these works of art appear to be worth about 500 gp, but no one in Maiserene will purchase them, as the phantoms recognize them and suggest returning the item to the castle gallery in the reception hall. If one of these items is destroyed, it reforms fully back in the location it was found 8 hours later. Restoring all 13 art objects to the gallery is one of the required conditions to achieve this Adventure Path’s @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.iIIzG8EEQwsCV7an]{secret ending}, but PCs who neglect to do so can still later sell each of the items they’ve gathered for 500 gp once they escape Bastardhall.

Returning the Artwork

If the party takes a few minutes to count them up, they’ll find that there are 13 empty display slots in the gallery—7 works of art on the lower floor in area D14a, and 6 paintings upstairs on the walls at area D14c. Each missing display has a small plaque indicating the missing artwork’s name. All 13 missing works are found throughout Bastardhall; after placing a missing work in its proper display, the artwork shimmers and becomes ghostly, then can’t be removed. Once all 13 works are returned here, all of the artwork in the gallery reverts to its original beauty, though the pieces still remain ghostly. Accomplishing this attracts Shelyn’s attention, fulfilling one of the three requirements for the PCs to attain a perfect victory over the Bastardhall Curse (see @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.iIIzG8EEQwsCV7an]{Secret Ending}), but it also invests the PCs with divine intercession.

The missing artwork and the locations where they can be found in Bastardhall are listed in the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.kKMa229quJDLEUfk#lost-artwork]{Adventure Toolbox}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.e0n7TTSgcI69OaYX]{Display Table}

Upon returning the 13th piece of artwork, in addition to the additional benefits listed in Reward below, a sudden flash of light draws attention to the central portion of the display table that runs the length of the middle of the gallery. Here, a pure soulheart has appeared. The first PC to touch the soulheart immediately understands how to activate this potent treasure.

Reward

Each time a PC returns a missing piece of artwork, that PC gains a variant of @UUID[Item.tilqIbJZLqeknTYo]{Shelyn's Minor Boon}—the next time that PC rolls a failure on a Diplomacy check, they get a critical success instead (at which point the boon fades). A PC can earn this boon multiple times, but if they already have the boon, it’s granted to a different PC in the party who doesn’t. If all PCs currently have the boon, no boon is granted for that work’s return.

Upon returning the 13th piece of art, instead of granting Shelyn’s minor boon, every PC is granted Shelyn’s moderate boon: they all gain the @UUID[Item.QLeMH5mQgh28sa5o]{Specialty Crafting} feat and @UUID[Item.lFwfUvH2708rl6i3]{Virtuosic Performer} feat in all categories of Crafting and Performance as bonus feats.

In addition, a 14th piece of art appears as well—a large painting of Bastardhall that floats in the air in the middle of the chamber at a level where it can be properly viewed only while on the upstairs balcony. Closer inspection reveals the vague shape of something with wings circling in the clouds above Bastardhall.
