A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EwgTZBWsc8qKaViP]{Investigates} the painting for a few minutes and then succeeds at a @Check[arcana|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} realizes this vague shape is that of a dragon, while a critical success allows them to identify it as a despair dragon. Grant the PCs 80 XP for returning all 13 pieces of art.

Trophy Hall.name: Trophy Hall
Trophy Hall.text:
The decor of this large hall leaves no mystery as to its function—this is a trophy hall. The walls are adorned with a wide range of mounted animals and monsters. An elegant bow is mounted on a display to the left of the fireplace, while to the right is a gnarled wooden staff carved with animal motifs. Yet the most astonishing decorations here are the three taxidermied creatures on display—an immense boar, an equally immense tarantula, and a black-and-red striped five-headed serpent the size of an elephant. A fourth display platform equal in size to the multi-headed serpent sits empty.

Over the generations, the trophies on display here were routinely swapped out as the castle’s newest lords replaced their ancestors’ triumphs with their own. Lord Raudltz, himself a talented taxidermist among his other hobbies, preserved all of the creatures on display here, but he never completed his work on the allosaurus he wanted to display on the empty stand (see area @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.UYzcuhyFPr5jTxCy]{E14}). The other displays of note include a daeodon, a giant tarantula, and a five-headed hydra.

The west door at area D15a leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1j}. The east door at area D15b leads to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1l}. The doors at the bottom of the stairs to the south at area D15c lead to area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.1O4BfvPuyfyznvYR]{A20}.

Encounter

Moderate 8

@UUID[Actor.htHIpxVMhoHrGiDu]{Arth Wiltur} @UUID[Actor.uNNOQFvuMq8ZsQkn]{Great White Shark x2}

Creatures: If the PCs enter this room at any time other than between the hours of 4:00 and 6:00 in the morning, the trophy hall is empty save for four servitor phantoms bustling about the place as they sweep, dust, and mop. In addition to any aid the phantoms might give the PCs (see @UUID[.bYyP1moxduDE7caw#servitor-phantoms-in-reception]{Servitor Phantoms in Reception}), they helpfully inform them that the scheduled fishing expedition won’t be gathering here until the early hours of the morning (between 4 and 6 a.m.), and that the PCs should return around that time if they wish to accompany the castle’s master of the hunt out onto Lake Laroba.

When the PCs enter this room during the aforementioned hours (even though by this point, “dawn” happens much later in the morning), they find that the room is occupied by a large number of phantasmal guests who mill about the room with tankards of ale in hand as they boisterously share improbable fishing stories with one another. While these tipsy fishers are all ghostly and harmless, one small, energetic, and foul-mouthed figure is an exception. The scene here echoes one of the typical all-day lake fishing expeditions that Castle Arudora’s master of the hunt, Arth Wiltur, enjoyed organizing.

Before the curse befell him, Arth was a strapping hunter who excelled at seeking prey on land and water alike, and his all-day excursions onto the lake were well loved by a cast of regular guests both because they allowed them to enjoy the lake while fishing in the small fleet of boats Arth kept, and because they afforded them the chance to engage in an early- morning round of libations and boasting. It’s just such a preliminary gathering that the PCs find themselves attending at this time.

While the curse struck in the early evening, Arth and his dozen eager fishers manifest here every morning to prepare for a trip they’ll never take. Unlike the visitors, though, Arth was transformed by the curse into a surly, fishing-themed fey known as a culdewen. Now about half his original size, Arth is twice as foul-mouthed and boastful as before, and he greets the PCs with a profanity-laden but good-natured greeting, welcoming them as “the morning’s stragglers” and chiding them for what he perceives to have been a choice to sleep in rather than prepare for the day’s excursion. He gestures toward the several kegs of Arudora ale with a wave of his hand, inviting the PCs to pour themselves drinks and then asking them to share their most outlandish fishing or hunting stories with the group.

If even one PC passes on the drink or the chance to tell stories, Arth hefts an oar and grows even more foul-mouthed and short-tempered, wondering aloud if perhaps that character would rather entertain the other guests with a bit of old-fashioned brawling. If a PC who passed on the drinking and boasting also passes on this final option, Arth’s eyes narrow, and he puffs up his chest before saying the following.

“Looks like we’ve got lily-livered landlubbers here, mates. No worries. We know how to handle lubbers like these. They don’t wanna go to the water, well, let’s bring the water to them! Along with Gasher and Frenzy... the two who got away!”

With this, the entire room suddenly seems to flood with water, although the “water” is, like the guests, nothing more than an unusual phantasm—the PCs can continue to breathe normally and cannot “swim” in the water. This isn’t the case for Arth Wiltur or for the two immense great white sharks that manifest at his side. Each of these sharks has several hooks dangling from their jaws and fins—the two legends that “got away” from him in his previous life. Though they “swim” through the phantasmal water with ease, both of these curse-conjured creatures are very much physical threats, and they attack the closest PC targets each round. Arth hangs back, attacking the PCs at range with his fish hook, and Swears. Neither he nor his sharks can pursue PCs out from this area, but they otherwise fight to the death. If the PCs escape and return the next morning, they find the scene reset and Arth both healed of his wounds and with no memory of the previous combat. If all the PCs agree to drink and boast, or if those who don’t instead agree to a brawl, they must each engage in the Entertain the Fishers activity below. There are 12 fishers in all, and to appease them and Arth, they must all be entertained.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Flood Trophy Hall" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to reveal the ghostly water tile!

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.276zNoegM7xXuEIw]{Entertain the Fishers}

@Embed[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.276zNoegM7xXuEIw inline]

If, after the last PC’s attempt to entertain, any of the 12 fishers aren’t entertained, then Arth shakes his head in disappointment and issues his challenge before attacking alongside the two conjured sharks. Once he and the sharks are defeated, or as soon as the PCs entertain all 12 fishers, Arth, the phantasmal fishers, and the sharks all fade away, their souls moving on to the afterlife.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.ApESlak4rt6NresM]{Fireplace Display}

The two weapons on display near the fireplace are a greater animal staff and a +1 thundering striking longbow.

Reward

If the PCs manage to entertain Arth and the fishers and resolve this room’s threats without combat, grant them XP as if they’d defeated Arth and the two sharks normally. Note that when the PCs finally compel Alisendra to manifest, she’ll be at a disadvantage because the PCs have successfully stolen away the phantom fishers’ attention.

Lord's Balcony.name: Lord's Balcony
Lord's Balcony.text:
An elegant wooden railing surrounds this balcony, the floor of which is covered with deep mauve carpeting. The main entrance lies twenty feet below. To the east, a set of comfortable-looking chairs sit around a low table on which a few objects sit.

Areas D16a and D16b both lead down to area @UUID[.goyxlKit1QLHYYuh]{D1}.

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.buABPmUgUvhWxVaS]{Servitor Phantoms x2}

Creatures: A pair of servitor phantoms quietly work to clean these balconies, judiciously ignoring any events that take place in the entrance hall below. They react as detailed in @UUID[.bYyP1moxduDE7caw#servitor-phantoms-in-reception]{Servitor Phantoms in Reception} to any PCs who approach them.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.MubGKRPvqtxzQRoG]{Tabletop}

The balcony at area D16c was set up for visitors to relax and enjoy drinks or snacks. From here, the view of the lake and far shore is remarkable, but of greater interest are the lesser clarity goggles that sit on the tabletop along with a few empty plates and mugs.

Visitor's Walkway.name: Visitor's Walkway
Visitor's Walkway.text: This open-air walkway connects the reception halls’ upper floor to the arrival plaza and is the primary route through which important visitors and guests entered Castle Arudora. The symbolism of “never having to set foot on the common castle grounds” was not lost on most of those who arrived via carriage over the Laroba Causeway. The sides of this walkway have 3-foot-tall stone railings, beyond which is a 20-foot drop into the castle yard below.

Ruined Conservatory.name: Ruined Conservatory
Ruined Conservatory.text:
None of the glass that once lined the walls and roof of this conservatory remains intact, resulting in an interior strewn with jagged shards. Two lines of planter boxes that may have once held a wide array of foliage are now broken and ruined.

Encounter

Low 8

@UUID[Actor.N2OqLnVCfvuWYez1]{Weak Dezullon}

Creature: One plant has survived in this conservatory thanks to a buried source of sinister nutrition. This plant is a dezullon, and even though it’s survived, it’s weaker than a normal one, with its leaves appearing brittle and its coloration a mix of grays and browns. Still, the monstrous plant hungers, and as soon as anyone enters the conservatory, it lurches forward to attack. The dezullon pursues fleeing PCs even down into the castle grounds or out to the haunted shore, but it won’t chase them indoors.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.5eu2PJYePje94XRw]{Conservatory Cache}

Carefully searching the interior of the conservatory takes an hour of work. Still, such a Search is fruitful, for a PC who conducts it discovers a +1 striking vitalizing sickle that was left behind and buried by fallen glass and dead plants. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in the northernmost portion of the conservatory can find the sickle much more quickly with a successful @Check[perception|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check.

The same search turns up a dormant vile remnant buried in the soil under the place where the dezullon had been lurking for years. In fact, it was this corrupt artifact that helped to keep the dezullon alive all these years by maintaining it with just enough supernatural energy to keep it from withering away entirely.

Groundskeeper's Tower.name: Groundskeeper's Tower
Groundskeeper's Tower.text:
This tower chamber seems to have served as storage for grounds-keeping tools, although most of what was once kept here is now long ruined.

The stairs lead down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.7eQTwEElJ8KZ4KY0]{C8} of the castle cellars.

Arrival Plaza.name: Arrival Plaza
Arrival Plaza.text:
Before you describe this plaza, note that the creature that dwells here has used a 5th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HBJPsonQnWcC3qdX]{Mirage} to make the area look like an overgrown swamp—the spell has made the towers and support pillars appear as trees and the ruined wagons as thick tangles of brambles. Once a PC disbelieves the illusion, the following read-aloud text applies.

This plaza is open to the air, while stone platforms and two towers rise up to support an opaque ghostly structure that looms above. To the west, an even more impressive spectral structure extends out over the lake—a fifty-foot-wide causeway of green, flickering ectoplasm that seems to reach the far side of the lakeshore. On the plaza itself, no fewer than ten brightly colored, gaudy, and decrepit carnival wagons have been tucked away wherever there’s room, leaving barely any space for more carriages or horses to pass through.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Disbelieve Swamp Illusion" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to hide the swamp illusion and reveal this area for what it is!

The ghostly image of the Lake Laroba Causeway flickers into view once the reception halls are unlocked, but the causeway itself is nothing more than a ghostly image until the Bastardhall Curse is lifted—any attempt to step onto the causeway results in a fall to the castle grounds 40 feet below. The stairs in the tower at area D20a lead down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.JdWKi5eQMFgU0eFf]{B16b}, while those in the tower at area D20b lead to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.JdWKi5eQMFgU0eFf]{B16e}. At area D20c, an open-air ramp leads down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1d} of the castle grounds, while the doors at area D20d open into area @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.k9ECGjicvbLkrZvs]{J2}. Until the castle towers are unlocked, however, opening these doors reveals only an impassible wall of green mist.

The wagons all bear colorful signs and banners that proclaim they belong to a traveling carnival called Mister Moxie’s Traveling Oddities. All wagons have slowly crumbled into disrepair, the passage of time taking its toll, but if the PCs take 10 minutes to Investigate them, they can tell that this group of traveling entertainers focused on transporting strange creatures around and showing them off to paying customers. Among their most interesting offerings were an “astounding great ape” from Mwangi, a “man-eating lion” from Katapesh, “terrifying birds of terror” from the Shackles, and—housed in the most devastated wagon—a sign promising the horrors of the legendary “Mushfens Monster.” Other wagons that obviously belonged to different entertainers rather than to strange beasts from distant lands include the following: an escape artist called “Danrasteian the Magnificent,” the fortune-teller “Madame Skerzana and her All-Seeing Eyes,” someone known as “Grampa Sizzle, the Fire-Breathing Clown,” and the troupe’s manager, “Mister Moxie, Purveyor of Wonders and Whimsies.” The PCs can encounter most of the troupe’s members elsewhere in Bastardhall, but one of them has remained here.

Mister Moxie’s pride and joy, as well as his most dangerous exhibit, was a horned ceratosaurus dinosaur that was a secret exhibit in a different traveling menagerie bound for Magnimar via ship. All of the ship’s passengers perished when it sank in a storm a day out from port, but the ceratosaurus made it to shore and into the Mushfens. The dinosaur thrived, and rumors of the “Mushfens Monster” spread quickly through Magnimar’s farmlands until Mister Moxie and his hunters captured it, then made it the centerpiece of their menagerie. Thereafter, they traveled east, eventually reaching Ustalav, where the entire show went missing along with the rest of Bastardhall in 4213. The disappearance was a big deal at the time, and a PC can recall the story Mister Moxie and the Mushfens Monster if they succeed at a @Check[society|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}.

Encounter

Low 8

@UUID[Actor.XwUby1tFKvbakwLR]{The Mushfens Monster}

Creature: Of course, Charg’s influence wasn’t content to leave the Mushfens Monster merely a dinosaur, and on the night his curse swept through the castle, the ceratosaurus was transformed into a very real and cunning actual monster—a tikbalang. In his new form, the Mushfens Monster retains his saurian head (complete with short nasal horn), but his body looks unsettlingly hairy and humanoid. The Mushfens Monster’s mirage spell functions at 5th-rank. He hides in the ruins of his old wagon to the north, observing the PCs as they approach, then uses Change Shape to adopt the appearance of a human man and calls out for help.

The creature pretends to be stuck in the thorns and promises to lead the PCs to a treasure he’s hidden away if they can rescue him (claiming to be the eponymous Mister Moxie if they ask for a name); he leads only one PC there, however, as he claims to trust one of that PC’s specific features (their ancestry or their apparent class).

If the PCs let the party member the Mushfens Monster chooses be led away to the treasure, the monster leads the PC out to the haunted shore and out of sight before assuming his true form and attacking them. Afterward, he changes shape again to disguise himself as that PC. Since he can’t assume a specific creature’s form, he assumes that PC’s ancestral form, then does his best to disguise himself in their gear and clothing before returning to the rest of the PCs to repeat his divide and conquer plot. As soon as anyone sees through his deception (or if the PCs simply refuse to be split up), he roars in frustration, assumes his true form, and attacks. He’ll pursue PCs relentlessly, even chasing them into the castle, but he gives up the chase if the PCs remain out of sight for at least a minute. If reduced to fewer than 50 HP, he attempts to flee and hide himself, seeking somewhere on the haunted shore to take shelter, rest, recover, and then seek revenge on the party.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.XppDngWh2SUumlE9]{Ruined Wagons} @UUID[Actor.vm9qViseCBijqmpf]{Embedded Gear}

If the PCs spend a half hour Searching the ruined wagons, they’ll uncover 70 gp in assorted coins and minor valuables along with the illusionist’s hat Mister Moxie sometimes used to augment his collection. They also find a suit of garishly colored blue, yellow, and red +1 resilient studded leather armor that he left behind, as he always did, when putting on shows. In addition, the PCs find a bronze gear embedded in the wall near the doorway at area D20d. A successful @Check[athletics|dc:28] check is required to wrest the gear free from where it became lodged after being hurled from the temple. See @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

Visitor's Study.name: Visitor's Study
Visitor's Study.text:
A pair of brick fireplaces stand vigil in this study, which also features several couches, chairs, and low coffee tables for visitors to relax. A shelf along the east wall contains several books, although they’re stacked somewhat haphazardly. A pair of elegant silver candleholders stand on the central table.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.1CTRFtAl7QpOZC9s]{Central Table} @UUID[Actor.0omc0khXpNqQtYjg]{Hidden Stash}

The two silver candleholders are each worth 5 gp, but the true treasure in this room is hidden in a secret panel on the southern fireplace’s mantel. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} near the fireplace or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the room for 10 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check notices the hidden latch that opens a small nook in which someone stashed several rings, necklaces, and other small pieces of jewelry. In all, the pieces here is worth 140 gp, but one of the items is a moderate armory bracelet that still retains a charm for a bow, club, flail, knife, polearm, spear, and sword.

Laroba Bar.name: Laroba Bar
Laroba Bar.text:
A long countertop runs along the east side of this drinking room, while opposite it sit three tables with built-in benches. The wall past the bar contains a wealth of shattered bottles as well as a few that still seem to contain some sort of liquid. A single softly glowing gemstone sits between two of these still-filled bottles.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.sCNErTRquVfbZnAT]{Wall of Drinks} @UUID[Actor.qumtpXxvAQvTQwXF]{Bar}

There’s 19 surviving bottles on the shelves here, but of those, a dozen have gone bad. Of the remaining seven bottles, five have aged well and are worth 20 gp apiece—as long as they remain unopened, at least!

The glowing crystal is a greater soulheart. Its presence has transformed the full bottles to either side of it into potions of quickness. The first PC to touch the greater soulheart receives a brief memory of Aron Mordimus and his lover Brensen Firecask having a long, friendly debate at the bar about what sort of alcohol went best with the view of Lake Laroba. Aron favored much less intense drinks than Brensen, who saw the lake as something to be wary of.

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} near the bar and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check or who Searches the room for 10 minutes discovers a leatherbound ledger tucked into a niche behind the bar. This ledger was used to track visitors’ drink preferences, behaviors, and other tidbits so the servants could customize their services to repeat visitors, but a fair amount of space has been devoted to notes taken on Augsten Arudora, whose frequent visits to bully the staff in front of visitors he felt would be impressed warranted extensive documentation. None of the notes in the ledger were written in such a way that someone (like Augsten himself) would realize what was being tracked at a glance. The PCs can use them to research Augsten.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.7ZSvhlTTOzKZNUJZ]{Augsten Arudora}

Laroba Bar Ledger: The PCs spend an hour poring over the ledger to decipher the coded notes about Augsten Arudora that the servants were collecting in their search for potential leverage for some future confrontation that never came to pass.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[labor-lore|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to intuitively understand the type of metaphors used by the help, @Check[society|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to decipher the coded writing, or @Check[perception|dc:29|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to stumble upon passages that just happen to make sense.

Visitor's Lounge.name: Visitor's Lounge
Visitor's Lounge.text:
This comfortable-looking room features several chairs and low tables, a pair of sofas, and a large fireplace in the corner. A faint red light pulses from under the ashes and dust in the fireplace.

Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.Nsxqf22Ox43lWuNA]{No Light Shall Guide Thee}

The flickering glow in the ashes comes from the 24 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.lfrhhbTG1nf0fNAQ]{evercursed crystals} that the will-o’-wisps took from the light sources in the upper halls (area @UUID[.I5xBZSgIpeHNyb21]{D21}). While these individual items are of little value to the PCs, their concentrated presence here has interacted with the ambient curse energies of Bastardhall, resulting in an accumulation of malign magic that lashes out at anyone who disturbs the ashes.

Temple's View.name: Temple's View
Temple's View.text:
This open-air plaza offers a narrow view of the castle grounds to the northwest and is otherwise surrounded by the looming castle in all other directions. Providing a view doesn’t seem to be the primary purpose of this area, however. Instead, it seems to have been set up to host a small traveling carnival and features three large tents and a wooden platform on which a structure similar to a gallows has been erected. Signs above the tents and gallows describe their one-time attractions.

A pair of wooden tables with built-in benches provide seating areas, while to the north, near a ramp leading down to the castle courtyard, sits a large brick oven near a grilling station. A few dozen crates and barrels marked with the traveling carnival’s colors of green and purple have been stacked against the southern wall.

This area, referred to as “Temple’s View” back in the day for how the castle’s temple and clocktower loomed overhead (these remain ghostly, hazy manifestations until the temple is unlocked), was one of Alisendra’s favorite places to host outdoor events if the weather permitted it. As it so happened, she’d engaged the services of a traveling troupe of entertainers and animal trainers called Mister Moxie’s Traveling Oddities and tasked them with setting up a truncated version of their larger carnival offerings in the plaza to entertain the numerous guests who had gathered for one of the many other events she’d organized in the castle.

If the PCs arrive here after dark, they find the tents and outdoor furnishings to be ragged and in tatters and discover nothing of note to investigate (save for the additional treasures that could be discovered in the containers to the south). Likewise, observing the plaza from afar during the day gives the impression of abandonment, but if the PCs set foot onto the plaza during the day, the space suddenly shimmers and appears to be freshly set up and ready for visitors. Ghostly images of phantasmal guests mill about the plaza, engaging in muted applause or cooing quietly at the entertainment, but the PCs quickly find themselves called to by one of the four acts being put on by Mister Moxie and his crew. These acts are detailed below under the expanded information for areas @UUID[.qd0rZC81vsO1ai2z]{D26c}–@UUID[.gUDPxoJcihKYLZRq]{D26f}.

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.7KhhBPqRFYMDZmtm]{Servitor Phantoms x2}

Area D26a leads down to area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.h3vd0Lg6iWiJDQU5]{B1g} of the castle grounds. If the PCs arrive after dark, they encounter a pair of servitor phantoms here, bustling about as they clean the place for the next day’s performances; they react to the PCs as detailed in @UUID[.bYyP1moxduDE7caw#servitor-phantoms-in-reception]{Servitor Phantoms in Reception} and suggest they come back tomorrow to take part in Mister Moxie’s extravaganza. Area D26b is a grilling station with an outdoor fireplace. During the day, the two servitor phantoms are stationed here, theoretically cooking snacks and handing them out—now, the meals are ghostly phantoms of what they once were.

Areas @UUID[.qd0rZC81vsO1ai2z]{D26c}, @UUID[.GBDZrpXoEXkQKLZT]{D26d}, @UUID[.fk4G37Tug5dnKsd9]{D26e}, @UUID[.gUDPxoJcihKYLZRq]{D26f} are detailed separately, but note that if the PCs start a fight with any of the creatures found here, all four groups swiftly team up against the party, resulting in a Moderate 8 encounter.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.6vywIBQ5Z01sK2If]{Carnival Crates}

A PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} through the crates, luggage, and barrels stacked tightly in area D26 finds that most of them contain food, water, supplies, clothing, and other essentials a traveling carnival needs to function, though most of it has decayed into ruin—with two exceptions. In one crate is a brittle leather pouch that contains a dozen shrinking potions (supplies the troupe sometimes needed to transport some of their larger exhibits through tight confines), while in another are a pair of brightly colored boots of bounding (an item the troupe’s clown sometimes used for acts where they had more room to spread out).

Reward

Each of the occupants of the individual attractions in the plaza have a challenge for the PCs to attempt. If the PCs can win at least three of these four challenges, their presence in Moxie’s carnival is disruptive enough to shift focus to them. In this case, note that when the PCs finally compel Alisendra to manifest, she’ll be at a disadvantage because they’ve stolen away the attention of the entertainers and their ghostly audience.

Birds and Beasts.name: Birds and Beasts
Birds and Beasts.text:
Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.fBZJxqMpEDzvDjwv]{Big Ardus}

The sign above this tent reads, “Behold! Birds and Beasts of Garund!” Within, three iron-barred cages originally displayed a lion, a gorilla, and a pair of terror birds; each of the cages is surrounded by curtains that can be individually raised or lowered and that allow for one creature to be shown at a time while also blocking line of sight between the cages to help keep their occupants calm.

Mister Moxie sold his gorilla to the castle’s groundskeeper, Milsindi, on the day the curse fell over the castle (see area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.2tXKE2JE45z1vCAd]{C38}), and in the mayhem that ensued when the curse took hold, the two terror birds escaped and became the cockatrices now found in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.O2hrZos99pNTSbdj]{C47}), leaving only the “man-eating lion” behind. The curse worked its power on this hapless great cat as well, transforming it into a dweomercat. The transformed lion’s first act was to eat the carnival’s trainer, Big Ardus, and in doing so, it gained Big Ardus’s voice and memories. Now, it exists in a strange dual role of exhibit and exhibitor.

When the PCs first enter this tent, the curtains for all three cages are parted, and all three cage doors are open. Big Ardus sprawls in a reclining pose in the middle of the northern cage but perks up as he notices the PCs. In a loud, boisterous voice, he apologizes for the lack of exhibits, claiming, “My precious pets done all run off, I’m afraid. Well... apart from me, but I done ate myself, too. Guess that’s a worthy sight, though! Come! See the lion tamer eaten by his lion and become his lion!”

With a raspy chuckle, Big Ardus tells the PCs that he’s eager to put some new creatures on display here and asks the party to help him out. If they can capture something worth of putting on display in one of his cages, then transport it back here alive, he promises not to put them into the cages for the guests’ entertainment! If the PCs agree to the task, Big Ardus notes that “anything will do, as long as it’s larger than you or I!” Any Large creature delivered alive (or in the case of undead creatures, still animated) to be placed in a cage fulfills Big Ardus’s request. If the PCs balk, he gives a feline shrug, then says, “I suppose that Mister Moxie’s illusionist’s hat would do just as well. It doesn’t make real monsters, but these rubes won’t know the difference. Problem is, I’m not sure where he left it. Bring me his hat, and that’ll do fine enough.” The illusionist’s hat can be found in area @UUID[.Xo2d6jZMY7tW2fwP]{D20}.

If the PCs refuse to help Big Ardus, he shrugs again, then says, “Well, I’ll be here if you change your minds. And no refunds if you paid to see the monsters!” If the PCs point out they didn’t pay to enter the tent, he smirks. “Good on you all, then!”

The dweomercat only attacks if the PCs attack him first, in which case his roars and yowls are easily loud enough to bring the occupants of areas @UUID[.GBDZrpXoEXkQKLZT]{D26d}, @UUID[.fk4G37Tug5dnKsd9]{D26e}, and @UUID[.gUDPxoJcihKYLZRq]{D26f} running to join the fight. In combat, Big Ardus prefers to focus his attacks on spellcasters—particularly Small spellcasters, but if any PC carries a whip, he targets them first. Big Ardus fights to the death.

Reward

If the PCs satisfy Big Ardus’s request, they win the challenge. The dweomercat purrs in delight, then fades away, the joint souls of both lion and man at last free to move on to the afterlife. Grant the PCs XP as if they’d defeated the dweomercat in combat; if they satisfied the request by delivering the illusionist’s hat, they can then reclaim the treasure for themselves.

Danrasteian the Magnificent.name: Danrasteian the Magnificent
Danrasteian the Magnificent.text:
The sign above this gallows-like device reads “Witness the Strength of Mum’s Embrace!” The contraption itself has been built on a wooden platform and is a stage prop used for daring exhibitions of escape. It consists of a square wooden frame from which dangle several chains attached to manacles, belts, and leather accessories like gloves, hoods, and even a vest. The entire contraption is attached to a set of gimbles and gears that allow it to twist, turn, and periodically tighten or constrict the bindings. It’s a complex contraption, to be sure, and was originally the pride and joy of its inventor, an elven escape artist named Danrasteian the Magnificent. Once one of the most well-known escape artists in the Avistani carnival circuit, a PC can recognize the name with a successful @Check[theater-lore|dc:22|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check or @Check[performance|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}; on a critical success, they even recall reading about his device, which he called “Mum’s Embrace” (this grants that PC a +2 circumstance bonus to checks made to Escape from Mum’s Embrace).

Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.fRjJkktWp7s8NBN7]{Danrasteian the Magnificent}

Creature: When the curse struck, Danrasteian was in the middle of a performance—the curse temporarily animated Mum’s Embrace and made it impossible for him to escape, and over the course of several agonizing hours, his bones were broken and his joints dislocated until he died. He was reincarnated soon afterward as a faceless stalker and now spends his time clambering into Mum’s Embrace, letting the machine bind him tight, then squirming loose—an obsession that sustains him as surely as food or drink ever did in life.

When the PCs first turn their attention to this area, Danrasteian has just escaped from his latest binding in Mum’s Embrace. Appearing in the form of his previous body as a handsome, wiry elven man, his skin glistening with a layer of sweat from his latest escape, he sits down on the steps leading to his device and is in the process of falling into a typical fit of post-escape melancholia. He doesn’t notice the PCs at first as they approach, and they’ll overhear him sighing and muttering under his breath. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:24] check understands enough of his mutterings to know that he is homesick for a place called the “Lost Coast.” If the PC then succeeds at a @Check[society|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to Recall Knowledge, they identify this as a reference to the southwestern coastline of Varisia.

Upon noticing the PCs, Danrasteian hops to his feet and puts on his entertainer’s face, welcoming them to Mister Moxie’s Traveling Oddities and asking if they think they can beat his record in escaping from Mum’s Embrace—a standard lead-in to his performances. If a PC asks Danrasteian about what’s bothering him and succeeds at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:24] check, he admits that he’s homesick and misses the west coast of Varisia. On a critical success, he also admits he “borrowed” some wine from the castle’s hosts but left the bottles in his room, and he shares that there were paintings in the castle’s hall of history that particularly spoke to him, and that the beautiful nephilim medium who recently caught his eye wore a traditional bladed scarf that reminded him of a long lost love. “So many echoes of my home here—enough to give a man dying of thirst a sip of reprieve, but little else!”

If the PCs bring Danrasteian some of these objects, they can distract him with nostalgia. Similar items won’t stack their effects, but for each type they hand over—a painting from area @UUID[.eud7t2JugdlGBTk7]{D3}, a bottle of wine from area @UUID[.fTnqkD249KyhYjdW]{D22}, or the scarf from area @UUID[.YEWYYZfoKnJcqp4j]{D29}—he agrees to grant anyone who attempts to escape from Mum’s Embrace an advantage in the form of an additional minute. In all, if the PCs deliver these three objects (including nostalgic items they might already own, at your discretion), they can earn a maximum of 3 additional minutes to escape. If combat ensues after such a delivery, Danrasteian starts the battle @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for a number of rounds equal to the items delivered (to a maximum of 3) as he’s distracted by his memories.

Normally, no one takes him up on his offer to try escaping from Mum’s Embrace, but if a PCs steps up to the challenge, his expression brightens with delight. He leads the PCs onto the platform, then explains that in order to beat his record, they’ll have to wriggle out of Mum’s Embrace in no less than 3 minutes. If the PC remains willing to try, Danrasteian helps them into the contraption, then pulls the straps and chains tight before winding a set of gears up at the base. Once Danrasteian gives the order to begin, Mum’s Embrace starts to rotate, twist, and stretch the PC, actively working against their escape attempts. Once per minute, the PC can attempt the Escape Mum’s Embrace activity described below. If they escape the device in three minutes or less, Danrasteian is impressed, but if they don’t, he cackles and simply watches, waiting to see how long it takes them to escape and cautioning any other PC against helping out. He even suggests they’ll pay “the ultimate price” if they dare interrupt the day’s entertainment.

Danrasteian only attacks the PCs if they attack him first, if they try to damage Mum’s Embrace, if they attempt to help a trapped PC get free, or in response to any of the area’s other occupants being attacked. If the PCs spur him to attack, his cries of outrage draw the other creatures in the area to his side to aid him. He reverts to his new true form on the first round of combat, but if reduced to fewer than 20 Hit Points, he attempts to flee into the castle and hide. Once he recovers, he may well track down the PCs for revenge, timing his new attack during a point where they’re already facing a different, powerful foe in combat.

Mum’s Embrace has AC 24, Fort +19, Ref +13, Hardness 15, and 62 HP (BT 31).

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.lsrjaHoc5KZs177E]{Escape Mum's Embrace}

  • Exploration

  • Manipulate

You spend a minute attempting to escape from Danrasteian's device even as the contraption works to tighten its bindings and twist you into increasingly uncomfortable positions. Attempt a @Check[thievery|dc:24|options:action:escape-mums-embrace|traits:exploration,manipulate] check to manipulate connectors and fasteners on the device to degrade their hold, a @Check[acrobatics|dc:25|options:action:escape-mums-embrace|traits:exploration,manipulate] check to contort yourself into a more advantageous position, a @Check[athletics|dc:26|options:action:escape-mums-embrace|traits:exploration,manipulate] check to tug at the bindings and loosen their grip, or a @Check[reflex|dc:29|options:action:escape-mums-embrace|traits:exploration,manipulate] save to simply wriggle and stretch in an attempt to squirm free, with the following results. (Any bonus that applies to any attempt to Escape applies to these checks.) Once you earn 3 Freedom Points, you escape!

Critical Success You make significant progress toward escaping and earn 2 Freedom Points.

Success You're on the way to escaping and earn 1 Freedom Point.

Failure You fail to make any progress toward escaping and take @Damage[2d8[bludgeoning]] damage from being twisted up.

Critical Failure As failure, but @Damage[4d8[bludgeoning]] damage. In addition, you must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:24|options:inflicts:drained] save to resist having your @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained} condition value increase by 1 as your bones begin to break and your joints start to dislocate.

Effect

@UUID[Item.Z0QY5fHPXKDFSRui]{Device Knowledge}

Use this effect to automate a PC's bonus to Escape from Mum's Embrace they might have gained from their Recall Knowledge checks.

Reward

If a PC escapes from Mum’s Embrace in time, they win the challenge. Danrasteian gasps in surprise, then fades away as his soul moves on to the afterlife. His gear remains behind. Grant the PCs XP as if they’d defeated him in combat.

The Mushfens Monster.name: The Mushfens Monster
The Mushfens Monster.text:
Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.3DaUib6ncSr0Ay5H]{Mister Moxie}

Creature: The sign above the entrance to this tent reads, “Gaze and Marvel! The Mushfens Monster!” Within, a single iron-barred cage stands empty, the interior strewn with straw and bones caked with dried mud. This cage was originally meant to display the eponymous beast—a ceratosaurus Mister Moxie’s hunters captured in the Mushfens, but which he wasn’t intending to showcase until the last day of his visit to Castle Arudora. When the curse struck on the first night, the Mushfens Monster transformed into a true monster (see area @UUID[.Xo2d6jZMY7tW2fwP]{D20}), leaving Mister Moxie without a finale.

For his part, Mister Moxie was slain by the terror birds he kept in area @UUID[.qd0rZC81vsO1ai2z]{D26c} after they escaped, but after the curse settled, he returned in undeath as a skeletal ringleader known as a bone croupier. When the PCs first enter this tent, they find the skeletal Mister Moxie, his once-flamboyant showman’s outfit ragged, faded, and reeking of decay, gripping the bars of the cage loosely as he leans against them. He presses his skull against the metal as he moans out variations of “Where have you gone, my pet?”

He’s distracted enough that the PCs can gain a +4 circumstance bonus to initiative if they simply attack, but unless they defeat him before he can actually act, his cries of outrage quickly draw the attention of his other allies, who swiftly come to his aid. In battle, he prefers to compel an adjacent foe to Pick a card from his harrow deck then attack with his whip. He fights to the death, but he won’t pursue PCs who flee from the area.

If the PCs don’t attack him, as soon as he notices them, he quickly covers up his melancholy, puffs up his empty chest, and proclaims, “I’m afraid the Mushfens Monster isn’t ready to be seen yet, but I can tell you’re looking for entertainment. Fancy, perhaps, a game of cards?” If the PCs agree, Mister Moxie eagerly explains the rules as he leads the PCs across the way to join him at one of the tables near the area’s eastern wall.

If the PCs know what became of the Mushfens Monster and let Mister Moxie know, he takes the news hard and sobs raggedly before gathering his dignity as best he can. Still, the damage is done, and for the next 24 hours, the bone croupier is distracted—he takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all attack rolls and skill checks during this time.

The game that Mister Moxie proposes is a somewhat complicated and obscure game called Fatesnatcher, which uses a deck of harrow cards and a wide range of tiny colored glass beads. There’s no need to explain the exact rules to the players other than to let them know that it’s an asymmetrical bluffing game that pits a group of prophets (the PCs) against the fickle whims of Pharasma (played by Mister Moxie). When the game begins, Mister Moxie gives each PC 10 glass beads (representing their 10 omens), then shuffles the cards and sets the deck face down on the table. If the PCs have distracted Mister Moxie by telling him about the Mushfens Monster, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus on all checks made to Play Fatesnatcher.

If a PC is about to attempt a check that could win them the game, Mister Moxie cheats by using Change of Luck to force the PC to roll the check twice; he does so only once per game, even if his Change of Luck ability recharges.

Effect

@UUID[Item.yDfz3Al8UOVXLLZ0]{Distracted Mister Moxie}

If the PCs distract Mister Moxie, use this effect to automate their bonus on the checks listed below to Play Fatesnatcher.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.4777eIkPMXyyyqC3]{Play Fatesnatcher}

  • Concentration

  • Exploration

Prophet's Turn: A game of Fatesnatcher plays out over several "ages." During each age, every prophet takes a turn (the PCs can decide in what order they act) by drawing a card from the harrow deck and then using that card as inspiration to spin a fate to Pharasma (Mister Moxie) that catches them by surprise. (At your discretion, you can have the players draw actual harrow cards and use them—if you feel they were particularly creative in coming up with their fate, grant them a +1 circumstance bonus to their skill check to resolve their turn.) The PC then attempts a @Check[games-lore|dc:22|options:action:play-fatesnatcher|traits:concentration,exploration], @Check[deception|dc:24|options:action:play-fatesnatcher|traits:concentration,exploration], or @Check[performance|dc:26|options:action:play-fatesnatcher|traits:concentration,exploration] check with the following results.

Critical Success The PC truly catches Pharasma off-guard. They keep their card and draw a second card from the deck to keep it as a bonus card. Once a PC has collected 10 cards, they win.

Success The PC catches Pharasma off-guard and keeps their card.

Failure The PC fails to catch Pharasma off-guard. They shuffle their card into the deck and lose 2 omens. If at any point a PC has no omens left, they're out of the game.

Critical Failure The PC fails catastrophically; they shuffle their card into the deck and lose [[/gmr 1d4+1#Lost Omens]] omens.

Pharasma's Turn: At the end of each age after every prophet has taken their turn, Pharasma grows more fickle. Mister Moxie attempts a @Check[games-lore|dc:24|options:action:play-fatesnatcher|traits:concentration,exploration] check with the following results. After adjusting DCs for the players as appropriate, play proceeds with the next age until all of the prophets have lost their omens or one prophet manages to achieve 10 fates (10 harrow cards).

Critical Success The DCs for all checks to spin a fate increase by 2.

Success The DCs for all checks to spin a fate increase by 1.

Failure The DCs to spin a fate do not change.

Critical Failure The DCs for all checks to spin a fate decrease by 1.

Losing the Game: The PCs lose the game as soon as all of them are out of omens. In this case, Mister Moxie cackles in delight, his despair at the missing Mushfens Monster forgotten for a few hours, after which he returns to his gloom in the tent. He agrees to play another game of Fatesnatcher with the party after 24 hours have passed, but in the meantime, each PC who played the game must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24|options:action:play-fatesnatcher,inflicts:stupefied|traits:concentration,curse,exploration] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 24 hours (or for an unlimited duration on a critical failure). This is a curse effect.

Winning the Game: The PCs win the game if any of them ever achieve 10 fates (10 harrow cards) or if at any point during the game there are no harrow cards left to draw (you can ignore this win condition if you're not playing with a real harrow deck for PCs to keep track of their fates). Mister Moxie is surprised but then delighted. He offers the winning PC his harrow deck as a prize.

Reward

If a PC wins a game of Fatesnatcher, they win the challenge. Mister Moxie bows in respect, then fades away as his soul moves on to the afterlife. His gear remains behind. Grant the PCs XP as if they’d defeated him in combat.

Sizzling Shenanigans.name: Sizzling Shenanigans
Sizzling Shenanigans.text:
Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.p7pbqkwEQ9EaVWGa]{Grampa Sizzle}

The sign above the entrance to this tent reads, “Gramps and Li’l Sizzle! Fire’s Never Been So Funny!” Within, a wooden stage stands near the western end. Atop it are six shelves filled with torches, oily rags, bottles of alcohol, and other bits of flammable-looking materials. On the other side of the tent, a ghostly crowd of excited onlookers sits on equally ghostly benches, the eager murmuring of their anticipation for the show filling the tent with an air of expectation.

Before the curse took hold, the “two-man act” of Gramps and Li’l Sizzle was performed by one person (“Gramps,” a man named Jordus Bellervin who dressed as an elderly clown) and his ventriloquist’s dummy (“Li’l Sizzle,” a miniature version of Jordus in his clown persona).

Their act consisted of a back-and-forth conversation where they regaled each other with light-hearted tales about fire and the harmless accidents it can cause, all while a group of assistants acted out these “accidents” using the props on stage. Gramps and Li’l Sizzle would react to these reenactments with astonishment, much to the amusement of the audience.

After the curse fell, Jordus was carried off by sahkils and thrown into the fire that consumed the Laroba Bridge. His dummy remained here and transformed into a soulbound doll when Jordus’s soul was bound to it by the curse. Now, the man exists as “Grampa Sizzle,” a combination of his human clown persona and his dummy. While he can still lead his act, it’s all going to flop without his assistants here to play out his shenanigans!

When the PCs first enter the tent, Grampa Sizzle lies in a heap on the stage, only to hop to his tiny feet and open his arms in greeting. In a high-pitched voice, he says, “And here they are! My beautiful arsonists! Come on up, my firebugs, and we’ll get this show started!” If the PCs ask for clarification, Grampa Sizzle sighs dramatically, then explains that they’re to act out the fiery antics described in the four stories he’s about to tell. He claps his hands and urges the party to take their places on the stage. If the PCs refuse, Grampa Sizzle’s eyes narrow and he says, “Excuse me? I must be going deaf in my old age, ’cause it sounded like the help just said they don’t want to help!” If the PCs continue to resist taking part in the act, Grampa Sizzle shrieks in rage—a sound loud enough to draw all the other creatures in the area to his aid—and attacks. Once he starts fighting, Grampa Sizzle is tenacious and pursues the PCs relentlessly. He gives up the chase if he loses track of the PCs for at least a minute, then returns here. Otherwise, he fights to the death.

If the PCs agree to take part in the show, Grampa Sizzle cackles in delight. Once at least two PCs are on the stage, he begins by telling the first of four short anecdotes about fiery shenanigans, pausing after each one to look expectantly at the PCs. At this point, one of the PCs must attempt one of two potential skill checks to act out the scene using the props on stage. While the props themselves are old and not real, the power of the curse infuses them with fire that can burn only flesh—PCs who do poorly in their performance disappoint Grampa Sizzle and get burned in the process!

The PCs can recreate the four scenes by taking part in the Sizzling Shenanigans activity.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.toGmgGDVDhjFruVK]{Sizzling Shenanigans}

  • Concentrate

  • Exploration

  • Manipulate

@Embed[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.toGmgGDVDhjFruVK inline]

Reward

If at the end of the four scenes, the party has accumulated at least 3 Laughter Points, they win the challenge. Grampa Sizzle cackles in delight, then fades away as his soul moves on to the afterlife. Grant the PCs XP as if they’d defeated him in combat.

Hero's Hall.name: Hero's Hall
Hero's Hall.text:
If the PCs approach this door from area @UUID[.I5xBZSgIpeHNyb21]{D21} to the north while that hall is unlit, they’ll automatically notice the light shining around the door’s edges.

This wide hall is well lit by several chandeliers and wall-mounted lanterns. Two stone statues stand in the central stretch of the hall. Both depict the same man—the northern one in a pose as he fights against a winged snake whose coils are wrapped around him while he holds its fangs at bay with a grip on its throat, and the southern one as he strikes a cowering devil down with his sword. Display cases along the wall present smaller scenes of the same hero accomplishing smaller feats of heroism in delicately constructed dioramas.

The man depicted in these statues and dioramas is Eragayl Arudora. Whether or not the scenes of him vanquishing monsters all recount his actual triumphs or if they’ve been embellished has been obscured by the passage of time, but the statues, at least, show two of his more famous triumphs against the Winged Serpent of Redleaf and the wine-poisoning devil of Cesca.

The stairs at area D27a lead up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.ndtRFPlOc0RB3Vc5]{F2b} of the private halls, but until that area is unlocked, the stairs end at a wall of impassible green mist before long. The opposite side of these stairs leads down to area @UUID[.78A34DGpyfbsAqFq]{D7c}.

Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.inA9IHhA3O9CMYQn]{What All Heroes Fear}

Hazard: This hall’s displays, once meant to celebrate the heroic legacies of Eragayl Arudora, have been transformed and corrupted by the Bastardhall Curse. As soon as anyone moves farther into the room, the lights dim (shifting from bright light to dim light), and the scenes depicted shift so that they show Eragayl being savaged and slain by the monsters he should be triumphing over.

Music Room.name: Music Room
Music Room.text:
The walls of this elegant-looking room are decorated in faded wallpaper depicting pastoral scenes, although sagging sheets, tears, and mildew lend the scenes an air of decrepitude. Sofas, chairs, benches, and shelves on which sit a wide array of small musical instruments and books have been placed throughout the room, while three larger musical instruments—a clavichord, harp, and grand piano—rest neglected and dusty.

This space once served as a haven for visiting musicians and for the Arudoras (who, at the time the curse first fell on them, were not particularly musically talented) to entertain smaller groups than those who could gather in the ballroom below. Once upon a time, the musical instruments on display here would have commanded a small fortune, but neglect has reduced most of them to unplayable junk.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.vIutUG9WhLUTPUqo]{Ruined Instruments} @UUID[Actor.SllAwgs7pd9NiHtD]{Inside the Piano}

One exception to the ruined instruments here is a dust-covered but fully functional greater trickster’s mandolin that the PCs can discover if they spend half an hour @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the room, or if they @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} near the northern shelves and succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The instrument hides under a thick layer of dust that can be easily cleaned.

A second treasure can be found here if the PCs spend the same amount of time Searching, or if they Seek near the grand piano in particular. Tucked in a nook inside the piano is a softly glowing greater soulheart. The first PC to touch the greater soulheart receives a brief memory of Esmira Vermidian playing a beautiful rhapsody for a small group of astonished aristocrats who obviously didn’t expect a woman from Maiserene to have such talent.

Game Room.name: Game Room
Game Room.text:
The decor of this space leaves no doubt as to its purpose—this was a well-furnished game room, complete with tables for playing cards or dice, shelves of gaming supplies, a billiards table, and five free-standing cabinet-like contraptions that feature various gaudy paintings and moving parts. A large fireplace looms to the west.

This room was a favorite place for small groups of castle guests to retire when the Arudora-provided entertainment grew too exhausting or bland—here, they could entertain themselves by taking part in one of many games. These supplies have largely fallen into disrepair, including the five clockwork cabinets, all of which were imported from a toy-maker in Absalom.

Each of these contraptions once allowed a player to manipulate the passage of a small brass figurine through a maze filled with various obstacles by manipulating levers and buttons, with the goal being to reach the end of the maze before the clockwork game’s winding ran down and the cabinet’s “guardian” (a dragon, a demon, a grim reaper, a leprechaun, or a Red Mantis assassin) would leap out like a jack- in-the-box to startle the player. These devices have stood the test of time and still function (with the exception of the assassin-themed game—see below), but they provide little actual benefit other than fun and relaxation. A PC who wants to play one of these games can do so by succeeding at a @Check[games-lore|dc:26] or @Check[perception|dc:28] check—during play, the PC gets [[/gmr 1d4#Number of attempts]] attempts before the guardian pops up.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.kNKfE3J0id288VO0]{Inside the Machine}

A PC who attempts to play the Red Mantis assassin–themed game finds that the contraption doesn’t seem to want to wind up. A successful @Check[crafting|dc:24|traits:concentrate,secret] check or @Check[perception|dc:28|traits:concentrate,secret] check made during a five-minute Investigation of the device allows the PC to discern why after they figure out how to remove one of the side panels—someone’s hidden a small but beautiful framed painting inside the machine. This painting depicts an elven man who’s dissecting himself, revealing that his interior is made of clockwork gears. The painting is Light Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it triggers a memory of Raudltz Arudora shaking his head in frustration upon first seeing this commissioned work, complaining that “the interior workings aren’t lifelike enough” while Alisendra assures him that it’ll look lovely in the gallery nevertheless. The painting itself was stolen by a guest who hoped to make off with it later in the evening and hid it here for safekeeping for the rest of the day, only to have the curse disrupt her plans. Of course, this painting belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}); see @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{Lost Artwork} for more details.

Spirit Chambers.name: Spirit Chambers
Spirit Chambers.text:
While this is technically a single large room, several heavy dark purple curtains are drawn along runners built into the ceiling to separate areas off from each other. Among Alisendra’s many interests was communicating with the dead—particularly the spirit of her first lover, a Varisian scoundrel named Vittorio Vancaskerkin. Raudltz was her second husband and a marriage more of financial opportunity than love, but Alisendra hoped some day to draw back Vittorio’s spirit so that he could possess Raudltz, allowing her to enjoy the best of both worlds. Many of the séances she held were private, invitation-only affairs—Alisendra had a small revolving list of mediums she trusted and invited only her closest friends to take part. She also understood, though, that other guests would likely want to seek answers from beyond as well, so she increasingly set up séances for visitors to enjoy.

Each individual part of this room is detailed separately in pages @UUID[.urM7BN4NgpXJYVdO]{D30a} to @UUID[.mp2jSvvSVejhua2M]{D30f}. The set of rooms here are unlit during the day, with curtains drawn tightly over what windows exist.

Foyer.name: Foyer
Foyer.text:
The floor of this room is carpeted in deep crimson, while the walls are paneled in dark red wood with black highlights. A pair of wood-carved statues of Pharasma stand in the corners to either side of the door, while to the south, thick purple curtains hang between the walls and pillars. Two round tables to the southeast and southwest hold seven unlit candles and two silver candleholders between them.

Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.GT0G3ELbvhtfCw1A]{Servitor Phantoms x2}

Creatures: During the day, a pair of servitor phantoms stand quietly in this room. They greet the PCs as detailed in @UUID[.bYyP1moxduDE7caw#servitor-phantoms-in-reception]{Servitor Phantoms in Reception} but also inform them that Madame Blackwell’s séance isn’t scheduled to start until 9:00 that night. They suggest the PCs return at that time if they wish to ask questions “of the beyond.”

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.qiWezeQWtNSrRRZN]{Tables}

Both of the silver candleholders are worth 20 gp each.

Waiting Room.name: Waiting Room
Waiting Room.text:
An immense stone fireplace towers against the eastern wall, with four tall-backed chairs around a low table facing it. Farther west, two long sofas sit to either side of another low table. Curtains line most of the room’s walls, while two free-standing bars loaded with dusty green bottles bearing yellow and red labels are to the south.

This room was a place for séance attendees to gather before the event to prepare their questions or discuss the answers afterward. If it’s after 9:00 p.m. but before 3:00 a.m. and the PCs make noise here or start lighting up the room, Madame Blackwell calls to them from area @UUID[.mp2jSvvSVejhua2M]{D30f}, alerting her visitors that she’s “ready to begin” when they are.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.ICaVvncftUW82ywb]{Waiting Room Carts}

The bottles of alcohol on the carts have aged well. There are a dozen bottles in all, each worth 10 gp.

The Approach.name: The Approach
The Approach.text:
Wooden statues of Pharasma have been placed to the north and south of this area, each carrying an unlit black candle.

If it’s between 9:00 p.m. and 3:00 a.m., Madame Blackwell calls out from area @UUID[.mp2jSvvSVejhua2M]{D30f}, advising those who wish to ask her questions to each take a candle, light it, and then step forward to “join the circle.”

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.Qckvy1hQJB3JmMVZ]{Pharasma Statues}

The candles are key parts of the séance and worth 5 gp each if unlit.

Candle Storage.name: Candle Storage
Candle Storage.text:
A shelf along the north wall here contains dozens of candles of various sizes.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.XcbhAjDgk50m7wPl]{Candle Shelf}

These candles are used to light the séance rooms and are rare and valuable; in all, there’s 150 gp worth of rare candles for use in casting call spirit here.

Miscellaneous Storage.name: Miscellaneous Storage
Miscellaneous Storage.text:
A shelf along the south wall stores a wide range of small objects, including but not limited to: incense, sheets of paper, vials of ink, various bottles, listening trumpets, slates, jars of chalk and salt, and more.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.JECWnlI5QkZfNQ8q]{Ritual Supplies Shelf}

Candles aren’t the only supplies that mediums use to run séances, and those other materials were kept here. These materials aren’t magical in and of themselves, but they’re worth a combined total value of 150 gp for the casting of rituals like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gsYEuWv04XTDxe91]{Call Spirit}.

Séance Chamber.name: Séance Chamber
Séance Chamber.text:
Curtains surround all of this red carpeted room’s walls, while in the far corners are wooden stands atop which sit empty silver candleholders. In the middle of the room, a long polished oak table is surrounded by five high-backed chairs.

If it’s not after 9:00 p.m. but before 3:00 a.m., this area is empty.

Encounter

Moderate 8

@UUID[Actor.qLUE00lfPwlt5dNM]{Amyleda Blackwell} @UUID[Actor.VotlWUsFKdOrHWF6]{Shadows x2}

Creature: On the night the curse took hold, one of Alisendra’s favorite mediums, a woman she regarded as a close friend, was ready to perform one of her séances here. Unknown to Alisendra, this medium was a con artist named Amyleda Blackwell, who used a combination of her cambion heritage and prodigious talent for performance to fund her extravagant tastes in entertainment by giving rich patrons what they wanted in exchange for money. Even as she prepared for the night’s ceremony (which would have been a precursor to one of Alisendra’s monthly séances and meant to entertain some well-connected guests), Amyleda managed to snatch a valuable art object from the gallery as a “bonus” to her pay.

When the curse hit Amyleda, it seized not just her deceptive nature and treacherous personality, but her supernatural heritage as well. The result was something that normally requires dying—a trip to the Boneyard and time spent in the Outer Rifts.

Consequently, it transformed her into a demon. Amyleda is now a succubus, although rather than feeding off mortal passions, she instead specializes in drawing out emotions from lovers left behind after their paramours have perished. As one who preys upon widows and widowers, Amyleda found a particularly easy mark in Alisendra, who, despite her recent marriage to Raudltz, secretly still pined for her first lover’s embrace.

Amyleda sits at the head of the table, taking no steps to hide her demonic appearance. Otherwise presenting herself as she did in life, she holds her arms out wide in welcome, a deck of harrow cards in one hand and a colorful bladed scarf draped over her shoulders and sparkling gown. She welcomes the PCs to voice their heart’s lost desires, then bids them to place their candles in the four candle holders before they have a seat with her at the table. If there are more than four PCs, she waves aside additional candles and suffers the wait while PCs drag additional chairs from area @UUID[.A9DrS1Z5IFpbDj3n]{D30b} into the room. Conversely, if there are fewer than four PCs, she asks that they light four candles in all and says she can still perform the séance with even a single PC.

If the PCs attempt to question Amyleda, she holds a hand up for silence, stating the following.

“I know you’re here for questions, but I can’t answer them. Only messengers from the beyond can give you what you seek. These specific harrow cards are finely attuned to the spirit world, and with them, I can guide those spirits here... with your participation, of course!”

If the PCs attack her, Amyleda’s true nature swiftly reveals itself as she fights back with a gleeful hiss. In combat, she’s joined by a pair of distorted spiritual forms—two shadows that manifest directly from the surrounding malevolence to fight at her side. Amyleda fights to the death but doesn’t pursue the PCs out of this room—if they return on another night, she welcomes them back for another séance, but partway through it, she ambushes them, rolling Deception for initiative and manifesting two new shadow guardians. This time, she pursues the PCs relentlessly; if they evade her, she’ll recruit other monsters and creatures from Bastardhall and form a group constituting a Severe encounter to seek them out and slaughter them.

If the PCs refuse to take part in her séance, she smiles mercurially and then notes that she’ll be here “the next night, when they return with braver souls.”

While Amyleda was a faker in her previous life, in her new existence, she’s got significant and actual powers that allow her to contact the spirit world. As the PCs are seated at her table, she proceeds to cast a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gsYEuWv04XTDxe91]{Call Spirit} ritual, and as the casting begins, she asks one of the PCs to be the fulcrum for the spirit world, explaining that they’ll be the one empowered to question the spirits summoned, with the other PCs providing metaphysical support. She adds that the fulcrum must be versed in occult or religious knowledge, since this PC will be the secondary caster for the ritual. Once she determines where the PCs’ specialties lie, she offers one of them a “little extra something to help them concentrate,” giving them her profane gift—if the PC declines, though, she simply shrugs and moves on with the ritual. During the casting, she uses the skill not being used by the PC.

The ritual takes 1 hour to cast. During this time, Amyleda is distracted enough that a canny PC who possesses a harrow deck of their own (such as the one they might have claimed in area @UUID[.fk4G37Tug5dnKsd9]{D26e}) can surreptitiously swap that deck out for Amyleda’s with a successful @Check[thievery|dc:27|name:PF2E.Actions.Steal.Title|options:action:steal|traits:manipulate] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.RDXXE7wMrSPCLv5k]{Steal}. If Amyleda notices the attempt, she breaks off the ritual and attacks, but if she doesn’t, she won’t discover the swap in her trance-like state until it’s too late—see @UUID[.#subverting-the-seance]{Subverting the Séance}.

At the end of the call spirit casting time, the fulcrum PC must attempt a @Check[occultism|dc:27|name:Call Spirit] or @Check[religion|dc:27|name:Call Spirit] check to fulfill their duty as the secondary caster. Other PCs taking part in the séance can assist by each attempting a @Check[will|dc:24] save to keep their own spirits focused—every successful Will save decreases the DC of the check by 1 (2 for each critical success). After this, Amyleda makes a skill check using either @Check[occultism|dc:29|name:Call Spirit] or @Check[religion|dc:29|name:Call Spirit] (whichever skill the fulcrum didn’t use), adjusting her skill check as normal for a secondary check’s success or failure. On a critical failure, rather than having evil spirits appear, Amyleda instead realizes who the PCs actually are and attacks in rage at being deceived into thinking they were legitimate guests.

If the ritual is successful, then it contacts several spirits associated with Castle Arudora, and the PCs can Speak to the Spirits for 15 minutes, after which the séance shifts in atmosphere and an unexpected visitor attempts to make contact—see @UUID[.#subverting-the-seance]{Subverting the Séance}.

Research

Several Topics (see below)

Speak to the Spirits: With the successful casting of call spirit, the PCs can attempt to Speak to the Spirits contacted to research @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.PAMDhjQNkAm8rB5R]{Bastardhall}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.UUqGlDCzpRnwqovv]{Bastardhall Curse}, the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.tbO0Ti0FI6DfZlgf]{Arudora Family}, or (if they’ve learned his name yet) @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.sKX1KQy64oUXrIvb]{Caydserris Arudora}. One PC can attempt a Research check every 5 minutes, and after three checks (regardless of success or failure), the opportunity to speak to the spirits passes—move on to Subverting the Séance. Alternatively, the PCs could specifically try to contact @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.QDo0K7VXLVH9D9tI]{Florin Kindler}—doing so allows them to Research her instead.

Maximum RP 2 per topic (Bastardhall, the curse, or the Arudora Family as a whole), or 3 per topic (Florin Kindler or Caydserris); Research Checks @Check[diplomacy|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to address the spirits courteously or @Check[intimidation|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to demand answers from the dead.

Subverting the Séance

Once the PCs have either reached the maximum RP for speaking to the spirits or 15 minutes have passed, Amyleda’s brow furrows, and she tosses her head in consternation a few times. The spirits the PCs were speaking to fade away as the medium mutters out, “What...? Who... who is this...? Who approaches...?” Then, a deep, mournful voice speaks out: “You can hear me... You can sense me... You can respond to me... Where is my love?”

The first actual and legitimate séance Amyleda’s ever performed has caught the attention of one spirit in particular—a spirit she pretended to channel many times before. In fact, even though she was faking her previous séances, this particular spirit has always replied and become frustrated by her inability to let him answer, for this is the mournful spirit of Vittorio Vancaskerkin, Alisendra’s first love. Amyleda lapses into a motionless trance, and it falls to the PCs to speak to Vittorio.

Vittorio desperately wants Alisendra to join him in death. He perished a year before her marriage to Raudltz, and while cynical players might assume she had something to do with his death, this isn’t the case. Their love was tempestuous, and after one particularly heated clash over something as simple as their interpretations of the implications of a play they’d attended called The Conception Exception, Vittorio threw his hands up in frustration and declared that he could never spend the night with someone who considered the play’s tragic heroine to be a weak-willed victim. As he backed into the street, giving Alisendra an exaggerated farewell, he was struck and slain by a runaway horse and carriage. When Alisendra later married Raudltz, it was more out of a need for financial stability than because she loved him, and while she grew fond of him and the comforts of her new life in time, she never truly lost the torch she continued to carry for Vittorio.

Some of this information may come to light depending on the questions the PCs ask of the mysterious spirit. The party can pose up to four questions, which Vittorio answers as truthfully as he can—try to phrase these answers in a way that at least conveys Vittorio’s name, and let them know that he and Alisendra had a complicated but true love for each other, and that he misses her dearly. When a PC asks the spirit a question, they can do so delicately and carefully with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:22] check, using traditional methods of interrogation used during a séance with a @Check[occultism|dc:24] check or by making forceful demands via a @Check[intimidation|dc:26] check. On a success, the answers Vittorio gives are more detailed, but more importantly, if the PCs succeed at least twice during their interrogation, the answers he gives echo through Bastardhall’s supernatural auras and distract Alisendra. Once the PCs ask their final question, Vittorio fades away, and Amyleda awakens. If they succeeded at least twice, proceed with the reward below, but if they failed to earn two successes, Amyleda is furious that they didn’t keep Vittorio around long enough for her to have time to properly interact with him. She sputters and rages, then attacks, but she’s distracted during the resulting combat and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for the duration of the fight.

Reward

If the PCs succeed at least twice during the four questions they can ask Vittorio, they win this particular challenge. As the séance comes to an end, Amyleda smiles, for the first time, in honesty. She thanks them for helping set her learn the true value of speaking with the other side, then fades away as her soul moves on to the afterlife. Her gear remains behind. Grant the PCs XP as if they’d defeated her and the two shadows in combat, and note that when the PCs finally compel Alisendra to manifest, she’ll be disadvantaged as a result of them communicating with Vittorio.

Laroba Boathouse.name: Laroba Boathouse
Laroba Boathouse.text:
Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

Note that this location is found on the Shore level, at the southeast area.

The main room of this building appears to be a boat workshop. A workbench sits in one corner, while three rowboats in various stages of repair lean against the southern wall. The central part of the main room is occupied by a wooden frame and hoist that would allow one to work on a rowboat with ease. To the north, beyond a parted curtain, is a small, humble bedroom that appears to have once been a fisher’s home, judging by the fish trophies on the walls and the fishing gear about the place. Above, the rafters serve as storage for all manner of nets, oars, and long timbers of wood, while below, the floorboards glisten with moisture and, in several places, are missing entirely, revealing the muddy water inches below.

The Laroba Boathouse was both the workshop and home of Castle Arudora’s master of the hunt, Arth Wiltur—a man who, in addition to serving as a guide for periodic hunting excursions, was responsible for the maintenance of the small fleet of fishing skiffs and rowboats used by the Arudoras and their guests for fishing excursions on the lake. Arth himself died on the night of the curse, and what became of him can be discovered in the trophy hall (area @UUID[.3hduGPZ55keA2HRA]{D15}), but his boathouse is far from uninhabited. While the PCs can certainly use the skiffs here to move around the perimeter of the island, remember that, as detailed on the @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.FHoSc4ZgjbMcE5dl#the-ethereal-plane]{Adventure Path Structure} section, attempting to row across the lake simply puts the PCs in the Ethereal Plane (if they do so, the skiff remains behind at the edge of the transition between lake and Ethereal Plane, so that the PCs can drift back to the skiff to reboard it and return to shore).

At the end of any round in which at least one Small or larger creature walks around in the boathouse, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:6]. On a failure, a board beneath one random walking creature’s foot gives way, and that creature stumbles partially through the floor into the shallow muddy water below, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of their next turn.

Encounter

Moderate 8

@UUID[Actor.hj7in3ZZlTu8n4vi]{Wihsaaks x2} @UUID[Actor.S1OFq9Ywrr4MHMAg]{Brood Leech Swarms x2}

Creatures: In life, Arth feared no beast or fish he could hunt or trap, yet an experience as a child left him with a lasting fear of things that creep and crawl. The idea of being overwhelmed by thousands of tiny biting animals unsettled the man the level of a phobia (one that left him a lifelong user of lures instead of live bait for fishing), and those fears often visited here as nightmares—nightmares that have attracted a pair of wihsaaks who cultivated those fears into a pair of leech swarms.

When the PCs first enter this area, the two wihsaaks lurk in the rafters above, hiding and waiting. As soon as a PC stumbles through a loose floor board or 2 rounds pass (whichever comes first), the two brood leech swarms that lurk below the boathouse slither up out of the water and into the cabin, squirming through the many gaps in the floorboards—a brood leech swarm can fully move from the water below into the building above like this as a single action with the move trait. The wihsaaks then attack, rolling Stealth for initiative. They fight to the death but do not pursue fleeing PCs. If they’re left alive, however, they may well decide it’s time to take their swarms on the road and could be encountered again later—for example, by plotting to ambush the PCs as they rest elsewhere in the castle.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.YkM8IugTJtg1bAAh]{Peg on the Wall} @UUID[Actor.04pbKW3sEeV2hWRj]{Under Mattress}

Arth’s mariner’s splint armor hangs from a peg on the wall in his bedroom—he never wore the armor except when he was out on the lake.
