Perhaps of more interest to the PCs is a set of journals tucked under Arth’s mattress—a PC can discover these with a successful @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check made while Seeking the bed or after 10 minutes of Searching the area. A brief perusal of these journals reveals that they’re partially records of Arth’s hunting and fishing expeditions, but also reveal his obsession with Alisendra Arudora—and the fact that he was trying to figure out a way to woo her away from Raudltz by obsessively gathering information about Alisendra’s likes, desires, and habits. While it’s creepy reading, these journals can be used to research Alisendra.

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.mJYN4Onwrp1JCt7X]{Alisendra Arudora}

Arth’s Journals: You spend two hours reading through Arth’s exacting notes on everything associated with his obsession: Alisendra Arudora.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[survival|dc:24|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to efficiently ignore the sections where Arth’s talking about expeditions and focus on the entries on Alisendra or @Check[perception|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to navigate the journal’s randomly organized entries more efficiently.

Upper Halls.name: Upper Halls
Upper Halls.text:
These halls are dark, as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.lfrhhbTG1nf0fNAQ]{Evercursed Crystals} that once glimmered inside the lanterns hanging along the hall were taken and hidden in the ashes of the fireplace in area @UUID[.8yjrUfFUti4blhaJ]{D25}.

This hallway has a deep mauve carpet and is dimly lit by the lower floor or cracks in windows. Paintings of pastoral landscapes hang between various rooms.

The paintings on display here, initially meant simply as minor decorations, are now infested with the curse. Anyone who looks closely at any of these paintings must attempt a @Check[will|dc:25|options:inflicts:frightened|traits:mental,fear] save. On a failure, the PC thinks they spot shadowy forms with sinister eyes looking out from between trees, behind rocks, or from shadowy cave entrances and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure).

The stairs at area D21a lead down to area @UUID[.Rgs6JrkwqfHvbTQn]{D4a}, while those at D21b lead to area @UUID[.Rgs6JrkwqfHvbTQn]{D4c}. The stairs at area D21c lead up to the private halls and area @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.ndtRFPlOc0RB3Vc5]{F2f}, but until the @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8]{private halls} are unlocked, these stairs end at a wall of impassable green mist.

Encounter

Trivial 8

@UUID[Actor.KgJq51AeYrENo3Db]{Will-o'-Wisps x2}

Unlike most of the monsters in Bastardhall, the denizens of the upper halls are neither reincarnated victims nor fiendish visitors. Every time Bastardhall manifests, its aura draws will-o’-wisps in like moths to the proverbial flame, and a few of them become caught and trapped here. The ambient fear exuded by Castle Arudora is enough to keep the wisps from starving, but only just—the paintings are like sips of water to a starving person, enough to trick the stomach into sensing fullness without providing nourishment. Even in their hunger, however, the wisps don’t abandon their subtle tactics as soon as they sense the PCs.

When the PCs first travel through these halls, one of the wisps remains @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} and follows behind the party, while the other sheds light as if from a lantern and aims to keep just around the next corner, hoping to lead the PCs further into the upper halls before going invisible again just near the doors to area @UUID[.klWkYac4yHUOYGlr]{D27}. It hopes that the PCs are attracted by the light coming from under the door there. If the PCs move into that area and trigger the haunt, the wisps move in to attack as well. If they’re confronted here in the halls, though, they don’t hold back and still fight, seeking to flank a foe. Here in the hall, a wisp can move up next to one of the many paintings hanging on the walls to try to draw attention to it with a @Check[deception|against:will] check against a PC’s Will save—on a success, the targeted PC must then save against the painting’s fear effect. After a fight begins, the wisps pursue PCs into specific bedrooms to continue the battle if needed, but note that due to their low Strength modifier and lack of hands, opening closed doors is complex for them and requires two Interact actions instead of one. The wisps fight to the death.

Guest Rooms.name: Guest Rooms
Guest Rooms.text:
Castle Arudora featured no less than 25 guest rooms of different sizes. Some of these featured multiple beds for groups, while others were single-bed accommodations. Each room is well appointed and tidy but covered with thick layers of dust. Furnishings include beds, a dressing table with a mirror, a desk and chair or two, a large trunk for the storage of personal items, and a bench fitted with a chamber pot in a small privacy closet (fortunately for the guests, they weren’t expected to empty their own chamber pots—such was the domain of the help). Most of the rooms did not feature fireplaces, and in the colder months, these Arudora guest rooms had a reputation for being so clammy and dank that no amount of heaped blankets or hot water bottles could help.

It takes 10 minutes to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} a guest room, but only two have anything of note (see Treasure below).

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.qUHpEAdvNikytTNd]{Western Guest Room} @UUID[Actor.AT86S1fRbKHwTYn0]{Mattress}

Area D22a was assigned to one of the more pretentious and demanding guests during the night the curse took hold—the elven escape artist Danrasteian the Magnificent. A PC who Searches this room turns up the three bottles of Varisian raspberry wine he “borrowed” from the wine cellar. Two of them are empty, but the third remains unopened and can be delivered to the chefs in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL#side-quest:-the-main-course]{C40} for the meal the PCs might need them to prepare. Any of these bottles (empty or full) could serve as a distracting memento for Danrasteian in area @UUID[.tmNCXndKaS4Bi3tD]{D26} (although multiple bottles don’t count as multiple distractions).

The other guest room of note is area D22b, which was given to one of Alisendra’s close friends, the medium Amyleda Blackwell. Every month, Amyleda visited the castle to perform a séance at Alisendra’s behest. While Alisendra thought of Amyleda as her close friend (in part because she believed the medium could contact several of Alisendra’s distant ancestors), Amyleda was in fact a gifted charlatan who’d long been using her monthly visits to Castle Arudora to steal from other guests or, increasingly, from the Arudoras themselves. On the night the curse befell the castle, she was scheduled to perform a séance, but earlier in the day, she snatched a scrimshaw from the Arudora gallery and replaced it with a cleverly designed counterfeit sculpture. The counterfeit artwork crumbled to dust when the curse took hold, but the original remains hidden in this room. If the PCs @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} near the bed or Search the room and succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check, they find the hidden scrimshaw tucked into the mattress. The scrimshaw is a sperm whale’s tooth and depicts a whaling vessel being attacked by an enormous octopus. It’s 1 Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it triggers a memory of Augsten Arudora using the tooth to commit his first murder—the slaying of a servant who dared backtalk him, and the subsequent cover-up by his father to keep Augsten out of legal trouble. This scrimshaw belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}); see @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{Lost Artwork} for more details.

Alisendra Arrives.name: Alisendra Arrives
Alisendra Arrives.text:
Encounter

Severe 8

@UUID[Actor.SudB6sBMNJr8tbaI]{Alisendra Arudora} @UUID[Actor.Gu0cJHGwPd547OtC]{Wraiths x2}

Creature: Alisendra Arudora enjoyed being the center of attention, and among the Arudoras, she coveted the adoration and admiration of other nobles and vaunted Ustalavic notables the most. Ever the ambitious hostess, she soon developed an uncanny knack for juggling multiple events at once, so that visitors who came to the castle to enjoy one particular performance might also enjoy a banquet, a poetry reading, a séance, or any number of frivolities that were also available to attend. When the curse fell, there were no less than five separate events in various stages of progress at Castle Arudora—a display of exotic creatures presented by a traveling carnival, a multi-course banquet scheduled to begin that very evening that would likely last well past midnight, musical performances from a troupe of musicians from Varisia who were scheduled to play for a masked ball, preparations for a group fishing excursion that would take place at the lake early the next morning, and a much-anticipated séance led by one of Ustalav’s most infamous mediums, where guests were hoping to make contact with several legendary heroes who gave their lives during the Shining Crusade.

By interrupting these five events, the PCs can disrupt the attention that Alisendra derives from the souls and spirits trapped in repeating these events over and over, forcing her to manifest physically. All the PCs need to do to disrupt these events is to kill the monsters now in charge of them, so that the souls of the guests who were transformed by the curse can move on to the afterlife. Doing so causes Alisendra to appear in the room in which the last of these disruptions took place, 10 minutes after the PCs complete the disruption, with two wraith accomplices at her side: a Severe 8 encounter.

But simply killing the monsters isn’t the most efficient solution. Each of these encounters can be disrupted in a nonviolent way that wrests attention away from Alisendra and focuses it on the PCs. For each one of these encounters disrupted in this way, Alisendra is weakened, as follows (the effects of these disruptions are cumulative):

  • 1 Nonviolent Disruption: Alisendra destroys one of her wraiths in anger, so when she arrives, only one wraith accompanies her.

  • 2 Nonviolent Disruptions: Alisendra destroys both of her wraiths and arrives to fight alone, reducing this to a Moderate 8 encounter.

  • 3 Nonviolent Disruptions: Alisendra loses access to her coven-granted spells.

  • 4 Nonviolent Disruptions: Alisendra becomes stupefied 2 with frustration; this condition persists for the rest of the Adventure Path. In addition, she’s slowed 1 for the first 2 rounds of combat.

  • 5 Nonviolent Disruptions: Alisendra gains the weak creature adjustment, reducing this to a Low 8 encounter.

Tokens

@UUID[Actor.SudB6sBMNJr8tbaI]{Alisendra Arudora} @UUID[Actor.Gu0cJHGwPd547OtC]{Wraiths x2}

Alisendra and her wraiths' tokens have not been pre-placed on the canvas, as her location depends on the order the PCs disrupt her events. Instead, you can drag the actors linked either in this block or in this encounter's header, onto whichever room Alisendra manifests in.

When Alisendra appears, she wears her own skin from when she was a human mortal—a costume afforded her by the curse. She appears as a beautiful Varisian woman with long red hair, clad in an elegant, eye-catching gown. In one hand she carries an equally elegant hand fan that she frequently uses to fan herself as an affectation, although as she confronts the PCs, it appears to be more a manifestation of her frustrations at their meddling. She has little interest in speaking to the PCs other than to accuse them of daring to think they’re the ones who matter when they’re really little more than common thieves—thieves she intends to put in their place!

On the first round of combat, Alisendra attempts to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm} the most heavily armored PC, hoping to encourage them to simply not take part in the fight in return for unmentioned rewards after the battle. On the second round of combat, she casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.KSAEhNfZyXMO7Z7V]{Outcast’s Curse} on the PC who she feels was the most disruptive if she still has access to her coven spells; if not, she casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.o4lRVTwSxnOOn5vl]{Sleep}, hoping to whittle down the party to a more manageable size. In the event she manages to charm and put all the PCs to sleep, she doesn’t kill them—instead she has them brought down into the holding cells (area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.gxVn7eUIGm4UF4FV]{C37}) after stripping them of their gear and placing that equipment on several of the cots in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.lQdheEdZiY5D3YIS]{C34}. She commands the bugbear tormentors there to keep an eye on them as she retreats to her tower to recover from the fight and to decide what to do with the PCs—in this case, you should give the PCs a chance to escape their fate, perhaps with some aid by servitor phantoms. Once they escape and reclaim their gear, they can force a new confrontation with Alisendra simply by entering the reception halls again; this time, however, she won’t be merciful and aims to kill.

If the PCs prove resistant to her magic or rush her to engage in melee, she switches tactics to engage them in melee herself attacking with her claws and jaws. If reduced to fewer than 75 HP, she Assumes Fiery Form to finish the fight. She’ll pursue the PCs throughout the reception halls but typically not beyond. She fights to the death. As soon as she’s slain, she shrieks in fury as burning blood erupts from across her body. This fire swiftly consumes her, burning her to ash as her soul spirals up through the ceiling to her tower at area @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.ZkDF1436uRUd7qzM]{J3e}. Left behind in the ashes of her body is her fan—the key to unlocking the dungeon of Bastardhall.

The Dungeon.name: The Dungeon
The Dungeon.text:
The dungeon below Castle Arudora served many purposes. They allowed castle deliveries to quietly come and go through an underground channel that connected the lake waters beneath the island from east to west. The same channel allowed for the disposal of waste through a series of middens throughout the castle, thanks to a waterwheel that encouraged flow through the sluices and tunnels. An alchemist’s workshop, a prison, and an ossuary rounded out the dungeon’s uses. The deepest secret of the Arudora dungeon, however, was its access to a series of Darklands caverns far below. Put in place by Irrokcis Arudora, who turned to cruelty and fiendish temptation in order to further his nefarious plans, this link set into motion events that, through the course of generations to come, eventually culminated in the Bastardhall Curse.

At the time the curse fell upon the castle, the dungeon was occupied by four different categories of people: prisoners, visiting suppliers with deliveries to the castle, servants who lived in nearby Maiserene, and a few “specialists”—the alchemist Junth Rundel, the dungeon warden Vink Cratched, and a man who had recently installed himself as the castle’s torturer: Dazerien Arudora. All of them were transformed into the monsters who now roam in the dungeon. They were soon joined by other horrors evolved from the vermin already lurking within the walls. Of all the terrors that await the PCs, the most dangerous is Dazerien—a man whose cruelties in life are reflected in his new existence as a jittery, cackling werewolf, his appetite for torture barely sated by the constant flow of reincarnating, forever-tormented souls.

Entering the Dungeon.name: Entering the Dungeon
Entering the Dungeon.text:
The Bastardhall dungeon is located approximately 100 feet below the lowest chambers in the castle cellars above, which places them about 10 feet above the level of the surrounding lake. The decision to build an extensive dungeon here rather than higher up and closer to the castle was one of convenience; there were already a few natural tunnels through the bedrock, including a narrow water channel, that made for an excellent place to get started. For Eragayl Arudora, transforming the area into a usable space that primarily served to ship and receive deliveries without of compromising the above-ground scene was certainly a bonus. Even as he enjoyed serving the people of Ustalav as a hero, he enjoyed the comforts of aristocracy just as much and shared the “noble” opinion that those who served the lords of the land should not unduly mix with their betters.

As such, once the dungeon is unlocked, the simplest and most direct way to enter them is through one of the two waterway approaches from the haunted shore. Other entrances from the castle above exist, but some of these are difficult to find or dangerous to navigate. Regardless, once the PCs return @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.kasxhW2drfCOZZq1]{Alisendra’s fan} to the fountain at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3}, the dungeon unlocking might not be immediately obvious. That no section of the castle above becomes solid should be a hint to the PCs to look elsewhere, but barring a return to one of the stairs or shafts in the castle itself that drop into the dungeon a hundred feet below, two significant developments along the haunted shore may catch their attention the next time they visit or look down from the castle walls above. The first, and most obvious, is that the beacon located on the west shore is now solid; after dark, the light at its peak shines down to the shore below at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Mr8Gsi42znsNq3XB]{A23}, where several piers once provided a place for visiting watercraft to dock. The second clue is a sudden churning of water flowing out of the eastern sluiceway at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.OWdcr3QHPHrYyFXD]{A15}. Now that the dungeon is unlocked, the waterwheel in area @UUID[.FBPDuStK6Zlej0n5]{E6} has resumed its function of flushing sewage and waste from the castle into the lake.

The Skies Above.name: The Skies Above
The Skies Above.text:
When the dungeon unlocks, the clammy fog gives way to an approaching storm. Rain falls in fitful drizzles all day and night, and the wind picks up again. Outdoors, vision-based Perception checks take a –1 circumstance penalty from the drizzle. The rain and wind aren’t quite enough to start the process of flooding the haunted shore and the dungeon, but PCs who succeed at a @Check[nature|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|options:action:recall-knowledge|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} note that such a development could be possible during a powerful and prolonged tempest. The temperatures are now uncomfortable and in the mild cold category, and Lake Laroba’s surface returns to its wind-tossed churn—it’s a @Check[athletics|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim} these waters. Distant peals of thunder sound a half-dozen times every 24 hours at random points, yet no lightning is yet visible.

Sunrise is at 10:00 a.m., and sunset is at 6:00 p.m. The days are 8 hours long and nights are 16 hours long.

Dungeon Ambushes.name: Dungeon Ambushes
Dungeon Ambushes.text:
Encounter

Low 9

@UUID[Actor.KgJq51AeYrENo3Db]{Will-o'-Wisps x4}

If the PCs rest in an unsafe area in the Bastardhall dungeon, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:7]. On a failure, they’re ambushed while camping by will-o’-wisps who attempt to lure a PC on watch into danger.

Lucid Nightmares.name: Lucid Nightmares
Lucid Nightmares.text:
After the dungeon is unlocked, the nightmare changes. The PC wakes inside a dungeon cell and watches as the hooded figure with the staff comes for their fellow PCs in nearby cells, one after the other, dragging them out of the prison into a nearby room where horrific sounds of torture and pain fill the air. Each time the figure returns, they’re increasingly blood-soaked. When the PC is the last one left, the figure comes for them and drags them into a torture chamber, and they awaken as the torments begin.

The Anticipation of Torture

Resist Nightmare @Check[will|dc:26|options:lucid-nightmare,the-anticipation-of-torture]

Critical Failure The PC wakes with hemophobia (fear of blood), and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} whenever they witness a creature within 30 feet take persistent bleed damage or endure a critical hit from a weapon Strike. This becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} if the PC is the target of the bleed damage or critical hit.

Research @Check[acrobatics|dc:28|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to squeeze out of your cell and escape or @Check[medicine|dc:31|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to know how to recover quickly from any torments inflicted upon you in the dream

Effect

@UUID[Item.sYZI41JKGiMH8aO0]{Hemophobia}

If a PC critically fails to resist this nightmare, use the linked effect to automate a Note reminder when they are critically hit or take bleed damage.

Dungeon Features.name: Dungeon Features
Dungeon Features.text:
Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

All locations in this chapter are found in the Dungeon level, with the following exceptions:

  • In area @UUID[.LPkJFQogdqN9LE0s]{E4}, E4b is found in the Cellars level, accessed by taking the lift in E4a.

  • @UUID[.AsVGoGtlVEkWPNv4]{E16} and @UUID[.DRgsJI73yaw9G8Jk]{E17} are found in the Shore level.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ZBc83HjWvKyjQIsn.PlaylistSound.wVrEBzaDKhx7FGaz]{Dungeon}

As the PCs begin exploring the dungeon, you can play this ambience sound.

The dungeon used to be lit by lanterns and torches—no extravagant expenses like everlight crystals were ever tried. While sconces and wall-mounted hooks still exist in most tunnels and chambers, the light sources that hung there are long gone. The dungeon dwellers have little need for light, so if the PCs want to see, they’ll need to bring their own light sources.

The walls, floors, and ceilings are lined with red brick and mortar. Ceiling heights average a lofty 15 feet in most rooms, with the water level being 10 feet lower than most of the surrounding floors. The doors are made of reinforced wood and, unless indicated in the text, cannot be locked. The entire place is cold, clammy, and musty-smelling at best, and fouled with the stink of decay or waste in other areas. Whenever a PC enters an area with fouled air or begins their turn in such an area, they must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:25|options:inflicts:sickened|traits:poison] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). This is a poison effect, and once a PC successfully saves against the stink, they’re temporarily immune to the fouled areas until they spend more than 8 hours outside the dungeon.

In certain areas of the dungeon, wooden walkways run along the edges of waterways. These wooden walkways are positioned only a foot above the water and, while they look unsound and creak alarmingly when trod upon, they can hold the weight of a Large or smaller creature with ease. These walkways are universally slick with algae, moisture, and sludge, though, and a PC who moves along them must @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.M76ycLAqHoAgbcej]{Balance} with a successful @Check[acrobatics|name:PF2E.Actions.Balance.Title|dc:20|options:action:balance,inflicts:prone|traits:move] check or risk falling @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} (into the nearby water on a critical failure).

No watercraft are in the dungeon, but the PCs can use those found in the boathouse to the south (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.SORum03a5tQWw4Xp]{D31}) to aid in navigating the tunnels if they wish.

Otherwise, swimming in the water here requires a successful @Check[athletics|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|options:action:swim|traits:move] check.

Delivery Entrance.name: Delivery Entrance
Delivery Entrance.text:
A twenty-foot wide flooded tunnel winds through a natural stone waterway here. The ceiling arches to a height of twenty feet above the dark water below. Sheets of glistening algae and fungus grow along the walls, hang from the ceiling like tendrils or soggy webs, or float in patches on the water surface.

The opening to the west leads out of the dungeon and into the haunted shore, at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.P8DWUDP9moicwHQC]{A11}. The water here is 10 feet deep.

Checkpoint.name: Checkpoint
Checkpoint.text:
The flooded tunnel opens up here. To the south, a ten-foot-wide circular tunnel with brick-lined walls winds out of sight around a corner, a slippery-looking wooden walkway clinging to its eastern side. There’s a large room to the north. A wooden boardwalk abuts the waterway with a nook for docking skiffs, and beyond this, the floors and walls are lined with red bricks. A short flight of steps leads up five feet to the northeast from the wood walkway to the main room above. Shattered furniture suggests this area may have once been some sort of guard post or checkpoint, while what appear to be large nests of fur and rotting plants lie heaped below on the wooden platform. The full dimensions of the area are hard to determine due to the tattered, moldy curtains that hang here and there from hooks in the ceiling.

The two nests on the wooden platform are homes to the Bastardhall rats that lurk outside in area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.P8DWUDP9moicwHQC]{A11}. Once the dungeon is unlocked, if these two rats still live, they eagerly return here to their nests and are encountered alongside the chamber’s other denizens (this increases this area to a Moderate 9 encounter). The secret door in the north wall can be discovered with a successful @Check[perception|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check if a PC @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in this area, or if someone @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the room for a half hour.

Encounter

Low 9

@UUID[Actor.L8qYcku10bEa1LhU]{Sludge Trolls x3}

Creatures: Once, guards in the employ of Maiserene’s sheriff ran this checkpoint, keeping diligent track of everything that came and went through the waterway. Most of what passed through here were supplies for the kitchens, firewood, and materials for maintenance and repairs in the castle above, but now and then stranger shipments bound for Junth Rundel’s laboratory (area @UUID[.8h6QErLBhi0Ro2tn]{E7}) arrived. These were stored near the secret door, left for Junth to gather and transport back to his workshop at his convenience.

The guards today have only vague memories of their previous lives, and no memories at all of the secret door, now that the curse has transformed them into gangly, hideous amphibious monsters known as sludge trolls. One of the trolls sits on the ground in the middle of the room, his long legs dangling over the edge to brush against the walkway below. As soon as he spots anyone passing by to the south, he calls out in a phlegm-thickened voice: “Stop! State yer business!” The PCs can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie} to him with any half-plausible story (or even a quarter-plausible one), and as long as they can succeed at a @Check[deception|dc:21|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|options:action:lie|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check, the bored troll snorts and waves them on to continue east or west. Any attempt to tell the truth, clamber up onto the walkway, or attack causes the troll to leap to his feet with a hoot of excitement. He attacks at once, starting with sludge cough Strikes and then moving to melee soon thereafter.

Of course, this troll is not actually alone. Three others lurk nearby—one behind the curtains to the west, one behind the curtains to the north, and one underwater in the cut-out area of the walkway. These three trolls join any fight using Stealth for initiative.

The trolls pursue fleeing PCs throughout areas @UUID[.mJ7qNpJ3GNVNEVcR]{E1}–@UUID[.FBPDuStK6Zlej0n5]{E6}, but they know the non-troll dangers that await there; if the PCs stumble into any such area, the trolls hang back and make sludge cough Strikes. Once only one troll remains alive, he flees to area @UUID[.0CdaOwJhcWtoKSkm]{E3} to report the invasion to Boss Cratched.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.6Szbc06kG6nMeAmd]{Checkpoint}

Any valuables the sludge trolls come across, regardless of the rarity of such an occurrence, is delivered to Boss Cratched in area @UUID[.0CdaOwJhcWtoKSkm]{E3}. That said, one object in particular has escaped the notice of the trolls, as they don’t realize its worth. This is a stone tablet onto which has been carved an image of an elk-headed humanoid standing atop a hill overlooking a vast lake.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:25] or @Check[society|dc:25] check recognizes it as an ancient Kellid carving of Erastil overlooking Lake Encarthan—one that, curiously, doesn’t feature an island visible at its center. The PC also recognizes the item’s architectural and artistic value. The stone carving is 2 Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it triggers a memory of an angry Ausken Dast reprimanding a sullen soldier for “borrowing” the artwork from the gallery, noting that “even if its religious significance would be better represented elsewhere, it is, unfortunately, the legal property of Lord Raudltz in the government’s eyes.” The memory concludes as the soldier promise to leave the carving hidden here and to return it later that evening during the night’s galas in return for Ausken’s promise to not report the near theft. This carving belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14})—see @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{Lost Artwork}.

Cistern.name: Cistern
Cistern.text:
This large, flooded cavern arches to a height of thirty feet above the water. A wooden construction built into the northern portion of the cave blocks off a twenty-five-foot- wide section of the water beneath a hole in the ceiling. To the south, a wooden boardwalk runs alongside the water, ending at a short flight of steps leading up to a large brick- walled room to the south.

The original dungeon architects chose to leave this large lake-cavern as they found it, as its placement under the castle was perfect for a well—the hole in the ceiling (which leads up from its exit in the thirty-foot-high ceiling a further 80 feet to area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0LMAGxf5oiQklEFh]{C39} above). The wooden construction surrounding the water under the well opening is a filter that extends all the way down to the lake bed 15 feet below, forming an underwater cage composed of hundreds of submerged slats that trap larger impurities. Of course, the water itself was still far from pure and needed to be boiled if it was intended to be used for drinking.

Encounter

Moderate 9

@UUID[Actor.NUDYN5z3klNDlkfS]{Vink Cratched} @UUID[Actor.L8qYcku10bEa1LhU]{Sludge Trolls x2}

Creatures: Today, though, the cage-like area under the well serves a different purpose. It’s where the leader of the sludge trolls, a lanky green creature who in a previous life was dungeon ward Vink Cratched, traps and stores her meals for later. Most of feasts consist of otters or fish that swim through the area from the surrounding lake, but now and then larger creatures end up being snatched and tossed in here to await Vink’s next feeding.

Vink Cratched, or “Boss Cratched” as she prefers to be addressed by the sludge trolls who serve her, spends most of her time slumbering underwater in the middle of the cavern, leaving a pair of loyal sludge trolls to guard her while she rests. Those two sludge trolls lurk in hiding just north of the east and west exits, and as soon as they notice any PCs moving into this area, they stealthily swim down to alert the boss. (If they notice fighting to the south in area @UUID[.LPkJFQogdqN9LE0s]{E4}, they do the same, but they and Vink don’t confront the PCs until they move into the cistern proper.)

Once she’s aware of the visitors, Vink leaves her two guards below water and rises up to half emerge, leaning against the weir under the well as she calls out to the PCs. As with the sludge trolls in area @UUID[.k9MS0A9QhgJfPA7G]{E2}, she demands to know what they’re up to, but she’s a bit more observant than the others—a PC wishing to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie} to her must succeed at a @Check[deception|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|options:action:lie|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check. If what the PCs propose includes traveling through the cistern in any way, Vink demands a toll for their passage unless they critically succeeded at that Deception check. Vink accepts any payment in coin or valuables worth at least 500 gp after shrewdly sizing up the PCs. Failure to pay results in a chuckle and an admission: “I was hoping you’d be stingy. You look too delicious to be anything other than dinner!”

Vink rolls Intimidation for initiative in this case, while her two guards roll Stealth and begin combat with Aquatic Upsurge. The trolls fight to the death as long as Vink lives, but once she’s slain, the other trolls flee—one going west and the other east—to spread the grim news to the other trolls at areas @UUID[.k9MS0A9QhgJfPA7G]{E2} and @UUID[.FBPDuStK6Zlej0n5]{E6}. If any trolls remain there, they bicker and argue for a moment about “who’s the new boss” before deciding that the best way to find out is whoever kills the most of the new invaders. After a few minutes, the trolls band up and begin hunting the PCs, eager to use their deaths to solve their latest conundrum. Once only one troll remains alive, they flee into Lake Laroba, unlikely to return.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.W9JLeYgCzYKuEjU6]{Underwater Heap}

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the lake discovers a sizable amount of treasure stashed in an underwater heap near the north wall of the cavern. Most of the items are rusted and ruined, but among the rusted weapons and ruined armor are items of value, including 330 sp; 90 gp; different types of rings, necklaces, and bracelets worth a total of 200 gp; a +1 resilient breastplate; a +1 striking grievous low-grade silver warhammer; and a set of greater bracers of missile deflection. Safely gathering the treasure takes a half hour of diving, 10 minutes if done by someone who’s at least expert in Athletics, or just a few minutes if the diver can breathe water.

Food Storage.name: Food Storage
Food Storage.text:
This room’s brick walls and ceiling are supported by several wooden pillars and buttresses above. To the north, it looks out over an underground lake. To the east, a ten-foot-square wooden platform sits in an alcove; thick ropes attached to its corners lead up into the darkness of a shaft above. A winch on the nearby wall appears to control this lift. Many crates, barrels, and other containers lie haphazardly to the northwest near a pier alongside the lake shore, while to the south, a wooden shelf covered with dusty objects runs the length of the wall. A single round table and chair sits in the southeast corner, while a stack of several coffins sit nearby.

Food supplies were often stored here before they were hauled up to the castle above. Area E4b to the east is 80 feet above the main room, connected by a shaft in which a hand-operated lift provides transit. The wooden lift is currently in its lower position—it can be winched upward or downward by turning the nearby crank in either room at a rate of 5 feet per round. The device has safety locks so that if someone stops turning the crank, the lift remains stationary at its current height, but that doesn’t mean the lift is entirely safe—see Hazard, below. Note that while either winch can be turned by anyone, they won’t turn themselves, forcing the PCs to make multiple trips if one of them is needed to operate the machinery.

The brick-lined shaft walls can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climbed} with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check (@Check[athletics|dc:15|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] if one of the lift ropes are used). The stairs leading up from area E4b lead to the kitchen in the castle cellars above (area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40}).

Encounter

Low 9

@UUID[Actor.DlkyUtA9bcC8TpgG]{Mummy Guardians x4} @UUID[Actor.DKWpT0kAVTcD7dn7]{Collapsing Lift}

Creatures: The sight of the coffins in the room should make PCs nervous, as they were used to ship several mummies to Castle Arudora for processing into mummiranth dough in the kitchens above. And just as was the fate of the mummy in the cellar kitchen, the Bastardhall Curse animated the four remaining here in storage. The mummies lie inside their coffins, but are awake and aware; if the PCs make too much noise or bring bright light into the area, they smash out of the flimsy coffins to attack, fighting until they’re destroyed and pursuing fleeing PCs relentlessly. Raising or lowering of the lift is more than enough to get the mummies worked up—PCs who are being lowered from area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40} above find themselves greeted by four angry mummies as soon as they reach bottom (or fall from a collapsed lift).

Hazard: The lift’s ropes may look suspect, but they’re quite sound—the problem lies in the corners of the wooden platform where the ropes are anchored.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Open Coffins" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to break open the coffins and reveal the mummies within!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.vBnWDyIcnnZn006w]{Foodstuffs} @UUID[Actor.TMNAKD87Rd2nW82X]{Shallow Depression}

A PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} this room’s stores discovers that the vast majority of the foodstuffs here are either ruined from the damp or relatively mundane, but succeeding at either a DC 24 Lore check of any type associated with food or @Check[perception|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check made during the search allows the PC to realize that one sealed glass jar of thick, crystallized red syrup could work well as an ingredient for the brewers in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.jVrtk8KjGIvJavQ9]{C46} to work with. Delivering the syrup to the brewers in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.jVrtk8KjGIvJavQ9]{C46} adds @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.aSvDtG5i5l7scgru]{arbor wine} to the list of concoctions they can prepare.

A softly glowing chaplain’s cudgel dropped by one of the last people to use the lift before the curse struck remains hidden in the shallow depression in the ground where the wooden lift rests when it’s lowered. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in the pit while the platform is raised spots the cudgel automatically—otherwise it requires a successful @Check[perception|dc:29|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check to notice the faint glow.

Middens.name: Middens
Middens.text:
Four similar chambers found throughout the dungeon serve as castle middens. As the PCs approach a midden, the growing stink of decaying sewage grows; these areas have become festering clots of horror under the influence of the Bastardhall Curse. Adjust the following text as needed to match the particular midden the PCs enter.

The air in this room is foul almost beyond imagining and thick with clouds of glistening buzzing flies. Heaps of sewage, mold, decaying rat corpses, and more cake the floors and walls, or float in foamy masses atop the oily, polluted water. Openings in the ceiling lead upward, no doubt to pit toilets somewhere above.

The air in each of these four areas is fouled (see @UUID[.YbrXOAsT3pQnXsIN]{Dungeon Features}). Each also features a shaft in the ceiling that connects to one of the pit toilets in the cellars, about 100 feet above. A PC who becomes immersed in the waters of any of the middens is exposed to blinding sickness.

Blinding Sickness

Disease 7

  • Disease

Endemic to jungles of the Mwangi Expanse, blinding sickness is transmitted by dirty water or the bites of certain creatures.

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:23|options:inflicts:blinded,inflicts:enfeebled|traits:disease]

Stage 1 carrier with no effects (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} (1 day)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} (1 day)

Stage 4 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} and permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} (1 day)

Stage 5 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 4} (1 day)

Stage 6 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} (1 day)

Stage 7 death

North Midden.name: North Midden
North Midden.text:
The shaft above leads to the pit toilet in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.ZM9XEVZigDMxLmeK]{C9a}.

Encounter

Trivial 9

@UUID[Actor.q0oGxk1fX3pdlu8I]{Let My Torments Be Yours}

Hazard: A human skeleton encrusted with detritus and filth sits slumped the northwest corner of this room. These are the remains of a prisoner who managed to escape Dazerien’s clutches the day before the curse struck. He hid here, hoping to sneak out after dark, but succumbed to his torture wounds before then. His despair and hopelessness as he died was like nectar to Charg’s attention, and after the curse struck, the poor victim’s flesh congealed down in his ribcage, transforming into a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JmlPFAbjPvbhhKeu]{Vile Remnant} whose presence further tormented the prisoner’s soul in a dangerous haunt.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.mdgywcPUbOxmoQz0]{Skeleton Ribcage}

The vile remnant can be extracted with ease from the skeleton’s ribcage once the haunt is no more.

Central Midden.name: Central Midden
Central Midden.text:
The shafts above lead to the pit toilets in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.R02RcDGIWSa2Ygk9]{C20}.

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.8esAIVj311p8wg7K]{Middenworms x4}

Creatures: The waters of this midden hide more than filth—four glistening monstrous invertebrates known as middenworms have dwelled here since before the curse struck. Now sustained by the curse’s power, the hideous creatures hungrily slop up out of the waters to attack anyone who enters the chamber. The middenworms pursue foes relentlessly but give up the chase a round after they lose sight of their prey.

South Midden.name: South Midden
South Midden.text:
The shaft above leads to the pit toilet in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.TE8crk2kfOeKF5yG]{C24a}.

Encounter

@UUID[Actor.ZewiNUvkgINdnehu]{Middenworm Infestation}

Hazard: The middenworms laid eggs in the corpse of a dead Bastardhall rat that floats in the water here.

East Midden.name: East Midden
East Midden.text:
The shaft above leads to the pit toilet in area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.XXXge4mgm6Ye0xrQ]{C29a}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.hVC6QG5KsO9GGw0q]{East Midden}

Apart from the fouled air, there are no dangers in this midden. Indeed, a PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the midden and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check (or who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} underwater) discovers a +1 striking astral silver sword cane in the water directly under one of the shafts above—a weapon stolen from a visiting noble by a guard who nearly got caught before he dropped it down one of the pit toilets.

Waste Management.name: Waste Management
Waste Management.text:
This larger square room has brick walls and floors, with several wooden beams supporting wooden rafters against the brick ceiling twenty feet above. A twenty-foot-wide waterway winds through the room from east to west about ten feet below the floor, its banks lined with mud. A short boardwalk and stairs provide access to the water from the north half of the room, while a wooden bridge allows easy crossing to the east. Under the bridge churn long paddles that encourage a slow flow of water to the east, while in the southeast corner of the room is a large nest of rotting plants, broken timbers, rags, and bones.

This room was an additional area for visitors to go from the cellars above, but its primary purpose was to promote the flow of wastewater from the middens to the east into the lake. The water is 10 feet deep.

The stairs at area E6a lead up about 100 feet, twisting back and forth through a few landings, before reaching area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.MYRPJK8EXNQC5NLs]{C44d}. A 10-foot section of wall in the southwest corner is a large secret door that can be discovered with a successful @Check[perception|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check made by a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the area or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the entire room for 30 minutes. When opened, the door rotates on a central access, revealing a 10-foot-wide path forward into the tunnel to the south.

Encounter

Moderate 9

@UUID[Actor.L8qYcku10bEa1LhU]{Sludge Trolls x4} @UUID[Actor.F0t6Eogd0KJdboXq]{Bastardhall Rats x4} @UUID[Actor.Gxn47A5xWacBglVu]{Grinder-Widget}

Creatures: Another one of Raudltz’s grinder-widgets eternally works to power the turning of the paddles below the bridge to encourage water flow by rotating a wheel attached to ropes and pulleys down on the shore below the upper walkway. This creature ignores combat that breaks out in the room.

Likewise, the sludge trolls and Bastardhall rats that dwell here ignore the grinder-widget—yet the same cannot be said of the PCs. The four Bastardhall rats lurk in the nest and burst out to attack the PCs as soon as they set foot in the southern half of the room, fighting until at least two of them are slain before the others flee east out of the dungeon at area @UUID[.htYveToKD0tnBIiJ]{E8}.

In addition, four sludge trolls lurk in the waters of the room, but they’re alert and keep an eye on travelers. Unlike the others in the dungeon, they don’t bother to ask what the PCs are doing here—they attack either as soon as a PC moves up to the edge of either platform, lurching out of the water, or on the second round of combat with the rats. Once only one sludge troll remains alive, he flees west to area @UUID[.0CdaOwJhcWtoKSkm]{E3} to report to the boss.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.ifeLz7sY52PcCkRY]{Rat Nest}

While the sludge trolls have given over their treasures to their boss, the rats have not—a PC who Seeks their nest or Searches the room finds a few shiny valuables that have been stashed in the filthy rubbish if they succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. These treasures include a gold and ivory comb set with aquamarines worth 90 gp, a frozen lava of Pale Mountain, a greater potency crystal, and a greater pendant of the occult.

Alchemist Workshop.name: Alchemist Workshop
Alchemist Workshop.text:
The air in this large brick-lined chamber is acrid and foul enough to bring tears to the eyes and a sting to the throat. Large wood timbers support the ceiling. A pool of scummy water sits to the southwest, connected to a nearly flooded tunnel leading further south. Prison cells line the walls, each containing a slumped skeleton, while to the northwest and northeast stand immense metal tanks, each fitted with a round metal hatch on the front. A pair of bronze pipes run from the base of each tank down into a recessed area below, featuring shelves, alchemical workbenches, and a second pool of water. The pipes themselves attach to a large aquarium-like container, itself filled with murky green water that affords only faint hints of two strange shapes submerged within. A final curiosity sits to the east of the aquarium—a large wood and metal chair with dozens of surgical tools on armatures arrayed around it. A skeleton clad in a stained leather laboratory coat sits in the chair, most of its skull hidden by a large metal bowl-like hood attached to the back of the chair.

The air in this chamber is fouled (see @UUID[.YbrXOAsT3pQnXsIN]{Dungeon Features}). A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} in the southwest corner or spends an hour @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} the room and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check discovers the secret door (see area @UUID[.k9MS0A9QhgJfPA7G]{E2}).

The skeletons in the seven alcove cells are all mundane bodies, prisoners who agreed to a shorter sentence in exchange for time spent volunteering as subjects for castle apothecary experiments. All the cell doors are locked (@Check[thievery|dc:25|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock} or @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open}—these DCs increase by 5 if they’re attempted from inside the cell).

Encounter

Moderate 9

@UUID[Actor.eqHTr6Wj1JadHSa1]{Junth Rundel} @UUID[Actor.I0uOygen8uTlf3Wh]{The Glorious Ones x2} @UUID[Actor.8esAIVj311p8wg7K]{Middenworms x2}

Creatures: This large alchemical laboratory was the pride and joy of the castle’s latest alchemist and apothecary, a brilliant but antisocial Varisian man named Junth Rundel. Before the curse fell, Junth spent most of his time sleeping at his workbench and often skipping meals entirely. Kept on the payroll to attend to the alchemical needs of the Arudoras, Junth was delighted that these requests were relatively few, leaving him plenty of time to dabble in his own experiments. In the months leading up to the curse, Junth’s drug smuggling operation had started to fall apart. After he learned the castle guards were likely to soon confront him, he began destroying the evidence—including the prisoner “lab rats” in the cells who could all serve as witnesses.

He’d just finished poisoning the prisoners with a toxin that would make it look like they all succumbed to an unfortunate case of dysentery (Junth even had some falsified evidence ready to implicate one of the castle’s chefs), but the curse solved his problems for him.

When Charg’s curse reached Junth, a curious thing happened. Sensing his misanthropic attitude and alchemical brilliance, it didn’t transform him—instead it inspired him. Junth spent the first several years after the curse perfecting a new invention: a chair that would take his body, extract his brain, and transplant it into a new creation.

Junth’s experiment was a success, and he’s left the remains of his previous body there in the chair as decoration while he’s moved on to pursue a wide range of other experiments in his new noxious needler body. Junth’s experiments change every few decades, but the raw supplies he needs are always provided by the curse in the form of tormented reincarnated prisoners from his cells. Junth’s latest experiment involves placing two prisoners into the large tanks in the northern end of the room then using the slow-acting flesh-melting toxins extracted from a pair of middenworms also within, attempting to fuse several human bodies into a single enormous and glorious mass of life. Why? Why not?

While having a constantly renewing supply of reincarnated stock to experiment on has been a blessing, it’s also frustrated Junth. He’s come to believe he needs new stock to bring his experiments to the next level: the creation of a new and immortal body. The PCs represent opportunities to Junth, who clatters to his mechanical feet as soon as he notices the party, stepping toward them and speaking through a mechanized tube in his torso, asking them if they wish to be part of something glorious. Junth makes no attempt to hide his plans to reduce their “meat and bones and sinews and blood down to the raw protoplasmic slurry from which all life spawns” and promises that if he can perfect the method of creating immortal new bodies, he’ll build each of them new bodies as well. Of course, foolish PCs who submit to this process should end up experiencing painful and agonizing deaths that leave Junth more frustrated than ever at having wasted these “gifts” of new raw material.

Junth is quick to react to any perceived insult (including if even one of the PCs turns down his offer to be reduced to slurry) and shrieks: “You’ll do just fine in my vats whether or not you want it!” before he smashes a lever on a nearby workbench. This causes the aquarium walls to collapse—releasing the two middenworms kept within and spilling the nasty-smelling water out to flood the lower area to a depth of an inch or two; it also opens the tanks to the northeast and northwest, releasing Junth’s latest masterpieces: masses of protoplasmic flesh that appear to be several humans blended together into a boneless mass of skin, exposed organs, eyes, sobbing mouths, and hair. These creatures are called “the Glorious Ones” by Junth, and he eagerly orders them to capture the PCs.

Junth is smaller than the typical noxious needler, and he retains his original intellect. He lacks the ability to Generate Bombs and throw them; instead, he can fire razor-sharp hollow tubes attached to long leather hoses that he can use to drain blood from his victims from afar. He lets the middenworms and Glorious Ones do most of the fighting while he stays back, attempting to siphon blood from PCs each round until they force him into melee, at which point he fights until destroyed. He won’t pursue fleeing PCs out of this area, but the middenworms and Glorious Ones will.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Flood Alchemist's Workshop" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to break open the aquarium tank, freeing the middenworms, flooding the central area with water, and opening the northern tanks revealing the globsters!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.H69ZvgQ3YV9dOOsl]{Workbenches} @UUID[Actor.UlUHf4haT6iiJ6HG]{Workshop Shelves}

If the PCs spend an hour Searching through all of the material found in this room, they’ll make a wide range of discoveries. A key to all the cell doors can be found amid the various items scattered across Junth’s many workbenches, along with 600 gp in raw materials for the crafting of alchemical items. In addition to these materials, the PCs can find a vial of sparkling pink crystals. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyAlchemy.Title|options:action:identify-alchemy|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to Identify Alchemy determines this is a key ingredient for @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Bajwrol5y2n2ZIVm]{moderate crackling bubble gum}. If the PCs deliver the crystals to the chefs in the kitchen (area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.0994DpbY2N8XFkhL]{C40}), the PCs add this alchemical food to their list of items they can prepare.

The shelves contain several alchemical items, including two greater antiplagues, a greater cheetah’s elixir, three moderate elixirs of life, a vial of moderate emetic paste, a greater glue bomb, an octopus bottle, and a vial of spider root. In addition, there’s enough tools and supplies here that, once gathered, constitute two expanded alchemist’s labs.

Additionally, a small glowing gemstone sits under a stack of papers on one of the shelves. This is a greater soulheart. The first PC to touch this greater soulheart receives a brief memory of Ilana Greenbough paying a visit to Junth Rundel after hearing stories about the alchemist’s talents, only to be disgusted and frightened by his personality when he casually started talking about some of his more unsavory experiments and suggested to Ilana he could make her “more beautiful” if she’d only just agree to undergo a brief stay in one of his tanks. Ilana rejected him and spent the rest of her time in Maiserene worrying that Junth might convince someone else desperate enough to fall for his promises to risk their life in one of his unsavory pursuits.

On one workbench sit stacks of loose papers, scrolls, documents, and leather folders. A silver sickle sits on the top of the stack (see Side Quest Completion, below). The stack constitutes a wealth of information that Junth had been collecting for blackmail purposes on a wide range of frequent visitors to Castle Arudora. While most of these notes are centuries out of date, they can make for entertaining reading. And valuable research materials as well, as among those Junth had been collecting notes on were three of the Arudoras themselves!

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.mJYN4Onwrp1JCt7X]{Alisendra} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.BzucncWfHopUCsz3]{Dazerien} @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.m0khEHYdDxDw9B1G]{Raudltz}

Junth’s Blackmail Material: Among the notes are several documents of information gathered about Alisendra, Dazerien, and Raudltz Arudora. A PC can spend 2 hours studying the notes to research any of these three Arudoras.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[crafting|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to be able to understand Junth’s alchemist’s shorthand scattered throughout the notes or @Check[perception|dc:28|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to organize the notes and sift through them for clues.

Side Quest Completion

Delivering the silver sickle to Banijer Greely completes his @UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.UTLSqT61vU6a2H9C#side-quest]{side quest}.

East Entrance.name: East Entrance
East Entrance.text: The waters exit from the dungeon here in a slow flow powered by the paddles in area @UUID[.8h6QErLBhi0Ro2tn]{E7}, emerging on the haunted shore at area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.OWdcr3QHPHrYyFXD]{A15a}.

Vault Stairs.name: Vault Stairs
Vault Stairs.text:
A stone spiral staircase winds downward in the center of this large domed chamber. The walls and floor are made of brick, but the stone pillar in the center of the room is polished deep-purple porphyry.

These stairs end at an impassible wall of green mist after making one complete revolution down into the darkness. Once the PCs unlock the Vaults, the mist clears, and these stairs descend 410 feet down into area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.Sro3nm6CPZYejFdY]{H1}.

Ossuary.name: Ossuary
Ossuary.text:
Shelves are stacked five high along the walls of this twisting hallway. Several of the shelves have been stacked with all manner of humanoid bones, but many more lie scattered all over the floor, making for uneven footing.

This is the castle’s ossuary, a place intended to house bones moved out of graves or crypts as needed. Castle Arudora never quite had the need to fill many of these shelves in the mere 95 years it existed, but once the curse took over, the bones stored here multiplied. Each time a new body dies within the castle walls, be they visitor or reincarnated soul, their bones eventually end up here, and those have begun spilling out of the shelves onto the floors. This makes the floor in this area into difficult terrain for most (but see Creatures, below).

The door to the west is unlocked and leads to a flight of stairs, but progress beyond the first landing is blocked by a wall of impenetrable green mist. Once the temple is unlocked, this mist clears and the stairs can be taken all 100 feet up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.e6z8NTXgpq400EZk]{G5a}.

The secret door in the southern wall can be found by a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} the area (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the whole ossuary for an hour) and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check.

Encounter

Low 9

@UUID[Actor.mX47c0W9rizbmMBM]{Basilisks x6}

Creatures: Six acolytes were down here organizing and cleaning when the curse struck and transformed them into basilisks. Bone-white in coloration, the half-dozen basilisks spend most of their time lurking beneath piles of bones in the halls, where they’re well camouflaged and gain a +10 circumstance bonus to their Stealth checks. Their white eyes are huge and bulbous—when these bulging eyes protrude from the bones, they look uncannily like the tops of skulls. Choose which squares the basilisks are in—they let the PCs clamber over the first few before attacking from all sides, rolling Stealth for initiative (unless they’re spotted early by PCs who approach and succeed at @Check[perception|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] checks to notice the basilisks).

The basilisks fight to the death but won’t pursue foes out of the ossuary. These basilisks are more than just camouflaged in the bones—they’re quite adroit at slithering through the tangles and don’t treat this room as difficult terrain. A mound of bones rattling and moving toward the PCs before a basilisk rears up from them should be an unsettling sight as combat begins!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.TUKZ0cgJqRT7G0No]{Among the Clutter} @UUID[Actor.aNVvFl9KkSRbAK2u]{Bone Corner}

The amazing amount of bones cluttering the ossuary makes searching it a daunting task, but if the PCs spend two hours Searching, they’ll find a couple of items of interest. The first is a wand of vital beacon left here by the doomed priests. The second is a bronze gear the size of a dinner plate that’s embedded in the floor in the southwest corner of the room—another fragment hurled from the clock tower far above. This one phased downward until it became embedded here. A successful @Check[athletics|dc:28] check is required to wrest the gear free from where it became lodged in the floor. See @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.t1s9G6BjLx2VvxXt#missing-gears]{Missing Gears} for more details.

Prison.name: Prison
Prison.text:
This large brick-walled room has been fitted with just under a dozen cells. Each ten-foot-by-fifteen-foot area is sealed off with thick iron bars and cage-like doors, while within lie heaps of straw, a bucket, and a few old bones. Several of the cell doors are ajar, including four to the south that contain actual cots with furs and pillows. To the west, a set of shelves contain short clubs, straitjackets, coils of rope and chains, and other supplies one might expect in a prison aimed more at punishment than rehabilitation. To the east sits a stout wood desk and chair. The room is lit by lanterns hanging from hooks affixed to the central pillars.

All of the cell doors here are unlocked. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} at the spot where the southern secret door is located, or a PC who spends 30 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} this room, can discover the secret door to area @UUID[.rE5yeZ8h5hPBo5Hu]{E13} with a successful @Check[perception|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check.

Encounter

Trivial 9

@UUID[Actor.OOJs2UIxegZTGPp7]{Dazerien's Guards x4} @UUID[Actor.F0t6Eogd0KJdboXq]{Bastardhall Rats x2}

Creatures: The hapless prisoners once kept here became the Bastardhall rats or middenworms that now infest the dungeon. Today, the cells are kept unlocked, with four of them serving as places for four transformed guards to rest. These guards are now redcaps, all loyal to Dazerien Arudora. The first time the PCs enter this room, they find the redcap guards focused on the central cell to the north, cheering and howling in excitement. Inside the cell, a furious battle plays out between two raggedy-looking Bastardhall rats clad in collars attached to chains. These chains are threaded through the bars of the cells to the left and right, then out into the main area, so that the redcaps can take turns giving the chains slack or dragging them back as they try to cruelly maximize the length of time it’ll take the two rats to kill each other.

Once they notice the PCs, the two redcaps holding chains take time to secure them in place while a third steps forward and, seething with barely-hidden contempt, “politely” informs the PCs that visiting hours in the cell are over—unless they’re here to deliver new prisoners, of course! The four redcaps slowly pace around the place, sizing up the PCs as they draw out the conversation, waiting for an opportune moment to attack.

The guards shriek in delight if they can surround the PCs—or alternatively, as soon as the PCs “break the ice” and attack. They focus on unarmored PCs first and attack mercilessly.

If a PC opens the door to the rat cage, the two Bastardhall rats join the fight, attacking the redcaps. They flee into the sewers once the redcaps are dead and won’t attack the PCs unless they’re attacked first.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.u9kJCmNi641mfsEH]{Southwestern Cell}

The southwestern most cell contains this chamber’s only item of value—a softly flickering greater soulheart under an overturned bucket. If the PCs shutter the lanterns and plunge the room into darkness, they automatically notice the flickering; otherwise, they can discover the greater soulheart if they lift the bucket or succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:20|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check while Seeking or spending 30 minutes Searching the room. The first PC to touch this greater soulheart receives a brief memory of Banijer Greeley as he languishes in one of the cells here, seething at the fact that he’d been betrayed by his partner in a smuggling operation that ended up with him serving time in this dreary dungeon.

Torture Chamber.name: Torture Chamber
Torture Chamber.text:
There can be no doubt as to the purpose of this grim, brick- walled chamber. Wood pillars connect to rafters fifteen feet above, while all about the room are instruments of torture—iron maidens, stretching racks, strappados, tables filled with grisly tools, and iron cages. Chains dangle from hooks in the ceiling throughout, jangling softly as if jostled by a breeze despite the stillness of the air. A large furnace to the south has a wide array of brands stashed nearby, while a reeking pool to the north has been fitted with two more cages attached to armatures to allow for immersion in the sewage as desired by the torturer on duty. The foul stink in the air is only partially issuing from this polluted pool, for everywhere, lumps of fly-ridden rotten meat lie discarded on tables, dangle from spikes, or glisten in small heaps.

The air in this chamber is fouled (see @UUID[.YbrXOAsT3pQnXsIN]{Dungeon Features}). Moving through this room is awkward because of the large number of chains hanging from the ceiling and the fact that many bear spikes—only in the central area surrounded by the pillars are the chains absent. Everywhere else, moving through this room is treated as difficult terrain.

The stairs north of this room at area E12a lead up about 100 feet, twisting back and forth through a few landings, before reaching area @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48c}.

A PC @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeking} along the south wall can discover the secret door with a successful @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The door leads to a short hallway that ends in a set of double doors that opens into area @UUID[.UYzcuhyFPr5jTxCy]{E14}. In addition, the hallway between areas E12 and @UUID[.rE5yeZ8h5hPBo5Hu]{E13} contains a secret door that a PC can discover with a successful @Check[perception|dc:24|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|options:action:seek|traits:concentrate,secret] check. This door opens to a hallway with sets of stairs that lead down to area @UUID[.Zkj5BrXf9tgddGZ7]{E15}. This secret door is immediately obvious from the other side.

Encounter

Moderate 9

@UUID[Actor.qzkqAbdVRtqtMaZ5]{The Muse of Pain} @UUID[Actor.8esAIVj311p8wg7K]{Middenworms x4}

Creatures: Unless the PCs are quiet and sneaky when they enter this room, the awful inhabitant of the torture chamber takes note. This tormented soul is a hideous mound of body parts, faces, teeth, and fingers stitched together with black twine or held in place by tightly lashed leather straps. A manifestation of all those who felt pain from the tools and devices here, this monstrosity is a horrific, aching paean to agony that Dazerien regards as a sort of “muse” for his torturous pursuits.

The Muse of Pain attacks on sight, lurching toward the PCs and unleashing their Soul Scream as soon as they can. The Muse is treated as an irnakurse fleshwarp, but their twisted, distorted features combine elements of many more ancestries than just elves—the torturer of Castle Arudora did not discriminate among guests. As soon as the Muse of Pain attacks, four middenworms that lurk in the pool to the northeast slither up out of the waters to join the fight.

If combat begins here after dark, it’s only a matter of time before Dazerien Arudora arrives to investigate—noises of combat from his redcap guards in area @UUID[.yWa39YchcEgjuo0x]{E11} don’t disturb him, but the shrill howls of the Muse of Pain bring him running. If he lives, he bursts through the western door at the start of the third round of combat, howling in rage as he joins the fight. With Dazerien involved, this becomes a Severe 9 encounter.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.Mj5h6M6DgjWYjLdq]{Torture Schematics} @UUID[Actor.SHSd1s3joEf1kNoK]{Iron Maiden}

If the PCs spend 30 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} this room, they’ll find two things of interest. The first is a large collection of Dazerien’s notes and journals. Most of these are schematics for torture or records of previous brutalities, but a PC can use these to learn more about him—see @UUID[.#research]{Dazerien’s Notes} below.

The second item of interest sits within an iron maiden standing upright in the southwest corner. Opening this iron maiden allows a human skeleton to tumble out.

Once that fright is finished, a softly glowing greater soulheart can be found clenched in the skeleton’s jaws. The first PC to touch this greater soulheart receives a brief memory of Shirail Animender being hustled into this chamber in the dead of night by a panicked Augsten Arudora, who convinced her by a mix of threats and appeals to her kindness to accompany him to the chamber where Augsten’s cousin nearly killed an aristocrat’s son wrongfully imprisoned by Augsten’s false accusation. Shirail managed to save the aristocrat’s life and agreed to keep quiet about Augsten’s role in return for a promise of several healing potions and other supplies for her church. Unfortunately for the aristocrat, his saved life ended only a few nights later when Dazerien recaptured him and stuffed him in this iron maiden.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Open Iron Maiden" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to open the southwestern iron maiden, revealing the skeleton within!

Research

@UUID[JournalEntry.YwM6UU2fCnRTjzO2.JournalEntryPage.BzucncWfHopUCsz3]{Dazerien Arudora}

Dazerien’s Notes: They’re unsettling to look at, in part because of the lovingly detailed sketches of various methods of torture Dazerien includes in the journals’ pages, but a PC can spend 2 hours studying these partially encoded documents to learn more about him.

Maximum RP 3; Research Checks @Check[society|dc:26|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to make sense of Dazerien’s shorthand and notations or @Check[crafting|dc:28|name:Research|options:action:research|traits:concentrate,exploration] to be able to more efficiently navigate the portions of the text where Dazerien gets distracted by detailing his ideas for new torture implements.

Torturer's Room.name: Torturer's Room
Torturer's Room.text:
A lit and strangely smokeless fire pit flickers in the middle of this room between four wooden beams supporting the ceiling fifteen feet above. The brick walls to the northeast and northwest are adorned with several wooden shelves on which are displayed a staggering array of small torture implements or jars containing preserved... things... in cloudy liquid. Deep crimson curtains block off the southern portion of the chamber.

Beyond the curtains lies the personal quarters of Dazerien Arudora, although he didn’t actually move in here until after the Bastardhall Curse took over and transformed the chamber’s previous occupant, warden Vink Cratched, into a troll. True to his nature, Dazerien has decorated this room with a wide range of objects used for torture—most of which are things he crafted himself. The jars of preserving fluid contain various organs, including an unsettling preponderance of hearts, that Dazerien has “collected” from his torture victims over the years.

A PC can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic} in the fire pit in the middle of the room with a successful @Check[occultism|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[religion|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[arcana|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], or @Check[nature|dc:28|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|options:action:identify-magic|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check. A success reveals that the fire pit is an immobile magic item that continually burns without the need for fuel or the side effect of producing smoke. Dozens of bones litter the bottom of the fire pit—Dazerien is fond of allowing his “guests” to watch their severed body parts cook slowly.

Those guests stay in the cramped, spiky, and currently empty cage that Dazerien keeps in the southeast corner of his room. The cage door can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Forced Open} with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:31|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|options:action:force-open|traits:attack] check, or it can be opened with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:26|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|options:action:pick-a-lock|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock} (both of these DCs increase by 5 if the attempt is made from inside the cage). Alternatively, the key Dazerien keeps in his desk can unlock it.

Encounter

Moderate 9

@UUID[Actor.9nWMGCqmJ62CUKIU]{Dazerien Arudora}

Creature: The first time the PCs enter this room, Dazerien is found in the southern part of the chamber. Since every night in Bastardhall is a full moon, and by this point the days are 8 hours long, Dazerien spends the entirety of each day sleeping off the fatigue caused by the previous night’s Moon Frenzy. If the PCs visit during the day, he is fatigued.

After dark, he’s in his Moon Frenzy-enhanced hybrid form, seated on the floor at his desk (since he’s too large to sit in the chair), either designing or tinkering with a small torture implement.

If Dazerien is awake and hears the Muse of Pain cry out, he abandons his work to rush to area @UUID[.eqVhH8FR4IerjtmY]{E12}, as described there. Otherwise, as soon as he notices the PCs have entered his room (likely by hearing them unless the PCs are taking pains to be quiet) he calls out a warning to them from beyond the curtains: “Remain where you are, do not look beyond the curtain, and we can talk.” If at any point the PCs ignore this request and pull aside the curtains or move into the southern part of the room, Dazerien snarls in a mix of frustration and excitement and attacks—assuming hybrid form at the start of combat if he’s not in that form already. If the PCs manage to find him asleep in his bed, when he awakens he’s shocked and flustered. He gathers the sheets around himself and orders the PCs to give him some privacy; if the PCs do so and close the curtains, things proceed as detailed below.

If the PCs speak to Dazerien through the curtains, his cultured voice and aristocratic accent won’t suggest that they’re speaking with a 12-foot-tall werewolf. He starts combat by making an uncanny assumption—read the following to the players.

“Thank you for your manners; most uncommon a feature in these times. I presume you are the intruders who have been causing such a ruckus above, picking off my cousins and aunt? Well done, if so, and in that case we have something to discuss. If you’re not who I think you are, then kindly leave your gear behind and get the hell out of my room.”

If the PCs refuse to speak or successfully @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie} that they’re not the ones killing Arudoras, Dazerien emerges in hybrid form to attack—either immediately if he doesn’t hear them setting down their gear or after that bit of advice is followed otherwise. Once combat begins, Dazerien is eager and violent in his choices in battle, frequently using a third action in a round to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize} a PC. He does his best not to kill any PCs, since he’d prefer to capture them alive to torture later.

If the PCs secure an audience through the curtains, Dazerien has an unusual proposal for them.
