He felt it each time the PCs slew one of his family members, and he freely admits that while he’s relatively certain he could kill some or all of them in battle, he’s not ready to risk it. And so, he offers a proposal—is there anything he can offer the PCs in return for them leaving him alone? If they can work out an agreement, he promises to leave them alone as well.

Dazerien doesn’t understand how the PCs are unlocking regions of Bastardhall. If the PCs explain that they need a memento of his to return to the statue at area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fvc3WQXfj5Bcg2lM]{B3} of the castle grounds, he realizes that the PCs need his “@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.HKSpj0db5owAuA1v]{lucky thumbscrew}.” When he was a younger lad, Dazerien tormented a schoolmate with the thumbscrew; as the first item he ever used for such a purpose, it holds nostalgic memories for the sadist. He offers the thumbscrew to them as a peace offering. If he doesn’t come to this conclusion, he may or may not agree to any other offers the PCs propose (at your discretion), although in this case, they won’t be able to proceed into the private halls as he’ll still have his memento at his side.

Of course, Dazerien isn’t being completely honest here. As a sadist, he prefers the long game of torment and torture to the shorter game of personal combat. He’s hoping that the PCs assume he’ll keep his word, giving him the chance to go on a hunt soon thereafter. If the PCs leave Dazerien alive, he waits for a time (at least until nightfall if it’s not already night) before he emerges from this room to go to area @UUID[.yWa39YchcEgjuo0x]{E11} and gather his redcap guards if they still live. If they don’t, he seeks other potential allies. With his four redcaps at his side, a fight against Dazerien becomes a Severe 9 encounter—if he looks for other allies, you should create a roughly equivalent encounter by choosing creatures still living in Bastardhall that he can browbeat into service. Dazerien then goes on the hunt, stalking quietly through Bastardhall as he seeks information about the PCs.

Every night, Dazerien can attempt a @Check[bastardhall-lore|dc:25|traits:secret] check. On a success, he learns about the party’s basic habits, as well as the fact that they’ve gathered allies in Maiserene. On a critical success, he correctly predicts where the PCs are likely to rest the next time they do so. If he knows where they’re camping, Dazerien and his cronies ambush the PCs that evening—his goal is to abduct the smallest PC and return with his captive to area @UUID[.eqVhH8FR4IerjtmY]{E12} and begin torturing them, hoping to repeat this hit and run tactic nightly until he’s got all of the PCs captured. If he doesn’t know where they’re going to camp on a particular night, he instead abducts one of the Maiserene phantoms who have become physical and brings them to area @UUID[.eqVhH8FR4IerjtmY]{E12} for torture—in this case, he makes sure to leave enough clues for the PCs that they’ll know where their ally has been taken. Upon arriving in area @UUID[.eqVhH8FR4IerjtmY]{E12}, the PCs should face at least a severe encounter—perhaps even an extreme one—with a fight between themselves and Dazerien and any allies he can gather, turning their arrival in the torture chamber into an ambush. Regardless, you should give the party ample opportunity to rescue anyone Dazerien abducts!

As soon as Dazerien is slain, he howls in rage and thrashes about in his death throes before he topples forward, reverts to his human form, and then grows ghostly and translucent before rising upward, his soul returning to his tower at area @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.GEtrwYJ9Wy5A0qyw]{J3b}. His gear remains behind, and Dazerien’s thumbscrew is the key to unlocking the private halls of Bastardhall.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.4sBGtLTkoGSXNg08]{Torturer's Desk} @UUID[Actor.a3TlVYELysPY6Bcd]{Torturer's Bed}

A search of Dazerien’s desk reveals several partially completed and cruel-looking torture implements—some painfully obvious in their intended usage and others unsettlingly unclear as to how they might be used to torment a victim. None of these implements are worth much, but a PC who Searches the desk for 5 minutes discovers a small bronze key that unlocks the cage here, along with a stash of five moderate healing potions that Dazerien keeps around.

A well-read book sits on one of the pillows on the bed—one of Dazerien’s favorites, and a work of art he convinced an unsettled Ilves Mondain to let him borrow from the Arudora gallery. This book is a rare first edition printing of a notorious play called The Conception Exception, penned by famed author Merivesta Olinchi. It tells the sordid story of a Nexian noble whose attempt to usurp an inheritance through magical manipulation of bloodlines was a thinly veiled parable about certain shady practices being performed by some powerful politicians with whom Merivesta had a long-going feud. Merivesta became the first person to be assassinated by the Red Mantis during the premiere of her play, a doom that ensured this book would become a much sought-after prize. The first time it’s handled, the book triggers a memory of a version of this play being put on for the entire family and many friends up in the ballroom (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.BzbrB5DMMnjAcyag]{D11}). During this memory, the PC experiencing it notices just how uncomfortable and nervous Lord Raudltz Arudora grows during a portion of the performance that hinges on a bastard challenging his father for his inheritance. This book belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}); see @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{Lost Artwork} for more details.

Lord's Workshop.name: Lord's Workshop
Lord's Workshop.text:
Several wooden beams, many built into the brick walls, support the vaulted thirty-foot-tall ceiling of this enormous chamber, which is very obviously a combination showroom and workplace. Numerous animal and monster heads are displayed on the walls as trophies, while full-body taxidermy creatures stand on displays in the room or on shelves mounted to the walls. A set of three cluttered workbenches have been placed in the southern portion of the room, while a large stone tub filled with acrid-smelling water sits near the center of the room.

This chamber is Raudltz’s taxidermy workshop, chosen to constrain the foul- smelling chemicals and other odors that come with the hobby—as a result, the air in this room is fouled (see @UUID[.YbrXOAsT3pQnXsIN]{Dungeon Features}). Feel free to describe the numerous trophies on the walls (mostly big cats, bears, antlered ungulates, and large reptiles) and the three trophies on stands, which include an enormous taxidermy anaconda coiled around the beam at the center of the northwest stand and an equally immense centipede coiled around the southeast stand. But the most impressive display here is the largest one to the northeast—see Creature below.

The chemicals in the stone tub were used to help preserve hides or deflesh bones, depending on the needs at the time, but now the stuff in there is the primary source of the acrid stink in the room. A splash of the stuff deals @Damage[1d4[acid]] damage, while a creature that’s fully immersed takes @Damage[2d6[acid]] damage per round (@Check[reflex|dc:25|basic|traits:acid] save). The spiral stairs beyond the southwest door lead up to a wall of impassible green mist after only one revolution, unless the PCs have unlocked the @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8]{private halls}, in which case they lead all the way up to area @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.ndtRFPlOc0RB3Vc5]{F2e} above.

Encounter

Moderate 9

@UUID[Actor.YG6fgp2Kv0WtP8RH]{Taxidermy Allosaurus}

Creature: Raudltz’s latest pride and joy is the enormous taxidermy allosaurus that he’s posed to the northeast. Preparing this specimen required him to have his servants haul down the chopped up parts of the carcass after it was delivered, and then he had to preserve and prepare them swiftly before he stitched everything back together. The result was one that Raudltz was quite proud of, and the allosaurus looks very lifelike. In fact, the Bastardhall Curse has a lot to do with that. When its fell magic swept over the castle, it animated this dinosaur’s remains, transforming it into a powerful and unique scarecrow.

The taxidermy allosaurus doesn’t immediately animate as soon as it notices the PCs but instead bides its time, relying on its appearance to blend in with the other, real taxidermy in the room. It lurches to life and attacks as soon as any PC attempts to damage or manipulate it, but otherwise waits until it believes the PCs are distracted then steps off its perch with unnerving silence to creep up and attack, rolling Stealth for initiative. The sight of the animated dinosaur’s jaws opening in a silent roar to expose the straw stuffing down in its throat is unnerving indeed.

Campaign Manager

@UUID[Macro.HBpiP42BZc4EFbdN]{Open Campaign Manager}

You can use the "Animate Taxidermy Allosaurus" toggle found in the Areas tab of the campaign manager to hide the inanimate allosaurus tile and reveal its token!

As the fight continues, the allosaurus smashes apart other displays, shelving, workbenches, and even the stone tub; only the wooden beams are sturdy enough to withstand its actions. The fact that the dinosaur is so huge that it had to be dismantled before it was brought down here potentially gives the PCs an advantage—while the taxidermy allosaurus does try to pursue foes out of this room if they flee, it must @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeeze} with a @Check[acrobatics|dc:34|name:PF2E.Actions.Squeeze.Title|options:action:squeeze|traits:exploration,move] check to make progress down a 10-foot-wide hallway, and it can’t pursue at all up the stairs or through smaller tunnels. It returns here if it loses sight of its prey but otherwise fights to the death.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.uCzJs2T9UPwi13zq]{Lord's Workbench}

Raudltz kept very little of value here apart from a complete set of sterling artisan’s tools for taxidermy projects, but sitting on the southwestern workbench is a project he was working on restoring. He’d more or less finished the day the curse descended but hadn’t yet returned this taxidermy fey dragonet to the gallery for display. The workmanship on this curio is much finer and more elegant than the still-impressive job that Raudltz did on the other displays. The taxidermy dragonet’s wings have been gilt in gold, and its eyes are sparkling spheres of jade. It’s 1 Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it invokes a memory of an argument between Irrokcis and Zasha Arudora over the thing, which was a wedding gift from the Ordranti family in Caliphas. Irrokcis is delighted by the artistry, but Zasha was disgusted by the notion of putting a once-sapient creature on display; the memory ends with Irrokcis proclaiming that the gift would be put on display in the gallery and his newly-wedded wife storming off to lock herself away in a spare bedroom for the night. The taxidermy belongs in the castle gallery (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN]{D14}). See @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{Lost Artwork} for more details.

Carrion Pit.name: Carrion Pit
Carrion Pit.text:
The brick-lined walls of this room rise to a dome above. Patches of mold and partially dried puddles spot the floor, visible through the thin pale yellow mist that clings to the ground. A pit twenty-five feet in diameter yawns in the center of the room, and the mist roils and plumes above it rhythmically as if something immense down in the pit were slowly breathing.

The air in this chamber is fouled (see @UUID[.YbrXOAsT3pQnXsIN]{Dungeon Features}) with the smell of decay wafting up from the pit—even though its depths become impassable after descending a mere 5 feet as the hole becomes blocked by green mist. This mist clears once the PCs open @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X]{the vaults}, at which point the shaft drops straight down 440 feet into a contaminated pool of water—area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.mrOzlklF18CqGW2D]{H3}. A PC who falls into the shaft at this point can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.3yoajuKjwHZ9ApUY]{Grab an Edge} with a successful @Check[reflex|dc:25|options:action:grab-an-edge|traits:manipulate] save, otherwise they face a likely fatal fall; even if a PC lands in the mound of cushioning corpses below in area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.mrOzlklF18CqGW2D]{H3}, this fall deals @Damage[210[bludgeoning]|options:fall-damage] damage. A PC can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb} the mildew-slick brick walls of the shaft with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:30|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|options:action:climb|traits:move] check, although after descending 290 feet the shaft opens into a vast cavern, leaving no choice but to drop, fly, or start the long climb back up.

Laroba Beacon Entrance.name: Laroba Beacon Entrance
Laroba Beacon Entrance.text:
A central pillar of stone rises inside of this tower, surrounded by a wooden and metal flight of stairs that wind upward around it to the tower heights above. Several slate boards on the wall bear old smudges of writing in chalk.

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EwgTZBWsc8qKaViP]{Investigates} the slates can see that they were once used to track schedules of incoming visitors to the island from across the lake, so that the beacon could be activated to guide travelers to the nearby (now ruined) piers. The stairs lead up to area @UUID[.DRgsJI73yaw9G8Jk]{E17}.

Scene Levels

@UUID[Scene.z8wkbcziQufR7jWG]{Arudora Isle}

Note that this location and @UUID[.DRgsJI73yaw9G8Jk]{E17} appear on the west side of the Shore level.

Laroba Beacon.name: Laroba Beacon
Laroba Beacon.text:
While there may have once been elegant circular windows in the four walls of this chamber, all four of those windows are now smashed out. In the middle of the room, a curving flight of stairs winds down around a stone pedestal above which floats a spherical cage of iron mesh. To the northwest sits a wood and metal box covered with runes and fitted with a wheel, while above, rafters crisscross the interior of the tower’s conical rooftop.

This area is 180 feet above the tangled ground of area @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.Mr8Gsi42znsNq3XB]{A23} below. The stairs lead down to area @UUID[.AsVGoGtlVEkWPNv4]{E16}.

Among the many wonders and extravagances that Eragayl Arudora was able to include in the construction of his new home was this beacon tower. Similar to a lighthouse, this tower helped light the way for those who approached the castle via the lake after dark or in one of the region’s frequent fogs. Unlike a mundane lighthouse, though, this beacon used magic and a trapped creature to provide its light. The beacon no longer functions as originally intended, and the creature once kept within is now free to vent their anger on anyone who approaches.

Encounter

Moderate 9

@UUID[Actor.Cch6izfaVt5gnJSK]{Weak Shining Child}

Creature: The light here is provided by a single shining child. Eragayl spared no expense in having them bound into the cage to serve as the beacon’s source of light, and he felt little concern for this imprisonment due to the shining child’s wicked nature. Now, the wards fail the instant the PCs enter the area, allowing the shining child to activate their blinding aura and immediately blast the area with light. They attack, believing the PCs to be the source of their torment. Fortunately for the PCs, the creature has been weakened by their long imprisonment. As soon as the shining child is reduced to fewer than 150 HP, they fly off into the Ethereal Plane, never to return.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.NmlFronyWgA8U1sD]{Beacon Rooftop}

One of the gears from the clock tower shot out across the haunted shore when things went bad. This 1-foot-diameter brass gear embedded itself in the conical rooftop of the beacon, and a PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} this area from within notices the gear protruding through the roof above. It’s much easier to reach the gear from inside, as clambering through the rafters only requires succeeding at a @Check[athletics|dc:15] check. See @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.t1s9G6BjLx2VvxXt#missing-gears]{Missing Gears}.

Bastion of Blasphemies.name: Bastion of Blasphemies
Bastion of Blasphemies.description:
Every hundred years, a sinister coach drives across a ghostly causeway bridge from Castle Arudora and scours the land, hunting for any remaining members of the Arudora family. The PCs were hired by a woman searching for her parents who were snatched by this coach. Upon arriving at the shores of the lake that surrounds the castle, called Bastardhall by the locals since a curse befell the place, the PCs find they’re trapped and must unravel the mysteries of Bastardhall and the Arudora family if they hope to see freedom. Bastion of Blasphemies is a complete adventure for 5th- to 13th-level characters.

Content Warning: This adventure includes themes some readers might find troubling, including body horror, confinement, dismemberment, family violence, gore, spiders, and torture, as well as certain encounters that may be evocative of experiences with disordered eating. Additionally, recurring nightmares meant to represent common fears (of open water, open spaces, crowds, and fire, among others) are present throughout. Before beginning this campaign, understand that player consent (including that of the Game Master) is vital to a safe and fun play experience for everyone. You should talk with your players before beginning the adventure and modify descriptions of the narrative as appropriate.

Pharasma - Minor Boon.name: Pharasma - Minor Boon
Pharasma - Minor Boon.description:
You see a momentary, prophetic glimpse of your fate.

Once, you gain a +2 status bonus to a single check; you can apply this bonus after you determine the result, and it can potentially change the degree of success.
Pharasma - Minor Boon.gmnote: Granted each time a PC returns a @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{Missing Gear}. A PC can earn this boon multiple times, but if they already have the boon, it’s granted to a different PC in the party who doesn’t have the boon. If all PCs currently have the boon, no boon is granted for that gear's return.

Shelyn - Minor Boon.name: Shelyn - Minor Boon
Shelyn - Minor Boon.description: When you roll a failure on a Diplomacy check, you get a critical success instead (at which point the boon fades).
Shelyn - Minor Boon.gmnote: Granted each time a PC returns a @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#returning-the-artwork]{missing piece of artwork}. A PC can earn this boon multiple times, but if they already have the boon, it’s granted to a different PC in the party who doesn’t

Specialty Crafting (All Categories).name: Specialty Crafting (All Categories)
Specialty Crafting (All Categories).description:
Your training focused on Crafting one particular kind of item. Select one of the specialties listed below; you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Crafting checks to Craft items of that type. If you are a master in Crafting, this bonus increases to +2. If it's unclear whether the specialty applies, the GM decides. Some specialties might apply only partially. For example, if you were making a morningstar and had specialty in woodworking, the GM might give you half your bonus because the item requires both blacksmithing and woodworking.

Specialty Applicable Items
Alchemy* Alchemical items such as elixirs
Artistry Fine art, including jewelry
Blacksmithing Durable metal goods, including metal armor
Bookmaking Books and paper
Glassmaking Glass, including glassware and windows
Leatherworking Leather goods, including leather armor
Pottery Ceramic goods
Shipbuilding Ships and boats
Stonemasonry Stone goods and structures
Tailoring Clothing
Weaving Textiles, baskets, and rugs
Woodworking Wooden goods and structures

* You must have the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.is3Oz9wt11lNq62K]{Alchemical Crafting} skill feat to Craft alchemical items.

Virtuosic Performer (All Categories).name: Virtuosic Performer (All Categories)
Virtuosic Performer (All Categories).description:
You have exceptional talent with one type of performance. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus when making a certain type of performance. If you are a master in Performance, this bonus increases to +2. Select one of the following specialties and apply the bonus when attempting Performance checks of that type. If it's unclear whether the specialty applies, the GM decides.

SpecialtyExamples
ActingDrama, pantomime, puppetry
ComedyBuffoonery, joke telling, limericks
DanceBallet, huara, jig, macru
KeyboardsHarpsichord, organ, piano
OratoryEpic, ode, poetry, storytelling
PercussionChimes, drum, gong, xylophone
SingingBallad, chant, melody, rhyming
StringsFiddle, harp, lute, viol
WindsBagpipe, flute, recorder, trumpet

Effect: Arudora Library.name: Effect: Arudora Library
Effect: Arudora Library.description: You gain a +2 item bonus to your next check to Recall Knowledge or Research.

Effect: Bone Camouflage.name: Effect: Bone Camouflage
Effect: Bone Camouflage.description: You gain a +10 circumstance bonus to your Stealth checks.

Effect: Cathedral Initiative Bonus.name: Effect: Cathedral Initiative Bonus
Effect: Cathedral Initiative Bonus.description: You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to initiative.

Effect: Crafting Inspiration.name: Effect: Crafting Inspiration
Effect: Crafting Inspiration.description: You gain a +1 item bonus to Crafting checks to Craft.

Effect: Device Knowledge.name: Effect: Device Knowledge
Effect: Device Knowledge.description: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks made to Escape from Mum's Embrace.

Effect: Distracted Mister Moxie.name: Effect: Distracted Mister Moxie
Effect: Distracted Mister Moxie.description: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks made to Play Fatesnatcher.

Effect: Diversion Assistance.name: Effect: Diversion Assistance
Effect: Diversion Assistance.description: You gain a circumstance bonus to your skill checks to divert attention away from Alisendra.

Effect: Flare-Up Protection.name: Effect: Flare-Up Protection
Effect: Flare-Up Protection.description: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus on Reflex saves against the schoolhouse fire.

Effect: Unholy Consecration.name: Effect: Unholy Consecration
Effect: Unholy Consecration.description: You take a –1 status bonus to attack rolls, skill checks, saving throws, and Perception checks.
Effect: Unholy Consecration.gmnote: Worshippers of Urathoa take a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, skill checks, saving throws, and Perception checks. The PCs take a penalty to these rolls instead.

Effect: Wooden Object Repairs.name: Effect: Wooden Object Repairs
Effect: Wooden Object Repairs.description: You gain a +2 item bonus to checks made to Craft or Repair wooden objects.

Effect: Aracnophobia.name: Effect: Aracnophobia
Effect: Aracnophobia.description: When in combat against creatures that resemble spiders, you're off-guard. Whenever a spiderlike creature scores a critical hit on you with a Strike, or whenever you become affected by spiderwebs, you also become slowed 1.

Effect: Aracnophobia (Note).name: Effect: Aracnophobia (Note)
Effect: Aracnophobia (Note).description: If you are critically hit by a spider-like creature, you become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} from growing panic.
Effect: Aracnophobia (Note).gmnote: Foundry Note: This effect is automatically applied via an Ephemeral Effect rule element in @UUID[Item.pXJNt2NxwKZHPFPj]{Effect: Aracnophobia}.

Effect: Enochlophobia (Note).name: Effect: Enochlophobia (Note)
Effect: Enochlophobia (Note).gmnote: Foundry Note: This effect is automatically applied via an Ephemeral Effect rule element in @UUID[Item.skaR0p8AEpv7FvBs]{Effect: Enochlophobia}.

Effect: Hemophobia.name: Effect: Hemophobia
Effect: Hemophobia.description: Whenever you witness a creature within 30 feet take persistent bleed damage or endure a critical hit from a weapon Strike, you become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}. This becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} if you are the target of the bleed damage or critical hit.

Effect: Hemophobia (Note).name: Effect: Hemophobia (Note)
Effect: Hemophobia (Note).description: You become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} whenever you take are critically hit by a weapon Strike.
Effect: Hemophobia (Note).gmnote: Foundry Note: This effect is automatically applied via an Ephemeral Effect rule element in @UUID[Item.sYZI41JKGiMH8aO0]{Effect: Hemophobia}.

Effect: Nyctophobia.name: Effect: Nyctophobia
Effect: Nyctophobia.description: Whenever you are not in an area of bright light, you suffer a –1 circumstance penalty to Will saves. This increases to a –2 circumstance penalty when in darkness.

Effect: Proditiophobia.name: Effect: Proditiophobia
Effect: Proditiophobia.description: You can no longer benefit from the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.HCl3pzVefiv9ZKQW]{Aid} action and you can't flank foes with your allies.

Effect: Pyrophobia.name: Effect: Pyrophobia
Effect: Pyrophobia.description: You become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} whenever you take fire damage.

Effect: Teraphobia.name: Effect: Teraphobia
Effect: Teraphobia.description: At the start of any combat against a monstrous foe, you must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:31|options:lucid-nightmare,food-for-the-typhoon-wheel,inflicts:slowed,inflicts:stunned] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for the duration of the combat (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3} then slowed 1 on a critical failure).

Effect: Thalassophobia.name: Effect: Thalassophobia
Effect: Thalassophobia.description: You take a –2 status penalty to Athletics checks made while the waters of Lake Laroba are in sight.

Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 4).name: Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 4)
Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 4).description: Your vision-based Perception checks take a –2 circumstance penalty, and fog grants @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealment} to creatures 50 feet away.

Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 5).name: Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 5)
Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 5).description: Your vision-based Perception checks take a –1 circumstance penalty.

Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 6).name: Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 6)
Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 6).description: Your vision-based Perception checks take a –2 circumstance penalty and your ranged Strikes take a –1 circumstance penalty.

Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 7).name: Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 7)
Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 7).description: Your vision-based Perception checks take a –3 circumstance penalty and your ranged Strikes take a –2 circumstance penalty.

Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 8).name: Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 8)
Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 8).description: You take a –3 circumstance penalty on vision-based Perception checks and on ranged Strikes.

Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 9).name: Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 9)
Effect: The Skies Above (Chapter 9).description: You take a –3 circumstance penalty on vision-based Perception checks and on ranged Strikes.

Spell Effect: Lucinero's Illusory Disgui.name: Spell Effect: Lucinero's Illusory Disguise
Spell Effect: Lucinero's Illusory Disgui.description:
Granted by @UUID[Actor.EW55vYwOpZPT9kRd]{Lucinero}'s @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.i35dpZFI7jZcRoBo]{Illusory Disguise}

Lucinero receives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through his disguise, and he can add his level to such Deception checks even if untrained.

Dazerien's Bronze Key.name: Dazerien's Bronze Key
Dazerien's Bronze Key.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.rE5yeZ8h5hPBo5Hu]{E13}. This key can open the door leading to @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.GEtrwYJ9Wy5A0qyw]{J3b}.

Desk Keys.name: Desk Keys
Desk Keys.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.gxVn7eUIGm4UF4FV]{C37}. These keys open the cell doors in the same area.

Guard's Iron Key.name: Guard's Iron Key
Guard's Iron Key.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.wO8FX9GQqMgltKx6]{C28}. This key opens the chests in areas @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.bRpv2EG2zFh0BKHX]{C48} and @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.WUfxobQnHYYwiStb]{C49}.

Large Key Ring.name: Large Key Ring
Large Key Ring.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.5NSykzgTFMXg8qGD]{F8}. The majority of these keys are non-magical, and each matches one of the locks to one of the bedrooms upstairs (area @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.Mcpm8IomhSfb7Idn]{F10}); the vampires unlock those doors whenever they wish to “harvest” one of the meals trapped within.

Raudltz's Key Ring.name: Raudltz's Key Ring
Raudltz's Key Ring.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.tbuXpUsjFaPXpEM2]{F18}. These keys unlock the wall-mounted wheels for the Observatory shutters, as well as the door into @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.HiXOGKLx6aYdwEd4]{F1}, and the door to @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.ndtRFPlOc0RB3Vc5]{F2e}'s stairwell.

Rusty Iron Key.name: Rusty Iron Key
Rusty Iron Key.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.C41oEEjfo9D4rtgH.JournalEntryPage.NoRsDoZrbNHsWUCD]{A22}, this rusty iron key can open the door at the top of the stairs behind the shrine.

Small Bronze Key.name: Small Bronze Key
Small Bronze Key.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.rE5yeZ8h5hPBo5Hu]{E13}. This key opens the cage in the same area.

Small Iron Key.name: Small Iron Key
Small Iron Key.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.uvh9KJliEvdWQknO]{C4}. This key unlocks the eastern door in @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.2tXKE2JE45z1vCAd]{C38}.

Sturdy Iron Key.name: Sturdy Iron Key
Sturdy Iron Key.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.E1mrufqRAF8FwaWT]{B2}. This key opens the door to the armory (area @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.mG5rb8xF7l3JNp75]{B7}).

Workbench Key.name: Workbench Key
Workbench Key.gmnote: Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.8h6QErLBhi0Ro2tn]{E7}. This is a key to the cell doors in the same area.

Returned Alisendra's Fan.name: Returned Alisendra's Fan
Returned Alisendra's Fan.description: The DCs for all checks made to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} are reduced by 1 for the rest of the Adventure Path.

Returned Augsten's Cudgel.name: Returned Augsten's Cudgel
Returned Augsten's Cudgel.description: For the rest of the Adventure Path, you gain a +1 bonus to any initiative rolls; this special bonus combines with all other bonuses.

Returned Dazerien's Thumbscrew.name: Returned Dazerien's Thumbscrew
Returned Dazerien's Thumbscrew.description: For the rest of the Adventure Path, when you take your 8-hour period of rest, you recover an additional number of Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1) times your level.

Returned Irrokcis's Medallion.name: Returned Irrokcis's Medallion
Returned Irrokcis's Medallion.description: Your weapon Strikes deal an additional 1 spirit damage for the rest of the Adventure Path.

Returned Jinnivere's Riding Crop.name: Returned Jinnivere's Riding Crop
Returned Jinnivere's Riding Crop.description: PC companions (such as familiars, eidolons, and animal companions) gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws for the remainder of this Adventure Path.

Returned Raudltz's Telescope.name: Returned Raudltz's Telescope
Returned Raudltz's Telescope.description: Reduce all Perception DCs made when Seeking or Searching by 2 for the rest of this Adventure Path.

Returned Ryhasphinea's Hourglass.name: Returned Ryhasphinea's Hourglass
Returned Ryhasphinea's Hourglass.description: For the rest of this Adventure Path, the DCs for all recovery checks made by a dying PC are reduced by 2.

Bolster Maiserene Phantom.name: Bolster Maiserene Phantom
Bolster Maiserene Phantom.description:
Your maximum Hit Points increase for as long as you remain within Bastardhall while the castle remains cursed.

Note: Increase this effect's badge value by right-clicking its icon on the upper left corner panel to reflect the Hit Points increased by the Bolster Maiserene Phantom activation.

Effect: Ignore Difficult Terrain.name: Effect: Ignore Difficult Terrain
Effect: Ignore Difficult Terrain.gmnote: Note: At certain points during this Adventure Path, PCs and NPCs can ignore difficult terrain. You can apply this effect to a character for their token to bypass difficult terrain automated via Scene Regions.

Brass Gear.name: Brass Gear
Brass Gear.gmnote:
One of the clocktower's @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.UXOb2poQhtYDEFn3#missing-gears]{missing gears}. The first time a PC touches it, they hear the sound of a muffled explosion from the clock tower above the temple followed by the conviction that only does this gear not belong where it was found, but it yearns to be returned to the machinery it was once a part of.

Each of these brass gears resist corrosion and might be worth 25 gp to a clockwork technician or collector. No one in Maiserene will purchase them, as the phantoms instinctively recognize that they belong in the clock tower and suggest @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.osl3dmryGXkoTcAc]{returning them}.

If this gear is destroyed, it reforms back in the location it was found in 8 hours. Restoring all 13 gears to the clockworks is one of the required conditions to achieve this Adventure Path’s @UUID[JournalEntry.h6TuEj9PSqTQZ8le.JournalEntryPage.iIIzG8EEQwsCV7an]{secret ending}.

Polearm Flag.name: Polearm Flag
Polearm Flag.description: This flag’s embroidery features songbirds in flight carrying a wide range of flowers in their beaks and is exquisitely crafted.
Polearm Flag.gmnote:
"Glaive flag from Shining Crusade circa 3801 AR"

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.mG5rb8xF7l3JNp75]{B7}. This is an elegant, small flag meant to adorn the haft of a polearm that bears the colors of Shelyn. This flag’s embroidery features songbirds in flight carrying a wide range of flowers in their beaks and is exquisitely crafted. It belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery} and triggers flashes of memory when first handled. It was stolen a few days before the curse fell by a brash young guard who hoped to impress a paramour when they returned from a long trip to Caliphas. The curse fell first, and the flag has remained stashed here ever since.

Painting of a Beautiful Man.name: Painting of a Beautiful Man
Painting of a Beautiful Man.description: This painting depicts a strikingly beautiful man with long, dark hair standing along the edge of gentle stream in the middle of a forested valley beneath the light of an unusually large moon.
Painting of a Beautiful Man.gmnote:
“His Moonlit Tarn (Minialee Dreelish, 4213 AR)”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.YJC6FQzwcNy7rPBL.JournalEntryPage.fQvQS0zYiON5P7HI]{B15}. It depicts a strikingly beautiful man with long, dark hair standing along the edge of gentle stream in the middle of a forested valley beneath the light of an unusually large moon. It’s a beautiful, if haunting, work of art—and it was slated to be put on display in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery} only to be accidentally lost here a week before the curse struck.

The first time the artwork is handled, it triggers a flash of memory—of a man and a woman in love, enjoying a romantic night alone on the shore of a remote lake with the knowledge that one of them (the same man depicted in the painting) must return home to Castle Arudora come morning.

As the PCs might eventually discover, the man with the long dark hair was Ilves Mondain, the curator of the castle gallery.

Oil Portrait of a Serene, Beautiful Woma.name: Oil Portrait of a Serene, Beautiful Woman
Oil Portrait of a Serene, Beautiful Woma.description: This oil portrait features a serene, beautiful woman in an elegant wedding gown.
Oil Portrait of a Serene, Beautiful Woma.gmnote:
“Lady Tasifinie Arudora (Aerni Danvindr, 4117 AR)”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.2Ybt21NaXnVfBBQl]{C14}.This is an oil portrait of a serene, beautiful woman in an elegant wedding gown. If the PCs have accumulated at least 1 Research Point on the topic of Tasifinie Arudora, they automatically recognize the portrait’s subject as she appeared on her wedding day. The oracle had just finished restoring this painting (which had suffered some minor water damage), but hadn’t yet returned it to where it belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

The first time the portrait is handled, it triggers a memory of Tasifinie’s joy at wedding her lover, Eragayl. The PC experiencing the memory hears her whisper, “I love you, my brave tiger”—a playful lover’s nickname she had for him that could be useful to the PCs if they later encounter Eragayl’s ghost in the vaults below (area @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.MG8bJRohTuzWIbDI]{H6}).

Unicorn Statuette.name: Unicorn Statuette
Unicorn Statuette.description: A small alabaster statuette of a unicorn with a dawnsilver horn.
Unicorn Statuette.gmnote:
“Elven unicorn statuette, circa 3300 AR”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.66AjlvD5BncHDYJw.JournalEntryPage.c6GZaHL5hNIM6y3x]{C45}. The first time the statuette is handled, it triggers a memory of Jinnivere’s first (and only) time spotting a unicorn in the wild—a unicorn that tossed its head in disdain before racing away from the disappointed equestrian. This unicorn statuette belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

Portrait of Battle Against Undead.name: Portrait of Battle Against Undead
Portrait of Battle Against Undead.description: This portrait depicts a powerful figure fighting several undead monstrosities upon a grisly battlefield
Portrait of Battle Against Undead.gmnote:
“Arazni’s Answer (Vanch Bandresian, 3878 AR)”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.3bUvrSflCdnQOijp]{D12}. This portrait depicts a powerful figure fighting several undead monstrosities upon a grisly battlefield—a PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:15] check identifies the figure as Arazni and understands that this is a depiction of the Shining Crusade.

The first time this painting is handled, it triggers a memory of Alisendra Arudora attempting to duplicate it, only to become frustrated at her lack of skill. This drawing belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

Scrimshaw.name: Scrimshaw
Scrimshaw.description: The scrimshaw is a sperm whale’s tooth and depicts a whaling vessel being attacked by an enormous octopus.
Scrimshaw.gmnote:
“Cuttle scrimshaw, Mediogalti Isle, circa 4000 AR”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.fTnqkD249KyhYjdW]{D22}.This scrimshaw is a sperm whale’s tooth and depicts a whaling vessel being attacked by an enormous octopus. The first time it’s handled, it triggers a memory of Augsten Arudora using the tooth to commit his first murder—the slaying of a servant who dared backtalk him, and the subsequent cover-up by his father to keep Augsten out of legal trouble. This scrimshaw belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

Dissection Painting.name: Dissection Painting
Dissection Painting.description: This painting depicts an elven man who’s dissecting himself, revealing that his interior is made of clockwork gears.
Dissection Painting.gmnote:
“My Clockwork Mystery (Talia Vinsarlos, 3999 AR)”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.YEWYYZfoKnJcqp4j]{D29}. The first time it's handled, it triggers a memory of Raudltz Arudora shaking his head in frustration upon first seeing this commissioned work, complaining that “the interior workings aren’t lifelike enough” while Alisendra assures him that it’ll look lovely in the gallery nevertheless. The painting itself was stolen by a guest who hoped to make off with it later in the evening and hid it here for safekeeping for the rest of the day, only to have the curse disrupt her plans. Of course, this painting belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

Stone Carving.name: Stone Carving
Stone Carving.description: This is a stone tablet onto which has been carved an image of an elk-headed humanoid standing atop a hill overlooking a vast lake.
Stone Carving.gmnote:
“Isgeri Kellid carving of Erastil, circa –100 AR”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.k9MS0A9QhgJfPA7G]{E2}. This is a stone tablet onto which has been carved an image of an elk-headed humanoid standing atop a hill overlooking a vast lake. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:25] or @Check[society|dc:25] check recognizes it as an ancient Kellid carving of Erastil overlooking Lake Encarthan—one that, curiously, doesn’t feature an island visible at its center. The PC also recognizes the item’s architectural and artistic value. The stone carving is 2 Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it triggers a memory of an angry Ausken Dast reprimanding a sullen soldier for “borrowing” the artwork from the gallery, noting that “even if its religious significance would be better represented elsewhere, it is, unfortunately, the legal property of Lord Raudltz in the government’s eyes.” The memory concludes as the soldier promise to leave the carving hidden here and to return it later that evening during the night’s galas in return for Ausken’s promise to not report the near theft. This carving belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

The Conception Exception.name: The Conception Exception
The Conception Exception.description: This book is a rare first edition printing of a notorious play called The Conception Exception, penned by famed author Merivesta Olinchi.
The Conception Exception.gmnote:
“The Conception Exception, 1st ed (Merivesta Olinchi, 3923 AR)”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.rE5yeZ8h5hPBo5Hu]{E13}. This book is a rare first edition printing of a notorious play called The Conception Exception, penned by famed author Merivesta Olinchi. It tells the sordid story of a Nexian noble whose attempt to usurp an inheritance through magical manipulation of bloodlines was a thinly veiled parable about certain shady practices being performed by some powerful politicians with whom Merivesta had a long-going feud. Merivesta became the first person to be assassinated by the Red Mantis during the premiere of her play, a doom that ensured this book would become a much sought-after prize.

The first time it’s handled, the book triggers a memory of a version of this play being put on for the entire family and many friends up in the ballroom (area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.BzbrB5DMMnjAcyag]{D11}). During this memory, the PC experiencing it notices just how uncomfortable and nervous Lord Raudltz Arudora grows during a portion of the performance that hinges on a bastard challenging his father for his inheritance. This book belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

Taxidermy Dragonet.name: Taxidermy Dragonet
Taxidermy Dragonet.description: This taxidermy dragonet’s wings have been gilt in gold, and its eyes are sparkling spheres of jade.
Taxidermy Dragonet.gmnote:
“Fey Dragonet taxidermy (Diorius Ordranti, 4149 AR)”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.nj5uoJ3qBt7TStpZ.JournalEntryPage.UYzcuhyFPr5jTxCy]{E14}. The taxidermy dragonet’s wings have been gilt in gold, and its eyes are sparkling spheres of jade. It’s 1 Bulk, and the first time it’s handled, it invokes a memory of an argument between Irrokcis and Zasha Arudora over the thing, which was a wedding gift from the Ordranti family in Caliphas. Irrokcis is delighted by the artistry, but Zasha was disgusted by the notion of putting a once-sapient creature on display; the memory ends with Irrokcis proclaiming that the gift would be put on display in the gallery and his newly-wedded wife storming off to lock herself away in a spare bedroom for the night. The taxidermy belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

Music Box.name: Music Box
Music Box.description: The elegant music box plays a mournful Pharasmin dirge after it’s wound, and as it plays, little metal psychopomps pop up, dance, and move about inside of a glass dome atop it.
Music Box.gmnote:
“Pharasmin dirge box, crafter unknown, circa 4100 AR”

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.VMYvmrodRtjKL4n8.JournalEntryPage.4L6DULkZXAHEDZOI]{F7}. The first time a PC handles this music box, it triggers a memory of Alisendra Arudora bringing the music box here to test a visiting singer to see if she could perform the same dirge, only to humiliate her with a scathing review that sent her fleeing form the lounge in tears. The music box belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

Oil Painting of Defeated Champion.name: Oil Painting of Defeated Champion
Oil Painting of Defeated Champion.description: This painting depicts a scene from the Shining Crusade that never occurred: a pre-ascension Iomedae being slain by Tar-Baphon.
Oil Painting of Defeated Champion.gmnote:
“The Champion’s Fall” (Vanch Bandresian, 3880 AR)

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.LlsmjbqschdcAUSk.JournalEntryPage.xusIZ6ZnpPAUUJTS]{G8}. A companion piece to the painting in area @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.3bUvrSflCdnQOijp]{D12} that depicts a scene from the Shining Crusade that never occurred: a pre-ascension Iomedae being slain by Tar-Baphon. Ryhasphinea was taken with the painting and had plans to some day get it retouched to depict Iomedae being slain by Urgathoa, but she never got around to it and kept the painting in storage here. The first time the painting is handled, it triggers a memory of Eragayl arguing with his son Irrokcis about the appropriateness of displaying this near-blasphemy in the castle gallery. This painting, despite its provocative subject matter, belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

Wedding Portrait.name: Wedding Portrait
Wedding Portrait.description: An elegant painting of a man and his wife that depicts the two on their wedding day. Both look happy and carefree.
Wedding Portrait.gmnote:
“Lord and Lady Arudora” (Danch R. Gresswell, 4118 AR)

Found in @UUID[JournalEntry.GPl5VHF2ksW5wL8X.JournalEntryPage.MG8bJRohTuzWIbDI]{H6}. This is a glamorous portrait of Eragayl and his wife that depicts the two on their wedding day. Both look happy and carefree. This elegant painting was a wedding gift, and for many years, it hung in the Arudora gallery, but Irrokcis stole it and mounted it here to torment his father soon after imprisoning him (the other family members never learned the truth and thought the painting had been stolen by one of Eragayl’s enemies).

The first time the painting is handled, it triggers a memory of Eragayl’s anguish as his son, Irrokcis, mockingly puts the painting on display just out of reach but in full sight of his prison. This painting belongs in the @UUID[JournalEntry.l9OoOYdCKdM5VdWi.JournalEntryPage.PQNrZpJKI1yCx0UN#lost-artwork]{castle gallery}.

Spell Effect: Zizminarial's Illusory Dis.name: Spell Effect: Zizminarial's Illusory Disguise
Spell Effect: Zizminarial's Illusory Dis.description:
Granted by @UUID[Actor.VQrtNCtgkoNuCaxn]{Zizminarial}'s @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.i35dpZFI7jZcRoBo]{Illusory Disguise}

Zizminarial receives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through his disguise, and he can add his level to such Deception checks even if untrained.

Bastardhall Familiarity.name: Bastardhall Familiarity
Bastardhall Familiarity.description: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks made to notice secret doors or hidden caches in the castle.

Arudora Familiarity.name: Arudora Familiarity
Arudora Familiarity.description: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus on all checks made to research individual Arudoras, or the creatures they have become.
